Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Gesomun on the north wall of Pyongyang, arms flung wide
Xue Rengui in white armour in the Andong Protectorate yard, a real Tang compound on Goguryeo ground
images.prompt: Cinematic historical still, 16:9, of a REAL Tang protectorate courtyard: rammed-earth walls, a white banner, timber halls. Xue Rengui in pale armour stands small in the yard. A thin red of old Goguryeo hills on the horizon. Painterly cinema, iconic but geographically real. Flat sky, no clouds. No text, no watermark.

blocks.html: In the high mountains of Manchuria, a young man is caught in the snow by a Goguryeo soldier.
blocks.ko: 만주의 높은 산속, 한 청년이 눈밭에서 고구려 병사에게 붙잡힌다.

blocks.html: He is taken to the outpost of Commander Yeon (29), the Eternal General — a ruthless military general.
blocks.ko: 그는 무자비한 무장, 영원의 대장군 연 장군 (29)의 초소로 끌려간다.

blocks.caption: Twenty-nine. He holds the eastern border in his father’s name, and nobody here calls him a son.
blocks.ko: 스물아홉. 아버지의 이름으로 동쪽 국경을 쥐고 있고, 여기서 그를 아들이라 부르는 이는 없다.

en: Do you know what happens to traitors, young man...?

blocks.html: It is over quickly, and it is not clean. Nobody in the yard looks away, because looking away is also a report.
blocks.ko: 금방 끝났고, 깔끔하지 않았다. 마당에 선 누구도 눈을 돌리지 않는다. 눈을 돌리는 것 또한 보고가 되니까.

blocks.html: The guards talk about him the way men talk about weather. “He’s a monster, you know. Out here they call him the Red Sun of Pyongyang. He’s made the Eastern Commandery the safest in the kingdom. The barbarians run if they hear his name.”
blocks.ko: 경비병들은 날씨 얘기하듯 그를 입에 올린다. “저 사람 괴물이야, 알지? 여기선 평양의 붉은 해라고들 해. 동부 도호부를 나라에서 제일 안전한 데로 만들어 놨잖아. 오랑캐들은 이름만 들어도 도망간다니까.”

blocks.html: Gaesomun*, also called Gaegeum. His surname was Yeon. He claimed he had been born in water, to awe the crowd. He was imposing to look at, and bold and free in spirit.
blocks.ko: 개소문*은 개금이라고도 한다. 성은 연씨이다. 스스로 물속에서 태어났다고 말하여 무리를 현혹하였다. 풍채가 웅장하고 위엄 있었으며, 기개가 호방하였다.
blocks.hanja: 蓋蘇文，或云蓋金。姓淵氏。自云生水中，以惑衆。儀表雄偉，意氣豪逸。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun

notes.html: The Korean annals spell him Gaesomun. This book says Gesomun. One man, five swords.
notes.ko: 기록의 개소문이 곧 이 책의 연개소문이다. 영어 표기만 다르다.

blocks.html: The outpost is also a building site. Three summers ago, the Tang flattened Goguryeo's pile of enemy bones. Goguryeo got the message. Now it builds a wall. A thousand li of it. When Yeon isn't killing anybody, he walks it with a plumb line and kicks the crooked stones.
blocks.ko: 초소는 공사장이기도 하다. 세 해 전 여름, 당이 고구려의 적군 뼈 무덤을 밀어 버렸다. 고구려는 알아들었다. 그래서 지금 성을 쌓는다. 천 리나. 연은 누굴 죽이지 않을 때면 다림줄을 들고 그 성을 걸으며 삐뚤어진 돌을 걷어찬다.

blocks.html: Tang sent Zhangsun Shi, adjutant of Guangzhou, to bury the bones of the Sui soldiers, sacrifice to them, and pull down the mound of bones raised in those days. In spring, the second month, the king called out the people to build a long wall, from Buyeo Fortress in the northeast to the sea in the southwest, more than a thousand li. It took sixteen years to finish.
blocks.ko: 당이 광주사마 장손사를 보내 수나라 전사들의 해골을 묻고 제사 지내게 하고, 그때 세운 경관을 허물었다. 봄 2월, 왕이 무리를 동원하여 장성을 쌓으니, 동북으로 부여성에서 서남으로 바다에 이르기까지 천여 리였다. 무릇 16년 만에 공사를 마쳤다.
blocks.hanja: 唐遣廣州司馬長孫師，臨瘞隋戰士骸骨，祭之，毁當時所立京觀。春二月，王動衆築長城，東北自扶餘城，東西南至海千有餘里，凡一十六年畢功。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 20, Goguryeo Annals — King Yeongnyu, yr. 14 (631)

blocks.html: In the fifth year an edict sent Zhangsun Shi, adjutant of the Guangzhou command, to gather and bury the bones of those killed in the Sui wars, and to pull down the mound of bones Goguryeo had raised. The king, Geonmu*, afraid his country would be invaded, built a long wall from Buyeo Fortress in the northeast to the sea in the southwest, more than a thousand li.
blocks.ko: 5년, 조서를 내려 광주도독부 사마 장손사를 보내 수나라 때 전사한 이들의 해골을 거두어 묻게 하고, 고구려가 세운 경관을 허물게 하였다. 건무*는 나라가 정벌당할까 두려워 장성을 쌓으니, 동북으로 부여성에서 서남으로 바다에 이르기까지 천여 리였다.
blocks.hanja: 五年，詔遣廣州都督府司馬長孫師往收瘞隋時戰亡骸骨，毀高麗所立京觀。建武懼伐其國，乃築長城，東北自扶餘城，西南至海，千有餘里。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo, Zhenguan 5 (631)

notes.html: Geonmu (建武) was the king’s own name. This book calls him King Yeongnyu, the name the court gave him after he died.
notes.ko: 건무는 왕의 이름이다. 이 책은 죽은 뒤에 받은 이름, 영류왕으로 부른다.

lines: 자네가... 우리 기밀을 적에게 유출했다 했지.
반역자에게는... 어떤 벌이 내려지는 지 알고 있나?
en: They say you… leaked our secrets to the enemy.
Do you know what punishment is given to a traitor?

blocks.speaker: Prisoner
en: I have… no name.
Of course. The barbarians always show more respect.

blocks.html: A month before the Summit, in a Mohe village the Eastern Command has finished with, there is a boy who will not move out of the doorway of a house that no longer has a roof. Snow is settling on the ash. He has a shaved crown and two braids, and he holds a stick the way he has seen men hold spears. Yeon gets down off the red bay and walks up until the stick touches his chest.
blocks.ko: 제가회의 한 달 전, 동부대가 일을 마치고 떠난 말갈 마을에, 지붕이 없어진 집 문간에서 비키지 않는 사내아이가 하나 있다. 재 위로 눈이 내려앉는다. 정수리를 밀고 머리를 두 갈래로 땋은 아이가, 어른들이 창 잡는 걸 본 대로 막대기를 쥐고 서 있다. 연은 붉은 밤색 말에서 내려, 막대기 끝이 가슴에 닿을 때까지 걸어온다.

en: Move.
Do you understand me.

blocks.html: He does not. Yeon looks at him for what his officers later agree was an unreasonable length of time. Then he laughs, the slap of a laugh they will learn to dread, and pulls off his gloves.
blocks.ko: 알아듣지 못한다. 연은 부하들이 뒷날 지나치게 길었다고 입을 모으는 시간 동안 아이를 본다. 그러다 웃는다. 부하들이 두려워하게 될, 뺨을 치는 듯한 웃음이다. 그러고는 장갑을 벗는다.

lines: 이놈 봐라. 다 타 버린 집을 지키고 섰네.
en: Look at this one. Guarding a house that’s already burned.
Good. This is what Goguryeo looks like.
Get on. The second horse.

blocks.html: He hands the gloves down. They do not fit. The boy gets on the second horse anyway, the stick still in his fist.
blocks.ko: 장갑을 내려 준다. 맞지 않는다. 아이는 그래도 막대기를 쥔 채 두 번째 말에 오른다.

blocks.caption: An old Yeon friend. The one man at the outpost who asks the commander questions.
blocks.ko: 연의 오랜 벗. 초소에서 장군에게 질문을 하는 단 한 사람.

en: …You are taking him?

lines: 저 아이가 크면 어디에 서 있을 것 같으냐.
en: Where do you think that boy is standing when he is grown.
…Opposite us, I should think.
That is why I am taking him.

blocks.html: He gives him the name Gulgul, which is not a Goguryeo name and is not a Mohe one either, and raises him in Pyongyang alongside his own sons — one step behind them at every meal.
blocks.ko: 그는 아이에게 걸걸이라는 이름을 준다. 고구려 이름도 아니고 말갈 이름도 아니다. 그리고 평양에서 제 아들들과 함께 기른다. 끼니마다 아들들보다 한 걸음 뒤에서.

blocks.caption: A Mohe boy who guarded a burned house. Now he guards whatever Yeon points at.
blocks.ko: 타 버린 집을 지키던 말갈 아이. 이제는 연이 가리키는 것을 지킨다.

blocks.html: Years later, on the north wall of Pyongyang in a winter worse than this one, Yeon stands with the grown boy a step behind him and the river frozen white below. He says the thing he says every winter, to anyone in earshot, as if the cold might forget it otherwise.
blocks.ko: 여러 해 뒤, 이번보다 더 혹독한 겨울, 평양 북쪽 성벽 위에 연이 서 있다. 다 큰 아이가 한 걸음 뒤에 있고, 아래로는 강이 하얗게 얼어 있다. 연은 겨울마다, 듣는 사람만 있으면 누구에게나 하는 말을 한다. 추위가 잊어버리기라도 할 것처럼.

en: Cold?
…No, sir.

lines: 그래도 기억해. 왕은 죽고, 조정은 지치고, 성은 무너져도—
en: Liar. I’m cold too.
Remember it anyway. Kings die, courts get tired, walls come down—
Goguryeo never dies.

blocks.html: Gulgul grows up quiet. When Yeon sends him to guard the northern marches, he gives him a surname. Dae. Big, as big as the country. Dae Gulgul watches that border for thirty years, and nobody writes down anything else about him. They write a great deal about his son.
blocks.ko: 굴굴은 조용히 자란다. 연은 그를 북쪽 변경으로 보내며 성을 하나 붙여 준다. 대(大). 나라만큼 크라고. 대굴굴은 삼십 년을 그 국경에서 보내고, 그에 대해선 아무도 더 적지 않는다. 그의 아들에 대해선 아주 많이 적는다.

blocks.caption: A surname at last. Big, as big as the country.
blocks.ko: 드디어 성이 생겼다. 크다. 나라만큼.

blocks.html: The summons isn't addressed to him. It's addressed to his father, who still holds the Eastern seal. Yeon Taejo sat in the capital's big chair for twelve years. Now he is too old to ride that far. The son has done the work for years. The seal is still the old man's.
blocks.ko: 소집령은 그에게 온 게 아니다. 아직 동부의 인장을 쥔 아버지에게 왔다. 연태조는 도성의 큰 자리에 열두 해를 앉아 있었다. 이제는 거기까지 말을 탈 수 없을 만큼 늙었다. 일은 몇 해째 아들이 해 왔다. 인장은 아직 노인의 것이다.

blocks.caption: The old Eastern Commander. He sat in the big chair long enough to know what it costs.
blocks.ko: 늙은 동부 대가. 큰 자리에 오래 앉아 봐서, 그 값을 안다.

lines: 인장 가져가라. 올해는 네가 내 자리에 앉는다.
en: Take the seal. You sit in my place this year.
…And say half of what you think.

lines: 제가요? 평양엔 제가 왜 가야 합니까?
어차피 쓸데없는 소리나 하려고 주둥이 벌리는 데인데...
en: Me? Why do I have to go to Pyongyang?
It’s a place where mouths open only to say useless things…

lines: 안다. 내가 열두 해를 앉아 있었다.
en: I know. I sat in it for twelve years.
Half, son. Half.

blocks.html: He promised his father half. He has never said half of anything. Next stop: Pyongyang, and a room full of men counting grain…!
blocks.ko: 아버지께 반만 하겠다고 했다. 그는 평생 무엇이든 반만 해 본 적이 없다. 다음은 평양. 곡식을 세는 사내들로 가득한 방이다…!

Yeon Gesomun a small figure standing on the TALLEST block only. Face matches the attached portrait: thick black beard, crow-stamped armor. Striking silky Goguryeo court-military, premium red silk sheen, few hues. ONE accent: a black three-legged-crow mark. Flat charcoal void. No army. No palace clutter. No clouds. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.alt: Bird's-eye onto the High Summit's tall five-sided table: one Goguryeo commander at each side under red banners
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE watercolor painting, minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop. Night in the great hall of Pyongyang palace. High bird's-eye angle. ONE device: a tall raised PENTAGON table, five equal sides of dark timber standing at chest height, the five-pointed shape reading clearly from above. One Goguryeo commander stands at each of its five sides, five men only, in court-military dress with Goguryeo red #C30000 cloth, each with his commandery's red banner hanging in the dark behind him. Young Yeon Gesomun stands at one side leaning in; old High Commander Yeon Gusesa stands at the next side, composed. A single bronze lamp hangs low over the centre of the pentagon; beyond, the king's dais is only a dim step in shadow. Background and foreground are a Renaissance tenebrist oil painting: glazed umber and oxblood darks, timber and pillars carved out of black by the one lamp, sfumato edges; the webtoon figures painted into that oil space in ink line and watercolor wash under the same key. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | YEON GUSESA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_commander_1.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b2554a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Pyongyang (평양성) — attached board /pl_pyongyang_city.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang: Goguryeo walled city on the Taedong, stone walls and red munru gate pavilions. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. BACKGROUND AND FOREGROUND are a high-contrast Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST OIL PAINTING in their own right (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt, late Titian): a warm umber-to-black ground; walls, timber, stone, drapery, tables and the dark foreground shapes modelled in glazed oil and pulled out of the darkness by the one candle, lamp or window, with soft sfumato falloff into black — the webtoon figures are set INTO that old-master oil space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. blocks.html: So Yeon rides to Pyongyang in his father's place. Five commanders, one king, one room. They call it the High Summit.
blocks.ko: 그래서 연이 아버지 대신 평양으로 간다. 대가 다섯, 왕 하나, 방 하나. 제가회의라 부른다.

blocks.html: He rides in at the red two-tier gate. Pyongyang already knows the sound of those hooves.
blocks.ko: 그는 붉은 이중 문루로 들어간다. 평양은 이미 그 발굽 소리를 안다.

blocks.html: Goguryeo works like this. Five commanders argue. The High Commander holds the first sword. The king has the last word.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 이렇게 돌아간다. 대가 다섯이 다툰다. 막리지가 첫 칼을 쥔다. 마지막 말은 왕이 한다.

blocks.html: Their highest office is called Daedaero, the High Commander. It ranks with our first grade, and its holder oversees all the business of the state. It changes hands every three years, though a man who does the job well is not held to the term. On the day of handover, if the parties will not submit to each other, they all call out their troops and fight, and the winner takes the post. Their king simply shuts the palace gates and guards himself. He cannot stop it.
blocks.ko: 그 벼슬 가운데 큰 것은 대대로라 부르니, 1품에 견주며 나랏일을 모두 맡는다. 3년마다 한 번 바뀌되, 직책을 잘 해내는 자는 햇수에 구애받지 않는다. 교대하는 날 서로 복종하지 않으면 모두 군사를 거느리고 서로 공격하여, 이긴 자가 그 자리를 차지한다. 그 왕은 다만 궁궐 문을 닫고 스스로를 지킬 뿐, 이를 막지 못한다.
blocks.hanja: 其官大者號大對盧，比一品，總知國事，三年一代，若稱職者，不拘年限。交替之日，或不相祗服，皆勒兵相攻，勝者爲之。其王但閉宮自守，不能制禦。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

blocks.hanja: 諸加會議
blocks.html: The meeting of the ka. A ka was a tribal chief, back when Goguryeo was five roofs in one valley. The roofs became commands, the chiefs became generals, and the meeting kept its old name, the way old men keep their nicknames.
blocks.ko: 가(加)들의 모임. 가는 고구려가 한 골짜기의 지붕 다섯이던 시절의 부족장이다. 지붕은 군단이 되고, 족장은 장군이 됐지만, 모임은 옛 이름을 그대로 썼다. 노인들이 어릴 적 별명을 버리지 않듯이.

blocks.title: 제가회의 · The Commanders’ Council
blocks.caption: Five commands around one table, and the High Commander at its head. The king sits just outside the ring. He has the last word, and they make sure it is the last.
blocks.ko: 한 상에 둘러앉은 다섯 부, 그 머리에 막리지. 왕은 고리 바로 바깥에 앉는다. 마지막 말은 왕의 것이고, 그들은 그 말이 정말 마지막이 되도록 한다.

blocks.html: The chamber is already loud when Yeon arrives — not with strategy, with arithmetic. Every banner wants a larger share of the same winter grain.
blocks.ko: 연이 들어올 때 전각은 이미 시끄럽다 — 전략이 아니라 셈으로. 깃발마다 같은 겨울 군량의 더 큰 몫을 원한다.

en: Enough.
I did not call five commands to Pyongyang to divide a granary.
I will be the “King for All” — Samhan under one roof. Silla and Baekje first.
lines: 곳간이나 나누자고 오부를 평양에 부른 것이 아니다.
짐이 “삼한왕검”이 되리라 — 삼한을 한 지붕 아래로. 신라와 백제부터.

en: Then the Southern Command takes the next levy.
Yushin’s banners have been testing the passes. If His Majesty wants Samhan, give me men — not speeches.
lines: 유신의 깃발이 고개를 두드리고 있습니다. 폐하께서 삼한을 원하시면 병력을 주십시오 — 연설이 아니라.

en: And leave the north bare?
The Mohe burned three villages last frost — Haemosu’s sun does not reach the north in winter, and neither do Central’s warehouses. I need the cavalry remounts promised at the last Summit.
lines: 지난 서리 때 말갈이 마을 셋을 태웠소. 겨울 북방엔 해모수의 해도 안 닿고, 중부 창고의 물자도 안 닿소. 지난 제가회의에서 약속한 기병 보충은 어디 있소.

en: The Liao watch needs timber and iron, not another southern adventure.
If we strip the west to chase Samhan, we gift the Tang a road.
lines: 요하 봉수에 필요한 건 목재와 쇠지, 또 한 번의 남정(南征)이 아니오.
서부를 벗겨 삼한을 쫓으면, 당에게 길을 선물하는 셈이오.

blocks.caption: The High Commander. He chairs the room like a feast and counts it like a granary.
blocks.ko: 막리지. 잔치처럼 회의를 주재하고, 곳간처럼 셈한다.

en: (mild, as if chairing a feast)
Each front believes it is the only front. That is why we meet.
Eastern Command has kept the marches quiet. Let us not reward noise over results.
lines: 전선마다 자기만 전선이라 믿지. 그래서 모이는 것이오.
동부대는 변방을 조용히 지켜 왔소. 성과보다 목소리를 상 주지 맙시다.

en: My grandfather still toasts Ulchi at the Colossal River — Salsu, the old men say — as if a drowned Sui host were a harvest.
Ansi’s walls are not a toast. They are a bill we keep paying in stone.
lines: 우리 할아버지는 아직도 살수 — 늙은이들은 그리 부르지 — 을지에게 잔을 든다. 익사한 수나라 대군이 수확이라도 되는 양.
안시 성벽은 축배가 아니다. 돌로 계속 갚는 빚이다.

en: Then stop paying the West in gold for another quiet decade.
Rivers remember who feeds them. So do fortresses.
lines: 그러면 또 한 번의 조용한 십 년을 금으로 서쪽에 사지 마라.
강은 누가 먹였는지 기억한다. 산성도 그렇다.

en: Quiet?
I have been killing tribes so this room can argue about who gets the horses.
Meanwhile the Second Emperor is not a tribute account. He is a man who murders brothers for a throne and then invents a reason.
lines: 이 방이 말 배분을 놓고 다투라고 내가 오랑캐를 베어 온 줄 아시오.
그사이 당 황제는 조공 장부가 아니오. 왕좌를 위해 형제를 죽이고 나서 이유를 발명하는 사내요.

en: Commander Yeon. Watch your tongue about foreign kings.
We have bought decades with gold. We will buy more — and spend the peace on Samhan.
lines: 연 장군. 외국 임금 혀를 조심하게.
금으로 수십 년을 샀고, 더 살 것이다 — 그 평화로 삼한을 사겠다는 뜻이야.

en: You cannot buy a man who has already decided the price of your head.
I have watched how courts die: they starve the wall that is screaming, and fatten the wall that flatters.
Give the west grain. Give the north horses. Give the south whatever fairy tale you like —
but do not sit here pretending the Second Emperor is a weather we can ignore because tribute is habit.
lines: 제 목의 값을 이미 정한 사내에게는 살 수 없소.
조정이 죽는 꼴을 보았소: 비명 지르는 성벽을 굶기고, 아첨하는 성벽을 살찌운다.
서부에 군량을. 북부에 말을. 남부엔 원하는 동화를 —
그러나 조공이 습관이라 황제를 무시할 날씨처럼 여기는 이 자리는 참지 못하겠소.

en: Easy for the East to lecture. You fight people without cities.
I fight Kim Yushin. Send me the next levy or stop talking about Samhan.
lines: 동부가 훈계하긴 쉽지. 당신들은 성 없는 놈들과 싸우니까.
나는 김유신과 싸운다. 다음 징발을 주든지, 삼한 이야기는 그만두시오.

en: And I will not freeze another winter while Central counts my remounts twice.
lines: 중부가 내 보충 말을 두 번 세는 동안 또 한 겨울을 얼어 죽고 싶진 않소.

en: Nor will I strip the Liao for a king’s poem about one peninsula.
lines: 임금의 반도 시 때문에 요하를 벗기지도 않겠소.

blocks.html: Yeon’s hands are flat on the table. The nails have gone white. This is the face of a man who has already fought the war the room refuses to schedule.
blocks.ko: 연의 손이 상 위에 납작하다. 손톱이 하얘졌다. 방이 일정에 넣기를 거부하는 전쟁을, 이미 싸워 본 사내의 얼굴이다.

en: Listen to yourselves.
Horses. Timber. Bodies. A crown-word.
When the Second Emperor comes he will not ask which of you was most polite in committee.
lines: 당신들 말하는 꼴 좀 들어 보시오.
황제가 오면, 이 중 누가 회의에서 제일 공손했는지는 묻지 않을 거요.

en: If you keep defying the king, Commander Yeon…
we may have to name you a traitor.
(to Yeon, almost kindly — which is worse)
Nephew. Sit down. The Summit does not run on prophecies.
lines: 조카. 앉게. 제가회의는 예언으로 돌지 않네.

en: Then keep your Summit.
Keep your tribute. Keep your Samhan dream carved into a budget fight.
When the Second Emperor’s drums reach the Liao, remember who tried to spoil the feast.
lines: 조공도, 예산 싸움으로 깎아 낸 삼한의 꿈도.
황제의 북이 요하에 닿거든 — 잔치를 망치려 한 자가 누구였는지 기억하시오.

blocks.html: He walks out before it ends. Outside, the corridor is very long and very cold. Behind him the chamber returns to numbers — as if he had never brought an emperor into the room.
blocks.ko: 그는 회의가 끝나기 전에 나와 버린다. 밖으로 나서니 복도가 몹시 길고 몹시 차다. 등 뒤에서 전각은 다시 숫자로 돌아간다 — 그가 황제를 방에 들여온 적도 없었다는 듯이.

en: Heaven above… help this foolish country…!

blocks.html: In the yard the Eastern banners answer him anyway — a roar that has nothing to do with the Summit’s minutes.
blocks.ko: 마당의 동부 깃발들은 그래도 그를 받아 준다 — 제가회의 회의록과는 상관없는 함성으로.

en: Look at that — see how Pyongyang loves you.
Of course. The people have never once abandoned me.
It is the politicians…!
lines: 당연하지. 백성은 날 버린 적이 없어.

en: His Majesty wants Samhan under one roof.
The Summit wants the roof itemised.
…Get the horses. I would rather sleep in a tent tonight.
lines: 폐하께서는 삼한을 한 지붕 아래 두고 싶어 하시지.
제가회의는 그 지붕을 항목별로 적고 싶어 하고.
…말 준비해라. 오늘 밤은 천막에서 자는 게 낫겠다.

blocks.label: Birth of Namseng
blocks.ko: 남생의 탄생

blocks.html: Yeon’s wife labours in a Goguryeo timber chamber blasted white with daylight — no extra bodies, no portrait-frame crowd. Only the midwife who opens a birth, and the mother. The rest of the world falls out of the light.
blocks.ko: 연씨 부인의 해산은 고구려 목조 방 안, 햇빛이 하얗게 터진 빛 속에서다. 다른 몸 없고, 액자 구경꾼 없다. 숨을 여는 산파와 어머니뿐. 세상의 나머지는 그 빛 밖으로 떨어진다.

en: Samsin…
This child alone — please.
…This time — please.

blocks.html: The portrait does not stay paint. Samsin steps from the frame the way steam steps from a kettle — one midwife of the living world under Little Star — and lays a hand where mortal hands have failed.
blocks.ko: 초상은 그림으로 남지 않는다. 삼신이 주전자에서 김이 오르듯 액자에서 내려온다 — 소별왕 아래 이승의 산파 하나 — 그리고 사람의 손이 닿지 못한 곳에 손을 얹는다.

blocks.caption: The birth goddess. She does not knock.
blocks.ko: 아이를 점지하는 여신. 문을 두드리지 않는다.

en: Do not weep.
I will open the breath.
The name — that is yours to give.

blocks.html: So the first heir arrives under Samsin's hand, the year of the Summit. They call him Namseng. A son is born. Nobody wanted a poem in the name. It's the sound the room makes when the baby breathes.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 삼신의 손 아래, 제가회의가 열린 해에 맏아들이 온다. 남생. 사내가 났다는 뜻이다. 이름에 시를 넣고 싶은 사람은 없었다. 아기가 숨을 쉴 때 방이 내는 소리, 그게 이름이다.

en: Namseng.
…Heavier than it sounds.
This country. You will have to keep it.

blocks.html: His surname was Cheon, 'Spring'; his name, Namseng; his courtesy name, Wondeok. He was a man of Pyongyang. His distant line came out of a spring: it took its blessing from a spirit, and named its clan after the place of its birth. … His great-grandfather Jayu and his grandfather Taejo both served as Mangniji.
blocks.ko: 공의 성은 천이요, 휘는 남생이며, 자는 원덕이니, 요동군 평양성 사람이다. 그 먼 계보를 살피면 본래 샘에서 나왔으니, 신에게 의탁하여 복을 내려받고, 태어난 곳을 따라 겨레의 이름을 지었다. …… 증조 자유와 조부 태조는 모두 막리지를 지냈다.
blocks.hanja: 公姓泉，諱男生，字元德，遼東郡平壤城人也。原夫遠系，本出於泉，旣託神以隤祉，遂因生以命族。……曾祖子遊，祖太祚，並任莫離支。
blocks.source: Epitaph of Yeon Namseng (泉男生墓誌)

blocks.html: Once, Goguryeo did not argue about grain. It had a king with sixty-four fortresses. To meet him, we go back two centuries…!
blocks.ko: 한때 고구려는 곡식을 두고 다투지 않았다. 성 예순넷을 가진 왕이 있었으니까. 그를 만나려면 이백 년을 거슬러 가야 한다…!

images.alt: Napoleon Crossing the Alps as a Neoclassical oil painting: Gwanggaeto on a rearing white horse, red cloak whipping, pointing south under a red sun
images.prompt: A parody of Jacques-Louis David’s NAPOLEON CROSSING THE ALPS, painted exactly like the real canvas: polished Neoclassical oil, smooth glazes, crisp contours, old varnish and fine craquelure, grey storm sky. Same composition and pose: a white horse rearing on a steep rocky slope, mane and tail whipped by wind, the rider calm and upright pointing up and forward, a great red cloak billowing in an arc behind, tiny soldiers far below. The rider is GWANGGAETO THE GREAT (attached portrait: face) in gray steel lamellar armor (attached lamellar ref) with a Goguryeo helmet (attached kingdom ref, ignore its labels), red wing shoulder-flaps #C30000 and a red #e0442e cloak. A red sun behind the storm clouds with a small black three-legged crow crossing it. Korean granite peaks and pines instead of the Alps. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.alt: The Alexander Mosaic in tesserae: Gwanggaeto bareheaded on horseback charging through a forest of spears, the Wa commander twisting in flight
images.prompt: A parody of the ALEXANDER MOSAIC from Pompeii (the Battle of Issus), made exactly like the real Roman floor mosaic: thousands of small stone tesserae, limited palette of ochre, brick red, black, white and grey, patches of missing tiles, a dark broken border. Same composition: on the left the young conqueror charges on horseback, bareheaded, eyes wide, spearing an enemy; on the right the enemy leader, in a chariot, twists back in horror and flings out an arm as his army turns to flee; a forest of long spears slanting across the sky; a bare dead tree. blocks.html: Silla is drowning. An army from across the sea is inside its walls. Then Gwanggaeto sends fifty thousand horsemen south, and the Wa are gone.
blocks.ko: 신라가 무너지고 있다. 바다 건너 온 군대가 도성 안에 있다. 그때 광개토가 기병 오만을 남으로 내려보내고, 왜는 사라진다.

blocks.caption: Goguryeo’s widest king. The stele ran out of room before he ran out of fortresses.
blocks.ko: 고구려에서 가장 넓은 임금. 성이 바닥나기 전에 비석 자리가 먼저 바닥났다.

blocks.html: A red sun. The three-legged crow rides south on his banners. The stele will list sixty-four fortresses. It will not list the nerve it took.
blocks.ko: 붉은 해. 세발까마귀가 그의 깃발에 실려 남으로 간다. 비석은 성 예순넷을 적을 것이다. 거기 든 배짱은 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: Sixty-four fortresses, one reign. The stele at his tomb lists them all.
blocks.ko: 한 치세에 예순네 개의 성. 능비가 그 전부를 새기고 있다.

blocks.caption: Watch the red run south. One reign did that.
blocks.ko: 붉은빛이 남쪽으로 번지는 걸 보라. 한 사람의 치세가 한 일이다.

blocks.html: Silla had asked. That's the part everyone forgets. A Silla king, with foreigners inside his capital, sent north and begged. Fifty thousand horsemen came down and cleared the peninsula. Then they didn't leave for fifty years.
blocks.ko: 신라가 청했다. 다들 잊는 대목이다. 도성 안에 적을 들인 신라 왕이 북에 사람을 보내 빌었다. 기병 오만이 내려와 반도를 쓸어 냈다. 그리고 오십 년 동안 떠나지 않았다.

en: They did save us.
So why are they still here?

blocks.html: Silla’s crown princes go north as hostages. Silla’s court takes Goguryeo titles. Silla’s army takes Goguryeo orders. It lasts two generations. Silla does not forget it.
blocks.ko: 신라의 태자들이 볼모로 북으로 간다. 신라의 조정이 고구려의 관작을 받는다. 신라의 군대가 고구려의 명을 받는다. 두 세대가 그렇게 흐른다. 신라는 그것을 잊지 않는다.

blocks.html: Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Surabol will know exactly what that costs, because it has been done to them before.
blocks.ko: 이백사십 년 뒤 한 신라의 왕자가 외국 황제 앞에 서서 군대를 청한다. 그리고 서라벌의 모든 사람이 그 값을 정확히 안다. 전에 이미 당해 봤기 때문이다.

blocks.hanja: 庶寧其業 國富民殷 五穀豊熟
blocks.ko: 서민이 그 업에 편안하고, 나라는 부유하며 백성은 은성하고, 오곡이 풍성히 익었다.
blocks.html: The common people were at peace in their work; the country was rich and the people abundant; the five grains ripened in plenty.
blocks.source: Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑), south face, ll. 3–4 (414 CE); Best, “The Kwanggaeto Stele,” p. 147

blocks.html: Bupmin is fifteen now. The Hwarang have five rules, and his uncle has one question: which will you break first…?
blocks.ko: 법민이 열다섯이 되었다. 화랑에게는 계율이 다섯, 외숙에게는 질문이 하나 있다. 너는 무엇을 제일 먼저 어길 것 같으냐…?

images.alt: In torchlight Yushin stands over seventeen-year-old Bupmin and lifts the kneeling boy’s chin with the tip of a long wooden practice staff
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 2:1 still composed like a symbolic old-master history painting — the STRONG, DISCIPLINED UNCLE AND THE APPRENTICE NEPHEW. INTIMATE CLOSE-UP, low angle from the dirt: seventeen-year-old Bupmin on his knees, face and shoulders large in the lower-right, sweat and dust on his cheek, head tipped back, eyes burning up at his teacher. Yushin stands over him in the upper-left holding a long plain wooden practice staff at full arm’s length; its blunt tip rests under the boy’s chin. Yushin looks down, stern, almost proud. ONE DEVICE: the long staff diagonal from the standing mentor to the kneeling student’s chin. A torch below-right lights Bupmin’s face hot gold; Yushin falls into cold shadow. Background pure black with ember bokeh. Wood only. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | BUPMIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_bupmin_hwarang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Bupmin in red, running through the night yard
Bupmin grinning, holding a scroll up
Four hwarang spar in the sandy yard, seen from above

blocks.label: Flowering Youth
blocks.ko: 화랑의 꽃

blocks.html: It is the spring Bupmin turns fifteen.
blocks.ko: 법민이 열다섯이 되는 봄이다.

blocks.html: The Hwarang train under the Marshal: horse, bow, verse, and above all gyuku, a horse-ball game a lazier age will call polo.
blocks.ko: 화랑은 장군 밑에서 배운다. 말, 활, 노래, 그리고 무엇보다 격구. 훗날 게으른 시대가 폴로라 부를, 말 위의 공놀이다.

blocks.html: Bupmin (15) is old enough for the headband and too young to invent a country alone. His father is in the Council chamber collecting votes. His uncle keeps the yard.
blocks.ko: 법민 (15)은 머리띠를 맬 만큼은 컸고, 혼자 나라를 발명하기엔 아직 어리다. 아버지는 화백 회의실에서 표를 모으고 있다. 외숙이 연무장을 지킨다.

blocks.html: Bupmin was striking in bearing, quick of mind, and full of strategy.
blocks.ko: 법민은 풍채가 빼어나고, 총명하며 지략이 많았다.
blocks.hanja: 法敏姿表英特，聰明多智略。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — opening portrait of Bupmin

blocks.title: Yard as state · 화랑
blocks.caption: Class 51 still sits together — Bidam, Yushin, Alchun.
blocks.ko: 51기는 아직도 같이 앉는다 — 비담, 유신, 알천.

blocks.html: Yushin does not soften the yard because the boy is royal. He softens nothing. The new boys sleep six to a hall and learn each other's snores before each other's ranks. They trade rumours about the Marshal like relics. He took forty fortresses. He bathes in a haunted lake. He can hear a lie drop a shoulder at fifty paces.
blocks.ko: 유신은 소년이 왕손이라고 연무장을 무르게 두지 않는다. 무엇 하나 무르게 두지 않는다. 새로 온 소년들은 한 방에 여섯씩 자며, 서로의 골품보다 코 고는 소리를 먼저 익힌다. 장군 소문은 성물처럼 오간다. 성 마흔 개를 떨어뜨렸다더라. 귀신 나오는 호수에서 목욕한다더라. 오십 보 밖에서도 거짓말에 어깨 처지는 소리를 듣는다더라.

blocks.html: Girls crowd the fence of the yard the way other towns crowd a market — not for the ball, for the Hwarang. They pretend they came for the verse.
blocks.ko: 소녀들이 연무장 울타리에 모인다. 다른 고을이 장터에 몰리듯 — 공 때문이 아니라, 화랑 때문에. 노래 들으러 왔다고 한다.

blocks.html: Nobody in Surabol would dream of calling gyuku a pastime — it is a ranking system with horses, and a boy’s seat among the Hwarang is half his blood and half his swing. Handicaps are argued the way ministers argue borders, only with less honesty.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 격구를 유희라 부를 사람은 없다 — 그것은 말을 탄 서열이고, 화랑 안에서 소년의 자리는 피가 반, 스윙이 반이다. 핸디캡을 두고 다투는 모양새는 신하들이 국경을 다투는 것과 같은데, 정직함만 그보다 적다.

blocks.html: Then there are the clubs. A premium gyuku club is not a stick. Third-growth cypress from the south ridge of Namsan, seasoned seven years in the shade of Hwangnyong, the grip wrapped in indigo the Queen’s seamstresses will not sell. The head travels in its own box. If you cannot name the forest, you are not asked back.
blocks.ko: 그리고 채가 있다. 프리미엄 격구채는 막대기가 아니다. 남산 남쪽 능선의 삼대목 측백, 황룡사 그늘에서 일곱 해 말린 것, 여왕의 침방이 평민에게는 팔지 않는 쪽빛 비단으로 감은 손잡이. 머리는 제 함에 넣어 다닌다. 어느 숲 나무인지 대면 다음 경기에 안 부른다.

lines: 저 채, 가야 쇠심 박은 거냐?
아니 — 월성 측백이지. 작년 시즌 거.
en: That club — Gaya ironwood core?
No — Wolseong cypress. Last season’s.
…Last season? And he brought it out?

lines: 진골은 지난 시즌 채를 안 든다.
en: A True Bone does not play last season’s shaft.
Is that law?
Worse.
Again.
A king for all who cannot hold a saddle is a poem, not a country.
lines: 안장도 못 잡는 모두를 위한 임금은 시이지, 나라가 아니다.

en: Uncle—
I said that when I was six.
lines: 그건 여섯 살 때 한 말이에요.

en: Then make it true at fifteen.
The Hwarang do not train for your father’s cleverness. They train for the hour the cleverness runs out.
lines: 화랑은 네 아비의 꾀를 위해 닦는 게 아니다. 꾀가 바닥날 시각을 위해 닦는다.

en: We ride the eastern practice roads until the Fortress of Radiance looks small behind us.
Westward, Baekje’s Yellow Mountain pass is where their grain carts complain in dry weeks — learn a landscape before it learns your name.
lines: 명활산성이 작게 보일 때까지 동쪽 연무길을 달린다.
서쪽으로, 백제 황산 고개는 마른 주에 곡식 수레가 투덜대는 곳이다 — 지형이 네 이름을 배우기 전에 네가 지형을 배워라.

blocks.html: The Hwarang follow a set of Five Principles.
blocks.ko: 화랑은 세속오계를 따른다.

blocks.name: The Five Secular Precepts
blocks.ko: 세속오계
blocks.note: A monk wrote rules for boys who would never be monks. They mostly kept them.
blocks.noteKo: 스님이, 끝내 스님이 되지 않을 소년들을 위해 쓴 계율. 소년들은 대체로 지켰다.

lines: 사군이충 (事君以忠): 충성으로 임금을 섬긴다.
사친이효 (事親以孝): 효도로써 부모를 섬긴다.
교우이신 (交友以信): 믿음으로써 벗을 사귄다.
임전무퇴 (臨戰無退): 전쟁에 나가 물러서지 않는다.
살생유택 (殺生有擇): 살아있는 것을 죽일 때에는 가림이 있어야 한다

blocks.name: Serve the king with loyalty
blocks.ko: 사군이충
blocks.note: First on the list, so nobody can say they missed it.
blocks.noteKo: 맨 앞에 두었다. 못 들었다는 소리는 못 하게.

blocks.name: Serve your parents with devotion
blocks.ko: 사친이효
blocks.note: Easy, until the king and your father want different things.
blocks.noteKo: 쉽다. 임금과 아버지가 서로 다른 걸 원하기 전까지는.

blocks.name: Keep faith with your friends
blocks.ko: 교우이신
blocks.note: The one boys swear to first and keep longest.
blocks.noteKo: 소년들이 제일 먼저 맹세하고, 제일 오래 지키는 것.

blocks.name: Never retreat in battle
blocks.ko: 임전무퇴
blocks.note: The one they elbow each other at. For now.
blocks.noteKo: 소년들이 서로 팔꿈치로 찌르는 대목. 아직은.

blocks.name: Be choosy about killing
blocks.ko: 살생유택
blocks.note: The quiet one. Boys skip it. Old soldiers don’t.
blocks.noteKo: 조용한 계율. 소년들은 건너뛰고, 늙은 병사들은 그러지 않는다.

blocks.html: At dusk he gathers the flower youth under the eaves and speaks the Five Principles the way other houses recite ancestors — not as decoration, but as the only map that still works when bone rank fails. The boys mouth the words along with him, elbowing each other at no retreat, going quiet at no needless killing, each privately certain the Marshal is looking straight at him. He is looking at all of them.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘 그는 처마 아래 꽃다운 소년들을 모으고 세속오계를 다른 집이 조상을 외듯 말한다 — 장식이 아니라, 골품이 실패할 때에도 남는 유일한 지도로. 소년들은 그를 따라 입을 움직인다. 임전무퇴에서는 서로 팔꿈치를 찌르고, 살생유택에서는 조용해지고, 저마다 장군이 바로 자기를 보고 있다고 남몰래 확신한다. 장군은 그들 모두를 보고 있다.

en: Loyalty to the sovereign.
Filial duty to parents.
Trust among friends.
No retreat in battle.
No needless killing.
Bupmin — which one will you break first?
lines: 법민아 — 너는 무엇을 제일 먼저 어길 것 같으냐.

en: …Retreat.
When Gotaso rides too fast I always pull up first. Every time.
If I am to be a king for all, I cannot be the boy who only follows.
lines: 고타소가 말을 너무 빨리 몰면 제가 늘 먼저 고삐를 당겨요. 매번요.
모두를 위한 임금이 되려면, 따라가기만 하는 아이여서는 안 됩니다.

blocks.html: Gwisan shouted, "I once heard it from my teacher: 'A man in the army does not retreat.' How could I dare run?"
blocks.ko: 귀산이 큰 소리로 말하였다. "내 일찍이 스승에게서 '선비는 군에 있을 때 물러섬이 없어야 한다'고 들었다. 어찌 감히 달아나겠는가."
blocks.hanja: 貴山大言曰：「吾嘗聞之師曰：『士當軍無退』，豈敢奔北乎。」
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 45, Biographies — Gwisan (602)

en: Good.
Then see the country the way a Hwarang sees a field — who holds, who falters, who dies for a vow they meant.
I am marshal of this order. You will learn loyalty here before you learn how to sit on a throne.
lines: 그럼 화랑이 벌판을 보듯 나라를 봐라 — 누가 버티고, 누가 흔들리고, 누가 뜻한 맹세를 위해 죽는지.
나는 이 무리의 원수다. 왕좌에 앉는 법을 배우기 전에, 여기서 충성을 배울 것이다.

blocks.html: The yard has two names it still whispers. Tonight the Marshal says them out loud…!
blocks.ko: 연무장이 아직도 목소리를 낮추는 이름이 둘 있다. 오늘 밤, 장군이 그 이름을 소리 내어 말한다…!

images.alt: Tiny Sadaham on a vast empty Gaya road — ice-blue accent, monumental emptiness
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Sadaham, God of the Hwarang, fifteen, taking Great Gaya. ONE geometric device: a long empty ROAD as a pale wedge receding to a hard horizon; tiny silky Hwarang figure in the lower third, standing, not kneeling. Face matches the attached Sadaham portrait only as a tiny likeness. Ice-blue #6fa8ff as the single accent on silk. REAL empty country road, natural dusk sky. Monumental emptiness. No army catalog. No crescent halo. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.at: asked to ride against Great Gaya
images.alt: Fifteen-year-old Sadaham kneels on the stone floor of Jinheung’s hall at night, head up, asking to ride
images.prompt: Worm’s-eye from the stone floor of King Jinheung’s timber hall at night, an oil lamp set on the floor in the sharp foreground. Sadaham, fifteen, kneels mid-bow but with his head already up, chin out, refusing to look down, in his Hwarang coat; the lamp rakes up across his jaw and the ice-blue of his collar. Behind and above him, out of focus on the dais, King Jinheung leans forward on one fist, half amused, half doubtful, red robe catching the same lamp. Pillars recede at an angle; Sadaham’s shadow climbs the floor toward the dais. CANON — SADAHAM — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sadaham.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Hwarang taken Gaya at fifteen; ice-blue #6fa8ff cloth on campaign; dies young of grief. #6fa8ff as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KING JINHEUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_jinheung.png (face only; invent a new pose). #2f6fd4 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. blocks.label: The First Class
blocks.ko: 제일기

blocks.html: Every yard has its ghosts. This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.
blocks.ko: 연무장마다 귀신이 있다. 이곳엔 둘이다. 점호에 빠진 적이 한 번도 없다.

blocks.html: The lamps go up under the eaves. Nobody sends the boys to bed. They decide this is an honour, and they are right, though not for the reason they think.
blocks.ko: 처마 아래 등이 걸린다. 아무도 소년들을 재우러 보내지 않는다. 소년들은 이를 영광으로 여긴다. 맞는 말이다. 다만 그들이 생각하는 이유는 아니다.

blocks.html: The Marshal does not let trust among friends stay a pretty line. He tells the new boys of the first class — the two names the yard still lowers its voice for.
blocks.ko: 장군은 교우이신을 예쁜 문장으로 두지 않는다. 새로 온 소년들에게 제일기를 말한다 — 연무장이 아직도 목소리를 낮추는 두 이름.

en: Before your fathers were born, the first class had two.
Sadaham. Mugwan. They swore to die together. Then, the year Great Gaya fell, one of them kept the swear without asking the other.
lines: 너희 아비가 태어나기 전에, 제일기에 둘이 있었다.
사다함. 무관랑. 함께 죽기로 맹세했다. 그러고 대가야가 떨어진 해, 한 쪽이 상대에게 묻지 않고 맹세를 지켰다.

en: Which one, Uncle?
Which one kept it?
Sit down and you’ll find out.
Is this the one about the haunted lake?
blocks.speaker: A new boy

en: No. That one’s about me.

blocks.html: Back then the yard was new, and so was the idea. The king wanted boys who would ride ahead of the army and not ask why. The first year, he got a lot of them. Two of them got each other.
blocks.ko: 그때는 연무장도 새것이었고, 그 생각도 새것이었다. 왕은 군대보다 앞서 달리면서 이유를 묻지 않을 소년들을 원했다. 첫해에 그런 소년은 많이 왔다. 그중 둘은 서로를 얻었다.

blocks.html: Sadaham is thirteen and talks like a dare. Mugwan is thirteen too, and says less than his horse. The hall has one gap, so they share it. They argue for a month about who snores.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 열셋이고, 말마다 내기를 건다. 무관랑도 열셋인데, 자기가 타는 말보다도 말수가 적다. 방에 빈자리가 하나뿐이라 둘은 한 방에 든다. 누가 코를 고는지 한 달을 다툰다.

blocks.caption: The first class’s brightest boy. He makes promises the way other boys throw stones.
blocks.ko: 제일기에서 가장 빛나던 소년. 다른 아이들이 돌을 던지듯 약속을 던진다.

en: You snore.
Don’t argue. The whole hall heard you.
That was you.
…Then prove it. Stay up and listen.

blocks.html: Mugwan stays up. It is the first of a great many nights he will stay up for Sadaham, and the only one either of them will find funny.
blocks.ko: 무관랑은 안 자고 듣는다. 앞으로 사다함 때문에 지새울 수많은 밤 가운데 첫날이고, 둘 다 웃을 수 있는 건 그날 밤뿐이다.

blocks.html: Their first spring, the yard sends them down to the river for stones. Mugwan turns one over and goes very still. Somebody has cut writing into it.
blocks.ko: 첫봄, 연무장은 둘을 냇가로 보내 돌을 날라 오게 한다. 무관랑이 돌 하나를 뒤집더니 꼼짝도 않는다. 누군가 거기에 글을 새겨 두었다.

en: Come here.
Read this.
You read it. You’re the one who studies.

blocks.hanja: 壬申年六月十六日二人幷誓記天前誓今自三年以後忠道執持過失无誓若此事失天大罪淂誓若國不安大舐世可容行誓之又別先辛未年七月卄二日大誓詩尙書礼傳倫淂誓三年
blocks.html: Year imsin, sixth month, sixteenth day. The two of us swear together and write it down. We swear before Heaven: from today, for three years, we will hold fast to the way of loyalty and commit no fault. If we break this, we swear it is a great sin against Heaven. If the country is not at peace and the world falls into great disorder*, we swear we will go and do it. And apart from this: before, on the twenty-second day of the seventh month of the year sinmi, we swore a great oath, to master in turn the Odes, the Documents, the Rites and the Tradition† within three years.
blocks.ko: 임신년 6월 16일, 두 사람이 함께 맹세하여 적는다. 하늘 앞에 맹세한다. 지금부터 3년 동안 충도를 굳게 지니고 허물이 없기를 맹세한다. 이 일을 어기면 하늘에 큰 죄를 짓는 것이라 맹세한다. 만약 나라가 편안하지 않고 세상이 크게 어지러워지면*, 나아가 행할 것을 맹세한다. 또 따로, 앞서 신미년 7월 22일에 크게 맹세하였으니, 시경·상서·예기·전†을 차례로 3년 안에 익히기로 맹세하였다.
blocks.source: Imsin Oath Stone (壬申誓記石), Silla, year imsin (552 or 612); found 1934 at Seokjang-dong, Gyeongju; Gyeongju National Museum, Treasure No. 1411

back.html: Face down in the river mud. That is how two boys found it, and how they put it back.
back.ko: 냇가 진흙에 엎어진 채. 두 소년이 찾았을 때도, 도로 놓았을 때도.

notes.html: The stone’s character here is worn. The database prints 舐; nearly every editor reads it as 亂, “disorder”.
notes.ko: 이 자리의 글자는 닳아 있다. 판독문은 舐로 적지만, 거의 모든 연구자가 亂(어지러울 란)으로 읽는다.

notes.html: The Tradition (傳) is usually taken as the Zuo commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
notes.ko: 전(傳)은 보통 『춘추좌씨전』으로 본다.

blocks.html: No names. Two boys from before the yard had a name promised Heaven three years of books, and a war if the country wanted one. What became of them, the stone doesn’t say. Stones rarely do.
blocks.ko: 이름은 없다. 연무장에 이름이 붙기도 전의 두 소년이, 책으로 3년, 나라가 원하면 전쟁을 하늘에 약속했다. 그 둘이 어떻게 됐는지 돌은 말하지 않는다. 돌은 원래 말이 없다.

en: Three years?
That’s all they had in them? Give me your knife.
That’s not ours. Put it back.
lines: 그거 우리 거 아니야. 도로 놔.

en: Not that one. We get our own.
lines: 그거 말고. 우리 건 따로 만들 거야.

blocks.html: He finds a smaller stone, flat and grey, and scratches at it until the light goes. His characters are terrible. He leaves out the books entirely. What’s left fits in a closed hand.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 더 작은 돌을 찾는다. 납작하고 잿빛이다. 해가 질 때까지 긁어 댄다. 글씨는 엉망이다. 책 얘기는 아예 뺀다. 남은 것은 주먹 하나에 다 들어간다.

en: Read it.
…“Two of us. One dies, the other follows.”
That’s it?
What else is there?

blocks.html: Mugwan takes the knife. Under the bad characters he cuts one more, small and neat: friend. Then he puts the old stone back exactly where they found it, face down, as if they had never been there.
blocks.ko: 무관랑이 칼을 받아 든다. 엉망인 글씨 아래에 한 글자를 작고 반듯하게 더 새긴다. 벗. 그러고는 옛 돌을 찾았던 자리에 그대로, 엎어서 도로 놓는다. 둘이 거기 온 적도 없다는 듯이.

blocks.html: A museum in Gyeongju keeps the first stone now. Nobody has ever found the second. Good.
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 돌은 지금 경주의 박물관에 있다. 두 번째 돌은 아무도 찾지 못했다. 다행이다.

en: So who snored?
blocks.speaker: A new boy

en: Both. That is not the story.

blocks.html: Two summers on, Great Gaya stops paying. The king calls the war in his hall, and the hall fills up with men old enough to have opinions.
blocks.ko: 두 해 뒤 여름, 대가야가 공물을 끊는다. 왕은 전당에서 전쟁을 정하고, 전당은 할 말이 있을 만한 나이의 사내들로 가득 찬다.

blocks.html: A hill kingdom that has just stopped saying yes.
blocks.ko: 막 “예”라고 하기를 그만둔 산골 왕국.

blocks.html: Sadaham was fifteen when he asked to ride against Great Gaya. He asked on his knees, in front of everyone. It is the only way a boy can ask a king for anything and not be sent outside.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 열다섯에 대가야를 치겠다고 청했다. 무릎을 꿇고, 모두가 보는 앞에서. 소년이 왕에게 무언가를 청하면서 쫓겨나지 않는 방법은 그것뿐이다.

en: Go home. Grow a beard.
War is not a yard. Nobody hands the ball back.
lines: 전쟁은 연무장이 아니다. 공을 돌려주는 놈이 없어.

en: Then I’ll ask again tomorrow.

blocks.html: He does. And the day after. The old general leading the campaign once took an island by frightening it with wooden lions. He tells the king it will be quicker to bring the boy than to keep hearing him.
blocks.ko: 청한다. 그다음 날도. 원정을 맡은 늙은 장군은 예전에 나무 사자로 겁을 줘서 섬 하나를 통째로 받아 낸 사람이다. 그가 왕에게 아뢴다. 저 아이를 데려가는 편이 저 아이 말을 계속 듣는 것보다 빠르겠다고.

en: Fine. Take him.
If he dies, it was his idea. Write that down.
lines: 죽으면 제 생각이었던 거다. 적어 둬라.

en: You’re going.
We’re going.
I told them you’re my second. Don’t make me a liar.
lines: 네가 내 부장이라고 했어. 나 거짓말쟁이 만들지 마.

en: You didn’t ask me.
I’m asking now.
…Well?
…I’ll get the horses.
And the battle? Uncle, what happened at the gate?
lines: 그래서 싸움은요? 외숙부, 성문에서 어떻게 됐어요?

en: Any old man in the market will give you the gate. He’ll get it wrong, but he’ll give it to you.
I am telling you about the rice.
lines: 시장 노인 아무나 붙잡아라. 성문 얘기는 해 줄 거다. 틀리게 하겠지만, 해는 줄 거다.

blocks.html: Ninth month. Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish it, with Sadaham as his second. Sadaham rode ahead with five thousand horse, went in through the Jeondan Gate and planted a white banner. The people in the city were terrified and did not know what to do. When Isabu brought up his troops, they surrendered all at once.
blocks.ko: 9월, 가야가 배반하니 왕이 이사부에게 명하여 치게 하고, 사다함을 부장으로 삼았다. 사다함이 기병 5천을 거느리고 앞서 달려 전단문으로 들어가 흰 깃발을 세우니, 성안 사람들이 두려워 어찌할 바를 몰랐다. 이사부가 군사를 이끌고 다다르자 한꺼번에 모두 항복하였다.
blocks.hanja: 九月，加耶叛，王命異斯夫討之，斯多含副之。斯多含領五千騎先馳，入栴檀門，立白旗，城中恐懼，不知所爲。異斯夫引兵臨之，一時盡降。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinheung, yr. 23 (562)

blocks.html: Year twenty-three, spring, first month. Silla struck down and destroyed the Mimana office, Yamato's name for Gaya.
blocks.ko: 23년 봄 정월, 신라가 임나관가를 쳐서 멸하였다.
blocks.hanja: 廿三年春正月。新羅打滅任那官家。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 19, Emperor Kinmei, yr. 23 (562)

blocks.html: Afterward the king pays him the way kings pay: in people. Three hundred Gaya captives, roped in a line, his to keep. Sadaham walks down the line once. Then he starts cutting rope.
blocks.ko: 싸움이 끝나자 왕은 왕들이 늘 하는 방식으로 값을 치른다. 사람으로. 줄줄이 묶인 가야 포로 삼백, 그의 몫이다. 사다함은 줄을 따라 한 번 걸어 내려간다. 그러고는 밧줄을 끊기 시작한다.

en: The court will say you’re showing off.
lines: 조정에선 네가 잘난 척한다고 할 거다.

en: Then the court can have them back.
Help me with this knot.

blocks.html: The land they give him instead is a strip of stones by the Alcheon that nobody wanted. The chronicle calls this virtue. Mugwan calls it typical, and holds the knot.
blocks.ko: 대신 받은 땅은 알천 가의, 아무도 원하지 않던 돌밭이다. 기록은 이를 덕이라 한다. 무관랑은 늘 그렇다고 하고, 매듭을 잡아 준다.

en: My father would have found a use for three hundred people.
lines: 아버지셨으면 삼백 명을 어디 쓸 데를 찾으셨을 거예요.

en: Your father would have found a use for three hundred and one.
lines: 네 아비라면 삼백한 명 쓸 데를 찾았을 거다.

blocks.html: That winter Mugwan catches a cough he cannot put down. Sadaham sits by the mat and counts his breathing, the way they used to count snores.
blocks.ko: 그 겨울, 무관랑은 내려놓을 수 없는 기침을 얻는다. 사다함은 자리 옆에 앉아 숨소리를 센다. 예전에 코 고는 소리를 세던 것처럼.

blocks.html: The little grey stone sits on the sill. Neither of them looks at it. Both of them know exactly where it is.
blocks.ko: 작은 잿빛 돌이 창턱에 놓여 있다. 둘 다 그쪽을 보지 않는다. 둘 다 그게 어디 있는지 정확히 안다.

en: Go eat. You smell like a sickroom.
lines: 가서 밥 먹어. 너한테 병자 냄새 나.

en: You remember what we swore.
We were thirteen. We also swore to marry the same girl.
If you die first, I will not eat.
So don’t.
lines: 네가 먼저 죽으면 나는 안 먹는다.

en: If I die first— you already know.
lines: 내가 먼저 죽으면 — 너는 이미 알지.

en: Then neither of us is allowed to be late.
lines: 그럼 우리 둘 다 늦으면 안 된다.

blocks.html: Mugwan pushes the stone across the mat with two fingers. It is the last thing he does on purpose.
blocks.ko: 무관랑이 두 손가락으로 돌을 자리 너머로 밀어 준다. 그가 마음먹고 한 마지막 일이다.

blocks.html: Mugwan died of illness not long after the campaign. He did it quietly, the way he did everything, before dawn, so as not to wake anyone.
blocks.ko: 무관랑은 전역이 끝난 지 얼마 되지 않아 병으로 죽었다. 무엇이든 그렇게 했듯 조용히, 새벽이 오기 전에, 아무도 깨우지 않으려는 듯이.

blocks.html: Sadaham did not take food for seven days. The cooks left bowls by his door. The order sent its oldest men to argue with him. He thanked them, and did not eat.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 이레 동안 음식을 들지 않았다. 부엌에선 문 앞에 그릇을 두었다. 화랑은 가장 나이 든 이들을 보내 그를 설득했다. 그는 고맙다고 하고, 먹지 않았다.

blocks.html: He keeps the stone in his fist. At night he holds it up to the lamp, as if the bad characters might have changed.
blocks.ko: 그는 돌을 주먹에 쥐고 지낸다. 밤이면 등잔에 비춰 본다. 엉망인 글씨가 바뀌기라도 했을 것처럼.

en: …It’s quiet in here. Nobody snoring.

blocks.html: On the seventh night the bowl by the door is still full. He lies down on Mugwan’s side of the mat.
blocks.ko: 이레째 밤에도 문 앞의 그릇은 그대로다. 그는 자리의 무관랑 쪽에 눕는다.

en: …Wait up.
I’m not late.

blocks.html: He was seventeen. The order buried two headbands beside him, and one small stone with terrible handwriting. It kept the story, because a Hwarang who outlives his vow is only a boy with a nice coat.
blocks.ko: 열일곱이었다. 화랑은 그 곁에 머리띠 둘과, 글씨가 엉망인 작은 돌 하나를 묻었다. 그리고 이야기를 남겼다. 맹세보다 오래 사는 화랑은, 옷만 좋은 소년에 불과하므로.

blocks.html: The lamp under the eaves has burned down a finger’s width. Nobody has moved. One boy is pretending he has something in his eye, and the others are kind enough to look at the lamp.
blocks.ko: 처마 아래 등잔 기름이 손가락 한 마디만큼 줄었다. 아무도 움직이지 않았다. 한 소년은 눈에 뭐가 들어간 척하고, 나머지는 친절하게도 등잔만 본다.

en: That is friends. Not a song.
If your vow is lighter than a meal, do not wear the headband.
lines: 맹세가 밥보다 가벼우면 머리띠를 매지 마라.

en: You will still say first class when your hair is grey. Our class. His class.
The Harmony Council is the yard with better chairs — almost every sleeve there once slept six to a hall.
lines: 머리가 희어도 제일기라 말할 것이다. 우리 기. 그 기.
화백은 의자만 나은 연무장이다 — 그 소매의 거의가 한 방에 여섯으로 잤다.

en: Uncle.
Who would you stop eating for?

blocks.html: Yushin looks at the boy for a long moment. You can probably name her. He doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 유신은 한참 동안 소년을 본다. 당신은 아마 그 이름을 댈 수 있을 것이다. 그는 대지 않는다.

en: …Go to bed. Gyuku at dawn.

blocks.html: When his sister rides too fast, Bupmin always pulls up first. Gotaso never pulls up. Not for horses. Not for anyone…!
blocks.ko: 누나가 너무 빨리 달리면 법민은 늘 먼저 고삐를 당긴다. 고타소는 당기지 않는다. 말 앞에서도, 누구 앞에서도…!

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 9:16 poster. Kim Pumsuk, Hwarang of Class 74, guardian of Daeya. ONE geometric device: an ice-blue HEADBAND as a thin HORIZONTAL BAR of #7EB8F0 across the upper third of the frame — a rank-strip, not a crescent halo. Face below it in shadow, ready stance. Face matches the attached portrait: blue headband with a white crescent mark kept as a tiny mark on the bar, not a halo around the head. Thin ice-blue rim-light on one shoulder. Striking silky Hwarang court-military. Eighty percent black void. Form defined by the bar and rim. No army. No palace clutter. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.alt: The green-jacket ceremony, painted: Alchun holding open a green silk coat while Pumsuk shrugs into it, polo stick in hand
images.prompt: A painted parody of the MASTERS GREEN-JACKET CEREMONY photo, as a painterly anime-adjacent illustration with loose brushwork: bright afternoon, blurred painted crowd and pines behind. Same staging: last year’s champion stands behind the winner holding open a green jacket while the winner slips one arm into the sleeve, both grinning stiffly at unseen cameras. At the edge of a Silla gyuku (polo) field: ALCHUN (attached portrait: face and garments) holds open a bright GREEN silk Silla coat; PUMSUK (attached portrait: face, sky-blue #7EB8F0 silk) shrugs into it, flushed and cocky, a polo stick in his other hand with presentation silk still wrapped on its head. Painted horses and nobles in hanbok behind. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.alt: Gotaso and Pumsuk share a lantern above the lantern-lit water
Gotaso and Pumsuk leap off the wall together
Pumsuk talking, Gotaso listening, in the lamplit yard
Pumsuk kneels before Gotaso on the bench
