images.at: He brings the weight on his saddle back

images.alt: Nangbi: the white horse in the night forest

blocks.html: Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
blocks.ko: 김유신. 삼한 어디서든 두려움을 부르는 이름. 아마 이래서일 것이다.

blocks.html: Autumn. Silla’s army is breaking against a Goguryeo wall. The men who should be charging are sitting in the trenches. Yushin is thirty-four, a banner captain. His white horse doesn’t even have a name.
blocks.ko: 가을. 신라군이 고구려의 성벽 앞에서 부서지고 있다. 돌격해야 할 병사들이 참호에 주저앉아 있다. 유신은 서른넷, 깃발 하나를 맡은 대장이다. 그의 흰 말에는 아직 이름도 없다.

blocks.html: A Goguryeo wall that is about to make somebody famous.
blocks.ko: 곧 누군가를 유명하게 만들 고구려의 성벽.

blocks.html: He rides back to his father’s command post, gets down, and takes off his helmet, which is how a son asks permission in front of an army.
blocks.ko: 그는 아버지의 지휘소로 말을 몰아 돌아와 내리고, 투구를 벗는다. 군대 앞에서 아들이 허락을 구하는 방식이다.

lines: 옷깃을 쥐고 떨쳐야 갖옷이 바로 서고, 벼리를 들어야 그물이 펴진다고 했습니다.
en: Father. We’re losing.
They say you shake a coat by the collar to make it hang straight, and lift the head-rope to open a net.
…Let me be the collar.
…Put your helmet on.
Then go.

blocks.html: The white horse takes the trench in one jump that the men in it will describe for the rest of their lives, usually with their hands. In, out. In again. The third time Yushin comes back there is something heavy hanging from his saddle, and the men in the trench are already climbing out.
blocks.ko: 흰 말은 단번에 참호를 뛰어넘는다. 그 안에 있던 병사들이 평생, 대개는 손짓까지 해 가며 이야기하게 될 도약이다. 들어갔다, 나왔다. 다시 들어간다. 세 번째로 유신이 돌아올 때 안장에는 묵직한 것이 매달려 있고, 참호의 병사들은 벌써 기어 나오고 있다.

blocks.html: Then he mounted, drew his sword and rode straight at the enemy line. Three times he went in and three times he came out, and each time he went in he either cut down a commander or tore down a banner.
blocks.ko: 이에 말을 타고 칼을 빼 들고는 적진으로 향하여 곧바로 나아가 세 번 들어가고 세 번 나옴에, 매번 들어갈 때마다 장수의 목을 베고 혹은 깃발을 뽑았다.
blocks.hanja: 乃跨馬拔劒 向敵陣直前 三入三出 每入或斬將或搴旗
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinpyeong, year 51 (629)

blocks.html: He brings the weight on his saddle back to the command post and sets it down in the mud in front of his father, wrapped in a torn banner, because he does not know what else a son is supposed to do with a general’s head. The staff officers wait for the speech. Seohyeon looks at the bundle, then at the boy, for long enough that someone coughs.
blocks.ko: 그는 안장에 매달린 것을 지휘소로 가져와 아버지 앞 진흙 위에 내려놓는다. 찢긴 깃발에 싸여 있다. 장군의 머리를 아들이 어떻게 해야 하는지, 그는 모른다. 참모들이 연설을 기다린다. 서현은 보따리를 보고, 아들을 본다. 누군가 헛기침을 할 만큼 오래.

en: …Your helmet’s crooked.

blocks.html: He reaches up and straightens it himself, both hands, the way you fix a boy’s collar before a feast, and then turns away and shouts for his officers before anyone can see his face. It is the most Kim Seohyeon has ever said to his son about anything, and Yushin will carry it longer than the helmet.
blocks.ko: 그는 손을 뻗어 직접 바로잡는다. 두 손으로, 잔치 전에 아이 옷깃을 매만지듯. 그리고 누가 얼굴을 보기 전에 돌아서서 장교들을 부른다. 김서현이 아들에게 무엇에 대해서든 해 준 말 중 가장 긴 말이다. 유신은 그것을 투구보다 오래 지니고 다닌다.

blocks.html: That night he asks the groom what the white horse is called. The groom says it has no name; it came from the royal stable as a spare. Yushin looks at it for a long time, at the mud on its chest and the way it still will not quite stand still.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 마부에게 흰 말의 이름을 묻는다. 이름은 없다고, 왕실 마구간에서 여벌로 온 말이라고 마부가 답한다. 유신은 오래도록 말을 바라본다. 가슴팍의 진흙을, 아직도 가만히 서 있지 못하는 모양을.

en: Hangyul.
…It means steady. It came back steady. All three times.

blocks.html: The few who get out of Nangbi walk north for nine days with the story, and it grows a little at every well. By Pyongyang the white horse has cleared the trench at a gallop with a general’s head in one hand and a banner in the other, and the man on it has a name the Goguryeo clerks must write down for the first time.
blocks.ko: 낭비성을 빠져나간 몇 안 되는 자들이 이야기를 들고 아흐레를 북으로 걷는다. 이야기는 우물을 지날 때마다 조금씩 자란다. 평양에 닿을 무렵 흰 말은 한 손에 장군의 머리, 한 손에 깃발을 들고 전속력으로 참호를 넘었고, 그 위의 사내에게는 고구려 서기들이 처음으로 받아 적어야 하는 이름이 생겨 있다.

blocks.html: In Pyongyang the report is read to the king twice, the second time because he asks for it. At the back of the hall the Yeon heir, twenty-four, stands with his arms folded, the way he stands everywhere.
blocks.ko: 평양에서 보고는 왕 앞에서 두 번 읽힌다. 두 번째는 왕이 다시 읽으라 해서다. 전각 뒤편에서 연씨 가문의 후계자, 스물넷이 팔짱을 끼고 서 있다. 그는 어디서나 그렇게 선다.

en: Kim Yushin… a banner captain.
We have never heard the name.

lines: 놈 하나가 도랑 하나 넘었는데 우리 오천이 드러누웠소. 그게 당주요? 칼이지.
en: You’ll hear it again.
One man jumps one ditch and five thousand of ours lie down. That’s a captain? That’s a sword.
Silla’s sword.

blocks.label: The High Commander’s House
blocks.ko: 막리지의 집

blocks.html: Gesomun’s family lives in the big house below the palace hill. His father, Yeon Taejo, has run the Summit for ten years. Long enough to outlive most of the men who voted for him. None of the ones who voted against. Most nights he comes home in a silence the servants have learned to walk around.
blocks.ko: 개소문의 집안은 왕궁 언덕 아래 큰 집에 산다. 아버지 연태조는 십 년째 회의의 윗자리를 지키고 있다. 그를 밀어준 사람들이 대부분 먼저 죽을 만큼 긴 세월이다. 반대한 사람들은 하나도 안 죽었다. 거의 매일 밤 그는 말없이 돌아오고, 하인들은 그 침묵을 비켜 다니는 법을 익혔다.

blocks.html: Tonight he does not take off his boots. He sits at the low table with a copy of the Nangbi report, the one the king asked to hear twice, and reads it a third time with his finger under the lines.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 그는 신도 벗지 않는다. 낮은 상 앞에 앉아, 왕이 두 번 읽으라 한 낭비성 보고의 사본을 펼쳐 놓고, 손가락으로 줄을 짚어 가며 세 번째로 읽는다.

en: Father. You’re still on that?
It’s one fortress. We take it back by spring.

lines: …오천 수급이다. 한 번 뛰어들어서. 그런 놈을 몇이나 봤느냐?
en: Sit.
…Five thousand heads. Off one charge. How many men have you seen do that?
One.
You. At the Colossal River.

lines: 나한텐 삼만 군사가 있었고 강도 우리 편이었다.
이놈은 도랑 하나에 말 한 필이다.
en: I had thirty thousand men and a river on my side.
He had a ditch and a horse.

blocks.html: Gesomun has seen his father angry, drunk and bleeding, and once, when he was seven, riding home from the Colossal River with a Sui banner rolled under his arm like a bolt of cloth. He has never seen him frightened of a piece of paper. He finds he does not know where to put his hands.
blocks.ko: 개소문은 아버지가 화내는 것도, 취한 것도, 피 흘리는 것도 보았다. 일곱 살 때는 수나라 깃발을 비단 한 필처럼 옆구리에 말아 끼고 살수에서 돌아오는 것도 보았다. 종이 한 장을 두려워하는 아버지는 처음 본다. 손을 어디 둬야 할지 모르겠다.

lines: 서른넷에 아직 당주다. 신라 놈들이 가야 손자를 더 빨리 올려 줄 리가 없지.
썩히고 있는 거다. 언제까지나 썩히진 않을 거고.
en: Thirty-four, and still a banner captain. Silla won’t let a Gaya grandson climb any faster.
They’re wasting him. They won’t waste him forever.

lines: 그럼 그 전에 제가 죽이면 됩니다.
en: Then I’ll kill him before they stop.

lines: 잘 들어라. 그놈이 고른 땅에선 절대 싸우지 마라. 화났을 때도 마라. 그리고 이 도성이 그놈을 고작 당주라고 하거든, 믿지 마라.
en: You’ll try.
Listen to me. Never on a field he picked. Never when you’re angry. And when this city tells you he’s only a captain, don’t believe it.
His Majesty already did.

lines: 전하는 두 번 들으시고 회의에 물으셨지.
회의가 뭘 했는지 아느냐? 성 다시 쌓는 값을 누가 낼지 반나절을 싸웠다. 아무도 그놈 이름을 입에 안 올렸어. 한 번도.
십 년을 그 방에 앉아 있었다. 저것들은 곳간 하나씩 이 나라를 잃어버릴 거다. 그러고는 신중했다고 하겠지.
en: His Majesty heard it twice and asked the Summit what to do.
Do you know what the Summit did? Argued half a day over who pays to rebuild the fort. Nobody said his name. Not once.
Ten years I’ve sat in that room. They’ll lose this country one granary at a time and call it caution.

blocks.html: Each of them learns his country at home. Euija learns the great clans at his father’s table. Chunchu learns the council from the day it walked his grandfather off the throne. And Gesomun learns this city here, from an old man reading one report three times by lamplight. Nobody else in the city would read it once.
blocks.ko: 셋 다 나라를 집에서 배운다. 의자는 아버지의 밥상머리에서 큰 가문들을 배운다. 춘추는 회의가 할아버지를 왕좌에서 걸어 내려보낸 그날에서 회의를 배운다. 그리고 개소문은 여기서 이 도시를 배운다. 등불 아래 같은 보고서를 세 번 읽는 늙은이에게서. 이 도시의 누구도 한 번 읽지 않을 보고서를.

en: …Kim Yushin.

blocks.html: That’s where the name comes from. Not from his own capital, which likes its titles stamped and filed. From the people he beat. Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning. On the border, mothers use it to get children indoors before dark. Thirteen years later, Gesomun will hear that sword is riding for the prince in his prison. He’ll remember a hall, a report read twice, and his father reading it a third time.
blocks.ko: 그 이름은 거기서 나왔다. 칭호에 도장 찍어 철해 두기 좋아하는 제 나라 도읍에서가 아니다. 그에게 진 사람들에게서다. 고구려가 먼저 그를 신라의 검이라 부른다. 경고의 뜻으로. 국경의 어머니들은 해 지기 전 아이들을 불러들일 때 그 이름을 쓴다. 십삼 년 뒤, 개소문은 그 검이 자기 감옥의 왕자를 구하러 온다는 소식을 듣는다. 그는 한 전각을, 두 번 읽힌 보고서를, 그리고 그것을 세 번째로 읽던 아버지를 떠올릴 것이다.

blocks.html: Thirteen years on, the banner captain has a queen, a title, and a long list of Baekje fortresses. He's working through it…!
blocks.ko: 십삼 년 뒤, 그 깃발 대장에게는 여왕과 칭호, 그리고 백제 성들의 긴 목록이 있다. 그는 그 목록을 하나씩 지워 나가는 중이다…!

BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. blocks.html: In the meantime Queen Sunduk sends her general, Kim Yushin, against Baekje.
blocks.ko: 그사이 선덕여왕은 장군 김유신을 백제로 보낸다.
blocks.art: Close on Yushin’s hand: the Gaya fish openwork in his ring pommel, readable; he does not sheathe it to hide it.

en: I-i-it’s Kim Yushin!!
You’ve never heard of Kim Yushin…?

lines: 이 바보야 — 김유신이 삼한 최강의 칼이야…!
연개소문, 계백 장군 — 다 비키라고 해. 아니면 계백에게 그 칭호가 아직 다툼 중이라고 해. 웃지 않을 거다.
en: You fool — Kim Yushin is the Greatest Blade of Samhan…!
Yeon Gesomun, General Gyebek — tell them all to stand aside. Or tell Gyebek the title is still disputed. He will not laugh.

blocks.html: Over the next few years Yushin takes more than forty fortresses.
blocks.ko: 이후 몇 해에 걸쳐 유신은 마흔 개가 넘는 성을 얻는다.

blocks.html: Autumn, ninth month. The queen made him Supreme General and sent him with troops against seven Baekje fortresses, Gahye, Seongyeol, Donghwa and the rest. He won a great victory and opened the Gahye crossing.
blocks.ko: 가을 9월, 왕이 그를 상장군으로 삼아 군사를 이끌고 백제의 가혜성·성열성·동화성 등 일곱 성을 치게 하니, 크게 이기고 이어 가혜 나루를 열었다.
blocks.hanja: 秋九月，王命為上將軍，使領兵伐百濟加兮城、省熱城、同火城等七城，大克之，因開加兮之津。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin I, Queen Seondeok yr. 13 (644)

blocks.caption: Forty fortresses, along a border nobody could draw the same way twice.
blocks.ko: 두 번 같게 그릴 수 없는 국경을 따라, 마흔 개의 성.

blocks.html: In Baekje’s markets they spit when they say his title. At home they toast it. Both sides add, quietly, that Gyebek hasn’t met him yet. Until he does, “greatest blade” is a tavern argument with two right answers.
blocks.ko: 백제 장터에선 그의 칭호를 말할 때 침을 뱉는다. 고향에선 축배를 든다. 양쪽 다 누군가 조용히 덧붙인다. 계백과는 아직 붙어 보지 않았다고. 붙기 전까지 ‘최강의 칼’은 정답이 둘인 주점 논쟁이다.

en: After the twentieth, nobody was counting.
And you kept taking them anyway.

lines: …멈추면, 멈춘 이유를 저들이 알아서 지어낼 테니.
en: …If I stopped, they would invent a reason for my stopping.

blocks.html: Yushin rode past his own gate without looking back. About fifty paces on he stopped his horse, had a drink of water fetched from the house, sipped it, and said, "The water at home still tastes the way it used to."
blocks.ko: 유신은 집 문 앞을 지나면서도 돌아보지 않고 갔다. 오십 걸음쯤 가서 말을 세우고, 집에서 마실 물을 떠 오게 하여 마시며 말하였다. "우리 집 물은 아직도 옛 맛이 나는구나."
blocks.hanja: 庾信過門，不顧而行，至五十步許，駐馬，令取漿水於宅，啜之曰：「吾家之水，尚有舊味。」
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin I (645)

blocks.html: Between campaigns he still goes alone to the cavern lake. The stone in the story is his father’s. His own pocket is empty. He undresses anyway.
blocks.ko: 원정 사이, 그는 여전히 홀로 동굴 호수로 간다. 이야기 속의 돌은 아버지 것이다. 제 주머니는 비어 있다. 그래도 벗는다.

en: You came with a question, or you came because the hill opened.
Either is fine. Sit down before you fall in again. And take the rest off. I want the question from a bare man.
lines: 질문을 들고 왔든, 언덕이 열려서 왔든.
둘 다 괜찮아요. 다시 빠지기 전에 앉아요. 그리고 남은 것도 벗어요. 질문은 벗은 몸에서 들을래요.

en: Three things.
The northern door. The queen’s count. How long I may stay.
lines: 북쪽 문. 여왕의 수. 얼마나 있어도 되는지.

en: Stay is not a number, marshal.
Sit. Unnie will do the other two. I’ll do the one she pretends isn’t counsel.
lines: 앉아. 나머지 둘은 언니가 해. 언니가 충고가 아니라고 하는 건 내가 할게.

en: It involves my mouth.

blocks.html: Hyullé does not speak. She has already warmed the far ledge. Her eyes are on his mouth while Narim answers the north. He will ride before I finish a sentence.
blocks.ko: 혈레는 말이 없다. 이미 먼 턱을 데워 두었다. 나림이 북쪽을 답하는 동안 눈은 그의 입에. 문장 끝내기 전에 탈 거야.

en: Yeon’s door is a guest-door only from one side.
The queen’s count is the one they will not let her finish. Bring her the west in numbers. Do not stand in front of the chair.
Take what you need. Leave before Golhwa asks you to stay. She will ask.
lines: 여왕의 수는 끝내게 두지 않는 수예요. 서쪽을 숫자로 가져와요. 의자 앞에 서지 말아요.
필요한 것만 가져가요. 골화가 남으라 하기 전에 가요. 할 테니까.
앉으려고도 할 거야. 경고는 그중 하나만 하는 거고.
en: She will also try to sit on you. I’m only warning you about one of those.
Stay. In the water.

lines: 내 위에, 막내가 먼저인 걸 견딜 수 있으면.
en: On me, if you can bear the youngest being first.
Guest-door. Numbers. Behind the chair. Leave before stay.
I have the three answers. That is enough.
lines: 손님 문. 숫자. 의자 뒤. 남기 전에 떠남.
자네 이름만 들어도 우리 애들이 밥을 안 먹어.
en: Yushin, my friend~~
My men stop eating at the sound of your name.

blocks.html: One star over Samhan tonight. Three men are looking up at it, and every one of them wants to be the King for All…!
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 삼한 위에 별 하나. 세 사내가 그 별을 올려다본다. 셋 다 “삼한왕검”이 되고 싶다…!

en: Well — is it enough now?
We have given Baekje a proper beating…
So then… do you mean to drag the King of Baekje back too?

lines: 그런데 뭔가 다른 것이 움직이고 있고, 그건 제가 움직이는 게 아닙니다.
en: Brother… the grudge is mine. I know that.
But something else is moving, and it is not me moving it.
Brother… I had little interest in any of it.
A wife I loved, a peaceful household.
I believed that much would be enough.
But the world—
Chunchu, what on earth are you saying…
The eastern star shines especially bright tonight…
Brother… let us go and take it now.
That old palace of ours…
the dream we had when we were young…
The “King for All”, I mean…!
…I told you. That one is a planet.
Thirty years and you are still saying that.

lines: 계백아. 너는 저 궁 안에서 자랐다.
의자 하나 잡겠다고 미쳐 가는 사내들을 숱하게 봤겠지.
왕관 쓴 노비도 있고, 서문 앞에서 빌어먹는 임금도 있다.
en: Gyebek. You grew up inside that palace.
You have watched men go mad reaching for a chair.
A man is one of two things — a king, or a slave.
There are slaves in crowns and kings begging at the west gate.
One request.
I will obey.

lines: 내가 언젠가 어리석은 명을 내릴 게다. 한 번이 아닐 게고.
왕관은 내가 쓴다. 그래도 네 삶의 임금은 너다…!
en: No. Do not follow me.
One day I will give you a stupid order. More than one.
Judge it yourself.
I wear the crown. You are still the king of your own life…!

lines: 폐하... 이 얘기를 저에게 왜 해 주시는 겁니까?
en: Your Majesty… why are you telling me this?

lines: 계백아… 사내는 더 큰 꿈을 품어야지.
en: Gyebek… a man should hold a larger dream.
The “King for All”, I mean…!
Your Majesty.
I saw Gesomun again.

blocks.html: He touches the left side of his neck when he says it, where the old burn scar runs down under his collar.
blocks.ko: 그 말을 하며 그는 왼쪽 목덜미를 만진다. 오래된 화상 자국이 깃 아래로 이어지는 자리다.
blocks.art: Close on Gyebek’s hand at the burn scar down the left side of his neck (왼쪽 목덜미의 화상 자국), drawn exactly as on the prisoner at Yeon’s outpost in 1.6.

blocks.html: The banquet hall has been scrubbed for three nights. Yeon climbs to a cave in the hill above the river. Nobody prays there lightly. The marches say the stone still remembers bowstrings.
blocks.ko: 연회장의 피를 씻어 낸 지 사흘 밤. 연은 강 위 언덕의 동굴로 오른다. 그곳에선 아무도 가볍게 빌지 않는다. 변방 사람들은 그 돌이 아직 활시위 소리를 기억한다고 믿는다.

blocks.html: He kneels at the mouth and lays a crow-stamped ring-pommel on the stone. He does not ask forgiveness for the hall. He asks for witnesses.
blocks.ko: 그는 동굴 입구에 무릎을 꿇고, 삼족오가 찍힌 환두대도를 돌 위에 내려놓는다. 전각의 일로 용서를 구하지는 않는다. 증인을 구한다.

blocks.html: East of the capital there is a great cave called the Sacred Tunnel. Every tenth month the king sacrifices there himself.
blocks.ko: 도성 동쪽에 큰 굴이 있으니 신수라 부른다. 해마다 10월이면 왕이 몸소 제사를 지낸다.
blocks.hanja: 國城東有大穴，名神隧，皆以十月，王自祭之。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

en: The Holy King forged a country here.
I too… will forge one with my own hands.

lines: …평생을, 제가 무엇에 쓰일 것인지 모르고 살았습니다.
사람은 대개 태어나서, 얼마쯤 살다가, 죽습니다.
en: …All my life I did not know what I was for.
Most men are born, and live a while, and die.
You gave me monsters.
Thank you for giving me a direction.

lines: 제 몸의 뼈가 다 부서질 때까지.
제 마음의 구슬이 다 금 갈 때까지.
en: Until every bone in me is broken.
Until every jewel in my heart is cracked through.
I will not let go of this.
The “King for All”, I mean…!

blocks.html: Gesomun wants a country. Far to the west, the man who owns half the world is trying to pronounce his name…!
blocks.ko: 개소문은 나라를 원한다. 저 멀리 서쪽, 천하의 절반을 가진 사내가 그 이름을 입속으로 굴려 보는 중이다…!

blocks.html: Far to the west, a man who owns half the world hears a new name. He turns it over on his tongue, like a grape he hasn’t decided to eat.
blocks.ko: 저 멀리 서쪽, 천하의 절반을 가진 사내가 새 이름 하나를 듣는다. 그는 삼킬지 말지 아직 정하지 않은 포도알처럼 그 이름을 혀 위에서 굴린다.

blocks.html: Half the world sends tribute here and calls it friendship.
blocks.ko: 세상의 절반이 조공을 바치고, 그걸 우정이라 부르는 곳.

blocks.html: On the dingsi day, Zhang Jian, Governor-General of Yingzhou, reported that Quan Gai Suwen*, Great Man of Goguryeo's Eastern Division, had murdered his king, Wu†.
blocks.ko: 정사일, 영주도독 장검이 아뢰기를, 고구려 동부 대인 천개소문*이 그 왕 무†를 시해하였다고 하였다.
blocks.hanja: 丁巳，營州都督張儉奏高麗東部大人泉蓋蘇文弒其王武。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 196, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 16 (642), 11th month

notes.html: Quan (泉) is Tang’s stand-in for Yeon (淵), a character it could not write. Gai Suwen is Gaesomun read in Chinese. Together: Yeon Gesomun.
notes.ko: 천(泉)은 당이 쓸 수 없던 연(淵) 대신 쓴 글자다. 곧 연개소문이다.

notes.html: Wu is Geonmu (建武), the king this book calls Yeongnyu.
notes.ko: 무는 건무, 이 책의 영류왕이다.

blocks.html: Gai Suwen has murdered his lord and seized the government. It is truly not to be borne. With the forces we have today, taking the place would not be hard. But I do not wish to wear out the common people. For now I would have the Khitan and the Mohe harass them. What do you say?
blocks.ko: 개소문이 그 임금을 시해하고 나라의 정사를 오로지하니, 참으로 참을 수 없다. 오늘의 병력으로 그를 취하기는 어렵지 않으나 백성을 수고롭게 하고 싶지 않다. 우선 거란과 말갈을 시켜 그들을 어지럽히려 하는데, 어떻겠는가?
blocks.hanja: 蓋蘇文弒其君而專國政，誠不可忍。以今日兵力，取之不難，但不欲勞百姓，吾欲且使契丹、靺鞨擾之，何如？
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 17 (643)

blocks.caption: The Second Emperor of Tang. He owns half the world, and he is curious about the other half.
blocks.ko: 당의 두 번째 황제. 세상의 절반을 가졌고, 나머지 절반이 궁금하다.

en: Gai Suwen…?
zhLatn: Gài Sūwén…?

blocks.html: The seventh invasion of Goguryeo has not begun. It has only found its excuse. Now it needs four dragons…!
blocks.ko: 고구려 일곱 번째 침공은 아직 시작되지 않았다. 구실을 찾았을 뿐이다. 이제 용 네 마리만 있으면 된다…!

images.alt: Ancient Korean scroll unfurling dramatically with blue and gold calligraphy by candlelight
Ink-painted poster: the gold dragon coils out of black storm ink around the Second Emperor on the Hanyuan terrace, his hand resting on its snout
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; heads and the dragon’s head stay inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night on the top terrace of the Hanyuan Hall at the Daming Palace, the palace roofs below dissolving into black ink. Low angle. TWO SUBJECTS: a human-scale emperor AND a huge dragon. INTERACTION: the gold Tang dragon Huanglong (gold ink-brush dragon from the attached board, three claws) pours out of a black ink storm in one great S around and behind the Second Emperor and lowers its huge head right beside him, jaws closed, whiskers drifting like brush strokes; the emperor stands at the balustrade scowling toward the east, one hand resting flat on the dragon’s snout. One lamp-fire key (#c97a2e) from below catches his gold thread, his beard and the dragon’s jaw; everything else is ink-black. TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) on rice paper — heavy black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding, splashed ink smoke and storm, dry calligraphic brush strokes for roofs, columns, robes and cloud, ink splatters and drips at the frame edges, bare paper only where the edges dissolve; the gold ink-brush dragon is the main colour in the dark, with a few small vermilion and flame accents. THE ONE EXCEPTION: the Second Emperor himself is a full-colour Korean webtoon figure — clean ink linework, drawn face matching the attached portrait, warm skin, imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade, black futou — a coloured man inside an ink empire; nothing else in the frame is in full colour. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, big dark masses, one bright break of light, NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp, no calligraphy characters. Not photoreal, not 3D, not a realistic scaled dragon. No glow aura, no halo — the accent is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — THE SECOND EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_taizong.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Bearded Tang emperor: black futou cap with an upright pin, thick black beard and moustache, fierce scowl. Dress: Imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade. Demeanor: Commands; never asks. Conqueror's contempt that curdles at Ansi. Presence: THE SON OF HEAVEN — every frame he is in bends around him. He is SHROUDED IN DARKNESS: the black of the hall gathers around him like a mantle. One close practical light (a lamp, a brazier, a lamp-tree) rakes across him from below or from the side and SCULPTS him — the heavy yellow silk breaks into deep protruding folds brushed in loaded oil strokes that follow each fold, gold thread flicked in with impasto, the beard and cheekbones carved — and then falls off into black across his body and half his face; that falloff is the darkness, never a flat backlit silhouette. The camera sits BELOW his eyeline (low angle or worm’s-eye) and he is always placed HIGHER than anyone near him — on the dais, on a step, standing while others kneel or sit. He reads larger than life through lens and staging, not as a giant: broad shoulders, the robe spreading wide and heavy into the dark like a mountain, his shadow enormous on walls and floor. Unhurried, heavy stillness — never fidgeting, never casual, never a colleague at someone’s shoulder; when he smiles or laughs it is a predator’s ease, and the room goes quiet around it. Everyone else in frame is smaller, lower, less lit, turned toward him. The aura is darkness, scale and the hush around him — never a glow, never a halo, never rays behind his head. #c97a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Korean ring-pommel sword; Korean lamellar. | HUANGLONG (황룡, taizong's yellow dragon, guardian of the Tang throne) — attached board /obj_yellow_dragon.png: TANG-DYNASTY dragon painted in gold ink-brush: lean long-necked serpentine body in an S-curve, four lean leonine legs striding, THREE claws on each foot, long open-jawed snout with fangs, two backswept horns, whiskers and mane flung out as dry calligraphic gold brush strokes, whip tail ending in a flame tuft; burnished gold-yellow scales with ochre-umber shading — match the board, not a later Ming/Qing five-claw dragon, never a realistic scaled 3D dragon. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, coiling through black ink cloud and lamp smoke; light catches the scales as real light, never a glow outline. Its stills are predominantly dark and intimidating Chinese ink painting: splashed black ink, smoke, the gold dragon the main colour in the dark; every figure is ink-painted except the Second Emperor, who stays a full-colour webtoon figure. Owned by no one but sits behind whoever holds the dais; it coils over Chang'an and turns its head only for the Son of Heaven. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) — black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding into rice paper, dry calligraphic brush for roofs, columns, smoke and robes, the vermilion and gold reduced to small accents in a world of ink; officials, guards and other Tang figures are ink figures too. The ONE exception is the Second Emperor himself: he keeps the house webtoon figure render in full colour (yellow robe, black futou, drawn face), a coloured man inside an ink empire. Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. images.alt: The young monk Shinsung kneels and sets the smallest temple bell on the bare floor of a lesser house.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior night, WORM'S-EYE from floor level inside a small, bare lesser temple house in Pyongyang. ONE device: rough dark floorboards running away from the lens to a single open door. The young monk Shinsung, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, shaven head, grey monk's robe and kasaya, kneeling as he sets a small bronze temple bell down on the bare floor with both hands — there is no frame to hang it from — palms still resting on its shoulder, face calm, eyes lowered. Foreground: the out-of-focus rim of the bell catching the lamp. A clay oil lamp on the floor beside him rakes light across the bronze, the folds of his robe and his knuckles. Through the open door, far off in blue haze, the big temple up the hill glows with strange lanterns that are no longer his. Old-master canvas texture, umber-to-black darks. CANON — SHINSUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_shinsung.png (face only; invent a new pose). #8f7b70 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. blocks.html: The Second Emperor of the West resides in the Palace. Seventeen years ago he murdered his brothers to become the Son of Heaven, and he has spent every year since folding nations under imperial rule — the Turks, the Xueyantuo, the Tibetans.
blocks.ko: 서토의 황제가 궁에 있다. 17년 전 형제들을 죽이고 천자가 된 그는, 그 뒤의 모든 해를 나라들을 제국의 지배 아래 접어 넣는 데 썼다 — 돌궐, 설연타, 토번.

blocks.html: The inner palace is a country of its own — so many women the hall cannot hold them all at once, silk stacked like tribute, a very large harem that moves when he moves.
blocks.ko: 내전은 그 자체로 나라다 — 대전이 한 번에 담지 못할 만큼 많은 여인, 공물처럼 쌓인 비단, 그가 움직이면 함께 움직이는 아주 큰 후궁.

blocks.html: He’s known by many names. The Heaven-Sent General. The Khan of Heaven.
blocks.ko: 그를 부르는 이름은 많다. 천책상장. 천가한.

blocks.html: One more thing about him, which nobody in Samhan quite believes when they are told it: nobody says his name.
blocks.ko: 그에 대해 한 가지 더. 삼한 사람들은 듣고도 잘 믿지 못하는 것인데 — 아무도 그의 이름을 부르지 않는다.

blocks.html: He never quite forbids it. The two characters of his given name simply vanish from the empire, quietly: a ministry renamed because one of them sat in its title, a bodhisattva’s name shortened by a syllable, scribes copying old books leaving one stroke off — and everyone understands.
blocks.ko: 그가 금하는 일은 끝내 없다. 다만 그의 이름 두 글자가 제국에서 조용히 치워질 뿐이다. 부(部)의 이름에 한 글자가 들어 있다는 이유로 부의 이름이 바뀌고, 보살의 이름은 한 음절이 짧아지고, 옛 책을 베끼는 서리들은 그저 획 하나를 빼놓는다 — 그리고 모두가 알아듣는다.

en: …They don’t say his name? At all?
They don’t write it either. Not on paper.

blocks.html: So the Second Emperor of the West is a man who has not heard another person say his own name since he was crowned, and there is nobody left alive who is allowed to.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 서토의 황제는, 즉위한 뒤로 다른 사람이 제 이름을 부르는 것을 들어 본 적 없는 사내다. 그리고 그럴 수 있도록 허락된 사람은 이제 살아 있지 않다.

blocks.html: The Grand Minister is dying. At the foot of the bed the court diarist, Chu Suiliang, writes down everything the emperor says.
blocks.ko: 대신이 죽어 가고 있다. 침상 발치에서는 기거주를 맡은 저수량이 황제의 말을 하나도 빠짐없이 받아 적는다.

lines: 폐하. 신이 죽으면, 폐하께 «아니되옵니다»라고 말할 사람이 없습니다.
en: Your Majesty. When I am gone, there will be no one left to tell you no.
zh: 陛下。臣死之後，再無人敢對陛下言「不可」矣。
zhLatn: Bìxià. Chén sǐ zhī hòu, zài wú rén gǎn duì Bìxià yán “bùkě” yǐ.

en: Why else do you think I put up with you for twenty years.
zh: 不然朕何苦容忍你二十年。
zhLatn: Bùrán zhèn hékǔ róngrěn nǐ èrshí nián.

lines: 구리로 거울을 삼으면 의관을 바로 하고,
en: With bronze for a mirror, a man straightens his robes.
With history for a mirror, he sees the rise and fall of states.
With a man for a mirror, he sees his own faults.
…Today I lose one of my mirrors.
zhLatn: Yǐ tóng wéi jìng, kěyǐ zhèng yīguān;
Yǐ gǔ wéi jìng, kěyǐ zhī xīngtì;
Yǐ rén wéi jìng, kěyǐ míng déshī.
…Zhèn jīnrì shī yī jìng yǐ.

lines: 수나라의 실수를 다시 반복해서는 안 된다…!
en: The Great Tang is still a young dynasty.
We must not repeat the mistakes of the Sui…!
Not if the western dream is to be realised.
zhLatn: Dà Táng shàng shǔ yòu cháo.
Bùkě zài dǎo Suí zhī fùzhé…!
Ruò yù chéng xītǔ zhī mèng.

en: The western dream?
zhLatn: Xītǔ zhī mèng?

lines: 수나라가 통일했지만, 정신나간 양제 때문에 30년도 채 안 돼서 망했어.
en: The great revival of the Central Plain dynasties.
Han was the finest civilisation in the world.
And then—
Four hundred years. Four hundred years of being savaged by barbarians!!
Sui reunified it, then fell in less than thirty years because of that lunatic Emperor Yang.
And here I am. The Prince of Qin!
zh: 四百年。四百年為蠻夷所蹂躪！！
隋一統之，卻因那瘋子煬帝，不到三十年便亡。
zhLatn: Zhōngyuán wángcháo zhī wěidà fùxīng.
Hàn nǎi tiānxià zuì shèng zhī wénmíng.
Ér hòu——
Sìbǎi nián. Sìbǎi nián wéi mányí suǒ róulìn!!
Suí yītǒng zhī, què yīn nà fēngzi Yángdì, bù dào sānshí nián biàn wáng.
Ér zhèn——Qín Wáng shì yě!

blocks.html: By the next spring the dream has left the sickroom. Over every ward gate in Chang’an the sign-painters letter it in gold on red, THE GREAT TANG DREAM, each banner at the same height and the same distance from the next. Nobody can say who ordered it, which is how the best orders travel.
blocks.ko: 이듬해 봄, 그 꿈은 병상을 떠나 있다. 장안의 방문(坊門)마다 간판장이들이 붉은 바탕에 금색으로 〈대당몽(大唐夢)〉이라 써 붙인다. 모두 같은 높이, 모두 같은 간격. 누가 시켰는지는 아무도 모른다. 가장 좋은 명령은 원래 그렇게 퍼진다.

blocks.html: Later that month Chu Suiliang brings in the reports from everywhere the empire touches.
blocks.ko: 그달 말, 저수량이 제국이 닿는 온 곳의 보고를 들고 들어온다.

lines: 천축에서는, 현장법사가 아직도 순례 중이라 합니다!
그런데 무슨 괴상한 이야기도 담더라고요, 날아다니는 원숭이라든동,
서역에서는, 새로운 제국이… 있습쉼? 이슬람? 이라는 새로운 가르침을 따른다고 합니다.
페르시아와 로마제국이 망했다고 하니, 막강한 세력인 듯 합니다.
en: From India — they say the monk Xuanzang is still on his pilgrimage!
Though he sends back the strangest tales — flying monkeys and the like,
and in the western regions a new empire… Islam? A new teaching they follow.
Persia and Rome are said to have fallen, so it must be a formidable power.
And in the east — the King of Goryeo has been murdered by his own subject…
zh: 天竺那邊——據說玄奘法師仍在西行！
不過他寄回的奇談怪事——什麼飛猴之類，
西域則有新帝國……伊斯蘭？一種新的教法。
波斯與大秦皆聞已亡，可見其勢不可輕。
海東則——高麗王為其臣所弒……
zhLatn: Tiānzhú nàbiān——jùshuō Xuánzàng fǎshī réng zài xīxíng!
Bùguò tā jì huí de qítán guàishì——shénme fēihóu zhī lèi,
Xīyù zé yǒu xīn dìguó… Yīsīlán? Yī zhǒng xīn de jiàofǎ.
Bōsī yǔ Dàqín jiē wén yǐ wáng, kějiàn qí shì bùkě qīng.
Hǎidōng zé——Gāolí wáng wéi qí chén suǒ shì…

en: Wait.
Gai Suwen…?
zhLatn: Qiě màn.
Gài Sūwén…?

blocks.html: Chang’an writes the name without the Yeon. Yeon, 淵, was the given name of the emperor’s late father, and nobody in this palace writes it. It is an old house. Nearly seven hundred years ago, in Jolbon, its crow-clan chieftain Yeon Tabal looked down at a soaked exile called Jumong and weighed him.
blocks.ko: 장안은 그 이름에서 ‘연’을 뺀다. 연(淵)은 황제 선친의 이름자라, 이 궁에서는 아무도 그 글자를 쓰지 않는다. 오래된 집안이다. 칠백 년 가까이 전, 졸본에서 이 집안의 까마귀 씨족 족장 연타발이 흠뻑 젖은 망명객 주몽을 내려다보며 저울질했다.
blocks.art: One panel: Yeon Tabal in his hall in Jolbon, looking down at the soaked Jumong on his knees (callback to the Jumong side story).

en: The King of Goryeo was a friend I valued.
His name… ah…
…Yeongnyu! King Yeongnyu!
zhLatn: Gāolí wáng shì zhèn suǒ zhòng zhī yǒu.
Qí míng… ā…
…Róngliú! Róngliú Wáng!

blocks.html: Everything is in place. It has been for some time; he was simply waiting to be bored enough.
blocks.ko: 판은 다 짜였다. 사실 진작에 짜여 있었고, 그는 다만 충분히 지루해지기를 기다렸을 뿐이다.

lines: 폐하, 벌써 여섯 번이나 쳐들어갔습니다. 또 가자는 말씀이십니까?
en: Majesty, we have invaded six times already — and you would go again?
zh: 陛下，已征六次——還要再去？
zhLatn: Bìxià, yǐ zhēng liù cì——hái yào zài qù?

en: Because I have not gone myself.
Life is not theory. It is practice.
zhLatn: Yīnwèi zhèn shàngwèi qīnzhēng.
Rénshēng fēi lǐlùn, nǎi shíjiàn.

blocks.html: He launches the Seventh Invasion of Goguryeo. It’s the seventh army out of the West, and the first he leads himself. The clerks need three days to read the muster aloud. Horse from the frontier. Foot from the rivers. Five hundred hulls riding low with a year of grain.
blocks.ko: 그는 고구려 일곱 번째 침공을 일으킨다. 서쪽에서 온 일곱 번째 군대이고, 그가 직접 이끄는 첫 군대다. 서기들이 소집 명부를 소리 내어 읽는 데만 사흘이 걸린다. 변방의 기병. 강가 고을의 보병. 한 해 치 곡식을 싣고 낮게 뜬 배 오백 척.

blocks.html: Four dragon banners go up over the muster: white, red, blue and black.
blocks.ko: 소집 위로 용의 깃발 넷이 오른다. 흰 용, 붉은 용, 푸른 용, 검은 용.
blocks.art: Draw the Four Dragons table (next block) as these four banners over the muster, each general’s name sewn under his dragon; no table on the page.

blocks.caption: The Blue Dragon. The emperor’s most patient general, which is its own kind of danger.
blocks.ko: 청룡. 황제의 장수 가운데 가장 참을성이 많다. 그것도 일종의 위험이다.

blocks.html: The fifth banner has no name on it at all. Everyone knows whose it is.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 깃발에는 아예 이름이 없다. 그래도 그게 누구 것인지 모르는 사람은 없다.

blocks.title: The Seventh Invasion
blocks.caption: Three roads in and five hundred hulls. Goguryeo’s wall was built to stop one army at a time.
blocks.ko: 들어오는 길 셋, 배 오백 척. 고구려의 성벽은 한 번에 한 군대씩 막으라고 쌓은 것이다.

blocks.html: Two of the four dragons were born on the steppe. The Red Dragon is a steppe prince who keeps felt tents inside the capital walls. The White Dragon walked his whole tribe across the border as a boy. The steppe has its own title for the emperor, and he answers to it. Even his favourite horses came from out there. The Black Dragon is the empress’s brother. He argued against this war in council. He’s riding to it anyway.
blocks.ko: 네 마리 용 가운데 둘은 초원에서 태어났다. 붉은 용은 도성 담장 안에 펠트 천막을 치고 사는 초원의 왕자다. 흰 용은 어린 나이에 부족 전체를 이끌고 국경을 넘어왔다. 초원은 황제를 따로 부르는 칭호가 있고, 그는 그 이름에 대답한다. 아끼는 말들마저 그쪽에서 왔다. 검은 용은 황후의 오라비다. 그는 회의에서 이 전쟁을 반대했다. 그리고 지금 그 전쟁으로 말을 달린다.

blocks.label: The Third Leg
blocks.ko: 세 번째 다리

blocks.html: In the third month an envoy arrives from Pyongyang with a request nobody in the Ministry of Rites has seen before. The new master of Goguryeo would like some Daoists.
blocks.ko: 삼월, 평양에서 사신이 온다. 예부의 누구도 본 적 없는 청을 들고. 고구려의 새 주인이 도사를 좀 보내 달라는 것이다.

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo envoy
lines: 막리지께서 이르시길, 솥은 다리 셋으로 선다 하셨습니다.
천자께서 하나 내어 주실 수 있다면, 셋째 다리를 청하신답니다.
en: The Mangniji says a cauldron stands on three legs.
We have the Buddha. We have Confucius.
He would like the third leg, if the Son of Heaven can spare one.
zh: 莫離支言：三教譬如鼎足，闕一不可。
zhLatn: Mòlízhī yán: sān jiào pìrú dǐng zú, quē yī bù kě.
Jīn yǒu fó, yǒu rú.
Wéi quē dàojiào, qǐ tiānzǐ cì zhī.

lines: 줘라. 어차피 우리 집안이 그 노인네 후손이다. 고구려가 짐의 조상한테 절하면서 그걸 도라고 부르게 두어라.
en: He wants Laozi?
Give him Laozi. Our house descends from the old man anyway. Let Goguryeo bow to my ancestor and call it theology.
zh: 給他老子。朕家本是老君之後。讓高麗拜朕的祖宗，還叫它作道。
zhLatn: Tā yào Lǎozǐ?
Gěi tā Lǎozǐ. Zhèn jiā běn shì Lǎojūn zhī hòu. Ràng Gāolí bài zhèn de zǔzōng, hái jiào tā zuò dào.

blocks.html: Eight Daoists go east with a copy of the Daodejing. In Pyongyang the Mangniji gives them lodgings, and the lodgings he gives them are temples. The monks are moved out the same week, with their bells.
blocks.ko: 도사 여덟이 도덕경 한 질을 들고 동쪽으로 간다. 평양에서 막리지는 그들에게 숙소를 내주는데, 내준 숙소가 절이다. 같은 주에 승려들이 쫓겨난다. 종까지 들려서.

blocks.html: A young monk named Shinsung carries the smallest bell down the hill himself, to a lesser house that has no frame to hang it from, and sets it on the floor. He does not complain to anyone. The bell stays on the floor for twenty-five years.
blocks.ko: 신성이라는 젊은 승려가 제일 작은 종을 손수 지고 언덕을 내려가, 종 걸 틀도 없는 작은 절에 바닥에 내려놓는다. 아무에게도 불평하지 않는다. 종은 이십오 년 동안 바닥에 놓여 있다.

blocks.html: All conditioned things are impermanent; this is the law of arising and passing away. … When arising and passing away have themselves passed away, that stillness is bliss.
blocks.ko: 모든 지어진 것은 덧없으니, 이것이 나고 사라지는 법이다. …… 나고 사라짐이 다 사라지고 나면, 고요히 사라짐이 즐거움이 된다.
blocks.hanja: 「諸行無常，是生滅法。」……「生滅滅已，寂滅為樂。」
blocks.source: Nirvana Sutra (大般涅槃經) fasc. 14, Noble Practice (聖行品), tr. Dharmakṣema · T12n0374, pp. 450a, 451a

blocks.label: Three Choices
blocks.ko: 세 가지 안

blocks.html: In the ninth month an envoy comes from Silla, which is losing fortresses to Baekje faster than it can count them, and asks for an army. The Second Emperor offers him a choice of three.
blocks.ko: 구월, 신라에서 사신이 온다. 백제에게 성을 세는 것보다 빨리 잃고 있는 나라다. 군대를 청한다. 황제는 세 가지 중에 고르라 한다.

lines: 하나. 거란과 말갈을 요동에 풀어, 고구려가 한 해 동안 북쪽만 보게 하겠다.
둘. 붉은 군복 몇천 벌과 당의 깃발을 주겠다. 성벽에 세워 두어라. 백제가 보면 짐이 온 줄 알고 달아날 게다.
en: One. I send the Khitan and the Mohe into Liaodong, and Goguryeo looks north for a year.
Two. I give you a few thousand red coats and Tang banners. Stand them on your walls. Baekje will think I have come, and run.
Three.
zh: 其一，朕發契丹、靺鞨直入遼東，使高麗北顧一年。
其二，朕給爾絳袍丹幟數千，立於城上，百濟見之，以為朕至，必走。
zhLatn: Qí yī, zhèn fā Qìdān, Mòhé zhí rù Liáodōng, shǐ Gāolí běi gù yì nián.
Qí èr, zhèn gěi ěr jiàngpáo dānzhì shù qiān, lì yú chéng shàng, Bǎijì jiàn zhī, yǐwéi zhèn zhì, bì zǒu.
Qí sān.

lines: 너희 나라는 여인이 다스린다. 이웃들이 업신여기는 게 그 때문이다. 그래서 자꾸 쳐들어오는 거고.
짐의 종친 하나를 너희 왕으로 보내 주마. 지킬 병사 몇과 함께. 나라가 편안해지면, 그때 돌려받아라.
en: Your country is ruled by a woman, and your neighbours despise you for it. That is why they keep coming.
I could send you one of my own clan to be your king, with a few soldiers to look after him. When the country is safe, you may have it back.
zh: 爾國以婦人為主，為鄰國所輕，故寇不息。
朕遣一宗支，與為爾國主，自將兵以衛之，待爾國安，任爾自守。
zhLatn: Ěr guó yǐ fùrén wéi zhǔ, wéi línguó suǒ qīng, gù kòu bù xī.
Zhèn qiǎn yì zōngzhī, yǔ wéi ěr guó zhǔ, zì jiāng bīng yǐ wèi zhī, dài ěr guó ān, rèn ěr zì shǒu.

blocks.html: The envoy says yes, and then no, and then nothing at all. The emperor watches him for a while.
blocks.ko: 사신은 예, 했다가, 아니, 했다가, 끝내 아무 말도 못 한다. 황제는 한동안 그를 지켜본다.

lines: 용렬한 자로구나. 물에 빠진 나라가 보낼 위인은 아니다.
en: A mediocre man. Not the sort a country sends when it is drowning.
zh: 庸鄙之人，非乞師告急之才也。
zhLatn: Yōngbǐ zhī rén, fēi qǐ shī gàojí zhī cái yě.

blocks.html: The report reaches Surabol in the twelfth month. The Harmony Council has the third option read aloud twice. Bidam reads it once, and folds it small.
blocks.ko: 보고는 섣달에 서라벌에 닿는다. 화백회의는 세 번째 안을 두 번 소리 내어 읽게 한다. 비담은 한 번 읽고, 작게 접는다.

lines: 떠돌이 개한테 절밥 내놓듯이 왕을 내주겠다는군.
…그런데 이 방엔 그 밥그릇에 절할 사람도 있지.
en: He offers us a king the way a temple puts out rice for a stray.
…And there are men in this hall who would bow for the bowl.

blocks.label: Longmen Field
blocks.ko: 용문

blocks.html: In a poor field at Longmen, a farmer named Xue Rengui is planning to rebury his ancestors. Millet, rammed earth, a hut that doesn’t pretend to be anything. He has the right soil for graves. He doesn’t yet know he has the wrong year for quiet.
blocks.ko: 용문의 척박한 밭에서 설인귀라는 농부가 조상의 무덤을 다시 쓰려 한다. 조밭, 다진 흙, 아무것도 아닌 척하지 않는 오두막. 무덤 쓸 흙은 제대로 골랐다. 조용히 살 해를 잘못 골랐다는 건 아직 모른다.

blocks.caption: A poor farmer with good soil for graves. His wife thinks he could do better.
blocks.ko: 무덤 쓰기 좋은 땅을 가진 가난한 농부. 아내는 그가 더 큰일을 할 사람이라고 본다.

blocks.html: The cloth on his back is plain yellow peasant hemp. Not a banner. Not the white armour the mountain will learn later. Just the cheapest dye the village still sells, the colour of millet at the wrong hour. He hoes. His wife, Liu, keeps the hut door.
blocks.ko: 등에 걸친 것은 평범한 노란 농부의 삼베다. 깃발이 아니다. 나중에 산이 배우게 될 흰 갑옷도 아니다. 마을이 아직 파는 가장 싼 물감, 잘못된 시각의 기장 빛. 그는 호미질한다. 아내 유씨가 흙집 문을 지킨다.

blocks.html: The Son of Heaven is calling up troops for Liaodong. The edict reaches villages that have never seen a palace, and wives who have never left the furrow.
blocks.ko: 천자가 요동으로 군사를 부른다. 조서는 궁을 본 적 없는 마을과, 이랑을 떠나 본 적 없는 아내들에게 닿는다.

blocks.html: The edict comes on red paper, pasted to the well-house wall at the height of a man’s eyes: SERVE THE EMPEROR. Under it, in smaller characters, the quota. It does not ask for Xue Li. It asks for one man from every household with the right number of hands, and any man with hands will do.
blocks.ko: 칙령은 붉은 종이로 온다. 우물가 담벼락, 사람 눈높이에 붙는다. 〈천자를 위해 봉사하라〉. 그 아래 작은 글씨로 할당량. 칙령은 설례를 부르지 않는다. 손이 제대로 달린 사내를 집마다 하나씩 부를 뿐이고, 손만 있으면 누구라도 된다.

blocks.title: Handwritten edict to the realm
blocks.hanja: 高麗蓋蘇文弒主虐民，情何可忍！今欲巡幸幽、薊，問罪遼、碣，所過營頓，無為勞費。……昔隋煬帝殘暴其下，高麗王仁愛其民，以思亂之軍擊安和之眾，故不能成功。今略言必勝之道有五：一曰以大擊小，二曰以順討逆，三曰以治乘亂，四曰以逸敵勞，五曰以悅當怨，何憂不克！佈告元元，勿為疑懼！
blocks.html: Gesomun of Goguryeo has murdered his lord and savages his people. Who could bear it? We mean to ride out to You and Ji and call Liao and Jie to account. Wherever We camp or halt, let nothing be wasted and no one be burdened. … Emperor Yang of Sui was cruel to those beneath him, and the king of Goguryeo was kind to his people. An army that longed for revolt struck a people at peace, and so it failed. Now, in short, there are five ways We are certain to win. One: the great strikes the small. Two: the loyal punishes the rebel. Three: order rides down disorder. Four: the rested meets the weary. Five: the glad meets the bitter. Why fear we will not prevail? Tell it to all the people. Let no one doubt, and no one be afraid.
blocks.ko: 고구려의 개소문이 임금을 죽이고 백성을 학대하니, 어찌 참을 수 있으랴! 이제 유주와 계주로 나아가 요동과 갈석에 죄를 묻고자 한다. 지나는 곳마다 진을 치고 머무는 데 헛된 수고와 비용이 없게 하라. …… 옛날 수 양제는 아랫사람에게 잔인하였고 고구려 왕은 백성을 아꼈다. 난을 꿈꾸는 군대로 편안하고 화목한 무리를 쳤으니 이기지 못한 것이다. 이제 반드시 이기는 길 다섯 가지를 대략 말한다. 첫째, 큰 것으로 작은 것을 친다. 둘째, 순리로 역적을 친다. 셋째, 다스려진 것으로 어지러운 것을 탄다. 넷째, 편안한 몸으로 지친 적을 맞는다. 다섯째, 기쁜 마음으로 원망하는 자를 상대한다. 어찌 이기지 못할까 걱정하랴! 백성에게 널리 알려 의심하거나 두려워하지 말게 하라!
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 18 (644), eleventh month · cf. Samguk Sagi bk. 21 (以理乘亂)

en: The mounds… they’re not done.
Not the dirt. The hands.
The edict — I heard it. I did.
zhLatn: Fén hái méi yuán.
Búshì quē tǔ. Shì quē shǒu.
Zhàoshū——tīngjiàn le. Tīngjiàn le.

lines: 손 없다고 무덤이 기다려 주진 않아요.
당신은 호미가 아니라… 극을 들 사람이에요. 내가 아는 한.
en: Mounds don’t wait because a man is short of hands.
And the edict doesn’t wait either.
You’re not a hoe. You’re a ji. As far as I can tell.
zh: 你不是鋤。你是戟。就我看。
zhLatn: Quē shǒu, fén yě bù huì děng.
Zhàoshū gèng bù huì děng.
Nǐ búshì chú. Nǐ shì jǐ. Jiù wǒ kàn.

en: The ji is in the shed.
The yellow clothes are here.
Liu. If I go — this door.
zhLatn: Jǐ zài péng lǐ.
Huángyī zài zhèr.
Liǔshì. Wǒ ruò zǒu——zhè mén.

lines: 때를 만나야 빛이 나는 법이에요. 지금이 그 때면 — 가면 돼요.
en: I’ll shut the door.
Don’t you start worrying about doors.
Talent needs its hour. If this is the hour — then go.
zh: 才須遇時。若是此時——便去。
zhLatn: Mén wǒ guān.
Nǐ bié cāoxīn mén.
Cái xū yù shí. Ruò shì cǐ shí——biàn qù.

blocks.html: The chronicler does not invent her sentence. The Xin Tangshu already wrote it down, and it is sharper than anything a field would volunteer twice.
blocks.ko: 연대기는 아내의 말을 지어내지 않는다. 신당서가 이미 적어 두었고, 밭이 두 번 입 밖으로 꺼내지 않을 만큼 날카롭다.

blocks.hanja: 夫有高世之材，要須遇時乃發。今天子自征遼東，求猛將，此難得之時，君盍圖功名以自顯？富貴還鄉，葬未晚。
blocks.ko: 무릇 세상을 넘을 재주가 있어도, 때를 만나야 드러난다. 지금 천자께서 몸소 요동을 치시며 맹장을 구하시니, 이는 얻기 어려운 때이다. 공은 어찌 공명을 도모하여 스스로를 드러내지 않는가? 부귀하여 고향에 돌아온 뒤에 장사하여도 늦지 않다.
blocks.html: A man of talent that outstrips his age must meet his hour before it can issue. Now the Son of Heaven himself campaigns against Liaodong and seeks fierce generals: this is a time rarely met. Why should you not seek merit and make yourself known? When you return in wealth and honour, it will not be too late to bury them.
blocks.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 111, biography of Xue Rengui (薛仁貴) — speech of his wife, née Liu (妻柳)

blocks.html: He goes. She is right, and a man who can lift a ji should not spend the invasion stacking earth for the dead.
blocks.ko: 그는 간다. 아내 말이 맞고, 극을 들 수 있는 사내가 침공의 해를 죽은 자 흙 쌓는 데 쓰면 안 된다.

en: …Ancestors. Wait a little longer.
Until I come back carrying this ji.
The yellow clothes — I’ll leave them here.
zhLatn: …Lièzǔ lièzōng. Zài shāo dài piànkè.
Zhízhì wǒ chí cǐ jǐ guīlái.
Huángyī——jiù liú zài zhèr.

blocks.html: He presents himself to general Zhang Shigui and signs his name under the Tang muster. The clerk writes Xue Rengui. The clerk does not look up. History will.
blocks.ko: 장군 장사귀 앞에 나가 당의 병적에 이름을 올린다. 서기는 설인귀라 적는다. 서기는 고개를 들지 않는다. 역사는 들 것이다.

blocks.hanja: 薛仁貴，絳州龍門人。貞觀末，太宗親征遼東，仁貴謁將軍張士貴應募，請從行。
blocks.ko: 설인귀는 강주 용문 사람이다. 정관 말에 태종*이 몸소 요동을 치니, 인귀가 장군 장사귀를 뵙고 응모하여 따라가기를 청하였다.
blocks.html: Xue Rengui was a man of Longmen in Jiangzhou. At the end of Zhenguan, Taizong* campaigned in person against Liaodong; Rengui presented himself to General Zhang Shigui, answered the muster, and asked to go.
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 83, biography of Xue Rengui

notes.html: Taizong is the temple name Tang gave him after death. In this book he is the Second Emperor.
notes.ko: 태종은 죽은 뒤 받은 묘호다. 이 책에서는 ‘두 번째 황제’다.

blocks.html: His weapon is the same one the storytellers later give to Lü Bu: the fangtian ji — crescent blade and spear-point on one shaft. In the Longmen shed it is a farmer’s choice. In the chronicle it becomes the shape you see before you see his face.
blocks.ko: 그의 무기는 훗날 이야기꾼들이 여포에게 쥐여 주는 것과 같다. 방천화극 — 초승달 날과 창끝이 한 자루에. 용문 헛간에서는 농부의 선택일 뿐이다. 이 연대기에서는, 얼굴보다 먼저 보이는 모양이 된다.

blocks.html: Later opera won’t leave Liu in the hut. It puts her in a cold kiln and gives her a fuller name the histories never wrote. And a song. Lovely song. Not history.
blocks.ko: 훗날의 경극은 유씨를 오두막에 두지 않는다. 차가운 가마 속에 앉히고, 사서가 적지 않은 긴 이름을 붙여 준다. 노래도 하나. 좋은 노래다. 역사는 아니다.

blocks.hanja: 兒夫投軍無音信，母子寒窯受苦情。
blocks.ko: 지아비는 종군하여 소식이 없고, 모자는 찬 가마에서 고통을 받는다.
blocks.html: My husband enlisted; there is no word. Mother and child suffer in a cold kiln.
blocks.source: Jingju Fenhewan (京劇《汾河灣》, also 仁貴打雁) — opening of Liu Yingchun; theatrical/folk, not the Tang official histories

blocks.html: By summer the yellow hemp is on a peg in Longmen, and the man who wore it is at Stallion Mountain, under the same Emperor who called him out of the field.
blocks.ko: 여름이 되면 노란 삼베는 용문의 못에 걸려 있고, 그것을 입었던 사내는 그를 밭에서 불러낸 바로 그 황제 아래, 주필산에 있다.

blocks.html: Yodong has never opened its gates to the West. Not for the Sui. Not in three summers. Here come the dragons…!
blocks.ko: 요동성은 서쪽에 문을 열어 준 적이 없다. 수나라에게도. 세 번의 여름 내내. 이제 용들이 온다…!

blocks.html: Goguryeo has spent fourteen years building a wall of forts along the river. The Blue Dragon simply walks around it. He shows his banners on the middle road, then turns north in the night. By morning his horse are across an unwatched ford. The first fortress shuts its gates. It holds exactly as long as the gates do.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 십사 년 동안 강을 따라 성의 벽을 쌓았다. 청룡은 그 벽을 그냥 돌아간다. 가운데 길에 깃발을 보여 주고, 밤에 북으로 꺾는다. 아침이 되자 그의 기병은 아무도 지키지 않던 여울을 건너 있다. 첫 성이 문을 닫는다. 딱 그 문이 버티는 만큼만 버틴다.

blocks.caption: Banners on the middle road, horses at the northern ford. Goguryeo watched the banners.
blocks.ko: 깃발은 가운데 길에, 말은 북쪽 여울에. 고구려는 깃발을 보고 있었다.

blocks.html: The New Fortress doesn’t fall. The emperor’s cousin spends ten days under its walls and leaves with nothing. So the Blue Dragon posts a guard on it and turns south. The next fort lasts a little over ten days. Seven hundred men Yeon sent to hold it are taken in the gate. They ask to serve the emperor instead.
blocks.ko: 신성은 무너지지 않는다. 황제의 사촌이 열흘을 성 아래 머물다 빈손으로 물러난다. 그래서 청룡은 신성에 감시병을 남기고 남으로 돈다. 다음 성은 열흘 남짓 버틴다. 연이 지키라고 보낸 칠백 명이 성문에서 붙잡힌다. 그들은 대신 황제를 섬기겠다고 청한다.

lines: 짐을 위해 싸우면, 막리지가 처자식을 다 죽일 게다.
한 사람의 힘을 얻자고 한 집안을 없애는 짓은 짐이 차마 못 하겠다. 돌려보내거라.
en: Their homes are all in Gasi, I am told.
If they fight for Us, the Mangniji will kill every wife and child they have.
To gain one man’s arm by wiping out his house — that We cannot bring Ourselves to do. Send them home.
zh: 若為朕而戰，莫離支必盡殺其妻子。
得一人之力而滅一家，朕不忍也。遣之歸。
zhLatn: Tīngshuō tāmen jiā dōu zài Jiāshī.
Ruò wèi zhèn ér zhàn, Mòlízhī bì jìn shā qí qīzǐ.
Dé yī rén zhī lì ér miè yī jiā, zhèn bùrěn yě. Qiǎn zhī guī.

blocks.html: They go home with grain for the road. It is a kindness, and it is also arithmetic: seven hundred men who have seen the size of this army will describe it to Gasi better than any envoy could.
blocks.ko: 그들은 길양식까지 받아 집으로 돌아간다. 자비이기도 하고 셈이기도 하다. 이 군대의 크기를 제 눈으로 본 칠백 명은 어떤 사신보다도 그것을 가시성에 잘 전할 것이다.

blocks.html: Between the army and the walls lies the Liao marsh. Two hundred li of mud. A Sui host once went in up to the knee and came out as a song. The emperor’s engineer lays a road of earth across it, wide enough for carts. When the last wagon is over, the emperor has the road torn up. Nobody goes home the way they came. He wants every man in the column to know it.
blocks.ko: 군대와 성벽 사이에 요하의 늪이 있다. 이백 리의 진흙. 수나라 대군이 무릎까지 빠져 들어갔다가 노래가 되어 나온 곳이다. 황제의 장인이 그 위에 수레가 다닐 만한 흙길을 깐다. 마지막 수레가 건너자 황제는 길을 걷어 내게 한다. 아무도 왔던 길로 돌아가지 못한다. 그는 대열의 모든 병사가 그걸 알기를 바란다.

blocks.html: Then the Eastern Fortress itself. It held off the last dynasty for three summers and never opened. The Blue Dragon has already driven one sortie back through the gate when the emperor arrives. He rides to the moat with a sack of earth across his saddle and throws it in. His officers can’t be seen carrying less than him. They carry two. The army rings the walls a hundred deep and beats the drums until the ground answers.
blocks.ko: 그리고 동쪽의 성, 그 자체. 지난 왕조를 세 번의 여름 동안 막아 내고 끝내 열리지 않은 성이다. 황제가 도착했을 때 청룡은 이미 한 번의 출격을 성문 안으로 밀어 넣은 뒤다. 황제는 안장에 흙 자루 하나를 얹고 해자 끝까지 달려가 그것을 던져 넣는다. 장수들은 황제보다 적게 나르는 모습을 보일 수 없다. 그래서 두 자루씩 나른다. 군대는 성을 백 겹으로 둘러싸고 땅이 대답할 때까지 북을 친다.

blocks.html: The gate the West keeps knocking on.
blocks.ko: 서쪽이 자꾸 두드리는 문.

blocks.html: Inside the walls there is a shrine to Jumong, the Holy King who founded the country. A coat of chain mail hangs in it, and a long sharp spear, and the town will tell you both came down from heaven in the days of the old Yan. By the eighth day stones are coming over the parapet. The elders choose a girl from the town, wash her, paint her, dress her in red silk and a bride’s crown, and walk her up to the shrine to be given to the god.
blocks.ko: 성안에는 나라를 세운 성왕 주몽의 사당이 있다. 사당에는 쇠사슬 갑옷 한 벌과 날 선 긴 창이 걸려 있는데, 성 사람들은 둘 다 옛 연나라 때 하늘에서 내려온 것이라고 말한다. 여드레째가 되자 성가퀴 너머로 돌이 날아든다. 어른들은 성안에서 처녀 하나를 골라 씻기고, 단장시키고, 붉은 비단과 신부의 관을 입혀, 신에게 바치러 사당으로 데려간다.

en: It’s… heavy. The dress.
…Tell my mum. Tell her I didn’t cry.
The Holy King… is smiling.
He has taken his bride! This city will stand whole!

blocks.html: They close the shrine door on her. The record does not say whether anyone opens it again.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아이를 들여보내고 사당 문을 닫는다. 그 문을 다시 연 사람이 있었는지, 기록은 말하지 않는다.

blocks.hanja: 城中有朱蒙祠，祠有鏁甲、銛矛，妄言前燕世天所降。方圍急，飾美女以婦神，巫言朱蒙悅，城必完。
blocks.html: In the city was a shrine to Jumong, and in the shrine a coat of chain mail and a sharp spear, which they falsely said had come down from heaven in the age of the Former Yan. When the siege grew desperate they adorned a beautiful woman as a wife for the god, and the shamans said: Jumong is pleased; the city will surely stand whole.
blocks.ko: 성안에 주몽의 사당이 있었는데, 사당에는 쇠사슬 갑옷과 날카로운 창이 있어, 전연 때 하늘에서 내려온 것이라고 망령되이 말하였다. 포위가 급해지자 미녀를 꾸며 신의 아내로 삼았고, 무당은 “주몽이 기뻐하니 성은 반드시 온전하리라” 하였다.
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197

blocks.html: The Holy King isn’t consulted again. The Blue Dragon’s throwers hurl rocks the size of grain jars over the walls. Towers roll up to the parapet. On the twelfth day a south wind rises. They fire the south-west tower, and the wind carries it into town. When the gate gives, the clerks count ten thousand dead, then lose interest and count the grain. The fortress a million men couldn’t open has lasted twelve days.
blocks.ko: 성왕께 다시 묻는 사람은 없다. 청룡의 포차가 독만 한 돌을 성벽 너머로 날린다. 공성탑이 성가퀴에 붙는다. 열이틀째 남풍이 인다. 그들이 서남쪽 망루에 불을 지르자 바람이 불길을 성안으로 실어 간다. 성문이 무너지자 서기들은 죽은 자를 만까지 세다가, 흥미를 잃고 곡식을 센다. 백만 대군이 열지 못한 성이 열이틀을 버텼다.

blocks.html: Veterans spit and say the real argument is still ahead: not this eastern gate, but Ansi, where stone has already outlasted more emperors than the court will admit over wine.
blocks.ko: 늙은 병사들은 침을 뱉으며 말한다. 진짜 논쟁은 아직 앞이다: 이 동쪽 문보다, 술자리에서 조정이 인정하는 것보다 더 많은 황제를 돌이 이겨 낸 안시.

blocks.html: Then the Second Emperor rides on to look at Ansi, and the man who holds it comes out onto the wall to look back. Nobody on the Tang side ever writes down his name.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나서 황제는 안시를 보러 말을 몬다. 안시를 지키는 사내가 성벽 위로 나와 그를 마주 본다. 당 쪽의 누구도 끝내 그의 이름을 적지 않는다.

blocks.caption: The man who holds Ansi. The other side never learns his name, and he never offers it.
blocks.ko: 안시를 지키는 사람. 저쪽은 끝내 그의 이름을 모르고, 그도 알려 주지 않는다.

lines: 역사에 자비 없는 학살자로 남을 것이다…!
영혼이 있는 사람들은 당신을 절대로 숭배 안 해…!
en: You will simply…
go down in history as a butcher without mercy…!
People with souls will never worship you…!

lines: 나는, 역사상 최고의 황제로 남게될 것이다.
en: History? I am the one writing it.
You will vanish, a nameless barbarian,
and I will remain the greatest emperor history has known.
To light up the civilised — and the savage—
that is my power.
zh: 而朕將永為史上最偉大之皇帝。
zhLatn: Lìshǐ? Xiě lìshǐ de shì zhèn.
Nǐ jiāng yānmiè, wúmíng mányí,
Ér zhèn jiāng yǒng wéi shǐshàng zuì wěidà zhī huángdì.
Zhào Huá、Yí——
Cǐ jí zhèn zhī lì.

lines: 짓밟고, 죽이고, 그 위에 올라서서 그걸 문명이라 부르는 거냐.
en: Civilised? You call this civilisation…?
You trample them, you kill them, and then you stand on the pile and call it civilisation.

blocks.label: The Rest of the Line
blocks.ko: 남은 성들

blocks.html: Meanwhile the rest of the line comes down like roof tiles. The clerks file it in a single column. At one fort Yeon’s riders break out and put a spear into the White Dragon’s waist. He has it bound and is back in the saddle by evening. The fort’s lord opens the gate anyway. Out on the southern cape, the fleet takes another in a month. Of all the forts Yeon spent fourteen years hauling stone for, two still fly Goguryeo’s banners.
blocks.ko: 그 사이 나머지 성들은 기왓장처럼 떨어진다. 서기들은 그것을 한 줄로 철해 둔다. 한 성에서는 연의 기병이 뛰쳐나가 흰 용의 허리에 창을 꽂는다. 흰 용은 상처를 동여매고 저녁이면 다시 안장에 올라 있다. 성주는 어쨌든 문을 연다. 남쪽 곶에서는 수군이 한 달 만에 성 하나를 더 빼앗는다. 연이 십사 년 동안 돌을 날라 쌓은 성들 가운데 아직 고구려 깃발을 단 곳은 둘뿐이다.

blocks.title: The rest of the line
blocks.caption: A spear in the White Dragon, a fleet on the cape. The tiles keep falling anyway.
blocks.ko: 흰 용의 허리에 창 하나, 곶에는 함대 하나. 기왓장은 그래도 계속 떨어진다.

head: Fortress 城
Month
Fate
rows: Falls in ten days; 700 Gasi men sent home

blocks.html: Goguryeo has been here before. To learn what one bad afternoon can cost a king, we go back four hundred years…!
blocks.ko: 고구려는 전에도 이런 적이 있다. 나쁜 오후 한 번이 왕에게 얼마를 치르게 하는지 알려면, 사백 년을 거슬러 가야 한다…!

blocks.html: King Dongchun picks a fight over a diplomatic spat. The war that comes back at him starts on a river named for boiling.
blocks.ko: 동천왕은 외교 시비 하나로 싸움을 건다. 되돌아온 전쟁은 ‘끓는 강’이라는 이름의 강에서 시작된다.

blocks.caption: A king who starts a war over a letter. This time, someone writes back.
blocks.ko: 편지 한 장으로 싸움을 거는 임금. 이번엔 답장이 온다.

blocks.html: The spat is this: Goguryeo raided the western commandery, the empire sent a general called Guanqiu Jian to explain why that was a mistake, and Goguryeo met him at the Boiling River and won, and then won again.
blocks.ko: 다툼의 내막은 이렇다. 고구려가 서쪽 군현을 쳤고, 제국은 그것이 왜 실수인지 설명하려 관구검이라는 장수를 보냈으며, 고구려는 비류수에서 그를 맞아 이겼고, 한 번 더 이겼다.

blocks.html: So the king took five thousand horse out to win a third time, on ground he had not looked at, and lost eighteen thousand men in an afternoon.
blocks.ko: 그래서 임금은 기병 오천을 이끌고 세 번째로 이기러 나갔다. 살펴본 적 없는 땅에서. 그리고 하루 오후에 만팔천을 잃었다.

en: …I did not look at the ground.

blocks.html: Hwando is burned. The king runs east with a handful of men and is saved by a single officer who dresses in the royal robes and walks out to be killed in his place.
blocks.ko: 환도성이 불탄다. 임금은 몇 사람만 데리고 동으로 달아나고, 왕의 옷을 입고 걸어 나가 대신 죽은 장수 하나 덕에 목숨을 건진다.

blocks.html: A mountain capital, built for the day the plain is lost.
blocks.ko: 들판을 잃는 날을 위해 지은 산 위의 수도.

blocks.html: The king said to his generals: “Wei’s great army is worse than our small one. Guanqiu Jian is Wei’s famous general, and today his life is in the palm of my hand.” He took five thousand armoured horse and advanced to strike. Guanqiu Jian formed a square and fought to the death; our army broke completely, and more than eighteen thousand died.
blocks.ko: 왕이 여러 장수에게 말하였다. “위의 큰 군대가 도리어 우리의 작은 군대만 못하다. 관구검은 위의 이름난 장수이나, 오늘 그 목숨이 내 손아귀에 있구나.” 이에 철기 5천을 거느리고 나아가 쳤다. 관구검이 방진을 치고 죽기로 싸우니, 우리 군사가 크게 무너져 죽은 자가 1만 8천여 명이었다.
blocks.hanja: 王謂諸將曰：「魏之大兵，反不如我之小兵。毋丘儉者魏之名將，今日命在我掌握之中乎。」乃領鐵騎五千，進而擊之。儉為方陣，決死而戰，我軍大潰，死者一萬八千餘人。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 17, Goguryeo Annals — King Dongcheon, yr. 20 (246), 8th month

blocks.html: Gung, king of Goguryeo, led twenty thousand foot and horse up to the Boiling River and gave battle at Liangkou; Gung was beaten again and again and fled. Guanqiu Jian then bound up his horses and roped up his carts to climb to Hwando, put the Goguryeo capital to the sword, and took heads and captives by the thousand.
blocks.ko: 구려 왕 궁이 보병과 기병 2만을 거느리고 비류수 가로 진군하여 양구에서 크게 싸웠으나, 궁은 잇달아 패하여 달아났다. 관구검은 마침내 말을 묶고 수레를 매달아 환도에 올라 구려의 도읍을 도륙하니, 베고 사로잡은 자가 천으로 헤아려졌다.
blocks.hanja: 句驪王宮將步騎二萬人，進軍沸流水上，大戰梁口，宮連破走。儉遂束馬縣車，以登丸都，屠句驪所都，斬獲首虜以千數。
blocks.source: Sanguo Zhi (三國志) bk. 28, Biography of Guanqiu Jian (毌丘儉傳), Zhengshi era (c. 244)

blocks.html: Goguryeo takes forty years to be a kingdom again. It is the first time in this story that a Samhan capital burns because of one bad afternoon, and it is not the last, and every king in this record has heard about it.
blocks.ko: 고구려가 다시 나라 꼴을 갖추는 데 사십 년이 걸린다. 이 이야기에서 하루 오후의 잘못으로 삼한의 도성이 불탄 첫 번째 일이고, 마지막은 아니며, 이 기록의 모든 임금이 그 이야기를 들어 알고 있다.

blocks.html: Four hundred years later, another Goguryeo army marches to meet an emperor in the open. In the Tang line, a farmer puts on white…!
blocks.ko: 사백 년 뒤, 또 한 고구려 군대가 들판에서 황제를 맞으러 나선다. 당나라 진영에서는 한 농부가 흰 갑옷을 입는 중이다…!
