images.alt: Caravaggio’s Calling of St Matthew: the Emperor points out of the dark at the kneeling farmer in white
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Caravaggio’s Calling of Saint Matthew. Inside the Emperor’s dark campaign pavilion at dusk: from the right, in shadow, the Second Emperor stretches out his arm and points across the frame; Li Shiji at his shoulder. Left, Xue Rengui kneels on one knee in dirt-streaked white armour, looking up, the fangtian ji upright in his fist, its crescent blade wet and glistening. A single hard shaft of low sun slants in through the open tent flap above the Emperor’s pointing hand and lands on Xue’s face and the ji; the rest of the pavilion is black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — XUE RENGUI — FACE and garments from attached /ch_xue_rengui.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Tang's white-robed champion; showman of the charge. Carry: Fangtian ji halberd — no ring sword at all. #e8e3d5 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: ring-pommel sword. | THE SECOND EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_taizong.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Bearded Tang emperor: black futou cap with an upright pin, thick black beard and moustache, fierce scowl. Dress: Imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade. Demeanor: Commands; never asks. Conqueror's contempt that curdles at Ansi. Presence: THE SON OF HEAVEN — every frame he is in bends around him. He is SHROUDED IN DARKNESS: the black of the hall gathers around him like a mantle. One close practical light (a lamp, a brazier, a lamp-tree) rakes across him from below or from the side and SCULPTS him — the heavy yellow silk breaks into deep protruding folds brushed in loaded oil strokes that follow each fold, gold thread flicked in with impasto, the beard and cheekbones carved — and then falls off into black across his body and half his face; that falloff is the darkness, never a flat backlit silhouette. The camera sits BELOW his eyeline (low angle or worm’s-eye) and he is always placed HIGHER than anyone near him — on the dais, on a step, standing while others kneel or sit. He reads larger than life through lens and staging, not as a giant: broad shoulders, the robe spreading wide and heavy into the dark like a mountain, his shadow enormous on walls and floor. Unhurried, heavy stillness — never fidgeting, never casual, never a colleague at someone’s shoulder; when he smiles or laughs it is a predator’s ease, and the room goes quiet around it. Everyone else in frame is smaller, lower, less lit, turned toward him. The aura is darkness, scale and the hush around him — never a glow, never a halo, never rays behind his head. #c97a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Korean ring-pommel sword; Korean lamellar. | BLUE DRAGON — FACE and garments from attached /ch_blue_dragon.png (face only; invent a new pose). #4b78c9 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: By summer the farmer from Longmen is no longer a name on a muster roll. He is at Stallion Mountain, under the same Emperor who called him out of the yellow hemp.
blocks.ko: 여름이 되면 용문의 농부는 더 이상 병적의 이름 하나가 아니다. 노란 삼베에서 그를 불러낸 바로 그 황제 아래, 주필산에 있다.

blocks.html: Named for where an emperor stopped. Emperors name a lot of things.
blocks.ko: 황제가 멈춰 선 자리라 붙은 이름. 황제들은 이름 붙이길 좋아한다.

blocks.caption: Goguryeo sends a hundred and fifty thousand down the crow road. The emperor sends himself.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 까마귀 길로 십오만을 내려보낸다. 황제는 자기 자신을 보낸다.

blocks.html: At Stallion Mountain the Second Emperor does not wait behind the line.
blocks.ko: 주필산에서 황제는 진 뒤에서 기다리지 않는다.

en: I myself am the vanguard…!
zhLatn: Zhèn jí shì xiānfēng…!

blocks.html: Goguryeo sends a relief army — Go Yeonsu and Go Hyejin, tens of thousands under banners that think numbers are an argument.
blocks.ko: 고구려가 구원군을 보낸다 — 고연수와 고혜진, 머릿수가 논증이라 믿는 깃발 아래의 수만.

blocks.html: In the Tang line stands a guard captain whose accent still has the sea in it. Sul Gedu left Silla twenty-four winters ago, in the hold of a merchant ship. When the emperor called for volunteers, he put his own name down. It’s the only way a foreigner gets a captain’s sash. Across the field, the enemy’s banners are close enough to read.
blocks.ko: 당나라 진영의 근위 대장들 사이에, 말투에 아직 바다가 묻어 있는 사내가 하나 있다. 설계두는 스물네 해 전 상선 짐칸에 숨어 신라를 떠났다. 황제가 지원자를 부르자 그는 제 이름을 써넣었다. 이방인이 대장의 띠를 받는 길은 그것뿐이다. 들판 건너편, 적의 깃발이 글자가 읽힐 만큼 가깝다.

lines: 어이, 설 과의. 저쪽 놈들 말이오… 삼한 사람들이라던데.
en: Hey, Captain Xue. That lot over there… they say they’re Samhan men.
Aren’t you from Samhan as well?
zh: 喂，薛果毅。對面那些人……聽說是三韓人。
zhLatn: Wèi, Xuē guǒyì. Duìmiàn nàxiē rén… tīngshuō shì Sānhán rén.
Nǐ bù yě shì Sānhán lái de ma?

lines: 신라에선 사람 쓸 때 뼈부터 따져. 재주가 아무리 크고 공이 아무리 커도, 뼈가 아니면 못 넘어. 그냥 못 넘어.
그래서 바다 건너왔지. 천자 곁에서 관 쓰고 띠 두르고 칼 차고 드나들어 보려고.
en: Samhan. Silla.
In Silla they count your bones before they hire you. Doesn’t matter how big your talent is or how big your deeds — wrong bones, and you don’t get over the wall. You just don’t.
So I crossed the sea. To walk in and out at the Son of Heaven’s side with a cap and a sash and a sword.
…That’ll do me.
zh: 新羅用人，先論骨頭。才再大、功再高，骨頭不對，就是過不去。就是過不去。
所以我渡海來了。想在天子身邊，戴冠束帶、佩劍出入。
zhLatn: Sānhán. Xīnluó.
Xīnluó yòng rén, xiān lùn gǔtou. Cái zài dà, gōng zài gāo, gǔtou bú duì, jiùshì guò bú qù. Jiùshì guò bú qù.
Suǒyǐ wǒ dù hǎi lái le. Xiǎng zài tiānzǐ shēnbiān, dài guān shù dài, pèi jiàn chūrù.
……Zhè jiù gòu le.

blocks.html: The soldier laughs, not sure he was meant to. Sul Gedu ties off his helmet cord and does not look at the banners again.
blocks.ko: 병사는 웃어도 되는 건지 모른 채 웃는다. 설계두는 투구 끈을 묶고, 다시는 그 깃발 쪽을 보지 않는다.

blocks.html: In the Tang line a low officer decides the field needs a mark it cannot look away from. He puts on white armour — not for mourning, for visibility — hangs two bows at his waist, takes up the fangtian ji, and rides into the front so hard the relief army has to notice him or die without knowing why.
blocks.ko: 당진의 낮은 장교 하나가, 이 벌판에 눈을 떼지 못할 표식이 필요하다고 판단한다. 흰 갑옷을 입는다 — 상중이 아니라, 보이려고 — 허리에 활 둘을 차고 방천화극을 들어, 구원군이 알아채거나 모른 채 죽게 되도록 선두로 달린다.

en: Make a path.
If you will not — the ji will.
zhLatn: Ràng lù.
Ruò bù ràng——jǐ zì huì ràng.

blocks.html: No one in the Goguryeo line stops him for long, and the Tang officers, seeing the white coat cut a road, pour in after it. The formation breaks. The mountain learns a new colour.
blocks.ko: 고구려 진에서 그를 오래 막는 자는 없고, 흰옷이 길을 내는 것을 본 당의 장교들이 그 길로 쏟아져 들어온다. 진형이 무너진다. 산이 새 색깔을 배운다.

blocks.html: Just then came thunder and lightning. Xue Rengui, a man of Longmen, in strange clothing, broke into the enemy line with a great shout, and nothing could stand before him. The Goguryeo troops gave way; the main army followed through, and the Goguryeo troops broke completely…
blocks.ko: 마침 천둥과 번개가 쳤는데, 용문 사람 설인귀가 기이한 옷을 입고 크게 소리치며 적진을 무너뜨리니 향하는 곳마다 대적할 자가 없었다. 고구려 군사가 쓰러지듯 흩어지자 대군이 그 틈을 타니, 고구려 군사가 크게 무너졌다…
blocks.hanja: 會有雷電，龍門人薛仁貴著奇服，大呼陷陳，所向無敵；高麗兵披靡，大軍乘之，高麗兵大潰…
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 198, Tang Zhenguan 19 (645), 6th month

blocks.html: Just then came thunder and lightning. Xue Rengui, a man of Longmen, in strange clothing, broke into the line with a great shout, and nothing could stand before him; our army gave way. The main army followed through, and our army broke completely…
blocks.ko: 마침 천둥과 번개가 쳤는데, 용문 사람 설인귀가 기이한 옷을 입고 크게 소리치며 진을 무너뜨리니, 향하는 곳마다 대적할 자가 없어 우리 군사가 쓰러지듯 흩어졌다. 대군이 그 틈을 타니 우리 군사가 크게 무너졌다…
blocks.hanja: 會，有雷電，龍門人薛仁貴，著奇服，大呼陷陣，所向無敵，我軍披靡。大軍乘之，我軍大潰…
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 21, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 4 (645)

en: Who is that man in white armour.
The one at the tip of the spear.
zhLatn: Nà báijiǎ shì hérén.
Máojiān nà hànzi.

en: Xue Rengui, Your Majesty.
A soldier… who was a farmer.
zhLatn: Xuē Rénguì, Bìxià.
Yī jiè… céng wéi nóngfū zhī bīng.

blocks.html: They bring him up. Dirt on the white. Blood on the crescent of the ji. He kneels like a man who has never been in a palace and does not intend to apologise for it.
blocks.ko: 그를 앞으로 불러낸다. 흰옷에 흙. 극의 초승달에 피. 그는 궁에 들어와 본 적 없는 사람처럼 무릎을 꿇고, 그걸 사과할 생각은 없어 보인다.

lines: 변경의 일을 맡길 날랜 장수를 고르려 하거늘 — 경만 한 자가 없도다.
짐은 요동을 얻은 것보다, 경을 얻은 것이 더 기쁘다.
en: My old generals are all aged.
I have been looking for a fierce one to entrust the frontier to — and I find none better than you.
I am less happy about gaining Liaodong than about gaining you.
zh: 欲擇猛將托邊事——無有過於卿者。
朕得遼東之喜，不及得卿。
zhLatn: Zhèn jiùjiàng jiē lǎo yǐ.
Yù zé měngjiàng tuō biānshì——wú yǒu guòyú qīng zhě.
Zhèn dé Liáodōng zhī xǐ, bùjí dé qīng.

lines: 다만 이 극이, 폐하의 길을 조금 넓혀 드렸을 뿐입니다.
en: A farmer… how could he dare.
This ji only widened Your Majesty’s road a little.
zh: 此戟不過略開陛下之路罷了。
zhLatn: Nóngfū… ān gǎn.
Cǐ jǐ bùguò lüè kāi Bìxià zhī lù bàle.

blocks.html: They give him gold, silk, a general’s title, and a place among the men who stand at the northern gate. The white coat stays. So does the ji.
blocks.ko: 금과 비단과 장군의 호와, 북문을 지키는 자리까지 내린다. 흰옷은 남는다. 극도 남는다.

blocks.html: When the dust settles, the two relief commanders walk into the Tang camp and surrender. Thirty-six thousand men walk in behind them. The officers are sent inland, to be subjects far from any border. The common soldiers are sent home. The three thousand Mohe riders who came south with them are marched into a valley and buried alive.
blocks.ko: 먼지가 가라앉자 구원군의 두 장수가 당나라 진영으로 걸어 들어가 항복한다. 그 뒤로 삼만 육천 명이 따라 들어온다. 장교들은 국경에서 먼 내지로 보내져 당의 백성이 된다. 병졸들은 집으로 돌려보내진다. 그들과 함께 남하한 말갈 기병 삼천은 골짜기로 끌려가 산 채로 묻힌다.

blocks.html: Go Yeonsu does not live out the year. The records say he died of grief, which is the only cause of death the Tang ever let a surrendered general keep.
blocks.ko: 고연수는 그해를 넘기지 못한다. 기록은 그가 울화로 죽었다고 적는다. 항복한 장수에게 당이 남겨 준 사인은 그것 하나뿐이다.

blocks.html: There is another foreigner in the reckoning that night. Riding over the ground where the Goguryeo centre stood, the emperor finds Sul Gedu farther in than any of his own men got, face down among the dead he made.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 공을 헤아리는 자리에는 이방인이 하나 더 있다. 고구려 중군이 서 있던 땅을 말을 타고 지나던 황제는, 자기 군사 누구보다 깊이 들어간 자리에서, 제가 쓰러뜨린 시신들 사이에 엎어져 있는 설계두를 찾는다.

blocks.hanja: 至遼東，與麗人戰駐蹕山下，深入疾鬪而死，功一等。皇帝問是何許人，左右奏新羅人薛罽頭也。皇帝泫然曰：「吾人尙畏死，顧望不前，而外國人爲吾死事，何以報其功乎？」問從者，聞其平生之願，脫御衣覆之，授職爲大將軍，以禮葬之。
blocks.html: Reaching Liaodong, he fought the men of Goguryeo below Stallion Mountain; he went deep, fought hard and died, and his merit was ranked first. The emperor asked what manner of man he was, and those about him reported that he was Xue Jitou, a man of Silla. The emperor wept and said: “Our own men still fear death and look about them and will not advance, yet a man of a foreign country has died in Our cause. How shall We repay his merit?” He asked the man’s companions and learned the wish of his life; he took off the imperial robe and covered him with it, granted him the office of Grand General, and buried him with full rites.
blocks.ko: 요동에 이르러 주필산 아래에서 고구려 사람들과 싸웠는데, 깊이 들어가 맹렬히 싸우다 죽으니 공이 일등이었다. 황제가 어떤 사람이냐고 묻자, 좌우가 신라 사람 설계두라고 아뢰었다. 황제가 눈물을 흘리며 말하였다. “우리 사람들도 오히려 죽음을 두려워하여 두리번거리며 나아가지 않는데, 외국 사람이 우리를 위하여 죽었으니 무엇으로 그 공을 갚겠는가?” 따르던 자에게 물어 그의 평생 소원을 듣고는, 어의를 벗어 덮어 주고 대장군의 직을 내려 예로써 장사 지냈다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies 7, Seol Gyedu

blocks.html: The cap, the sash and the sword, more or less. He gets them lying down.
blocks.ko: 관과 띠와 칼, 대강 그것이다. 그는 그것을 누워서 받는다.

blocks.html: Fame is a short leash. Before the army even settles into the Ansi siege, Goguryeo stops trying to kill the man in white in the open and starts trying to keep him.
blocks.ko: 명성은 짧은 밧줄이다. 군이 안시 포위에 자리를 잡기도 전에, 고구려는 흰옷의 사내를 벌판에서 죽이려 하기보다 가두려 한다.

blocks.html: They take him in a night fight east of the Liao — nets, numbers, the ji knocked from his hands — and drag him inland to a lesser fortress that is not Ansi and does not want to be famous. Iron on the wrists. A cell under the wall. The white coat cut off him like a trophy.
blocks.ko: 요하 동쪽의 밤싸움에서 그를 잡는다 — 그물, 머릿수, 손에서 떨어진 극 — 그리고 안시가 아닌, 유명해지고 싶지 않은 작은 성으로 끌고 간다. 손목의 쇠. 성벽 아래 감방. 하얀 옷은 전리품처럼 벗겨진다.

en: …The ji.
Where is the ji.
zhLatn: …Jǐ.
Jǐ zài héchù.

blocks.html: They laugh. A farmer asking for his farming tool.
blocks.ko: 그들은 웃는다. 농사 연장을 찾는 농부라고.

blocks.html: Then a runner comes up the stair, out of breath.
blocks.ko: 그러다 급보가 숨을 헐떡이며 층계를 올라온다.

lines: 오늘 밤, 이 성에. 성왕이시여, 굽어살피소서.
en: The Second Emperor… is coming this way.
Tonight. To this fortress. Holy King, look down.

blocks.html: Xue Rengui hears it the way a chained animal hears the key.
blocks.ko: 설인귀는 그 말을, 묶인 짐승이 열쇠 소리를 듣듯 듣는다.

en: …Before His Majesty arrives.
I will have to be out.
zhLatn: …Bìxià jiàdào zhī qián.
Wǒ děi chūqù.

blocks.html: He breaks the irons. He breaks the door. The white coat only made him easy to see.
blocks.ko: 쇠사슬을 부순다. 문을 부순다. 하얀 옷은 그를 보이게만 했을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: He finds the ji on a rack in the yard, still sticky from someone else’s hands, and takes the wall the way water takes a crack. By the time the Second Emperor’s banners show on the ridge, the cell is empty and the fortress is explaining itself to no one.
blocks.ko: 마당 시렁에서 남의 손이 묻은 극을 찾아 들고, 물이 틈을 찾듯 성벽을 넘는다. 황제의 깃발이 능선에 보일 즈음, 감방은 비어 있고 성은 아무에게도 설명을 하지 못한다.

en: …That white coat again.
Arriving before Us, I see.
zhLatn: …Yòu shì nà shēn báiyī.
Jìng bǐ zhèn xiān dào.

lines: 폐하를 오래 기다리게 할 수 없었습니다.
en: I could not keep Your Majesty waiting.
The chains… were impolite.
zhLatn: Bù gǎn ràng Bìxià jiǔ hòu.
Nàxiē suǒliàn… tài wúlǐ le.

blocks.html: The Second Emperor laughs once — short, relieved — and does not ask how. A sovereign who has to ask how has already lost the man.
blocks.ko: 황제는 짧게, 안도하며 한 번 웃고, 어떻게 했는지는 묻지 않는다. 어떻게를 물어야 하는 군주는 이미 그 사내를 잃은 것이다.

blocks.html: Among the prisoners taken at the mountain are two boys, eleven and eight, sent south with the baggage train by a father who thought the rear was safer.
blocks.ko: 주필산에서 잡힌 포로 중에는 열한 살과 여덟 살 난 사내아이 둘이 있었다. 후방이 더 안전하리라 여긴 아버지가 치중대와 함께 남쪽으로 보낸 아이들이었다.

lines: 너희 아비는 임금을 죽였다. 짐은 형제를 죽였고.
en: So. Gai Suwen’s sons.
Your father killed his king. I killed my brothers.
So you see, he and I understand one another.
zh: 如此，朕與他倒有相通之處。
zhLatn: Yuánlái shì Gàisūwén zhī zǐ.
Ěr fù shā jūn. Zhèn shā xiōngdì.
Rúcǐ, zhèn yǔ tā dào yǒu xiāngtōng zhī chù.

lines: 무릎을 꿇고 대당의 신하가 되겠다 하면, 둘 다 관작을 주마.
장안의 집, 비단, 이름. 고려에서는 평생 못 가질 것들이다.
en: Here is my offer.
Kneel, call yourselves servants of the Great Tang, and I will give you both titles.
A house in Chang’an, silk, a name. Things Goryeo will never give you.
zh: 跪稱大唐臣子，朕賜爾二人官爵。
長安宅第、絲綢、名號。高麗永不能予者。
zhLatn: Zhèn yǒu yī yì.
Guì chēng Dà Táng chénzǐ, zhèn cì ěr èr rén guānjué.
Cháng'ān zháidì、sīchóu、mínghào. Gāolí yǒng bùnéng yǔ zhě.

en: Brother.

blocks.html: Namseng is eleven. He works out, quite quickly, that the Second Emperor wants two and will settle for one, and that only one of them has to be the one who refuses.
blocks.ko: 남생은 열한 살이다. 그는 꽤 빠르게 계산해 낸다. 황제는 둘을 원하지만 하나로도 만족할 것이고, 거절하는 역할은 둘 중 하나만 맡으면 된다는 것을.

lines: 폐하. 제 아우는 어립니다. 아무것도 모릅니다.
거절하는 건 접니다. 벌은 저에게 주십시오.
en: Your Majesty. My brother is small. He understands nothing.
It is I who refuse. Give the punishment to me.
…You are the elder?
zhLatn: …Nǐ shì xiōngzhǎng?

en: I am.

blocks.html: They flog him in front of his brother and send them both back across the Liao in the spring, as a gesture. Namgun does not speak for the whole journey.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아우가 보는 앞에서 그를 매질했고, 봄이 되자 아량이라며 둘 다 요하 너머로 돌려보냈다. 남건은 돌아오는 내내 한마디도 하지 않았다.

en: You took it for me.
I am the elder.

blocks.html: The Second Emperor isn't the first emperor to come for Goguryeo. The last one met a general who surrendered seven times…!
blocks.ko: 고구려를 노린 황제는 그가 처음이 아니다. 앞선 황제는 일곱 번이나 항복하는 장수를 만났다…!

images.alt: Emperor Yang of Sui's vast host marches on Goguryeo in 612
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of salsu flashback, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (612), scene: Great River, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: Emperor Yang of Sui invades Goguryeo in the year 612.
images.alt: The endless Sui host crosses the Liao on pontoon bridges while Ulchi Munduk watches from a ridge
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE battle frame. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. The Battle of the Colossal River (Salsu), summer 612: a broad shallow river over pale gravel bars between low pine hills in northern Goguryeo. Sui banners are dull gold and black, Goguryeo banners red, their marks illegible brush strokes. The Sui host crossing the Liao River on three long pontoon bridges: a sea of spears and gold-and-black banners under towering dust clouds lit orange by the low sun, columns stretching to the horizon. In the dark foreground on a pine ridge, Ulchi Munduk on horseback, small, watching. Device: the three bridges as long diagonals across the water. HEEWON BATTLE STYLE — this is a battle frame, and every still of this battle shares ONE look so the set plays as one film. Copy the BRUSHWORK AND STYLIZATION of the two attached style_battle boards ONLY — never their ships, flags, figures or composition (the painted board shows 19th-century steam and sailing ships; this battle is 7th-century East Asia). The look is the background art of a hand-painted 2D animated epic crossed with an East Asian woodblock battle scroll. SMOKE AND CLOUD are the big shapes: towering sculpted columns and rolling banks painted as broad soft gouache masses, lit warm orange from the fires underneath and cooling to slate and charcoal at the top; where they curl they break into stylised scroll-cloud spirals outlined in thin ink, like a painted screen. WATER is Hokusai: heavy slate-teal swells with claw-like cream-white foam crests drawn in ink line, spray as stippled dots. blocks.html: Emperor Yang of Sui invades Goguryeo in the year 612.
blocks.ko: 서기 612년, 수 양제가 고구려를 침공한다.

blocks.title: Edict for the Liao campaign
blocks.hanja: 而高麗小醜，迷昏不恭，崇聚勃、碣之間，荐食遼、獩之境。……此而可忍，孰不可容！……於是親總六師，用申九伐，拯厥阽危，協從天意，殄茲逋穢，克嗣先謨。
blocks.html: And Goguryeo, that petty villain, sits lost in its own fog and shows no respect. It herds itself together between the Bo and the Jie and keeps eating into the lands of Liao and Ye. … If this can be borne, what cannot? … So We take the six armies in hand Ourselves and carry out the ninefold punishment: to pull the endangered back from the edge, to follow the will of Heaven, to wipe out this runaway filth, and to finish what Our fathers planned.
blocks.ko: 그런데 고구려라는 하찮은 무리가 어둡고 미혹하여 공손하지 않다. 발해와 갈석 사이에 무리를 모으고, 요동과 예의 땅을 거듭 갉아먹는다. …… 이것을 참는다면 무엇인들 참지 못하랴! …… 이에 짐이 몸소 여섯 군대를 거느리고 아홉 가지 정벌을 펴, 위태로운 이들을 건지고, 하늘의 뜻을 따르며, 이 도망친 더러운 무리를 없애고, 선대의 계획을 잇고자 한다.
blocks.source: Sui Shu (隋書) bk. 4, Annals of Emperor Yang (煬帝下), Daye 8 (612), first month

blocks.caption: Nine armies over the Liao, a fleet up the Taedong. The Sui planned everything except the walk home.
blocks.ko: 요하를 건너는 아홉 군단, 대동강을 오르는 함대. 수나라는 돌아가는 길만 빼고 다 계획했다.

blocks.html: On the Colossal River, Ulchi Munduk breaks the Western Army. A century later, men will still point at other rivers and hope for the same appetite.
blocks.ko: 대하에서 을지문덕이 서쪽 군대를 꺾는다. 백 년 뒤에도 사람들은 다른 강을 가리키며 같은 식욕을 바란다.

blocks.html: Ask a Goguryeo grandfather. He will raise a cup first.
blocks.ko: 고구려 할아버지에게 물어보라. 잔부터 들 것이다.

blocks.html: Munduk walks into the enemy camp himself first, to look at them. He surrenders seven times on the way south and runs seven times, and each running pulls the Western army further from its supply and closer to a river.
blocks.ko: 문덕은 먼저 제 발로 적진에 걸어 들어가 그들을 살펴본다. 남으로 내려오며 일곱 번 항복하고 일곱 번 달아난다. 그 달아남마다 서토의 군대는 보급에서 멀어지고 강에는 가까워진다.

blocks.title: The walk home
blocks.caption: They marched to within thirty li of Pyongyang. Munduk had been counting on exactly that.
blocks.ko: 평양 삼십 리 앞까지 왔다. 을지문덕이 바란 게 바로 그거였다.

blocks.title: The Salsu, 612
blocks.note: Of 305,000 who crossed the Liao, the record says 2,700 came back.

blocks.title: Poem sent to the Sui general
blocks.hanja:
神策究天文
妙算窮地理
戰勝功旣高
知足願云止
blocks.html:
Your godlike strategy has searched out the patterns of heaven;
your wondrous reckoning has mastered the lie of the land.
Your victories have already won you high merit —
know it is enough, and I pray you stop.
blocks.ko:
그대의 귀신 같은 계책은 하늘의 이치를 다 헤아렸고
신묘한 계산은 땅의 이치를 통달했다
전쟁에 이겨 쌓은 공이 이미 높으니
만족함을 알고 그치기를 바라노라
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 44, Biographies — Eulji Mundeok

blocks.html: Munduk is honored with the title “The Defender” after the battle.
blocks.ko: 문덕은 전투 후 «수호신»이라는 칭호를 받는다.

blocks.html: Autumn, seventh month: they reached the Salsu. When the army was halfway across, our troops struck its rearguard from behind, and General Xin Shixiong of the Right Garrison fell fighting. At that all the armies broke, and nothing could stop them.
blocks.ko: 가을 7월, 살수에 이르러 군사가 반쯤 건넜을 때, 우리 군사가 뒤에서 그 후군을 치니 우둔위장군 신세웅이 싸우다 죽었다. 이에 여러 군대가 모두 무너져 막을 수가 없었다.
blocks.hanja: 秋七月，至薩水，軍半濟，我軍自後擊其後軍，右屯衛將軍辛世雄戰死。於是，諸軍俱潰，不可禁止。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 20, Goguryeo Annals — King Yeongyang, yr. 23 (612)

blocks.html: When the nine armies crossed the Liao there were three hundred and five thousand of them. When they got back to the Liaodong fortress there were two thousand seven hundred. Stores and weapons by the tens of thousands were lost, every one.
blocks.ko: 처음 아홉 군대가 요수를 건넌 것이 모두 30만 5천이었는데, 요동성으로 돌아온 것은 겨우 2천 7백 명이었다. 수만을 헤아리던 군량과 기계도 모두 잃어버렸다.
blocks.hanja: 初，九軍渡遼，凡三十萬五千，及還至遼東城，唯二千七百人，資儲器械巨萬計，失亡蕩盡。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 181, Sui Daye 8 (612), 7th month

blocks.html: Yodong fell. The forts fell. One wall is left, held by a madman whose name nobody wrote down…!
blocks.ko: 요동이 무너졌다. 성들이 무너졌다. 남은 성벽은 하나. 그 성을 지키는 미치광이의 이름은 아무도 적어 두지 않았다…!

blocks.html: The Guardian of Ansi Fortress is an eccentric man. When Yeon took the country, the Guardian refused him to his face. He kept the old king’s colours on the wall. Yeon had drowned a whole court for less. He looked at that wall, weighed the siege, and rode away. Ansi answers to no one.
blocks.ko: 안시성의 성주는 괴짜다. 연이 나라를 쥐었을 때, 성주는 그의 면전에서 복종을 거부했다. 성벽 위에는 옛 왕의 깃발을 그대로 두었다. 연은 그보다 못한 일로 조정 하나를 물에 잠기게 한 사내다. 그는 그 성벽을 바라보고, 공성의 값을 셈해 본 뒤, 말머리를 돌렸다. 안시는 누구의 명도 받지 않는다.

blocks.html: One small fortress, and one stubborn man on top of it.
blocks.ko: 작은 성 하나, 그 위에 고집 센 사내 하나.

blocks.html: Nobody writes his name down. To the people inside the walls he is just the chief, and that turns out to be enough.
blocks.ko: 누구도 그의 이름을 적어 두지 않았다. 성 안 사람들에게 그는 그저 성주였고, 결국 그것으로 충분했다.

blocks.caption: The emperor wants Pyongyang. One small fortress is in the way.
blocks.ko: 황제는 평양을 원한다. 작은 성 하나가 길을 막고 있다.

en: They will not give us his name. Only the Wall that Stopped an Emperor — as if a wall could have a pulse.
lines: 이름을 안 주더군. 황제를 막은 성벽이라니 — 벽에도 맥박이 있기라도 한 것처럼.
blocks.speaker: Tang supply clerk
blocks.art: Reaction panels: two Tang supply clerks at a tally table in the siege camp, under breath.

en: And they say the Eternal General is standing behind him.
Just put it down in the books as “unfinished.”
lines: 그 뒤엔 영원의 대장군이 버티고 있다더라.
blocks.speaker: Another clerk
blocks.art: Reaction panel: the second clerk, at the next table.

en: Ansi… so that man is still alive.
He dares refuse the Supreme Commander’s order?
I have heard that a true man needs only
one person to cherish,
and one person to serve,
and that is enough.

blocks.html: The ring at his hip is Goguryeo iron — a hollow circle the same red as the wall.
blocks.ko: 허리의 환두는 고구려 쇠다. 빈 고리. 성벽과 같은 붉은빛.
blocks.art: Wordless.

blocks.html: Six hundred li to the south, a Silla marshal had said something close to the same thing, to a queen, on the day she was crowned. Neither man will ever learn of the other.
blocks.ko: 남쪽으로 육백 리 떨어진 곳에서, 신라의 한 장군이 즉위하던 날의 여왕에게 거의 같은 말을 했었다. 두 사내는 서로를 끝내 알지 못한다.

blocks.html: The Second Emperor tries the wall first. When the wall does not work he tries the ground, which is the sort of thing only an empire can afford to try. Red wings on the parapet watch him do it.
blocks.ko: 황제는 먼저 성벽을 시험한다. 성벽이 듣지 않자 이번엔 땅을 시험한다. 제국이 아니면 시도조차 못 할 방식이다. 여장 위의 붉은 날개들이 그것을 지켜본다.

en: How many baskets is that now?
blocks.speaker: Tang hauler
blocks.art: Tang haulers on the mound’s slope at dusk, baskets of earth on their backs.

en: Don’t count. It gets heavier when you count.
blocks.speaker: Another hauler

lines: 성주님, 저놈들 벌써 예순 날째 저럽니다.
en: Chief, that’s sixty days they’ve been at it.
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier
blocks.art: Night. Torches on the inner wall; the garrison passing stones hand to hand, raising the wall course by course while the mound’s black shoulder looms outside.

lines: 그럼 우리는 예순 밤째다. 돌 넘겨.
en: Then it’s sixty nights for us. Pass the stone.

blocks.html: Five hundred thousand man-days, sixty days of hauling, and a mountain of packed earth rises outside the south wall until its crown looks down into the fortress. From up there you can count the cook fires.
blocks.ko: 연인원 오십만, 예순 날의 흙짐. 남쪽 성벽 밖에 다져 올린 흙산이 솟아, 마침내 그 꼭대기가 성 안을 내려다본다. 거기 서면 밥 짓는 불까지 셀 수 있었다.

blocks.title: Ansi Fortress, sixth to ninth month, 645
blocks.note: Every night the defenders built their wall higher than the mound had grown that day. The siege became a race between shovels.

blocks.html: Then it rains, and the mountain slumps — sideways, into the wall it was built to overlook, taking a stretch of Ansi down with it. Both sides stare at the gap.
blocks.ko: 그러다 비가 온다. 산이 무너진다. 내려다보려 쌓은 그 성벽 쪽으로 옆으로 무너지며, 안시성 한 자락을 함께 무너뜨린다. 양쪽 모두 그 틈을 바라본다.

en: Chief, the wall—
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier

lines: 벽은 됐고. 저 위에 지금 누가 있냐?
en: Never mind the wall. Who’s up on that thing right now?

blocks.html: The officer who was supposed to be holding the mound has stepped away.
blocks.ko: 흙산을 지켜야 할 장수는 자리를 비운 참이었다.
blocks.art: Cut to the mound’s crown: an empty command stool in the rain.

en: …There’s nobody up there.
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier

en: Then it’s ours.

blocks.html: A few hundred men come out through the gap, take the mountain, pile timber on its slope and set it alight. The Tang cannot get near it for three days.
blocks.ko: 무너진 틈으로 병사 수백이 나와 산을 차지하고, 비탈에 나무를 쌓아 불을 지른다. 당군은 사흘 동안 근처에도 가지 못한다.

blocks.html: The Second Emperor has Fu Fuai, the officer who left the mound, beheaded, and orders three days of assault.
blocks.ko: 황제는 흙산을 비운 장수 부복애의 목을 베고 사흘간의 총공격을 명한다.

blocks.html: On the second day an arrow finds the helmet. Whether it was the wall or a stone the size of a cooking-pot, the lacquered bowl leaves his head and rings once on packed earth, then keeps rolling. Sweat. Yellow camp light. For the first time the face is simply there.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 화살이 투구를 찾는다. 성벽이었는지, 솥만 한 돌이었는지, 옻칠한 바가 정수리에서 벗겨져 다진 흙 위에서 한 번 울리고는 계속 굴러간다. 땀. 노란 진중 불. 처음으로, 얼굴이 그냥 있다.

blocks.html: Then the cold comes early, the grass on the plain gives out, and there is nothing to feed the horses.
blocks.ko: 그러나 추위가 일찍 왔고, 벌판의 풀이 다했으며, 말을 먹일 것이 없었다.

blocks.html: That day, for the first time in his life, the Second Emperor knew defeat and retreat.
blocks.ko: 그날, 황제는 생애 처음으로 패배와 퇴각을 알았다.

blocks.title: The Seventh Invasion, start to finish
blocks.caption: All those arrows in, and two dotted lines out. One small wall did that.
blocks.ko: 들어간 화살은 저렇게 많은데, 나온 건 점선 두 줄. 작은 성벽 하나가 한 일이다.

blocks.hanja: 魏徵若在 不使我有是行也
blocks.ko: [대신이] 살아 있었다면, 나로 하여금 이 걸음을 하게 하지 않았을 것이다.
blocks.html: Had [the Grand Minister] been alive, he would not have let me make this expedition.
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) Tang Zhenguan 19 (645), return from Liaodong; Zhonghua Shuju ed., vol. 13 · cf. Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

lines: 내가 천하의 군사를 가지고도 작은 오랑캐에게 곤욕을 당한 것은 무엇 때문인가?
en: With all the armies under heaven, how was I humiliated by so small a barbarian land?
zh: 朕以天下之兵，何以見辱於蕞爾蠻邦？
zhLatn: Zhèn yǐ tiānxià zhī bīng, héyǐ jiànrǔ yú zuì'ěr mánbāng?

blocks.html: After the battle, the Guardian of Ansi is added to the Great Heroes of Goguryeo.
blocks.ko: 전투가 끝나고, 안시의 수호자는 고구려 영웅들의 반열에 오른다.

en: Madman…
Still — he does what must be done.

blocks.html: On the day the army turned for home, the Second Emperor sent a hundred bolts of silk up to the wall, for a man whose name he never learned.
blocks.ko: 군을 돌리던 날, 황제는 이름조차 알지 못한 사내에게 비단 백 필을 성 위로 올려보냈다.

blocks.html: He paraded his troops below Ansi and turned for home; inside the walls everyone kept out of sight. The lord of the city climbed the wall and bowed his farewell. The emperor, admiring how stubbornly he had held, gave him a hundred bolts of silk, to encourage those who serve their lords.
blocks.ko: 이에 안시성 아래에서 군세를 뽐낸 뒤 돌아가니, 성안에서는 모두 자취를 감추고 나오지 않았다. 성주가 성에 올라 절하며 작별하니, 황제가 그 굳게 지킨 것을 가상히 여겨 비단 백 필을 내리고 임금 섬기는 일을 권하였다.
blocks.hanja: 乃耀兵於安市城下而旋，城中皆屏跡不出。城主登城拜辭，上嘉其固守，賜縑百匹，以勵事君。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 198, Tang Zhenguan 19 (645), 9th month

blocks.html: The eastern campaign came to grief at Ansi, so its lord may be called a hero out of the common run. Yet history has lost his name… It is a great pity.
blocks.ko: 동쪽 정벌의 공이 안시에서 꺾였으니, 그 성주는 비상한 호걸이라 할 만하다. 그런데 역사가 그 성명을 잃었으니… 몹시 애석하다.
blocks.hanja: 東征之功，敗於安市，則其城主，可謂豪傑非常者矣。而史失其姓名…甚可惜也。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 21, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 4 (645), historian’s comment (論曰)

lines: 수가 많은 것도 알고, 머리가 좋은 것도 알겠소.
그런데 서토 양반, 한 가지만은 장담하리다.
당신들은 절대로 우리보다 미치지는 못할 거요…!
en: You may outnumber us. You may outthink us.
But hear this, you of the West —
you will never be crazier than we are…!
blocks.art: On the wall the day the Tang turn for home, the bolts of silk at his feet.

blocks.html: Every Goguryeo wall prays to the Holy King. Who was he? We go back seven hundred years, to the day the sun stopped…!
blocks.ko: 고구려의 모든 성벽은 성왕께 빈다. 그는 누구였나? 칠백 년 전, 해가 멈춘 그날로 거슬러 간다…!

Poster key art at the misty pond of Gonyeon: King Geumwa rests his forehead against the old brown horse that found him, the boulder at the water's edge behind them
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; no title, no lettering. Dusk at the reed-ringed pond of Gonyeon on the Buyeo plain: still black water, mist, one great grey boulder at the water's edge. Poster composition: the king and the horse fill the frame together as one bold silhouette on the right two-thirds, seen from a low angle at the water line. INTERACTION: King Geumwa, gold crown and red-burgundy court robe, stands pressed against the old chocolate-brown steppe horse Gonyeon, his forehead resting on the horse's broad forehead, eyes closed, one ringed hand cupping its cheek under the shaggy forelock; the horse leans into him with its eyes half shut, breath steaming between them — an old man and the animal that found him under a stone. The boulder looms behind them on the left, reflected in the pond. Above, half the frame is a splashed-ink storm sky with one break of low gold sunset; that gold light (#a89a72) rakes in from the left and catches the crown, the king's cheek, the horse's mane and the gold frog charm on its halter; the rest falls into ink-black and indigo. Reeds as dark dry-brush strokes in the near foreground. Tiny far off, the timber palisade of Buyeo dissolving in mist. CANON — KING GEUMWA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_geumwa.png (face only; invent a new pose). #a89a72 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | GONYEON (곤연, geumwa's brown horse, guardian of Buyeo) — attached board /obj_gonyeon.png: Stocky, powerful northern steppe horse — deep-bodied and shorter-legged than a war horse, thick crested neck, round barrel, heavy quarters, broad forehead, large kind dark eyes; coat an even deep CHOCOLATE BROWN (not red bay, not black) with a lighter mealy tan muzzle; THICK SHAGGY dark-brown mane falling both sides, long full tail nearly to the ground; plain old leather halter with one small gold frog charm at the brow band — match the board. Old, patient and wise. Stopped at the pond of Gonyeon and wept at a boulder until King Haeburu had it turned over, and the gold-frog child Geumwa was underneath; it has walked beside him ever since. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Five dragons pull Haemosu’s chariot across the noon sky
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Five dragons in one yoke pull a small chariot in a great arc across the sky; Haemosu stands in it, laughing; the dragons are huge black coils with flying-white whiskers; the Amnok river is a thin pale line far below. ONE device: the dragon arc across the sky. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

blocks.html: The sky is empty first. Then come five dragons in the yoke, gold, crimson, azure, jade and white, and behind them a small gold chariot cutting the noon on the run they make every day. From the ground it is a fleck and a wheel, nothing a bather could call a face. The driver stands in it the way a man stands in a doorway he owns, one palm on the rail, laughing at nothing in particular.
blocks.ko: 하늘이 먼저 비어 있다. 그러고 멍에를 멘 용 다섯이 온다. 금빛, 진홍, 푸른빛, 비취, 흰빛. 그 뒤로 작은 금 수레가 매일 하는 그 운행으로 한낮을 가른다. 땅에서 보면 금빛 점 하나와 바퀴 하나, 목욕하는 사람이 얼굴이라 부를 만한 것은 없다. 몰이꾼은 제 문간에 선 사내처럼 수레에 서서, 난간에 손바닥을 얹고, 딱히 누구한테랄 것 없이 웃는다.

blocks.html: Dawn, noon, dusk, night, always the same route. Below, the Amnok is a line he is not supposed to break: wet stone, morning shallows with no boat in them, rocks that are only rocks.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 한낮, 해질녘, 밤, 늘 같은 길이다. 아래로 압록은 그가 넘으면 안 되는 선이다. 젖은 돌, 배 한 척 없는 아침 여울, 그냥 바위일 뿐인 바위.

blocks.html: Every god’s road crosses it. Most of them keep going.
blocks.ko: 신들의 길은 모두 이 강을 건넌다. 대개는 그냥 지나간다.

blocks.html: Haemosu, god of the sun, has kept this hour since before the river had daughters. Today the Amnok flashes under the wheel. He looks down, and the hour breaks.
blocks.ko: 태양신 해모수는 강에 딸이 생기기 전부터 이 시각을 지켜 왔다. 오늘은 바퀴 아래로 압록이 번뜩인다. 그가 내려다보고, 시각이 깨진다.

blocks.caption: The sun god. Punctual since before the rivers, until this afternoon.
blocks.ko: 태양신. 강이 생기기 전부터 시간을 지켰다. 오늘 오후까지는.

blocks.html: In the shallows, three river-daughters are bathing: Yuhwa and her two sisters. Wet hair down their backs, the river at their hips. Nobody dressed for heaven. He falls in love and in lust in the same glance.
blocks.ko: 얕은 물에서 강의 딸 셋이 멱을 감는다. 유화와 두 언니다. 젖은 머리칼은 등을 타고 흐르고, 강물은 허리까지 찼다. 아무도 하늘을 위해 옷을 차려입지 않았다. 그는 한눈에 사랑과 욕정에 동시에 빠진다.

blocks.caption: The river’s eldest daughter. Heaven is about to ruin her afternoon, or make it.
blocks.ko: 강의 맏딸. 하늘이 그녀의 오후를 망치려 한다. 아니면 만들어 주거나.

blocks.html: Hwahye and Wihye have left their silk on the rocks. The eldest folded hers once; the middle did not bother. Yuhwa’s ice-blue is still on her shoulder, wet.
blocks.ko: 화혜와 위혜의 비단은 바위 위에 있다. 언니는 한 번 접어 두었고, 둘째는 귀찮아했다. 유화의 얼음빛은 아직 어깨에, 젖은 채로 있다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa kneels in the shallows with her hair in one fist like a dark rope and rinses the river out of it without hurrying. Heaven can wait on a rinse; she has decided that without saying it. With her back to the sky she looks over her shoulder, as if someone up there had said her name.
blocks.ko: 유화가 여울에 무릎을 꿇고, 검은 밧줄 같은 머리채를 한 손에 쥔 채 서두르지 않고 강물을 헹궈 낸다. 하늘은 헹굼쯤 기다려도 된다. 말은 안 했지만 그렇게 정했다. 하늘을 등진 채, 위에서 누가 이름이라도 부른 것처럼 어깨 너머로 돌아본다.

en: …Stop. Stop the chariot.
Those thighs…
The water…
Unni.
Go. I’m here.
…I was going to say don’t look up.
Hey. In.
Now. You hear me?

blocks.html: Hwahye dives first and does not look back. The eldest treats the sky like a timetable she will not miss.
blocks.ko: 화혜가 먼저 잠수하고 뒤를 안 본다. 언니는 하늘을 놓치면 안 되는 시간표처럼 다룬다.

en: Pfft— wait up.
You, seriously—
Whatever, I’m going—

blocks.html: Wihye laughs and follows, a splash that is mostly amusement.
blocks.ko: 위혜가 웃으며 따라간다. 물보라의 대부분이 재미다.

blocks.html: Two wakes cut the shallows and close. Yuhwa stays. She gets up off her knees, looks straight up as if she had been waiting for heaven to notice, and draws her wet hair over one shoulder.
blocks.ko: 물살 두 줄이 여울을 가르고 닫힌다. 유화는 남는다. 무릎을 펴고 일어나, 하늘이 알아채기를 기다리던 사람처럼 위를 똑바로 올려다보고, 젖은 머리를 한쪽 어깨로 넘긴다.

blocks.html: She draws the wet silk higher, one hip and then the other, and lets the sun finish looking.
blocks.ko: 젖은 비단을 더 끌어올린다. 한쪽 엉덩이, 그리고 다른 쪽. 해가 보기를 끝내게 둔다.

lines: 왜 안 숨어? 그렇게 쳐다보면… 나 내려간다.
en: Hey—
Wait. Hey. You.
Why aren’t you hiding? Look at me like that and I’m coming down.
Heaven looks down every day.
So today I’m supposed to blush?
…Come closer, if you want to see.
Into the water.
And decide… where your hands are going.
…Your name.
I need it… before I come down.
Or… I kiss you without one.
Come down first.
From the sky it’s an order.
At the water… I’ll hear it as a request.
Ask with your mouth… and I’ll answer with my name.

blocks.html: He forgets how to swallow, a god doing a mortal’s small panic. Then he grins, and the grin arrives before the plan. He leaves the rail and the hour in the same motion, the dragons keep the joke going without him, and the water takes him at the knee.
blocks.ko: 삼키는 법을 잊는다. 신이 인간의 작은 공황을 겪는다. 그러고 웃는데, 계획보다 웃음이 먼저 온다. 난간과 시각을 한 동작으로 떠나고, 용들은 그 없이 농담을 잇고, 물이 무릎에서 그를 받는다.

blocks.html: He wades close. She does not run. He stops where a stranger should stop. Then he doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 가까이 걸어 들어온다. 그녀는 도망가지 않는다. 낯선 사람이 설 자리에서 선다. 그러고 안 선다.

en: Why didn’t you run away?
Your sisters did.
…Didn’t see any reason.
The water’s cold. You’re warm. That’s all there is to it.
lines: 물은 차갑고, 당신은 따뜻하고. 그게 다예요.

en: Look straight at the sun
and you burn.
Oh, is that so?
Then I should blink.
It’ll burn your eyes out.
I’m not a lamp.
I like what I see.
I’m looking anyway. You came down.
Don’t make me say it twice.

blocks.html: He swallows. The grin survives it. Barely.
blocks.ko: 그가 삼킨다. 웃음은 산다. 간신히.

blocks.html: She tips her mouth and asks whether the sun likes what it sees, silk already losing the argument with the water.
blocks.ko: 입을 기울여 묻는다. 해는 보이는 게 좋으냐고. 비단은 이미 물과의 말다툼에서 지고 있다.

en: This way. The bank.
The sky has too many sisters.

blocks.html: He follows like the hour had been her idea.
blocks.ko: 시각이 그녀의 생각이었다는 듯이 따라간다.

blocks.html: The copper room rises on the bank like a kiln. He builds it the same afternoon, because the open sky has become too many witnesses.
blocks.ko: 구리 방이 강턱에 가마처럼 올라온다. 같은 날 오후 짓는다. 열린 하늘이 너무 많은 증인이 되어서.

lines: 구리에 기대면… 어디에 데었는지 구분 못 하실 거예요.
en: Copper gets hot in summer.
…You’ll know if you touch it.
My back, too.
If you press me to it… you won’t tell which burned you.
I know.
That’s why I can’t take my hands off you.
Or my mouth.
Then don’t.
Not while heaven is watching.
And while it watches… deeper.

blocks.html: She kisses him with river still on her mouth. The kiss tastes like the shallows. He makes a sound he will deny.
blocks.ko: 입에 강이 남은 채로 그를 입 맞춘다. 키스는 여울 맛이다. 그는 나중에 부인할 소리를 낸다.

blocks.html: Inside, the copper has kept the afternoon’s heat. She leans into it and does not look away from him. Gold lies across wet skin in a hard bar, and the ice-blue silk slips from one shoulder, then gives up the other.
blocks.ko: 안에서 구리는 오후의 열을 간직하고 있다. 그녀는 거기 기대어 그에게서 눈을 떼지 않는다. 젖은 살 위로 금빛이 단단한 띠처럼 눕고, 얼음빛 비단이 한쪽 어깨에서 흘러내리더니, 이윽고 다른 쪽도 내준다.

en: If you want it, say so.
I’m not asking twice.
Give me— all of it.
Don’t save any.

blocks.html: The copper is already hot. He puts her back to it anyway. The river-silk is gathered at her hip and her thighs close around a sun-god who has never learned to be gentle with an hour. She takes him in with the same wet hand that washed her hair for heaven, and when he is all the way inside her she laughs, as if this were what she had meant by looking.
blocks.ko: 구리는 이미 뜨겁다. 그래도 그는 그녀의 등을 거기 댄다. 강의 비단이 허리께에 모이고, 시각을 살살 다룰 줄 모르는 태양신을 그녀의 허벅지가 감싼다. 하늘을 위해 머리를 감던 그 젖은 손으로 그를 이끌어 들이고, 그가 끝까지 들어오자, 올려다본 게 이거였다는 듯이 웃는다.

en: Haa— is heaven always this heavy?
More— against the copper— don’t stop—
I broke the hour.
I don’t care.
Your name— now—
Yuhwa— ah— it’s Yuhwa—
Stay— stay inside me—
All of it— the whole sun—

blocks.html: He takes her through the heat of the wall, gold on wet skin, and every stroke knocks a sound out of her that the river throws back. She comes first and loudly, looking up as if heaven were still watching. Then he spills into her, a god’s whole careless heat, and does not draw back, because she told him not to, and because the hour is already ruined.
blocks.ko: 벽의 열 속에서 그가 그녀를 안는다. 젖은 살 위에 금빛이 앉고, 한 번 움직일 때마다 그녀에게서 터져 나오는 소리를 강이 되던진다. 그녀가 먼저, 크게 끝에 닿는다. 하늘이 아직 보고 있는 것처럼 위를 올려다보며. 그러고 그가 그녀 안에 쏟는다. 신의 무심한 열 전부를. 그리고 물러나지 않는다. 그러지 말라고 했으니까. 시각은 이미 깨졌으니까.

blocks.html: The copper keeps the afternoon. Outside, the river goes on being a river.
blocks.ko: 구리가 오후를 간직한다. 밖에서는 강이 계속 강이다.

blocks.label: Habek's Court
blocks.ko: 하백의 조정

blocks.html: The copper is still warm when the river notices. The Amnok keeps its own court: Habek, god of the river and father of three daughters, stands on the wet stones as if the current were a hall. Mist is the dais. He does not need a chair.
blocks.ko: 구리가 아직 따뜻할 때 강이 알아챈다. 압록에는 제 조정이 있다. 강의 신이자 세 딸의 아버지인 하백이 여울이 대청이라도 되는 듯 젖은 돌 위에 선다. 안개가 대좌다. 의자는 필요 없다.

en: Who stopped the chariot. Say a name.
lines: 수레를 멈춘 게 누구냐. 이름을 대라.

en: I… looked up.
I just— looked. That’s all it was.
You don’t sleep in my mist after that.
You smell like copper.
lines: 그 다음엔 내 안개에서 자지 못한다.

en: Go. The bank is closed.

blocks.html: Hwahye and Wihye do not argue the sentence. The eldest watches the current. The middle one watches the copper glow die. Neither looks at their father’s face.
blocks.ko: 화혜와 위혜는 판결을 논하지 않는다. 언니는 여울을 본다. 둘째는 죽어 가는 구리 빛을 본다. 둘 다 아버지 얼굴은 안 본다.

blocks.html: Habek kicks Yuhwa out with a look, not a foot. The bank understands.
blocks.ko: 하백이 유화를 내쫓는다. 발이 아니라 눈으로. 강턱이 알아듣는다.

blocks.html: The pavilion walkway does not catch her. Habek’s sleeve is already the closed door. She hits packed earth with ice-blue still wet from the copper.
blocks.ko: 누각 복도가 받아주지 않는다. 하백의 소매가 이미 닫힌 문이다. 구리가 덜 마른 얼음빛으로 다진 흙에 엎어진다.

blocks.html: For a while nobody comes. The mist that used to be a bed is just weather. She sits where the river can see her and does not look up.
blocks.ko: 한동안 아무도 안 온다. 침대였던 안개가 그냥 날씨다. 강이 보이는 자리에 앉아서, 올려다보지 않는다.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S1 ends here.

blocks.html: The sky talks first. She hears him before she sees anything with paws.
blocks.ko: 하늘이 먼저 말한다. 발 달린 걸 보기 전에 그 목소리를 듣는다.

en: Hey.
Wait. Don’t sit in the dust.
Follow the fox.

blocks.html: The fox is already on the packed earth, pale gold-white, looking back once as if she might miss the joke. Yuhwa follows it south, barefoot, the ice-blue gone dull with dust: pine shade, a river-bend that is not the Amnok, a pass of bare stone where she is smaller than the ridge. The fox does not explain the map.
blocks.ko: 여우가 이미 다진 흙 위에 있다. 창백한 금빛 흰 털, 농담을 놓칠까 봐 한 번 돌아본다. 유화는 맨발로, 먼지에 탁해진 얼음빛으로 그 뒤를 따라 남쪽으로 간다. 소나무 그늘, 압록이 아닌 강굽이, 능선보다 그녀가 작아지는 벗은 돌 고개. 여우는 지도를 설명하지 않는다.

blocks.html: From the river, Buyeo’s capital is a palisade of timber teeth and a hill of grey roofs. The studded doors open. King Geumwa, the gold-frog king, comes out to the yard himself.
blocks.ko: 강에서 보면 부여의 도읍은 나무 이빨 같은 목책과 잿빛 기와 언덕이다. 징 박힌 문이 열린다. 금개구리 왕 금와가 몸소 마당으로 나온다.

blocks.caption: The gold-frog king. Found under a rock, raised in a palace, kind to strays.
blocks.ko: 금개구리 임금. 바위 밑에서 발견되어 궁에서 자랐고, 떠돌이에게 너그럽다.

blocks.html: An old kingdom that takes in strays and keeps count.
blocks.ko: 떠돌이를 받아 주고, 셈은 해 두는 오래된 나라.

en: Come in. I’ve got a room free.
The yard can learn your name later.

blocks.html: I am Habek’s daughter, and my name is Yuhwa. I was out with my sisters when a man who called himself Haemosu, son of the Heavenly Emperor, lured me into a room by the Amnok below Mount Ungsim and lay with me. Then he went away and did not come back. My parents blamed me for following a man without a go-between, and so I was banished to the Ubal River.
blocks.ko: 나는 하백의 딸로, 이름은 유화다. 아우들과 나가 놀 때에 한 사내가 스스로 천제의 아들 해모수라 하며, 나를 웅심산 아래 압록 가의 방으로 꾀어 정을 통하고는 가서 돌아오지 않았다. 부모는 내가 중매도 없이 남자를 따랐다고 꾸짖었고, 마침내 나는 우발수로 쫓겨나 살게 되었다.
blocks.hanja: 我是河伯之女，名柳花。與諸弟出遊，時有一男子，自言天帝子解慕漱，誘我於熊心山下鴨淥邊室中私之，卽往不返。父母責我無媒而從人，遂謫居優渤水。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 13, Goguryeo Annals — King Dongmyeong, accession: Yuhwa’s answer to King Geumwa

blocks.html: A sun-shaft finds her where she kneels to wring the river out of her sleeve. When she crosses the yard at night it moves with her, a bar of gold keeping her sleeve.
blocks.ko: 해 한 줄기가, 소매에서 강을 짜내려 무릎 꿇은 그녀를 찾아낸다. 밤에 마당을 건너면 그 빛이 따라 움직인다. 소매를 지키는 금빛 막대.

blocks.html: Yuhwa’s ice-blue sleeve is the first roof the boy will remember, though he is not a boy yet.
blocks.ko: 유화의 얼음빛 소매가 첫 지붕이다. 아이는 그걸 기억할 것이다. 아직 아이가 아닌데.

blocks.html: In time Yuhwa lays a great egg. Geumwa has the egg taken from her before the court has agreed what a river-daughter is allowed to bear.
blocks.ko: 때가 되어 유화가 커다란 알을 낳는다. 금와가 알을 빼앗아 간다. 조정은 강의 딸이 무엇을 낳아도 되는지 아직 합의하지 못했다.

blocks.html: Geumwa found her strange and shut her away in a room. The sunlight shone on her; she drew herself aside, and the sun’s shadow followed and shone on her again. From this she conceived, and bore an egg about the size of five pecks.
blocks.ko: 금와가 이를 기이하게 여겨 방 안에 깊이 가두었다. 햇빛이 그녀를 비추어 몸을 끌어 피하면, 해 그림자가 또 따라와 비추었다. 그로 인해 아이를 배어 알 하나를 낳으니, 크기가 닷 되들이쯤 되었다.
blocks.hanja: 金蛙異之，幽閉於室中，爲日所炤，引身避之，日影又逐而炤之。因而有孕，生一卵，大如五升許。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 13, Goguryeo Annals — King Dongmyeong, accession

blocks.html: …Habek’s daughter was shut in a room by the king of Buyeo. The sunlight shone on her; she drew herself aside, and the sun’s shadow followed. Before long she conceived, and bore an egg the size of five pecks.
blocks.ko: …하백의 딸은 부여 왕에 의해 방 안에 갇혔다. 햇빛이 그녀를 비추어 몸을 끌어 피하면, 해 그림자가 또 따라왔다. 얼마 뒤 아이를 배어 알 하나를 낳으니, 크기가 닷 되만 하였다.
blocks.hanja: …河伯女，為夫餘王閉於室中，為日所照，引身避之，日影又逐。既而有孕，生一卵，大如五升。
blocks.source: Wei Shu (魏書) bk. 100, Account of Goguryeo (高句麗傳)

blocks.html: Dogs won't eat it. An axe won't split it. What on earth is inside Yuhwa's egg…?
blocks.ko: 개도 먹지 않는다. 도끼로도 쪼개지지 않는다. 유화의 알 속에는 대체 무엇이 들어 있는가…?

Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.
