blocks.label: The Egg
blocks.ko: 알

blocks.html: Dogs and pigs will not eat it; the sty refuses the guest, and the ministers pretend that is a kind of answer. In the road, cattle and horses step around it, hooves knowing better than the hall. In the open field, birds cover it with their wings instead of pecking, and the yard goes quiet at that.
blocks.ko: 개와 돼지가 먹지 않는다. 돼지우리가 손님을 거절하고, 신하들은 그걸 대답인 척한다. 길에 버리면 소와 말이 피해서 간다. 발굽이 대청보다 낫다. 들에 두면 새들이 쪼지 않고 날개로 덮는다. 마당이 그걸 보고 조용해진다.

blocks.html: An axe is brought. The axe will not split the egg. The edge sings and the shell does not bother to crack.
blocks.ko: 도끼를 가져온다. 도끼로도 알이 안 깨진다. 날이 울고, 껍질은 갈라질 생각도 안 한다.

blocks.html: Someone winds up with both arms and hurls it off the palisade. It meets the stones and stays whole.
blocks.ko: 누군가 두 팔로 자세를 잡더니 목책 밖으로 내던진다. 알은 돌에 부딪히고도 멀쩡하다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa wraps it warm in her own sleeve and takes it back upstairs, and nobody reaches for the axe again.
blocks.ko: 유화가 제 소매로 따뜻하게 싼다. 다시 위층으로 가져간다. 다시 도끼에 손대는 사람이 없다.

blocks.html: Then the shell gives, and out comes a baby boy, wet and furious, already trying to focus. He looks up as if the room had owed him an explanation.
blocks.ko: 그러고 껍질이 열리고 사내아이가 나온다. 젖고, 화가 나 있고, 벌써 초점을 맞추려 한다. 방이 해명이라도 빚진 것처럼 올려다본다.

blocks.html: They name him Jumong, the good shot, because in those days people were named for what heaven had plainly already decided. He grows up with his brothers Daeso and Galsa, and the better he shoots, the smaller their smiles become.
blocks.ko: 사람들은 아이를 주몽, 활 잘 쏘는 이라 이름 짓는다. 그 시절에는 하늘이 이미 정해 둔 것을 따라 이름을 지었기 때문이다. 주몽은 형 대소, 갈사와 함께 자라고, 활이 늘수록 웃음은 작아진다.

blocks.html: They are boys first, three princes at one stake in one square, before anybody is an heir on purpose. They shoot with borrowed bows, too long in the arm.
blocks.ko: 처음에는 그냥 아이들이다. 마당 하나, 말뚝 하나에 왕자 셋. 누가 일부러 태자가 되기 전이다. 빌린 활로 쏜다. 팔보다 긴 활이다.

blocks.html: Jumong can find a fly’s wing with an arrow before the bow fits his arm.
blocks.ko: 팔에 활이 맞기도 전에, 주몽은 화살로 파리의 날개를 찾아낸다.

blocks.caption: The best archer in Buyeo. The princes have noticed.
blocks.ko: 부여에서 활을 제일 잘 쏘는 아이. 왕자들도 눈치챘다.

en: I’ll take the fly.

blocks.html: Daeso teaches the grip, then resents the hit. The lesson ends the moment the arrow is better than the teacher.
blocks.ko: 대소가 쥐는 법을 가르치고, 맞히면 분을 낸다. 화살이 스승보다 나아지는 순간 수업이 끝난다.

blocks.html: The yard hears the wood take it, a clean tick, and the praise does not arrive. Daeso keeps his hands on his own bow as if applause were a confession. Galsa looks at the dirt instead of the hit.
blocks.ko: 마당이 나무가 화살을 받는 소리를 듣는다. 깨끗한 딱 소리. 칭찬은 오지 않는다. 대소는 박수가 자백이라도 되는 듯 손을 제 활에 둔다. 갈사는 맞은 자리 대신 흙을 본다.

blocks.html: They sleep in a pile like dogs under one quilt, and in the morning the quilt has taken sides. Jumong steals the last millet and grins through it, which is worse than the theft.
blocks.ko: 개들처럼 이불 하나에 뭉쳐 자고, 아침이면 이불이 편을 든다. 주몽은 마지막 기장을 훔치고, 훔치면서 웃는다. 도둑질보다 그게 더 나쁘다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa watches from the hall door, ice-blue sleeve on the post, not stepping into the boys’ weather.
blocks.ko: 유화가 대청 문에서 본다. 기둥에 얼음빛 소매. 아이들 날씨 안으로 들어가지 않는다.

blocks.html: They grow apart in the same square, a hand’s width more between bowls each season.
blocks.ko: 같은 마당에서 서로 멀어진다. 계절마다 그릇 사이가 손바닥만큼.

blocks.html: Only two come back talking from the stake. The third has already started a country in his head.
blocks.ko: 말하면서 돌아오는 건 둘뿐이다. 셋째는 이미 머릿속에서 나라를 시작했다.

blocks.html: Grown, they still shoot at the princes’ mark-stake. Daeso stands too close when Jumong’s arrow lands.
blocks.ko: 다 자라서도 왕자들은 과녁 말뚝에 쏜다. 주몽의 화살이 꽂힐 때 대소는 너무 가까이 서 있다.

lines: 먹여 주는 집보다 멀리 쏘지 마라.
en: Do not outshoot the house that feeds you.
Then put the mark farther.
If it lands, I meant to applaud.

blocks.html: Jumong keeps the grin because grinning is cheaper than asking why, and Daeso hates the price.
blocks.ko: 주몽은 웃음을 유지한다. 왜냐고 묻는 것보다 웃음이 싸서. 대소는 그 값을 싫어한다.

blocks.html: Galsa will not stay to be the second smile in that hall. East of Buyeo he splits a smaller country and names it for himself — Galsa-Buyeo.
blocks.ko: 갈사는 그 대청의 두 번째 웃음으로 남지 않는다. 부여 동쪽에서 작은 나라를 가르고 자기 이름을 붙인다 — 갈사부여.

blocks.html: Jumong’s arranged marriage to Lady Ye is a hall’s solution: a wife, a lamp, a door that still opens onto Buyeo.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 정략혼은 대청의 해법이다. 아내, 등잔, 아직 부여로 열리는 문.

blocks.html: Lady Ye gets pregnant with their son Yuri while the yard is still pretending the foundling is a guest.
blocks.ko: 예씨부인이 아들 유리를 밴다. 마당은 아직 그 주워 온 아이를 손님인 척한다.

blocks.html: Geumwa will not take the heir’s counsel, so Daeso takes the ministers into a side room. Lamp low. If they write it down, the scandal arrives before the knife.
blocks.ko: 금와가 태자의 말을 받지 않아서, 대소가 신하들을 곁방으로 부른다. 등잔은 낮고. 적으면 칼보다 소문이 먼저 온다.

en: Do it before the next hunt.
Quiet is fine.

blocks.html: Geumwa answers his heir the way tired kings answer. He refuses the knife and gives the foundling a chore instead: Jumong is sent to the royal stables, which in Buyeo is where a hall keeps a prince it would rather not see at dinner.
blocks.ko: 금와는 지친 왕들이 답하는 식으로 맏아들에게 답한다. 칼은 거절하고, 주워 온 아이에게는 일거리를 준다. 주몽은 왕의 마구간으로 보내진다. 부여에서 마구간은, 저녁상에서 마주치고 싶지 않은 왕자를 두는 곳이다.

blocks.html: The king did not listen, and set him to tending the horses. Jumong knew which ones were swift; he cut their feed and made them lean, and fed the sluggish ones well and made them fat. The king rode the fat ones himself and gave the lean one to Jumong.
blocks.ko: 왕은 듣지 않고 그에게 말을 기르게 하였다. 주몽은 날랜 말을 알아보고 먹이를 줄여 여위게 하고, 둔한 말은 잘 먹여 살찌게 하였다. 왕은 살찐 말을 자기가 타고, 여윈 말을 주몽에게 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 王不聽 使之養馬 朱蒙知其駿者 而減食令瘦 駑者善養令肥 王以肥者自乘 瘦者給朱蒙
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 13, Goguryeo Annals — Jumong; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1

blocks.html: Yuhwa comes to the stable after the lamps are out, a river-daughter in a frog-king’s straw, and finds her son brushing the best horse in Buyeo as if he could apologise to it in advance.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 꺼진 뒤 유화가 마구간에 온다. 개구리 왕의 짚더미에 선 강의 딸. 아들은 부여에서 제일 좋은 말을 빗질하고 있다. 미리 사과라도 해 두려는 듯이.

en: This one, isn’t it?
The fast one.
…How’d you know?
I didn’t tell anyone.

lines: 너 이 녀석만 빗질을 오래 하잖아.
나중에 미안하다 하고, 배 터지게 먹이고.
en: You brush this one longer than the others.
I’ll give you a needle. Put it in his tongue.
Say sorry later, and feed him till he bursts.
Mother, you’re terrifying.
…For how many days?
Until Daeso’s done sharpening.

blocks.html: By the next moon the fastest horse in the yard looks like a rack of kindling with a mane, and the slow ones shine like lacquer. Geumwa walks the stalls, picks the fattest for himself, and tosses the thin one to the foundling with a joke about how well they match. Daeso laughs loudest, which is a pity, because he is the one man in Buyeo who should have looked twice.
blocks.ko: 다음 달이 되자 마구간에서 제일 빠른 말은 갈기 달린 장작더미가 되어 있고, 느린 말들은 옻칠한 듯 번들거린다. 금와는 마구간을 돌며 제일 살찐 말을 자기 몫으로 고르고, 여윈 말은 주워 온 아이에게 던져 준다. 둘이 참 닮았다는 농담과 함께. 대소가 제일 크게 웃는다. 안됐다. 부여에서 두 번 쳐다봤어야 할 사람은 그 하나뿐이었는데.

lines: 둘 다 내 밥을 먹고도 마르는구나.
en: Suits you.
You both eat my rice and still stay thin.
Thank you, Majesty.
I’ll take good care of him.

blocks.html: He pulls the needle out that night. The horse eats until dawn.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 바늘을 뽑는다. 말은 새벽까지 먹는다.

blocks.html: Before the next hunt, a knife finds Jumong in the dark and misses.
blocks.ko: 다음 사냥 전에, 어둠 속의 칼이 주몽을 찾아왔다가 빗나간다.

en: Leave Buyeo. Tonight.
I’ll keep the lamp.
Leave the door half open.
So I know which way is still yours.
lines: 어느 쪽이 아직 네 건지 알게.

blocks.html: Night at the palisade. Iron studs, a red sleeve, and a wife who does not come out to wave.
blocks.ko: 목책의 밤. 쇠 못, 붉은 소매, 손 흔들러 나오지 않는 아내.

blocks.html: His friends Oi, Mari and Hyupbo take the hills with him. Behind them come the riders Daeso sent, less a hunt than a net, and under the pines it closes from above.
blocks.ko: 벗 오이, 마리, 협보가 그와 함께 산으로 든다. 뒤로 대소가 보낸 기병이 따라붙는다. 사냥이라기보다 그물이고, 소나무 아래에서 그물은 위에서부터 조여 온다.

blocks.caption: Buyeo behind him, Daeso’s riders behind that, and a river ahead with no bridge on it. Yet.
blocks.ko: 등 뒤엔 부여, 그 뒤엔 대소의 기병, 앞엔 다리 하나 없는 강. 아직은.

blocks.label: The Flight
blocks.ko: 달아남

blocks.html: They split in the pines before the river, four men and one horse between them, the one Geumwa thought was thin.
blocks.ko: 강 앞 소나무 숲에서 넷이 갈라진다. 사람은 넷, 말은 한 마리. 금와가 여위었다고 여긴 그 말이다.

en: We’ll take the ridge.
Find us when you still have a bow.

lines: 능선 길은 너희가 더 멀어. 강은 내가 혼자 건널게.
en: Take him.
Your road over the ridge is longer. I’ll do the river alone.
Are you crazy? He’s your horse.
Exactly. Fatten him up for me.
…I’ll come find you.

blocks.html: He runs until the pines smear. Behind him the net is spears in the dark, points only, no faces he is allowed to know.
blocks.ko: 소나무가 번질 때까지 뛴다. 뒤에서 그물은 어둠 속의 창이다. 날만 있고, 알아도 되는 얼굴은 없다.

blocks.html: Something keeps pace with him above the trees, black on black, going from branch to branch without seeming to hurry. A crow. He is too frightened to count its legs.
blocks.ko: 나무 위로 무언가가 그와 나란히 간다. 검은 위의 검은 것, 서두르는 기색도 없이 가지에서 가지로. 까마귀다. 다리를 셀 정신이 그에게는 없다.

blocks.html: Jumong reaches the water alone, his death already written down for that day. No ford. No boat. The friends are a ridge away, on purpose.
blocks.ko: 주몽이 홀로 물에 닿는다. 그날 죽기로 이미 적혀 있는 목숨이다. 여울도 배도 없다. 벗들은 일부러 능선 하나 떨어져 있다.

blocks.html: Haewonmek, the reaper who collects each day’s dead, is already in the air. He skims the river toward him. Black hat, black silk, mouth bound shut. Jumong doesn’t see him. He’s looking at the water and the rain.
blocks.ko: 그날의 죽은 자를 거두는 저승사자 해원맥이 벌써 공중에 떠 있다. 그는 강물 위를 스치듯 날아 그에게 다가온다. 검은 갓, 검은 비단, 꽁꽁 묶인 입. 주몽은 그를 보지 못한다. 그는 물과 빗줄기만 보고 있다.

blocks.caption: A fetch of the underworld. Black hat, black silk, and a mouth bound shut so he can’t haggle.
blocks.ko: 저승의 차사. 검은 갓, 검은 비단, 흥정 못 하게 묶인 입.

blocks.html: A root takes his foot. He goes down on the wet stones, pine needles in his mouth, the bow a pace off as if it had been the first thing taken. Haewonmek crouches over him to collect what is owed, and the blow is already coming down.
blocks.ko: 뿌리가 발을 잡는다. 젖은 돌 위로 넘어지고, 입에는 솔잎, 활은 먼저 빼앗긴 것처럼 한 걸음 떨어져 있다. 해원맥이 거둘 것을 거두러 그 위에 엎드리고, 일격은 이미 내려오고 있다.

blocks.html: The cloak arrives before the face. Rain fills it. A hand closes on Haewonmek’s wrist from behind, and the strike simply stops — the way an elder stops a sleeve that has gone too far.
blocks.ko: 망토가 얼굴보다 먼저 온다. 비가 그것을 채운다. 뒤에서 손이 해원맥의 손목을 잡고, 일격은 그냥 멈춘다 — 너무 멀리 간 소매를 맏이가 멈추듯.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S2 ends here.

blocks.html: Jumong’s cheek is in the mud. Haewonmek looks back. Behind him, in a dark hood, the sun god is holding his wrist and laughing, as if the night had grabbed the wrong man. The night is Haewonmek’s road. The joke is Haemosu’s.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 뺨은 진흙에 있다. 해원맥이 돌아본다. 그 뒤에서 검은 두건을 쓴 태양신이 그의 손목을 잡은 채 웃고 있다. 밤이 사람을 잘못 집었다는 듯이. 밤은 해원맥의 길이다. 농담은 해모수의 것이다.

en: Haemosu…
The night is not your domain…!

lines: 바다를 건너다 네가 오는 소리가 들리더군.
en: Heh…
Do you really think the sun disappears at night?
I was just crossing the ocean when I heard you coming over.
This man is fated to die today…
You are not to interfere with Yumla’s domain…!

lines: 아우가 새 일 하는 동안은 가만 둘 셈이었다.
염라가 할 말 있으면, 직접 와서 보라 해라.
en: Hey, Haewonmek.
I’ll leave my little brother alone while he’s at his new job.
But this is my son.
And he still hasn’t completed his purpose in this world.
And besides… I outrank you.
If Yumla has any complaints, tell him to come see me himself.

blocks.html: He puts Haewonmek aside and leans to Jumong’s ear. Jumong cannot see him, only the night, the river, a warmth that should not be there. The idea arrives as breath.
blocks.ko: 해원맥을 옆으로 밀어 두고 주몽의 귀에 입을 댄다. 주몽은 그를 보지 못한다. 밤과 강과, 거기 있어서는 안 될 온기뿐. 생각은 숨결로 온다.

blocks.label: The Crossing
blocks.ko: 건넌 강

lines: 나는 태양의 주인, 위대한 해모수의 아들이다!
en: I am the son of the great Haemosu, the lord of the sun!
Make way for me!

blocks.html: The river answers. Tortoises rise and lock shell to shell in the dark. Jumong runs the wet backs as if they had always been a road.
blocks.ko: 강이 응답한다. 자라들이 떠올라 어둠 속에서 등딱지를 잇는다. 주몽이 젖은 등 위를 달린다 — 원래부터 길이었던 것처럼.

blocks.html: Of old, the founder King Chumo laid the foundations. He came out of North Buyeo, son of the Heavenly Emperor; his mother was Habek’s daughter; he broke the egg and came down into the world… The king came to the ford and said: “I am King Chumo, son of August Heaven, whose mother is Habek’s daughter. Link the reeds and float the turtles for me.” At his voice the reeds linked and the turtles floated, and so he crossed.
blocks.ko: 옛날 시조 추모왕이 나라의 터를 열었다. 북부여에서 나왔으니 천제의 아들이요, 어머니는 하백의 딸로, 알을 깨고 세상에 내려왔다… 왕이 나루에 이르러 말하였다. “나는 황천의 아들이요, 어머니는 하백의 딸인 추모왕이다. 나를 위하여 갈대를 잇고 거북을 띄워라.” 그 소리에 응하여 곧 갈대가 이어지고 거북이 떠오르니, 그제야 건넜다.
blocks.hanja: 惟昔始祖，鄒牟王之創基也。出自北夫餘，天帝之子，母河伯女郎，剖卵降世…王臨津言曰：「我是皇天之子，母河伯女郎，鄒牟王，為我連葭浮龜。」應聲，即為連葭浮龜，然後造渡。
blocks.source: Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑) face I, opening lines (414)

blocks.html: Jumong spoke to the water: “I am the son of the Sun, and Habek’s grandson through my mother. Today I flee, and the soldiers chasing me are nearly here. How can I cross?” At that the fish and turtles rose together and made a bridge for him. Jumong crossed; the fish and turtles scattered, and the riders chasing him could not cross.
blocks.ko: 주몽이 물에 고하였다. “나는 해의 아들이요 하백의 외손이다. 오늘 달아나는데 쫓는 군사가 거의 이르렀으니, 어떻게 건너겠는가?” 이에 물고기와 자라가 함께 떠올라 다리를 이루니, 주몽이 건넜다. 물고기와 자라가 곧 흩어지니, 쫓던 기병은 건너지 못하였다.
blocks.hanja: 朱蒙告水曰：「我是日子，河伯外孫，今日逃走，追兵垂及，如何得濟？」於是魚鼈並浮，為之成橋，朱蒙得渡，魚鼈乃解，追騎不得渡。
blocks.source: Wei Shu (魏書) bk. 100, Account of Goguryeo (高句麗傳)

blocks.html: I am the son of the Heavenly Emperor, Habek’s grandson. Today I flee, and those who pursue me have nearly arrived — what shall I do? Thereupon the fish and turtles formed a bridge…
blocks.ko: 나는 천제의 아들이요, 하백의 손이다. 오늘 도망하는데 쫓는 자가 거의 이르렀으니, 어찌하리오. 이에 물고기와 자라가 다리를 이루었다…
blocks.hanja: 我是天帝子河伯孫，今日逃遁，追者垂及，奈何？於是魚鼈成橋…
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders 1 — Goguryeo (高句麗)

blocks.html: The two brothers stay on the near stones. Jumong is already a red speck on the far dark. Haemosu throws an arm across Haewonmek’s shoulder and laughs like the job is done. Haewonmek’s gat is still askew — the look of a clerk whose ledger just walked off.
blocks.ko: 두 형제는 가까운 쪽 돌에 남는다. 주몽은 이미 먼 어둠의 붉은 점이다. 해모수가 해원맥의 어깨에 팔을 걸치고, 일이 끝난 듯이 웃는다. 해원맥의 갓은 아직 비뚤다 — 명부가 제 발로 걸어 나간 서기의 얼굴.

en: He is still mortal…

lines: 허나 말이야… 사람은 누구나 이승에 온 까닭이 있다.
때가 되면, 그때는 네가 데려가게 두지.
en: Yes, of course.
But you know… every man comes into this world for a purpose.
He’s going to do great things.
When his time comes, I’ll let you take him.
Look at him go.
That's my boy.
You just robbed a ledger.
I borrowed a day.
I'll give it back.
Yumla isn’t going to like this…
blocks.art: Grumbling.

blocks.html: The bird that watches him is not an ordinary crow. On Goguryeo’s banners it will stand on three legs under a red sun, the samjoko, the bird that can look at the day without blinking.
blocks.ko: 그를 지켜보는 새는 여느 까마귀가 아니다. 훗날 고구려의 기에서 그 새는 붉은 해 아래 세 다리로 설 것이다. 삼족오, 해를 깜빡이지 않고 바라보는 새.

blocks.html: It is sitting on a rock on the far bank when he comes off the last shell, soaked, laughing like an idiot because he is alive. This time he counts.
blocks.ko: 마지막 등껍질에서 내려섰을 때 그것은 건너편 강가 바위에 앉아 있다. 그는 흠뻑 젖어서, 살아 있다는 게 우스워 바보처럼 웃고 있다. 이번에는 센다.

en: …One, two.
Three?
Hey. Why’ve you got three legs?

blocks.html: The crow looks at him without blinking, which is either rude or holy, then drops off the rock, flies ten paces into the pines, lands again, and looks back.
blocks.ko: 까마귀는 눈도 깜박이지 않고 그를 본다. 무례하거나 신령하거나 둘 중 하나다. 그러고는 바위에서 내려앉아 소나무 숲으로 열 걸음 날아가 다시 앉고, 돌아본다.

lines: ……너 나 곰한테 데려가면 진짜 구워 먹는다.
en: Follow you?
…If you’re leading me to a bear, I swear I’m roasting you.
Three legs. There’d be one to spare.

blocks.html: He follows it all afternoon, uphill, through pines that stop being Buyeo’s and start being nobody’s. It keeps ten paces ahead and never once lets him catch up. At dusk it lands on a stone lip above a dark opening in the hill and stays there, folded, like a doorman whose shift is over.
blocks.ko: 그는 오후 내내 그것을 따라 오르막을, 부여의 것이기를 그만두고 누구의 것도 아니게 된 소나무 숲을 간다. 까마귀는 늘 열 걸음 앞에 있고 한 번도 따라잡히지 않는다. 해 질 녘 그것은 산허리에 난 어두운 입구 위 돌턱에 내려앉아, 날개를 접고 그대로 있다. 교대를 마친 문지기처럼.

en: …Here?
Thanks. Really.
Can’t roast you now, can I.

blocks.html: Before the valley has a name for him he goes in, into stone and leaf-light and a country-shaped dark. In what will be called the Jumong cavern, he prays for a roof of his own.
blocks.ko: 골짜기가 그를 부를 이름을 갖기도 전에, 그는 그 안으로 들어간다. 돌과 잎빛과 나라 모양의 어둠. 훗날 국동대혈이라 불릴 그곳에서, 제 지붕 하나를 빈다.

blocks.html: A soaked exile, a hall full of spears, and a chieftain's daughter who won't look at him. Jumong's luck is about to get complicated…!
blocks.ko: 흠뻑 젖은 망명자, 창이 가득한 전각, 그리고 끝까지 그를 쳐다보지 않는 족장의 딸. 주몽의 운이 복잡해지기 시작한다…!

images.alt: High crane: the five Jolbon chieftains sit on five animal hides around one fire in Tabal's hall — crow feathers, horse, cow, pig, dog
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE watercolor painting, minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop with nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night inside Tabal's timber hall at Jolbon: packed-earth floor, rough timber posts, a smoke hole in the dark roof, ONE low fire pit at the exact centre as the only light. High crane angle looking steeply down. ONE device: FIVE ANIMAL HIDES laid flat on the earth floor in a ring around the fire like five petals, each a different skin: a spread mat of glossy BLACK CROW FEATHERS; a chestnut HORSE hide with a strip of black mane; a brown-and-white COW hide; a bristly dark grey-black PIG hide; a shaggy pale grey-white DOG pelt. EXACTLY FIVE men, one sitting cross-legged on each hide, facing the fire, nobody else in the hall: Yeon Tabal on the crow feathers (red headband, black beard); the Horse Ka, heavy and bearded, dark robe with a red sash, on the horse hide; the Cow Ka, youngest, red headband and white feathers in his long hair, on the cow hide; the Pig Ka, thick and heavy, on the pig hide; the Dog Ka, the eldest, white beard and grey headband, on the dog pelt. FACES ONLY from the attached chieftain portraits: IGNORE the tiger pelts and bear heads drawn on the portraits — nobody wears a tiger or bear skin; they wear plain hemp and leather tunics, wrapped forearms and their headbands, and the only animal skins in the frame are the five hides on the floor. Unstrung bows lie flat beside them. They lean in and argue — one stabbing a finger at the dirt, one with arms folded, one laughing, one weighing with his palms — not posing. Ember-orange firelight as the one hard key from below, faces carved out of total darkness, the five men's long shadows thrown outward across the floor like spokes, smoke rising into black. Background and foreground are a Renaissance tenebrist oil painting: umber-to-black timber posts and earth floor modelled in glazed oil, sfumato into black at the frame edges, a dark out-of-focus post in one foreground corner; the webtoon figures are painted into that oil space in watercolor washes under the same fire key. CANON — YEON TABAL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_tabal.png (face only; invent a new pose). #a97c4a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | HORSE KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_horse_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #2c2c30 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | COW KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_cow_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #c45a2a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PIG KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_pig_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #6b4a32 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | DOG KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dog_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #c8d0d4 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. BACKGROUND AND FOREGROUND are a high-contrast Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST OIL PAINTING in their own right (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt, late Titian): a warm umber-to-black ground; walls, timber, stone, drapery, tables and the dark foreground shapes modelled in glazed oil and pulled out of the darkness by the one candle, lamp or window, with soft sfumato falloff into black — the webtoon figures are set INTO that old-master oil space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Not kissing. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — JUMONG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dongmyung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean archer; black hair half-bound under a knotted red headband with long tails; dark warm eyes, easy grin. CLEAN-SHAVEN before he is king — ignore the moustache and chin hair on his portrait. Dress: Red silk jeogori and po over a charcoal underlayer, rope-tied sash, wrapped forearms; bow across his back. Demeanor: Fun: grins, laughs, winks, easy eyes when Sosuno is mean; scared and a little stupid when it matters. Never: facial hair before he is king; grim founder-statue face; sword-duel hero pose. | SOSUNO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sosuno.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_sosuno.png when the head is visible. Look: Long straight black hair with a high topknot pinned by her gold binyeo, a thin red headband with a center jewel; sharp brows, cool appraising eyes. Dress: Dusty-rose hanbok over white sleeves, black wrap sash with red cords, red-wrapped wrists; bow and quiver on her back. Her hex is lamplight or a ground stamp — never gold robes. Demeanor: Sharp, quick, too much, then covering; a merchant's appraising glance. #e8a04a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold robes; meek downcast pose. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. images.prompt: White paper. NOT a diagonal cliff. Above it, empty white, and one dry arc of the same brush as a moon, hairs visible, not a perfect circle. A tiny clean-shaven walker on the river stroke, one small cinnabar robe flick. Only one person. No mountain slope. No text, no seal.

Modest chest, closed silk pulled tight between them, not exposed, not a large bust. FACES match the portraits, Korean, dark eyes. Binyeo matches the pin. Crushed black, one lamp. No text, no halo.

Sitting on a packed-earth riverbank at dusk, one knee up, laughing with eyes closed. FACE matches the attached portrait; ignore portrait clothes. Ordinary skin, NO red mark, NO glowing spot on the cheek, NO lamp painted on the face. Dusk light only. Clean manhwa line, cel shading, NOT photoreal. No text, no watermark, no halo, no glow.

A tiny archer figure at the right end of the stroke, one small red flick #e8563f on the headband only. A thin white ground line. Vast black emptiness elsewhere. No seal, no calligraphy, no signature, no red stamp, no second person, no facial hair detail.

blocks.label: The Scouts
blocks.ko: 척후

blocks.html: He is still wet from the river when the pines stop being empty. Two men in Yeon leather, spears too casual to be hunting, too careful to be lost. Jolbon scouts find him first. The bow is already in the pine needles. His hands are empty and shaking anyway.
blocks.ko: 강물기가 채 마르기 전에 소나무가 빈 곳이 아니게 된다. 연씨 가죽 두 사람, 사냥이라기엔 창이 너무 대충이고, 길 잃었다기엔 너무 조심스럽다. 졸본 척후가 먼저 찾는다. 활은 이미 솔잎 위. 손은 비었는데도 떤다.

blocks.html: Pine valleys, crow clans, and nobody waiting for a king.
blocks.ko: 소나무 골짜기, 까마귀 가문, 그리고 임금을 기다리는 이는 아무도 없다.

blocks.caption: From a borrowed stable to a valley of five roofs. The turtles handled the middle part.
blocks.ko: 빌린 마구간에서 지붕 다섯 개의 골짜기까지. 가운데 구간은 거북이들이 맡았다.

blocks.speaker: Scout
en: Stop— stop stop—
Bow—

blocks.speaker: Second scout
en: I got him I got—
Red. That’s not ours.
Down. It’s down.
Don’t— spear. Please.
Water—

blocks.speaker: Scout
en: Hands. Hands where I can see.
You deaf?
Yeah. Yeah look.
Just— I ran. River. That’s it.

blocks.speaker: Second scout
en: Name. Fast.
If Tabal has to come out here I’m blaming you.
lines: 타발 어른이 여기까지 나오면 너 탓이다.

en: Jumong.
Jumong. That’s— that’s the name.

blocks.speaker: Scout
en: You’ll get Tabal.
Walk. If you trip I swear—

blocks.html: He looks past the spear. The pine behind the man is a better door than the man’s face.
blocks.ko: 창 너머를 본다. 남자 뒤의 소나무가 그 얼굴보다 나은 문이다.

blocks.html: They bring him in at dusk, not as a guest. One scout keeps looking back like the pines might grow more men. The valley opens under grey giwa. On the porch Yeon Tabal, chieftain of Jolbon, holds a cup he is not drinking.
blocks.ko: 해질녘에 그를 데려오지만 손님으로는 아니다. 척후 하나가 소나무에서 사람이 더 자라 나오기라도 할 것처럼 자꾸 뒤를 본다. 회색 기와 아래 골짜기가 열린다. 누대에는 졸본의 족장 연타발이 잔을 들고 있다. 마시지는 않는다.

blocks.label: Tabal’s Hall
blocks.ko: 연타발의 대청

blocks.html: Tabal walks him across the packed earth like a man showing a storeroom to a thief: grain porch, well, pine, five roofs that will not share a yard.
blocks.ko: 타발은 도둑에게 곳간을 보여 주듯 그를 데리고 다진 흙을 걷는다. 곡식 누대, 우물, 소나무, 마당을 나누지 않는 지붕 다섯.

blocks.caption: The chief of Jolbon. He shows thieves his storeroom on purpose.
blocks.ko: 졸본의 우두머리. 일부러 도둑에게 곳간을 보여 준다.

blocks.html: Inside, the hall is torches and a man who has not offered a mat. They put Jumong on his knees, packed earth in the weave of his red silk. He tries a grin. It does not survive the torches.
blocks.ko: 안으로 들어가면 대청은 횃불뿐이고, 자리를 내주지 않은 남자가 있다. 그들이 주몽을 무릎 꿇린다. 붉은 비단 결에 다진 흙이 밴다. 웃어 본다. 웃음은 횃불 앞에서 살아남지 못한다.

en: So who sent you.
Nobody sent me.
Your men grabbed me. I was just— here.
lines: 당신 사람들이 잡았어요. 그냥… 여기 있었어요.

en: I asked for a name.
Jumong.
That’s the name.
Your clothes don’t look like anything nearby.
Mohe? Khitan? Or the commandery?
lines: 네 옷은 이 근처 어디에도 안 닮았다.

blocks.html: At Tabal’s shoulder stands a woman in dusty-rose silk with a tally-stick in her hand. She has not looked at him once.
blocks.ko: 타발의 어깨 곁에 회분홍 비단 차림의 여자가 셈 막대를 쥐고 서 있다. 그를 한 번도 쳐다보지 않았다.

en: Pretty. Just—
Eyes. Front.
Count the dirt.
Not him.
Ow— I said it.

blocks.html: He thinks it with his mouth shut: So this is how I die, for a compliment, in a hall that smells like pine smoke.
blocks.ko: 입을 다문 채로 생각한다. 이렇게 죽는구나. 칭찬 한마디에, 솔 연기 냄새 나는 대청에서.

blocks.html: Tabal notices the bow. The wood is wrong for every hand in the room except one.
blocks.ko: 타발이 활을 알아본다. 이 방의 손들 중 하나를 빼고는 다 맞지 않는 나무.

blocks.html: They put Jumong’s bow in Tabal’s hands. He cannot pull the string, and the limb does not do him the courtesy of bending.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 활을 타발 손에 쥐여 준다. 시위를 당길 수가 없다. 몸통은 휠 예의도 없다.

en: Stop!
Hands off him.
…Whose son are you.
Son of Haemosu.
The bow knows. I didn’t ask it to.
lines: 활이 알아요. 제가 부탁한 건 아닌데.

blocks.html: He gives it back, and the wood stays as it was, which is worse than if it had snapped.
blocks.ko: 돌려준다. 나무는 원래대로 남는다. 부러진 것보다 그게 더 나쁘다.

en: You're a slave. My daughter's.
Shed. You hunt, you eat.
I do not want ash tracked into my hall.
lines: 내 마루에 재 끌어들이고 싶지 않다.

blocks.html: For a week Tabal uses him like a tool he has not paid for. West millet has a boar. Two cousins have a ditch and a knife each. Jumong hits both problems and sits in the dirt until someone tells him to stand. Tabal does not thank him. He just stops inventing work.
blocks.ko: 일주일 동안 연타발은 값을 안 매긴 연장처럼 그를 쓴다. 서쪽 조에 멧돼지. 사촌 둘은 도랑 하나와 칼 하나씩. 주몽은 둘 다 맞히고 일어서라는 말을 기다리듯 흙에 앉는다. 연타발은 고맙다는 말을 안 한다. 일만 안 만든다.

en: The millet likes you. I don’t.
Stay anyway.
Shed stays the shed.
Yes sir.
…The well’s nicer though.
Then go fetch. Out.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S3 ends here.

blocks.label: The Hunt Muster
blocks.ko: 사냥 점고

blocks.html: Tabal’s daughter Sosuno, a widow, is already on the grain porch, running Jolbon before she has priced the exile: spear-count, west line, who eats, who rides. The yard answers her first and her father second.
blocks.ko: 연타발의 딸 소서노는 과부다. 그녀는 이미 곡식 누대에 있고, 망명객의 값을 매기기도 전에 졸본을 굴리고 있다. 창 점고, 서쪽 줄, 누가 먹고 누가 타는지. 마당은 아버지보다 그녀에게 먼저 대답한다.

blocks.caption: Tabal’s daughter. She has priced every man in the yard, and she has not finished with this one.
blocks.ko: 타발의 딸. 마당의 사내 값을 모두 매겼고, 이 사내는 아직 셈이 안 끝났다.

en: West line. Two short.
You. Spear. Not that one, the one that isn’t bent.
We leave at first light. If you’re late I leave you.
lines: 너. 창. 그거 말고, 안 휜 거.

blocks.speaker: A hunter
en: Yes—
Not yes. The count.
East, you’re overlapping. Split.
If I have to say it twice you sit the hunt out.
lines: 두 번 말하게 하면 사냥 빠져.

blocks.speaker: A hunter
en: —Split. Sorry.

blocks.html: She does not smile when they move. She does not thank them. She does not raise her voice. The spears go where the chin points.
blocks.ko: 움직이면 웃지 않는다. 고맙다는 말도 없다. 목소리를 높이지 않는다. 창은 턱이 가리키는 데로 간다.

blocks.html: Then the wet man is in the yard. Red silk. A back she has not counted. The yard goes quiet. Nobody dropped a spear. They just stopped being loud, because she did.
blocks.ko: 그때 젖은 사내가 마당에 있다. 붉은 비단. 세지 않은 등. 마당이 조용해진다. 창을 떨어뜨린 사람은 없다. 그녀가 먼저 입을 다물어서, 다들 따라 다물었을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: Something in her goes stupid while the chin stays up. His father’s name she heard in the hall and filed under nonsense. The line of a shoulder she cannot file anywhere. She will deny all of this to the millet.
blocks.ko: 턱은 그대로인데 그녀 안의 무언가가 바보가 된다. 그의 아버지 이름은 대청에서 듣고 헛소리로 치워 두었다. 어깨 선은 치워 둘 데가 없다. 이 모든 걸 기장한테는 부인할 것이다.

en: …Next.
I said next.
Don’t look at me. Look at the line.

blocks.html: Little Sosuno is purring so loud she can hear it in her teeth. Hungry. Stupid. Staring at his mouth like it is a job. She keeps the spear-count going with a voice that does not shake. The other voice is not for the yard.
blocks.ko: 작은 소서노가 그르렁거린다. 이빨까지 들린다. 배고프고. 바보고. 입이 일인 것처럼 본다. 창 점고는 안 떨리는 목소리로 한다. 다른 목소리는 마당 것이 아니다.

en: Oh you like him. You like him immediately. Shut up.
Look at that face. That chest. Wet. I could—
Not here. Not with father. Purr quieter. I said quieter—
lines: 저 얼굴. 저 가슴. 젖었어. 내가—
여기선 안 돼. 아버지 앞에서. 좀 작게 그르렁거려. 작게—

en: Sosuno.
The line.
I have the line.
West is short two. I said that.
Sun’s in my eyes.

blocks.html: Chin up, she is her father’s hall. Then his red back crosses the packed earth and the chin fails when nobody is looking. Heat at the throat.
blocks.ko: 턱을 들면 아버지의 대청이다. 붉은 등이 다진 흙을 가로지르면, 보는 사람 없을 때 턱이 무너진다. 열이 목.

blocks.html: The counting-voice says one, two, three. The other voice puts his mouth at her neck. Outside, she is already walking away.
blocks.ko: 세는 목소리는 하나, 둘, 셋. 다른 목소리는 그의 입을 목덜미에 둔다. 겉으로 그녀는 이미 걸어가고 있다.

blocks.html: She starts calling him names because looking is worse. Big idiot is the one that sticks. He answers to it on the third day, cheerful, which makes it worse.
blocks.ko: 보기보다 싼 게 욕이라서 욕을 시작한다. 큰 바보가 남는다. 사흘째에 그가 그 이름으로 대답한다. 기분 좋게. 그게 더 싫다.

blocks.html: She points him at the west millet with two fingers, the way she points at weather, and he hauls the sacks grinning as if the job were a favor. The porch hears the laugh and pretends it is a cough.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 날씨를 가리키듯 두 손가락으로 서쪽 기장을 가리키고, 그는 일이 무슨 부탁이라도 되는 양 웃으며 가마니를 나른다. 누대는 그 웃음을 듣고 기침인 척한다.

en: Wrong stack. Do it again.
Ditch. Now. And don’t talk in the ditch.
Count the sacks. Don’t grin.

blocks.html: She makes him wring the rope until his hands complain, and she watches the hands, not the grin.
blocks.ko: 줄을 짜게 한다. 손이 불평할 때까지. 그녀는 웃음이 아니라 손을 본다.

en: Pull. Don’t chat with the rope.
Grinning’s extra. I didn’t order it.

blocks.html: She tells the yard, and herself, Work first. Looking later. The yard believes her. She doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 마당에게, 그리고 자신에게 말한다. 일이 먼저. 보는 건 나중. 마당은 믿는다. 그녀는 아니다.

blocks.html: Soon the porch has a name for him too: Sosuno’s worker. She hates how easily it fits.
blocks.ko: 곧 누대도 그를 부르는 이름이 생긴다. 소서노의 일꾼. 그녀는 그게 너무 쉽게 맞아떨어지는 게 싫다.

en: It's not like that. Worker.
Move the sack.
That’s my worker.
Not yours to stare at.
So how long has it been.
Don’t— don’t grin like you found something.
lines: 웃지 마, 뭐 찾은 것처럼 웃지 마.

en: Then why are you furiously blushing.
I’m also not stopping.
The count. Not you.
Move.
Hi.
Not hi.
Around. Big idiot.
Don’t follow me.
Wasn’t.
Well’s that way.
Other water exists.
Use it.
Moving.
See? Moved.
You’re fun when you’re like this.
I’m not fun.
I’m working.
Don’t grin at the work.

blocks.html: One morning she dumps a bucket at his boots and does not bother pretending it slipped. He laughs. Then he says it like it is nothing.
blocks.ko: 어느 아침, 그녀는 그의 신발에 두레박을 쏟고 미끄러진 척도 하지 않는다. 그는 웃는다. 그러고는 아무것도 아닌 것처럼 말한다.

en: Watch it.
Or don’t. Drown. Whatever.
Hey.
You’re pretty when you’re mean.
Like— actually. Sorry. Not sorry.
Ha—!?
Who’s— pretty, what—
It’s not like that!!
Big idiot. Go. Go go—
lines: 이 큰 바보. 가. 가 가—

en: Going. Going.
Sleeve’s wet. Thanks.

blocks.html: He wrings the sleeve on the way to the shed. She waits until the yard is empty. Then she hides her whole face in the dusty-rose, red to the hairline, whispering idiot at nobody.
blocks.ko: 그는 헛간으로 가며 소매를 짠다. 마당이 빌 때까지 기다린다. 그제야 회분홍에 얼굴을 묻고, 머리끝까지 빨개진 채로, 없는 사람을 향해 바보라고 한다.

blocks.label: Upstairs
blocks.ko: 윗방

blocks.html: She does not stay in the yard. Chin still up, she takes the loft stairs two at a time like a woman with grain to count. The window faces the millet: his shirt off, red silk knotted at the hip, a back doing work. Whose son he is can wait. The muscles cannot.
blocks.ko: 마당에 남지 않는다. 턱은 든 채, 곡식 세러 가는 여자처럼 다락 계단을 두 칸씩 오른다. 창은 기장밭을 향한다. 저고리를 벗고, 붉은 비단을 허리에 묶은, 일하는 등. 누구 아들인지는 나중 문제다. 근육은 아니다.

blocks.html: Sosuno lies on her thatched bed the first night and tells the thatch she is only tired.
blocks.ko: 첫날 밤 소서노가 초가지붕 침상에 눕고, 초가에게 그냥 피곤한 거라고 말한다.

blocks.html: She tries to fight it with a count. The count knows his mouth.
blocks.ko: 숫자로 싸워 보려 한다. 숫자는 그의 입을 안다.

blocks.html: His face comes first, then the rest of him, arriving in the dark behind her eyes; she gets stuck on the bare back the yard already ruined her with. Her hand slips down between her legs while the other stays over her mouth, as if the mouth were the scandal. She imagines him inside her and hates the thought even as she spends it, then scolds the heat for using his face. The heat does not apologize.
blocks.ko: 얼굴이 먼저, 그다음 나머지가 눈 뒤의 어둠으로 들어온다. 마당에서 이미 그녀를 망쳐 놓은 그 맨등에 생각이 걸린다. 한 손은 다리 사이로 미끄러지고, 다른 손은 입을 막는다. 입이 추문이라도 되는 것처럼. 그가 안에 들어오는 것을 상상하고, 그 상상을 다 써 버리면서도 싫어하고, 그의 얼굴을 빌려 쓴 열을 꾸짖는다. 열은 사과하지 않는다.

blocks.html: The first night does not leave the bed. Morning will have to come up the stairs and fetch her.
blocks.ko: 첫날 밤은 침상을 떠나지 않는다. 아침이 계단으로 올라와 데려가야 한다.

blocks.html: Another afternoon. The dusty-rose is hiked, her thighs apart on the timber, one hand over her mouth and the other talking to the part of her that does not run a hunt: Little Sosuno.
blocks.ko: 또 다른 오후. 회분홍을 걷어 올리고 나무 바닥에 허벅지를 벌린 채, 한 손으로 입을 막고, 다른 손으로는 사냥을 돌리지 않는 쪽의 자신에게 말을 건다. 작은 소서노.

en: Idiot. Don’t grin in my head.
This is your fault, big idiot.
Little Sosuno… you’re hungry today aren’t you…
I don’t blame you…. mmm! look at him…
Those big muscles…. chest…. back….
Ah fuck dripping wet again…
Out hunting for meat…
I want you to fill me up with some of that meat….

blocks.html: Tabal is in the doorway of the yard, not the loft, and his voice still climbs the stairs.
blocks.ko: 타발이 마당 문간에 있다. 다락이 아니다. 목소리는 그래도 계단을 올라온다.

en: Sosuno!
West count. Now.
Don’t make me climb.

소서노. 네가 골랐으면 네가 지켜. 잔치 없다.

blocks.html: Tabal sets a vermilion cord where a feast would have been, a short red line, two people who have already spent the night.
blocks.ko: 연타발이 주홍 끈을 놓는다. 잔치가 있었을 자리에. 짧은 붉은 선. 이미 밤을 보낸 두 사람.

blocks.label: Five Tribes
blocks.ko: 오부

blocks.html: Jolbon is five roofs that will not share a yard. Cousins cut cousins over a ditch, a ford, a winter store. Jumong watches it for a week and then says it in the hall, easy, the way he hauls sacks.
blocks.ko: 졸본은 마당을 안 나누는 지붕 다섯이다. 사촌이 사촌을 벤다. 도랑, 여울, 겨울 곳간 때문에. 주몽은 일주일을 보다가 대청에서 말한다. 가마니 나르듯, 쉽게.

blocks.hanja: 五部
blocks.html: Five roofs, five chiefs, five animals on five banners, and one valley too small for all of them. Remember the shape. Six hundred years from now they will be Goguryeo’s five commands, and they will still not share a yard.
blocks.ko: 지붕 다섯, 족장 다섯, 깃발마다 짐승 하나, 그리고 다 들어가기엔 좁은 골짜기 하나. 이 모양을 기억해 두라. 육백 년 뒤 이들은 고구려의 다섯 부가 되고, 그때도 마당을 나눠 쓰지 않는다.

en: You keep cutting each other.
A ditch is not a country.
I crossed a river on turtles. You fight over who owns the mud.
lines: 나는 자라 타고 강을 건넜소. 여기는 진흙 주인 싸움이오.

en: …Watch your mouth.
Those are my cousins.
They have been mine longer than you have been dry.
Then make them one hall.
Five fires, one roof.
Or keep the ditches. I can leave a bow on dirt again.
lines: 아니면 도랑이나 지키시오. 활은 또 흙에 둘 수 있소.

blocks.html: He does not conquer them. He walks the five yards with the same grin he used on Sosuno, and the same refusal to be impressed by a feud. Grain is counted in one book. Fords are shared. A cousin who draws in the ditch finds Jumong already there, bow unstrung, talking about weather until the cousin looks stupid.
blocks.ko: 정복하지 않는다. 소서노에게 쓰던 그 웃음으로 다섯 마당을 걷고, 원한에 감명받은 척을 거부한다. 곡식 셈은 하나로 합친다. 여울은 같이 쓴다. 도랑에서 칼을 뽑는 사촌 앞에, 이미 주몽이 있다. 활시위는 풀어 두고, 날씨 이야기를 해서 사촌이 바보가 되게 한다.

blocks.html: What he calls a talk, the valley will call the first summit of the five tribes: five fires in a ring the yard can hold, no dais, knees, a ditch demoted to a line on the ground. For once the smoke agrees.
blocks.ko: 그가 이야기라 부르는 것을 골짜기는 다섯 부족의 첫 회의라 부를 것이다. 마당이 감당할 만한 고리에 불 다섯, 대좌 없이 무릎들, 땅 위의 선으로 강등된 도랑. 이번만은 연기가 동의한다.

blocks.label: The First King
blocks.ko: 초대 왕

blocks.html: After the marriage the five tribes sit in Tabal’s hall and do the thing they hate more than a ditch: they agree. They vote Jumong first king. Nobody remembers him asking; the grin had already become a roof.
blocks.ko: 혼인 뒤에 다섯 부족이 연타발의 대청에 앉아 도랑보다 싫은 일을 한다. 합의다. 주몽을 첫 왕으로 뽑는다. 그가 청했다고 기억하는 사람은 없다. 그 웃음이 이미 지붕이 되어 있었다.

blocks.html: The Crow roof votes with the others, a dark sleeve, a short nod, the king already grinning like it hurts.
blocks.ko: 까마귀 지붕이 다른 이들과 함께 표를 던진다. 어두운 소매, 짧은 고개. 왕은 이미 아픈 것처럼 웃고 있다.

en: …Fine.
King, then.
If the ditches start again I will say I told you.
Eat. Stay. Wear it.
lines: 도랑이 다시 열리면 내가 그랬다고 한다.

en: I will.
Not for the chair.
For the roof.

blocks.html: Sosuno is the first queen of a country that still smells like millet. The cord is still new. The sacks have not learned to be tribute.
blocks.ko: 소서노는 아직 기장 냄새 나는 나라의 첫 왕비다. 끈은 아직 새것이다. 가마니는 조공을 아직 배우지 못했다.

blocks.html: Sosuno was the daughter of Yeon Tabal, a man of Jolbon… She lived as a widow in Jolbon. Later, when Jumong was no longer tolerated in Buyeo… he fled south to Jolbon, founded a capital called Goguryeo, and took Sosuno as his consort. She gave a great deal of help in laying the foundations and building the kingdom, so Jumong favoured her with especial warmth…
blocks.ko: 소서노는 졸본 사람 연타발의 딸이다… 졸본에서 과부로 살았다. 뒤에 주몽이 부여에서 용납되지 못하여… 남쪽으로 달아나 졸본에 이르러, 도읍을 세워 고구려라 부르고 소서노를 맞아 왕비로 삼았다. 그녀가 나라의 터를 열고 업을 세우는 데 내조가 자못 컸으므로, 주몽이 그녀를 특히 두텁게 아꼈다…
blocks.hanja: 召西奴，卒本人延陁勃之女…寡居于卒本。後朱蒙不容於扶餘…南奔至卒本，立都號高句麗，娶召西奴為妃。其於開基創業，頗有内助，故朱蒙寵接之特厚…
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 23, Baekje Annals — King Onjo, accession (variant account, 一云)

blocks.html: King and queen on packed earth, no throne between them, the yard they already know how to fight in.
blocks.ko: 다진 흙 위의 왕과 왕비. 사이에 옥좌 없이. 이미 싸울 줄 아는 마당.

blocks.html: He sleeps beside a queen who still counts fires, one, two, three, even with a crown in the room.
blocks.ko: 여전히 불을 세는 왕비 곁에서 잔다. 하나, 둘, 셋. 방에 왕관이 있어도.

blocks.html: In the new room the dusty-rose has gone richer; the dare is the same. She turns him over and looks at the back she once inventoried from a porch.
blocks.ko: 새 방에서 회분홍은 더 짙어졌고, 도전은 그대로다. 그녀가 그를 돌려 눕히고, 예전에 누대에서 하나하나 훑던 그 등을 본다.

en: Like a queen, then.
Don’t you dare be gentle about the title.

blocks.html: The blushing queen still hides her mouth in her own wrist.
blocks.ko: 붉어지는 왕비가 여전히 제 손목에 입을 숨긴다.

en: I’m blushing— don’t you dare stop

blocks.label: The Pine Kingdom
blocks.ko: 소나무 나라

blocks.html: Word reaches the millet porch: Oi, Mari, and Hyupbo did not vanish. They reached a pine roof that is not Tabal’s.
blocks.ko: 기장 누대에 소식이 닿는다. 오이, 마리, 협보는 사라지지 않았다. 연타발의 것이 아닌 솔 지붕에 닿았다.

blocks.html: It is the Pine Kingdom, a stand of old pines with a hall under them, where Song Yang, king of the pine roof, has been feeding them and deciding what they are worth. Jumong goes to fetch them himself.
blocks.ko: 소나무 나라다. 오래된 솔숲 아래 대청이 있고, 거기서 솔 지붕의 임금 송양이 셋을 먹이며 그 값을 따져 왔다. 주몽이 몸소 데리러 간다.

blocks.html: Old trees, older pride, and a king who got here first.
blocks.ko: 오래된 나무, 더 오래된 자존심, 그리고 먼저 와 있던 임금.

lines: 이 솔나라는 네가 알에서 나오기 전부터 이름이 있었다.
en: This pine country had a name before you hatched.
Then put the name on the mark.
One arrow. Then we talk.

blocks.html: Song Yang’s arrow is honest and short. It hits wood. It does not hit the knot.
blocks.ko: 송양의 화살은 정직하고 짧다. 나무에 맞는다. 옹이에는 안 맞는다.

en: The pine country is under this roof.
Take the three. They ate.

blocks.html: At dusk the three come out of the pine hall, earth-tone silk, thinner, grinning like men who were not sure of the door.
blocks.ko: 해질녘 셋이 솔 대청에서 나온다. 흙빛 비단, 더 야위고, 문을 확신 못 했던 사람들의 웃음.

blocks.html: Years later, the bow will wait on packed earth, and the yard will be quieter than a feast, which is how this country keeps a death.
blocks.ko: 몇 해 뒤, 활은 다진 흙 위에서 기다리게 될 것이다. 마당은 잔치보다 조용할 것이다. 이 나라는 그렇게 죽음을 지킨다.

blocks.label: Dawn in the Cavern
blocks.ko: 동굴의 새벽

blocks.html: Later he goes back to the mouth in the hill, the same stone and the same leaf-light, to pray the way a man prays when a hall has already named him and he still does not quite believe the name. Night thins. At dawn the light breaks through.
blocks.ko: 나중에 그는 산허리의 그 입으로 돌아간다. 같은 돌, 같은 잎빛. 대청이 이미 이름을 붙여 준 뒤에도 그 이름을 다 믿지 못하는 사람이 비는 방식으로 빈다. 밤이 얇아진다. 새벽에 빛이 틈을 낸다.

en: Father!
If you’re listening— they made me king. Me. Of a whole valley. What am I supposed to do with it?
lines: 듣고 계시면… 저더러 왕을 하래요. 제가요. 골짜기 하나를요. 이걸 어떻게 해야 돼요?

blocks.html: Gold where the dark had been, and too tall for a lamp. Haemosu lets himself be seen at last: silver-white hair, the sun’s hour delayed on purpose, looking at his son the way he once looked down from a chariot rail.
blocks.ko: 어둠이던 자리에 금빛이 들고, 등잔이라기엔 너무 크다. 해모수가 마침내 모습을 드러낸다. 은빛 흰 머리, 일부러 늦춘 태양의 시각, 한때 수레 난간에서 내려다보던 눈으로 아들을 본다.

en: Jumong…. my son…
Father… are you even listening to me?
lines: 아버지... 제 말을 듣기는 하시는 거예요?

en: It is to build a new world.
Build a world of your own…. my son…!

blocks.html: He comes out of the cavern a king the valley already voted for, and a son who finally saw the face that had been the hour. The chronicles start the years from here. His descendants will push the borders until Goryeo is the largest kingdom in Samhan — a later argument, a later map. This morning is only a roof, a grin, and a gold break in the stone.
blocks.ko: 골짜기가 이미 뽑은 왕으로, 시각이던 얼굴을 드디어 본 아들로, 동굴에서 나온다. 편년은 여기부터 해를 센다. 자손은 국경을 밀어 삼한에서 가장 큰 나라를 만들 것이다 — 나중의 싸움, 나중의 지도. 이 아침은 지붕과 웃음과, 돌 틈의 금빛뿐.

blocks.label: Two Sons
blocks.ko: 두 아들

blocks.html: Sosuno’s boys, Onjo and Biryu, watch the well the way other boys watch a hunt. Rope, bucket, their mother’s chin.
blocks.ko: 소서노의 아들 온조와 비류가 우물을 본다. 다른 아이들이 사냥을 보듯. 줄, 두레박, 어머니 턱.

blocks.caption: Sosuno’s younger boy. He watches everything, including his brother.
blocks.ko: 소서노의 작은아들. 모든 걸 지켜본다. 형까지도.

en: Mother’s counting again.
I’m staying near the porch.
I’m going farther. When I’m bigger.
Don’t tell her I said that.
lines: 난 더 멀리 갈 거야. 크면.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S5 ends here.

blocks.label: Dongmyung
blocks.ko: 동명성왕

en: You learn something from founding a country twice.
The second one is easier.
lines: 나라는 두 번 세워 보면 아는 게 있습니다.

blocks.html: Word comes from Buyeo while the new country is still learning its name. Yuhwa has stopped. The hall that took her in keeps the body. The door that opens next is not a mortal door.
blocks.ko: 새 나라가 아직 제 이름을 익히는 동안, 부여에서 소식이 온다. 유화가 멈췄다. 그녀를 거둔 대청이 몸을 지킨다. 다음에 열리는 문은 사람 문이 아니다.

blocks.html: Heat in a room that had gone cold. Gold where the lamp had failed. Haemosu is simply there — chariot left in the yard like a horse someone could not bear to stable.
blocks.ko: 식은 방에 열기가 든다. 등잔이 죽은 자리에 금빛. 해모수가 그냥 있다 — 마당에 세워 둔 수레는, 차마 외양간에 넣지 못한 말처럼.

en: Yuhwa.
I didn’t give this to my little brother.
Your hand.
You’re late.
The copper room… stayed warm. Even when you weren’t in it.

lines: 빈 자리가 하나 있다. 내가 지는 쪽에.
en: That time I came down.
This time you come up.
There’s an empty seat. On the side where I set.

lines: 그 빛… 여울에서 올려다보던 거랑은 다르네요.
en: That light… it isn’t the one I looked up at from the shallows.
It’s cold.
Still… across from you is fine.
Then come.
The chariot yields the night.

blocks.html: He does not ask a question. She takes the hand that once could not let go of her. Buyeo keeps a grave. Its records say a river-daughter died. The sky, which keeps poorer records, has a moon the next night.
blocks.ko: 그는 묻지 않는다. 한때 그녀를 놓지 못하던 그 손을, 유화가 잡는다. 부여는 무덤을 지킨다. 그곳 기록은 하백의 딸이 죽었다고 한다. 하늘은 기록을 덜 남기는 편이라, 이튿날 밤부터 달이 있다.

blocks.html: Jumong spends the rest of his life driving the western commanderies from the river valleys, and the country grows the way countries grow in old stories: one bowshot, one bride, one sworn brother at a time. He dies in the autumn of the year Yuri comes south. The hall names him Dongmyung, Bright of the East, and leaves his bow on the packed earth.
blocks.ko: 주몽은 남은 생을 중원의 군현을 강가 골짜기에서 몰아내는 데 쓰고, 나라는 옛이야기 속 나라들이 자라는 방식으로 자란다. 화살 한 발, 신부 한 사람, 의형제 한 명씩. 유리가 남으로 온 그해 가을, 그는 죽는다. 대청은 그를 동명, 동쪽의 밝음이라 부르고, 그의 활을 다진 흙 위에 놓아 둔다.

blocks.html: The chronicles will not write that the Yeon hall never forgot weighing a Go exile. Centuries later another Yeon will speak in the same short heat — and call the country by its longest name, as if shortening it were already kneeling to a softer king.
blocks.ko: 사가는 연 집안이 고씨 망명을 저울질한 일을 잊지 않았다고 쓰지 않을 것이다. 수백 년 뒤 또 다른 연이 같은 짧은 열기로 말할 것이고 — 나라를 가장 긴 이름으로 부를 것이다. 줄이는 일이 이미 부드러운 임금에게 무릎 꿇는 일이라도 되는 양.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S6 (hands into Season 2) ends here.

blocks.html: Back in Surabol, the queen is failing and the council must name who's next. It only takes one hand to lock the door…!
blocks.ko: 다시 서라벌. 여왕은 기울고, 화백은 다음 왕을 정해야 한다. 문을 잠그는 데는 손 하나면 충분하다…!

toneNote: Deliberation chambers and countdown nights — politics as a contact sport, with young flowers training at the edges.

images.alt: Chunchu standing in magenta silk at the left edge; a diagonal cascade of blank magenta map-planes across a black void
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Kim Chunchu, strategist. ONE geometric device: a diagonal cascade of blank unfurled map-sheets as hard translucent planes cutting from upper-right to lower-left — no writing, no labels. Face matches the attached portrait — short goatee, wavy dark hair with a lock on the forehead, knowing calm — rim-lit in the lower-left corner, standing (not lotus, not cross-legged meditation), one hand at his chin. Magenta #D8258C as the robe and the sheet tint; navy collar and sash the only other hue. Striking silky court hanbok, few hues, premium silk sheen and weight. Flat charcoal void. No army. No palace clutter. No clouds. No lotus. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.at: Nobody writes any of this down, which is why it needs saying.
images.alt: Ink genre painting after Shin Yun-bok: an empty floor of pale paper, Munhee tiny and kneeling at one edge knotting a travel bundle, one pink ribbon the only color
images.prompt: A Korean genre painting in the manner of Shin Yun-bok (Hyewon), fine elegant ink line with pale washes on aged hanji, wide horizontal album leaf. ICONIC MINIMAL LAYOUT: almost the whole leaf is empty pale paper standing for a bare wooden floor, one thin ink line for the edge of a folding screen at the far right. ONE device: a long low row of neatly tied travel bundles (bojagi cloth bundles) receding across the lower third like stepping stones, each one a quiet tan wash. At the near end, MUNHEE (face and garments from the attached portrait, a mature noblewoman) kneels, head bowed, pulling the knot of the last bundle tight with both hands, sleeves folded back; her dusty-pink #E07FA8 chima and the pink ribbon on the knot are the only colour. No other figures, no writing brush, no paper on the floor. One blank red seal square. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

blocks.html: Chunchu decides to travel to the East, guided by his friend Takamuko no Kuromaro.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 벗 다카무코노 구로마로의 안내로 왜국으로 건너간다.

blocks.html: Munhee packs for him. She has packed for every trip he’s ever taken. She will pack for one more. Nobody writes any of this down, which is why it needs saying.
blocks.ko: 문희가 그의 짐을 싼다. 그가 떠난 모든 길의 짐을 그녀가 쌌다. 한 번 더 쌀 것이다. 아무도 이걸 적어 두지 않는다. 그래서 말해 둘 필요가 있다.

en: How many months this time?
…I don’t know.
Then I will pack for more.

blocks.html: The King of the East receives him politely, which is its own kind of answer.
blocks.ko: 왜왕이 그를 정중히 맞는다. 그 정중함 자체가 하나의 대답이다.

blocks.caption: The King of the East. His politeness comes with a price list.
blocks.ko: 동쪽의 왕. 그의 정중함에는 값이 매겨져 있다.

lines: 백제 — 천록의 나라, 부처님의 나라 — 는 우리의 동맹이오.
en: Baekje — the Land of the Heavenly Deer, Land of the Lord Buddha — is our ally.
With respect — I must refuse peace with the Divine Country.

恐れ多いが——新羅との和睦は拒む。
jaLatn: Kudara wa warera ga meiyū.
Osore ōi ga——Shiragi to no waboku wa kobamu.

en: Baekje is a country on its way to ruin…

lines: 개소문 한 명 만큼 훌륭한 사내가 없구려.
en: Our sacred country has produced no end of talent,
and yet not one man the equal of Goryeo’s Gesomun.
You… speak our language remarkably well.

jaLatn: Sonata… waga kotoba o migoto ni ayatsuru na.

lines: 손자병법에 의하면, 최고의 전략은, 싸우지 않고 이기라는 거라고 했습니다.
이 춘추가 한마디만 더하자면, 결코 싸워야 한다면, 최고의 전략은 남의 손을 빌려서 싸우는 것입니다.
신라의 청년들이 벌써 너무 많이 숨졌습니다...!
제가 어떻게 그 부모들을 보고 체면을 서겠습니까?
en: Sun Tzu says the highest strategy is to win without fighting.
If Chunchu may add one word: if fight you must, the highest strategy is to fight by borrowing another’s hand.
Too many of Silla’s young men have already died…!
How am I to face their parents?

blocks.html: He asks for troops. He asks twice.
blocks.ko: 그는 군사를 청한다. 두 번 청한다.

blocks.html: Silla sent its high minister, the Daeachan Kim Chunchu, with others, escorting home the scholar Takamuko no Kuromaro and Nakatomi no Oshikuma; they presented a peacock and a parrot. Chunchu was kept as a hostage. Chunchu was handsome, and good at talk and laughter.
blocks.ko: 신라가 상신 대아찬 김춘추 등을 보내, 박사 소덕 다카무코노 구로마로와 소산중 나카토미노 무라지 오시쿠마를 바래다주고, 공작 한 마리와 앵무새 한 마리를 바쳤다. 이에 춘추를 볼모로 삼았다. 춘추는 용모가 아름답고 담소를 잘하였다.
blocks.hanja: 新羅遣上臣大阿飡金春秋等，送博士小德高向黑麻呂、小山中中臣連押熊來，獻孔雀一隻、鸚鵡一隻。仍以春秋為質。春秋美姿顏，善談咲。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 25, Emperor Kōtoku — Taika 3 (647)

lines: 춘추… 정말 주변 나라에 다 빌러 다닐 셈인가?
야마토에도 영원의 대장군과 신국의 검 소문은 들어 왔다. 신라가 예전만 못해도, 백제와 고구려는 우리 힘으로도 싸울 수 있어.
en: Chunchu… do you truly mean to go begging to every country around you?
Even Yamato has heard of the Eternal General and the Sword of the Divine Country. Silla may not be the power it once was, but we have strength enough to fight Baekje and Goryeo ourselves.
ja: 春秋よ……本気で周り中へ物乞いに行くつもりか？
新羅は往時ほどではないが、百済と高麗を自ら討つ力はある。
jaLatn: Shunjū yo… honki de mawari-jū e monogoi ni iku tsumori ka?
Shiragi wa ōji hodo de wa nai ga, Kudara to Kōrai o mizukara utsu chikara wa aru.

en: If you reach the eastern islands, my lord, ask after their lacquer.
And if you reach Chang’an again — ask after a woman who finishes the emperor’s sentences. Merchants hear weather early.
lines: 장안에 다시 가시거든 — 황제 문장을 끝내는 여인을 물어보십시오. 상인은 날씨를 일찍 듣습니다.

blocks.label: The Harmony Council
blocks.ko: 화백회의

blocks.html: An old High Councillor still holds the first chair. Under him sit six councillors, Yushin and Bidam among them. They still decide only by unanimity. It’s the only way this council selects anything.
blocks.ko: 늙은 상대등이 여전히 첫 자리를 지킨다. 그 아래 여섯 화백이 앉는다. 유신과 비담도 그중에 있다. 그들은 여전히 만장일치로만 정한다. 이 회의가 무엇을 고르는 방법은 그것뿐이다.

blocks.html: The technique has not changed since they crowned Dukman: initial vote, deliberation, final vote. Six Councillors. One High Councillor. Nothing moves unless the circle closes.
blocks.ko: 기법은 덕만을 세울 때부터 같다. 초투표, 숙고, 최종 투표. 대등 여섯. 상대등 하나. 원이 닫히지 않으면 아무것도 안 움직인다.

blocks.title: Session machine · 화백의 기법
blocks.caption: Initial vote → deliberation → final vote. Unanimity or the name dies in the room.
blocks.ko: 초투표 → 숙고 → 최종 투표. 만장일치가 아니면 그 이름은 방에서 죽는다.

blocks.html: Then the room turns to the question everyone has been circling: when Her Majesty fails, who next. The Sacred Bone has thinned to a sister. Someone says the name Princess Seungman the way you set a cup down that you expect everyone to drink from.
blocks.ko: 그다음 방은 모두가 돌고만 있던 질문으로 돌아선다. 폐하가 못 하시게 되면, 다음은 누구인가. 성골은 누이로 줄어 있다. 누군가 승만공주라는 이름을, 모두가 마실 줄 알고 잔을 내려놓듯 말한다.

blocks.html: One by one the hands go up. In a unanimous council a raised hand is a kind of weather — once it starts, it finishes. Yushin’s hand is among them. He has served one queen; he will serve her sister.
blocks.ko: 손이 하나씩 오른다. 만장일치 회의에서 손이란 일종의 날씨다 — 한 번 시작되면 끝난다. 유신의 손도 그 안에 있다. 여왕 하나를 섬겼으면 그 누이도 섬긴다.

blocks.html: Only one hand stays down.
blocks.ko: 손 하나만 내려와 있다.

blocks.html: Five pieces go to the yes side of the cup. Bidam’s piece stays on the no side.
blocks.ko: 패 다섯은 잔의 찬성 쪽. 비담의 패만 반대 쪽에 남는다.

blocks.title: Harmony Veto · 화백 거부
blocks.caption: Five assent, Bidam’s hand stays down. The sister’s name cannot pass.
blocks.ko: 다섯이 찬성하고 비담의 손이 내린다. 누이의 이름은 통과하지 못한다.

en: Bidam. This is the initial vote.
Five are up. What is there to deliberate.
We cannot even open the final vote.
You locked the door.

lines: 손 하나만 내리면 이 방은 끝나요.
en: One hand down and this room is finished.
You know that, and you still put it down?
I object.

blocks.html: The room does the small silence of men who have already counted themselves finished. Unanimity has failed. The name cannot pass. Someone laughs once, short, the laugh you make when a junior spoils a dinner.
blocks.ko: 방은, 이미 끝났다고 세어 둔 사내들의 짧은 침묵을 한다. 만장일치가 깨졌다. 그 이름은 통과할 수 없다. 누군가 짧게 한 번 웃는다 — 후배가 저녁을 망쳤을 때 내는 웃음.

en: Bidam… alone?
It is Princess Seungman.

lines: 성골이라는 이유만으로 나라를 맡길 수는 없습니다.
열세 해 전, 제가 덕만공주를 밀었을 때는, 그분이 제일 총명해서였습니다.
en: Princess Seungman is not as clear-sighted as Her Majesty.
We cannot hand the country over for Sacred Bone alone.
Thirteen years ago, when I stood for Princess Dukman, it was because she was the cleverest.
Now you ask me to throw that measure away.
Bidam.
Same blood. Same house.
The sister of the queen you raised.

lines: 우리는 화랑 때 백팔 대 백팔이오.
춘추 공이 장안으로 눈을 돌리는 이 밤에 — 또 한 명의 약한 성골을 올리면, 이 나라는 누가 팝니까.
en: That is why I object all the harder.
Brother.
We are one hundred and eight to one hundred and eight from our Hwarang days.
A country is not a scoreboard.
On a night when Lord Chunchu’s eyes turn toward Chang’an — if we seat another soft Sacred Bone, who sells this country.

blocks.html: Yushin does not answer the count. Something in his face closes that has been open since they were boys on the yard. The Council adjourns with no successor named.
blocks.ko: 유신은 그 수에 대답하지 않는다. 연무장 소년 시절부터 열려 있던 얼굴의 한 곳이 닫힌다. 화백은 후계 없이 파한다.

blocks.html: Class 51’s first morning. Packed earth still dark. Bidam is sixteen. His father walks him as far as the yard gate and no further — Musan hall does not hover.
blocks.ko: 오십일기의 첫 아침. 다진 흙은 아직 어둡다. 비담은 열여섯. 아버지는 연무장 문까지만 걷는다. 무산 대청은 달라붙지 않는다.

en: Bidam…
Do you know the meaning of your name.

lines: 아비달마, 더 높은 가르침에서 따온 이름입니다. 그건—
en: Yes, father…
I was named after the Abhidharma, the higher teaching. It—

lines: 젊은이로서, 화랑으로서, 그걸 지키는 게 네 일이다.
아무도 그 진실에 동의하지 않아도… 그걸 입 밖에 내면 사람들이 너를 헐뜯고 비웃어도…
너는 진실을 향해 걸어야 한다. 혼자라도. 다른 길은 없다.
이런 말, 들어 봤을 거다. 이기면 임금, 지면 역적.
아들아… 나는 네가 불의한 임금보다, 의로운 역적이 되기를 바란다.
en: Yes… the higher teaching.
And as a young man, and as a Hwarang, your duty is to uphold that.
And remember this:
Even if no one else agrees with the truth… even if speaking it out loud causes others to defame and mock you…
You must always walk toward the truth, in isolation if you must. There is no other way.
You may have heard the saying: upon victory, a king; upon defeat, a traitor.
성즉군왕 패즉역적.
Son… I need you to be a man who would rather be a righteous traitor than an unrighteous king.
Bidam… I love you…!
Go make us proud, son…!

blocks.html: He does not name the Gaya-born boy who will share the class. He only ties Bidam’s headband once, tight, and lets the gate take him.
blocks.ko: 같은 기수를 나눌 가야 난 아이는 이름 대지 않는다. 머리띠만 한 번, 팽팽히 매 주고, 문에 맡긴다.

blocks.html: In the emptied hall the incense has burned down to a stub. Bidam has not left the table. His fist is still on the wood.
blocks.ko: 텅 빈 회의장에서 향은 끄트머리만 남기고 다 탔다. 비담은 아직 탁자를 떠나지 않았다. 주먹은 여전히 나무 위에 있다.
blocks.art: Wide: the emptied council hall, every seat empty but Bidam’s, his fist still on the table.

blocks.label: Princess Seungman
blocks.ko: 승만공주

blocks.html: Princess Seungman catches him at the palace gate. Word has reached her before he has.
blocks.ko: 승만공주가 궁문에서 그를 붙잡는다. 소문이 그보다 먼저 와 있었다.

en: Bidam…! What is this I hear?
Surely not…

lines: 고려의 개소문 한 명 만큼 훌륭한 사내가 없구려.
en: Our sacred country has produced no end of talent,
and yet not one man the equal of Goryeo’s Gesomun.

blocks.html: He starts counting who would come with him, and the first door he knocks on is Alchun’s.
blocks.ko: 그는 자기를 따를 사람을 꼽아 보기 시작하고, 맨 먼저 두드리는 문은 알천의 문이다.

en: The problem is these rotten ministers!

lines: 야, 임마. 무식한 소리 좀 고마해라.
백성이 총명했다면, 대신들도 눈치채고 일을 잘하겠지.
en: Oi. Enough of that ignorant talk.
The level of the ministers is the level of the country.
If the people were clear-sighted, the ministers would notice and do their jobs.
What are you talking about!
Do you look down on the people of this sacred country?
They have always—

lines: 아니, 이렇게까지 썩었는데 아무것도 안하고 누워있으면, 지도 어느 정도 책임을 져야지.
왜 항상 나라에서 제일 무식한 것들이 맨날 “내 나라 최고”라고 하는 걸까....
en: Yes. I look down on them. So what?
If everything is this rotten and you lie there doing nothing, some of the blame is yours.
Why is it always the most ignorant in a country who shout loudest that it is the greatest…

lines: …그라고 머리 좀 써 봐라. 승만공주가 못 오르면 그 자리에 누가 앉노? 춘추다. 지가 앉을 끼다.
en: …And use your head. If Princess Seungman doesn’t take the throne, who sits there? Chunchu. He’ll take it himself.

lines: 춘추 공께서 안 그러시겠다고 이미 들었습니다.
en: I have already heard that Lord Chunchu says he will not.

lines: 절대로, 한 순간 동안도 그 입에서 나오는 말을 믿으면 안돼...!
en: Chunchu is the most cunning man in Samhan…!
Never — not for one moment — believe a word that comes out of that mouth…!

blocks.html: Before the month is out, Supum is thanked for his years and sent home, and the queen makes High Councillor of the one man who told her council no.
blocks.ko: 그달이 가기 전에 수품은 그간의 노고를 치하받고 물러나고, 여왕은 자기 회의에 아니라고 말한 단 한 사람을 상대등에 앉힌다.
blocks.art: One panel: Sunduk sets the High Councillor’s seal before Bidam across the council table; Supum’s seat empty.

blocks.html: Summer, fifth month: Taizong* marched in person against Goguryeo, and the queen sent thirty thousand troops to help him. Baekje took the chance and seized seven fortresses in the west of the country. Winter, eleventh month: the ichan Bidam was made High Councillor.
blocks.ko: 여름 5월, 당 태종*이 몸소 고구려를 치니, 왕이 군사 3만을 내어 도왔다. 백제가 그 빈틈을 타 나라 서쪽의 일곱 성을 습격하여 빼앗았다. 겨울 11월, 이찬 비담을 상대등으로 삼았다.
blocks.hanja: 夏五月，太宗親征高句麗，王發兵三萬以助之。百濟乘虚，襲取國西七城。冬十一月，拜伊飡毗曇爲上大等。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Seondeok, yr. 14 (645)

notes.html: Taizong is the temple name Tang gave him after death. In this book he is the Second Emperor.
notes.ko: 태종은 죽은 뒤 받은 묘호다. 이 책에서는 ‘두 번째 황제’다.

blocks.caption: First chair of the Harmony Council. Every vote now passes through his hands.
blocks.ko: 화백의 첫째 자리. 이제 모든 표가 그의 손을 지난다.

blocks.html: That night Bidam takes the old black headband out of the chest where he keeps it. There is still blood on it, gone brown with the years. He does not remember whose.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 비담은 궤짝에서 낡은 검은 머리띠를 꺼낸다. 아직도 피가 묻어 있다. 세월이 흘러 갈색으로 변한 피다. 누구의 피였는지는 기억나지 않는다.

en: …I gave this to that boy, back then.
Told him nobody would trouble him if he had it.

lines: 괴롭히는 사람이 나라가 될 줄은 몰랐고.
en: I did not know the one troubling him would turn out to be the country.

blocks.label: Yumjong
blocks.ko: 염종

blocks.html: Bidam does not recruit with speeches, whatever the Council thinks of him. He recruits with tea and long silences, and the first man to drink the tea is Yumjong, a True Bone whom nobody has ever accused of anything, because nobody has ever noticed him.
blocks.ko: 평의회가 어떻게 여기든, 비담은 연설로 사람을 모으지 않는다. 차와 긴 침묵으로 모은다. 그 차를 처음 마신 사람은 염종이다. 아무도 그를 무엇으로 탓한 적이 없는 진골. 아무도 그를 눈여겨본 적이 없어서다.

en: How many men, Councillor?

lines: 논은 한나절에 심는 게 아니오, 염종. 모 하나, 또 하나, 그다음은 물이 알아서 하지.
명활성을 채울 만큼. 폐하의 숨이 다하실 무렵까지는.
en: A paddy is not planted in a morning, Yumjong. One shoot, and then the next, and then the water does the rest.
Enough for the Fortress of Radiance. By the time Her Majesty’s breath runs out.
And the Marshal?

lines: 유신은 폐하가 서신 자리에 서오. 늘 그랬지.
폐하가 가시면 다음 분이 서는 자리에 설 거고, 그걸 충이라 부를 거요. 심지어 맞는 말이기도 하고.
en: Yushin stands where the Queen stands. He always has.
When she is gone he will stand where the next one stands, and he will call it loyalty, and he will even be right.

lines: 가야요. 증조부가 금관을 열쇠도 식기 전에 넘겼지요. 외성 군사들이 들으면 좋아할 겁니다.
en: He’s not even Silla, you know.
Gaya. His great-grandfather handed over Geumgwan with the keys still warm. The men in the outer works would like hearing that.

blocks.html: Bidam’s beads stop. He has said the word to Yushin’s face a hundred times on the yard, and Yushin has laughed every time. He has never heard it said like this, by a man who means it as a door.
blocks.ko: 비담의 염주가 멈춘다. 연무장에서 유신의 얼굴에 대고 그 말을 백 번은 했고, 유신은 그때마다 웃었다. 그 말을 문으로 쓰려는 사내의 입에서 이렇게 나오는 것을 들은 적은 없다.

lines: 남의 대문에 대고 외친 말은 제 집으로 돌아오는 법이오. 가야라.
en: …Careful, Yumjong.
A word you shout at a man’s gate comes back to your own. Gaya.

blocks.html: He says it once more, under his breath, as if testing the weight.
blocks.ko: 그는 숨결 아래로 한 번 더 그 말을 해 본다. 무게를 달아 보듯.

blocks.html: Gaya. A word six hundred years old that still cuts a marshal. Where did it come from? Six eggs, falling out of the sky…!
blocks.ko: 가야. 육백 년 묵은 말 한마디가 아직도 장군을 벤다. 그 말은 어디서 왔나? 하늘에서 떨어진 알 여섯 개에서…!

blocks.html: This is the story of the Gaya confederacy.
blocks.ko: 이것은 가야 연맹의 이야기다.

blocks.html: Gaya doesn’t have a crown. It has a league of iron harbours, six of them, give or take. No one king can lock the vote. Surabol would find that exhausting.
blocks.ko: 가야에는 왕관이 없다. 쇠의 항구들이 맺은 연맹이 있다. 대략 여섯. 어느 한 왕도 표를 잠글 수 없다. 서라벌이라면 진이 빠졌을 것이다.

blocks.html: The harbour that sells iron to everyone, enemies included.
