blocks.title: Gaya Confederacy · 가야
blocks.caption: Not one crown — a league of iron harbours.
blocks.ko: 왕관 하나가 아니다 — 철과 항구의 연맹.

blocks.html: Before the sons, there is a look from very high up. Ibiga keeps the sky the way other gods keep a hall — cloud is his body, the living world a map he does not usually read. Then he looks down.

blocks.caption: The sky god. Cloud is his body, and he does not usually look down.

blocks.html: On her mountain the Lady of the Right View is on watch. At first she is the ridge — jade stone, mist, a woman’s shape the mountain has not admitted yet. The mountain is a woman before it has a face. Then a face comes out of the stone. She is guarding the mountain as if it were a country. She does not look up. She does not need to. Then the sky occupies the path. Cloud comes down to the ridge.
blocks.ko: 산 위에서 정견모주가 지킨다. 처음엔 능선이다 — 옥빛 돌, 안개, 산이 아직 인정하지 않은 여자의 형. 산이 얼굴보다 먼저 여자다. 그러다 돌에서 얼굴이 나온다. 나라를 지키듯 산을 지킨다. 올려다보지 않는다. 그럴 필요가 없다. 그러다 하늘이 길을 차지한다. 구름이 능선으로 내려온다.

blocks.caption: The mountain goddess. The ridge was a woman before anyone noticed.
blocks.ko: 산신. 누가 알아채기 전부터 능선은 여인이었다.

lines: 이 길을 천 번도 더 날았는데. 왜 산이 나를 보냐.
en: That ridge…
That woman.
I have flown this path a thousand times. Why is the mountain looking back.

blocks.html: Love arrives as weather — sudden, unasked. He cannot keep the hour. He falls before he lands. The sky comes down to touch the mountain, and does not leave.
blocks.ko: 사랑은 날씨처럼 온다. 허락을 묻지 않는다. 시각을 지키지 못한다. 닿기 전에 먼저 떨어진다. 하늘이 산에 닿으러 내려오고, 떠나지 않는다.

en: Mountain.
Your shoulder… is warmer than cloud.
Your waist… steeper than cliff.
Why has heaven come down.
To look?
Or… to touch.
If to touch… kneel first.
To touch.
I looked… and could not hold back.
The knees… already are.
Then closer.
Ridges do not keep guests long.
Tonight I will make an exception.
I will keep your mouth… at my throat.

lines: 보면 볼수록 바르지 않은 생각이 든다.
네 허벅지 사이로… 하늘을 넣고 싶다.
en: Your name… Right View.
The longer I look, the less rightful my thoughts become.
I want to put heaven… between your thighs.

lines: 하늘이 산 위에 엎드리는 밤이… 그리 잦지 않으니.
en: Then stay wrongful.
Nights when heaven kneels on a mountain… are not so common.
Kneel.
All the way.

blocks.html: Cloud covers the ridge. What happens under it is not for the song. By the time the cloud thins, neither of them is kneeling, and neither of them has let go.
blocks.ko: 구름이 능선을 덮는다. 그 아래에서 일어나는 일은 노래의 것이 아니다. 구름이 옅어질 때쯤이면, 둘 다 무릎은 아니며, 둘 다 놓지 않았다.

blocks.html: He holds her with one arm. The other is cloud. The ridge is still a mountain; the mountain is still a woman. She does not look up. She does not have to.
blocks.ko: 한 팔로 안는다. 다른 팔은 구름이다. 능선은 산이고, 산은 아직 여자다. 올려다보지 않는다. 그럴 필요가 없다.

blocks.html: By morning the ridge remembers two gods who would not let go. From that heat come eggs, and from the eggs, kings.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되면 능선은 놓지 않던 두 신을 기억한다. 그 열기에서 알이 나오고, 알에서 임금이 나온다.

blocks.html: The sky god Ibiga and mountain goddess Lady of the Right View give birth to two sons, King Suro and King Ijinasi.
blocks.ko: 하늘신 이비가와 산신 정견모주가 두 아들을 낳으니, 수로왕과 이진아시왕이다.

blocks.caption: King Suro. Born from a golden egg, and in no hurry to marry anyone local.
blocks.ko: 수로왕. 황금알에서 났고, 동네 처녀와 혼인할 생각은 없다.

blocks.html: On Earth, the people sing a song to call for a new king.
blocks.ko: 땅에서는 사람들이 새 임금을 부르는 노래를 부른다.

lines: 龜何龜何 구 하 구 하 거북아 거북아
首其現也 수 기 현 야 머리를 내어라
若不現也 약 불 현 야 내어놓지 않으면
燔灼而喫也 번 작 이 끽 야 구워서 먹으리

blocks.hanja: 龜何龜何 首其現也 若不現也 燔灼而喫也
blocks.ko: 거북아 거북아 머리를 내어라. 내어놓지 않으면 구워서 먹으리.
blocks.html: Turtle, turtle — show your head. If you do not, we will roast and eat you.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 2, Wonder 2 — King Suro / Turtle Song; Ha & Mintz tr., p. 158

blocks.html: The people find a box of six eggs. Six babies hatch, Suro and Ijinasi among them. They found six kingdoms:
blocks.ko: 사람들이 알 여섯 개가 든 궤짝을 찾아낸다. 아기 여섯이 깨어나고, 수로와 이진아시도 그중에 있다. 이들이 여섯 가야를 세운다:

en: …Eggs, you said?
Six. In a box. From the sky.

blocks.html: Nobody in Samhan finds this remarkable. Silla’s founder came out of an egg. Goguryeo’s founder came out of an egg. Here are six more. At some point one has to ask what the birds were doing.
blocks.ko: 삼한의 누구도 이것을 이상하게 여기지 않는다. 신라의 시조가 알에서 나왔다. 고구려의 시조가 알에서 나왔다. 여기 여섯이 더 있다. 어느 지점에서는 그 새들이 대체 무엇을 하고 있었는지 물어야 한다.

blocks.html: Queen Heo, an Indian princess, becomes the first queen of Golden Gaya.
blocks.ko: 인도의 공주 허왕후가 금관가야의 첫 왕비가 된다.

blocks.caption: Heo Hwang-ok. She sailed farther than anyone in Samhan had heard of, and arrived dressed for it.
blocks.ko: 허왕후. 삼한의 누구도 들어 본 적 없는 먼 곳에서 배를 타고, 그에 걸맞게 차려입고 왔다.

blocks.html: She arrives on a red-sailed ship at twenty-one — foreign, luminous, built like nowhere on this coast. The beach is only a door. The first time Suro falls in love is not on the sand.
blocks.ko: 스물하나에 붉은 돛을 달고 온다. 이 해안에 없는 몸. 바다는 문일 뿐이다. 수로가 사랑에 빠지는 첫 순간은 모래가 아니다.

blocks.html: In the timber court of Golden Gaya she presents herself — no servant speaking for her, her own name, silk that does not belong to this hall. He is already on the dais. He meant to receive a princess. He receives a woman, and love hits him before protocol can stand up.
blocks.ko: 금관가야의 나무 조정에서 스스로 선다. 대신 말하는 하인 없이, 제 이름, 이 전각에 없는 비단. 수로는 이미 자리에 있다. 공주를 받으려 했다. 한 여자를 받고, 예법이 일어서기 전에 사랑에 맞는다.

blocks.html: Protocol is still trying to stand. He is already off the dais. He comes down with one arm — gold around violet, the same hold the sky used on the ridge, only this time the hall has columns and a floor.
blocks.ko: 예법이 아직 일어서려 한다. 그는 이미 자리에서 내려온다. 한 팔로 내려온다 — 금이 자주를 안고, 하늘이 능선에 쓰던 그 안음. 다만 이번엔 기둥이 있고, 바닥이 있다.

blocks.html: Servants had been sent to the ship. She refused them. So the court is where they meet — and the moment he sees her, speech leaves him like heat from an open kiln.
blocks.ko: 배로 하인을 보냈다. 거절했다. 그래서 조정에서 만난다. 보는 순간 말이 가마의 열처럼 달아난다.

en: Have you come to fetch me…
or have you already begun to take me.
With your eyes.
Your mouth… looks dry.
……You.
Your mouth…
Yes.
My mouth.
When the king looks at me like that… I get warmer.
Your hands… where do you mean to put them.
Even if you can’t speak — your hands know.
Your waist…
I mustn’t…
If I touch…
Then touch.
Since the king can’t choose… I’ll choose for you.
Here.
And here.
You’re shaking.
…Hungry…
I can’t… speak…
Then don’t speak.
If you’re hungry… take me first.
Slowly.
Not like a king — like a man.

blocks.html: He makes a sound that is nowhere near a word, and she smiles as if it were the only answer she came across the sea for.
blocks.ko: 그는 낱말이라 하기 어려운 소리를 내고, 그녀는 그것이야말로 바다를 건너온 이유의 전부라는 듯 웃는다.

blocks.html: On the hill she offers her silk trousers to the mountain spirit. He watches as if the rite were meant for him alone — jaw tight, hands useless at his sides.
blocks.ko: 언덕에서 그는 비단 바지를 산신에게 바친다. 왕은 그 의례가 자기 하나만을 위한 것처럼 본다 — 턱에 힘이 들어가고, 손은 옆구리에서 쓸 데가 없다.

en: …How will we know the mountain accepted it?

lines: 왕의 눈을 보면 압니다. / 받으신 분 표정이시네요.
en: I can tell from the king’s eyes. / You look like someone who has already received.
…It is not I who received. / …I am going mad wanting to.

lines: 이 나라요. / 그리고 오늘 밤 안엔… 왕까지.
en: This country. / And by tonight… its king.

blocks.html: Two nights in a tent by the water before anyone may say marriage. By the second dusk he can barely keep his voice steady when she says his name — and she says it into his mouth so he has to swallow it.
blocks.ko: 혼인이라는 말 전에 물가 장막에서 두 밤. 둘째 날 해질녘이면, 그가 제 이름을 부를 때 왕의 목소리가 겨우 유지된다 — 그리고 그는 그 이름을 왕의 입 안으로 넣어, 삼키게 한다.

blocks.html: She turns so he can see the curve of her hip catching lamp, and he is kissing the throat he will marry before he has permission to call it a country.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 돌아서, 등이 잡은 엉덩이 곡선을 보이게 하고, 그는 그것을 나라라고 부를 허락이 생기기도 전에 혼인할 목덜미에 입을 맞춘다.

blocks.html: When he turns to the lamp she looks at the width of his back — muscle under purple-gold silk, a king’s body that the court never sees — and does not hide how that look sits on her mouth.
blocks.ko: 그가 등잔 쪽으로 돌아설 때, 그는 그 등의 너비를 본다 — 자줏빛 금사 아래의 근육, 조정이 보지 못하는 왕의 몸 — 그리고 그 시선이 제 입에 앉는 것을 숨기지 않는다.

en: Slowly.
Your tongue — here.
The way you say my name.
The lower lip.
Below that.
More.
…At this rate I will learn the language.
Or I won’t.
I think I will fall apart first.
Inside you…

lines: 그러면 제가 매일 밤 다시 세워야 하니까.
en: Then fall.
That way I have to put you back together every night.
With hands.
With mouth.
Until the king is a king again.

blocks.html: The lamp burns low. She has taught him a dozen words since the dais, and in the dark she teaches him the rest without any — her hand on his wrist, showing him where, laughing when he is slow, then not laughing at all. She is twenty-one and crossed a sea with a stone pagoda in her ship’s hold to stop the waves; he is a king who hatched from an egg and has never once been told how. Neither of them is a god tonight. They are clumsy and greedy, and by the second hour they are good at it.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 낮게 탄다. 대청에서부터 그녀는 그에게 말 열몇 개를 가르쳤고, 어둠 속에서는 나머지를 말없이 가르친다 — 그의 손목을 잡아 어디인지 보여 주고, 그가 더디면 웃고, 이내 웃지 않는다. 그녀는 스물하나, 파도를 누르려고 배 밑창에 돌탑을 싣고 바다를 건너왔다. 그는 알에서 깨어난 왕이고, 어떻게 하는지 누구에게도 배운 적이 없다. 오늘 밤 둘 다 신이 아니다. 서툴고 욕심 많고, 한 시진이 지나면 잘한다.

en: Say it— say it again—
In your Ayuta tongue— my name—
…I have forgotten what my own country is called—

lines: 하아— 제 나라 말에도 이런 말은 없어요—
en: My king— more—
Haa— my country has no word for this either—
Not yet— don’t go—

blocks.html: The second night she is on top, violet silk off her shoulders and the gold tiger-pins still in her hair, because she refuses to take them out for a man who cannot yet say good morning in her language. He loses his own words again. She keeps hers. When she comes apart she says something in the tongue of Ayuta that nobody on this coast will ever translate, and he decides it was his name.
blocks.ko: 둘째 밤엔 그녀가 위에 있다. 자줏빛 비단은 어깨에서 흘러내리고, 금 호랑이 비녀는 머리에 그대로다 — 제 나라 말로 아침 인사도 못 하는 사내 때문에 빼 줄 생각은 없으니까. 그는 또 말을 잃는다. 그녀는 제 말을 지킨다. 무너지는 순간 그녀는 이 해안의 누구도 옮기지 못할 아유타 말을 하고, 그는 그게 제 이름이었다고 정한다.

en: My king’s— ah—
Stay— just like that—
…Wife. It is morning. / I cannot… take my hands away.

lines: 압니다. / 그런데 저는 아직 이 나라 시각을 못 배웠습니다.
en: I know. / But I have not yet learned this country’s hours.

lines: …신하들이 밖에 있소. / 들어가기 전에… 한 번만 더.
en: …The ministers are outside. / Before I go in… once more.
Once? / What a modest king.
I am not modest. / …I am only holding on. / Barely.

lines: 이제 있습니다. / 제가 가져왔으니까요 — 그 소리, 그 밤.
en: It does now. / I brought it with me — that sound, that night.

blocks.html: They are married a hundred and fifty years — the record is firm about this and entirely untroubled by it — and have ten sons. She asks that two of them carry her name instead of his. He agrees without an argument, which in the whole of this history is the single strangest thing any king does.
blocks.ko: 둘은 백오십 년을 부부로 산다. 기록은 이 대목에 단호하고 조금도 개의치 않는다. 아들 열을 둔다. 그가 그중 둘에게 왕의 성이 아니라 제 성을 물려 달라 청하자, 왕은 두말없이 그리한다. 이 역사를 통틀어 어느 왕이 한 일 중 가장 이상한 일이다.

lines: 제 나라는 이제 없습니다. 이름만 남았어요.
en: My country is gone. Only the name is left.

lines: 그러면 이름을 남깁시다. 나라는 내가 하나 더 만들면 되니.
en: Then we keep the name. I can always make another country.

blocks.html: She dies at a hundred and fifty-seven. He follows ten years later and asks to be laid where he can see her hill.
blocks.ko: 왕비는 백쉰일곱에 세상을 떠난다. 왕은 십 년 뒤에 뒤따르며, 그의 언덕이 보이는 자리에 묻어 달라 청한다.

blocks.html: Ten days of grain. One dying queen. One banner on the Radiance wall. Start counting…!
blocks.ko: 열흘 치 곡식. 죽어 가는 여왕 하나. 명활성 위의 깃발 하나. 이제 날을 센다…!

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 2:1 still composed like a symbolic old-master history painting — SISTERLY COUSINS. INTIMATE CLOSE-UP in three-quarter profile: Queen Sunduk (grey hair coiled at the back, red robe with an ochre collar) leans back against her cousin, eyes closed, a small tired smile. Seungman (long black hair loose, dark red silk with gold horses, no crown) bends her head over Sunduk’s, eyes lowered and wet, both hands at the back of the Queen’s head pushing the gold crescent binyeo into the grey bun. ONE DEVICE: the cousin’s two hands cradling the back of the Queen’s head. One small oil lamp below-left lights both faces; the right half of the frame is pure black with a faint lattice shadow. No crowns. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — QUEEN SUNDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sunduk_old.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_sunduk.png when the head is visible. Look: Pale oval face, dark calm eyes; black hair in a full coiled updo; when crowned, the gold Silla tree-and-antler crown hung with jade gogok. Dress: Crimson court robe with gold phoenix brocade, blue embroidered cape-collar, a red ribbon bow at the chest. Demeanor: Composed, faint smile, wit in the eyes; looks up at the sky (Cheomseongdae). Never weepy, never cowed. #E8552B as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Tang empress costume; fantasy tiara in place of the Silla gold crown. | QUEEN JINDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_jinduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_jinduk.png when the head is visible. #9d7bd0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.ko: 짐은 아무 해 아무 달 아무 날에 죽을 것이니, 나를 도리천 가운데에 장사 지내라.
blocks.html: I shall die in such a year, on such a month and day. Bury me in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonder 1 — Queen Seondeok knows three things in advance; Ha & Mintz tr., p. 73 · Ilyeon, Lee Byong-do ed., p. 98

blocks.html: Princess Seungman sits on the edge of the sickbed with a comb, because somebody has to do the Queen’s hair and the maids’ hands shake. They are cousins, five years apart, the last two Sacred Bone women in the world, and they have been doing each other’s hair since the younger one was tall enough to reach.
blocks.ko: 승만 공주가 빗을 들고 병상 가장자리에 앉는다. 누군가는 여왕의 머리를 해야 하고, 시녀들은 손이 떨린다. 둘은 다섯 살 터울의 사촌, 세상에 남은 마지막 두 성골 여인이고, 동생 쪽 키가 닿을 만해졌을 때부터 서로의 머리를 해 왔다.

en: Hold still, unni.
…You’ve gone thin at the temple. When did that happen.

lines: 네가 안 볼 때. 다 그때 일어나.
높이 꽂아. 도리천 가는데 신들보다는 커 보여야지.
en: While you weren’t looking. That’s when everything happens.
Pin it high. If I’m going to the Thirty-Three Heavens I want to look taller than the gods.

lines: 어디 가는 걸 장 보러 가는 것처럼 말하지 마.
en: Don’t.
Don’t talk about where you’re going like it’s the market.

lines: 미안해. 딱딱한 자리야. 방석은 하나 두고 갈게.
en: …Seungman-ah. You’ll have to sit in it.
I’m sorry. It’s a hard chair. I’ll leave you a cushion.

blocks.html: Seungman pins the binyeo high, exactly where the Queen asked, and does not answer, which is the only way she has ever won an argument with her.
blocks.ko: 승만은 여왕이 말한 바로 그 자리, 높이 비녀를 꽂는다. 그리고 대답하지 않는다. 그녀가 언니를 상대로 말다툼에서 이겨 본 방법은 그것뿐이다.

blocks.html: Bidam and Yumjong raise men at the Fortress of Radiance. The slogan is old. They only give it a banner. Yumjong holds the outer muster. Bidam walks the rampart as if the stones owed him rent. Inside the palace, the stewards count the grain and arrive at ten days. Nobody says the number aloud. Everybody schedules by it. The rebels tie on black headbands, Bidam’s old colour from the yard, so they can tell their own from the palace blue.
blocks.ko: 비담과 염종이 명활성에서 군사를 일으킨다. 구호는 오래된 것이다. 그들은 거기에 깃발만 달아 줄 뿐이다. 염종이 바깥 소집을 맡는다. 비담은 돌들이 자기에게 세라도 밀린 듯 성벽 위를 걷는다. 궁 안에서는 집사들이 곡식을 세다가 열흘이라는 답에 이른다. 아무도 그 숫자를 소리 내어 말하지 않는다. 모두가 그 숫자에 맞춰 일정을 짠다. 반란군은 비담이 화랑 시절 쓰던 검은 머리띠를 맨다. 궁의 푸른색과 제 편을 가리기 위해서다.

blocks.html: Close enough to the palace to shout at it.
blocks.ko: 궁궐에 고함이 들릴 만큼 가까운 성.

blocks.html: He carries the heavenly-horse sword in the dark. The robe eats the lamp. Only the ring pommel holds the light — a gold circle at the end of old-hall steel.
blocks.ko: 어둠 속에서 그는 천마환도를 든다. 도포가 등을 삼킨다. 고리 손잡이만 빛을 받는다 — 옛 전당의 강철 끝에 금빛 원.

blocks.hanja: 毗曇等屯於明活城 王師營於月城 攻守十日不解
blocks.ko: 비담 등이 명활성에 주둔하고, 왕사는 월성에 진을 치니, 공수한 지 열흘이 되어도 풀리지 않았다.
blocks.html: Bidam and the others encamped at Myeonghwal Fortress; the royal army camped at Wolseong. Attack and defence lasted ten days without being broken.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin (Bidam’s rebellion, 647); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2

blocks.html: Before the banner goes up he lights a stick of incense on the rampart and waits for it to take, because a man raised on this soil’s sutras does not begin a thing without the smoke. His hand is steady. Under the sleeve the beads have not moved once since the muster began.
blocks.ko: 깃발을 올리기 전, 그는 성벽 위에서 향 한 대에 불을 붙이고 연기가 잡히기를 기다린다. 이 땅의 불경으로 자란 사람은 연기 없이 일을 시작하지 않는다. 손은 흔들리지 않는다. 집결이 시작된 뒤로 소매 아래 염주는 한 번도 움직이지 않았다.

blocks.html: Mind is the root of all things: mind is the master, mind sets them moving. If the heart thinks evil and then speaks it and does it, guilt and suffering follow of themselves, as the wheel rolls in the rut.
blocks.ko: 마음은 모든 법의 근본이니, 마음이 주인이 되고 마음이 부린다. 속으로 악을 생각하여 그대로 말하고 그대로 행하면, 죄와 괴로움이 저절로 뒤따르니 수레바퀴가 바퀴 자국을 따라 구르는 것과 같다.
blocks.hanja: 心為法本，心尊心使，中心念惡，即言即行，罪苦自追，車轢于轍。
blocks.source: Dhammapada (法句經) ch. 9, The Twin Verses (雙要品), tr. Weiqinan & Zhu Jiangyan · T04n0210, p. 562a

lines: 女主不能善理 — 여주가 즉위하던 해에 방이 말했고, 날씨인 척했다.
en: A woman cannot rule well.
女主不能善理 — the room said it the year she was crowned and pretended it was weather.
Today we stop pretending.

lines: 비담 상대등께서 오신다 — 오늘은 예의가 아니라 깃발이다.
en: Open the Radiance gate.
High Councillor Bidam comes — today it is the banner, not courtesy.

blocks.html: Before noon Alchun is summoned twice — once by the Sword of Silla, once by the High Councillor with a banner — and he answers both.
blocks.ko: 정오 전에 알천은 두 번 불린다 — 신라의 도검에게 한 번, 깃발을 든 상대등에게 한 번 — 그리고 둘 다에게 답한다.

lines: 물론 우리 모두 어린 화랑 시절엔 공주를 사랑했지. 아름다운 공주였고, 우리는 젊은 사내였으니까.
나라를 위해 무엇이 최선인지 판단해야 한다. 신국은 네가 사적 충성심에 눈이 가려지지 않기를 요구한다 — 신국을 위해 무엇이 최선인지 판결하라.
en: Yushin…
Of course we all loved the princess as young Hwarang. She was a beautiful princess, and we were young men.
But those days are over now.
You need to judge what is best for the nation — and the nation demands that you not be blinded by your personal loyalties, and judge what is best for the divine nation.

lines: 너는 화랑에 충성을 맹세했고, 신국은 너에게 상대등 — 이 땅 최고의 직 — 의 권한을 맡겼다.
왕실을 향해 무기를 드는 것은 최고의 반역이다.
en: Bidam…
You swore allegiance to the Hwarang, and the divine nation has vested you with the authority of the High Councillor — the highest office in the land.
For you to take up arms against the crown would be an act of highest treason.

lines: 열흘째에 다시 물어라. 그때도 겁쟁이일 수 있다 — 다만 정확한 겁쟁이로.
en: I will not raise a blade against Bidam.
I will not raise a banner against Her Majesty.
Ask me again on the tenth day. I may still be a coward — but I will be a precise one.

blocks.html: Neither man answers him in a way that would satisfy a clerk. Yushin stares at the eastern palace. Bidam smiles as if treason were a word invented by cowards. Alchun walks back to the space between the camps and eats alone.
blocks.ko: 어느 쪽도 서기가 만족할 만한 답을 하지 않는다. 유신은 동궁을 바라본다. 비담은 반역이 겁쟁이가 만든 단어인 양 웃는다. 알천은 진영 사이 공간으로 돌아가 혼자 먹는다.

blocks.label: DAY 2
blocks.ko: 둘째 날

blocks.html: Night. Between the camps a small pavilion goes up, open on every side. No chairs. Only a low wooden table. No banner on the ridgepole. Tea already poured. A half moon in an empty sky. They meet the way they used to after sparring: gloves off, courtesy on.
blocks.ko: 밤. 두 진영 사이에 사방이 트인 작은 정자가 선다. 의자는 없다. 낮은 나무 탁자 하나뿐. 용마루엔 어느 편 깃발도 없다. 차는 이미 따라져 있다. 빈 하늘에 반달. 그들은 예전 대련이 끝난 뒤처럼 만난다. 장갑은 벗고, 예의는 갖추고.

lines: …육촌이 서라벌을 세울 때 — 이, 최, 정, 손, 배, 설.
en: Yushin.
Tea first.
…When the Six Elders raised Surabol — Lee, Choi, Jeong, Son, Bae, Seol.
Park came from an egg.
There was no Kim.
…And?

lines: 그리고 지금 이 성 안의 두 김 가문은 —
en: And now the two Kim houses inside this wall —
Surabol Kim, Alji Kim —
both imports.
I alone… am Six-Elder blood.

blocks.html: The tea cools between them. Neither man drinks enough to call it peace. Bidam smiles as if nothing ugly had been said — the same smile he wore when he crowned a woman king. Yushin sets his cup down unfinished.
blocks.ko: 차가 그 사이 식는다. 둘 다 평화라 부를 만큼은 마시지 않는다. 비담은 못된 말을 한 적 없는 것처럼 웃는다 — 여왕을 세울 때 쓰던 그 미소다. 유신은 잔을 비우지 않은 채 내려놓는다.

blocks.html: Three Hwarang. One princess. The yard remembers what the Council never wrote down.
blocks.ko: 화랑 셋. 공주 하나. 연무장은 화백이 끝내 적지 않은 것을 기억한다.

blocks.html: Bidam, Alchun, and Yushin — same Hwarang line, same bruised knuckles, same impossible orbit around Princess Dukman. They do not say the word love. The gyuku field says it for them, badly.
blocks.ko: 비담, 알천, 유신 — 같은 화랑 계보, 같은 멍든 손등, 덕만공주를 도는 같은 불가능한 궤도. 사랑이라는 말은 하지 않는다. 격구장이 대신 서툴게 말한다.

lines: 성골에 남자가 바닥나면, 가장 총명한 여자를 고르시오.
나는 어린 시절부터 덕만을 안다. 총명함에는 성별이 없다.
en: If the Sacred Bone runs out of men, pick the cleverest woman.
I have known Dukman since we were children. Cleverness is not a gender.
Well stood.
Tomorrow on the yard — the hundred-and-ninth is mine.

lines: 너희 둘은 점수 때문에 서로를 죽일 거다.
나는 가운데 있는 아이 때문에 나를 죽일 거다.
en: You two will kill each other over a score.
I will kill myself over the girl in the middle.
…That was a joke. File it as a joke.

blocks.html: Nobody writes down that Bidam’s hall shares blood-whisper with the great Sadaham — the Hwarang who conquered Gaya and refused a slave girl as prize. The chronicle only lets the resemblance show in the jaw, and in the way Bidam treats victory as something that must stay clean.
blocks.ko: 비담의 대청이 가야를 정복하고 노비를 상으로 거절한 화랑 사다함과 핏줄 소문을 나눈다는 것은 아무도 적지 않는다. 기록은 턱선과, 승리를 깨끗하게 유지하려는 버릇으로만 닮음을 보여 준다.

blocks.html: Even their names take sides. Bidam’s sounds like this soil and its sutras. Chunchu’s is a foreign classic. Any clerk across the sea could file it without asking. Nobody notices yet. Names are patient.
blocks.ko: 이름들조차 편을 든다. 비담의 이름은 이 땅과 그 경전의 소리가 난다. 춘추의 이름은 남의 나라 고전이다. 바다 건너 어느 서기라도 묻지 않고 철해 둘 수 있다. 아직은 아무도 눈치채지 못한다. 이름은 참을성이 많다.

lines: 너희 중 누가 사소한 이유로 저 아이를 울리면 — 얼굴로 점수를 맞추겠다.
en: Yushin.
Alchun.
If either of you ever makes her cry for a small reason — I will even the score on your face.

blocks.label: DAY 3
blocks.ko: 셋째 날

blocks.html: Arrows trade; messengers lie; the Harmony Council discovers it can convene without deciding anything, which is its highest form. Chunchu’s clerks call the unanimity rule quaint. Bidam calls it ours.
blocks.ko: 화살이 오가고, 전령이 거짓말하고, 화백회의는 아무것도 결정하지 않고도 모일 수 있음을 발견한다. 그것이 회의의 최고 형태다. 춘추의 서기들은 만장일치 규칙을 예스럽다고 부른다. 비담은 우리 것이라고 부른다.

blocks.html: Third night. Same pavilion. Same half moon. Bidam has brought a map — not of the siege, of the roads west.
blocks.ko: 셋째 밤. 같은 정자. 같은 반달. 비담은 포위도가 아니라 — 서쪽 길 지도를 가져왔다.

lines: 삼한은 피로도, 마음으로도 식민지가 되고 있어.
유신 — 네 눈 색은 예쁘다. 서쪽에서 온 색이다.
…내가 먼저 일어섰을 때는, 그들이 나를 개화파라 불렀지.
en: Samhan is being colonized — in blood, and in the mind.
Tang sends institutions. India sends…
…through Queen Heo’s blood, sutras.
Yushin — your eyes are handsome. They are a western colour.
…When I stood first, they called me the liberal.

lines: 열다섯 해 전, 네가 그렇게 말했을 때 — 일어나라고 했소.
en: Gaya blood came from the west too.
I… stood up.
Fifteen winters past, when you spoke — you told me to stand.
That was when you were weak.
…A joke. Drink your tea.

blocks.html: On the wall Bidam looks west and remembers a cleaner war — Jade Gate Valley, when the enemy still had the courtesy to be foreign.
blocks.ko: 성벽 위에서 비담은 서쪽을 보며 더 깨끗했던 전쟁을 떠올린다 — 옥문곡, 적이 아직 외국인이라는 예의를 지키던 때.

blocks.html: Baekje sends five hundred armoured men to slip through a valley in the dark. Their job is to bite a fortress from behind. The queen hears about it from a pond of toads. She sends steel instead of prayers.
blocks.ko: 백제가 갑옷 입은 오백 명을 보낸다. 어둠을 틈타 골짜기를 지나, 성 하나를 뒤에서 물어뜯으라고. 여왕은 그 소식을 두꺼비 우는 연못에서 듣는다. 그리고 기도 대신 칼을 보낸다.

lines: 비담 — 왼쪽 능선. 나는 마른 시내.
우소가 안장을 풀면, 위원회를 기다리지 않는다.
en: Bidam — left ridge. I take the dry creek.
If Uso loosens a saddle, we do not wait for a committee.
Finally — an enemy I am allowed to hate in public.
Alchun. On my mark.

blocks.html: They fall on the Baekje camp at dusk. Uso climbs a boulder and empties a quiver; the quiver ends before the argument does. Alchun takes the general. Bidam takes the valley’s silence.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘 백제 진영을 덮친다. 우소는 큰 돌 위에 올라가 화살을 비운다. 화살이 먼저 바닥난다. 알천이 장군을 잡고, 비담이 골짜기의 침묵을 갖는다.

lines: 목표가 성 밖이면 우리는 좋은 짝이다.
en: We make a good pair when the target is outside the wall.
Inside the wall… we will see.
Inside the wall is still the sacred country.
I do not miss.

blocks.html: Eleven years later, on Radiance’s rampart, Bidam will remember Okmun-gok as the last time Alchun stood on his side without hesitating.
blocks.ko: 십일 년 뒤 명활성 성벽에서, 비담은 옥문곡을 — 알천이 망설임 없이 자기 편에 섰던 마지막 순간으로 — 기억할 것이다.

blocks.html: Before the fourth night’s tea, Wolseong tries a quieter weapon. Chunchu sends Bupmin (21) to the steam — the water that shows a man’s inner conscience, the past that is driving his hand. Yushin is told only to keep him talking.
blocks.ko: 넷째 밤의 차 전에, 월성은 더 조용한 무기를 쓴다. 춘추가 법민 (21)을 김으로 보낸다 — 사람의 속마음과, 그 손을 움직이는 과거를 보여주는 물. 유신에게는 말만 붙들어 두라고만 한다.

lines: 샘은 네 외숙이 아는 곳이다. 네가 김씨니까 문이 열릴 거다.
en: Bupmin.
Take a jar.
The spring is a place your uncle knows. You’re a Kim — the door will open.
Splash him.
Father…
What does the water do to a man…
I understand. I’ll go.

blocks.html: This is the first time the cavern goddesses meet Bupmin. He is twenty-one. He does not yet have a king’s name. He has a jar and Chunchu’s weather.
blocks.ko: 동굴 여신들이 법민을 만나는 첫날이다. 스물하나. 아직 왕의 이름은 없다. 항아리와, 춘추의 날씨만 있다.

lines: 너… 너는 양쪽의 최선이야. 어깨는 가야. 입은 서라벌. 서 있으면 골화가 타고 오를 거야. 앉아.
en: A Kim.
Sit. No — the jar first.
You… He is the best of both. Gaya in the shoulders. Surabol in the mouth. Golhwa is going to climb you if you stay standing. Sit.

lines: 물 받아. 양심이 달라붙어. 트라우마. 원한. 그 손을 움직이는 거.
en: Oh.
A Kim we haven’t had. He’s both.
Take the water. Conscience sticks to it. Trauma. Grudge. Whatever’s driving the hand.
…And stop standing like that.

lines: 나 언덕이려 하는데, 너는 무릎 위에 두고 싶은 문제처럼 생겼어.
en: I’m trying to be a hill and you are shaped like a problem I want in my lap.
…Be careful.
If you splash it, you see why he’s doing it.
If you don’t see anything… that’s its own answer.
…He’s pretty. I’ll be quiet. I won’t be calm.
Goddesses…
Thank you. I was only—
I’ll just take the water.

blocks.html: He fills the jar. He does not stay for the lake’s other lessons. He is the best of both, and he leaves because his father told him to.
blocks.ko: 항아리를 채운다. 호수의 다른 수업은 받지 않는다. 그는 양쪽의 최선이고, 아버지가 시키니까 돌아간다.

blocks.label: DAY 4
blocks.ko: 넷째 날

blocks.html: Wolseong’s wells drop. Rumour rises to replace them. Chunchu files contingency letters the way other men file prayers.
blocks.ko: 월성의 우물이 준다. 소문이 그 자리를 채운다. 춘추는 다른 사람이 기도를 정리하듯 비상 서한을 정리한다.

blocks.html: Fourth night. Same low table under the half moon. Bidam reads a rumoured draft — never enough secretariat, never enough emperor. His voice stays pleasant. The sentences do not.
blocks.ko: 넷째 밤. 반달 아래 같은 낮은 상. 비담은 소문난 초안을 읽는다 — 집사부는 늘 부족하고, 황제는 늘 부족하다. 목소리는 여전히 부드럽다. 문장만 그렇지 않다.

lines: 화백의 만장일치 — 우리가 남긴 유일한 것 — 을 태울 셈이지.
en: What Chunchu wants…
is a country that fits inside a Tang envelope.
Central rule. Emperor. Clerks.
He would burn the Harmony Council’s unanimity — the one thing we kept.
Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.

lines: …그 여인이 즉위하던 해엔 나도, 여주를 위해 일어선 개화파였는데.
지금은 삼한 피를 지키는 자라 부르는구나. 아이러니하지, 유신?
en: Yes — and that is why you always win.
On the yard, and here.
Effort… speaks louder than my blood.
…The year they crowned her, I was the liberal who stood for the woman king.
Now they call me the blood-and-soil man. Ironic, Yushin?
…That young Hwarang is still here.
Where?

blocks.html: He folds the rumoured draft. The next sentences have been waiting in the sleeve all night.
blocks.ko: 그는 소문난 초안을 접는다. 다음에 올 문장은 밤 내내 소매 안에 있었다.

lines: 승만공주와, 김춘추의 횡포 — 둘 다 반대다.
저 파가 이기면 삼한은 그 천 해를 중국의 번국으로 살게 된다.
제 앞날을 제 손으로 정하지 못하는 나라로.
en: Princess Seungman, and the tyranny of Kim Chunchu — I stand against both.
He speaks of a thousand-year kingdom.
If his faction wins, Samhan will spend those thousand years as a Chinese vassal.
A country that never again turns its own wheel.

lines: 이 개혁이 서고, 승만공주의 인도로 가면 —
몇 해 안에 신라가 삼한에서 가장 강한 나라가 될 수도 있소.
해동 전체에서 — 동쪽 끝까지 — 일등일 수도 있소.
en: With these reforms, under Princess Seungman’s guidance —
a few harvests more, and Silla may stand first in Samhan.
First, even, in all of Haedong — 해동, the East.

lines: 이웃이 서로의 이름을 아는 나라를 원하지.
한 담장을 나누는 남이 아니라 — 진짜 겨레.
en: I do not need the strongest nation.
I want neighbours who still know one another’s names.
The young lifting the old.
A true people — not strangers who happen to share a wall.

lines: 신라가 백제와 고려에 뒤처지면, 고개로 들어오는 것은 칼과 기근이오.
en: The people’s livelihood hangs on the nation’s fullness.
Fullness hangs on institutions — on a government that can still stand.
If Silla falls behind Baekje and Goryeo, what comes through the pass is spear and famine.
Then tell me how the neighbours keep their names.

lines: 너나 왕실이, 백성이 어떻게 사는지 아느냐.
공주들이 — 춘추조차 — 도성 밖에서 한 해를 살아 본 적 있느냐.
서라벌은 사방 십 리도 못 된다. 진짜 신라가 그 둘레를 두르고 있지.
우리가 여기서 다투는 동안, 백성 — 진짜 신라인 — 은 외황제의 횡포 아래 살기를 원하지 않는다.
en: Yushin.
Do you — does the royal house — know how common people live?
Have the princesses, or even Chunchu, spent so much as one year beyond the capital?
I have.
Surabol is scarcely ten square miles, ringed by the true Silla.
While we argue here, the common people — the real Sillans — have no wish to live under a foreign emperor’s yoke.

lines: 그런데 서라벌이 어찌 진짜 신라가 아니란 말이오.
바깥사람 이야기로 치자면 — 비담 공, 바깥사람은 평생 공이 아니라 나일 것이오.
육촌의 피를 이은 공이 그 높은 집을 그리 얕보시는데,
정복당한 나라의 막내아들인 나는 목숨을 바쳐 이 땅을 지킬 각오가 돼 있소.
en: Surabol is where Hyukgosé was crowned.
Where the Six Elders laid this country’s first stone.
How, then, is Surabol not the real Silla?
As for standing outside — Lord Bidam, I will forever be more outsider than you.
You, of Six-Elder blood, speak so poorly of the halls that raised this land —
while I, last son of a conquered kingdom, am prepared to defend it with my life.

blocks.html: Yushin does not close the argument. He asks again about the pass, about names, about harvests — anything that keeps Bidam’s back to the dark. Behind the 정자, Bupmin’s jar ticks once against a post.
blocks.ko: 유신은 논쟁을 닫지 않는다. 고개, 이름, 수확 — 비담의 등이 어둠을 향하게 붙들어 두는 것이면 된다. 정자 뒤에서 법민의 항아리가 기둥에 한 번 닿는다.

lines: 그 십 리 바깥 이야기, 한 번만 더.
백성이 황제를 원치 않는다 — 그 말은, 어디서 들었소.
en: Bidam.
That ten-mile story. Once more.
The people have no wish for an emperor — where did you hear that.

blocks.html: Bupmin comes from behind to splash the water. It is ugly and precise — cavern water as a hard sheet across Bidam’s shoulders, beads and all.
blocks.ko: 법민이 뒤에서 와 물을 끼얹는다. 흉하고 정확하다 — 동굴 물이 비담의 어깨와 염주 위로 딱딱한 면처럼 떨어진다.

en: Ha…
What is this…

lines: 유신 공… 왜 아무 일도 없는데…?
en: Your trauma….
Yushin… why isn’t it doing anything…?

blocks.html: Nothing rises. No childhood. No princess. No grudge-film in the steam. The water runs off the black robe as if it had mistaken a man for a wound. Chunchu, at the pavilion’s edge, does not move. The stoic act holds; the eyes do not.
blocks.ko: 아무것도 안 뜬다. 어린 시절도, 공주도, 김 속의 한 필름도. 물은 흑의를 타고 내린다. 사람을 상처로 착각한 것처럼. 정자 가장자리의 춘추는 움직이지 않는다. 담담한 연기는 유지된다. 눈만 아니다.

lines: 들어 본 적 있어… 이 물이지…?
en: Oh… haha…
I’ve heard of this… this is that water, isn’t it…?
HAHAHAHAHA!

lines: 정녕 내가 무슨 개인적 트라우마가 있어야 한다고 생각했느냐??
한순간이라도… 단 일 초라도… 너희 생각이 그냥 형편없을 가능성…
제정신인 사내라면 누구나 반대할 가능성… 생각해 본 적 있느냐?
아니면 너희가 하는 일은 전부 옳고…
누구든 반대하는 이유는 정신의 병 뿐이라고…
하… 친구들, 오늘 밤 너희가 한 일이라곤 제 논리를 증명한 것뿐이다.
어느 나라도 이끌 자격이 없다는 걸 스스로 증명했어.
en: Behold, the arrogance of the sacred bone class!!
You really thought I had to have some sort of personal trauma??
That that was the reason I was doing all of this?
That I hated the princess? The queen?
That I hated you, Chunchu, or Yushin?
Have you ever… even for a SECOND… considered the POSSIBILITY…
that your ideas are simply terrible?
That they’ll lead this nation to ruin?
That ANY reasonable man would oppose them?
Or are you so ARROGANT to assume… that EVERYTHING you lot do is correct…
and that the ONLY reason for ANYONE to disagree… is because they were suffering some sort of mental disease? Because they were angry and bitter?
Ha… well, my friends, I’m afraid all you’ve done tonight is prove your point.
You’ve proven yourself to be unworthy of leading any country.
So please… my friends… step aside…!

blocks.html: Alchun, arriving late with a lamp, goes pale. An officer asks whether to seize the jar. Nobody answers. Bidam is still laughing, and still alive, and the beads are still counting.
blocks.ko: 늦게 등을 들고 온 알천의 얼굴이 하얘진다. 장교 하나가 항아리를 빼앗을지 묻는다. 대답하는 사람이 없다. 비담은 아직 웃고, 아직 살아 있고, 염주는 아직 세고 있다.

blocks.html: The bodhisattva relies on the perfection of wisdom, and so his mind has no hindrance. Having no hindrance, he has no fear; he passes far beyond upside-down, dreaming thought and reaches nirvana at last.
blocks.ko: 보리살타는 반야바라밀다를 의지하므로 마음에 걸림이 없고, 걸림이 없으므로 두려움이 없어서, 뒤바뀐 헛된 생각을 멀리 떠나 완전한 열반에 들어간다.
blocks.hanja: 菩提薩埵依般若波羅蜜多故，心無罣礙；無罣礙故，無有恐怖，遠離顛倒夢想，究竟涅槃。
blocks.source: Heart Sutra (般若波羅蜜多心經), tr. Xuanzang, 649 · T08n0251, p. 848c · Sanskrit: Prajñāpāramitāhṛdaya, short text (Vaidya ed.)
blocks.native: बोधिसत्त्वस्य प्रज्ञापारमितामाश्रित्य विहरत्यचित्तावरणः । चित्तावरणनास्तित्वादत्रस्तो विपर्यासातिक्रान्तो निष्ठनिर्वाणः ।
blocks.nativeLatn: bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitām āśritya viharaty acittāvaraṇaḥ | cittāvaraṇanāstitvād atrasto viparyāsātikrānto niṣṭhanirvāṇaḥ |

lines: 비담이 이기면 집사부는 고상한 취미가 된다.
비담이 져도, 우리에게는 죽어 가는 여왕과 서쪽의 당 모양 구멍이 남는다.
그 사람은 좋은 생각도 당나라 봉투에 담겨 오면 태울 사람이다. 강령의 전부가 그것이고 — 인기는 좋다.
en: If Bidam wins, the Secretariat becomes a quaint hobby.
If Bidam loses, we still have a dying queen and a Tang-shaped hole in the west.
The man would burn a good idea for arriving in a Tang envelope. That is the whole platform — and it polls well.
Munhee — pack for either weather.

lines: 여왕이 즉위하던 해에 쌌다. 너는 포위 때만 눈치챈다.
en: I already packed.
I packed the year the Queen was crowned. You only notice in sieges.

blocks.html: Alchun eats alone between the camps. Both sides send him wine. He drinks neither. Surabol will later call it treason with better stationery.
blocks.ko: 알천은 진영 사이에서 혼자 먹는다. 양쪽이 술을 보낸다. 그는 어느 쪽도 마시지 않는다. 서라벌은 나중에 더 좋은 편지지의 반역이라 부를 것이다.

blocks.label: DAY 5
blocks.ko: 다섯째 날

blocks.html: Fifth night — the pavilion again. They sit on the floor, alone, the way they used to meet on the training ground. The tea is cold before anyone raises a blade.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 밤 — 다시 그 정자. 두 사람은 바닥에서 단둘이 앉는다. 옛날 연무장에서 만나던 것과 같은 방식으로. 차가 식고 나서야 누군가 칼을 든다.

lines: 삼한의 둘째 칼 — 비담이여!! 무기를 내려놓고 푸른 달께 충성을 돌려드려라!!
en: Second Blade of Samhan — Bidam!! Lay down your arms and give your loyalty back to the Blue Moon!!

blocks.html: For a breath they are only the old score again — one hundred and eight to one hundred and eight — two boys who never let the other keep a lead. Then Bidam speaks, and the yard is gone.
blocks.ko: 한순간 둘은 다시 옛 점수판일 뿐이다 — 백팔 대 백팔 — 상대를 앞서 두지 않던 소년 둘. 그러다 비담이 입을 열고, 연무장은 사라진다.

lines: 이 나라에서 제일 똑똑한 자들은 이 나라를 미워하고,
en: Yushin.
In this country the smartest people hate this country,
and the most patriotic people… are all stupid.
That’s Silla.
The country you’re trying to sell.
Yushin….
And besides — you…
you were never even of Silla…!
Blood is inevitable.

blocks.html: The tea has not been touched. He says it like a compliment that curdled — still the gentleman, still the black robe, still the voice that once shielded this same man from the yard.
blocks.ko: 차는 손대지 않았다. 상처 주는 칭찬처럼 말한다 — 여전히 군자, 여전히 흑의, 여전히 연무장에서 이 같은 사람을 막아 세던 그 목소리.

lines: 비담 공... 우리는 함께 인생에 맹세로 한 걸로 기억하는데...
en: Lord Bidam… I remember we swore our lives to this together…

lines: 너한테는 원래 나라가 없으니, 이 나라를 팔아먹는 것도 거슬리지 않겠지...
하지만 우리는 다르다. 우리는 이 땅에서 뗄 수 없는 관계야…
내 조상이 세운 나라를 황제한테 넘겨줄 셈이냐...!
en: You never had a country of your own — selling this one must cost you nothing…
But we are different. We cannot be cut from this land…
Would you hand the country my ancestors built to an emperor…!
I am a son of the sacred country.

lines: 춘추 공은 당의 제도를 배우자는 것뿐이오. 백제는 문장이 아니라 칼로 오니까.
en: Selling — I have sold nothing.
Lord Chunchu only asks that we learn Tang’s institutions. Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.

lines: 춘추 — 春秋. 이름부터가 중국 책이다.
그런 자에게 신국의 내일을 쓰게 하겠단 말이냐.
남의 제도를 오래 배우다 보면 — 어느 아침엔, 배운 것만 남아 있을 것이다.
en: Chunchu — 春秋. The man is named after a Chinese book.
And you would let him write the sacred country’s tomorrow.
Learn another country’s institutions long enough — and one morning, the learning is all that is left.
I will raise the sacred country’s glory again,
I will return the sacred country’s future to its own people!

blocks.html: The yard after rain. Two Hwarang, neither willing to leave the mud with the score uneven.
blocks.ko: 비 온 뒤 연무장. 화랑 둘. 점수가 기우는 채로 진흙을 떠나려 하지 않는다.

en: One hundred and seven…!
Brother — today I take the lead!

lines: 일어서라. 기우는 숫자는 밤에 못 잔다.
en: One hundred and eight.
Get up. An uneven number does not sleep.

lines: 가야 피가 신라 피한테 졌다고 적히면 창피해서 그러시오?
en: Ha!
Afraid it will be written that Gaya blood lost to Silla blood?
Written or not.
I am still your elder brother.
Again.

blocks.html: They end the evening even. They always do.
blocks.ko: 그날 저녁도 비긴다. 언제나 그랬다.

blocks.html: “You were never even of Silla.” To see where that began, we go back to a Gaya prince nobody names…!
blocks.ko: “애초에 신라 사람도 아니잖아.” 그 말이 어디서 시작됐는지 보려면, 아무도 이름을 대지 않는 가야의 왕자에게로 거슬러 가야 한다…!

images.alt: Kim Muryuk of Golden Gaya kneels in surrender before Jinheung of Silla
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of gaya surrender, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (562), scene: The Fall of Gaya, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: For five hundred years the people of Gaya lived by iron
images.alt: Night wide: Gaya mountain seongmun, stone and giwa, one purple iron-spark accent
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 still. Bird’s-eye night, chiaroscuro. Inland Gaya mountain fortress: weathered stone seongmun, giwa munru, timber doors, packed earth. ONE device: gate as a dark wedge with a purple #8B5CF6 iron-spark seam. Tiny figures lower third. Crushed blacks. No army. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Dutch night charge: Sadaham in steel lamellar, ice-blue cloth peek, pointed Silla helm
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9. Dutch charge, night tenebrism. ONE Sadaham mid-stride snarl. FACE ch_sadaham. Steel-gray lamellar; ice-blue #6fa8ff cloth peek; pointed Silla helm. Spear as diagonal device. No clone. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Before the charge, Sadaham grins back over his shoulder at Mugwan as their horses break into a run under a storm sky
images.prompt: Low three-quarter from beside a galloping horse’s churning forelegs, dusk storm on a Gaya ridge. Sadaham, fifteen, in steel lamellar and pointed Silla helm, leans forward over his horse’s neck and looks back over his shoulder with a wide reckless grin; a sword at his hip. Just behind him, Mugwan spurs his own horse to catch up, mouth open mid-shout. One cloud-break shaft lands on the two riders; behind them Silla banners on poles bleed into haze, and far ahead a Gaya seongmun is a dark notch on the ridge. Torn grass and flying mud as dark foreground blur. CANON — SADAHAM — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sadaham.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Hwarang taken Gaya at fifteen; ice-blue #6fa8ff cloth on campaign; dies young of grief. Armor: Silla kit: steel lamellar cuirass and skirt, tall pointed jonghyeongju helm with a short plume. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. #6fa8ff as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | MUGWAN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_mugwan.png (face only; invent a new pose). #7aa0c8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. blocks.html: For five hundred years the people of Gaya lived by iron and by six eggs, and they enjoyed great peace.
blocks.ko: 오백 년 동안 가야 사람들은 쇠와 여섯 알로 살며 태평을 누렸다.

blocks.caption: Five hundred years of iron, gone in thirty.
blocks.ko: 오백 년의 쇠, 서른 해 만에 사라지다.

blocks.html: The Cloud King and his boy-general Sadaham come for Gaya.
blocks.ko: 구름왕과 그의 소년 장수 사다함이 가야로 쳐들어온다.

en: They said too young.
The gate didn’t.
Don’t die first.
Then keep up.

blocks.html: The vanguard thought otherwise. After the city fell he opened the prize-cages and kept only Alcheon dirt. Take the land. Leave the people.
blocks.ko: 선봉은 그렇지 않았다. 성이 떨어진 뒤 상으로 받은 우리를 열고 알천의 박토만 받았다. 땅은 가져라. 사람은 놔둬라.

blocks.hanja: 九月 加耶叛 王命異斯夫討之 斯多含副之 異斯夫引兵臨之 一時盡降
blocks.ko: 구월에 가야가 배반하니, 왕이 이사부에게 토벌하라 명하고 사다함으로 보좌하게 하였다. 이사부가 군사를 이끌고 이르니, 일시에 모두 항복하였다.
blocks.html: In the ninth month Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish them, with Sadaham as deputy. Isabu brought up the army, and they all surrendered at once.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinheung, yr. 23 (562), 9th month; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 98

en: Alcheon dirt.
That’s enough.

blocks.html: Thirty years earlier, the last lord of Geumgwan had already handed his kingdom over, to the king before this one. Three sons rode in the cart behind him. The youngest was Muryuk. His grandson will be Kim Yushin. But before the hall, the field. The tall Gaya cone still fights.
blocks.ko: 그보다 서른 해 전, 금관의 마지막 임금은 이미 나라를 넘겼다. 지금 임금의 앞 임금에게. 그의 수레 뒤에 아들 셋이 탔다. 막내가 무력이다. 무력의 손자가 김유신이 된다. 하지만 전각보다 먼저, 들판. 높은 가야 고깔은 아직 싸운다.

blocks.caption: The youngest son in the cart. Gaya handed over its crown. It did not hand over him.
blocks.ko: 수레에 탄 막내아들. 가야는 왕관을 내주었다. 그까지 내준 건 아니다.

blocks.hanja: 金官國主金仇亥 與妃及三子 以國帑寶物來降
blocks.ko: 금관국주 김구해가 왕비 및 세 아들과 더불어 나라의 곳간과 보물을 가지고 와서 항복하였다.
blocks.html: The lord of Geumgwan, Kim Guhae, came with his queen and three sons, bringing the treasury and precious things of the country, and surrendered.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Beopheung, yr. 19 (532); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 86

lines: 제 아버지의 아들들이 신라에서 부끄럽지 않게 살게 해 주십시오…
en: If we are to surrender, I have one condition…
Let my father’s sons live in Silla without shame…
And what do you mean by that?

lines: 신라에서는... 사람의 성분이 모든 걸 좌지우지한다고 알고 있습니다...
성골, 진골... 이미 다 알고 있습니다...
제 자손... 수로왕과 허왕후의 아들과 딸들이 좋은 자리에 자리잡을 수만 있다면...
저 또한 신라를 목숨을 바칠 준비가 되어있습니다...
en: In Silla… I know a man’s blood decides everything…
Sacred Bone, True Bone… I know it all…
If my descendants — the sons and daughters of Suro and Heo — can take a worthy place…
then I too am ready to give Silla my life…

lines: 알겠다. 너희 후손들은 신라의 진골로 추대해주마.
en: Very well. Your descendants shall be raised as True Bones of Silla.

blocks.html: Three generations later, his grandson will still be told he is not really one of them.
blocks.ko: 세 대가 지난 뒤에도, 그의 손자는 여전히 «진짜 우리 편은 아니다»라는 말을 듣게 된다.

en: Your grace is boundless… Your Majesty…!
Yushin…

blocks.html: Back to the siege. Sixth night. Bidam has poured two cups of tea. Yushin isn't coming… is he?
blocks.ko: 다시 포위전. 여섯째 밤. 비담은 찻잔 두 개를 채워 두었다. 유신은 오지 않는다… 정말 그럴까?
