images.alt: Dutch angle in the side hall: Chunchu holds the small royal seal into the lamp’s pool while three clerks lean in behind him
images.prompt: Dutch angle, low three-quarter, inside a small cleared side hall of the moon palace at night. Chunchu mid-turn toward three clerks, holding a small bronze royal seal up between two fingers close to the lens, the seal sharp in the foreground. A single oil lamp on the bare table below rakes up across his face and magenta silk; three clerks out of focus behind, one already lifting a brush. Timber pillars recede at an angle, his shadow climbing the wall. ONE device: the seal held into the lamp’s pool. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KIM CHUNCHU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_chunchu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: For three months a border petition has been circling the Harmony Council like a bird that cannot find a roof. Chunchu has counted the seals. He has counted the men who must touch a paper before a soldier may move. He has stopped counting aloud, because the room mistakes counting for patience.
blocks.ko: 석 달째, 변방의 청원이 화백회의를 지붕 못 찾는 새처럼 돈다. 춘추는 어보를 세어 보았다. 병사가 움직이려면 몇 사람이 종이를 만져야 하는지도 세어 보았다. 이제는 소리 내어 세지 않는다. 방이 그걸 인내로 알아듣기 때문이다.

blocks.title: Royal Secretariat · 집사부
blocks.caption: Fourteen ministries under one 중시. Tang’s 三省六部 copied and exceeded. Never enough.
blocks.ko: 중시 아래 열네 부. 당의 삼성육부를 본따 더했다. 결코 충분하지 않다.

blocks.title: Council, ornamental · 화백의 빈 의자
blocks.caption: The chairs stay polished. Nothing of consequence waits for them anymore.
blocks.ko: 의자는 여전히 닦인다. 더 이상 중대한 일은 화백을 기다리지 않는다.

blocks.html: He clears a side hall in the palace — small enough that the old clans will call it irregular, large enough for the work. Three clerks. One courier captain. A table that has never held a feast. He practices the sentence the way other men practice a sword form.
blocks.ko: 궁의 곁채 하나를 비운다 — 늙은 성골들이 변칙라 부를 만큼 작고, 일하기엔 넉넉한 크기. 서리 셋. 파발 장 하나. 잔치를 올려 본 적 없는 상. 그는 다른 사내가 칼법을 익히듯 문장을 익힌다.

blocks.html: What he brought home from the west is a grammar. One seal. One speed. Fewer uncles. When the old council finally falls, nobody will proclaim it. It will just be a table that has never held a feast.
blocks.ko: 그가 서쪽에서 가져온 건 문법이다. 어보 하나. 속도 하나. 줄어든 삼촌들. 옛 회의가 마침내 무너질 때, 아무도 그것을 선포하지 않을 것이다. 잔치를 치러 본 적 없는 탁자 하나가 있을 뿐이다.

en: A petition.
A seal.
A courier.
Are you getting it?
These are not three separate offices.
This is one office.
We call it the Royal Secretariat.
Today, the king will reinvent the kingdom.

blocks.html: Nobody laughs. The youngest clerk writes the name down as if the words had always been waiting for ink. Outside, the Harmony Council is still debating the same petition. Inside, the petition has somewhere to land.
blocks.ko: 아무도 웃지 않는다. 가장 어린 서리가, 그 이름이 처음부터 먹물을 기다리고 있었던 것처럼 적는다. 바깥에서는 화백이 같은 청원을 아직도 논한다. 안에서는, 청원이 내려앉을 곳이 생겼다.

blocks.html: Chunchu establishes the Royal Secretariat — an institution that reports to the king alone. The clans will call it a shortcut. He will call it Tuesday.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 집사부를 세운다 — 임금에게만 직속으로 보고하는 기구. 성골들은 지름길이라 부를 것이다. 그는 화요일이라 부를 것이다.

en: Petition. Seal. Courier.
I can do that before the Council finishes clearing its throat.
lines: 화백이 목청 가다듬기 전에 끝낼 수 있습니다.

en: Then you are 중시 — Premier of the Royal Secretariat.
True Bone. Young Hwarang. My confidante.
In Chang’an the emperor does not wait for every uncle to agree. I watched that power and wanted it for this country — not for my vanity. For speed.
lines: 그럼 네가 중시다. 집사부는 네 자리다.
장안에서 황제는 모든 삼촌의 동의를 기다리지 않더라. 그 힘을 보고 이 나라에 갖고 싶었다 — 허영이 아니라. 속도를 위해.

blocks.html: Second month: the old treasury office was remade as the Royal Secretariat, and the pajinchan Jukji was appointed its Premier, to take charge of confidential affairs.
blocks.ko: 2월, 품주를 고쳐 집사부로 삼고, 이어 파진찬 죽지를 집사 중시로 임명하여 기밀 사무를 맡게 하였다.
blocks.hanja: 二月，改稟主爲執事部，仍拜波珍飡竹旨爲執事中侍，以掌機密事務。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, yr. 5 (651)

blocks.html: The Harmony Council still meets on the appointed days, in polished chairs, reciting the unanimity rule to a room that no decision of consequence waits for anymore. They have been made lame ducks without the dignity of abolition — and they know it by the third week, when a border petition returns sealed before their debate has chosen a speaker.
blocks.ko: 화백회의는 여전히 정한 날에, 반들반들 닦인 자리에 모여, 이제는 어떤 중대사도 기다려 주지 않는 방을 향해 만장일치 규정을 외운다. 폐지라는 존엄조차 없이 식물 의회가 된 것이다 — 그리고 셋째 주가 되면 그들도 안다. 변방의 상소가, 토론의 발언자를 정하기도 전에 인장이 찍혀 돌아올 때.

blocks.html: In the market a storyteller invents a joke that sticks: Our prince is in love with the emperor. Another version: enamored with China. Chunchu hears both and does not correct them. Munhee, packing a different set of bags, corrects them for him.
blocks.ko: 저자거리에서 이야기꾼이 들러붙는 농담을 만든다. 우리 왕자는 황제와 연애 중이라네. 다른 판: 중국에 반했대. 춘추는 둘 다 듣고 고치지 않는다. 문희가 — 다른 짐을 싸며 — 대신 고친다.

en: He is in love with a door that opens when he knocks.
Call that China if you like. I call it not waiting for twelve men to finish a sentence.
lines: 그걸 중국이라 불러도 돼요. 나는 열두 사람이 문장 끝낼 때까지 안 기다리는 거라 불러요.

en: The Council asked what my title means.
I told them: 侍中 — I stand beside the work.
They did not laugh. That was how I knew it had worked.
lines: 侍中이라고 했습니다 — 일 옆에 선다고.
안 웃더군요. 그래서 된 줄 알았습니다.

blocks.label: Tang Dress
blocks.ko: 당의 옷

blocks.html: The chest of court robes from the west is opened at the new year. By spring every senior official has been measured for one. A year later the kingdom stops counting its own years and starts counting the emperor’s. Bupmin sails west with the queen’s ode woven into a length of silk. The emperor in Chang’an admires it extravagantly.
blocks.ko: 서쪽에서 온 관복 상자가 새해 첫 달에 열린다. 봄이 되자 높은 관리들은 모두 치수를 잰다. 이듬해 나라는 제 연호를 버리고 황제의 연호를 센다. 법민이 여왕의 송가를 짜 넣은 비단 한 필을 들고 서쪽으로 간다. 장안의 황제는 그것을 요란하게 칭찬한다.

blocks.html: The queen wove brocade with a five-character Ode to Great Peace, and sent Chunchu’s son Bupmin to present it to the Tang emperor.
blocks.ko: 왕이 비단을 짜서 오언 태평송을 지어 넣고, 춘추의 아들 법민을 보내 당 황제에게 바쳤다.
blocks.hanja: 王織錦作五言太平頌，遣春秋子法敏，以獻唐皇帝。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, yr. 4 (650), 6th month

blocks.title: Ode to Great Peace (太平頌)
blocks.hanja:
大唐開洪業，巍巍皇猷昌，
止戈戎威定，修文繼百王。
統天崇雨施，理物體含章。
深仁偕日月，撫運邁時康。
幡旗何赫赫，錚鼓何鍠鍠。
外夷違命者，剪覆被天殃。
淳風凝幽顯，遐邇競呈祥。
四時和玉燭，七曜巡萬方。
維嶽降宰輔，維帝任忠良。
五三成一德，昭我唐家皇。
blocks.html:
Great Tang has opened its vast work; lofty, lofty, the imperial plan shines.
The spear is stilled and its might has settled all; letters are cultivated, heir to a hundred kings.
It rules as Heaven does and honours the falling rain; it orders all things and keeps their beauty within.
Its deep kindness keeps pace with sun and moon; its fortunes outrun the years of peace.
How bright, how bright the banners blaze; how loud, how loud the gongs and drums.
Outer tribes who defy its command are cut down by Heaven’s punishment.
Pure custom settles on the seen and the unseen; near and far vie to offer good omens.
The four seasons turn in tune like a jade candle; the seven lights wheel over ten thousand lands.
The holy peaks send down ministers; the emperor trusts the loyal and good.
The Three and the Five are made one virtue: shine on, sovereign of our Tang house!*
blocks.ko:
위대한 당이 큰 업을 여니, 높고 높은 황제의 계책 빛나도다.
창을 거두니 무위가 천하를 평정하고, 글을 닦아 백 왕의 뒤를 잇도다.
하늘을 거느려 비를 내리듯 은혜를 베풀고, 만물을 다스려 아름다움을 품었도다.
깊은 어짊은 해와 달과 나란하고, 시운을 어루만져 태평한 때를 넘어서도다.
깃발은 어찌 그리 빛나며, 징과 북은 어찌 그리 우렁찬가.
명을 어기는 바깥 오랑캐는 하늘의 재앙을 입어 엎어지리라.
순박한 풍속이 보이는 곳과 보이지 않는 곳에 엉기니, 멀고 가까운 곳이 다투어 상서를 바치도다.
사계절은 옥촉처럼 고르고, 일곱 별은 온 세상을 도는도다.
산악이 재상을 내리고, 황제는 충성스럽고 어진 이를 쓰도다.
삼황오제의 덕이 하나가 되니, 우리 당나라 황제를 빛내도다!*
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, yr. 4 (650), sixth month · cf. Jiu Tangshu bk. 199上 (止戈戎衣定)

notes.html: The emperor liked it. He made Bupmin a Chief Minister of the Treasury and sent him home.
notes.ko: 황제는 이를 가상히 여겨 법민을 태부경으로 삼아 돌려보냈다.

en: Father. The collar itches.

lines: 회의에 입고 가서, 어느 삼촌이 긁는지 봐라.
en: Everything new itches.
Wear it to the Council, and watch which uncles scratch.

blocks.label: Tsukushi
blocks.ko: 쓰쿠시

blocks.html: In the summer of 651 a Silla tribute ship puts in at Tsukushi with its envoys dressed in the new robes. The Yamato court takes one look at them and sends them home.
blocks.ko: 651년 여름, 신라의 조공선이 새 관복을 입은 사신들을 싣고 쓰쿠시에 닿는다. 야마토 조정은 그들을 한 번 쳐다보고는 돌려보낸다.

blocks.html: This year the Silla tribute envoys, the sachan Jiman and others, put in at Tsukushi wearing Tang clothes. The court hated this wilful change of custom, rebuked them and sent them back.
blocks.ko: 이 해에 신라의 공조사 지만 사찬 등이 당나라 옷을 입고 쓰쿠시에 배를 대었다. 조정은 제멋대로 풍속을 바꾼 것을 미워하여, 꾸짖어 쫓아 돌려보냈다.
blocks.hanja: 是歲，新羅貢調使知萬沙飡等，著唐國服泊于筑紫。朝廷惡恣移俗，訶嘖追還。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 25, Emperor Kōtoku — Hakuchi 2 (651)

blocks.speaker: Kose no Ōmi
lines: 지금 신라를 치지 않으면 뒷날 반드시 후회할 것입니다.
나니와 나루에서 쓰쿠시 바다까지 배를 이물과 고물이 닿게 띄우고, 신라를 불러 그 죄를 물으면 쉬운 일입니다.
en: If we do not strike Silla now, we will regret it later.
Fill the sea from Naniwa to Tsukushi with ships, bow to stern, and call them to account. It would be easy.
ja: 今新羅を討たずば、後に必ず悔いあらん。
難波の津より筑紫の海まで、艫舳を連ねて浮かべ、新羅を召してその罪を問わば、たやすく得べし。
jaLatn: Ima Shiragi o utazuba, nochi ni kanarazu kui aran.
Naniwa no tsu yori Tsukushi no umi made, tomo-he o tsuranete ukabe, Shiragi o meshite sono tsumi o towaba, tayasuku u-beshi.

blocks.html: Emperor Kōtoku does not fill the sea. His successors will remember the idea.
blocks.ko: 고토쿠 천황은 바다를 메우지 않는다. 그의 후계자들이 그 생각을 기억해 둘 것이다.

blocks.title: Sealed letter to the king of Baekje
blocks.hanja: 至如海東三國，開基自久，並列疆界，地實犬牙。近代已來，遂構嫌隙。戰爭交起，略無寧歲。遂令三韓之氓，命懸刀俎，尋戈肆憤，朝夕相仍。……新羅使金法敏奏書：「高麗、百濟，脣齒相依，競舉兵戈，侵逼交至。大城重鎮，並爲百濟所並；疆宇日蹙，威力並謝。乞詔百濟，令歸所侵之城。若不奉詔，即自興兵打取。但得故地，即請交和。」……王所兼新羅之城，並宜還其本國；新羅所獲百濟俘虜，亦遣還王。……王若不從進止，朕已依法敏所請，任其與王決戰；亦令約束高麗，不許遠相救恤。高麗若不承命，即令契丹諸蕃渡遼澤入抄掠。王可深思朕言，自求多福，審圖良策，無貽後悔。
blocks.html: The three kingdoms east of the sea were founded long ago. Their borders run side by side and bite into each other like dogs’ teeth. In recent times they have fallen out. War follows war, and there is hardly a year of peace. So the people of Samhan live with their lives on the chopping block, and spears are taken up in rage from morning to night. … Silla’s envoy, Kim Bupmin, presented a letter: “Goguryeo and Baekje lean on each other like lips and teeth. They raise arms by turns and press on us from both sides. Our great cities and strongholds have all been swallowed by Baekje; our land shrinks by the day and our strength is gone. We beg you to command Baekje to return the cities it took. If it will not obey, we will raise troops and take them back ourselves. Give us our old land, and we ask only for peace.” … The Silla cities you have taken must all go back to their own country, and the Baekje prisoners Silla holds will be sent back to you. … If you will not do as you are told, We have already granted Bupmin’s request: he may settle it with you in battle. We will also restrain Goguryeo and forbid it to come to your aid from afar. And if Goguryeo will not obey, the Khitan and the other tribes will be sent across the Liao marshes to raid it. Think hard on Our words, King. Seek your own good fortune, plan well, and leave yourself nothing to regret.
blocks.ko: 바다 동쪽의 세 나라는 나라를 연 지 오래되었고, 국경을 나란히 하여 땅이 개의 이빨처럼 맞물려 있다. 근래 들어 마침내 틈이 벌어져, 전쟁이 번갈아 일어나 편안한 해가 거의 없다. 그리하여 삼한의 백성은 목숨이 도마 위에 걸렸고, 창을 들고 분을 터뜨리는 일이 아침저녁으로 이어진다. …… 신라의 사신 김법민이 글을 올려 아뢰었다. “고구려와 백제가 입술과 이처럼 서로 기대어 다투어 군사를 일으키고, 번갈아 침범해 옵니다. 큰 성과 중요한 진은 모두 백제에게 빼앗겼고, 강토는 날로 줄어 힘이 다하였습니다. 백제에 조서를 내려 빼앗은 성을 돌려주게 하소서. 조서를 받들지 않으면 저희가 스스로 군사를 일으켜 되찾겠습니다. 옛 땅만 얻으면 곧 화친을 청하겠습니다.” …… 왕이 차지한 신라의 성은 모두 그 나라에 돌려주고, 신라가 잡은 백제 포로도 왕에게 돌려보내게 하라. …… 왕이 따르지 않는다면, 짐은 이미 법민의 청에 따라 그가 왕과 결전하도록 맡겼다. 또 고구려를 단속하여 멀리서 구원하지 못하게 할 것이다. 고구려가 명을 받들지 않으면 거란과 여러 번국에게 요택을 건너 노략하게 할 것이다. 왕은 짐의 말을 깊이 생각하여 스스로 복을 구하고, 좋은 계책을 살펴 뒷날 후회를 남기지 말라.
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje, Yonghui 2 (651) · cf. Samguk Sagi bk. 28, King Uija, yr. 11

images.alt: Ink-painted poster: the dying Second Emperor, still in colour, lifts his hand and the gold dragon lowers its head through black ink gauze to meet it
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; heads and the dragon’s head stay inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night in a summer palace bedchamber: gauze curtains as pale grey washes, the bed and the room sinking into black ink, one lamp. High three-quarter angle over the bed. TWO SUBJECTS: a dying man AND a huge dragon. INTERACTION: the dying Second Emperor lies propped on pillows, grey and gaunt, cap removed, and lifts one thin hand; the gold Tang dragon Huanglong (gold ink-brush dragon from the attached board, three claws) has wound its body around the bed frame and lowers its huge head through the gauze, snout pressed into his palm, eyes half-closed. Its coils fill the black around the bed. The single lamp (#c97a2e) catches his face, his hand and the dragon’s muzzle. TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) on rice paper — heavy black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding, splashed ink smoke and storm, dry calligraphic brush strokes for roofs, columns, robes and cloud, ink splatters and drips at the frame edges, bare paper only where the edges dissolve; the gold ink-brush dragon is the main colour in the dark, with a few small vermilion and flame accents. THE ONE EXCEPTION: the Second Emperor himself is a full-colour Korean webtoon figure — clean ink linework, drawn face matching the attached portrait, warm skin, imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade, black futou — a coloured man inside an ink empire; nothing else in the frame is in full colour. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, big dark masses, one bright break of light, NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp, no calligraphy characters. Not photoreal, not 3D, not a realistic scaled dragon. No glow aura, no halo — the accent is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — THE SECOND EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_taizong.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Bearded Tang emperor: black futou cap with an upright pin, thick black beard and moustache, fierce scowl. Dress: Imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade. Demeanor: Commands; never asks. Conqueror's contempt that curdles at Ansi. Presence: THE SON OF HEAVEN — every frame he is in bends around him. He is SHROUDED IN DARKNESS: the black of the hall gathers around him like a mantle. One close practical light (a lamp, a brazier, a lamp-tree) rakes across him from below or from the side and SCULPTS him — the heavy yellow silk breaks into deep protruding folds brushed in loaded oil strokes that follow each fold, gold thread flicked in with impasto, the beard and cheekbones carved — and then falls off into black across his body and half his face; that falloff is the darkness, never a flat backlit silhouette. The camera sits BELOW his eyeline (low angle or worm’s-eye) and he is always placed HIGHER than anyone near him — on the dais, on a step, standing while others kneel or sit. He reads larger than life through lens and staging, not as a giant: broad shoulders, the robe spreading wide and heavy into the dark like a mountain, his shadow enormous on walls and floor. Unhurried, heavy stillness — never fidgeting, never casual, never a colleague at someone’s shoulder; when he smiles or laughs it is a predator’s ease, and the room goes quiet around it. Everyone else in frame is smaller, lower, less lit, turned toward him. The aura is darkness, scale and the hush around him — never a glow, never a halo, never rays behind his head. #c97a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Korean ring-pommel sword; Korean lamellar. | HUANGLONG (황룡, taizong's yellow dragon, guardian of the Tang throne) — attached board /obj_yellow_dragon.png: TANG-DYNASTY dragon painted in gold ink-brush: lean long-necked serpentine body in an S-curve, four lean leonine legs striding, THREE claws on each foot, long open-jawed snout with fangs, two backswept horns, whiskers and mane flung out as dry calligraphic gold brush strokes, whip tail ending in a flame tuft; burnished gold-yellow scales with ochre-umber shading — match the board, not a later Ming/Qing five-claw dragon, never a realistic scaled 3D dragon. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, coiling through black ink cloud and lamp smoke; light catches the scales as real light, never a glow outline. Its stills are predominantly dark and intimidating Chinese ink painting: splashed black ink, smoke, the gold dragon the main colour in the dark; every figure is ink-painted except the Second Emperor, who stays a full-colour webtoon figure. Owned by no one but sits behind whoever holds the dais; it coils over Chang'an and turns its head only for the Son of Heaven. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. blocks.label: The Cuiwei Palace
blocks.ko: 취미궁

blocks.html: The emperor dies in the Cuiwei Palace in the fifth month. He is fifty-one. The room is kept too warm, and the silk on the bed is the colour of late wheat.
blocks.ko: 오월, 취위궁에서 황제가 붕어한다. 쉰한 살. 방은 너무 덥게 데워져 있고, 침상의 비단은 늦은 밀 빛이다.

blocks.hanja: 駕崩
blocks.html: “The carriage collapses.” Nobody in Chang’an may say the emperor died. Kings die. The Son of Heaven’s carriage simply falls, and the whole empire is meant to hear it land.
blocks.ko: ‘수레가 무너진다’. 장안에서는 아무도 황제가 죽었다고 말하지 못한다. 왕은 죽는다. 하늘의 아들은 수레가 내려앉을 뿐이고, 온 제국이 그 소리를 들어야 한다.

blocks.html: The crown prince has been sitting since before dawn. He is twenty-one. He has the shoulders for the armour and not yet the face for the title. When the breathing stops, he does not move for a long time — long enough that the ministers begin to look at one another instead of at the bed.
blocks.ko: 태자는 동이 트기 전부터 앉아 있었다. 스물한 살. 갑옷을 견딜 어깨는 있으나, 아직 그 이름에 맞는 얼굴은 없다. 숨이 멎어도 그는 오래 움직이지 않는다 — 대신들이 침상이 아니라 서로의 얼굴을 보기 시작할 만큼.

en: ……Father.
Not yet——
zhLatn: …Fùhuáng.
Shàngwèi——

blocks.html: Someone touches his elbow. Someone else is already writing. The empire does not wait for grief to finish its sentence.
blocks.ko: 누군가가 팔꿈치를 건드린다. 다른 누군가는 이미 붓을 들고 있다. 제국은 슬픔이 문장을 끝낼 때까지 기다려 주지 않는다.

blocks.html: The court kneels, and the young man rises — the same hands that would not leave the bed now accepting the seal, the edict, the yellow silk that means the West has a new centre.
blocks.ko: 조정이 엎드리고, 젊은이가 일어선다 — 침상을 떠나려 하지 않던 그 손이, 이제 인장과 조서와, 서쪽에 새 중심이 생겼다는 뜻의 노란 비단을 받는다.

en: I receive the late emperor’s last command.
From this day——
……We will listen.
zhLatn: Zhèn shòu xiāndì yízhào.
Zì jīnrì qǐ——
…Zhèn dāng tīng zhī.

blocks.html: He does not say I. He says the word that empties a man of his own name. The hall answers like a single throat.
blocks.ko: 그는 “나”라고 하지 않는다. 사람의 이름을 비워 버리는 그 말을 쓴다. 대전이 하나의 목구멍처럼 대답한다.

blocks.html: The will is long on mourning and short on everything else, except one line, which the new emperor reads twice. The war in Liaodong is to stop.
blocks.ko: 유조는 상례에 대해서는 길고 나머지에 대해서는 짧다. 딱 한 줄만 빼고. 새 황제는 그 줄을 두 번 읽는다. 요동의 전쟁을 그만두라는 것이다.

blocks.html: The great emperor is given a temple name — Taizong. The clerks write it in the register and close the book.
blocks.ko: 위대한 황제에게 묘호 태종이 올려진다. 서리가 등록부에 쓰고 책을 덮는다.

lines: 위대한 황제의 묘호를, 태종(太宗)이라 정한다.
en: The great emperor’s temple name is hereby set as Taizong (太宗).
zh: 大行皇帝廟號，定為太宗。
zhLatn: Dàxíng huángdì miàohào, dìng wéi Tàizōng.

blocks.html: On the renshen day the death was announced in the Taiji Hall, the testamentary edict was proclaimed, and the crown prince took the throne. … The Liaodong campaign and all the building works were called off.
blocks.ko: 임신일, 태극전에서 상을 알리고 유조를 선포하니 태자가 즉위하였다. … 요동의 전역과 여러 토목 공사를 그만두게 하였다.
blocks.hanja: 壬申，發喪太極殿，宣遺詔，太子即位。…罷遼東之役及諸土木之功。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 199, Tang Zhenguan 23 (649), 5th month

blocks.html: Eighth year, summer, fourth month: Taizong* of Tang died. His testamentary edict called off the Liaodong campaign.
blocks.ko: 8년 여름 4월, 당 태종*이 죽었다. 유조로 요동의 전역을 그만두게 하였다.
blocks.hanja: 八年，夏四月，唐太宗崩。遺詔罷遼東之役。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 22, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 8 (649)

notes.html: Taizong is the temple name Tang gave him after death. In this book he is the Second Emperor.
notes.ko: 태종은 죽은 뒤 받은 묘호다. 이 책에서는 ‘두 번째 황제’다.

blocks.html: The empire is told how to grieve. The edict fixes the days of mourning by rank, and at dusk in every ward of Chang’an the ward chief walks the lanes and listens at the doors, to be sure the weeping inside is of the proper length.
blocks.ko: 제국은 어떻게 슬퍼할지 지시받는다. 칙령은 품계에 따라 상복 입을 날수를 정하고, 해 질 녘이면 장안의 방마다 방정이 골목을 돌며 문에 귀를 댄다. 안의 곡소리가 정해진 길이만큼인지 확인하려고.

blocks.html: Two of his dragons, the Red and the White, both of them Turks, petition to be killed and laid beside him, to guard the tomb the way the six stone horses will. It is the highest loyalty the steppe knows. The court is moved. The young emperor reads the petition twice.
blocks.ko: 그의 용 둘, 적룡과 백룡이 순장을 청한다. 둘 다 돌궐인이다. 죽어서 그의 곁에 묻혀, 여섯 돌말처럼 능을 지키겠다는 것이다. 초원이 아는 가장 높은 충성이다. 조정은 감동한다. 젊은 황제는 그 상소를 두 번 읽는다.

en: Denied.
…Father already has six horses waiting at his door.
He would scold Us for wasting two good generals.
lines: …선제 문 앞엔 이미 말 여섯이 기다리고 있다.
멀쩡한 장수 둘을 버렸다고, 짐을 꾸짖으실 게다.
zh: 他會怪朕白白折了兩員良將。
zhLatn: Bù zhǔn.
……Xiāndì mén qián, yǐ yǒu liù jùn xiāng hòu.
Tā huì guài zhèn báibái shé le liǎng yuán liáng jiàng.

blocks.html: Ashina She’er and Qibi Heli* asked to kill themselves and be buried with him. The emperor sent word that, by the late emperor’s own wishes, it was not permitted.
blocks.ko: 아사나사이와 계필하력*이 스스로 목숨을 끊어 순장되기를 청하였으나, 황제는 사람을 보내 선제의 뜻을 들어 허락하지 않았다.
blocks.hanja: 阿史那社爾、契苾何力請殺身殉葬，上遣人諭以先旨不許。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 199, Tang Zhenguan 23 (649), 8th month

notes.html: Qibi Heli: the steppe prince this book calls the White Dragon.
notes.ko: 계필하력, 이 책의 흰 용(백룡)이다.

blocks.html: In Chang’an the new emperor is still learning how to stand. In Sabi, another king is learning how to be afraid.
blocks.ko: 장안에서는 새 황제가 아직 서는 법을 배우고 있다. 사비에서는 다른 왕이 두려워하는 법을 배우고 있다.

blocks.html: King Euija grows more watchful of the Great Clans. Tang has gone quiet, and quiet from that direction rarely stays put.
blocks.ko: 의자왕은 대성팔족을 더욱 경계한다. 당이 조용해졌고, 그쪽에서 오는 조용함은 오래 머물지 않는다.

blocks.html: Gyebek already knows what the silence means. A house that fights itself does not need an emperor to finish it.
blocks.ko: 계백은 그 고요함의 뜻을 이미 안다. 스스로와 싸우는 집은, 황제가 없어도 끝난다.

blocks.html: The news crosses the sea in the eighth month. In Surabol, Chunchu reads the will through to the line about Liaodong, and then reads that line again.
blocks.ko: 소식은 팔월에 바다를 건넌다. 서라벌에서 춘추는 유조를 요동 대목까지 읽고, 그 줄을 다시 읽는다.

lines: 나더러 끝내 달라고 약속하게 해 놓고.
en: He made me promise to finish it.
And then he left orders to stop.
…Very well. Then it is mine.

blocks.html: In an anteroom a young concubine waits with the other women who must not be seen grieving too loudly. Her name is not yet heavy. Her attention already is. She watches how a seal moves from a dead hand to a living one — and files the lesson where ambition keeps its dry goods.
blocks.ko: 곁방에서 젊은 후궁이, 너무 크게 울면 안 되는 여인들과 함께 기다린다. 이름은 아직 무겁지 않다. 시선은 이미 그렇다. 죽은 손에서 산 손으로 인장이 옮아가는 법을 보고 — 야심이 마른 식량을 두는 곳에 그 수업을 넣는다.

en: (soft, to no one)
So that is how an empire changes owners.
Quietly. With someone else speaking the first sentence.
lines: 조용히. 첫 문장은 남이 말하게 두고.
zh: 原來帝國換主人是這樣。
靜靜地。讓別人說第一句。
zhLatn: (Qīngshēng, duì wú rén)
Yuánlái dìguó huàn zhǔrén shì zhèyàng.
Jìngjìng de. Ràng biérén shuō dì yī jù.

blocks.html: The late emperor’s women who bore him no children are sent to the Ganye Temple, to shave their heads and pray for him for the rest of their lives. Wu goes with them.
blocks.ko: 선제의 후궁 가운데 자식을 낳지 못한 여인들은 감업사로 보내져, 머리를 깎고 평생 그를 위해 기도하게 된다. 무도 그들과 함께 간다.

blocks.html: A year later, on the anniversary, the new emperor comes to the temple to burn incense for his father. A nun in grey looks up at him from the second row, and does not look down again.
blocks.ko: 한 해 뒤 기일에, 새 황제가 아버지에게 향을 올리러 그 절에 온다. 둘째 줄의 잿빛 승복 하나가 그를 올려다보고, 다시는 눈을 내리깔지 않는다.

blocks.html: When Taizong died, she became a nun and lived at the Ganye Temple. The new emperor saw her at the temple…
blocks.ko: 태종이 죽자 마침내 비구니가 되어 감업사에 머물렀다. 대제가 절에서 그녀를 보았다…
blocks.hanja: 及太宗崩，遂為尼，居感業寺。大帝於寺見之…
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 6, Annals of Empress Wu (則天皇后本紀)

en: Lady Wu.
…They cut your hair.
zhLatn: Wǔ niángzi.
…Tāmen tì le nǐ de tóufa.

en: Hair grows back, Majesty.
(and already the room tilts a degree toward her)
lines: (그리고 이미 방이 그녀 쪽으로 한 치 기운다)
zhLatn: Tóufa huì zhǎng huílái de, Bìxià.
(Ér fángjiān yǐ xiàng tā piān guò yī cùn)

blocks.html: Seven years of a polite queen and a busy nephew. Sooner or later, Silla has to admit who's really sitting in the chair…!
blocks.ko: 칠 년 동안 점잖은 여왕과 바쁜 조카. 언젠가 신라는 그 자리에 정말 누가 앉아 있는지 인정해야 한다…!

images.at: For seven years the crown has sat on
images.alt: Poster key art: Queen Jinduk weaves her ode of peace into silk at a lamp-lit loom while the white heavenly horse watches over her shoulder through the open door
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night in a tenebrist Silla palace chamber: one oil lamp, a big wooden loom, a long length of silk with woven lines of verse, the timber door slid open onto a moonlit courtyard. Over-shoulder two-shot. INTERACTION: Queen Jinduk sits at the loom in violet-and-white silk and gold crown, shuttle in hand, mid-throw; the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma has pushed its head and long neck in through the open door and rests its chin on her shoulder, watching the shuttle; without looking she reaches back and scratches its jaw. The woven silk glows only where the lamp touches it. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. The lamp is the only key (#9d7bd0 bounce off the silk): it catches her profile, the shuttle, the horse’s eye and muzzle; the room falls into umber-black. Loom frame as a dark foreground shape. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — QUEEN JINDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_jinduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_jinduk.png when the head is visible. #9d7bd0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Dawn on the long stone stair of the Seorabeol palace, giwa roofs behind, one storm cloud splitting. Low angle up the stair diagonal. INTERACTION: King Muyeol (Kim Chunchu as king — royal crown and magenta-and-gold court robe, older, heavy-lidded clever eyes) walks down the steps beside the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma, one hand buried in its mane, leaning in to murmur something sly into its ear; the horse has turned its head toward him, one ear cocked as if it has heard this sort of thing from him before. Two subjects on the stair diagonal, the rest empty stone. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. One magenta-gold sunrise break (#D8258C) from behind the roofs edges his crown, profile and the horse’s neck; the stair falls into blue-grey shadow and ink. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING MUYEOL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_muyeol.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Now: King Muyeol (stage portrait): royal robes and crown; heavier, tired eyes. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. blocks.html: For seven years the crown has sat on Queen Jinduk. The work has sat on her nephew’s table. Nobody has ever called her foolish. She’s simply outnumbered by seals.
blocks.ko: 칠 년 동안 왕관은 진덕여왕의 머리에 있었다. 일은 그녀 조카의 탁자 위에 있었다. 아무도 그녀를 어리석다 한 적 없다. 그저 도장 수에서 밀렸을 뿐이다.

en: Nephew.
When I die, do not pretend I ruled.
Say I kept the chair warm until the country was ready to admit who was already sitting in it.
lines: 내가 죽거든 내가 다스렸다고 하지 마라.
나라가, 이미 앉아 있던 사람을 인정할 준비가 될 때까지 자리를 따뜻하게 지켜 줬다고 해라.

en: Aunt.
You ruled the only way left to Sacred Bone — by lasting.
lines: 성골에게 남은 유일한 방식으로 다스리셨습니다 — 버팀으로.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads her name three times — Jinduk. Jinduk. Jinduk. — the ledger's habit before a Sacred Bone line closes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 그녀의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 진덕. 진덕. 진덕. — 성골의 혈통이 닫히기 전 명부의 버릇대로.

en: Majesty.
Sacred Bone ends on your breath. One question.
Did you keep the crown warm for the next hand — or keep it from cooling into a man’s?
lines: 성골이 당신 숨에서 끝납니다. 질문 하나.
다음 손을 위해 왕관을 따뜻이 두셨습니까 — 아니면 사내의 것으로 식지 않게 지키신 겁니까?

en: …I kept a seat from becoming a joke.
That is all the Sacred Bone had left to do.
Then the minutes are clean.
Walk.

blocks.html: Queen Jinduk is dead. With her, the Sacred Bone bloodline has finally gone extinct.
blocks.ko: 진덕여왕이 승하했다. 그녀와 함께 성골의 혈통은 완전히 끊겼다.

blocks.html: The Harmony Council meets again to enthrone the next king.
blocks.ko: 화백회의가 다시 모여 다음 임금을 세운다.

blocks.html: Again the rule is unanimity. Again the room discovers how long a single withheld hand can last — until Alchun laughs the holdout down, and the first True Bone king Silla has ever crowned is made by the same math that once made a queen.
blocks.ko: 이번에도 규칙은 만장일치다. 이번에도 방은 손 하나가 얼마나 오래 버틸 수 있는지 알게 된다 — 알천이 그 반대를 웃어 넘길 때까지. 신라 최초의 진골 임금이, 한때 여왕을 만든 것과 같은 셈법으로 세워진다.

blocks.hanja: 臣老矣 無德行可稱 今之德望崇重 莫若春秋公 實可謂濟世英傑矣
blocks.ko: 신은 늙었고, 칭할 만한 덕행이 없습니다. 지금 덕망이 높고 중한 이는 춘추공만 한 이가 없으니, 실로 세상을 건질 영걸이라 이를 만합니다.
blocks.html: Your servant is old, and has no virtuous conduct worth naming. In virtue and standing none now is weightier than Lord Chunchu; he may truly be called a hero who can save the age.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — King Muyeol, accession (654); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 134

lines: 다~ 뻔히 춘추인걸 모르는 사람이 없나~~
en: Come now~ is there anyone who doesn’t know it will be Chunchu~~

lines: 진골이 왕이 되는 건 나라가 선 이래 처음이오.
…그건 누가 좀 적어 둬야 하지 않겠소.
en: A True Bone on the throne. First since there was a throne.
…Somebody had probably better write that down.
This servant can find no reason to object.
Nor could anyone else.
The age of Kim Chunchu begins.

blocks.html: Munhee becomes queen. Years ago her sister sold her a dream on a hill. She married in disgrace, to a man with no claim to anything. Now she stands beside his throne.
blocks.ko: 문희가 왕비가 된다. 오래전 언니가 언덕 위에서 그녀에게 꿈을 팔았다. 그녀는 아무것도 물려받을 것 없는 사내에게 망신스럽게 시집갔다. 이제 그 사내의 왕좌 곁에 선다.

lines: 언니가 그 꿈을 비단 치마 한 벌에 팔았습니다. / 지금 생각하면 헐값이었지요.
en: My sister sold me that dream for one silk skirt. / In hindsight she undercharged.

lines: 사적인 원한으로 나라를 망국의 길로 인도하시는 것은 어진 일이 아니라 봅니다...!
en: Your Majesty… even so….
To lead the country down a road of ruin for a private grudge — that is not the act of a wise king…!

lines: 자네들, 나를 진정 그렇게 보고 있었나?
내 딸의 죽음에 미쳐 복수를 가르는 노인으로?
en: ….What? A private grudge?
Is that truly how you have all seen me?
An old man maddened by his daughter’s death, sharpening revenge?
How… disappointing.
I am a man looking at the thousand-year flourishing of the sacred country.
I was raised on the study of kingship from childhood…

lines: 무서워 해야 할지, 동경해야 할 지 모르겠다....
en: I do not know whether to fear him or admire him….
And yet—
Kim Chunchu…

blocks.hanja: 國人謂始祖赫居世至眞德二十八王 謂之聖骨 自武烈至末王 謂之眞骨
blocks.ko: 나라 사람들이 이르기를, 시조 혁거세로부터 진덕에 이르는 스물여덟 왕을 성골이라 하고, 무열로부터 끝 왕에 이르기까지를 진골이라 하였다.
blocks.html: The people of the country said: from the founder Hyeokgeose to Jindeok, twenty-eight sovereigns, they called Sacred Bone; from Muyeol to the last kings, they called True Bone.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, death notice (654); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 134

blocks.html: That night a letter leaves Surabol for Chang’an, written in a hand that still remembers the Wei River. It begins without titles: Zhi — I kept the appointment. Do not let the coat eat you.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 서라벌에서 장안으로 편지가 떠난다. 위수를 아직 기억하는 손씨. 존호 없이 시작한다. 治 — 약속 지켰네. 겉옷에게 먹히지는 말게.

blocks.html: I wrote to Zhi as a brother. I did not write what I had seen in that woman’s eyes. Some warnings cannot be put in a letter without becoming a prophecy you cannot take back.
blocks.ko: 나는 治에게 형제로 편지를 썼다. 그 여인의 눈에서 본 것은 쓰지 않았다. 어떤 경고는 편지에 넣는 순간, 거둘 수 없는 예언이 된다.

lines: 말을 보내게. 그리고 여기 먼지엔 불편한 사람 하나 더 들어갈 자리가 있다고 전하게.
en: He became king.
Of course he did.
Send him horses. And tell him the dust here still has room for one more inconvenient man.
zh: 送他馬。並告訴他——這兒的塵土還容得下一個不便之人。
zhLatn: Tā chéng le wáng.
Guǒrán.
Sòng tā mǎ. Bìng gàosu tā——zhèr de chéntǔ hái róng de xià yīgè bùbiàn zhī rén.

blocks.html: Far west, the Third Emperor’s court learns a new gravity. The young woman who once waited in an anteroom now finishes sentences the emperor starts. Clerks say her influence is growing by the day. They say it softly.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 멀리, 고종의 조정은 새 중력을 배운다. 곁방에서 기다리던 젊은 여인이 이제 황제가 시작한 문장을 끝낸다. 서기들은 영향력이 날로 커진다고 한다. 작게 말한다.

blocks.html: Before Bupmin was anybody's heir, he was a prince with bad arithmetic. Ten years back, a harbour girl is about to tell him so…!
blocks.ko: 법민이 누구의 후계자이기도 전, 그는 셈이 서툰 왕자였다. 십 년 전 어느 항구, 한 아가씨가 그 사실을 대놓고 말해 주려 한다…!
