blocks.html: Yushin sends Bupmin to the coast to work under Kim Seonpum. It is a season with a tide book instead of a training yard. The quay does not care that he is a prince. It cares whether the sums close.
blocks.ko: 유신은 법민을 바닷가로 보내 김선품 밑에서 일하게 한다. 연무장 대신 조수 장부를 붙든 한 철이다. 항구는 그가 왕자든 말든 상관없다. 셈이 맞는지만 따진다.

blocks.html: Silla’s only door to the western sea. Everyone knows which door.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 바다로 난 신라의 단 하나뿐인 문. 다들 그 문이 어딘지 안다.

blocks.html: Her name is Jahee. Tonight she is the daughter who keeps Seonpum’s inkstones, and she has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy.
blocks.ko: 그녀의 이름은 자희다. 오늘 밤 그녀는 선품의 벼루를 지키는 딸이고, 그의 셈이 헐겁다고 이미 결론을 내렸다.

en: Your sums are wrong.
The tide does not care that you are a prince.
Count again.
While I am watching.
…Where.
No — / Please show me.

blocks.html: She corrects the sum with a brush he was not supposed to steal. Warehouse lamp. Salt on the page. He watches her mouth instead of the numbers, and she lets him, once, because the tide will not wait for dignity.
blocks.ko: 그가 훔치면 안 되는 붓으로 그녀는 셈을 고친다. 창고 등. 페이지 위의 소금. 그는 숫자 대신 입을 보고, 그녀는 한 번 허락한다. 조수는 체면을 기다려 주지 않으니까.

blocks.html: Rain finds the eave. They stand inside a hard rain-curtain with a wet ledger between them, and almost do the stupid thing, and do not — until there is a stolen brush between their mouths, and then they do.
blocks.ko: 비가 처마를 찾는다. 그들은 젖은 장부를 사이에 두고 단단한 빗줄기 커튼 안에 서서, 바보 같은 일을 거의 하고, 하지 않는다 — 훔친 붓이 입 사이에 놓일 때까지. 그리고 그때는 한다.

en: Father is coughing.
From the warehouse shadow.
…Which is why it has to be now.
Before the tide comes in.
Do not close the book.
If you close it I…
will not know where to go.

blocks.html: Seonpum coughs once from the dark and pretends he did not see a prince learning the harbour by kissing the girl who can count. Years later the court will name her Jayi. The quay already had the true name.
blocks.ko: 선품이 어둠에서 한 번 기침하고, 셈할 줄 아는 소녀에게 입 맞추며 항구를 배우는 왕자를 보지 못한 척한다. 여러 해 뒤 조정은 그녀를 자의라 부를 것이다. 항구는 이미 진짜 이름을 가지고 있었다.

blocks.html: His queen, Queen Jayi, was the daughter of the pajinchan Seonpum. Bupmin was striking in looks, bright, and full of wise plans.
blocks.ko: 왕비 자의왕후는 파진찬 선품의 딸이다. 법민은 용모가 빼어나고, 총명하며 지략이 많았다.
blocks.hanja: 妃慈儀王后，波珍飡善品之女也。法敏姿表英特，聰明多智略。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, accession

blocks.label: The Next King
blocks.ko: 다음 임금

blocks.html: Two queens come and go. Bupmin rides with the Hwarang through both. He never becomes the best gyuku player in Surabol. He becomes the one who remembers why the game was invented. When “a king for all” finally fits a grown mouth, the words already have dust on them.
blocks.ko: 여왕 둘이 오고 간다. 법민은 그 내내 화랑과 함께 말을 달린다. 서라벌 최고의 격구 선수는 끝내 못 된다. 대신 그 놀이가 왜 생겼는지 기억하는 사람이 된다. ‘모두의 왕’이라는 말이 마침내 다 큰 입에 맞을 무렵, 그 말엔 이미 먼지가 앉아 있다.

en: Marshal.
When I said king for all — did I mean every kingdom, or every person who bleeds for one?
lines: 모두를 위한 임금이라 했을 때 — 모든 나라를 말한 겁니까, 아니면 하나를 위해 피 흘리는 모든 사람을 말한 겁니까.

en: Ask the yard again tomorrow.
If the answer is only a speech, you are still six.
If it costs you a bruise — you are becoming Hwarang.
lines: 멍이 값이면 — 화랑이 되어 가는 거다.

blocks.html: Bupmin wants to be a king for all. So did Silla’s first. To meet him, go back to a white horse kneeling…!
blocks.ko: 법민은 모두의 왕이 되고 싶다. 첫 임금도 그랬다. 그를 만나려면, 들판에 무릎 꿇은 흰 말에게로 거슬러 올라가야 한다…!

images.at: crown as king while he is still a boy
images.alt: The six chiefs crown the thirteen-year-old Hyukgose on a riverbank mound at dusk
images.prompt: History, not myth: the six village chiefs of Saro crown the boy king. Low three-quarter worm’s-eye on a packed-earth ritual mound above the Alcheon river at dusk, 57 BC: no palace yet, only thatch, timber and earth. The six chiefs in plain wide-sleeved robes and black jougwan stand in a half-ring; the eldest, white-bearded, raises the gold crown in both hands over a THIRTEEN-YEAR-OLD boy, Hyukgose, kneeling on a straw mat with his head up and unafraid (his face is a boy’s version of the attached portrait). A brazier just outside the frame at lower right rakes firelight up across the boy’s face, the chiefs’ sleeves and the raised gold; behind them the river and the six villages’ thatched roofs dissolve into blue dusk haze, small lamps as bokeh. ONE device: the half-ring of chiefs converging on the raised crown. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 still, low strip composition at night. Five low grass burial mounds (Oreung) in a row across the lower third, in mist among dark pines at Seorabeol. ONE device: the flat line of the mounds against a vast moonlit cloud field. High in the clouds, barely there, a cloud shaped like a winged horse running upward — ambiguous, it could be weather. Moon behind thin cloud as the key, cool #6f9fe8 light, long blue shadows. No people. Granulated watercolor mist. CANON — CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: White winged heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style — match the board. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, not a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. HEEWON STYLE: a hand-painted ANIME film frame composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are anime: clean ink linework, simplified anime faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is watercolor and oil: skies, dust, ground and light are visibly hand-painted — wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation, soft bleeding edges, dry-brush dust, rich oil glazes in the darks, faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into wash. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Not a katana, not a tsuba, not a short jian, not a ball pommel. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow aura / emissive skin around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide; katana / tsuba / random sabre length instead of sw_bidam 환두대도.

The only colour is a pale translucent blue wash on the eggshell. ONE device: the black crack splitting the egg. blocks.html: After the fall of Old Joseon, the local chiefs gather to select a new king when a White Horse suddenly leaves an egg — blue sky above, and later the court will keep the moon as its quiet sign.
blocks.ko: 고조선이 무너진 뒤, 여섯 마을의 촌장들이 새 임금을 뽑으러 모였을 때 — 흰 말 한 마리가 알을 남기고 푸른 하늘로 오른다. 훗날 조정은 그 고요한 표지로 달을 지킬 것이다.

blocks.html: At a well in the hills, the horse knelt and cried. Six chiefs dug where it stood. They lifted out a great egg. The shell opened on a boy who already looked like a king. He learns fast. The chiefs say the land has been waiting.
blocks.ko: 산골 우물가에서 말이 무릎을 꿇고 울었다. 여섯 촌장이 그 자리를 팠다. 큰 알 하나가 나왔다. 껍질이 갈라지자, 벌써 임금 얼굴을 한 사내아이가 있었다. 배우는 게 빠르다. 촌장들은 이 땅이 그를 기다려 왔다고 한다.

blocks.html: A young boy is born from the egg, whom the chiefs name Hyukgosé — to rule with brightness — and crown as king while he is still a boy; tradition says thirteen.
blocks.ko: 그 알에서 사내아이가 태어나니, 촌장들은 혁거세 — 세상을 밝히는 빛 — 라 이름 짓고, 어린 나이에 — 전통은 열세 — 임금으로 세운다.

blocks.caption: Hyukgose. Born from an egg, crowned before his voice broke.
blocks.ko: 혁거세. 알에서 태어나, 목소리가 굵어지기도 전에 왕관을 썼다.

blocks.hanja: 白馬跪而悲鳴 掘地得大青卵 開之有童男 號曰赫居世
blocks.ko: 흰 말이 무릎 꿇고 슬피 울자, 그 자리를 파니 큰 푸른 알이 있었다. 알을 여니 동자가 있어, 이름하여 혁거세라 하였다.
blocks.html: A white horse knelt and cried aloud; they dug the ground and found a great blue egg. They opened it, and there was a boy-child; they named him Hyeokgeose.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonder 1 — Founding of Silla (Hyeokgeose); Ha & Mintz tr., pp. 49–50

blocks.html: The chroniclers disagree about the colour of the egg and agree about the horse. Before anyone dug, the six chiefs saw it from the ridge of Mount Yang: a light hanging down beside Najeong like lightning that had forgotten to leave, and under it a white horse folded onto its knees, as if someone important were waiting in the grass.
blocks.ko: 알의 빛깔을 두고는 사서들이 다투지만, 말에 대해서는 다투지 않는다. 땅을 파기도 전에 여섯 촌장은 양산 능선에서 그것을 보았다. 나정 곁으로 떠나기를 잊은 번개처럼 빛이 드리워 있고, 그 아래 흰 말 한 마리가, 풀숲에 귀한 이라도 기다리는 듯 무릎을 꿇고 있었다.

en: That’s… a horse, right?
Why’s a horse kneeling? Who to?

lines: 날개 달린 말 본 적 있어? 난 없어.
en: You ever seen a horse with wings? I haven’t.
…That one’s got wings, though.
Slow. Go slow. If it spooks—

blocks.html: It does not spook. It lets them come close enough to see that its wings are folded the way a bird folds them and that its eyes are on the grass, not on them. Then it looks up and sees six grown men creeping at it through the pines with their sleeves held out like nets.
blocks.ko: 말은 놀라지 않는다. 새가 날개를 접듯 날개를 접고 있다는 것, 눈이 그들이 아니라 풀숲에 가 있다는 것이 보일 만큼 가까이 오게 둔다. 그러다 고개를 들고, 다 큰 사내 여섯이 그물처럼 소매를 벌린 채 소나무 사이로 기어 오는 것을 본다.

blocks.html: Below Mount Yang, beside Najeong well, a strange vapour like a flash of lightning hung down to the ground, and there was a white horse kneeling as if in obeisance. They went to look and found a purple egg (one account says a great blue egg). The horse saw the men, gave a long neigh, and rose up to heaven.
blocks.ko: 양산 아래 나정 곁에 번개 같은 이상한 기운이 땅에 드리웠고, 흰 말 한 마리가 절하듯 꿇어앉아 있었다. 찾아가 살펴보니 자줏빛 알 하나가 있었다(푸른 큰 알이라고도 한다). 말은 사람을 보자 길게 울고 하늘로 올라갔다.
blocks.hanja: 楊山下蘿井傍 異氣如電光垂地 有一白馬跪拜之狀 尋撿之 有一紫卵(一云靑大卵) 馬見人長嘶上天
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders 1 — Silla Founder Hyeokgeose (新羅始祖 赫居世王)

blocks.html: Six chiefs stand in a wet field with their arms still out, holding nothing. Much later, when the country has a name and a calendar and a clerk for everything, the horse will be painted on a saddle-flap and buried with a king and called Chunma, the heavenly horse. That morning nobody calls it anything. Alpyung is the first to look down at what it was kneeling over.
blocks.ko: 여섯 촌장이 젖은 들판에 팔을 벌린 채, 아무것도 쥐지 못하고 서 있다. 한참 뒤, 나라에 이름과 달력과 무엇에나 서기가 생긴 뒤, 그 말은 말다래에 그려져 어느 왕과 함께 묻히고 천마라 불릴 것이다. 그날 아침엔 아무도 그것을 무어라 부르지 않는다. 발밑, 말이 꿇어앉아 있던 자리를 처음 내려다본 것은 알평이다.

lines: 파 봐. 다들 뭐 해, 파 보라니까.
en: …It left something.
Dig. What are you all doing? Dig.

blocks.html: A few years later, Lady Alyoung is born from a Chicken Dragon’s rib at Alyeongjeong well — matched omen to matched omen — and she and Hyukgosé fall in love as two children the country already knew were throne-sized. They marry because they want each other. The omens agree.
blocks.ko: 몇 해 뒤, 계룡의 왼쪽 갈비뼈에서 알영부인이 알영정 우물가에 태어난다 — 알과 알, 징조와 징조 — 그리고 혁거세와 그녀는 나라가 이미 왕의 크기라 알았던 두 아이로서 사랑에 빠진다. 서로 원해서 혼인한다. 징조도 같은 편이다.

blocks.caption: Lady Alyoung. Born from a dragon’s rib, and the one person in Seorabeol who can tell the king no.
blocks.ko: 알영부인. 계룡의 갈비뼈에서 났고, 서라벌에서 임금에게 안 된다고 말할 수 있는 단 한 사람.

en: One from an egg, one from a chicken.
…Did this country start in a kitchen?

blocks.html: Why did Old Joseon fall?
blocks.ko: 고조선은 왜 무너졌는가?

blocks.html: We’re going to create a brand new country — where families care for one another as one great house, and no one is left outside the gate.
blocks.ko: 우리는 아주 새로운 나라를 만들 것이다 — 가문들이 한집안처럼 서로를 돌보고, 누구도 문밖에 버려지지 않는 나라를.

blocks.html: The Royals will watch over all the people, like their very own children.
blocks.ko: 왕족은 백성을 제 자식처럼 보살필 것이다.

blocks.html: The Nobles will be wise and righteous, making decisions for the good of the nation.
blocks.ko: 귀족은 지혜롭고 의로울 것이며, 나라를 위해 판단할 것이다.

blocks.html: We will divide the common people into 6 ranks, according to their virtues. This is going to be the start of a New Unity… Silla!
blocks.ko: 백성은 그 덕에 따라 여섯 등급으로 나눌 것이다. 이것이 새로운 하나 됨의 시작이다… 신라!

blocks.html: Six families end up running everything. In every new country, six families always do.
blocks.ko: 여섯 가문이 정치를 쥔다. 새 나라는 어디든, 결국 여섯 가문이 쥔다.

blocks.html: They say the first king learned love before law: one person to cherish, one person to serve — and the moon over Seorabeol was enough light for both.
blocks.ko: 첫 임금은 법보다 사랑을 먼저 배웠다고 한다. 아끼는 이 하나, 섬기는 이 하나 — 서라벌 위의 달빛이면 둘 다에 족했다.

en: I have heard that a true man needs only
one person to cherish,
and one person to serve,
and that is enough.

blocks.html: Sixty-one years later, the chronicle says, the king went up into the sky, and seven days after that his body came down again in five pieces, scattered over the ground. Nobody records a horse. Everybody in Seorabeol says there was one.
blocks.ko: 예순한 해 뒤, 편년은 말한다. 왕이 하늘로 올라갔고, 이레 뒤 그 몸이 다섯 조각으로 땅에 흩어져 내려왔다고. 말이 있었다고 적은 사람은 없다. 서라벌 사람들은 모두 있었다고 말한다.

blocks.html: He ruled the country sixty-one years, and the king rose up to heaven. Seven days later his remains fell scattered to the ground… The people wished to bury them together, but a great serpent chased them off; so they buried the five parts separately and made the Five Tombs, also called the Serpent Tombs.
blocks.ko: 나라를 다스린 지 예순한 해에 왕이 하늘로 올라갔다. 이레 뒤 유체가 땅에 흩어져 떨어졌다… 나라 사람들이 합쳐 장사 지내려 하자 큰 뱀이 쫓아 막으므로, 다섯 몸을 따로 묻어 오릉으로 삼았다. 사릉이라고도 한다.
blocks.hanja: 理國六十一年 王升于天 七日後 遺體散落于地 … 國人欲合而葬之 有大蛇逐禁 各葬五體爲五陵 亦名蛇陵
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders 1 — Silla Founder Hyeokgeose (新羅始祖 赫居世王)

blocks.html: A chest rides the tide in, a magpie screaming over it. Whatever is inside needs a house. Preferably someone else’s…!
blocks.ko: 밀물을 타고 궤짝 하나가 들어온다. 까치 한 마리가 그 위에서 울어 댄다. 안에 든 놈은 집이 필요하다. 되도록이면 남의 집이…!

images.at: a chest comes in on the tide at
images.alt: A chest rides the tide into Ajinpo under a crying magpie
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. A heavy timber chest rides a towering ink swell into the cove at Ajinpo, the sea splashed black with claw-shaped crests of bare paper; a black magpie wheels and cries above it; the shore is a dry-brush strip with one tiny old woman holding a rope. ONE device: the long diagonal of the wave carrying the chest. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.at: standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders
images.alt: In King Suro’s hall: Talhae, a man again, bows with feathers drifting off his shoulders; Suro on the throne, feathers settling, pale with relief
images.prompt: Inside King Suro’s torchlit Gaya hall at night, worm’s-eye from the floor, hard dutch tilt: a burst of brown sparrow feathers explodes outward around Talhae as he lands back in his own body, already dropping into a lopsided bow, grinning; behind and above him on the dais King Suro, falcon feathers still swirling off his shoulders, grips the throne arms, pale with relief. Feathers fly at the lens. MANGA ACTION FRAME: a single seinen historical-manga action panel painted in ink and oil — bold dry-brush sumi-ink SPEED LINES streaking along the direction of motion, radial FOCUS LINES converging on the face or the blade, motion smears on legs, mane, cloth and steel, flung ink-splatter dirt and dust, extreme foreshortening and a hard dutch tilt so the frame itself feels like it is moving; heavy black ink masses against a few hard highlights, one gold accent. Faces stay clean webtoon ink line with fierce narrowed eyes. Full-bleed single frame: NO panel borders, NO speech bubbles, NO onomatopoeia or sound-effect lettering, NO text of any kind. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — SEOK TALHAE. Look: Very tall (nine cheok), long-limbed and sea-weathered, tanned, broad easy grin, sly narrow eyes; black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands; clean-shaven as a young man, a short grey beard when he is old and king. Dress: Young: plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman’s cord belt. King: deep sea-green silk robe with a gold-ringed belt and a low gold diadem. Demeanor: A con man who became a king and never stopped enjoying the joke. Deadpan when caught, delighted when he wins. #5a7fa8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KING SURO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_suro.png (face only; invent a new pose). #e0a33c as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. images.prompt: Worm’s-eye from inside a freshly dug hole at the minister’s gate in low morning sun: the whetstone and charcoal lie black on the rim in the sharp foreground; above, magistrate’s men lean on spades, old Hogong, gourd at his waist, points down at Talhae in trembling outrage, and Talhae looks down into the hole with arms folded, deadpan. Long raking shadows. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — HOGONG. Look: Small, wiry old man from Wa, bald crown with a grey fringe tied back, thin white beard, quick indignant eyes. Dress: Faded indigo minister’s robe; a dried calabash gourd always tied at his waist on a cord. Demeanor: Perpetually outraged and perpetually loyal; the straight man to Talhae’s joke for forty years. #a8894a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | SEOK TALHAE. Look: Very tall (nine cheok), long-limbed and sea-weathered, tanned, broad easy grin, sly narrow eyes; black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands; clean-shaven as a young man, a short grey beard when he is old and king. Dress: Young: plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman’s cord belt. King: deep sea-green silk robe with a gold-ringed belt and a low gold diadem. Demeanor: A con man who became a king and never stopped enjoying the joke. Deadpan when caught, delighted when he wins. #5a7fa8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: The queen of Dapana lays her egg in a chest at the night shore
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Night shore of Dapana: a queen in layered robes kneels at the waterline, forehead pressed to a huge silk-wrapped egg lying inside an open chest among a few treasures; the chest lid is a black diagonal; the night sea is one solid mass of black ink and the moon a bare paper circle; far up the beach the king is a small black back walking away. ONE device: the open lid’s diagonal. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

blocks.html: Late in the first king’s reign, a chest comes in on the tide at a fishing beach. A magpie flies over it, crying.
blocks.ko: 첫 임금의 치세도 저물 무렵, 밀물을 타고 궤짝 하나가 갯마을 바닷가로 들어온다. 그 위로 까치 한 마리가 울며 난다.

blocks.html: It has come a long way. A thousand li north-east of Wa, the queen of a country called Dapana carried a child for seven years and was delivered of an egg. The king said a person who lays an egg is an ill omen and should get rid of it. She could not. She wrapped it in silk, packed it in a chest with treasure, and gave it to the sea.
blocks.ko: 먼 길을 왔다. 왜에서 동북쪽으로 천 리, 다파나라는 나라의 왕비가 아이를 일곱 해 품고는 알을 낳았다. 왕은 사람이 알을 낳는 것은 상서롭지 못하니 버리라 했다. 왕비는 그러지 못했다. 알을 비단에 싸서 보물과 함께 궤짝에 넣고, 바다에 맡겼다.

blocks.hanja: 脫解本多婆那國所生也。其國在倭國東北一千里。初，其國王娶女國王女爲妻，有娠七年，乃生大卵。王曰：「人而生卵，不祥也，宜棄之。」其女不忍，以帛裏卵并寶物置於櫝中，浮於海，任其所往。
blocks.html: Talhae was born in the land of Dapana, which lies a thousand li north-east of Wa. Its king had taken to wife the daughter of the king of the Land of Women. She was with child seven years, and then bore a great egg. The king said: “For a person to bear an egg is unlucky; it should be cast away.” She could not bear to, and wrapped the egg in silk, laid it in a chest with treasures, and set it afloat on the sea to go where it would.
blocks.ko: 탈해는 본래 다파나국에서 태어났다. 그 나라는 왜국 동북쪽 천 리에 있다. 처음에 그 나라 왕이 여국 왕의 딸을 아내로 맞았는데, 아이를 밴 지 일곱 해 만에 큰 알을 낳았다. 왕이 말하였다. “사람이 알을 낳는 것은 상서롭지 못하니 버려야 한다.” 그 여인은 차마 그러지 못하고, 비단으로 알을 싸서 보물과 함께 궤짝에 넣어 바다에 띄워, 가는 대로 맡겼다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: It reaches Gaya first. The people of Golden Gaya see a strange chest bobbing off their beach and, being sensible, leave it there.
blocks.ko: 궤짝은 먼저 가야에 닿는다. 금관가야 사람들은 이상한 궤짝이 바닷가에 떠다니는 것을 보고, 분별 있게도, 그냥 둔다.

blocks.html: Gaya tells it differently, and with more nerve. In the Gaya chronicle Talhae comes ashore a grown man, walks into King Suro’s hall, and asks for the throne.
blocks.ko: 가야는 이 이야기를 다르게, 더 배짱 좋게 한다. 가야의 기록에서 탈해는 다 큰 사내로 뭍에 올라 수로왕의 전각으로 걸어 들어가서는, 왕좌를 내놓으라고 한다.

blocks.caption: Seok Talhae. He arrived in a chest and talks like he owns the beach.
blocks.ko: 석탈해. 궤짝에 실려 왔는데, 말투는 해변 주인이다.

en: I’ve come for your throne.
You can fight me for it, or you can save us both the afternoon.
lines: 겨루어도 좋고, 서로 오후를 아껴도 좋소.

en: …Heaven gave it to me.
I— it isn’t mine to give. Or to… lose.
lines: 과인이— 내줄 수 있는 것이 아니오. 잃을 수 있는 것도…

blocks.html: So they fight the way kings fight in that country. Talhae becomes a hawk, and Suro becomes an eagle. Talhae becomes a sparrow, and Suro becomes a falcon. When Talhae is a man again he is standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders, and he bows.
blocks.ko: 그래서 둘은 그 나라에서 왕들이 겨루는 방식으로 겨룬다. 탈해가 매가 되자 수로는 독수리가 된다. 탈해가 참새가 되자 수로는 새매가 된다. 탈해가 다시 사람이 되었을 때 그는 어깨에 깃털을 얹은 채 전각 한가운데 서 있다. 그리고 절을 한다.

en: …That was a falcon.
Fine. I’ll find a country with a smaller king.
lines: 좋소. 왕이 좀 작은 나라를 찾아보지.

blocks.html: Either way, the chest goes on. At Ajinpo an old woman on the shore hauls it in with a rope and opens it, and there is a little boy inside, sitting among the treasure as if it were his luggage.
blocks.ko: 어느 쪽이든 궤짝은 계속 간다. 아진포 바닷가에서 한 노파가 밧줄로 궤짝을 끌어올려 열어 보니, 안에 사내아이 하나가 보물 사이에 짐 보따리라도 되는 듯 앉아 있다.

en: Well.
You’re not a fish.
No.
Is this the country?

blocks.html: She names him herself, since there is nobody else to ask. A magpie followed the chest in, so she takes the bird out of the character for magpie, and what is left, Seok, is his surname. He got loose from the chest and came out of it, so he is Talhae, the one who got loose.
blocks.ko: 달리 물어볼 사람도 없으니 이름은 그녀가 짓는다. 까치가 궤짝을 따라왔으니 까치 작(鵲) 자에서 새 조(鳥)를 떼어 낸다. 남은 석(昔)이 그의 성이다. 궤짝을 풀고 나왔으니 탈해(脫解), 풀려난 아이다.

blocks.hanja: 或曰：「此兒不知姓氏。初，櫝來時，有一鵲飛鳴而隨之。宜省鵲字，以昔爲氏。又解韞櫝而出，宜名脫解。」
blocks.html: Someone said: “Nobody knows this child’s surname. When the chest first came, a magpie flew after it, crying. Take part of the character for magpie and make Seok his surname. And since he undid the chest and came out of it, name him Talhae.”
blocks.ko: 어떤 이가 말하였다. “이 아이는 성씨를 알 수 없다. 처음 궤짝이 올 때 까치 한 마리가 울며 따라왔으니, 까치 작(鵲) 자를 줄여 석(昔)을 성으로 삼아야 한다. 또 싸인 궤짝을 풀고 나왔으니 탈해라 이름 지어야 한다.”
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: He grows nine cheok tall, fishes to feed the old woman and never once complains about it, and when she tells him that a boy with bones like his should study, he studies geography. Mostly the part about where the good ground is.
blocks.ko: 그는 아홉 자로 자라고, 고기를 낚아 노파를 먹이며 한 번도 싫은 내색을 하지 않는다. 너 같은 골격을 가진 아이는 공부를 해야 한다고 노파가 말하자, 그는 지리를 공부한다. 주로 좋은 땅이 어디 있는지에 관한 부분을.

blocks.label: The Crescent House
blocks.ko: 반월의 집

blocks.html: Looking over the city, he picks the best ground in it, a crescent-shaped rise above the river, and finds that someone already lives there. The house belongs to Hogong, a minister who came over the sea from Wa long ago with a gourd tied at his waist to float on, and has the name to prove it.
blocks.ko: 도성을 내려다보며 그는 그 안에서 가장 좋은 땅을 고른다. 강 위로 반달 모양으로 솟은 언덕. 그런데 이미 누가 살고 있다. 집주인은 호공이다. 오래전 허리에 박을 매달고 왜에서 바다를 건너온 대신으로, 그 이름이 증거다.

blocks.hanja: 瓠公者，未詳其族姓，本倭人，初以瓠繫腰渡海而來，故稱瓠公。
blocks.html: As for Hogong, his clan and surname are not known. He was a man of Wa, and at first he crossed the sea with a gourd tied at his waist; hence he was called Hogong, Lord Gourd.
blocks.ko: 호공은 그 족성을 자세히 알 수 없다. 본래 왜인으로, 처음에 박을 허리에 매고 바다를 건너왔으므로 호공이라 불렀다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Hyeokgeose, yr. 38

blocks.html: Talhae does not have a house. He has a plan. One night he buries a whetstone and a sack of charcoal beside Hogong’s gate, and in the morning he goes to the magistrate and says the house was his family’s, taken while they were away.
blocks.ko: 탈해에게는 집이 없다. 계획이 있다. 어느 밤 그는 호공의 대문 옆에 숫돌과 숯 한 자루를 묻고, 아침이 되자 관아에 가서 그 집이 원래 자기 집안 것이었는데 집을 비운 사이 빼앗겼다고 아뢴다.

en: I have lived in that house thirty years!
lines: 내가 저 집에서 삼십 년을 살았소!

en: And my family lived there before you. We were smiths.
Dig by the gate, if you don’t believe me.
lines: 그 전에는 우리 집안이 살았소. 대장장이였지.
못 믿겠거든 대문 옆을 파 보시오.

blocks.html: They dig. The whetstone and the charcoal come up out of the ground, black and convincing, and the magistrate gives Talhae the house.
blocks.ko: 파 본다. 숫돌과 숯이 땅속에서 나온다. 시커멓고, 그럴듯하게. 관아는 집을 탈해에게 준다.

en: …You buried those last night.
Prove it.

blocks.hanja: 望楊山下瓠公宅，以爲吉地，設詭計以取而居之，其地後爲月城。
blocks.html: He looked at Hogong’s house below Mount Yang and judged it auspicious ground; he laid a cunning plan, took it, and lived there. That ground later became Wolseong.
blocks.ko: 양산 아래 호공의 집을 바라보고 길한 땅이라 여겨, 속임수를 써서 빼앗아 살았다. 그 땅이 뒤에 월성이 되었다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: The ground becomes Wolseong, the Crescent Moon Fortress, where every king of Silla after him will live, which means every king of Silla lives in a stolen house. Nobody in the palace likes it when you mention this.
blocks.ko: 그 땅이 월성, 반월성이 된다. 그 뒤 신라의 모든 왕이 그곳에 산다. 다시 말해 신라의 모든 왕은 훔친 집에 산다. 궁에서는 누가 이 말을 꺼내면 다들 싫어한다.

blocks.html: King Namhae hears about the clever young man in the crescent house and marries him to his daughter. Two kings later Talhae is sixty-two and on the throne himself, and one of the first things he does is make Hogong his chief minister, which is either an apology or the best joke in the annals.
blocks.ko: 남해왕은 반달 언덕 집의 영리한 젊은이 이야기를 듣고 딸을 그에게 시집보낸다. 왕이 두 번 바뀐 뒤, 예순둘의 탈해가 몸소 왕위에 오른다. 그가 맨 먼저 한 일 가운데 하나는 호공을 대보로 삼은 것이다. 사과이거나, 아니면 사서 전체에서 가장 좋은 농담이거나.

blocks.hanja: 二年春正月，拜瓠公爲大輔。
blocks.html: Second year, spring, first month: he appointed Hogong Grand Minister.
blocks.ko: 이년 봄 정월, 호공을 대보로 삼았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

en: …Grand Minister.
You know the best ground in the city. I could use a man like that.
lines: 도성에서 제일 좋은 땅을 아는 사람 아니오. 그런 사람이 필요하오.

en: I knew it. You did bury them.
Prove it.

blocks.html: “Hogong. There’s a rooster in the woods.” It is the middle of the night. Roosters don’t crow at night…!
blocks.ko: “호공. 숲에서 닭이 운다.” 한밤중이다. 닭은 밤에 울지 않는다…!

images.at: a small box of gold hanging from a branch
images.alt: A small gold box hangs from a pine branch in Sirim; a white rooster crows beneath
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Sirim wood at first light: one bent black pine branch crosses the frame; from it hangs a small box on a cord, the only colour a translucent gold wash; beneath it a white rooster on the roots crows upward, left as bare paper; far off at the wood’s edge a tiny Hogong with a lantern. Mist as untouched paper. ONE device: the hanging cord from branch to box. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.at: I came in a box too
images.alt: The old king Talhae crouches over the opened golden box, grinning; the small boy inside looks back at him as if the king were the strange one
images.prompt: Point of view from inside the opened golden box looking up: old King Talhae, short grey beard, leans down over the rim grinning, his face foreshortened and huge; at the bottom edge of the frame the small boy’s tiny hand and white silk sleeve reach up. Courtiers lean in blurred behind the king; a lattice shaft of morning light falls past him into the box. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — SEOK TALHAE. Look: Very tall (nine cheok), long-limbed and sea-weathered, tanned, broad easy grin, sly narrow eyes; black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands; clean-shaven as a young man, a short grey beard when he is old and king. Dress: Young: plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman’s cord belt. King: deep sea-green silk robe with a gold-ringed belt and a low gold diadem. Demeanor: A con man who became a king and never stopped enjoying the joke. Deadpan when caught, delighted when he wins. #5a7fa8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KIM ALJI. Look: A small boy of about four, round solemn face, bright wide-awake black eyes, short black hair tied in a tiny tuft. Dress: Wrapped in a little white silk cloth with a thin gold thread edge. Demeanor: Unafraid; looks at kings as if they were the strange ones. #d4b86a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.
