images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Night over Sirim: a long band of cloud hangs straight down out of a black ink sky into the wood like a lowered scroll; at its foot, among black trunks, the small silhouette of a rooster crowing; the city’s roofs tiny and black in the far distance with one lit window. ONE device: the vertical cloud band. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

blocks.html: In the ninth year of his reign King Talhae wakes in the night to a rooster crowing in the woods west of the city, which roosters do not do at night.
blocks.ko: 즉위 아홉 해, 탈해왕은 밤중에 도성 서쪽 숲에서 닭이 우는 소리에 잠을 깬다. 닭은 밤에 울지 않는다.

en: Hogong. There’s a rooster in Sirim.
Go and see what it wants.
Majesty, it’s a rooster. It wants—
…Yes, Majesty. Going.

blocks.html: At first light Hogong walks into Sirim with a lantern he no longer needs, and finds a small box of gold hanging from a branch, and a white rooster underneath it, crowing at nothing.
blocks.ko: 날이 밝을 무렵 호공은 이제 필요도 없는 등불을 들고 시림으로 들어간다. 나뭇가지에 작은 금빛 궤짝이 걸려 있고, 그 아래에서 흰 닭 한 마리가 아무것도 없는 데를 향해 울고 있다.

blocks.hanja: 九年春三月，王夜聞金城西始林樹間有鷄鳴聲。遲明，遣瓠公視之，有金色小櫝掛樹枝，白雞鳴於其下。
blocks.html: Ninth year, spring, third month: in the night the king heard a cock crowing among the trees of Sirim, west of Geumseong. At daybreak he sent Hogong to look, and there was a small gold-coloured chest hanging from a branch, and a white cock crowing beneath it.
blocks.ko: 구년 봄 삼월, 왕이 밤에 금성 서쪽 시림의 나무 사이에서 닭 우는 소리를 들었다. 날이 밝자 호공을 보내 살피게 하니, 금빛 작은 궤짝이 나뭇가지에 걸려 있고 흰 닭이 그 아래에서 울고 있었다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: They bring the box to the king and open it, and inside is a little boy, handsome and wide awake, who looks at the king as if the king were the one who had turned up in a box.
blocks.ko: 궤짝을 왕 앞에 가져와 여니, 안에 잘생기고 눈이 말똥말똥한 사내아이가 있다. 아이는 궤짝에서 나타난 쪽이 왕이기라도 한 것처럼 왕을 쳐다본다.

en: Well.
I came in a box too, you know. Mine was bigger.
lines: 나도 궤짝 타고 왔다. 내 건 더 컸지.

blocks.hanja: 瓠公還告，王使人取櫝開之，有小男兒在其中，姿容奇偉。上喜，謂左右曰：「此豈非天遺我以令胤乎！」乃收養之。
blocks.html: Hogong came back and reported it. The king had the chest brought and opened, and inside was a little boy of remarkable looks. The king was glad and said to those around him: “Is this not Heaven sending me a fine heir?” And he took him in and raised him.
blocks.ko: 호공이 돌아와 아뢰자, 왕이 사람을 시켜 궤짝을 가져와 열게 하니, 그 안에 작은 사내아이가 있었는데 생김새가 뛰어났다. 왕이 기뻐하여 좌우에 말하였다. “이 어찌 하늘이 내게 훌륭한 아들을 보내 준 것이 아니겠는가!” 그리고 거두어 길렀다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: Because he came out of a golden box, he is given the surname Kim, gold. Because he is a child, he is called Alji. The wood where the rooster crowed is renamed Gyerim, Rooster Wood, and for a while the whole country goes by that name.
blocks.ko: 금빛 궤짝에서 나왔으니 성은 김, 금이다. 아이이니 이름은 알지다. 닭이 울던 숲은 계림, 닭의 숲으로 이름이 바뀌고, 한동안은 나라 전체가 그 이름으로 불린다.

blocks.hanja: 及長，聰明多智略，乃名閼智。以其出於金櫝，姓金氏。改始林名雞林，因以爲國號。
blocks.html: When he grew up he was bright and full of wise plans, and he was named Alji. Since he had come out of a golden chest, his surname was Kim. Sirim was renamed Gyerim, and that became the name of the country.
blocks.ko: 자라자 총명하고 지략이 많아 알지라 이름 지었다. 금궤에서 나왔으므로 성을 김씨로 하였다. 시림을 계림으로 고치고, 그것을 나라 이름으로 삼았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: Talhae has sons of his own and does not give Alji the throne, and Alji, by every account, does not ask for it. It takes his line seven generations to reach the crown. When they do, they keep it for six hundred years, call themselves the Kims of Surabol, and look down on a family from Gaya who have the same name for a different reason.
blocks.ko: 탈해에게는 제 아들들이 있어 알지에게 왕위를 주지 않고, 어느 기록을 보아도 알지는 그것을 청하지 않는다. 그의 핏줄이 왕관에 닿기까지 일곱 대가 걸린다. 닿고 나서는 육백 년을 지키고, 스스로를 서라벌 김씨라 부르며, 다른 이유로 같은 성을 가진 가야 출신 집안을 내려다본다.

blocks.html: Under a certain hill beyond the city, the steam says the same word every time it leaves the water. It will be a long time before anybody answers it.
blocks.ko: 도성 너머 어느 언덕 아래에서는, 김이 물을 떠날 때마다 같은 말을 한다. 누군가 그 말에 대답하기까지는 아직 오래 걸릴 것이다.

blocks.html: Back to Baekje. The king can’t sign a thing for three years. And the clans have a list with one name on it…!
blocks.ko: 다시 백제. 임금은 삼 년 동안 도장 하나 찍지 못한다. 그리고 가문들 손에는 이름 하나만 적힌 명단이 있다…!

images.prompt: Far wide from low in dry autumn stubble at storm dusk. On a low rise on the right third, a Silla general in steel lamellar with a tall pointed jonghyeongju helm, blue cloth peeking at the collar, on a chestnut horse, with four mounted escorts and limp blue banners on poles, all looking the wrong way toward smoke on the horizon. Across the vast empty field from the left, a tiny black horse and rider streak toward them flat out, one long thin plume of dust trailing behind like a drawn line. ONE device: that dust-line diagonal across the empty field. Half the frame granulated storm sky; one low cloud-break rakes gold across the stubble and catches the dust line. Dark out-of-focus grass heads in the foreground. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. Rides low and coiled, like he fights. Armor: Baekje kit: steel lamellar, rounded Baekje helm with neck guard; yellow cloth peeking, red sash/skirt accent — never a yellow metal cuirass. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Phoenix blade — Single-edged phoenix blade — straight, held backwards along the forearm, phoenix on the ring pommel; one side only, as he is. Pommel motif phoenix inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One phoenix-ring sword, scabbard worn edge-up on the left hip. Fighting: REVERSE GRIP (역수), like a Japanese warrior's backhand hold: the small RING pommel pokes out ABOVE his thumb, the blade exits BELOW his little finger and lies flat back along the outside of his forearm toward the elbow, edge facing out. Low coiled crouch, blade-arm held across his body like a shield; he draws and cuts in one rising backhand slash, then stabs downward. Mounted, the blade trails back along the horse's flank. The blade is still the STRAIGHT ring-pommel sword of sw_bidam (handle:blade 1:3) — reverse grip is the hold, not a different sword. This hold overrides the hanging-blade 'ring at the little-finger side' note in SWORD ANATOMY; the ring→band→grip→collar→blade order is unchanged. SIGNATURE MOVE (the general-killer): alone on Gomanari at a flat-out gallop, he comes out of nowhere across an empty field straight at the enemy general, body folded flat and aerodynamic along the horse’s neck, cheek almost on the mane, the reverse-gripped blade laid back along his forearm and the horse’s flank; on the pass he snaps one backhand draw-cut, swift and clean like a samurai iai cut, and is already past, the blade flicked out to the side, before the escort moves. Show speed through the long low line of horse and rider, streaming mane, flung mud, motion-blurred ground — never gore; the cut reads as a bright arc, a flying helm plume or a riderless horse. #d9b13a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: curved blade, katana or tsuba (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); forward textbook grip once the fight starts; yellow metal cuirass; smiling in battle. | GOMANARI (고마나리, gyebek's horse) — attached board /obj_gomanari.png: Jet-black war horse with a long flowing black mane and tail — match the board. Plain dark tack, a yellow cord at the bridle. The fastest horse in Samhan: at full gallop his body stretches long and low, neck level, ears pinned, mane and tail streaming flat behind, hooves barely touching. Named for Gomanaru (Ungjin); stands by its master's planted sword after the field. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Baekje banners: warm yellow silk with a darker gold door-lintel and three gold stars. Attached flag /flag_baekje.png. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). One low gold shaft cuts across his eyes; the rest heavy black ink. MANGA ACTION FRAME: a single seinen historical-manga action panel painted in ink and oil — bold dry-brush sumi-ink SPEED LINES streaking along the direction of motion, radial FOCUS LINES converging on the face or the blade, motion smears on legs, mane, cloth and steel, flung ink-splatter dirt and dust, extreme foreshortening and a hard dutch tilt so the frame itself feels like it is moving; heavy black ink masses against a few hard highlights, one gold accent. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Plain dark tack, a yellow cord at the bridle. The fastest horse in Samhan: at full gallop his body stretches long and low, neck level, ears pinned, mane and tail streaming flat behind, hooves barely touching. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. Here it is Tamla (Jeju) in exile: add one tiny standing figure beside the hut — GYEBEK (attached portrait, face barely suggested), in plain clothes, arms at his sides, looking at nothing — and a small basket of oranges at his feet in the only touch of color, faint yellow #d9b13a. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. blocks.html: Three years of it, by the rite. For three years the king may not sit in judgement, may not sign, may not overturn. Everyone in Sabi knows exactly how long three years is, and exactly what can be done inside them.
blocks.ko: 예법대로 삼 년이다. 삼 년 동안 왕은 판결할 수 없고, 서명할 수 없고, 뒤집을 수 없다. 사비의 누구나 삼 년이 얼마나 긴지 정확히 알고, 그 안에서 무엇을 할 수 있는지도 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: Ninth day of the first month, year of the Wood Tiger. Satek Jijuk of Naji Fortress, grieving that the body’s days go so easily and its months come back so hard, cut gold to build a precious hall and carved jade to raise a treasure pagoda.
blocks.ko: 갑인년 정월 초아흐레, 나지성의 사택지적은 몸의 날이 쉬이 가는 것을 서러워하고 몸의 달이 돌아오기 어려움을 탄식하여, 금을 뚫어 보배로운 법당을 세우고 옥을 깎아 보탑을 세운다.
blocks.hanja: 甲寅年正月九日 奈祇城砂宅智積 慷身日之易往 慨體月之難還 穿金以建珍堂 鑿玉以立寶塔
blocks.source: Stele of Satek Jijeok (砂宅智積碑), Buyeo, 654 — Buyeo National Museum

blocks.html: The Queen was Satek. Her death removes the clan’s hand from the king’s sleeve, and the clan understands, before the funeral rites are finished, that the sleeve is now free.
blocks.ko: 왕후는 사택이었다. 그의 죽음으로 왕의 소매에서 가문의 손이 떨어져 나간다. 그리고 가문은 장례가 끝나기도 전에, 그 소매가 이제 자유롭다는 것을 알아차린다.

blocks.html: The Satek clan begins to worry that Euija is about to exact revenge on them, especially his confidante — Hundred-Victories Gyebek.
blocks.ko: 사택씨는 의자가 자신들에게 보복하려 한다고 여기기 시작한다. 특히 그의 심복 — 백승 계백 — 을 경계한다.

blocks.html: They have watched him work. On the border, Gyebek earned his nickname mostly one way. He leaves the line to other men and goes looking for the general. His black horse, Gomanari, is the fastest thing on four legs in Samhan. Gyebek rides him flat along the neck like a thrown knife, the blade reversed along his forearm. The general sees a black shape where the field was empty. He starts to turn his horse, and does not finish turning. One cut on the pass. By the time the escort draws, the black horse is a speck on the far ridge. An army stands in a field with nobody left to tell it what to do.
blocks.ko: 그들은 그가 일하는 걸 본 적이 있다. 국경에서 계백이 그 별명을 얻은 방식은 대개 하나였다. 진은 남들에게 맡기고, 그는 장수를 찾아간다. 검은 말 고마나리는 삼한에서 네 발 달린 것 중 가장 빠르다. 계백은 던진 칼처럼 그 목에 납작 엎드려 달린다. 칼날은 거꾸로 쥐어 팔뚝을 따라 눕혔다. 장수는 비어 있던 들판에 검은 것이 나타난 걸 본다. 말머리를 돌리기 시작하고, 끝내 다 돌리지 못한다. 스치며 한 번 벤다. 호위들이 칼을 뽑을 즈음 검은 말은 먼 능선 위의 점이다. 한 군대가, 무엇을 하라고 말해 줄 사람 하나 없이 들판에 서 있다.

lines: 그 자는 군대한테 달려드는 게 아니오.
상이 끝나면, 그 말머리가 어느 집 쪽으로 돌 것 같소.
en: He doesn’t ride at armies.
He rides at one man.
When the mourning’s over, whose house do you suppose that horse turns toward.

blocks.html: Gyebek has no clan. That is the whole problem. A man with a clan can be bargained with — you find out what his family wants and you give them some of it. A man with no clan wants only what the king wants, and there is nothing to buy.
blocks.ko: 계백에게는 가문이 없다. 문제의 전부가 그것이다. 가문이 있는 사람과는 흥정할 수 있다. 그 집안이 무엇을 원하는지 알아내 조금 떼어 주면 된다. 가문이 없는 사람은 왕이 원하는 것만 원하고, 그러면 살 것이 없다.

blocks.html: They put him on a ship the way you put a problem past the horizon. The berth he leaves from is Satek water; the captain who will not meet his eyes holds a Yunbi winter contract. Even exile, in Baekje, has to borrow a clan’s harbour.
blocks.ko: 그들은 그를, 문제를 지평선 너머로 밀듯 배에 올린다. 그가 떠나는 선석은 사택의 물이고, 눈을 마주치지 않는 선장은 윤비의 겨울 계약을 쥐고 있다. 백제에서는 유배조차 가문의 항구를 빌려야 한다.

en: See him off cleanly.
If the orange island’s pilots gossip, let them gossip about weather — not about which house signed the sail.
lines: 귤섬 뱃사공이 수다 떨거든, 날씨 이야기로 떨게 하게 — 어느 집이 돛에 도장을 찍었는지가 아니라.

blocks.html: So the two largest houses in Baekje meet, which has not happened in living memory except across a body.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 백제에서 가장 큰 두 집안이 마주 앉는다. 살아 있는 사람의 기억으로는, 주검을 사이에 두지 않고 그런 일이 있었던 적이 없다.

blocks.html: They meet at night, at a monastery that belongs to neither of them, and each brings the same number of men, counted twice at the gate by both sides.
blocks.ko: 밤에, 어느 쪽 것도 아닌 절에서 만난다. 양쪽 다 같은 수의 사람을 데려오고, 그 수는 문간에서 양쪽이 두 번씩 센다.

lines: 연비 공. 우리가 이러고 지낸 지 몇 대째요?
en: Lord Yunbi. How many generations have we been at this?

blocks.speaker: 🎗 Yunbi
lines: 작년 등절에 죽은 셋 중 둘이 내 조카였소.
en: Four.
Two of the three who died at the lantern festival last year were my nephews.
One of them was my grandson.

blocks.html: Neither of them apologises. Nobody expected it and it would have ended the meeting.
blocks.ko: 어느 쪽도 사과하지 않는다. 아무도 기대하지 않았고, 했다면 그 자리로 끝났을 것이다.

blocks.html: Halfway through the wine, a servant finds a second set of footprints behind the monastery screen — too small for the counted guards, too careful for a pilgrim. Yunbi’s man and Satek’s man look at each other and, for once, do not accuse. Someone is listening for a third house. Or for the king.
blocks.ko: 술이 반도 안 갔을 때, 종이 사찰 병풍 뒤에서 발자국 한 벌을 더 찾는다 — 세어 둔 호위치고는 너무 작고, 순례치고는 너무 조심스럽다. 연비의 사람과 사택의 사람이 서로를 보고, 이번만큼은 서로를 탓하지 않는다. 누군가 세 번째 집을 듣고 있다. 아니면 임금을.

en: Spill the cups.
Tonight the doors matter more than the words.

blocks.speaker: 🎗 Yunbi
en: So why did you send for me tonight.
His Majesty has more than forty sons.
Where do you imagine he means to seat them.

blocks.speaker: 🎗 Yunbi
en: …In our chairs.
In the chairs of all eight houses.

blocks.html: It goes quiet. Outside, the two sets of men are standing apart in the courtyard, arranged by habit into the shape of a fight.
blocks.ko: 조용해진다. 밖에서는 두 편의 사람들이 마당에 떨어져 서 있다. 버릇대로, 싸움의 모양으로.

blocks.speaker: 🎗 Yunbi
en: We will destroy each other and lose everything.
…For how long.

lines: 그 뒤엔 다시 하던 대로 하십시다.
en: As long as it takes.
After that we go back to the way we were.

blocks.speaker: 🎗 Yunbi
en: Agreed.
What gets removed first.
The one with no house.

blocks.html: They do not say his name at the table. Two houses that have not agreed on anything since before the capital moved agree, in under an hour, on one soldier with no family — and the agreement is written down nowhere, because agreements like that never are.
blocks.ko: 그들은 상 위에서 그의 이름을 부르지 않는다. 도읍을 옮기기 전부터 어떤 것에도 합의한 적 없는 두 집안이, 한 시진도 안 되어 가문 없는 군인 하나를 두고 합의한다. 그 합의는 어디에도 적히지 않는다. 그런 합의는 원래 적히지 않는다.

en: There is no price on that man.
Things without a price get removed.

blocks.html: They try the ordinary way first: they offer him a name. A real one, an old one, the eighth branch of a minor house, papers and a grave-line and ancestors. It is a serious offer and it is the only thing he has ever wanted.
blocks.ko: 먼저 통상적인 방법을 쓴다. 이름을 준다. 진짜 이름을, 오래된 이름을. 작은 집안의 여덟째 갈래, 문서와 산소와 조상까지. 진지한 제안이고, 그가 평생 원해 온 단 하나의 것이다.

en: …I already have one.

lines: 그건 임금이 지어 준 것 아닌가.
en: The king made that one up.

lines: 예. 그래서 갚아야 할 데가 있는 겁니다.
en: Yes. Which is why it is owed to someone.

blocks.html: Hundred-Victories narrowly escapes an assassination attempt, and begins to take security measures.
blocks.ko: 백승은 암살을 간신히 피하고, 몸을 지킬 채비를 하기 시작한다.

blocks.html: The arrow comes through a tent wall at the Ungjin drill ground and takes the man standing next to him, who was taller. Nobody is ever charged. The fletching is Baekje army issue, which narrows it to about nine thousand people, which is the point of using it.
blocks.ko: 웅진 훈련장에서 화살이 장막을 뚫고 들어와, 그의 옆에 서 있던 더 키 큰 사내를 데려간다. 아무도 처벌받지 않는다. 화살깃은 백제 관군의 것이고, 그러면 범위가 구천 명쯤으로 좁혀지는데, 그것을 쓴 이유가 바로 그것이다.

blocks.html: He stops eating food he has not watched being cooked. He sleeps in a different room each night, which the ministers immediately report to the regency as the behaviour of a man planning something.
blocks.ko: 그는 만드는 것을 보지 않은 음식은 먹지 않는다. 매일 밤 다른 방에서 잔다. 재상들은 그것을 즉시 무언가를 꾸미는 자의 행실이라고 섭정에 고한다.

lines: 장군. 나가 계시는 게 낫습니다. / 반년만. 폐하께서 상을 마치실 때까지.
en: General. You should be away from here. / Half a year. Until His Majesty is out of mourning.
…I don’t run.
Which is exactly how they win.

blocks.html: The order comes down while the king is still in mourning and cannot countermand it. Hundred-Victories Gyebek is put on a boat.
blocks.ko: 명은 임금이 아직 상중이라 뒤집을 수 없는 사이에 떨어진다. 백승계백은 배에 태워진다.

blocks.html: Nine, by then. Gyebek had been counting for years, quietly, the way you keep an eye on a leak.
blocks.ko: 그때쯤엔 아홉이었다. 계백은 여러 해를 조용히 세고 있었다. 새는 곳을 지켜보듯이.

blocks.html: To worship your own kind blindly is foolish; to hate your own kind blindly is more foolish still.
blocks.ko: 자기 무리를 맹목적으로 숭배하는 것은 어리석은 짓이지만, 자기 무리를 맹목적으로 증오하는 것은 그것보다도 더 어리석은 짓이다.

blocks.html: The truce holds exactly as long as it needs to. Four generations of blood, suspended for the length of one signature, and both houses will go back to burning each other’s carts before the year is out.
blocks.ko: 휴전은 필요한 만큼만 간다. 사대에 걸친 피가 서명 하나의 길이만큼 멈춘다. 두 집안은 해가 가기 전에 다시 서로의 수레를 태울 것이다.

blocks.html: Gyebek is summoned to the hall and told to kneel, and the order is read out over his head.
blocks.ko: 계백은 대전으로 불려 나와 무릎을 꿇으라는 말을 듣고, 명이 그의 머리 위로 읽혀 내려간다.

blocks.html: The order is genuine. That is the craftsmanship of it. It bears the royal seal, because a king in mourning leaves his seal with the Assembly so that the country does not stop, and the Assembly has had it for four months.
blocks.ko: 명은 진짜다. 그 점이 이 일의 솜씨다. 옥새가 찍혀 있다. 상중의 왕은 나라가 멈추지 않도록 옥새를 정사암 회의에 맡기고, 회의는 그것을 넉 달째 쥐고 있었다.

blocks.html: It is read with the king’s formula and the king’s seal — but not by the king. Minister Satek holds the Assembly’s borrowed stamp; the voice in the hall is the Premier’s.
blocks.ko: 왕의 문투와 왕의 옥새로 읽힌다 — 그러나 왕이 읽는 것은 아니다. 사택지적이 정사암회의가 빌린 도장을 쥐고 있고, 대전에서 울리는 목소리는 상좌평의 것이다.

lines: 상좌평 사택지적 — 정사암 회의의 이름으로 읽는다.
en: The seal is set.
Minister Satek — I read this in the Assembly’s name.
Gyebek is hereby sent into exile!
…It is His Majesty’s will.

blocks.html: Remember the young Satek who just called it His Majesty’s will. He will say worse things in His Majesty’s name, later, to a much bigger king.
blocks.ko: 방금 ‘전하의 뜻’이라 말한 사택 집안 젊은이를 기억해 두라. 그는 나중에, 훨씬 큰 임금 앞에서, 전하의 이름으로 더한 말을 한다.

en: …What did you say?

blocks.html: He is put on the boat the same afternoon. Satek water at the berth; a Yunbi winter contract in the captain’s sleeve. Even exile borrows a clan harbour.
blocks.ko: 그날 오후 바로 배에 오른다. 선석은 사택의 물이고, 선장의 소매에는 윤비의 겨울 계약이 있다. 유배조차 가문의 항구를 빌린다.

blocks.html: This year, in the first month, the king’s mother died. And his brother’s son Gyogi, with his mother’s four sisters, the Inner Minister Gimi and more than forty men of high name, were banished to an island.
blocks.ko: 올해 정월에 국주의 어머니가 죽었다. 또 아우 왕자의 아들 교기와 그 어머니의 누이 넷, 내좌평 기미, 이름 높은 사람 마흔여 명이 섬으로 쫓겨났다.
blocks.hanja: 今年正月、國主母薨。又弟王子兒翹岐及其母妹女子四人、內佐平岐味、有高名之人卌餘、被放於嶋。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 24, Kōgyoku 1 (642), second month — report of the Baekje mourning envoys’ attendants

blocks.html: He wakes on a beach with sand in his teeth and no idea how many days it has been. The not-knowing is worse than the beach.
blocks.ko: 입 안에 모래를 문 채 바닷가에서 깨어난다. 며칠이 지났는지 알 수 없다. 모른다는 것이 바닷가보다 더 나쁘다.

blocks.html: The island where Baekje sends men it can’t afford to kill.
blocks.ko: 백제가 죽이기엔 아까운 사내들을 보내는 섬.

blocks.caption: Yuri Dora, king of Tamla. He tells stories to men nobody else will talk to.
blocks.ko: 탐라의 임금 유리도라. 아무도 말을 걸지 않는 사내들에게 이야기를 들려준다.

en: How many days.
Ah. Not one for greetings, then.
…How many days.
Eleven. Better?

blocks.html: It is better. Visibly. The islanders will spend five years noticing that this man is calmed by numbers and unsettled by almost everything else.
blocks.ko: 나아진다. 눈에 보이게. 섬사람들은 다섯 해에 걸쳐 알게 된다. 이 사내는 숫자로 가라앉고, 그 밖의 거의 모든 것으로 흔들린다는 것을.

en: Your name?
I am called Gyebek.
What? A man named turtle?

lines: 아닙니다. 계(階)는 섬돌이고 백(伯)은 맏이입니다.
en: No. Gye is the stone step, and baek is the eldest.
…It was a joke.
…Ah.

blocks.html: He says ah the way another man would say I will write that down. It would be a mistake to read the pause as slowness; somewhere behind those eyes, a ledger has just gained a line.
blocks.ko: 그는 아라고 말한다. 다른 사람이 적어 두겠습니다라고 말할 때의 그 말투로. 그 뜸을 둔함으로 읽으면 곤란하다. 저 눈 뒤 어딘가에서, 장부에 방금 한 줄이 늘었다.

blocks.label: The telling
blocks.html: A man who cannot hear a joke will hear an order perfectly. Be careful what you give him.
blocks.ko: 농담을 못 듣는 사람은 명령을 완벽하게 듣는다. 그에게 무엇을 주든 조심하라.

blocks.html: Euija completes his mourning period — and discovers that Gyebek has been exiled. Not by his hand. By the clans. By Minister Satek reading a sealed order while the king was barred from countermanding it.
blocks.ko: 의자는 상을 마치고 — 계백이 유배된 사실을 알게 된다. 제 손이 아니다. 가문들의 손이다. 임금이 뒤집을 수 없을 때 옥새 명을 읽던 사택지적의 손이다.

en: Who.
Who used my seal —
Who took my man —
Your Majesty… the Assembly—
In mourning the council—

lines: 내가 아주 그냥! 개소문처럼 확~~~ 엎어버려야지!!
내 사람을 배에 실어? 내 상을 틈으로 쓰고?
en: Minister Satek!
I swear I’ll just— overturn the whole lot of them like Gesomun did!!
You put my man on a boat? You used my mourning as a gap?

blocks.html: There is nothing theatrical in the fury. It is the sound a king makes on learning that three years of rite turned him into a stamp — and that the stamp signed away the one soldier who never asked him for a clan chair.
blocks.ko: 그 분노에 연극 같은 구석은 없다. 삼 년의 예법이 저를 도장으로 만들어 버렸다는 것을 — 그리고 그 도장이, 가문 자리 한 번 청한 적 없는 유일한 군인을 내보내 버렸다는 것을 알게 된 임금이 내는 소리다.

blocks.label: Black Rock
blocks.ko: 검은 돌

blocks.html: He trains at the same hour on the same slab of lava on the eastern shore, and when the tide takes that slab he waits for the tide rather than use another one.
blocks.ko: 동쪽 갯가의 같은 현무암 너럭바위에서, 같은 시각에 훈련한다. 물이 그 바위를 덮으면 다른 바위를 쓰지 않고 물이 빠지기를 기다린다.

en: The next rock is the same.
It is not the same.

blocks.html: The rock is porous and cruel and nothing like a drill ground. You cannot plant a foot on it twice in the same place. Two seasons of it and he no longer needs to know where his feet are.
blocks.ko: 그 바위는 구멍이 많고 모질며, 훈련장과는 조금도 같지 않다. 같은 자리에 두 번 발을 디딜 수 없다. 두 철을 그러고 나자, 그는 제 발이 어디 있는지 알 필요가 없어진다.

lines: 숨은 참는 게 아니라, 노래로 미는 거라.
en: You don’t hold the breath. You push it out with singing.
…I cannot sing.

lines: 못 하는 사람이 어딨노. 안 하는 사람만 있제.
en: Nobody cannot. There are only people who don’t.

blocks.html: The village children learn the count of his drills before they learn his name, and stand on the rocks doing it badly behind him, and he does not once turn round to stop them, because stopping would be an interruption and he does not interrupt.
blocks.ko: 마을 아이들은 그의 이름보다 그의 훈련 횟수를 먼저 익힌다. 바위에 서서 뒤에서 서툴게 따라 하는데, 그는 한 번도 돌아서서 말리지 않는다. 멈추는 것은 중단이고, 그는 중단하지 않는다.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: A man who cannot vary anything will be unbeatable on the ground he chose, and helpless on any other. Give him the choosing.
blocks.ko: 아무것도 바꾸지 못하는 사람은 제가 고른 땅에서는 무적이고 다른 땅에서는 속수무책이다. 그에게 고르게 하라.

blocks.label: Five Thousand
blocks.ko: 오천

blocks.html: He is asked, once, why he counts everything, and he answers honestly, which is the only way he has ever answered anything.
blocks.ko: 어째서 모든 것을 세느냐는 물음을 한 번 받는다. 그는 정직하게 답한다. 그가 무엇에든 답해 온 유일한 방식으로.

en: Numbers do not lie to me.
And people do?

lines: 사람은 속이려는 게 아니라, / 제가 못 알아듣습니다. / 얼굴을 읽는 법을 모릅니다.
en: People are not trying to. / I simply do not follow them. / I have never learned to read a face.

lines: 그럼 이십 년을 조정에서 어떻게 살았노.
en: Then how did you survive twenty years at a court?
I trusted one man.

blocks.html: The island considers this the saddest sentence anybody has said on it, and nobody explains to him why they have all gone quiet, and he does not ask, because he has not noticed.
blocks.ko: 섬은 그것을 여태 이 섬에서 나온 가장 슬픈 문장으로 여긴다. 아무도 그에게 왜들 조용해졌는지 설명해 주지 않고, 그는 묻지 않는다. 알아차리지 못했기 때문이다.

en: (Tamla fisher, laughing)
Hundred-Victories, they call him on the mainland — and here he counts oranges like they might desert.
lines: 본토에선 백승이라 부르지 — 여기선 귤이 도망갈까 봐 세고 있어.

blocks.html: He drills in units of five hundred. Four years from now he will take ten of those units to a field and leave the rest behind. The count is already in his mouth.
blocks.ko: 그는 오백을 한 단위로 훈련한다. 사 년 뒤 그는 그것 열 개를 벌판으로 데려가고 나머지는 남겨 둘 것이다. 숫자는 이미 입에 있다.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: Give a literal man one person to trust and you have not given him a friend. You have given him a hinge.
blocks.ko: 곧이곧대로인 사람에게 믿을 사람 하나를 주는 것은 벗을 준 것이 아니다. 돌쩌귀를 준 것이다.

blocks.html: First night on the island. A fire, two cups, and a storyteller who never asks permission. “Sit or don’t. Once there were two suns…”
blocks.ko: 섬의 첫날 밤. 불 하나, 잔 둘, 그리고 허락 따윈 구하지 않는 이야기꾼. “앉든 말든. 옛날에 해가 둘이었지…”

images.at: There’s nobody under heaven who can touch me.

Low angle: Sumyung Jangja, the smug rich man of the attached portrait (long grey beard, half-lidded contemptuous eyes, white robe, gold cord sash), standing with his chin up and arms folded in front of the tall timber door of his ninth storehouse, sure that nothing under heaven can touch him; above him the noon sky is a huge black ink mass swallowing the sun, a single bare-paper disc going dark; his kicking horse and his dog are tiny cowering ink shapes under the porch. Topknots, no brimmed hats. FULL-BLEED, no paper margin. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. blocks.html: Told on the first night, before he has agreed to listen to anything. Yuri Dora has a fire going, two cups, and no plan to ask permission.
blocks.ko: 첫날 밤, 그가 무엇이든 듣겠다고 하기도 전에 들려진 이야기. 유리도라에게는 피워 둔 불과 잔 두 개가 있고, 허락을 구할 생각은 없다.

en: I’ll start at the beginning.
Sit or don’t.

blocks.html: Gyebek stays standing by the door. Yuri Dora starts anyway.
blocks.ko: 계백은 문가에 선 채로 있다. 유리도라는 그냥 시작한다.

blocks.html: Heaven’s laying-out, set in order. Earth’s laying-out, set in order. Man’s laying-out too. The mountains’, the waters’, the kingdom’s, the king’s. And the gods take their seats at the altar.
blocks.ko: 하늘의 배포가 서고 땅의 배포가 선다. 사람의 배포도 선다. 산의 배포, 물의 배포, 나라의 배포, 임금의 배포. 이제 제청에 신들이 자리 잡는다.
blocks.source: Chogamje (초감제), Bepo-doeop-chim, recited by Gang Sun-seon (강순선), recorded by Heo Nam-chun, Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2009 — Tapdong Yeongdeung-gut, Jeju City (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: 천앙베포 도업 지왕베포, 도업입네다 인앙베포도 도업, 산베포는 물베포, 국베포 왕베포, 제청신도업이웨다∼.

blocks.html: In the beginning there were two suns and two moons. By day people dropped in the fields with their hoes still in their hands; by night they froze in their own doorways. Nobody ever had a decent night’s sleep or a decent harvest, and the old died faster than anyone could bury them.
blocks.ko: 처음에 해는 둘, 달도 둘이었다. 낮에는 사람들이 호미를 쥔 채 밭고랑에 쓰러졌고, 밤에는 제 집 문간에서 얼어 죽었다. 누구도 제대로 자 본 적이 없고 제대로 거둬 본 적도 없었으며, 늙은이들은 묻어 줄 손보다 빨리 죽어 나갔다.

blocks.html: Above all of it sat Heaven–Earth King, who ran the living and the dead out of one office and therefore never went home. One night he fell asleep at the desk anyway, and dreamed he was eating: one sun, one moon, swallowed whole, one of each.
blocks.ko: 그 모든 것 위에 천지왕이 있었다. 산 자와 죽은 자를 한 관청에서 다스렸으니 집에 갈 일이 없었다. 어느 밤 그는 기어이 책상에서 잠이 들었고, 꿈에서 무언가를 먹었다. 해 하나, 달 하나, 통째로, 하나씩.

blocks.caption: The god with two jobs and one desk. He dreams about breakfast.
blocks.ko: 일 두 개에 책상 하나인 신. 꿈에서 아침을 먹는다.

lines: 하하— 아들이다. 저걸 쏘아 떨굴 놈.
en: ……Huh.
One each.
I ate one of each.
Ha— that’s a son. Someone’s going to shoot those down.

blocks.html: He comes down to the world to find the mother of that dream, and finds her in the poorest house on the road: a girl the village calls the Lady of Wisdom, a hearth with no fire in it, and a rice jar she does not open in front of guests.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 꿈의 어미를 찾으러 세상에 내려왔고, 길가에서 가장 가난한 집에서 그를 찾았다. 총명아기라는 처녀, 불 없는 아궁이, 손님 앞에서는 열지 않는 쌀독.

en: Who are you.
Someone passing.
A hungry one.
……Sit, then.

blocks.html: She goes round the back and lifts the lid of the jar. The bottom of it looks up at her. She puts the lid back as if that might help, ties up her hair, and walks across the road.
blocks.ko: 그는 뒤꼍으로 돌아가 쌀독 뚜껑을 연다. 독 바닥이 그를 올려다본다. 그러면 나아지기라도 할 것처럼 뚜껑을 도로 덮고, 머리를 묶고, 길 건너로 간다.

blocks.html: Across the road lives Sumyung Jangja, who is rich the way a flood is wet. He has nine storehouses, a horse that kicks beggars, a dog that bites whatever the horse misses, and a rice measure that comes out a little smaller when he lends and a little larger when he collects.
blocks.ko: 길 건너에는 수명장자가 산다. 홍수가 젖은 것처럼 부자인 사내다. 곳간이 아홉, 거지를 걷어차는 말 한 마리, 말이 놓친 것을 무는 개 한 마리, 그리고 꿔 줄 때는 조금 작아지고 받을 때는 조금 커지는 됫박이 하나 있다.

en: Lend me one measure of rice.
I have a guest.

lines: 손님? 네 집에 올 손님이면 뻔하지.
en: One measure.
Two when you pay it back.
A guest? Anyone who’d come to your house, I can guess.
Two, then.

blocks.html: He fills the measure himself, with his back to her.
blocks.ko: 그는 등을 돌린 채, 제 손으로 됫박을 채운다.

blocks.html: She washes it nine times at the well and spends the last of her firewood on it. The king takes the first spoonful. Something in his mouth grinds.
blocks.ko: 그는 우물가에서 아홉 번을 씻고, 남은 장작을 다 때서 밥을 짓는다. 왕이 첫 숟가락을 뜬다. 입안에서 무언가 서걱거린다.

lines: 이 집 쌀은 씹는 맛이 있네.
en: Your rice has a bit of bite to it.
……It’s sand.
I washed it nine times.
Who gave it to you.
The house across the road.
I said I’d pay back two.

lines: 모래 섞은 한 되에, 두 되.
……먹어. 다 먹어. 나 잠깐 나갔다 올게.
en: Two.
One measure with sand in it, for two.
……Eat. Eat all of it. I’m stepping out for a minute.

blocks.html: Sumyung Jangja is counting his storehouses, which is how he prays, when the sky over the ninth one goes black at noon. The horse will not kick. The dog gets under the porch.
blocks.ko: 수명장자는 곳간을 세고 있다. 그것이 그의 기도다. 그때 아홉째 곳간 위 하늘이 한낮에 까맣게 내려앉는다. 말은 차지 않는다. 개는 마루 밑으로 기어든다.

lines: 하늘 아래 나 건드릴 놈은 없다.
en: Who’s there.
There’s nobody under heaven who can touch me.
That’s why I came from above.

lines: 쌀이오? 쌀이면— 두 되, 아니, 열 되, 곳간째로—
en: ……W-what is it you want.
Rice? If it’s rice— two measures, no, ten, the whole storehouse—
Without the sand?

blocks.html: The floor of the ninth storehouse opens. The richest man in the world goes down through it, past the dirt and past the dark, into the place under everything where the measures are honest. He is the first one there. He will not be lonely for long.
blocks.ko: 아홉째 곳간 바닥이 열린다. 세상에서 가장 부자인 사내가 그리로 떨어진다. 흙을 지나고 어둠을 지나, 모든 것의 밑, 됫박이 정직한 곳으로. 그가 처음 도착한 자다. 오래 외롭지는 않을 것이다.

blocks.html: He goes back across the road. He stays until the day the calendar allows, and the morning after, he is already tying his sleeves.
blocks.ko: 그는 길을 건너 돌아온다. 날을 받은 그날까지 머물고, 그다음 날 아침에는 벌써 소매를 묶고 있다.

en: You’re going?
Lots of work upstairs.
There are two suns, remember.

lines: 아들 둘이다. 먼저 나온 놈은 대별, 나중 놈은 소별.
en: Two sons. The first one out is Daebyeol, the second one Sobyeol.
When they turn fifteen, have them plant these.

blocks.html: Two gourd seeds in her palm, and half of a wooden comb. The other half goes into his sleeve.
blocks.ko: 그의 손바닥에 박씨 두 알, 그리고 얼레빗 반쪽. 나머지 반쪽은 왕의 소매 속으로 들어간다.

en: ……Fifteen years.
Thanks for the rice.

blocks.html: She has twins. The elder comes out quiet and looks at everything. The younger comes out already complaining. They grow up under two suns and two moons, and get asked whose sons they are in every yard in the village.
blocks.ko: 그는 쌍둥이를 낳는다. 형은 조용히 나와 모든 것을 둘러보고, 아우는 나오면서부터 투덜댄다. 둘은 해 둘, 달 둘 아래서 자라고, 마을 마당마다 누구네 아들이냐는 소리를 듣는다.

blocks.caption: Big Star, the elder twin. He would rather be right than first.
blocks.ko: 대별, 맏이. 먼저인 쪽보다 옳은 쪽을 고른다.

blocks.caption: Little Star, the younger twin. He would rather be first.
blocks.ko: 소별, 동생. 먼저인 쪽을 고른다.

en: Mom. Who’s our father.
The other kids are at it again.
Leave it. Mom’s tired.
……When you’re fifteen.

blocks.html: At fifteen she puts the seeds in their hands and the half comb in the elder’s. They plant them by the wall at dusk. By morning the vine has gone past the roof, past the clouds, and out of sight.
blocks.ko: 열다섯이 되자 그는 두 아들 손에 박씨를 쥐여 주고, 형의 손에는 빗 반쪽을 쥐여 준다. 둘은 해 질 녘 담 밑에 씨를 심는다. 아침이 되자 넝쿨은 지붕을 넘고 구름을 넘어 보이지 않는 데까지 올라가 있다.

en: Climb.
All the way up.
What about you?

lines: 난 여기 있어. 밥 해 놓을게.
en: I’ll be here. I’ll have rice on.

blocks.html: Sobyeol gets to the top first and pretends he wasn’t racing. The man at the top of the vine holds out his hand without getting up.
blocks.ko: 소별이 먼저 꼭대기에 닿고는 내기한 적 없는 척한다. 넝쿨 끝에 있던 사내는 일어나지도 않고 손을 내민다.

en: The comb.

blocks.html: Daebyeol puts the half in his palm. The king takes the other half out of his sleeve, where it has been for fifteen years, and fits them. The teeth close.
blocks.ko: 대별이 반쪽을 그 손바닥에 올린다. 왕은 열다섯 해 동안 소매 속에 있던 나머지 반쪽을 꺼내 맞춘다. 빗살이 맞물린다.

en: ……Fits.
You never came down. Not once.
……There were two suns.

blocks.html: He has a thousand geun of iron melted down into two bows and two arrows, heavy enough that nobody but a son of his could draw them, and walks the boys to the edge of the sky.
blocks.ko: 그는 무쇠 천 근을 녹여 활 둘과 살 둘을 만들게 한다. 그의 아들이 아니면 아무도 당기지 못할 무게다. 그리고 두 아들을 하늘 끝까지 데리고 간다.

lines: 열다섯 해 동안 네 엄마 지붕 위에 둘씩 떴다.
en: Two suns, two moons.
Two of each over your mother’s roof for fifteen years.
One each.

blocks.html: Daebyeol takes the sun at noon. He breathes out once and lets go, and the second sun breaks like a plate. Its pieces scatter east and stay there as stars. At midnight Sobyeol draws on the second moon and hits it square, and its pieces go west.
blocks.ko: 대별은 한낮에 해를 맡는다. 숨을 한 번 내쉬고 놓자, 두 번째 해가 접시처럼 깨진다. 그 조각들은 동쪽으로 흩어져 별로 남는다. 한밤중에 소별이 두 번째 달을 겨누어 정통으로 맞히고, 그 조각들은 서쪽으로 흩어진다.

en: Brother. Got it in one.
You saw?
I saw.

blocks.html: In the morning people go out to the fields and do not fall down. That night they sleep. Nobody thanks anyone, because nobody knows who to thank.
blocks.ko: 아침에 사람들은 밭에 나가서도 쓰러지지 않는다. 그날 밤에는 잠을 잔다. 아무도 누구에게 고맙다고 하지 않는다. 누구에게 해야 할지 아무도 모르니까.

lines: 산 쪽이랑 죽은 쪽. 누가 어디 갈지는 둘이 정해.
나는 안 정한다. 내가 정하면 꼭 나중에 따지더라.
en: Done. The world’s yours.
The living side and the dead side. You two decide who takes which.
I’m not deciding. Whoever I pick always comes back to argue.
I’m resting.

blocks.html: They decide it the way brothers decide things. Daebyeol proposes riddles, which suits the one who knows the answers.
blocks.ko: 둘은 형제들이 일을 정하는 식으로 정한다. 대별이 수수께끼를 내자고 한다. 답을 아는 쪽에게 어울리는 방법이다.

lines: 어떤 나무는 평생 잎이 안 지고, 어떤 나무는 잎이 지느냐.
en: Which trees keep their leaves all their lives, and which ones drop them?

lines: 속이 꽉 찬 나무는 안 지고, 속 빈 나무는 지지.
en: Solid ones keep them. Hollow ones drop them.

lines: 청대랑 갈대는 마디마디 비었어도 잎이 안 진다.
en: Poor little brother, don’t talk about what you don’t know.
Bamboo and reeds are hollow at every joint, and they keep their leaves.
……Another.

lines: 어째서 동산 풀은 짧고, 구렁 풀은 기냐.
en: Why is the grass short on the hill and long down in the hollow?

lines: 봄비 오면 동산 흙이 구렁으로 쓸려 내려가니까.
en: Spring rain washes the hill’s dirt down into the hollow.

lines: 그럼 사람 머리털은 왜 길고, 발등 털은 짧으냐.
en: Then why is the hair on your head long and the hair on your feet short?
That one’s cheating.

blocks.html: Two for two. Their father, who said he would not decide anything, leans over the edge of his rest and drops two flower seeds between them.
blocks.ko: 둘에 둘. 아무것도 정하지 않겠다던 아버지가 쉬던 자리에서 몸을 기울여, 둘 사이에 꽃씨 두 알을 떨어뜨린다.

en: Flowers.
Whoever grows the better one gets the living side.
……That’s me done interfering.

blocks.html: They plant them in two silver basins and sit up with them. Daebyeol’s flower comes up green and keeps coming, and by the third evening it has opened. Sobyeol’s comes up yellow and leans.
blocks.ko: 둘은 은동이 두 개에 씨를 심고 곁을 지킨다. 대별의 꽃은 푸르게 올라와 멈추지 않고, 사흘째 저녁에는 활짝 핀다. 소별의 꽃은 누렇게 올라와 기운다.

en: Let’s sleep, Brother.
We’ll look in the morning. See whose did better.
All right.

blocks.html: Daebyeol sleeps the way honest men sleep, all the way down. Sobyeol lies on his side and counts his brother’s breathing up to a hundred. Then he gets up, trades the basins, and lies down again in the same shape, so his brother will wake first.
blocks.ko: 대별은 정직한 사람이 자듯 잔다. 바닥까지. 소별은 모로 누워 형의 숨을 백까지 센다. 그러고는 일어나 은동이를 바꿔 놓고, 똑같은 모양으로 다시 눕는다. 형이 먼저 깨도록.

en: ……Brother! Wake up!
Look, it’s mine!

blocks.html: Daebyeol looks at the open flower in front of his brother, the one he watered for three days. He looks at the yellow one by his own hand.
blocks.ko: 대별은 아우 앞의 활짝 핀 꽃을 본다. 사흘 동안 제가 물을 준 꽃이다. 그리고 제 손 옆의 누런 꽃을 본다.

en: Yes. Your flower did well.

blocks.html: He gets up and brushes the soil off his knees.
blocks.ko: 그는 일어나 무릎의 흙을 턴다.

lines: 아우야, 이승에는 수많은 사람들이 산다. 그중에는 도둑놈도 있으며 사기꾼도 있지. 그들을 잘 다스리려면 힘과 슬기도 필요하지만 무엇보다도 참된 마음이 있어야 한다. 그러니 그들을 다스려서 아름답고 평화로운 세상을 만들기 바란다.
en: Brother, countless people live in the mortal world. Among them are thieves and swindlers. To govern them well you need strength and wisdom — but above all, a true heart. So govern them, and make a beautiful, peaceful world.

blocks.html: He is already walking toward the dark edge when he says the rest, and he does not turn round.
blocks.ko: 나머지 말은 이미 어두운 끝 쪽으로 걸어가면서 한다. 돌아보지는 않는다.

lines: 그런데 아우야. 훔친 꽃으로 받은 세상이다.
이승엔 살인이 많고, 역적이 많고, 도둑이 많고, 남의 계집 남의 사내 넘보는 일이 많을 거다.
en: But, little brother. You took it with a stolen flower.
The living world will have plenty of murder, plenty of treason, plenty of thieves, and plenty of people reaching for other people’s wives and husbands.
The law down below will run clear.
……Brother!
Brother, that’s—

blocks.html: Big Star goes down. Little Star keeps the warm side.
blocks.ko: 대별왕은 내려간다. 소별왕은 따뜻한 쪽을 갖는다.

blocks.html: It goes the way his brother said, and worse, because Sobyeol had never thought about the parts he didn’t want. The trees still talk. So do the birds, the cattle and the stones, mostly about him. When a mother calls her son’s name at dusk a ghost answers too, and the living and the dead walk the same roads in the same clothes, and nobody can tell which is which.
blocks.ko: 형이 말한 대로 된다. 더 나쁘게. 소별은 갖고 싶지 않은 쪽은 생각해 본 적이 없었으니까. 나무가 아직 말을 한다. 새도, 소도, 돌도 말을 한다. 대개 그의 이야기다. 해 질 녘 어미가 아들 이름을 부르면 귀신도 대답을 하고, 산 자와 죽은 자가 같은 옷을 입고 같은 길을 걸어, 누가 누군지 아무도 모른다.

lines: 나무가 말을 하오. 귀신이 대답을 하오. 누가 사람이고 누가 귀신인지 모르겠소.
en: Brother.
Brother, help me, just this once.
The trees talk. The ghosts answer. I can’t tell who’s a man and who’s a ghost.

blocks.html: Big Star comes up. He scatters five measures of pine-bark powder over the world, and the trees and the birds and the cattle go quiet and have stayed quiet since. Then he hangs a scale from the sky.
blocks.ko: 대별왕이 올라온다. 송피 가루 닷 말을 세상에 뿌리자 나무와 새와 짐승이 입을 다물고, 그 뒤로 다시는 말하지 않는다. 그러고는 하늘에 저울을 건다.

en: Line up.
A hundred geun or more, you stay up here.
Less, you come with me.
……And the thieves? The ones who kill people?
Those are your flower.

blocks.html: He goes back down with the light ones following him in a long quiet line. Since then the dead weigh less than the living, the law below runs clear, and the law up here belongs to Little Star. Under Big Star, Yumla judges, and the measures are honest.
blocks.ko: 그는 가벼운 자들을 긴 침묵의 줄로 거느리고 다시 내려간다. 그 뒤로 죽은 자는 산 자보다 가볍고, 아래의 법은 맑고, 위의 법은 소별왕의 것이다. 대별왕 아래서는 염라가 판결하고, 됫박이 정직하다.

blocks.html: The fire has gone low. Gyebek sat down at some point and does not remember when.
blocks.ko: 불이 사위었다. 계백은 언젠가 앉았는데, 언제였는지 기억하지 못한다.

en: ……Did the brother know. That the flowers were switched.
He knew.
And he gave it up anyway.

lines: 밑이 저승, 여기가 이승. 서쪽 끝에 꽃밭이 하나 더 있고, 그 위로 환인 어른이 계시다.
다 합쳐 삼계라 한다. 오늘 밤은 둘만 알면 된다.
en: He did. And he went down.
Down there is the dead world, up here the living. There’s a flower field out at the western end, and above all of it, old Lord Hwanin.
Three Realms, all told. Tonight you only need the two.
……Rice with sand in it.
Hm?
Nothing.

blocks.html: It is the first story on the island he does not inspect.
blocks.ko: 섬에서 들은 이야기 중, 그가 검사하지 않은 첫 번째 이야기다.

blocks.label: The telling
blocks.html: The world was not given to the better brother. Stop waiting for it to behave as if it was.
blocks.ko: 세상은 더 나은 형제에게 주어지지 않았다. 그런 척 굴기를 기대하지 마라.

blocks.html: The next night he hides on a roof. She tells it anyway. One woman made this island, and she was enormous…!
blocks.ko: 다음 날 그는 지붕 위로 숨는다. 그래도 이야기는 올라온다. 이 섬은 한 여자가 만들었다. 어마어마하게 큰 여자가…!

Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. images.alt: Seolmundae rises from the mountain, birds overhead
Birds over the crater

blocks.html: The next story is told to him on a roof, because he is on a roof, mending it, and Yuri Dora has decided that a man who will not sit down can still listen.
blocks.ko: 다음 이야기는 지붕 위에서 들려진다. 그가 지붕 위에서 그것을 고치고 있기 때문이고, 유리도라는 앉지 않으려는 사내도 듣기는 한다고 판단했기 때문이다.

lines: 이 섬은 여자 하나가 만들었다. 설문대할망.
en: One woman made this island. Sulmun.

blocks.html: Before the island there is a woman, and she is enormous. Sulmun, the Great Lady. The sea comes to her knee. She scoops the seabed up in her apron and piles it in one place until it stands high enough to lean on, and that is Mount Halla.
blocks.ko: 섬보다 먼저 한 여자가 있었고, 그 여자는 어마어마했다. 설문대할망. 바다가 무릎에 찼다. 치마폭으로 바다 밑을 퍼 올려 한자리에 쌓아 기대설 만큼 높아진 것, 그것이 한라산이다.

blocks.caption: Grandmother Sulmun. The sea comes to her knee, and she has opinions about the view.
blocks.ko: 설문대할망. 바다가 무릎까지밖에 안 오고, 경치에 대해 할 말이 많다.

blocks.html: The island’s spine, and a giantess’s favourite chair.
blocks.ko: 섬의 등뼈이자, 거인 할망이 즐겨 앉던 의자.

en: Was there a hole in the apron.
…How did you know that?

lines: 오름이 삼백육십여덟 개라 하셨습니다. / 한 번에 부었으면 하나여야 합니다.
en: You said there are three hundred and sixty-eight hills. / If it were poured in one place there would be one.

blocks.html: Yuri Dora looks at him for a while.
blocks.ko: 유리도라가 한참 그를 본다.

lines: 너는 이야기를 듣는 게 아니라 검사를 하는구나.
en: You do not listen to a story. You inspect it.
…Yes.

blocks.html: She had five hundred sons. In a famine she set a cauldron of porridge to boil for them, and slipped, and did not come out. The sons ate. It was the best they had ever tasted, and they said so, and then the youngest reached the bottom and found his mother’s bones.
blocks.ko: 그에게는 오백 명의 아들이 있었다. 흉년에 아들들을 먹이려 큰 솥에 죽을 끓이다가 미끄러져 빠졌고, 나오지 못했다. 아들들은 먹었다. 평생 먹어 본 중 가장 맛있었고, 그렇게들 말했고, 그러다 막내가 솥 바닥에서 어머니의 뼈를 건졌다.

blocks.html: The youngest walked into the sea and would not turn round, and stands there yet as a single rock off the shore. The other four hundred and ninety-nine went up the mountain and wept until they were stone. You can go and count them. Nobody has ever got the same number twice.
blocks.ko: 막내는 바다로 걸어 들어가 끝내 돌아보지 않았고, 지금도 바닷가에 홀로 선 바위로 서 있다. 나머지 사백구십아홉은 산으로 올라가 돌이 될 때까지 울었다. 가서 세어 보아도 좋다. 두 번 같은 수를 센 사람은 아직 없다.

blocks.html: Five hundred shrines before that mountain, five hundred temples before this one. Five hundred generals, five hundred teachers. One valley short, so it is an island that could raise no king, no tiger, no bear.
blocks.ko: 저 산 앞에는 당이 오백, 이 산 앞에는 절이 오백. 오백 장군에 오백 선생. 골짜기 하나가 모자라서, 왕도 범도 곰도 나지 못한 섬이다.
blocks.source: Chogamje (초감제), Nalgwa-guk-seomgim, recited by Gang Sun-seon (강순선), recorded by Heo Nam-chun, Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2009 — Tapdong Yeongdeung-gut, Jeju City (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: 저 산 압은 당 오벽, 이 산 압은 절 오벽, 오벽장군은 오벽선성, ᄒᆞᆫ 골이 부족허난, 왕도 범도 곰도, 못 내든 섬입네다.

blocks.html: She asked the islanders for one thing: clothes her size, a hundred rolls of silk, and she would lay a bridge to the mainland. They found ninety-nine. The collar was never finished. Neither was the bridge.
blocks.ko: 할망이 섬사람에게 청한 것은 하나였다. 제 몸에 맞는 옷 한 벌, 명주 백 동. 그러면 뭍까지 다리를 놓아 주겠다고. 사람들은 아흔아홉 동을 모았다. 옷깃을 끝내 짓지 못했고, 다리도 끝내 놓이지 않았다.

blocks.html: Well, she said if they made her a petticoat out of a hundred rolls of silk, she’d lay them a bridge as far as Chuja. They came up one roll short and couldn’t make it, so she never built it.
blocks.ko: 뭐, 비단 백 필로 속곳 하나 지어 주면 추자도까지 다리를 놓아 주마고 했다더라. 모으다 보니 한 필이 모자라 못 지어 주니, 다리를 안 놓아 줘 버렸다고.
blocks.source: Sulmun Halmang legend (설문대할망) told by An Yong-in (안용인), recorded by Hyeon Yong-jun and Kim Yeong-don, 1979 — Gimnyeong, Gujwa-myeon (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye 9-1)
blocks.native: 거 뭐, 비단 백필만 허영 소중기 맨들어 주민 추ᄌᆞ도ᄁᆞ지 ᄃᆞ리 놔 주멘 허였다고. 주문ᄒᆞ단 ᄒᆞᆫ 필이 부족하여서 못허여 주니 걸 아이 허여 줘 부렀다고.

en: They were one roll short.
They were.
…That is the worst amount to be short by.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: The bridge was not lost to the sea. It was lost to the last one per cent.
blocks.ko: 다리를 앗아 간 것은 바다가 아니었다. 마지막 백분의 일이었다.

blocks.html: Three princes climb out of the ground. “Not from an egg,” the island insists. Then a box drifts in from the sea…!
blocks.ko: 땅에서 왕자 셋이 솟아난다. “알에서 나온 게 아이다,” 섬은 힘주어 말한다. 그리고 바다에서 궤짝 하나가 떠밀려 온다…!

Sunset on Tamla’s black lava-rock shore, surf foaming, the great volcano of the island rising behind in cloud. Low angle from the rocks. One low orange sun (#ff9a3d) on the horizon edges his face, the orange and the pony’s white mane; the rocks and sea are ink-black and slate. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — YURI DORA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yuri_dora.png (face only; invent a new pose). #ff9a3d as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | GWAHAMA (과하마, yuridora's Jeju pony, guardian of Tamla) — attached board /obj_jeju_horse.png: SMALL sturdy WHITE Jeju pony, barely chest-high to a man — short strong legs, round barrel, thick neck, short head, big dark eyes, full thick white mane and tail; plain rope halter, no saddle — match the board. The horse small enough to ride under the fruit trees: an orange branch can clear its ears. Cheeky and unbothered. Steals oranges from the basket, follows Yuri Dora around the island like a dog, and refuses to hurry for anyone. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.
