HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: This is the story of the kingdom of Tamla.
blocks.ko: 이것은 탐라국의 이야기다.

blocks.title: Three Princes · 삼성혈
blocks.caption: Three divine princes rise from Samseonghyeol and divide the orange island.
blocks.ko: 삼성혈에서 세 신인이 나와 탐라를 나눈다.

blocks.html: Long after the Great Lady’s stone sons, three divine princes named Yang, Go and Bu climb out of a hole in the ground.
blocks.ko: 할망의 돌 아들들이 생기고 한참 뒤, 양·고·부라는 세 신인이 땅속 구멍에서 기어 나온다.

blocks.caption: Prince Go. Climbed out of the earth already arguing about who climbed first.
blocks.ko: 고을나. 땅에서 나오자마자 누가 먼저 나왔는지 따지기 시작했다.

blocks.caption: Prince Yang. He hunts, he shoots, and he would like a wife, please.
blocks.ko: 양을나. 사냥하고, 활 쏘고, 아내가 있었으면 좋겠다.

blocks.caption: Prince Bu. The quiet one, who looks out to sea first.
blocks.ko: 부을나. 조용한 쪽. 바다를 제일 먼저 내다본다.

lines: 이 섬은 그 점을 힘주어 말한다.
en: Not from an egg.
This island says that with feeling.
We divide the land. By arrow.
Shorter than talk. Good.
I aim east.

blocks.html: They each shoot an arrow and rule over each piece of the island.
blocks.ko: 세 신인은 저마다 화살을 쏘아, 섬을 셋으로 나누어 다스린다.

blocks.html: One day a box drifts from the East Sea — a messenger and three princesses inside.
blocks.ko: 어느 날 동쪽 바다에서 궤짝이 떠내려온다 — 사자 하나와 세 공주.

en: Marriage. Debate later.

blocks.html: They marry the three princesses at a pond. The box holds calves, foals, and the five grains — which is how Tamla learns to farm, and how Tamla learns that anything worth having tends to arrive by sea in a container.
blocks.ko: 세 신인은 못가에서 세 공주와 혼인한다. 궤짝에는 송아지와 망아지와 오곡이 들어 있다 — 그렇게 탐라는 농사를 배우고, 가질 만한 것은 대개 바다에서 궤짝에 담겨 온다는 것도 배운다.

blocks.html: In the beginning there were no people. Three divine men rose up out of the ground. … One day they saw a wooden chest sealed with purple clay drift ashore on the eastern beach. They opened it, and inside was a stone chest. … They opened the stone chest, and out came three maidens in blue, with foals, calves and the seeds of the five grains.
blocks.ko: 태초에 사람이 없었는데, 세 신인이 땅에서 솟아났다. … 하루는 자줏빛 진흙으로 봉한 나무 상자가 동쪽 바닷가에 떠밀려 오는 것을 보고 나아가 열었더니, 상자 안에 또 돌 상자가 있었다. … 돌 상자를 여니 푸른 옷의 처녀 셋과 망아지, 송아지, 다섯 곡식의 씨가 나왔다.
blocks.hanja: 太初無人物, 三神人, 從地聳出 … 一日見紫泥封藏木函, 浮至于東海濱, 就而開之, 函內又有石函 … 開石函, 出現靑衣處女三, 及諸駒犢五穀種.
blocks.source: Goryeosa (高麗史) bk. 57, Treatise on Geography — Tamla County (耽羅縣), quoting the island’s old record

blocks.html: At the Three Clans’ Hole: Go’s king at the hour of the rat, Yang’s king at the hour of the ox, Bu’s king at the hour of the tiger. An island founded by three clans.
blocks.ko: 고·양·부 삼성혈은, 자시에 고씨 왕, 축시에 양씨 왕, 인시에 부씨 왕. 세 성이 나라를 세운 섬이다.
blocks.source: Chogamje (초감제), Nalgwa-guk-seomgim, recited by Gang Sun-seon (강순선), recorded by Heo Nam-chun, Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2009 — Tapdong Yeongdeung-gut, Jeju City (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: 고량부 삼성혈은, 자시에 고이왕 축시엔, 양이왕 인시엔 부게왕 삼성친, 도업헌 섬입네다.

blocks.html: Ever since, the island has sent Baekje oranges and, when asked, men.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤로 섬은 백제에 귤을 보내고, 부르면 사람도 보낸다.

blocks.html: Ordinary Tamla does not play the mainland’s endless status games. A diver offers Gyebek grilled fish before she asks which Baekje office ruined him. A boy corrects his orange-peeling and laughs when he fails. Kindness here is not strategy. That, more than the stories, is what keeps him five years.
blocks.ko: 탐라의 보통 사람들은 육지의 끝없는 신분 놀이를 하지 않는다. 해녀는 백제의 어느 관직이 그를 망쳤는지 묻기 전에 구운 생선을 건넨다. 아이가 오렌지 까는 법을 고쳐 주고, 실패하면 웃는다. 여기 친절은 전략이 아니다. 이야기보다 그게 그를 오 년 붙든다.

en: Eat.
You look like a man who was promoted by being useful and punished for the same crime. That joke is how Little Star runs the living world.
lines: 쓸모 있어서 출세했다가 같은 죄로 벌받은 사람 얼굴이네. 소별왕 이승이 원래 그런 장난으로 굴러가지.

en: …That is an exact sentence.
We have those. We just don’t put them on banners.
lines: 우리도 있지. 깃발에만 안 쓸 뿐.

blocks.label: Baekjuto and Socheon-guk
blocks.ko: 백주또와 소천국

blocks.html: Told while he is stacking oranges badly, which Yuri Dora treats as invitation.
blocks.ko: 오렌지를 서툴게 쌓는 동안 들려진 이야기. 유리도라는 그걸 초대로 본다.

lines: 사냥의 신 소천국이 농사의 신 백주또와 혼인했다. / 백주또가 밭을 갈라고 소를 줬는데—
en: The hunting god married the farming goddess. / She gave him an ox to plough with—
He ate it.
…Have you heard this one?
No. But he is a hunter.

lines: 밭 갈라고 준 소를 먹었어? 통째로?
en: You ate the ox. The one I gave you to plough with. The whole ox?
…I also ate someone else’s.

blocks.html: They separated. It is the first divorce in the record, the grounds are livestock, and the islanders tell it as a comedy because it is one.
blocks.ko: 둘은 갈라섰다. 기록에 남은 첫 이혼이고 사유는 가축이며, 섬사람들은 우스개로 들려주는데 실제로 우습다.

blocks.html: Their son kicked his father in the chest at three years old. So they put the boy in an iron chest, locked it, and set it on the water.
blocks.ko: 그 아들이 세 살에 아비의 가슴을 걷어찼다. 그래서 사람들은 아이를 무쇠 궤에 넣고 자물쇠를 채워 물에 띄웠다.

blocks.html: It drifted for years and washed up in a foreign country, and the boy came out of it a warrior, and won that country’s wars, and married its princess. And then he came home.
blocks.ko: 궤는 여러 해를 떠돌다 낯선 나라에 닿았고, 아이는 그 안에서 장수가 되어 나와 그 나라의 전쟁을 이기고 그 나라의 공주와 혼인했다. 그리고 돌아왔다.

en: …Tell that part again.
Which part.
The part where he comes home.

lines: 돌아와서 지 땅의 신이 됐다. / 쫓아낸 사람들이 절하는 신이.
en: He came home and became the god of his own land. / The god the ones who threw him out have to bow to.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: The sea does not decide what a man is. It only decides how long he waits to be it.
blocks.ko: 바다는 사람이 무엇인지 정하지 않는다. 다만 그것이 되기까지 얼마나 기다릴지를 정할 뿐이다.

blocks.html: “Tomorrow’s isn’t a kind one, Turtle.” A serpent in a cave. A woman from the rock. A man who looks back…!
blocks.ko: “내일 건 순한 얘기가 아이다, 거북아.” 동굴 속의 뱀. 바위에서 나온 여자. 그리고 뒤를 돌아본 사내…!

en: Today’s is not a kind one.
That is acceptable.

blocks.html: There is Kangrim — but the island does not tell his full story until last. For now it is enough to know he comes for you, and that a crow once ruined his schedule.
blocks.ko: 강림이 있다 — 그러나 섬은 그의 전부를 마지막에야 말한다. 지금은, 그가 당신을 데리러 온다는 것과 까마귀가 한때 그의 일정을 망쳤다는 것만으로 충분하다.

en: …Would it be better to know.
For you it would.

blocks.html: There is the serpent in the cave at Gimnyeong that took a girl a year until a young magistrate went in and killed it, and was told on the way out not to look back, and looked back.
blocks.ko: 해마다 처녀를 하나씩 데려가던 김녕굴의 뱀이 있다. 젊은 판관이 들어가 그것을 죽였고, 나오는 길에 돌아보지 말라는 말을 들었고, 돌아보았다.

en: Why did he look back.
To check that he had won.

blocks.html: “Oh, sir, it’s raining blood.” He said it out loud. And the magistrate dropped dead right there. Just like that. He’d told him not to say a word.
blocks.ko: “아이고, 판관님, 피로 비가 옵니다.” 하고 말해 버렸다. 그 자리에서 그냥 즉사해 버렸다. 아무 말도 하지 말라고 했던 건데.
blocks.source: Gimnyeong Sagul legend (김녕사굴) told by An Yong-in (안용인), recorded by Hyeon Yong-jun and Kim Yeong-don, 1979 — Gimnyeong, Gujwa-myeon (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye 9-1)
blocks.native: “아이, 판관님, 피로 비가 옵니다.” 허여가지고 말해. 거기서 직ᄉᆞ허여 불었어. 그냥. 아뭇 이야기도 ᄒᆞ지 말라고 ᄒᆞᆫ 건디.

blocks.html: There is Sanbangduk, who came down out of the rock to love a poor man.
blocks.ko: 가난한 사내를 사랑하여 바위에서 내려온 산방덕이 있다.

lines: 바위에서 나왔는데… / 당신 손만 잡으면 돌이 아닌 것 같아요.
en: I came out of the rock… / and when I hold your hand I don’t feel like stone.

lines: 그럼 놓지 마시오. / 관리가 뭐라고 하든.
en: Then don’t let go. / Whatever the official says.

blocks.html: They don’t let go — until the official has the husband killed to take her. She walks back into the cliff. The spring inside it has not stopped since.
blocks.ko: 놓지 않는다 — 관리가 남편을 죽여 그를 뺏기 전까지. 그는 절벽 속으로 돌아간다. 그 안의 샘물은 그 뒤로 마른 적이 없다.

lines: 관리가 그를 원했습니다. 세상이 틀린 쪽을 원했습니다.
en: The official wanted her. The world wanted the wrong thing.
So she went back into the rock.
…Sometimes the rock looks cleaner.
Cleaner is not the same as finished.
Stone stays. It does not ride.

lines: 이 섬 이야기는 다 슬프게 끝납니까.
en: Do all the stories on this island end badly.

lines: 아이다. 다 돌로 끝난다. / 슬픈 거하고는 다르다. 돌은 남는 거 아이가.
en: No. They all end as stone. / That’s not the same as badly. Stone stays.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: Do not turn round to confirm the victory. The looking is what collects the price.
blocks.ko: 이겼는지 확인하려 돌아보지 마라. 값을 거두어 가는 것은 바로 그 돌아봄이다.

blocks.label: Gameunjang
blocks.ko: 가믄장아기

blocks.html: Told at a well, while he is fixing the rope.
blocks.ko: 두레박 줄을 고치는 동안, 우물가에서 들려진 이야기.

lines: 부잣집에 딸이 셋 있었다. 아비가 누구 덕에 사느냐고 물었지.
en: A rich man had three daughters. He asked them whose luck they lived on.

lines: 위의 둘은 아버지 덕이라 했고, 막내는 제 배꼽줄 덕이라 했다. / 그래서 쫓겨났다.
en: The elder two said his. The youngest said her own navel-string. / So she was thrown out.

blocks.html: “By whose grace did you come into the world?” “First, heaven’s. Second, earth’s. Third, Father’s. Fourth, Mother’s — but really, the line drawn under Mother’s navel.”
blocks.ko: “너는 누구 덕으로 태어났느냐?” “첫째는 하늘님 덕이요, 둘째는 땅님 덕이요, 셋째는 아버님 덕이요, 넷째는 어머님 덕입니다마는, 어머님 배꼽 아래 그어진 금 덕입니다.”
blocks.source: Samgong Bonpuri (삼공본풀이) recited by Jeong Tae-jin (정태진), recorded by Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2011 — Sanggari, Aewol-eup (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: “너는 누구 덕으로 나왓느냐?” “첫쩨는 하나님이 덕이요, 둘쩨는 지화님이 덕이요, 셋쩨는 아바님이 덕이요, 넷쩨는 어머님 덕입니다만은 어머님 벳똥 알 선그믓이 덕입니다.”

en: If she had lied she could have stayed.
…Yes. She could have.

blocks.html: She walked until she found three brothers digging yams and married the youngest, the only one who greeted her. In the spoil he had been throwing away as stones, she found gold.
blocks.ko: 그는 마를 캐는 삼 형제를 만날 때까지 걸었고, 자기에게 인사한 유일한 사람인 막내와 혼인했다. 그가 돌이라며 내던지던 흙 속에서 금을 찾아냈다.

blocks.html: Her parents lost everything and went blind. Years later she held a beggars’ feast that lasted three days, and served two old blind beggars herself, and said her name, and their eyes opened.
blocks.ko: 부모는 모든 것을 잃고 눈이 멀었다. 여러 해 뒤 그는 사흘 동안 거지 잔치를 열어, 눈먼 늙은 거지 둘에게 손수 상을 올리고 제 이름을 말했다. 두 사람의 눈이 뜨였다.

en: …So the child they threw away was the luck.

lines: 아이다. 복은 원래 지 것이었다. / 버린 쪽이 눈이 먼 거고.
en: No. The luck was always hers. / It was the ones who threw her out who went blind.

blocks.html: He does not answer that one. He finishes the rope, and tests it eleven times.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 말에는 답하지 않는다. 줄을 마저 고치고, 열한 번을 당겨 본다.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: Cast out what carries your fortune and you will not see it go. That is what blindness is for.
blocks.ko: 제 복을 지닌 것을 내치면, 그것이 떠나는 것을 보지 못한다. 눈이 머는 까닭이 그것이다.

blocks.html: Heaven sends for a man to keep its flower field. He leaves his pregnant wife to wait. He forgets to say how long…!
blocks.ko: 하늘이 제 꽃밭을 맡길 사내를 부른다. 그는 아이 밴 아내를 남겨 두고 떠난다. 얼마나 기다리라는 말은 하지 않는다…!

blocks.html: Told in the orange grove, in the hour after the picking, when Gyebek has finally been persuaded to sit on a basket.
blocks.ko: 귤밭에서, 따기가 끝난 뒤 한 시간, 귤 바구니에 앉으라는 설득에 그가 마침내 넘어갔을 때 들려진 이야기.

lines: 사라도령이란 사내가 있었지. 하늘이 서쪽 꽃밭을 지키라고 그를 불렀어.
아내는 배가 불러 있었고, 하늘이 바라는 만큼 빨리 걷지를 못했지. 그래서 사내는 어느 부잣집에 아내를 맡겨 두고 갔단다.
en: There was a man called Sara Doryeong. Heaven sent for him to keep its flower field in the west.
His wife was carrying. She couldn’t walk as fast as heaven wanted, so he left her at a rich man’s house to wait.
How long was she to wait.

lines: 그게 첫 번째 잘못이야. 세고 싶으면 세렴.
en: He didn’t say.
That’s the first mistake. Count it if you like.

blocks.html: The rich man wanted her. Wonganghami said no, and went on saying no for fifteen years, through every kind of work a rich man can find for a servant who says no. Her son was born in that house and grew up a servant in it. His name was Hallakgungi.
blocks.ko: 부자는 그녀를 원했다. 원강아미는 싫다 했고, 열다섯 해 동안 계속 싫다 했다. 싫다는 종에게 부자가 찾아낼 수 있는 온갖 일을 다 겪으면서. 그 집에서 태어난 아들은 그 집 종으로 자랐다. 그 이름이 할락궁이다.

blocks.caption: Hallakgungi. Born a servant, and he means to find his father.
blocks.ko: 할락궁이. 종으로 태어났고, 아버지를 찾아갈 작정이다.

lines: 아이가 클 만큼 크자 그녀는 아비가 어디 있는지 일러 줬어. 아이는 그날 밤 서쪽으로 떠났고.
부자는 아이가 없어진 걸 알고, 대신 어미를 죽여 대숲에 던졌지.
en: When he was old enough she told him where his father was. He went west that night.
And the rich man, when he found the boy gone, killed the mother instead and threw her into a bamboo grove.
…She knew he would.
She knew.
She told him anyway.

blocks.html: Hallakgungi found the flower field at the far end of the west, where the living maps run out, and his father at the gate of it. Sara Doryeong took him down the rows. Here, the flowers that put back bone, and flesh, and blood, and breath, and the soul last of all. Over there, the flowers that laugh a man to death, and the ones that make a house fight itself, and at the end of the row the one that ends a line altogether.
blocks.ko: 할락궁이는 산 사람의 지도가 끝나는 서쪽 맨 끝에서 꽃밭을 찾았고, 그 문간에서 아버지를 찾았다. 사라도령은 그를 데리고 꽃밭 고랑을 걸었다. 여기는 뼈를, 살을, 피를, 숨을, 맨 마지막으로 넋을 되살리는 꽃. 저쪽은 사람을 웃다 죽게 하는 꽃, 한 집안이 저희끼리 싸우게 하는 꽃, 고랑 맨 끝에는 한 핏줄을 아주 끊어 버리는 꽃.

en: Which did he take.

lines: 그 부잣집으로 돌아가서 작은 잔치를 열었지. 웃음꽃, 싸움꽃, 그리고 마지막 꽃. 그다음 대숲에 가서 어머니 뼈를 찾아, 순서대로 맞췄어. 뼈, 살, 피, 숨, 넋.
en: Both rows.

He went back to that rich man’s house and held a little party. Laughing flower, fighting flower, and the last one. Then he went to the bamboo grove and found his mother’s bones, and put her back together in order. Bone, flesh, blood, breath, soul.

blocks.html: “And this flower, what flower is it?” “This one is the flower that makes you laugh. This one is the flower that makes you fight. And this one, well — this is the flower that wipes out a line.”
blocks.ko: “이 꽃은 무슨 꽃입니까?” “이 꽃은 웃음 웃게 하는 꽃이다. 이 꽃은 싸움하게 하는 꽃이다. 이 꽃은, 그래, 씨를 멸족시키는 꽃이다.”
blocks.source: Igong Bonpuri (이공본풀이) recited by Lee Seung-sun (이승순), recorded by Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2011 — Sanggari, Aewol-eup (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: “요 고 꼿은 무신 꼿입니까?” “요 꼿은 웃음 웃일 꼿이여. 요 꼿은 싸움헐 꼿이여. 요 꼿은 야 이거, 씨멜족 시길 꼿이여.”

en: In order.
…Good.

blocks.html: Afterwards the son took the flower field over from his father and keeps it still. The island calls him the Gardener when it does not want to say his name, which is most of the time. The flowers that bring you back and the flowers that end you grow in the same rows, and he is the only one who knows which is which in the dark.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤로 아들이 아버지에게서 꽃밭을 물려받아 지금도 지킨다. 섬은 그 이름을 입에 올리기 싫을 때 그를 꽃감관이라 부르는데, 대개 그렇다. 되살리는 꽃과 끝장내는 꽃이 같은 고랑에서 자라고, 어둠 속에서 어느 게 어느 것인지 아는 이는 그 하나뿐이다.

en: Did the father go home with them.

lines: 아니. 아들이 그 문을 맡을 만해질 때까지 지켰지.
…거북아, 넌 맞는 질문을 꼭 엉뚱한 데서 하더라.
en: No. He kept the gate till the boy was ready for it.
…You ask the right questions in the wrong places, Turtle.

blocks.html: The flower that brings back and the flower that ends grow in the same row. Learn which is which before you need them.
blocks.ko: 되살리는 꽃과 끝내는 꽃은 같은 고랑에서 자란다. 필요해지기 전에 어느 게 어느 것인지 익혀 두어라.

blocks.label: Jacheongbi
blocks.ko: 자청비

blocks.html: Told in the rain, in a doorway, which is the only time anyone gets him to stand still.
blocks.ko: 비 오는 날 문간에서 들려진 이야기. 그를 가만히 세워 둘 수 있는 유일한 때다.

lines: 자청비는 하늘에서 온 도령을 따라 글을 배우고 싶었다. / 여자는 그 방에 못 들어가니, 머리를 자르고 남자 옷을 입었지.
en: Jacheongbi wanted to study beside a boy from the sky. / Women were not allowed in the room, so she cut her hair and put on a man’s clothes.

blocks.caption: Jacheongbi. Disguise, scholarship, and not one ounce of patience.
blocks.ko: 자청비. 변장, 학문, 그리고 인내심은 한 톨도 없음.

en: Did she break the rule.

lines: 아이다. 규칙에 여자가 남자 옷을 입으면 안 된다는 말은 없었거든.
en: No. The rule never said a woman could not wear a man’s clothes.
…Ah.

blocks.html: That one he likes. That one he asks to hear twice.
blocks.ko: 그 대목은 그의 마음에 든다. 그 대목은 두 번 들려 달라 청한다.

blocks.html: Three years at the same desk. She beat him at everything and let him believe it was close. On the last night at the parting stream she washed upstream of him and told him to look.
blocks.ko: 한 책상에서 삼 년. 그는 도령을 모든 것에서 이기고도 아슬아슬했다고 믿게 두었다. 헤어지던 마지막 밤 냇가에서, 그는 도령보다 위쪽에서 몸을 씻으며 보라고 말했다.

lines: 삼 년을 같은 상에서 먹고 자고 글을 읽었는데, 이제야 아느냐?
en: Three years at the same table — eating, sleeping, reading — and you notice now?
…I had no eyes.

lines: 이제 있으니까. / …보고만 있을 거예요? / 삼 년을 참았는데.
en: You have them now. / …Will you only look? / After three years of holding back.

lines: 참은 게 아니오. / 몰랐소. / 이제 알고 나니… 숨이 거칠어지오.
en: I was not holding back. / I did not know. / Now that I do… my breath is rough.

lines: 그럼 거친 채로. / 내 머리를 만져 봐요. / 짧게 잘랐던 그 머리.
en: Then stay rough. / Touch my hair. / The hair I cut short for you.

blocks.html: They killed him for it. Heaven does not care for that sort of marriage. So she walked west — past every gate — into the Western Flower Field.
blocks.ko: 사람들은 그 일로 도령을 죽였다. 하늘은 그런 혼인을 좋아하지 않는다. 그래서 그는 서쪽으로 걸었다 — 있는 문이란 문을 지나 — 서천꽃밭으로.

blocks.html: Every flower here does something. Ask before you pick.
blocks.ko: 여기 꽃은 다 하는 일이 있다. 꺾기 전에 물어보라.

en: Father retired.
This gate answers to Hallakgungi now.
What are you looking for.
The resurrection flower.
The one that puts bones back together.

lines: 다섯 — 뼈, 살, 피, 숨, 넋.
잘못된 순서로 꺾으면 산 것도 시든다.
en: Don’t touch the stem wrong.
Five — bone, flesh, blood, breath, soul.
Pick them out of order and even the living wilt.
I’ll pick them in order.

blocks.html: She took what she needed, put Mun Doryeong back together bone by bone, and brought the five grains down to Tamla.
blocks.ko: 그는 필요한 것을 가져가, 문도령을 뼈 하나하나로 되살리고, 오곡을 탐라로 내려왔다.

en: …Can the dead be fetched back.
In stories.
…I see.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: The rule is smaller than you think, and the door is usually in the wording. Read it again.
blocks.ko: 규칙은 생각보다 작고, 문은 대개 문구 안에 있다. 다시 읽어라.

blocks.html: The island keeps one story for last. It is about the one who comes for you, and the crow that lost his book…!
blocks.ko: 섬은 이야기 하나를 맨 끝까지 아껴 둔다. 당신을 데리러 오는 자, 그리고 그의 책을 잃어버린 까마귀 이야기다…!

Reapers in Yumla’s court, painted as a scroll

blocks.html: The island keeps one story for last. After it, every ending on the mainland has a broken clock already running.
blocks.ko: 섬은 이야기 하나를 마지막까지 아껴 둔다. 그 뒤로 육지의 모든 결말에는, 이미 고장난 시계가 돌아가고 있다.

en: Now the last one.
Kangrim.
Heaven did not send him.

blocks.html: A magistrate named Kimchi had a murder he could not try. Three brothers were killed for their silk and sunk in a pond. They came back as three flowers on the water. Burned, they became three beads. A woman swallowed them and bore three sons. The sons came home from the exams and died in one bow. Their mother would not stop writing petitions. So Kimchi sent his strongest man, Kangrim, to bring King Yumla up and close the case.
blocks.ko: 김치 원님에게는 산 자의 법으로 못 닫는 살인이 있었다. 형제 셋이 비단 때문에 죽어 연못에 가라앉았다. 셋은 물 위의 꽃 셋으로 돌아왔다. 태우니 구슬 셋이 되었다. 한 여인이 그걸 삼키고 아들 셋을 낳았다. 아들들은 과거 보고 돌아와 절하다 한꺼번에 죽었다. 어미는 소지를 멈추지 않았다. 그래서 원님은 제일 센 사내 강림을 보내, 염라대왕을 끌어올려 사건을 닫게 했다.

lines: …산 자를 시켜, 죽은 자의 판관을 잡으러 보냈다는 말입니까.
en: …He sent a living man to arrest the judge of the dead.
He did.

blocks.html: His wife kept the gate-god and the kitchen-god fed, so they put him on the road. At the last pond he shut his eyes and jumped, and stood up at the underworld gate. Someone was already walking that road with a red book. Haewonmek, the oldest fetch there is. Kangrim asked the way. Haewonmek pointed, and kept walking. Kangrim waited, and addressed King Yumla with court courtesy.
blocks.ko: 아내가 문신과 조왕을 잘 먹인 덕에, 신들이 그를 길에 올려 주었다. 마지막 연못에서 그는 눈을 감고 뛰어들었고, 저승문 앞에 서 있었다. 그 길엔 이미 붉은 책을 든 이가 걷고 있었다. 해원맥. 세상에서 제일 오래된 차사다. 강림이 길을 물었다. 해원맥은 손으로 가리키고, 계속 걸었다. 강림은 기다렸다가 염라대왕을 조정의 예로 불렀다.

lines: 사건이 하나 있습니다. 산 자의 법으로는 못 닫습니다.
en: Your Majesty. The living court requests you.
There is a case. Living law cannot close it.

blocks.caption: The judge of the dead. Every ledger in the dark ends on his desk.
blocks.ko: 죽은 자의 재판관. 어둠 속 모든 장부는 그의 책상에서 끝난다.

en: Go home.
I will come at the hour I name.

blocks.html: He came. The pond dried. The bones came up. The three brothers went home to their parents. The couple who had killed them did not. Yumla keeps the sentence. Then he turned to the magistrate and asked to borrow the man who had fetched him.
blocks.ko: 그가 왔다. 연못이 말랐다. 뼈가 드러났다. 형제 셋은 부모에게 돌아갔다. 그들을 죽인 부부는 돌아가지 못했다. 염라가 판결을 지킨다. 그런 다음 그는 원님에게, 자기를 데려온 그 사내를 빌려 달라고 했다.

lines: 그 사내를 빌려 다오. 심부름이 남았다.
en: Lend me that man. I still have errands.

lines: 원님은 거절했다. 혼 같은 건 믿지도 않았으니까.
그래서 둘로 갈랐다. 원님은 몸을 가졌다. 염라는 혼을 가지고 갔다.
en: The magistrate refused. He did not believe in a soul.
So they split him. The magistrate kept the body. Yumla took the soul.

blocks.html: That is how Kangrim died upstairs and woke as a chasa. The living official kept the half he could see. Death kept the other half.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 강림은 이승에서 죽고 차사로 깨어났다. 산 자의 관리는 눈에 보이는 쪽을 가졌고, 죽음은 나머지 쪽을 가졌다.

en: …They divided a man.
They both wanted him.

blocks.html: Yumla then put in his hands a ledger that told each living person their hour — eighty, and in order, the old before the young. On the way down Kangrim trusted it to a crow. The crow set the book on a wall to eat at a slaughter-field. A snake swallowed the writing. Caught, the crow cried a new rule so the blame would not sit on one bird: parents after children, children after parents. Since then the hour does not come in a just order.
blocks.ko: 염라는 그 손에 명부를 쥐여 주었다. 산 사람마다 죽을 시각을 적은 장부 — 여든에, 차례대로, 늙은이가 젊은이보다 먼저. 내려오는 길에 강림은 그것을 까마귀에게 맡겼다. 까마귀는 푸줏간 밭에서 먹으려고 책을 담 위에 내려놓았다. 구렁이가 글씨를 삼켰다. 들킨 까마귀는 죄가 새 한 마리에게 남지 않도록 새 규칙을 울었다. 부모는 자식 뒤에, 자식은 부모 뒤에. 그 뒤로 죽을 시각은 옳은 순서로 오지 않는다.

blocks.html: “Give me the red writ. When it’s the old one’s turn, let the child come. When it’s the child’s turn, let the old one come. I’ll bring them back like water running uphill, out of order.”
blocks.ko: “적배지를 나한테 주십시오. 어른 올 때 아이 오고, 아이 올 때 어른 오게 하여, 거꾸로 흐르는 물처럼 순서를 뒤집어 데려오겠습니다.”
blocks.source: Chasa Bonpuri (차사본풀이) recited by Go Yeon-ok (고연옥), recorded by Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2011 — Sanggari, Aewol-eup; sung as Cheseo Bonpuri (체서본풀이) (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: “적베질 나 줍서. 어룬 올떼 아이 옵서. 아이 올 떼 어룬 옵서. 건물에 건ᄃᆞ리 헤영 오쿠다.”

blocks.html: One errand was left. A man called Dongbangsak had lived three thousand years and would not come. Kangrim sat in a stream washing charcoal. Dongbangsak stopped. He had never, in all that time, heard of washing charcoal white. Kangrim took him by the sleeve. Only then did Yumla seat him as the one who comes for everyone else. That is why he asks a question at the threshold. Not for the sentence — Yumla keeps the sentence. A scrambled list still deserves accurate last words.
blocks.ko: 심부름이 하나 남았다. 동방삭이라는 자가 삼천 년을 살고도 오려 하지 않았다. 강림은 냇가에 앉아 숯을 씻었다. 동방삭이 걸음을 멈췄다. 그 긴 세월에, 숯을 희게 씻는다는 말은 들은 적이 없었다. 강림이 소매를 잡았다. 그제야 염라는 그를, 나머지를 데리러 가는 자로 앉혔다. 그래서 그는 문턱에서 질문을 한다. 판결을 위해서가 아니다. 뒤섞인 명부에도 정확한 마지막 말은 필요하니까.

lines: 명부가 뒤섞인 뒤로는, 내가 방에 들어서기 전엔 누구도 시각을 모른다.
en: I do not punish.
I collect — for His Majesty.
Since the list was scrambled, nobody knows the hour until I am already in the room.

lines: …그러면 신하가 임금보다 먼저 죽어도, 책은 그대로 열리겠군요.
en: …Then a man can die before his king, and the book still opens.

lines: 책은 길에서 틀어졌다. 걸음은 안 틀어졌다.
en: The book went wrong on the road. The walk did not.
That is the key.

blocks.label: The telling
blocks.html: The warrant said die in order. A crow lost it. You do not get a fair hour. You still get the door.
blocks.ko: 명부는 차례대로 죽으라 했다. 까마귀가 잃었다. 공평한 시각은 없다. 문은 여전히 있다.

blocks.html: Why does an orange island take Baekje’s exiles at all? Because once, long ago, it forgot to send the oranges…!
blocks.ko: 귤 섬은 왜 백제의 유배객을 받아 주는가? 아주 오래전, 귤 보내는 걸 한 번 잊었기 때문이다…!

images.alt: Tamla tribute ships heavy with oranges cross calm water toward Baekje, Mount Halla behind
images.prompt: Historical manhwa: small Tamla tribute ships riding calm morning water toward the Baekje coast, decks stacked with baskets of bright oranges, Mount Halla receding behind them — a peaceable, sunlit crossing. Match Halla ref. No text, --ar 3:2

images.alt: Three bright oranges against ocean blue - Tamla's precious tribute
images.prompt: Iconic minimal: Three bright orange tangerines arranged in a perfect triangle against vast Tamla ocean blue negative space

blocks.html: Tamla stops sending tribute. Rebellion would at least have been legible; this is closer to forgetting, which a large kingdom finds harder to forgive.
blocks.ko: 탐라가 조공을 끊는다. 반란이었다면 차라리 읽어 낼 수는 있었을 것이다. 이것은 잊어버림에 가깝고, 큰 나라에게는 그쪽이 더 용서하기 어렵다.

blocks.html: Baekje’s king marches an army to the southern harbour and stops. He lets the news cross the water on its own. It gets there faster than he would have.
blocks.ko: 백제 임금이 군사를 이끌고 남쪽 포구까지 가서 멈춘다. 소문이 제 발로 바다를 건너게 둔다. 소문이 그보다 빨리 닿는다.

blocks.html: Eighth month. Because Tamla had not sent its tribute, the king went out to punish it himself and got as far as Mujin Province. Tamla heard, sent envoys to beg pardon, and he stopped.
blocks.ko: 8월, 왕이 탐라가 공물과 부세를 바치지 않는다 하여 몸소 치러 나서 무진주에 이르렀다. 탐라가 이를 듣고 사신을 보내 죄를 비니, 그만두었다.
blocks.hanja: 八月，王以耽羅不修貢賦，親征，至武珍州。耽羅聞之，遣使乞罪，乃止。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 26, Baekje Annals — King Dongseong, yr. 20 (498), eighth month

blocks.html: Tamla apologises. Baekje accepts. Nobody is killed, everybody is satisfied, and the oranges resume. For a hundred and fifty years, that is the whole relationship.
blocks.ko: 탐라가 사죄한다. 백제가 받아들인다. 죽은 이는 없고 모두가 만족하며, 귤이 다시 온다. 이후 백오십 년 동안 두 나라 사이는 그것이다.

blocks.html: So when Baekje needs somewhere to put a man it cannot kill, there is an island, and the island owes it a favour.
blocks.ko: 그러니 백제가 죽일 수 없는 사람을 어딘가에 두어야 할 때, 섬이 하나 있고, 그 섬은 신세를 지고 있다.

blocks.html: Meanwhile, in Sabi, Euija calls the Assembly. He has a smile, a speech, and a proclamation printed before anyone sat down…!
blocks.ko: 그 무렵 사비. 의자가 회의를 소집한다. 미소 하나, 연설 하나, 그리고 다들 앉기도 전에 찍어 둔 포고문 한 장…!

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night in the Satek clan hall at Sabi: a low lacquered table, ONE oil lamp on it. Minister Satek at the head, scarred face lit from below, leaning forward on his fists; three older Satek lords leaning in along the sides. Every man wears the tall gilt-bronze noble crown, gold catching the lamp; their shadows climb the plaster wall behind. Low angle from the end of the table. Device: the table as a dark wedge toward the lamp. CANON — MINISTER SATEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_satek_minister.png (face only; invent a new pose). Crown: the great-clan gilt crown (see NOBLE CROWN), no jougwan. #c2a24a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | NOBLE CROWN: Baekje great-clan lord’s gilt-bronze crown (금동관), as the attached crown (ignore its museum stand and black backdrop): a tall pointed gilt cap shaped like a peaked hood, pierced all over with openwork dragon-and-flame scrolls, a broad engraved band across the brow, a curved openwork crest arching over the top, two small cup-shaped finials on thin stems rising at the back, a pointed bud finial at the crown, and a flat openwork leaf-plume at the front. Worn high over the topknot on court and assembly days; burnished gold-bronze catching the key light. It replaces the jougwan. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. Same staging: a dense, stiff, frontal group portrait on the steps of a government building at night, the ringleader dead centre in the front row grinning wide, the co-conspirators packed shoulder to shoulder in rising rows, smug, some clapping, one flash-lit. Here: KING EUIJA (attached portrait: face and garments) sits front and centre, laughing, amber #e08a2e lamplight on his face; around and behind him FORTY-ONE of his sons, young men and boys in new Baekje court robes and black hats, in five packed rows on the stone steps of the attached Sabi palace hall (red pillars, giwa eaves). At the edge, a row of empty lacquered Assembly chairs pushed aside. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. Euija on the throne, grinning in a shaft of light

blocks.html: He calls the assembly the way a gambler calls a final hand — smiling, sleeves perfect, already knowing which tiles he slipped into the set.
blocks.ko: 그는 마지막 패를 부르는 노름꾼처럼 어전회의를 소집한다 — 웃고, 소매는 반듯하고, 패 속에 자기가 섞어 둔 패가 무엇인지 이미 아는 얼굴로.

blocks.html: Euija calls a session of the Ministers’ Assembly at Deer Rock. The rock is dry. Someone forgot the brine, or remembered it and chose not to.
blocks.ko: 의자가 정사암에서 회의를 소집한다. 바위는 말라 있다. 소금물을 잊었거나, 기억하고도 바르지 않았다.

en: Beloved people.
As Eraha, I appeal to you with a heart that spits blood.

lines: 우리 백성의 자유와 행복을 약탈하는 파렴치한 친당 반국가세력을 일거에 척결하며,
en: To protect Baekje from the threat of Silla,
to eradicate in one stroke the shameless pro-Tang anti-state forces that plunder our people’s freedom and happiness,
and to safeguard the free order of this country —
I hereby declare emergency martial law.

lines: 이 비상계엄으로, 나라의 나락으로 떨어지는 백제를 재건하고 지키겠소.
이를 위해 지금까지 상습적으로 악행을 저질러 온 망국의 주범, 반국가세력을 반드시 뿌리 뽑겠소.
en: Through this emergency martial law, I will rebuild and protect Baekje, which is falling into the abyss of national ruin.
To that end I will absolutely eradicate the anti-state forces — the main culprits of national ruin — who have habitually engaged in heinous acts up till now.

lines: 이는 체제를 뒤엎으려는 반국가세력의 선동으로부터 백성의 자유와 안전, 나라의 지속을 보장하고,
후대에 제대로 된 나라를 물려주기 위한 불가피한 조치요.
반국가세력을 척결하고 가장 빠른 시일 안에 나라를 정상화하겠소.
en: This is an inevitable measure to guarantee the people’s freedom and safety, and the continuity of the nation, against anti-state forces that bid to overthrow the system —
so that we may pass on a proper country to future generations.
I will eradicate the anti-state forces and normalize the nation in the shortest possible time.

lines: 계엄 선포로 인해, 이 나라의 법도를 믿고 따라 온 선량한 백성에게 다소의 불편이 있을 수 있소.
그러나 그 불편은 최소화하는 데 힘을 쏟겠소.
이 조치는 백제 영속을 위한 불가피한 것이며,
왜 · 당을 포함한 이웃과의 외교 자세에는 변함이 없소.
en: Due to this declaration, there may be some inconveniences for the good people who have believed in and followed the lawful order of this country.
We will strive to minimize such inconveniences.
This measure is inevitable for the perpetuity of Baekje,
and there is no change in our foreign stance toward Wa, Tang, or any neighbour.

lines: 나는 오직 백성만을 믿고, 백제를 지키는 데 몸과 목숨을 바치겠소.
en: As Eraha, I earnestly appeal to the people.
I place my trust solely in you, and I will devote body and life to protecting Baekje.
Please trust me.

blocks.html: He has a script ready: dissolve the Assembly, seat his own blood, call the pause a rescue. The clans stare. He expected applause. The room stays quiet.
blocks.ko: 대본을 준비해 두었다. 거추장스러운 회의를 해산하고, 자기 피를 앉히고, 멈춤을 구원이라 부른다. 씨족들이 쳐다본다. 그는 박수를 기다린다. 방은 조용하다.

lines: 회의 전에 포고문을 찍어 두셨네. 먹 냄새 나요.
en: King Onjo preserve us — he’s lost his mind…
Also he printed the proclamation before the session. I can smell the ink.
The characters for “in one stroke” are still wet.

lines: 임시란 — 영구라고 말하기 두려울 때 영구가 시작되는 방식이지.
en: This is temporary.
Temporary is how permanent things begin when you are afraid to say permanent.

blocks.html: Then he unrolls a second scroll — shorter, denser, the kind of law that fits on one sheet because the power is in what it erases. The clerks name it before he does: the Law to Remedy the Distress of the People and the Country.
blocks.ko: 이어 두 번째 두루마리를 펼친다 — 더 짧고, 더 빽빽하고, 지우는 것에 힘이 있어서 한 장으로 충분한 법. 서리들이 그보다 먼저 이름을 붙인다. 백성과 나라의 곤경을 덜기 위한 법.

lines: 어라하가 명을 내려 법을 세울 수 있다.
옛 법도와 어긋나더라도 — 회의 그 자체를 없애지 않는 한 — 허용된다.
en: In addition to the procedure prescribed by the Assembly,
laws of Baekje may also be enacted by the Eraha’s command.
Such laws may deviate from the old custom — insofar as the Assembly as such is not abolished.

lines: 이 권한은 긴요한 조치에 필요할 때에만 쓰겠소.
회의의 존립은 위태롭지 않소. 상좌평의 자리도 그대로요.
en: The throne will make use of this authorization only insofar as it is essential for carrying out vitally necessary measures.
The existence of the Assembly is not endangered. The Premier’s chair remains undisturbed.
The rights of the temples will not be curtailed.
Your Majesty. That is… a law for emptying the Assembly.
It keeps the name. It changes the people.

lines: 이제 여러분 스스로 고르시오. 평화인가, 전쟁인가.
en: If the name remains, the country remains.
If the people remain, the people eat the country.
May you now choose for yourselves — peace, or war.

blocks.html: Nobody chooses war out loud. Choosing peace means raising a sleeve for the scroll. The rock does not sweat. The sleeves go up anyway — some of them already paid, some of them already afraid, some of them already his sons waiting in the corridor.
blocks.ko: 아무도 큰 소리로 전쟁을 고르지 않는다. 평화를 고른다는 것은 두루마리에 소매를 드는 일이다. 바위는 땀을 흘리지 않는다. 그래도 소매는 올라간다 — 이미 삯을 받은 자, 이미 겁난 자, 이미 복도에서 기다리는 제 아들들.

blocks.html: Euija names forty-one of his own sons to the Assembly, firing every single existing member. Eight houses spent four generations sharpening tricks on each other. Marriages. Roads. Clerks planted in rival counting-rooms. In one morning the king clears the board. He simply changes the pieces. By noon nobody has an answer.
blocks.ko: 의자는 제 아들 마흔하나를 좌평에 앉히고, 기존 인사를 모조리 내친다. 여덟 가문은 네 대에 걸쳐 서로를 겨눈 수를 갈아 왔다. 혼인. 길. 상대 계산방에 심어 둔 서기. 왕은 하루아침에 판을 쓸어 버린다. 그냥 말을 바꿔 버린 것이다. 정오가 되어도 받아칠 말이 없다.

blocks.html: Seventeenth year, spring, first month. The king made forty-one of his sons by lesser wives ministers of the first rank, and gave each of them a fief.
blocks.ko: 17년 봄 정월, 왕의 서자 마흔한 명을 좌평으로 삼고 저마다 식읍을 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 十七年, 春正月, 拜王庶子四十一人爲佐平, 各賜食邑.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 17 (657), first month

blocks.title: Deer Rock, after · 정사암, 그 후
blocks.caption: The same benches. Every one of them a son.
blocks.ko: 같은 자리. 전부 아들이다.

blocks.html: Forty-one sons need forty-one seats. None goes to the Ye family. They have held Bear Fortress for four generations and never once been asked to court. Ye Sikjin reads the list at home, twice. Then he puts it in a drawer.
blocks.ko: 아들 마흔하나에게는 자리 마흔하나가 필요하다. 예씨 몫은 하나도 없다. 네 대째 웅진성을 지켜 왔건만 조정에 한 번도 불려 간 적 없는 집안이다. 예식진은 집에서 명단을 두 번 읽는다. 그리고 서랍에 넣는다.

blocks.html: Four generations of the Ye family, and not one invitation.
blocks.ko: 예씨 가문 사 대, 초대장은 한 장도 없었다.

blocks.html: Then he hands out the quiet money that really runs Baekje. Harbour warehouses. River pilot fees. The stamp a ship needs before it sails east. The martial law was the noise. The stamps are what change.
blocks.ko: 그다음 그는 백제를 실제로 굴리는 조용한 돈을 다시 나눈다. 바닷가 창고. 강의 도선료. 동쪽으로 떠나는 배에 찍는 도장. 계엄은 소음이었다. 바뀌는 건 도장이다.

blocks.html: He cannot do what Yeon did. Baekje would not forgive it, and more to the point, he would not. He does not need a banquet. He needs a majority that looks like kinship.
blocks.ko: 연개소문이 한 짓은 하지 못한다. 백제가 용서하지 않을 것이고, 더 중요한 건 — 그 자신도 하지 않을 것이다. 잔치는 필요 없다. 혈연처럼 보이는 다수가 필요할 뿐이다.

blocks.html: The clans try to rally — Satek calling in four generations of favors, the old Assembly men lining up behind them. But a face-off only works if you know your opponent’s style, and Euija has spent twenty years teaching them his. They line up for a duel. He has already changed who is sitting.
blocks.ko: 씨족들이 뭉치려 한다 — 사택이 네 대의 빚을 부르고, 옛 회의 사람들이 그 뒤로 선다. 그러나 맞대결은 상대의 길을 알 때만 성립하고, 의자는 이십 년 동안 그 길을 가르쳐 왔다. 그들은 결투 줄에 선다. 그는 이미 앉는 사람을 바꿔 두었다.

blocks.html: He’s recruited Satek Chunbok, one of the clan’s own young men, as his eyes inside their hall — the oldest technique in the book, turned on the house that wrote the book.
blocks.ko: 씨족의 젊은이 사택천복을 제 눈으로 심어 두었다 — 책에서 제일 오래된 수법으로, 그 책을 쓴 가문을 겨눈다.

blocks.html: He’s also recruited the other clans — the houses Satek had crowded out of the light, every one of them delighted to lend the king a blade for this particular duel.
blocks.ko: 다른 씨족도 끌어들였다 — 사택이 빛에서 밀어낸 집들. 저마다 이 결투만큼은 왕에게 칼을 빌려 주기를 기뻐한다.

en: You too! You’re a Satek lackey, aren’t you??!!

blocks.html: Satek Chunbok is named Premier. His own clan finds out with everyone else. The Enabling Law did not abolish the chair. It only changed who sits in it.
blocks.ko: 사택천복이 상좌평에 오른다. 제 집안도 남들과 같은 때에 안다. 수권법은 자리를 없애지 않았다. 앉는 사람만 바꿨을 뿐이다.

blocks.caption: A Satek in the Satek chair, sitting for the king.
blocks.ko: 사택의 자리에 앉은 사택. 왕을 위해 앉았다.

lines: 폐하. 오늘은 몇 분이나 자르셨습니까? / …저희는 몇이나 남기시려고요.
en: Your Majesty. How many did you dismiss today? / …And how many of us will you keep.
All of them. / You… I keep.

lines: …무서워라. / 그런데 어쩌죠. 그런 폐하가… 더 가깝게 느껴져요.
en: …How frightening. / And yet — that kind of Majesty… feels nearer.
…What was your name again.

lines: 아직 없습니다. / 오늘 밤에 하나 지어 주세요. / 계백 장군한테 하셨듯이 — 오래.
en: I don’t have one yet. / Make me one tonight. / As you did for General Gyebek — take your time.

blocks.html: Eleven of them by nightfall.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘에는 열하나가 된다.

en: So… Baekje? What of Baekje—
zhLatn: Nàme… Bǎijì? Bǎijì yòu rúhé——

en: Do not trouble yourself over Baekje.

lines: 백제 족속들은 가문 싸움을 좋아해서, 서로 시기하다가 망할 것입니다.
en: Baekje will fall on its own.
Where blood ties are strong, the state grows weak.
The Baekje clans love a family feud — they will envy each other into ruin.
Then why am I needed at all?
zhLatn: Nà zhèn yòu hébì cúnzài?

lines: 아무리 약해도, 한 번의 충격은 줘야죠.
당군이 쳐들어온다고 하면, 그 소문만으로도 나라의 기세가 기울어질 것입니다.
en: However weak it is, it still needs one shock.
Say the Tang army is coming — the rumour alone will tip the country’s spirit.

blocks.html: He beat eight houses in one morning. Now he can’t sleep. In his dreams, somebody keeps counting…?
blocks.ko: 하루아침에 여덟 가문을 꺾었다. 그런데 이제 잠이 오지 않는다. 꿈속에서 누군가 자꾸 수를 센다…?

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night in the dark Sabi throne hall, tenebrist: red columns sinking into black, one brazier, an empty floor. Low dutch angle from the floor. INTERACTION: King Euija sprawls sideways on the throne, crimson robe loose, yellow-gold headband askew, a wine jar hanging from two fingers; the tall white-gold stag Sinrok stands behind the throne, its antlers rising above his head like a second crown, and lowers its muzzle to nudge his cheek; he leans his head against its face without opening his eyes, a bitter little smile. The two of them alone in the huge hall. The stag is a solid painted animal — no glow, no luminous outline. The brazier is the one key (#e08a2e): it catches his face, the jar, the stag’s muzzle and the antler tips; everything else is umber-black. Brazier sparks as painted bokeh. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | SINROK (신록, guardian deer of Baekje, guide of onjo and biryu) — attached board /obj_sinrok.png: Pale white-gold stag with tall branching antlers — match the board's animal, but ignore its glow outline: light catches the antlers and coat as real light. Owned by no one; leads the brothers south and stays with Onjo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism.
