images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Dawn on a black basalt shore of Tamla, the orange island. Low wide two-shot. ONE device: the waterline, a hard horizontal of white surf against black volcanic rock; a small open boat waits at the right edge, oars shipped. Gyebek, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, in plain travel clothes, unarmed, on one knee on the wet black rock, bowing low with his fists pressed together, head down. Yuri Dora, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, orange robe and white sash, standing over him, one big hand gripping Gyebek's shoulder, laughing and wet-eyed at once. On the hill behind, tangerine trees and low black-stone thatched houses dissolve into sea mist. Key: a low dawn sun break over the sea, orange #ff9a3d specular on wet rock and silk; slate storm sky. Foreground: an out-of-focus mooring rope. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. Rides low and coiled, like he fights. #d9b13a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: curved blade, katana or tsuba (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); forward textbook grip once the fight starts; yellow metal cuirass; smiling in battle. | YURI DORA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yuri_dora.png (face only; invent a new pose). #ff9a3d as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Somewhere in the fourth year he notices he has stopped counting the days. It frightens him for a week. Then it does not.
blocks.ko: 넷째 해 어디쯤에서, 그는 날수 세기를 그만두었음을 알아차린다. 한 주 동안 그것이 그를 겁먹게 한다. 그 뒤로는 아니다.

blocks.html: He stops correcting the people who call him Turtle, and carries water for the women who dive. For the first and last time in his life, he is in a place where being exactly what he is costs him nothing.
blocks.ko: 거북이라 부르는 사람들을 더는 바로잡지 않고, 물질하는 여자들의 물을 날라 준다. 평생 처음이자 마지막으로, 그는 있는 그대로의 자신이 아무 값도 치르지 않는 곳에 있다.

blocks.html: A boat comes for him in the fifth year. He is on the shore before they finish tying it up.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 해에 배가 온다. 배를 다 매기도 전에 그는 이미 물가에 서 있다.

lines: 거북아. 왜 그리 급하노. / 여기서 죽으면 편할 낀데.
en: Turtle. What is the hurry. / You could die comfortable here.
Nothing here is mine to keep.
Then what is yours.
…A promise.

blocks.html: He takes nothing off the island except the stories, which is the only export it has ever had.
blocks.ko: 그는 섬에서 아무것도 가져가지 않는다. 이야기만 빼고. 이 섬이 여태 내놓은 유일한 수출품이다.

lines: 거북아. 하나만 배워 가라. / 이야기는 끝을 정해 놓고 시작하는 게 아이다.
en: Turtle. Learn one thing before you go. / A story is not begun with its ending already fixed.
…Mine is fixed.

blocks.html: Five years of listening, and that is the one lesson that does not take.
blocks.ko: 다섯 해를 들었고, 끝내 배지 않은 가르침은 그 하나다.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: You can teach a man every story on the island. You cannot make him believe he is inside one.
blocks.ko: 섬의 모든 이야기를 사람에게 가르칠 수는 있다. 그러나 제가 그 안에 있다고 믿게 할 수는 없다.

blocks.html: He says goodbye at the water. It takes longer than he planned.
blocks.ko: 그는 물가에서 작별한다. 생각보다 오래 걸린다.

lines: 계백! 자네 같은 사내를 만날 수 있게 되서 난 너무 좋았다.
본토로 돌아가면, 이제 우리는 다시 볼 수 있을 지 모르겠지.
en: Gyebek! It gladdened me to know a man like you.
Once you go back to the mainland, who knows if we shall meet again.
Promise me just one thing.
Do not forget people.

lines: ... 성주. 저는, 가족도, 이름도 없는 아이였습니다.
그런데, 나라의 태자께서 저를 받아들여주시고, 길러주시고, 믿어주었습니다.
저는 글도 못 읽는 무식한 사내입니다.
en: …My lord. I was a child with no family and no name.
And then the crown prince of a kingdom took me in, raised me, and trusted me.
Such a debt—
I am an ignorant man who cannot even read.
But as a man, I will keep faith.

blocks.html: Before he marches he goes home. What he does there he does so that nothing of his can be used against him, and the histories record it in one line.
blocks.ko: 출전에 앞서 그는 집으로 간다. 거기서 한 일은, 제 것 가운데 그 무엇도 자신을 겨누는 데 쓰이지 않게 하기 위함이었다. 사서는 그것을 한 줄로 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 恐吾妻孥 沒爲奴婢 與其生辱 不如死快 遂盡殺之
blocks.html: I fear my wife and children will be taken and made slaves. Better a quick death than a life of shame. And so he killed them all.
blocks.ko: 내 처자가 붙잡혀 노비가 될까 두렵다. 살아서 욕을 보느니 차라리 죽는 것이 낫다. 마침내 모두 죽였다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies, Gyebaek

blocks.html: He comes out before the light is properly up. The yard is swept. Nothing in it is his any more except a black horse at the post. Gomanari is named for the bear ferry where Gyebek learned to ride. It is the one thing he owns that the Tang cannot sell in a slave market.
blocks.ko: 날이 채 밝기도 전에 그가 집에서 나온다. 마당은 쓸려 있다. 그 안에 이제 그의 것은 말뚝에 매인 검은 말 한 마리뿐이다. 고마나리. 그가 말 타는 법을 배운 곰나루에서 딴 이름이다. 당이 노예 시장에 내다 팔 수 없는, 그가 가진 단 하나다.

blocks.html: The groom, a boy from the next village who did not sleep in the house and is therefore alive, holds the bridle out at arm’s length and will not look at him.
blocks.ko: 마부는 옆 마을 아이다. 그 집에서 자지 않았고, 그래서 살아 있다. 아이는 팔을 한껏 뻗어 굴레를 내밀 뿐 그를 쳐다보지 못한다.

en: H-here, General.
…Gomanari too?
A horse can’t be made a slave.
A horse is just a horse.

blocks.html: He saddles it himself, counting the buckles under his breath, and when he is done he stands with his forehead against the black neck for exactly as long as it takes to count to ten. Then he mounts and does not look at the house.
blocks.ko: 그는 손수 안장을 얹는다. 버클을 입속으로 세면서. 다 얹고 나서는 검은 목덜미에 이마를 대고, 꼭 열을 셀 만큼만 서 있는다. 그러고는 말에 오르고, 집 쪽은 돌아보지 않는다.

blocks.html: Gyebek and his five thousand set out for the Yellow Mountain. It is the last latch on the road to Sabi. Merchants have cursed its summer dust for years.
blocks.ko: 계백과 그의 오천이 황산으로 떠난다. 사비로 가는 길의 마지막 빗장이다. 장사꾼들이 여름 먼지 때문에 몇 해째 욕하던 곳이다.

en: Long live Baekje….!

blocks.html: Five thousand march for the Yellow Mountain. High above them, in a pavilion made of clouds, someone has called a meeting…!
blocks.ko: 오천이 황산으로 간다. 그 까마득한 위, 구름으로 지은 정자에서 누군가 회의를 열었다…!

toneNote: The Three Realms gossip like any court — mythic-cosmic warmth.

blocks.html: Epilogue · Part II. The annual meeting is a small 정자: four posts, a raised floor, clouds for a yard. Living, dead, and western rows all fit if nobody stretches.
blocks.ko: 에필로그 · 제2부. 연례회의는 작은 정자에서 열린다. 기둥 넷, 마루 하나, 마당은 구름. 이승과 저승과 서쪽 이랑이 발을 들여놓을 자리는 그 정도면 된다.

blocks.html: Four posts, clouds for a yard, and very strict seating.
blocks.ko: 기둥 넷, 구름 마당, 그리고 아주 엄격한 자리 배치.

blocks.title: The Three Realms · 삼계
blocks.caption: Hwanin above; Living, Dead, and Western Flower Field below. Heaven is not a fourth peer realm.
blocks.ko: 환인이 위에 있고, 이승·저승·서천꽃밭이 아래에 있다. 하늘나라는 네 번째 계가 아니다.

blocks.html: Before the principals sit — servants first. The Three Realms under the Big Man Upstairs still gossip like any court.
blocks.ko: 본존들이 앉기 전 — 시종들 먼저. 위에 계신 어른 아래 삼계도, 여느 조정처럼 수다를 떤다.

lines: 아, 강림이…. 늘 그렇게 젊어 보이는군, 응?
en: Ah, Kangrim…. Looking as young as ever, eh?

lines: 닥쳐, 태양아. 지금은 말 섞을 때가 아니야.
en: Shut it, sun. We aren't supposed to talk right now.

lines: 어이, 어이… 아직도 그 일 때문에 화났냐?
en: Hey, hey… still pissed off about the thing?
It's been hundreds of years at this point.
H-hey, Samsin.

lines: 어머, 염라! 오랜만이네. 저승은 요즘 어때?
en: Oh, long time no see, Yumla! How's the Underworld these days?
Y-you know… full of dead people. (awkwardly)
Your Honour. Your face went purple for a second.
I won't put it in the ledger.

blocks.html: Then the midwife and the sun find the same rail. The rest of the pavilion develops a sudden, devout interest in clouds.
blocks.ko: 그러고 산파와 태양이 같은 난간을 찾는다. 정자의 나머지는 갑자기, 경건하게, 구름에 관심이 생긴다.

en: Hey, Haemosu.
Did you see Yumla’s face? Went straight purple.
And I barely hiked the skirt.

lines: 저쪽은 명부 얘기나 하고 — 살아있는 티는 우리 둘만 내네.
en: Barely? I felt that from the chariot.
They’re talking ledgers — and only the two of us look alive.

lines: 남편들은 얼굴만 빨개지고, 나는 허벅지가 먼저 기억나거든.
en: I’ll be honest.
After a birth… my hands get restless.
The husbands go red in the face, and my thighs remember first.
You?

lines: 물속에 허리 잠긴 사람 보면 — 바퀴가 알아서 서.
한 번 내렸다고 다들 난리야. 난 아직도 그 열기가 그립다니까.
이 정자에서 우리보다 배고픈 애 있어? 하나라도.
en: The shallows, for me.
Someone waist-deep in water — the wheels stop themselves.
They still freak out that I came down once. I still miss that heat.
Anyone in this pavilion hungrier than us? Name one.

lines: 강림이는 공책만 보고. 염라는 내가 숨만 쉬어도 보라색.
남자든 뭐든 — 너랑은 이런 수다 가능해서 좋아.
en: Ibiga? He flirts with weather.
Kangrim stares at his notebook. Yumla goes purple if I breathe.
We’re the only ones actually hot in here.
Man or not — I like that I can gossip like this with you.

lines: 사람들이 헐떡일 때 — 너도 나도 그 소리 제일 먼저 듣잖아.
차 마시면서 점잖은 척은… 저쪽에나 맡기자.
en: Obviously. Heat doesn’t have a gender.
When mortals pant — you and I hear that sound first.
Polite tea faces… leave that to the others.
…Nothing for the ledger.
And that’s correct.

lines: 해모수. 너 또 해 수레에서 내려온 거 자랑할 셈이냐.
en: Haemosu. About to brag about climbing off the chariot again?
In the middle of gossiping with Samsin.
Only once. / That is the whole of it.
Not bragging… reporting.

blocks.html: Then the principals duck the lintel — Hallakgungi alone, Big Star with his dark court, Little Star with sky and sun and birth.
blocks.ko: 그러고 본존들이 처마를 숙여 들어온다 — 할락궁이는 혼자, 대별왕은 어두운 조정과 함께, 소별왕은 하늘과 태양과 출산과 함께.

blocks.html: The 정자 was not built for three sovereignties. They sit anyway.
blocks.ko: 정자는 세 주권을 위해 지은 집이 아니다. 그래도 앉는다.

lines: 야, 소별왕… 위에 계신 어른이 아들 하나 이승으로 내려보냈다며?
그 애 어떻게 됐냐? (농담으로) 십자가에 못 박진 않았지?
en: Hey Little Star… didn't the Big Man Upstairs send his son to the mortal domain a while back?
What happened to him? (joking) You didn't crucify him, did you?

lines: 단군이 세운 나라를 다시 하나로 모으겠다는 소리가, 사람들 입에서 나오기 시작했어.
en: Speaking of which…
Big things are happening in the mortal realm.
The mortals are starting to speak of reunifying Dangun's kingdom.

lines: 꽃밭에선 부활이랑 멸망이 같은 이랑에 자라. 통일도 아마 비슷할걸.
en: Elder brother of the dead goes quiet again.
In my field, resurrection and ruin grow in the same rows. Reunification probably does too.
Sir.
Yes?

lines: 늘 궁금했습니다… 나리 밭에는 어떤 꽃들이 핍니까?
en: I've always been curious… what sorts of flowers grow in your fields?

lines: 하하… 뭐, 새 피를 돋우는 꽃, 새 살을 키우는 꽃, 새 뼈를 기르는 꽃…
솔직히 이젠 다 기억도 안 나. (웃음)
en: Haha… well, there are those that regenerate new blood, grow new skin, grow new bones…
To be honest, I can't even keep track of all of them anymore. (laughs)
Why do you ask?

blocks.html: “Seeing the Western Flower Field — what flower is this?” “The flower that gives back speech. This one, the flower that brings blood back. The flower that brings flesh back, the one for the organs and bowels, the flower that brings bones back.”
blocks.ko: “서천꽃밭 구경 가서 보니, 이 꽃은 무슨 꽃입니까?” “말하게 할 꽃, 이 꽃은 피 오를 꽃, 살 오를 꽃, 오장육부 오를 꽃, 뼈 오를 꽃이로다.”
blocks.source: Segyeong Bonpuri (세경본풀이) recited by Lee Seung-sun (이승순), recorded by Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2011 — Sanggari, Aewol-eup (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: “서천꼿밧 구경간 요 꼿은 미신 꼿입네까?” “말 ᄀᆞᆯ을 꼿, 이 꼿은 피 오를 꼿, ᄉᆞᆯ 오를 꼿 오장육부 오를 꼿 뻬 오를 꼿이로다.”

lines: 그냥 궁금해서요… 그 꽃들을 한꺼번에 쓰면…
en: I was just curious… using all of these flowers at once…
Is it… is it possible to resurrect a dead person?
(face hardens, becomes serious)
Grim Reaper Kangrim. What is this line of questioning?
Do you have something you need to tell me?
No, sir. I was—

lines: 내가 해 봤다… 단 한 사람뿐.
그러나 나는 인간 일에 끼어들지 않는다.
en: Well, to answer your question. It is possible.
I've done it… only for one person.
But I do not get involved in mortal affairs.

lines: 사람들이 서로 베는 것도… 내 작은 법이지.
그래도 — 단군을 다시 부르면, 위에 계신 어른이 웃을까, 한숨을 쉴까.
en: I cheated for the living world.
Them cutting each other… that is my small law too.
Still — when they call Dangun’s name again, does the Big Man Upstairs laugh, or sigh?

lines: 산 자들의 이야기는… 안건 맨 마지막이다.
en: Let the meeting begin.
Business of the living… last item on the agenda.

blocks.html: The minutes of that meeting never leave Heaven’s table. Down below, five thousand men are counting fifty thousand…!
blocks.ko: 그 회의록은 하늘의 탁자를 떠나지 않는다. 저 아래에서는 오천이 오만을 세고 있다…!

toneNote: A kingdom's last days told at full gravity — last stands, falling palaces, and the escort of the dead.

Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Gyebek kneels with his sword planted
Two generals leap at each other, blades crossed
A rider rears on the ridge at sunset
Gyebek grips his sword
Gyebek on his knees in the gold dust

blocks.label: Snow on the Steppe
blocks.ko: 초원의 눈

blocks.html: Three years before he sees Samhan, Su Dingfang wins a war in a blizzard. He is sixty-five. His enemy has camped for the winter, sure that nobody fights in snow two feet deep. Su marches all night and attacks at dawn. He takes the whole camp before anyone in it has found his boots.
blocks.ko: 삼한을 보기 세 해 전, 소정방은 눈보라 속에서 전쟁 하나를 이긴다. 그는 예순다섯이다. 적은 두 자 깊이 눈 속에서 싸울 놈은 없다고 믿고 겨울 진을 쳤다. 소정방은 밤새 행군해 새벽에 들이친다. 진 안의 누구도 신발을 찾기 전에 진영 전체를 손에 넣는다.

blocks.caption: The Red Fowl. Sixty-five, and he still prefers to march at night.
blocks.ko: 주작. 예순다섯, 아직도 밤에 진군하는 걸 좋아한다.

lines: 그 속에선 아무도 너를 기다리지 않는다. 눈이 좋은 건 그거 하나다.
en: Snow is just cold sand.
Nobody expects you in it. That’s the only good thing about it.
zh: 沒人料到你會在雪裡來。雪就這點好。
zhLatn: Xuě búguò shì lěng shā.
Méi rén liàodào nǐ huì zài xuě lǐ lái. Xuě jiù zhè diǎn hǎo.

blocks.html: He comes home with the qaghan in a cart and a red banner over his own tent, a bird with its wings spread, painted by a regiment that had decided he needed one. Chang’an is calling him the Red Fowl long before anyone official does.
blocks.ko: 그는 가한을 수레에 싣고 돌아온다. 그의 군막 위에는 붉은 깃발이 걸려 있다. 날개를 편 새 한 마리. 그에게 하나쯤 있어야 한다고 마음먹은 어느 부대가 그려 준 것이다. 장안은 관에서 그렇게 부르기 한참 전부터 그를 주작이라 부른다.

blocks.label: Deokmul Island
blocks.ko: 덕물도

blocks.html: That summer he sails east with a hundred and thirty thousand men and anchors off a small island. A hundred Silla ships come out to meet him. At their head is the crown prince, Bupmin. He is thirty-four, and trying not to stare at the size of the Tang flagship.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름, 그는 십삼만 군사를 싣고 동쪽으로 건너와 작은 섬 앞에 닻을 내린다. 신라 배 백 척이 그를 맞으러 나온다. 맨 앞에 태자 법민이 있다. 서른넷이고, 당나라 기함이 얼마나 큰지 빤히 쳐다보지 않으려 애쓰는 중이다.

blocks.caption: An empire crosses the sea. A prince rows out to meet it and tries not to stare.
blocks.ko: 제국이 바다를 건넌다. 왕자는 노를 저어 마중 나가며 빤히 쳐다보지 않으려 애쓴다.

en: You’re the son?
zhLatn: Nǐ shì érzi?

en: Kim Bupmin, General. My father the king sends his—

lines: 칠월 열흘. 사비 남쪽. 너희 군대와 내 군대가 같은 들판에, 같은 아침에.
en: Tenth day of the seventh month. South of Sabi. Your army and mine, on the same field, on the same morning.
Tell your father. Tell him twice.
zh: 七月十日，泗沘之南。你軍我軍，同一片地，同一個早晨。
zhLatn: Qīyuè shí rì, Sìbì zhī nán. Nǐ jūn wǒ jūn, tóng yí piàn dì, tóng yí ge zǎochén.
Gàosu nǐ fùqīn. Shuō liǎng biàn.

en: We will be there, General.

blocks.html: Bupmin is rowed back to his own ship. Behind him the Red Fowl says something to his staff that makes them laugh.
blocks.ko: 법민은 노를 저어 제 배로 돌아간다. 그 뒤에서 주작이 참모들에게 뭐라 하자 그들이 웃는다.

lines: 늦을 거다. 작은 나라는 늘 늦어. 물어볼 삼촌이 너무 많거든.
en: They’ll be late. Small countries always are. They have to ask too many uncles.
zh: 他們會遲到。小國總是遲。要問的叔伯太多。
zhLatn: Tāmen huì chídào. Xiǎo guó zǒngshì chí. Yào wèn de shūbó tài duō.

blocks.label: Geumdol Fortress
blocks.ko: 금돌성

blocks.html: The king rides as far as a hill fort and no farther. The field belongs to his son and to Yushin. Fifty thousand men march west with a date in their heads. Between them and the date is the pass at Tanhyeon. Beyond the pass is a man called Gyebek.
blocks.ko: 임금은 산성 하나까지만 오고 더는 오지 않는다. 들판은 아들과 유신의 몫이다. 오만 군사가 머릿속에 날짜 하나를 넣고 서쪽으로 간다. 그들과 그 날짜 사이에 탄현 고개가 있다. 고개 너머에는 계백이라는 사내가 있다.

lines: …유신. 당이 먼저 도착하게 하지 마라. 저들은 천 년 동안 그렇게 적을 거다.
en: The tenth day, then.
…Yushin. Don’t let the Tang get there first. They’ll write it down that way for a thousand years.

blocks.label: Gibeolpo
blocks.ko: 기벌포

blocks.html: On the ninth day, the Tang fleet sails into the river mouth at Gibeolpo. The shore there is a mile of grey mud. Baekje’s soldiers wait on the high ground. They watch the first Tang companies wade in up to the thigh.
blocks.ko: 아흐렛날, 당의 함대가 기벌포 강어귀로 들어온다. 그곳 물가는 십 리에 걸친 잿빛 진흙이다. 백제 군사들은 높은 땅에서 기다린다. 당의 첫 부대가 허벅지까지 빠지며 걸어 들어오는 것을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: A river mouth made of mud, and Sabi’s front door.
blocks.ko: 진흙으로 된 강어귀, 사비의 앞문.

en: Mud is just wet road.
Give it something to hold.
zhLatn: Ní búguò shì shī lù.
Gěi tā diàn diǎn dōngxi.

blocks.html: His men lay willow mats on the mud, one after another, a road made of baskets, and the army walks across it dry-shod. By evening the Baekje line is broken and the river is open to Sabi.
blocks.ko: 그의 병사들이 진흙 위에 버들 거적을 한 장 한 장 깐다. 광주리로 만든 길이다. 군대는 발을 적시지 않고 그 위를 건넌다. 저녁이 되자 백제의 진은 무너지고, 사비로 가는 강이 열린다.

blocks.html: The same morning, forty miles east, the Silla army comes down out of the hills onto the Yellow Mountain Fields, and finds five thousand men already standing in its way.
blocks.ko: 같은 날 아침, 동쪽으로 백 리 떨어진 곳에서 신라군이 산을 내려와 황산벌로 들어선다. 오천 명이 이미 길을 막고 서 있다.

blocks.caption: One army from the sea, one from the hills, and one road to the capital between them.
blocks.ko: 바다에서 한 군대, 산에서 한 군대. 그 사이로 도성 가는 길이 하나뿐이다.

blocks.label: Yellow Mountain Fields
blocks.ko: 황산벌

blocks.html: Hundred-Victories gets to the Yellow Mountain Fields first and picks his ground. Then he waits — for the Sword of Silla, or for arithmetic, whichever arrives with a banner. Yellow lacquer holds the palisade. When the Sword arrives it is a tall black helm and a blue rim. The tall Silla helm comes in at a gallop. They meet in the dust. Blue plume cuts yellow lacquer.
blocks.ko: 백승이 황산벌에 먼저 닿아 자리를 고른다. 그리고 기다린다 — 신라의 도검이든, 셈이든, 깃발을 달고 오는 쪽을. 황칠이 목책을 지킨다. 검이 올 때는 높은 검은 투구와 푸른 테다. 신라의 높은 투구가 달려 들어온다. 먼지 속에서 만난다. 푸른 깃이 황칠을 가른다.

blocks.html: Good ground for whoever gets there first.
blocks.ko: 먼저 온 자에게 좋은 땅.

blocks.html: He sets three camps across the three ways in. There is no fourth way in; that is why he chose the place.
blocks.ko: 그는 들어오는 세 길목에 세 진영을 세운다. 네 번째 길은 없다. 그래서 그곳을 골랐다.

blocks.html: He walked the ground for two days before choosing it, in the same direction each time, and he can still tell you the number of paces between the eastern camp and the stream.
blocks.ko: 그는 자리를 고르기 전 이틀 동안 그 땅을 걸었다. 매번 같은 방향으로 걸었다. 동쪽 진영에서 개울까지 몇 걸음인지 그는 지금도 말할 수 있다.

en: Four hundred and twelve.
…Nobody asked. I know.

blocks.hanja: 以一國之人 當唐羅之大兵 國之存亡 未可知也…
blocks.ko: 한 나라의 사람으로 당과 신라의 대병을 당하니, 나라의 존망을 알 수 없다…
blocks.html: With the men of one country I face the great armies of Tang and Silla, and whether the country lives or dies cannot be known…
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Gyebek; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2, p. 452

blocks.title: Hwangsanbeol, ninth day of the seventh month, 660
blocks.note: 5,000 against 50,000. Five clashes: Baekje held the first four; the fifth broke them.

en: And theirs?
Fifty thousand, my lord.
Five thousand against fifty thousand….

blocks.html: Then the air above the Yellow Mountain does what air should not. Kangrim hangs there in plain day — visible not to one dying man but to all five thousand at once. They have already finished negotiating with life.
blocks.ko: 그때 황산 위 공기가 하면 안 되는 일을 한다. 강림이 대낮에 떠 있다 — 죽어 가는 한 사람이 아니라 오천이 한꺼번에 본다. 그들은 이미 삶과의 협상을 끝냈다.

blocks.html: They cheer. They wave. Someone shouts a greeting as if King Yumla’s escort were a popular general arriving late to his own war. Kangrim, who has collected kings with less fuss for His Majesty, actually blinks.
blocks.ko: 그들은 환호한다. 손을 흔든다. 누군가는 염라대왕의 사신을 — 자기 전쟁에 늦게 도착한 인기 장군처럼 — 소리쳐 맞는다. 폐하를 위해 왕을 더 조용히 데려가 본 강림이 정말로 눈을 깜빡인다.

en: …You can all see me.
That is — new.
Ah. You have already decided. Of course.
Men of Baekje —
If even death showed up early, we must be on time.
Spears.
lines: 죽음이 일찍 왔다면, 우리는 제시각인 거다.

blocks.html: Gyebek kneels. He plants the phoenix ring in the yellow dust and keeps his hand on it. Gyebek stands when the dust has learned the shape.
blocks.ko: 계백은 무릎을 꿇는다. 봉환을 노란 먼지에 꽂고 손을 그 위에 둔다. 먼지가 그 모양을 기억하면, 계백은 선다.

blocks.html: Five thousand against fifty thousand — not a formation so much as a sentence written in bodies. Like the three hundred at Thermopylae in stories that have not yet reached Samhan, they arrange themselves to be remembered rather than rescued. The math does not change. The watching does.
blocks.ko: 오천 대 오만 — 진형이라기보다 몸으로 쓴 문장. 삼한에 아직 닿지 않은 이야기 속 삼백처럼, 구출되기보다 기억되도록 선다. 셈은 바뀌지 않는다. 응시가 바뀔 뿐.

blocks.html: Seventh-month heat sits on the Yellow Mountain like a second army. Dust rises white off the three roads. Downstream, Tang sails already crowd the river mouth. They are waiting for the inland door to open. This field is that door.
blocks.ko: 칠월의 더위가 황산 위에 두 번째 군대처럼 앉아 있다. 세 길목에서 먼지가 희게 오른다. 하류에서는 당의 돛이 벌써 강어귀를 메운다. 내륙의 문이 열리기를 기다리는 중이다. 이 들판이 그 문이다.

lines: 지난 날 중원의 구천(句踐)은 5천 명으로 오(吳)나라의 70만 대군을 격파하였다. 지금 오늘 마땅히 각자 힘써 싸워 승리함으로써 나라의 은혜에 보답하자.
en: Long ago Goujian of the Central Plain shattered Wu’s host of seven hundred thousand with five thousand men. Today let each of us fight with all his strength, and repay the country’s grace with victory.

lines: 주점들은 아직도 삼한 최강의 칼을 우리 둘로 나눈다. 그 논쟁, 여기서 끝낼까?
en: So — you are this Hundred-Victories Gyebek I have heard of?
The taverns still split the Greatest Blade of Samhan between us. Shall we settle their argument?

lines: 나는 주점에서 마시지 않소. 나는 셉니다. 오늘은 오 대 오십 — 칭호는 그 다음이오.
en: Then you must be the Sword of the Divine Country.
I do not drink in taverns. I count. Today the count is five against fifty — and titles after.
Fifty thousand is a number.
Five thousand that already waved at death is another kind of number.
Hold your ground, then. We will come and measure it.
lines: 이미 죽음에 손 흔든 오천은 다른 종류의 숫자요.
그럼 자리를 지키시오. 우리가 가서 재어 보겠소.

blocks.label: The First Clash
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 접전

blocks.html: Silla comes on the first time in three columns: Yushin centre, Heumsun left, Pumil right. Down the three roads at once, exactly as the arithmetic says. Uphill. In the heat. Into yellow shields set edge to edge. The archers wait to see which column is thickest, and loose at that one. All three camps throw them back into their own dust.
blocks.ko: 신라는 첫 공격을 세 갈래로 해 온다. 가운데 유신, 왼쪽 흠순, 오른쪽 품일. 산수가 시키는 그대로, 세 길로 한꺼번에. 오르막을. 땡볕에. 가장자리를 맞댄 노란 방패를 향해. 궁수들은 어느 줄이 가장 두꺼운지 보고 나서야 그 줄에 쏜다. 세 진영이 그들을 제 먼지 속으로 도로 밀어낸다.

en: One.

blocks.label: The Second Clash
blocks.ko: 두 번째 접전

blocks.html: The second time Silla does not spread itself across three roads. It comes down the northern road in one fist at the left camp, hwarang in front, on the theory that the camp which shot the most is the camp with the fewest arrows left. It is a good theory. The left camp has counted its arrows too, and has been shooting half of what it could. The fist opens on the stakes and goes back up the road carrying its own.
blocks.ko: 두 번째에 신라는 세 길로 흩어지지 않는다. 북쪽 길로 한 주먹이 되어 왼쪽 진영을 친다. 화랑을 맨 앞에 세우고. 가장 많이 쏜 진영이 화살이 가장 적게 남은 진영이라는 이론에서다. 좋은 이론이다. 왼쪽 진영도 제 화살을 세어 두었고, 쏠 수 있는 것의 절반만 쏘아 왔다. 주먹은 말뚝 앞에서 펴지고, 제 사람들을 메고 길을 되올라간다.

en: Two.
Report.
…Left camp still has arrows.
Centre has men.
Right has both, and less of each than an hour ago.
lines: 오른쪽은 둘 다 있고, 한 시진 전보다 둘 다 적습니다.

blocks.label: The Third Clash
blocks.ko: 세 번째 접전

blocks.html: The third time Pumil takes the southern road, where the ground is softest and the right camp sits lowest, and for the length of a held breath the right road almost opens — and closes again on spears counted in the night. The camp is not quite where Pumil’s scouts drew it at dawn. It is further back and higher, every pace of the difference is uphill, and the Silla line arrives at the stakes with nothing left in its legs.
blocks.ko: 세 번째에 품일이 남쪽 길을 탄다. 땅이 가장 무르고 오른쪽 진영이 가장 낮게 앉은 곳. 숨 한 번 참는 동안 오른쪽 길이 거의 열렸다가 — 밤에 세어 둔 창에 다시 닫힌다. 진영은 새벽에 품일의 척후가 그려 온 자리에 꼭 있지 않다. 더 뒤에, 더 높은 곳에 있고, 그 차이의 걸음은 전부 오르막이라, 신라의 대열은 다리에 남은 것 없이 말뚝에 닿는다.

en: Three.

blocks.label: The Fourth Clash
blocks.ko: 네 번째 접전

blocks.html: The fourth time Yushin rides at the head of the centre himself, on the white horse, and meets Hundred-Victories in the gap between the camps. Both armies stop to watch two men, which armies are not supposed to do. It lasts about as long as it takes a banner to fall and be picked up again, and then the white horse is going back the way it came with a red line along its shoulder, and the Sword of Silla is holding his left arm against his ribs.
blocks.ko: 네 번째에는 유신이 몸소 흰 말을 타고 가운데 맨 앞에 서서, 진영과 진영 사이의 틈에서 백승을 만난다. 양쪽 군대가 두 사내를 구경하느라 멈춘다. 군대가 해서는 안 되는 일이다. 깃발 하나가 쓰러졌다가 다시 들릴 만큼의 시간이다. 그러고 나면 흰 말은 왔던 길로 돌아가고 있고, 그 어깨에 붉은 줄이 하나 그어져 있으며, 신라의 도검은 왼팔을 갈비뼈에 붙여 안고 있다.

blocks.html: Behind him the fifty thousand sit down where they stand. Four times up the same slope in the same heat — the clerks will write that the soldiers’ strength was spent, which is the polite way to say that grown men are lying in the dust of their own road and cannot be made to get up.
blocks.ko: 그의 뒤에서 오만이 선 자리에 주저앉는다. 같은 더위에 같은 비탈을 네 번 — 서기들은 군사의 힘이 다했다고 적을 것이다. 다 큰 사내들이 제 길의 먼지에 누워 일으켜 세울 수 없게 되었다는 말을 예의 바르게 하는 방법이다.

en: Four.

blocks.html: Yushin and the others divided the army into three roads. They fought four times without advantage, and the soldiers’ strength was spent.
blocks.ko: 유신 등이 군사를 세 길로 나누어 네 번 싸웠으나 이롭지 못하여, 군사들의 힘이 다하였다.
blocks.hanja: 庾信等分軍爲三道 四戰不利 士卒力竭
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — King Muyeol, year 7

blocks.html: He led five thousand men sworn to die out to Hwangsan and fought the Silla army. Four times they met, and four times he won…
blocks.ko: 결사대 오천을 거느리고 황산으로 나가 신라 군사와 싸워, 네 번 맞붙어 네 번 다 이겼다…
blocks.hanja: 帥死士五千出黄山 與羅兵戰 四合皆勝之…
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, year 20

blocks.html: Both kingdoms wrote the morning down. They agree on the number, and on nothing else.
blocks.ko: 두 나라 모두 그 아침을 적었다. 숫자에는 동의한다. 그 밖엔 아무것도.

blocks.html: After the fourth time there is a lull, the kind both sides pretend is for water. Yushin rides out alone into the gap on the white horse, his sleeve tied off with his own sash, and stops at a distance where a bow would be bad manners. After a while the black horse comes out of the centre camp to meet him. Nobody is near enough to hear. The chronicle has it anyway, the way it has most things, from men who swore afterwards they had not been listening.
blocks.ko: 네 번째가 끝나고 소강이 온다. 양쪽 다 물 마시는 시간인 척하는 그런 소강이다. 유신이 제 띠로 소매를 동여맨 채 흰 말을 타고 혼자 틈으로 나와, 활을 쏘면 무례가 될 거리에서 멈춘다. 한참 뒤 가운데 진영에서 검은 말이 마중을 나온다. 들을 만큼 가까이 있는 사람은 없다. 그래도 기록에는 남아 있다. 대부분이 그렇듯, 나중에 자기는 안 듣고 있었다고 맹세한 사내들에게서.

blocks.html: Black horse, white horse, nose to nose in the yellow dust. From either line they look like a pair of go stones someone has forgotten to play.
blocks.ko: 검은 말, 흰 말, 누런 먼지 속에서 코와 코를 맞댄다. 어느 쪽 대열에서 보아도, 누가 두다 만 바둑돌 한 쌍 같다.

en: Your right camp. You moved it in the night.
Forty paces.
…You noticed.
On the third time. Not before.
…How old are you.

lines: 마흔. 그쯤이오. 아무도 적어 두지 않았소.
en: Forty. Near enough. Nobody wrote it down.

lines: 내가 마흔일 때 만났으면 내가 이겼을 거요.
en: Sixty-five.
If we had met when I was forty, I would have had you.
…No. I would not have.

blocks.html: Gyebek looks at the tied sleeve and does not say anything polite about it.
blocks.ko: 계백은 동여맨 소매를 본다. 그것에 대해 예의 바른 말은 하지 않는다.

lines: 네 번째엔 직접 나왔소. 안 그래도 됐을 텐데.
en: You came yourself, the fourth time. You did not have to.

lines: 애들이 봐야 했소. 할 수 있다는 걸.
en: The boys needed to see it could be done.
Could it?

lines: 오만을 데리고 왔소. 아직 사만 몇은 남았고. 그대는 오천을 데리고 왔지.
en: Not by me. Not today.
I came with fifty thousand. I still have forty-some. You came with five.
Four. Now.

lines: 알고 있소. 나도 셀 줄 아오.
en: I know. I can count too.
Then go home.
You first.

blocks.html: Neither of them laughs, but it is close.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 웃지는 않는다. 웃을 뻔했을 뿐이다.

en: Your taverns.
What about them.
Nothing. They will have a long winter.

blocks.html: They turn the horses at the same moment, black and white, as if somebody had rehearsed it, and ride back to their counts. In the Silla line Heumsun is already looking at his son.
blocks.ko: 둘은 같은 순간에 말머리를 돌린다. 검은 말과 흰 말, 누가 미리 맞춰 둔 것처럼. 그리고 각자의 셈으로 돌아간다. 신라 쪽 대열에서 흠순이 벌써 제 아들을 보고 있다.

blocks.html: The hwarang yard still tells its oldest story in two names: two boys who swore, and did not outlive the swear. Nobody here says the rhyme aloud. The field supplies it anyway. Bangul rides first. Gwanchang rides second.
blocks.ko: 화랑 마당은 아직도 제일 오래된 이야기를 두 이름으로 전한다. 맹세하고, 그 맹세보다 오래 살지 못한 두 소년. 여기선 아무도 그 노래를 입에 올리지 않는다. 들판이 알아서 채운다. 반굴이 먼저 나간다. 관창이 다음이다.

blocks.label: Bangul & Gwanchang
blocks.ko: 반굴과 관창

blocks.html: Heumsun calls his son to his stirrup. Bangul is fifteen, near enough, and Yushin’s nephew; he comes at a run, because he has been watching his father look at him since the white horse came back.
blocks.ko: 흠순이 아들을 등자 곁으로 부른다. 반굴은 얼추 열다섯, 유신의 조카다. 흰 말이 돌아온 뒤로 아비가 자기를 보고 있는 것을 줄곧 지켜보았기에, 그는 달려온다.

en: For a subject, nothing is greater than loyalty. For a son, nothing is greater than filial piety.
To see the danger and give your life to it — that keeps both, whole, at once.
lines: 신하로서는 충만 한 것이 없고, 자식으로서는 효만 한 것이 없다.
위태로움을 보고 목숨을 바치면 — 충과 효를 함께 온전히 하는 것이다.

en: I have heard you, Father.

blocks.html: Bangul rides out alone and does not come back. He goes into the Baekje line where it is thickest and fights there until it closes over him, and the place where it closed is the place Silla aims at next.
blocks.ko: 반굴이 홀로 말을 몰고 나가 돌아오지 않는다. 그는 백제의 대열이 가장 두터운 곳으로 들어가, 대열이 그를 덮을 때까지 싸운다. 대열이 닫힌 그 자리가, 신라가 다음에 겨누는 자리다.

blocks.html: Pumil does not call his son. He has him brought to stand in front of his horse, before all the generals, and points at him the way a man points at a map.
blocks.ko: 품일은 아들을 부르지 않는다. 장수들이 다 보는 앞에서 아들을 제 말 앞에 세우게 하고, 지도를 가리키듯 그를 가리킨다.

blocks.caption: Gwanchang. A hwarang so young they had to pad the helmet.
blocks.ko: 관창. 투구 안에 솜을 덧대야 할 만큼 어린 화랑.

en: My son is only sixteen, but his spirit is brave enough.
In today’s battle — can he be the mark the three armies aim by?
lines: 내 아이는 겨우 열여섯이나, 뜻과 기개가 자못 용감하오.
오늘 싸움에서 — 삼군이 겨눌 표적이 될 수 있겠느냐?

en: Yes.

blocks.html: He takes an armoured horse and one spear and goes straight at the Baekje centre. He gets further than Bangul did. Then they pull him off the horse alive and bring him to Gyebek.
blocks.ko: 그는 갑옷 입힌 말 한 필과 창 한 자루로 곧장 백제의 가운데로 달려든다. 반굴보다 더 깊이 들어간다. 그리고 산 채로 말에서 끌어내려져 계백 앞에 끌려온다.

blocks.html: Gyebek has the helmet taken off. Inside it is a boy’s face, sweat-striped, furious at being alive.
blocks.ko: 계백이 투구를 벗기게 한다. 그 안에 소년의 얼굴이 있다. 땀으로 줄이 지고, 살아 있다는 데 분해 하는 얼굴.

en: Silla cannot be withstood.
If a boy is like this — what are its grown men?
Go home.

blocks.html: They put him back on his horse and point it at the Silla line. At his father’s stirrup Gwanchang does not get down.
blocks.ko: 그들은 그를 다시 말에 태워 신라 쪽으로 머리를 돌려 보낸다. 아비의 등자 곁에서 관창은 말에서 내리지 않는다.

en: I went into their midst and could not cut down their general or take their banner.
It was not because I was afraid to die.
lines: 제가 적진에 들어가 장수를 베지도, 깃발을 뽑지도 못한 것은

blocks.html: Behind the Silla line there is a well, dug that morning for the horses. He scoops the water out with both hands, drinks, and rides back the way he came. Gyebek sends him home once. He comes back.
blocks.ko: 신라 대열 뒤에 그날 아침 말들을 위해 판 우물이 있다. 그는 두 손으로 물을 떠 마시고, 왔던 길로 다시 달려간다. 계백은 그를 한 번 돌려보냈다. 그는 다시 온다.

blocks.html: The second time, Gyebek has his helmet unstrapped again, looks at the face inside it for a while, and then does what he has to. He ties the head to the saddle and sends the horse back.
blocks.ko: 두 번째로 계백은 다시 그 투구를 벗기게 하고, 안에 든 얼굴을 한참 바라본 뒤, 해야 할 일을 한다. 그리고 그 머리를 안장에 매어 말을 돌려보낸다.

blocks.hanja: 階伯擒斬首，繫馬鞍送之。品日執其首…曰：「吾兒面目如生，能死於王事，無所悔矣。」
blocks.ko: 계백이 사로잡아 목을 베어 말안장에 매어 보냈다. 품일이 그 머리를 잡고 … 말하였다. “내 아들의 얼굴이 살아 있는 것 같구나. 나랏일에 죽을 수 있었으니 뉘우칠 것이 없다.”
blocks.html: Gyebek took him, cut off his head, tied it to the saddle and sent it back. Pumil held the head … and said: “My son’s face is as if he were alive. He was able to die in the king’s service. I have nothing to regret.”
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Gwanchang; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2, p. 454

blocks.html: He holds the head up in front of the army and wipes the blood from its face with his own sleeve, so that the three armies can see whose son it is.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 머리를 군사들 앞에 들어 올리고, 제 소매로 얼굴의 피를 닦는다. 삼군이 그것이 누구의 아들인지 볼 수 있도록.

blocks.label: The Fifth Clash · The Final Stand
blocks.ko: 다섯 번째 접전 · 최후의 항전

blocks.html: Nobody gives an order. The drums start on their own, one column and then the next, and fifty thousand men who could not be made to get up an hour ago are on their feet and shouting.
blocks.ko: 아무도 명령하지 않는다. 북이 저절로 울기 시작한다. 한 대열, 그다음 대열. 한 시진 전만 해도 일으켜 세울 수 없던 오만이 일어서서 함성을 지른다.

blocks.html: The Silla line, which has failed four times that morning, goes forward and does not stop. A father’s wet sleeve is worth more than a fourth failure. The left camp goes under first — not broken so much as used up. The right holds one more breath, then folds toward the centre like a hinge that has decided to finish.
blocks.ko: 그날 아침 네 번을 실패한 신라의 대열이 앞으로 나아가고, 이번엔 멈추지 않는다. 아비의 젖은 소매가 네 번째 실패보다 값이 크다. 왼쪽 진영이 먼저 가라앉는다 — 부서졌다기보다 다 쓰인 것에 가깝다. 오른쪽이 한 숨 더 버티다가, 끝내기로 한 경첩처럼 가운데로 접힌다.

blocks.html: On the Baekje side, nobody says five.
blocks.ko: 백제 쪽에서는, 아무도 다섯이라고 말하지 않는다.

blocks.html: By the fifth charge the left camp is a rumour of men. Gyebek’s centre is the last grammar the field still understands — a thin line of Baekje that refuses to become a paragraph about surrender. Spears shorten. Names stop answering. Kangrim, who has been hanging in the day like unfinished weather, comes down to speaking distance.
blocks.ko: 다섯 번째 돌격쯤이면 왼쪽 진영은 사람의 소문에 가깝다. 계백의 가운데가 이 벌판이 아직 알아듣는 마지막 문법이다 — 항복에 대한 문단이 되기를 거부하는 백제의 얇은 선. 창이 짧아진다. 이름이 대답을 멈춘다. 미완의 날씨처럼 대낮에 걸려 있던 강림이, 말 닿는 거리까지 내려온다.

blocks.html: He reads the general's name three times across the field — Gyebek. Gyebek. Gyebek. — though five thousand throats have already answered.
blocks.ko: 그는 벌판을 가로질러 장군의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 계백. 계백. 계백. — 오천의 목구멍이 이미 대답했어도.

en: General.
Your five thousand already waved. So I ask you alone.
When you killed your family to keep your oath: was that loyalty, or terror of becoming soft?
lines: 오천은 이미 손을 흔들었소. 그러니 당신에게만 묻겠소.
약조를 지키려 집안을 베었을 때: 그것이 충성이었습니까, 아니면 무르게 될까 두려운 것이었습니까?

en: …Loyalty.
If it was terror, do not tell them. Let them keep the prettier word.
And you — you were heaven’s messenger.
Sent to arrest King Yumla. You stayed. A crow mixed the pages of your ledger.
That is why nobody knows their hour until you are already in the room.
lines: 두려움이었다면 그들에게 말하지 마시오. 더 예쁜 말을 갖게 두시오.
염라대왕을 잡아 오라 보내졌고. 당신은 남았고. 까마귀가 명부의 장을 뒤섞었소.
그래서 당신이 이미 방에 들어오기 전엔, 아무도 제 시각을 모르는 것이오.

en: The island told you.
Living men are not supposed to finish that sentence.
How long have you been carrying my origin like a spare spear?
lines: 산 자는 그 문장을 끝까지 말하면 안 된다.
내 내력을 예비 창처럼 얼마나 들고 다녔나?

en: Five years of evenings on Tamla.
They save your story for last — after every kinder tale.
I counted the stories the way I count paces.
When you hung above us this morning, I already knew which kingdom’s marshal you were.
lines: 그들은 당신 이야기를 마지막에 한다 — 더 고운 이야기들 뒤에.
오늘 아침 우리 위에 걸렸을 때, 이미 어느 나라의 원수인지 알았소.

en: Surprise is rare in my work.
Thank you for that — His Majesty appreciates accurate minutes.

blocks.html: A nameless boy at the White River, newly called Gyebek, answers a prince the only way he knows.
blocks.ko: 백강의 이름 없는 아이, 새로이 계백이라 불린 소년은, 왕자에게 자신이 아는 유일한 방식으로 답한다.

en: I will complete my duty.
…Good.
That is a sharper vow than most crowns get.

blocks.html: The field returns. The vow has come due.
blocks.ko: 전장이 돌아온다. 맹세의 만기가 왔다.

en: Your Majesty… I have completed my duty.

blocks.html: Kangrim, who has been hanging in the day like unfinished weather, closes the distance.
blocks.ko: 낮에 미완의 날씨처럼 걸려 있던 강림이 거리를 좁힌다.

en: Walk, then. The underworld kingdom keeps better hours than Sabi ever did.
lines: 그럼 가시죠. 저승은 사비보다 시간을 잘 킵니다.

blocks.html: The man who counted everything finishes counting, and walks. The Yellow Mountain keeps the dust. The White River, downstream, opens.
blocks.ko: 모든 것을 세던 사내가 셈을 마치고, 걷는다. 황산은 먼지를 간직한다. 하류의 백강이 열린다.

blocks.html: The Silla clerks count too. Twenty-odd taken alive, two ministers among them. Nobody writes down how many of the five thousand were left to take.
blocks.ko: 신라의 서기들도 센다. 사로잡은 자 스무남은, 그 가운데 좌평 둘. 오천 가운데 사로잡을 사람이 몇이나 남아 있었는지는 아무도 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: Nobody can lead the black horse off the field. It stands over the place where he went down until the Silla grooms come at dusk with ropes, and it takes six of them, and in the night it breaks the line and goes south toward the ferry it was named for. Nobody on either side ever reports seeing it again.
blocks.ko: 아무도 그 검은 말을 들판에서 끌어내지 못한다. 말은 그가 쓰러진 자리를 지키고 서 있다가, 해 질 녘 신라 마부들이 밧줄을 들고 오자 여섯이 달라붙어야 하고, 밤이 되자 줄을 끊고 제 이름이 된 나루 쪽, 남으로 간다. 어느 편에서도 그 말을 다시 보았다는 보고는 없다.

blocks.html: The pass is open. The river is open. And in Sabi, the king’s big idea is to send the Tang dinner…!
blocks.ko: 고개가 열렸다. 강도 열렸다. 그리고 사비에서 임금이 낸 묘수는, 당군에게 저녁상을 보내는 것이다…!

images.alt: Wide Sabi: reddish munru on the long grey palace wall, green approach, misted mountains
images.prompt: Wide cinematic EXPOSITION still. SAME Sabi Palace as the attached place: reddish munru, long giwa wall, green fields. No text. No watermark.

images.at: The court hears about the Yellow Mountain Fields
images.alt: Fallen Sabi as a cavernous dark hall — one wine-red empty throne plane, tiny court silhouettes on a wet black floor
