LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: The court hears about the Yellow Mountain Fields the following morning.
blocks.ko: 조정은 이튿날 아침 황산벌 소식을 듣는다.

blocks.caption: Two arrows, one capital, and a king who has decided the answer is oxen.
blocks.ko: 화살 둘, 도성 하나, 그리고 답은 소 떼라고 정한 왕.

blocks.html: Euija’s first move is to send the Tang camp a feast: oxen, wine, three cartloads of rice cakes. The court is told this is diplomacy.
blocks.ko: 의자의 첫 수는 당의 진영에 잔칫상을 보내는 것이다. 소, 술, 떡 세 수레. 조정에는 이것이 외교라고 알린다.

en: Nobody burns a city on a full stomach.
Feed them. Then we’ll talk about what they want.

blocks.html: The oxen come back that afternoon, untouched, with the drovers walking behind them.
blocks.ko: 황소들은 그날 오후, 손도 안 댄 채, 몰이꾼들을 뒤에 달고 되돌아온다.

blocks.label: The Red Fowl’s Tent
blocks.ko: 주작의 군막

blocks.html: The Silla army reaches the Tang camp two days late. The Red Fowl has the Silla supply officer dragged to his tent gate. They open his collar for the sword.
blocks.ko: 신라군이 약속보다 이틀 늦게 당의 진영에 닿는다. 주작은 신라의 군량 담당 장교를 군막 문 앞으로 끌어낸다. 칼 받을 목깃을 풀게 한다.

lines: 열흘. 사비 남쪽. 두 번 말했다.
en: The tenth day. South of Sabi. I said it twice.
Take his head. Then we can start.
zh: 七月十日，泗沘之南。我說了兩遍。
zhLatn: Qīyuè shí rì, Sìbì zhī nán. Wǒ shuō le liǎng biàn.
Zhǎn le. Ránhòu kāishǐ.

blocks.html: Kim Yushin walks into the tent with a battle-axe in his hand.
blocks.ko: 김유신이 손에 큰 도끼를 들고 군막 안으로 걸어 들어온다.

lines: 늦었다는 걸 죄로 삼겠다면, 죄 없이 욕을 받을 수는 없소. 당군과 먼저 결판을 내고, 백제는 그다음에 치겠소.
en: The general did not see the Yellow Mountain Fields.
If you mean to punish us for being late, I will not be shamed for a crime I did not commit. I will fight the Tang first, and Baekje after.

blocks.hanja: 乃杖鉞軍門 怒髮如植 其腰間寶劍自躍出鞘
blocks.html: Then he stood at the camp gate leaning on his axe; his angry hair stood up like planted stakes, and the precious sword at his waist leapt of itself from its scabbard.
blocks.ko: 이에 도끼를 짚고 군문에 서니, 성난 머리털이 꽂아 세운 듯하고, 허리에 찬 보검이 저절로 칼집에서 뛰쳐나왔다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — King Muyeol, yr. 7 (660), seventh month

blocks.html: The Red Fowl’s second-in-command steps on his commander’s foot.
blocks.ko: 주작의 부장이 제 장군의 발을 슬쩍 밟는다.

blocks.speaker: Dong Baoliang
en: (low) The Silla army is about to turn on us, General.
zhLatn: (Dīshēng) Xīnluó bīng jiāng yǒu biàn yě.

blocks.html: Kim Munyeong’s collar is closed again. Nobody in the tent mentions the date for the rest of the war.
blocks.ko: 김문영의 목깃이 다시 여며진다. 그 전쟁이 끝날 때까지 군막 안의 누구도 날짜 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.html: Euija leaves Sabi at night for Bear Fortress, with fewer men than he expected to have.
blocks.ko: 의자는 밤에 사비를 떠나 웅진성으로 향한다. 데리고 갈 수 있는 사람은 생각보다 적었다.

blocks.caption: One river’s length north, to a fortress his grandfather trusted.
blocks.ko: 강 한 굽이 북쪽, 할아버지가 믿었던 성으로.

blocks.hanja: 王知不免 歎曰 悔不用成忠之言 以至於此
blocks.ko: 왕이 면할 수 없음을 알고 탄식하여 이르되, 성충의 말을 쓰지 아니하여 이에 이름에 이르렀음을 후회하노라.
blocks.html: The king knew he could not escape, and sighed: I regret that I did not use Seongchung’s words, and have come to this.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 20 (660); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 386

en: Kim Chunchu…
KIM CHUNCHU!!!
Hm?

lines: 삼한의 땅으로 외세를 끌어들이는 이 비랄한 만고의 역적아!!
en: Kim Chunchu, you wretch!!
You vile traitor of the ages, who dragged a foreign power onto the soil of Samhan!!
Heaven’s punishment will find you!!

blocks.html: Euija’s second son, left behind, crowns himself the next morning. A grandson takes one look at the Tang camp and does the sum. An uncle who stays will kill whoever opens the gate. So the grandson climbs down the wall on a rope with his household. Half the city follows him down it.
blocks.ko: 도성에 남은 의자의 둘째가 이튿날 아침 스스로 왕이 된다. 손자 하나가 당의 진영을 한 번 보고 셈을 한다. 남은 숙부는 성문 연 자를 다 죽일 것이다. 그래서 손자는 식솔을 데리고 밧줄을 타고 성벽을 내려간다. 성의 절반이 그 밧줄을 따라 내려간다.

blocks.html: The crown prince comes out of the gate. Chunbok walks a careful pace behind him. Bupmin has the prince knelt in the dirt before his horse, and spits in his face.
blocks.ko: 태자가 성문을 나온다. 천복이 조심스레 한 걸음 뒤에서 따른다. 법민은 태자를 제 말 앞 흙바닥에 꿇리고, 그 얼굴에 침을 뱉는다.

lines: 예전에 너의 아비가 나의 여동생을 억울하게 죽여 옥중에 묻은 적이 있다. (그 일은) 나로 하여금 20년 동안 마음이 아프고 골치를 앓게 하였는데, 오늘날 너의 목숨이 내 손 안에 있구나!
en: Long ago your father had my younger sister killed unjustly and buried in a prison. That deed left my heart sore and my head aching for twenty years — and today your life is in my hands!

blocks.html: Yung lies flat on the ground and says nothing.
blocks.ko: 융은 땅에 엎드려 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

lines: 장군들께서도 헤아리시겠지만, 성문은 백성을 위하여, 그리고 전적으로 그 뜻에 따라—
en: As the generals will surely appreciate, the gate was opened for the sake of the people, and in full accordance with—

blocks.label: Falling Flower Rock
blocks.ko: 낙화암

blocks.html: When the gate opens the palace women do not wait to be counted. They go out the back of the palace and up the ridge path to the cliff above the White River, where the rock drops straight into the water, and the soldiers coming up behind them find nobody at the top.
blocks.ko: 성문이 열리자 궁의 여인들은 세어지기를 기다리지 않는다. 궁 뒤로 빠져나가 백마강 위 벼랑까지 능선 길을 오른다. 바위가 물속으로 곧장 떨어지는 곳이다. 뒤따라 올라온 군사들은 꼭대기에서 아무도 찾지 못한다.

blocks.html: The stories that gave Euija three thousand women give them this cliff as well, and three thousand is the number they say went over it, their skirts opening on the way down like petals. That is why the rock is called Nakhwaam, the Rock of Falling Flowers. Nobody who was there wrote down how many it really was. There was no one left on the cliff to count.
blocks.ko: 의자에게 삼천 궁녀를 붙여 준 이야기들은 이 벼랑도 그들에게 준다. 그 위에서 떨어진 것이 삼천이었다고, 떨어지는 동안 치마가 꽃잎처럼 벌어졌다고 말한다. 그래서 그 바위를 낙화암, 꽃이 떨어진 바위라 부른다. 그 자리에 있던 누구도 실제로 몇이었는지 적지 않았다. 벼랑 위에는 셀 사람이 남아 있지 않았다.

blocks.label: Ungjin
blocks.ko: 웅진성

blocks.html: Bear Fortress belongs to the king the way a borrowed house belongs to a guest. The Ye family has held it for four generations. Ye Sikjin gives the king his own rooms, and goes up on the wall every morning to count the Tang sails on the river.
blocks.ko: 웅진성이 왕의 것인 건 빌린 집이 손님의 것인 것과 같다. 예씨 집안이 네 대째 지켜 온 성이다. 예식진은 왕에게 제 방을 내주고, 아침마다 성벽에 올라 강 위의 당나라 돛을 센다.

lines: 식진아! 좋은 놈. 네 할아비가 내 할아비 위해 이 바위를 지켰지?
다시 지키는 거다. 주작이 언제까지 진흙탕에 앉아 있겠냐.
en: Sikjin! Good man. Your grandfather held this rock for my grandfather, eh?
We’ll hold it again. The Red Fowl can’t sit in the mud forever.
My grandfather held it, Majesty.
…For whoever was king.

blocks.html: The first morning he counts forty sails. The second morning, sixty-two. He writes both numbers on the wall in charcoal, because that is what he does with numbers.
blocks.ko: 첫날 아침 그는 돛 마흔 개를 센다. 이튿날 아침에는 예순둘. 그는 두 숫자를 숯으로 성벽에 적어 둔다. 숫자를 보면 그렇게 하는 사람이다.

lines: 예순둘? 하! 뱃전에 대고 토하는 놈들이 예순두 척이로구나.
식진아, 멀미하는 소로는 밭을 못 간다. 하하!
술 가져오너라. 좋은 잔으로. 수비대 잔 말고.
en: Sixty-two? Ha! Sixty-two boatloads of men throwing up over the side.
Sikjin, you can’t plough with a seasick ox. Ha!
Bring wine. The good cups. Not the garrison ones.
The good cups are in Sabi, Majesty.
…I’ll bring the garrison ones.

blocks.html: On the third day a boatman comes up the river with Sabi still on his face. Ye Sikjin hears him out alone, on the wall. Then he takes him to the king, because that is the order things are done in.
blocks.ko: 사흗날, 사비에서 본 것이 아직 얼굴에 남은 사공 하나가 강을 거슬러 올라온다. 예식진은 성벽 위에서 혼자 그 말을 끝까지 듣는다. 그런 다음 그를 왕에게 데려간다. 일은 그 순서로 하는 것이니까.

lines: 태가 왕관을 썼다고? 그놈은 호박에 갓도 못 씌우는 놈이다!
…좋다. 꿇은 아들도 아들이지. 성을 되찾으면 한 달은 마당에 세워 두마. 하하!
en: Tae put on a crown? That boy couldn’t get a hat on a pumpkin!
And Yung… knelt.
…Fine. A son on his knees is still a son. When I take the city back, he can stand in the yard for a month. Ha!

blocks.html: That night his elder brother comes in by the river gate. Ye Gun is the family’s talker. He has been downriver all day, he says, looking at the weather. It has rained since noon. He comes back dry.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 형이 강 쪽 문으로 들어온다. 예군은 집안에서 말을 맡은 사람이다. 종일 강 아래로 날씨를 보러 갔었다고 한다. 정오부터 비가 왔다. 그는 젖지 않은 채 돌아온다.

lines: 그 장군은 진흙 얘기를 날씨 얘기하듯 하더라. 진흙은 젖은 길일 뿐이라나.
그리고 이 성에 방이 몇 개냐고 묻더군. 아우한테 물어봐야 한다고 했다. 세는 건 너니까.
en: That general talks about mud the way other men talk about weather. Mud is just wet road, apparently.
And he asked how many rooms this fortress has. I said I’d have to ask my brother. You’re the one who counts.
Thirty-nine, brother.
Counting the king’s.
And men?
Depends on the room.

lines: 수비대 술도 마시다 보니 정이 드는구나, 식진아!
끝나면 너는 조정으로 올라온다. 진짜 자리로. 앞줄로. 배 세는 짓은 그만이다.
얼굴이 왜 그러냐? 농담 아니다. 마셔라!
en: Garrison wine! It grows on you, Sikjin!
When this is over, you’re coming to court. A real seat. Front row. No more counting boats.
What’s that face? That wasn’t a joke. Drink!
You honour me, Majesty.
…Which seat?

lines: 하! 들었느냐? 어느 자리냐니! 아무 데나 골라라.
en: Ha! Listen to him. Which seat! Take your pick.
I’ve got forty-one of them.

blocks.html: That night he opens the drawer. The list is where he left it. Forty-one names. None of them his. He reads it a third time, being careful with numbers, and puts it back. He does not close the drawer. One day a Tang stonecutter will carve his father and grandfather into Baekje’s first rank. Neither of them was ever asked to court. Tombstones are generous that way.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 서랍을 연다. 명단은 넣어 둔 그대로다. 이름 마흔하나. 그의 이름은 없다. 숫자에 꼼꼼한 사람이라, 그는 세 번째로 읽고 도로 넣는다. 서랍은 닫지 않는다. 언젠가 당나라 석공 하나가 그의 아버지와 할아버지를 백제의 일품으로 새겨 줄 것이다. 둘 다 조정에 한 번 불려 간 적 없는 사람들이다. 묘비란 그렇게 너그럽다.

blocks.html: On the fifth night he comes into the king’s rooms with his brother and twenty men, and the king understands before anyone speaks.
blocks.ko: 닷새째 밤, 그는 형과 장정 스물을 데리고 왕의 방으로 들어온다. 왕은 누가 입을 열기도 전에 알아차린다.

blocks.html: By morning the king is on his way to the Red Fowl’s tent.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 임금은 주작의 군막으로 끌려가고 있다.

blocks.hanja: 其大將禰植又將義慈來降
blocks.html: Its great general Ye Sik also brought Uija and came to surrender.
blocks.ko: 그 대장 예식이 또 의자를 데리고 와서 항복하였다.
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 83, Biography of Su Dingfang

blocks.hanja: 於是 王及太子孝與諸城皆降
blocks.ko: 이에 왕과 태자 효와 여러 성이 모두 항복하였다.
blocks.html: Thereupon the king and Crown Prince Hyo, together with the several fortresses, all surrendered.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 20 (660); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 386

blocks.html: On the eighteenth day Euija, leading the crown prince and the troops of the Ungjin district commander, came out of Bear Fortress and surrendered.
blocks.ko: 18일, 의자가 태자와 웅진 방령의 군사들을 거느리고 웅진성에서 나와 항복하였다.
blocks.hanja: 十八日，義慈率太子及熊津方領軍等，自熊津城來降。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — King Muyeol, yr. 7 (660), seventh month

blocks.html: Euija, king of Baekje, his wife Eungo, his son Yung and the rest, with his ministers Chunbok, Guk Byeonseong, Son Deung and others, some fifty in all, were seized by General Su* on the thirteenth day of the seventh month and sent away to Tang.
blocks.ko: 백제왕 의자와 그 아내 은고, 그 아들 융 등, 그 신하 좌평 천복·국변성·손등 등 모두 쉰여 명이 가을 7월 13일에 소 장군*에게 붙잡혀 당나라로 보내졌다.
blocks.hanja: 百濟王義慈，其妻恩古，其子隆等，其臣佐平千福、國辨成、孫登等凡五十餘。秋七月十三日，為蘇將軍所捉，而送去於唐國。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 26, Saimei 6 (660), tenth month — note to the Baekje loyalists’ embassy

notes.html: General Su is Su Dingfang. Chang’an calls him the Red Fowl.
notes.ko: 소 장군은 소정방, 장안이 주작이라 부르는 사람이다.

blocks.html: Sikjin inherited the office, as the worthy follow the worthy. When Tang took Heaven’s mandate and marched east against the defiant, he at once led his king to submit to the Third Emperor. For this he was made Grand General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Laiyuan.
blocks.ko: 식진에 이르러 대대로 벼슬을 이으니, 어진 이를 본받은 것이다. 당이 천명을 받아 동쪽의 복종하지 않는 자를 칠 때, 곧 그 왕을 이끌고 고종 황제에게 의리로 돌아왔다. 이로써 좌위위대장군에 제수되고 내원군 개국공에 봉해졌다.
blocks.hanja: 洎子寔進世官，象賢也。有唐受命，東討不庭，即引其王歸義于高宗皇帝。由是拜左威衛大將軍，封來遠郡開國公。
blocks.source: Epitaph of Ye Inseu (禰仁秀墓誌), grandson of Ye Sikjin, Tang, 8th c.

blocks.html: In the fifth year of Xianqing, on the day the imperial army pacified his home country, he saw the moment, read the change, and, sword in hand, knew where to turn. Like You Yu leaving the Rong; like Jin Midi entering Han.
blocks.ko: 지난 현경 5년, 관군이 본국을 평정하던 날, 기미를 보고 변화를 알아 칼을 짚고 돌아갈 곳을 알았다. 유여가 융을 떠난 것과 같고, 김일제가 한에 들어간 것과 같았다.
blocks.hanja: 去顯慶五年，官軍平本藩日，見機識變，杖劍知歸。似由余之出戎，如金磾之入漢。
blocks.source: Epitaph of Ye Gun (禰軍墓誌), elder brother of Ye Sikjin, Tang, 678

blocks.html: His name was Sikjin, a man of Ungcheon in Baekje. His grandfather, Minister Yeda, and his father, Minister Saseon, both held the first rank of that vassal court. … Upright from birth and early marked for righteousness, he read the wind in a foreign land and went toward the sun in Chang’an.
blocks.ko: 공의 휘는 식진이요, 백제 웅천 사람이다. 할아버지 좌평 예다와 아버지 좌평 사선은 모두 번국 관직 정일품이었다. … 일찍이 곧은 법도를 타고나 의로운 절개를 드러내니, 이역에서 바람을 점치고 장안의 해를 향해 나아갔다.
blocks.hanja: 公諱寔進百濟熊川人也 祖佐平譽多父佐平思善竝蕃官正一品 … 夙禀貞規早標義節占風異域就日長安
blocks.source: Epitaph of Ye Sikjin (禰寔進墓誌), Tang, 672

blocks.html: Nobody counts them. Nobody has counted them for years. It had been two, once, and a joke, and a modest number a man was proud of.
blocks.ko: 아무도 세지 않는다. 여러 해 동안 아무도 세지 않았다. 한때는 둘이었고, 우스개였고, 한 사내가 자랑스러워하던 소박한 수효였다.

en: He’ll reach for us today, like yesterday.
He isn’t here today. / …But the body remembers.

blocks.html: The rock is called the Falling Flowers afterwards, which is a kind way of saying it, and Baekje’s last invention.
blocks.ko: 뒷날 그 바위는 낙화암이라 불린다. 부드럽게 이르는 말이고, 백제가 마지막으로 지어낸 것이다.

blocks.html: Chunchu finally arrives at the scene. He makes Euija pour his wine, and the Tang general’s beside it. Then he settles an old debt. Gumil, the man who opened his daughter’s gate, is put to death.
blocks.ko: 마침내 춘추가 당도한다. 그는 의자에게 제 잔에, 그리고 그 옆 당 장수의 잔에 술을 따르게 한다. 그리고 묵은 빚을 갚는다. 딸의 성문을 열어 준 검일이 목숨을 잃는다.

lines: 내가 너를 잡아들이려고 얼마나 고생했는지 아나?
거의 내 인생을 썼다, 이 자식아.
en: So… you are Euija.
The one who started all of this… Buyeo Euija.
Do you know what it cost me to bring you in?
Nearly my whole life, you bastard.

blocks.html: A cup is put into Euija’s hands, and he is made to pour.
blocks.ko: 의자의 손에 잔이 들려지고, 그는 술을 따르도록 강요당한다.

en: …Do you know what I said to Gesomun, once.
“I do not fear a man who kneels to another man.”

lines: 그 말을 들은 사람이 바로 나였으니까.
en: I know.
I was the man he said it about.
…And so — who is kneeling today?

lines: 너도 언젠가는 누군가 앞에 꿇을 거다.
en: Chunchu…
One day you will kneel before someone too.
Take this man away.

blocks.label: The Pagoda
blocks.ko: 정림사 탑

blocks.html: A month later the Tang carve their victory into a stone pagoda. They put it low, where anyone walking round has to read it. It calls the conquest a deliverance. About Baekje’s king it says:
blocks.ko: 한 달 뒤, 당은 돌탑에 제 승리를 새긴다. 탑을 도는 사람이면 누구든 읽을 수밖에 없는 낮은 자리다. 비문은 정복을 구원이라 부른다. 백제의 임금에 대해서는 이렇게 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 外棄直臣 內信妖婦
blocks.html: Abroad he cast off his upright ministers; at home he trusted a bewitching woman.
blocks.ko: 밖으로는 곧은 신하를 버리고, 안으로는 요사한 여인을 믿었다.
blocks.source: Datang ping Baekje guo beiming (大唐平百濟國碑銘), carved on the five-storey stone pagoda of Jeongnimsa, Buyeo (660)

en: Harmonized.

blocks.html: Then the Tang divide Baekje into five commanderies, with a Tang governor over each and Baekje men under them. Nothing in the arrangement is labelled Silla.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나서 당은 백제를 다섯 도독부로 나누고, 저마다 당의 도독을, 그 아래에 백제 사람들을 앉힌다. 그 배치 어디에도 신라라는 이름표는 없다.

lines: 아버님. 평양 이남과 백제 땅 전부. 그 말들 앞에서 그렇게 말했다고, 아버님이 그러셨잖습니까.
en: Father. Everything south of Pyongyang and the whole of Baekje. He said it in front of the horses. You told me.

lines: 천자의 말이 곧 문서라고도 했다. 붓을 챙겨 갈 걸 그랬어.
en: I did.
He also said an emperor’s word was the writing. I should have brought a brush.

blocks.html: In the Tang lines the Red Fowl’s staff officers are seen pacing out the distance to the Silla camp, which is not a thing allies measure. In the Silla council a man proposes that their soldiers put on Baekje clothes and fall on the Tang by night.
blocks.ko: 당의 진에서 주작의 참모들이 신라 진영까지의 거리를 걸음으로 재는 것이 보인다. 동맹끼리 잴 거리는 아니다. 신라의 군의에서 누군가가, 우리 군사에게 백제 옷을 입혀 밤에 당을 치자고 한다.

lines: 그러나 주인이 발을 밟으면 뭅니다. 개도 그쯤은 압니다.
en: A dog fears its master, Majesty.
But step on its foot and it bites. Even a dog knows that much.

blocks.html: Word of the conversation reaches the Red Fowl’s tent, as it was meant to.
blocks.ko: 그 대화는 의도한 대로 주작의 군막에 전해진다.

blocks.html: A month later the Red Fowl sails home with Euija, his sons and twelve thousand captives. He leaves ten thousand men to hold the city. Beside them sits a Silla army that has stopped smiling.
blocks.ko: 한 달 뒤, 주작은 의자와 그 아들들, 포로 만 이천을 싣고 귀국길에 오른다. 성에는 군사 만 명을 남긴다. 그 곁에는 더는 웃어 주지 않는 신라군이 있다.

blocks.html: Across the sea, a confession is waiting for Euija. It is already written, in a lovely hand. It only needs his name…!
blocks.ko: 바다 건너, 의자 앞으로 자백서 한 장이 기다린다. 고운 글씨로 이미 다 써 두었다. 이름 하나만 비어 있다…!

images.prompt: 2:1 drama power shot, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop. HIGH ANGLE OVER THE SHOULDER of THE THIRD EMPEROR on the throne dais: sharp dark foreground of his shoulder, black futou cap edge and yellow robe, lit warm by a gilt-bronze lamp-tree beside him. Below and far down the hall at true scale, KING EUIJA kneels alone on the polished dark stone floor, head up, glaring at the throne — one plain undyed WHITE robe, barefoot, long grey-streaked hair LOOSE over his shoulders, no headband, no topknot — two Tang guards with halberds a step behind him. Two lines of officials in dark robes and black caps face inward along the aisle between vermilion columns. The hall doors are open behind Euija: HARD COLD BLUE BACKLIGHT floods in around him, his long shadow stretching up the aisle toward the dais, his white robe and loose hair edged with cold light, the only pale shape in the hall. Incense haze makes the door light visible; candles along the columns reflect in the floor. Colour contrast: warm gold dais vs cold blue doorway. No writing. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE ONLY from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png; ignore the portrait's clothing, headgear, jewelry and hair styling — dress exactly as "Now" below (invent a new pose). Now: PRISONER IN THE TANG CAPITAL: broad bearded old king, heavy brows, cynical eyes. One plain undyed WHITE hemp robe and nothing else — no headband, no topknot, no crown, no gold, no crimson, no armor, no belt ornament, barefoot; his long black hair streaked grey hangs LOOSE and unbound past his shoulders; beard unkempt. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | THE THIRD EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gaozong.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8935a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Not a katana, not a tsuba, not a short jian, not a ball pommel. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. images.alt: Crane shot at night over the Tang palace stairs: the old king of Baekje in plain white lies alone on the steps, hair loose, as a line of torch-bearing officials walks away
images.prompt: 2:1 drama crane shot, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop. HIGH CRANE looking steeply down a long flight of stone stairs between white balustrades on the terrace of the attached palace, at night. Halfway down, small, EUIJA lies crumpled on his side — one plain undyed WHITE robe, barefoot, long grey-streaked hair LOOSE and fanned over the stone, no headband — a thin dark red line of blood running down three steps below him. Far up the stairs a procession of Tang officials walks away with torches and silk lanterns, backs turned: their WARM FIRE is the hard backlight, raking down the steps and throwing every balustrade post's long shadow across him. images.alt: Painted: the gilt-bronze Euija on his lotus plinth in a black hall, one candle low at his feet lighting the gold crown flowers from below

The same gilt-bronze King Euija standing on a lotus plinth in a dark museum-like hall: tall gold flower crown with hanging pendants, layered court robe cast in scaled bronze, hands at his sides, the face re-sculpted from the attached portrait — his loud royal grin softened into a proud, tired half-smile. Low three-quarter, the statue large on the left third. A single candle on the plinth step in the sharp foreground is the key, raking up across the gilding so every cast fold, scale and crown leaf stands up in burning gold highlights and falls into umber-black; the hall behind is 80% black with one far small statue dissolving in bokeh. Worn gilt over dark bronze, thick impasto on the brightest gold. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. blocks.html: In the Tang capital, Euija is brought forth before the Third Emperor.
blocks.ko: 당의 도성에서, 의자가 황제 앞에 끌려 나온다.

blocks.html: Eleventh month, first day. The emperor went up to the Zetian Gate tower to receive the Baekje captives, and released them all, from their king Euija down.
blocks.ko: 11월 초하루 무술일, 황제가 칙천문 누각에 나아가 백제의 포로를 받고, 그 왕 의자 이하를 모두 풀어 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 十一月，戊戌朔，上御則天門樓，受百濟俘，自其王義慈以下皆釋之。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 200, Tang Gaozong, Xianqing 5 (660), eleventh month

blocks.html: First day of the eleventh month. The king of Baekje, seized by General Su* and the rest, with Crown Prince Yung and the other princes, thirteen, Great Minister Satek Chunbok, Guk Byeonseong and thirty-seven others, some fifty people in all, were presented at the court hall and hurried before the Son of Heaven. By gracious edict the Son of Heaven released them where they stood.
blocks.ko: 11월 1일, 장군 소정방* 등에게 붙잡힌 백제왕 이하 태자 융 등 왕자 열셋, 대좌평 사택천복과 국변성 이하 서른일곱, 모두 쉰 남짓한 사람을 조당에 바쳤다. 서둘러 끌고 천자 앞으로 나아갔다. 천자가 은혜로운 칙명으로 보는 앞에서 풀어 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 十一月一日，為將軍蘇定方等所捉百濟王以下太子隆等諸王子十三人，大佐平沙宅千福、國辨成以下三十七人，并五十許人。奉進朝堂。急引趍向天子。天子恩敕見前放著。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 26, Saimei 6 (660), seventh month — note quoting the account of Iki no Hakatoko (伊吉連博德書), a Yamato envoy who saw it

notes.html: General Su is Su Dingfang. Chang’an calls him the Red Fowl.
notes.ko: 소 장군은 소정방, 장안이 주작이라 부르는 사람이다.

blocks.html: First, paperwork. A palace clerk hands the prisoner a confession, already written out in a fair hand. There is a space at the bottom for his name.
blocks.ko: 먼저 서류다. 궁의 서기가 포로에게 자백서를 건넨다. 단정한 글씨로 이미 다 써 놓았다. 맨 아래에 이름 쓸 자리만 비어 있다.

blocks.speaker: Tang clerk
en: Aloud, please. Clearly. The scribes are taking it down.
lines: 소리 내어 읽으시오. 또박또박. 사관들이 받아 적고 있소.
zh: 請高聲宣讀，字字清楚。史官在記。
zhLatn: Qǐng gāoshēng xuāndú, zìzì qīngchu. Shǐguān zài jì.

en: ‘I, the criminal Euija, having been liberated by the Great Tang—’
Liberated. Hm. So that’s what that was.
‘—confess with gratitude that without the Great Tang there would be no New Baekje—’
There isn’t one. You burned it.
‘—and resolve to serve the Emperor for ten thousand years.’
Ten thousand? I’m sixty. Ambitious fellow, your clerk.
lines: ‘—대당이 없었다면 새 백제도 없었음을 감사히 자백하며—’
만세? 내가 예순이다. 야심 한번 크구먼, 너희 서기.

en: It’s a bad story. Nobody’s afraid of anything, there’s no villain, and the hero is a building.
Who wrote this? I’ve done better drunk.
lines: 형편없는 이야기다. 겁나는 것도 없고, 악당도 없고, 주인공이 건물이야.
누가 썼냐? 난 취해서도 이보단 잘 썼다.

blocks.speaker: Tang clerk
en: Your name, please. Here.
zhLatn: Qǐng shǔmíng. Zhèlǐ.

blocks.html: He signs in a hand so large the name runs off the edge of the paper, and gives it back. The clerk files it without looking. A confession only needs a name, and has never much minded whose.
blocks.ko: 그는 이름이 종이 끝을 넘어갈 만큼 큼직하게 서명하고 돌려준다. 서기는 보지도 않고 철해 둔다. 자백서에 필요한 건 이름 하나뿐이고, 그게 누구 이름인지는 늘 별로 상관하지 않았다.

blocks.html: Afterwards the emperor asks his general a question in front of the whole court.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤 황제가 온 조정 앞에서 장군에게 묻는다.

lines: 경이 군대를 끌고 거기 있었는데, 어째서 내친김에 신라까지 치지 않았소?
en: You were there with an army. Why didn’t you take Silla while you were at it?
zh: 卿既在彼，何不因而伐新羅？
zhLatn: Qīng jì zài bǐ, hé bù yīn ér fá Xīnluó?

lines: 그 임금은 어질어 백성을 아끼고, 신하들은 충성으로 나라를 섬기며, 아랫사람은 윗사람을 아비와 형처럼 섬깁니다.
작은 나라이나, 꾀로 도모할 수는 없습니다.
en: Their king is kind and loves his people. His ministers serve the country loyally. Below, they serve those above like fathers and elder brothers.
It is a small country, Majesty. But it cannot be schemed against.
zh: 新羅其君仁而愛民，其臣忠以事國，下之人事其上如父兄。
zhLatn: Xīnluó qí jūn rén ér ài mín, qí chén zhōng yǐ shì guó, xià zhī rén shì qí shàng rú fù xiōng.
Suī xiǎo, bù kě móu yě.

en: Kim Chunchu…
KIM CHUNCHU!!!

blocks.html: Across the sea, in Surabol, King Muyeol is eating his supper.
blocks.ko: 바다 건너 서라벌에서, 무열왕이 저녁을 들고 있다.

en: Hm?

lines: 삼한의 땅으로 당을 끌어들이는 이 비랄한 만고의 역적아!!
en: Kim Chunchu, you wretch!!
You vile traitor of the ages, who dragged a foreign power onto the soil of Samhan!!
Heaven’s punishment will find you!!

blocks.html: The shouting burns out. What remains is a man who has finally run out of stories to sell — and one last story he cannot afford to keep.
blocks.ko: 고함이 사그라든다. 남은 것은 팔 이야기가 바닥난 사내 — 그리고 더는 쥐고 있을 수 없는 마지막 이야기 하나.

lines: 김춘추 — 네가 끝낸 것을… 끝내지 못하게…!
en: Let someone… avenge me…!
Let someone… raise Baekje again…!
Chunchu — what you finished… may it never stay finished…!

blocks.html: He is shouting at the man who won. Later men will call it Later Baekje, put a different crown on it, and argue whether the name counts.
blocks.ko: 그는 이긴 사내에게 고함친다. 후대는 후백제라 부르고, 다른 왕관을 얹고, 그 이름이 세는지 다툰다.

en: Heh… so you guys are real after all…
Any last words?

blocks.html: Euija waits. He has always been good at making a room lean in.
blocks.ko: 의자는 기다린다. 그는 언제나 방을 기울게 만드는 데 능했다.

en: No.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times in the Tang capital — Euija. Euija. Euija. — the underworld's receipt before the humiliation finishes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 당의 도읍에서 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 의자. 의자. 의자. — 능욕이 끝나기 전 저승의 영수증처럼.

lines: 백강의 아이. 당신이 준 이름이 아직 명부에 있습니다.
en: Eraha.
The boy at the White River. The name you gave him is still in the ledger.
…A friend.
Put the miracle on the cheap side of the page.
Then you die richer than the record will admit.
Come.

blocks.html: Euija dies, vengeful and emptied. His life flashes before his eyes.
blocks.ko: 의자는 원한을 남긴 채, 비워진 채 죽는다. 삶이 눈앞을 스친다.

blocks.html: He was the bright prince once. Then the conqueror. Now he is a man in his enemy’s capital with nothing left to command.
blocks.ko: 한때 그는 빛나는 왕자였다. 그다음엔 정복자였다. 이제 그는 적의 도성에서, 부릴 것 하나 남지 않은 사내다.

blocks.html: He pleads for someone, maybe in future generations, to finally avenge him.
blocks.ko: 그는 누군가가 — 훗날의 어느 세대가 — 자기 대신 복수해 주기를 빈다.

blocks.html: Somewhere far down the years, a stranger is already reaching for his banner.
blocks.ko: 아득한 세월 저편에서, 누군가 벌써 그의 깃발에 손을 뻗고 있다.

blocks.html: Thus was the end of Buyeo Euija.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 부여의자의 생은 끝났다.

blocks.html: A man the court once called the Zengzi of the East.
blocks.ko: 한때 조정이 «해동증자»라 부르던 사내였다.

blocks.html: Euija served his parents with a devotion people talked about, and was kind to his brothers; men of his time called him the Zeng and Min of the East. He reached the capital and died a few days later.
blocks.ko: 의자는 어버이를 효성으로 섬겨 이름이 났고 형제와 우애하니, 당시 사람들이 ‘해동의 증자·민자’라 불렀다. 경사에 이르러 며칠 만에 죽었다.
blocks.hanja: 義慈事親以孝行聞，友于兄弟，時人號「海東曾、閔」。及至京，數日而卒。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199A, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje

blocks.html: — Buyeo Euija —
blocks.ko: — 부여의자 —

blocks.html: He was right about everything, which is the particular cruelty of his case. A country is a story. He said so at forty-one, in a courtyard, to a boy he had named himself.
blocks.ko: 그는 모든 것에 대해 옳았다. 그 점이 그의 경우에 유독 잔인하다. 나라는 과연 하나의 이야기다. 그는 마흔한 살에 마당에서, 제가 이름 지어 준 아이에게 그렇게 말했다.

blocks.html: And then he learned the rest of it, which he had not thought about: that a story does not care who is telling it. That the moment you make yourself its author you have also made yourself a character in it, and characters can be revised.
blocks.ko: 그리고 그는 미처 생각하지 못한 나머지를 배웠다. 이야기는 누가 그것을 말하고 있는지 개의치 않는다는 것을. 스스로 그 이야기의 저자가 되는 순간, 자신도 그 안의 인물이 된다는 것을. 그리고 인물은 고쳐 쓰일 수 있다는 것을.

blocks.html: He broke the eight clans because they were strangling the throne, and he was correct. He seated his own sons instead, and was correct again — and then found himself alone in a room where every voice agreed with him — a room that had stopped being a court some years earlier, and become a mirror.
blocks.ko: 그는 여덟 가문이 왕좌의 목을 조르고 있었기에 그들을 꺾었고, 그것은 옳았다. 그 자리에 제 아들들을 앉혔고, 그것 또한 옳았다 — 그러고는 모든 목소리가 자신에게 동의하는 방 안에 홀로 남았다. 그 방은 이미 몇 해 전에 조정이기를 그만두고, 거울이 되어 있었다.

blocks.html: Seongchung told him. He put Seongchung in a cell. Heungsu told him. He had already exiled Heungsu. Gyebek would have told him, and he had put Gyebek on a boat. A man does not fall because nobody warned him. He falls because he arranged, patiently and over years, to be somewhere the warnings could not reach.
blocks.ko: 성충이 말했다. 그는 성충을 옥에 가두었다. 흥수가 말했다. 그는 이미 흥수를 내쫓은 뒤였다. 계백이라면 말했을 것이다. 그리고 그는 계백을 배에 태워 보냈다. 사람은 아무도 경고하지 않아서 무너지지 않는다. 여러 해에 걸쳐 참을성 있게, 경고가 닿을 수 없는 곳에 제 자리를 마련해 두었기 때문에 무너진다.

blocks.html: The Zengzi of the East. They called him that when he was young, and they meant it. The name was neither flattery nor wrong. He was never a fool. He was a clever man who won, and kept winning, until winning was the only instrument he had left, and then he tried to play a dying country on it.
blocks.ko: 해동증자. 젊은 시절 사람들은 그를 그렇게 불렀고, 진심이었다. 아첨도 아니고 틀린 말도 아니었다. 그는 결코 어리석지 않았다. 그는 이기고 또 이긴 영리한 사람이었고, 마침내 이기는 것 말고는 남은 악기가 없어졌을 때, 죽어 가는 나라를 그것으로 연주하려 했다.

blocks.html: He asked, at the end, for someone to avenge him. Two hundred and forty years later a man called Kyun Hwon raised his banner and used his name and lost as well. The story went on without either of them. It always does.
blocks.ko: 그는 마지막에 자기를 위해 복수해 줄 사람을 구했다. 이백사십 년 뒤 견훤이라는 사내가 그의 깃발을 들고 그의 이름을 쓰고, 또한 졌다. 이야기는 둘 중 누구도 없이 계속되었다. 언제나 그렇듯이.

blocks.html: Baekje is gone. Goguryeo still stands. And the man who arranged both can no longer get out of bed…?
blocks.ko: 백제는 사라졌다. 고구려는 아직 서 있다. 그리고 그 둘을 꾸민 사내가, 더는 자리에서 일어나지 못한다…?

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior late night, a quiet temple side hall at the edge of Surabol. Low WORM'S-EYE from the floor at the foot of the sick-mat. ONE device: a single thread of incense smoke rising straight up from a bronze burner on the floor. Munhee, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, fifty-five, hair dressed with the attached binyeo, sitting very upright beside the mat, one hand resting on the blanket over his hand, eyes on him, dry-eyed and steely. King Muyeol (Chunchu), FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, lying under the blanket, head turned toward her, a faint tired smile; his crown rests on a stand in the shadow. A clay lamp on the floor rakes gold up across her face and the folds; magenta #D8258C as a small specular on his silk collar. Background: a dim gilt Buddha barely readable in the dark. CANON — QUEEN MUNMYUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmyung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_munhee.png when the head is visible. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Yushin's younger sister, Chunchu's wife; quick and warm, the one who bought the dream. #E07FA8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: fantasy tiara instead of her binyeo. | KING MUYEOL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_muyeol.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Now: King Muyeol (stage portrait): royal robes and crown; heavier, tired eyes. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: They take him first to a Buddhist temple on the edge of Surabol — not for miracle, for quiet. Incense. Stone. A monk who knows when not to speak. Munhee sits where wives of True Bone have always sat when history arrives as a fever.
blocks.ko: 먼저 서라벌 가장자리 절로 옮긴다 — 기적이 아니라 고요를 위해. 향. 돌. 말없이 있을 때를 아는 스님. 문희는 진골의 아내들이 역사가 열병으로 올 때 항상 앉던 자리에 앉는다.

en: You reinvented a kingdom in a side hall.
Leave me the hours. I invent endings.
lines: 시간은 내게 남겨. 끝은 내가 발명할게.

blocks.html: It is the sixth month of 661. Baekje has fallen, Goguryeo has not, and the man who arranged both is fifty-eight and cannot get out of bed.
blocks.ko: 661년 유월이다. 백제는 무너졌고 고구려는 아직 서 있으며, 그 둘을 모두 꾸민 사내는 쉰여덟에 자리에서 일어나지 못한다.

blocks.html: Munhee (55) sits where she has sat since the spring. She has buried a sister who was a queen and a brother’s youth and a daughter she never got back, and she is still here — until their son comes and stands at the foot of the bed, already wearing a king’s silence he has not yet been allowed to begin.
blocks.ko: 문희 (55)는 봄부터 앉아 온 자리에 앉아 있다. 여왕이었던 언니를 묻었고, 오라비의 젊음을 묻었고, 끝내 돌려받지 못한 딸을 묻었다. 그러고도 여전히 여기 있다 — 아들이 들어와 침대 맡에 서기 전까지. 아직 시작도 허락받지 못한 왕의 침묵을, 벌써 입고 있는 아들.

en: Munhee. Have I… paid all of it?
Not yet. I’ll pay the rest.

blocks.html: He looks past her, to the boy who is no longer a boy. Bupmin (35) has his mother’s stillness and his father’s hunger, and for a moment the room holds all three of them the way a hill once held a promise.
blocks.ko: 그는 문희 너머로, 더 이상 아이가 아닌 아이를 본다. 법민 (35)에게는 어머니의 고요와 아버지의 허기가 있다. 잠시, 방이 예전 언덕이 약속을 품듯 셋 모두를 품는다.

en: Bupmin.
Father.

lines: 사람들은… 이 전쟁이 오직 네 누나를 위한 줄 알 거다.
그것도 맞다. 대야는 하루도 이 방을 나간 적이 없다.
en: People will say… this whole war was only for your sister.
Gotaso.
And they will not be wrong. Daeya never left this room for a single day.

lines: 네가 어릴 때 하던 말. 입에도 아직 안 맞는 입으로.
en: But that was never the only bill I was paying.
What you used to say when you were small. When the word still sat wrong in your mouth.
“A king for all.”
Not a king of Silla. Of everyone.
That was… your dream first, Father.
On the hill, with Uncle—

lines: 아이는 그렇게 훔친다. 제일 큰 것을.
나는 백제까지 길을 닦아 두었다. 고구려는 아직 서 있고, 당은 웃는 얼굴을 하고 있을 거다.
복수로 걷지 말고. 네가 여섯 살에 원했던 나라로.
en: I said it first. You took it.
That is how children steal. They take the largest thing in the room.
I cleared the road as far as Baekje. Goguryeo is still standing, and the Tang will be smiling.
The rest — walk it as king.
Not as my revenge. As the country you wanted when you were six.
…I promise.
Bupmin… I love you.

blocks.html: The escort arrives on schedule.
blocks.ko: 호위가 시간에 맞춰 도착한다.

blocks.html: He reads the king's name three times — Muyeol. Muyeol. Muyeol. — though the room still knows him as Chunchu.
blocks.ko: 그는 임금의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 무열. 무열. 무열. — 방은 여전히 그를 춘추로 알고 있어도.

blocks.html: He goes quiet between the two names. The room still knows him as Chunchu. The ledger has already written Muyeol.
blocks.ko: 두 이름 사이에서 그가 고요해진다. 방은 여전히 그를 춘추로 안다. 명부에는 이미 무열이 적혀 있다.

en: King Muyeol.
We have met before — in your daughter’s eyes, if not in yours.
Your son is packing. The West is already in the hall.
lines: 우리는 만난 적 있습니다 — 당신 눈이 아니라 따님의 눈에서.
아들은 짐을 싸고 있습니다. 서쪽은 이미 전각 안에 있습니다.

en: …I know.
I saw a room where they all absolutely obeyed one man — no matter what.
I never un-saw it. Tell Bupmin the packing list is his.
lines: 한 사람에게 — 무슨 일이 있어도 — 모두가 절대 복종하는 방을 보았소.
그걸 언-보지는 못했소. 법민에게 전하게. 짐 목록은 이제 그의 것이오.

en: I am… just going to keep walking west.
The ledger does not moralize — His Majesty only asks whether you knew. You knew.
Walk, Spring-and-Autumn. The underworld kingdom has a seat that keeps better silence than Chang’an.
lines: 명부는 도덕을 논하지 않습니다 — 폐하께서는 알았는지만 물으십니다. 당신은 알았습니다.
걸으시지요, 춘추. 저승 나라엔 장안보다 침묵을 잘 지키는 자리가 있습니다.

blocks.html: King Muyeol (58) dies.
blocks.ko: 무열왕 (58)이 승하한다.

blocks.html: Twelve years earlier an emperor had told him that Goguryeo was the one failure of his life, and that Baekje would be Chunchu’s. Only one of them was wrong.
blocks.ko: 십이 년 전, 한 황제가 그에게 고려는 제 인생의 유일한 실패이며 백제는 그대의 실패가 될 것이라 했다. 둘 중 한 사람만 틀렸다.

blocks.html: They give him a name for the dead: Muyeol. His temple name borrows the Second Emperor’s two characters. He was the first True Bone king ever crowned. He will be the last man anyone calls a diplomat.
blocks.ko: 그에게 죽은 자의 이름이 붙는다. 무열. 묘호는 이세 황제의 두 글자를 빌렸다. 진골로서 처음 왕관을 쓴 사람이다. 그리고 누군가 외교관이라 부를 마지막 사람이다.

blocks.html: — Kim Chunchu —
blocks.ko: — 김춘추 —

blocks.html: He was a boy on a hill who wanted one country and no more borders, and he got half of it, and left the rest in his son’s mouth — the same words, stolen honestly, when the boy was still small enough to believe a king could be for everyone.
blocks.ko: 그는 하나의 나라와 사라진 국경을 바라던 언덕 위의 소년이었고, 절반을 얻었으며, 나머지를 아들의 입에 남겨 두었다 — 같은 말, 정직하게 훔친 말. 그 아이가 아직 임금이 모두를 위한 것일 수 있다고 믿던 입으로.

blocks.html: First the politics, which he gave up for a wife and three children. Then the wife and the children, one of whom was taken from him at Daeya, which gave the politics back to him with interest. He did not choose the second time. That is what people never understand about him.
blocks.ko: 먼저 정치를 내놓았다. 아내와 세 아이를 위해. 그다음엔 그 아내와 아이들을 내놓았다. 그중 하나를 대야성에서 빼앗겼고, 그것이 정치를 이자까지 붙여 그에게 돌려주었다. 두 번째는 그가 고른 것이 아니었다. 사람들이 그에 대해 끝내 이해하지 못하는 지점이 그것이다.

blocks.html: He knelt to Gesomun, who despised him for it. He knelt to an emperor, who liked him for it and kept his son. Euija said he did not fear a man who kneels. Euija was wrong. It took eighteen years and a cup of wine to show him.
blocks.ko: 그는 연개소문에게 무릎을 꿇었고, 개소문은 그 때문에 그를 경멸했다. 황제에게 무릎을 꿇었고, 황제는 그 때문에 그를 아꼈고, 아들을 붙잡아 두었다. 의자는 무릎 꿇는 사내 따윈 두렵지 않다고 했다. 의자가 틀렸다. 그걸 보여 주는 데 열여덟 해와 술 한 잔이 들었다.

blocks.html: The charge against him is that he brought a foreign army onto Samhan soil, and the charge is true. He knew it while he was doing it. He did it anyway, and spent the rest of his life teaching his son how to get them out again.
blocks.ko: 그를 향한 죄목은 삼한의 땅으로 외세를 끌어들였다는 것이고, 그 죄목은 사실이다. 그는 그렇게 하는 동안에도 알고 있었다. 그래도 했고, 남은 평생을 아들에게 그들을 다시 몰아내는 법을 가르치며 보냈다.

blocks.html: He died with Baekje gone and Goguryeo still standing. Halfway. The last two names he said were his daughter’s and his son’s. Not the kingdom’s.
blocks.ko: 그는 백제가 사라지고 고구려는 아직 서 있는 채로 죽었다. 절반에서. 그가 마지막으로 부른 두 이름은 딸의 이름과 아들의 이름이었다. 나라의 이름이 아니었다.

blocks.html: Bupmin takes the throne. They will call him Munmu. He vows to finish it, for the country a six-year-old once named out loud.
blocks.ko: 법민이 왕위에 오른다. 사람들은 그를 문무라 부를 것이다. 그는 끝을 보겠다고 맹세한다. 여섯 살짜리가 언젠가 소리 내어 이름 붙였던 그 나라를 위해.

blocks.hanja: 文武王立 諱法敏 太宗王之元子
blocks.ko: 문무왕이 서니, 휘는 법민*이요, 태종왕†의 맏아들이다.
blocks.html: King Munmu was set up. His taboo-name was Beopmin*; he was the eldest son of King Taejong†.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, accession (661); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 140

notes.html: Beopmin is Bupmin, spelled the other way.
notes.ko: 영어 표기만 다를 뿐, 이 책의 법민이다.

notes.html: King Taejong is Chunchu, by the temple name Silla gave him. It is the same name Tang gave the Second Emperor, and Tang will notice.
notes.ko: 태종왕은 춘추다. 신라가 붙인 묘호인데, 당 태종과 같은 이름이라 당이 그냥 넘어가지 않는다.

blocks.html: Silla won the war. So why does the emperor’s new edict call its king a clerk…?
blocks.ko: 전쟁은 신라가 이겼다. 그런데 황제의 새 칙서는 왜 신라 왕을 고을 원님으로 적는가…?
