images.at: launches the Eighth Invasion of Goguryeo
images.alt: Ink-painted poster: the Third Emperor, in grey ink wash, points east from a palace terrace as the gold dragon spirals up out of a black ink storm
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; heads and the dragon’s head stay inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Storm dusk on a high terrace of the Daming Palace: balustrades and owl-tail roof ridges as black calligraphic strokes, a sky of splashed black ink. Worm’s-eye from the terrace floor. TWO SUBJECTS: a human-scale emperor AND a huge dragon. INTERACTION: the Third Emperor, young and uncertain, stands at the balustrade with his arm thrown out pointing east; the gold Tang dragon Huanglong (gold ink-brush dragon from the attached board, three claws) spirals up past him into the black storm, its body curling once loosely around his outstretched arm before it uncoils skyward, its head turned east along his pointing hand. One gold break in the storm (#b8935a) catches his face, his arm and the dragon’s coils. TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) on rice paper — heavy black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding, splashed ink smoke and storm, dry calligraphic brush strokes for roofs, columns, robes and cloud, ink splatters and drips at the frame edges, bare paper only where the edges dissolve; the gold ink-brush dragon is the main colour in the dark, with a few small vermilion and flame accents. Every figure, the Third Emperor included, is ink-painted in the same black-and-grey wash with only a thin wash of dull yellow on his robe; no full-colour figure in the frame. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, big dark masses, one bright break of light, NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp, no calligraphy characters. Not photoreal, not 3D, not a realistic scaled dragon. No glow aura, no halo — the accent is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — THE THIRD EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gaozong.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8935a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | HUANGLONG (황룡, taizong's yellow dragon, guardian of the Tang throne) — attached board /obj_yellow_dragon.png: TANG-DYNASTY dragon painted in gold ink-brush: lean long-necked serpentine body in an S-curve, four lean leonine legs striding, THREE claws on each foot, long open-jawed snout with fangs, two backswept horns, whiskers and mane flung out as dry calligraphic gold brush strokes, whip tail ending in a flame tuft; burnished gold-yellow scales with ochre-umber shading — match the board, not a later Ming/Qing five-claw dragon, never a realistic scaled 3D dragon. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, coiling through black ink cloud and lamp smoke; light catches the scales as real light, never a glow outline. Its stills are predominantly dark and intimidating Chinese ink painting: splashed black ink, smoke, the gold dragon the main colour in the dark; every figure is ink-painted except the Second Emperor, who stays a full-colour webtoon figure. Owned by no one but sits behind whoever holds the dais; it coils over Chang'an and turns its head only for the Son of Heaven. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) — black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding into rice paper, dry calligraphic brush for roofs, columns, smoke and robes, the vermilion and gold reduced to small accents in a world of ink; officials, guards and other Tang figures are ink figures too. The ONE exception is the Second Emperor himself: he keeps the house webtoon figure render in full colour (yellow robe, black futou, drawn face), a coloured man inside an ink empire. Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: Five Commanderies
blocks.ko: 다섯 도독부

blocks.html: When the capital fell, the Tang threw five commanderies over the country like a net over a pond. The biggest knot sits at Bear Fortress, where Euija was handed over. So far the net catches mostly rebels.
blocks.ko: 도성이 떨어지자 당은 연못에 그물을 덮듯 나라 위에 도독부 다섯을 씌웠다. 가장 큰 매듭은 의자가 넘겨진 웅진성에 있다. 아직까지 그 그물에 걸리는 건 대개 반란군이다.

blocks.html: Its land was then divided into five area commands, Ungjin and the rest, each governing its prefectures and counties, and its own chieftains were set up as commanders, prefects and magistrates.
blocks.ko: 이에 그 땅을 나누어 웅진 … 등 다섯 도독부를 두고 각기 주와 현을 거느리게 하였으며, 그 우두머리들을 세워 도독·자사·현령으로 삼았다.
blocks.hanja: 至是乃以其地分置熊津…等五都督府，各統州縣，立其酋渠爲都督、刺史及縣令。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199A, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje

blocks.label: The Black Tortoise
blocks.ko: 현무

blocks.html: That spring a new man takes over the Tang garrison. Nobody in Chang’an expected to see him in uniform again. Liu Rengui is sixty. Last year he lost a grain fleet in a storm and was stripped of office. Now he comes east as a commoner in white, to earn it back. In his baggage: the Tang calendar, and the list of names nobody may write.
blocks.ko: 그해 봄, 새 사람이 당의 주둔군을 맡는다. 장안의 누구도 그가 다시 군복을 입을 줄 몰랐다. 유인궤는 예순이다. 지난해 풍랑에 군량선을 잃고 관직을 빼앗겼다. 이제 백의종군으로 죄를 씻으러 동쪽에 왔다. 짐 속에는 당의 역서와, 아무도 써서는 안 될 이름들의 목록이 들어 있다.

blocks.caption: The Black Tortoise. Sixty, disgraced last year, and in an excellent mood.
blocks.ko: 현무. 예순, 작년에 파직당했고, 기분이 아주 좋다.

lines: 하늘이 이 늙은이를 부귀하게 하시려나 보오.
이 나라에 쓸 역서를 보내 주시오. 써서는 안 될 이름 목록도. 동쪽을 쓸어 평정할 거라면, 동쪽도 적어도 지금이 몇 년인지는 알아야지.
en: Heaven means to make an old man rich, it seems.
Send me the calendar for this country, and the list of names one must not write. If we are going to sweep the east clean, the east should at least know what year it is.
zh: 請頒曆及宗廟諱。吾欲掃平東夷，頒大唐正朔於海表。
zhLatn: Tiān jiāng fùguì cǐ wēng ěr.
Qǐng bān lì jí zōngmiào huì. Wú yù sǎopíng dōngyí, bān Dà Táng zhēngshuò yú hǎibiǎo.

blocks.html: The rebels come and go like weather, and between storms the Black Tortoise does what he actually came for, which is paperwork. He counts the households of Baekje village by village and writes them down as numbers. He mends dykes and bridges. He posts the Tang calendar at every crossroads, with the list of names that may not be written, so that the people of Baekje will know which characters to leave out of their letters home.
blocks.ko: 반란군은 날씨처럼 왔다 가고, 폭풍과 폭풍 사이에 현무는 그가 정말로 하러 온 일, 곧 서류를 한다. 그는 백제의 호구를 마을마다 세어 숫자로 적는다. 둑과 다리를 고친다. 네거리마다 당의 역서를 붙이고, 써서는 안 될 이름 목록도 함께 붙인다. 백제 사람들이 고향에 보내는 편지에서 어느 글자를 빼야 하는지 알도록.

lines: 올해가 몇 년인지 아는 마을은 세금을 제때 내오.
나루에도 하나 붙이시오. 사람은 배를 기다리면서 읽으니까.
en: A village that knows what year it is pays its tax on time.
Put one up at the ferry as well. People read while they wait for the boat.
zh: 渡口也貼一張。人等船時會讀。
zhLatn: Zhī niánsuì zhī cūn, nàshuì bú wù.
Dùkǒu yě tiē yì zhāng. Rén děng chuán shí huì dú.

blocks.label: Gyerim
blocks.ko: 계림

blocks.html: Then an edict arrives for the new king. It makes him Grand Commander of the Gyerim Prefecture. Gyerim is his country’s oldest name, the wood where a rooster crowed over a golden box. In the edict it is one province of the empire. And the king is its governor.
blocks.ko: 이윽고 새 임금 앞으로 칙서가 온다. 그를 계림주 대도독으로 삼는다는 내용이다. 계림은 이 나라의 가장 오래된 이름이다. 닭이 금궤 위에서 울던 숲. 칙서 안에서 그곳은 제국의 한 고을이다. 그리고 임금은 그 고을 원이다.

lines: 주라 하오, 외숙. 아버님의 나라를 주로 만들고, 나를 그 고을 원으로 삼았소.
en: A prefecture, Uncle. They have made my father’s country into a prefecture, and me its clerk.
Then sign as its clerk, Majesty.
And keep a copy.

blocks.html: The court is angrier than the king. Men in the Council hall who have not agreed on anything since the old queen died agree that a prefecture is an insult, and say so loudly, in rooms where no Tang officer is present.
blocks.ko: 조정은 왕보다 더 화가 났다. 옛 여왕이 죽은 뒤로 무엇 하나 합의해 본 적 없는 회의장의 사내들이, 주라니 모욕이라는 데에는 뜻을 모은다. 그리고 당의 관리가 없는 방에서 큰 소리로 그렇게 말한다.

lines: 그쪽 역법 보셨어요? 하루하루가 딱딱 맞아떨어집니다. 우리 책력은 동지가 언제인지도 저 혼자 우기는데.
en: They’re not wrong about everything, you know.
Have you seen their calendar? Every day accounted for. Our almanac can’t even agree with itself about the solstice.

blocks.html: Nobody answers him. A few men remember afterwards that he said it.
blocks.ko: 아무도 대꾸하지 않는다. 몇몇은 뒷날 그가 그 말을 했다는 것을 기억해 낸다.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

blocks.html: In Chang’an the Third Emperor is told that Baekje is finished and that its king has died in the capital of a broken heart, and he takes out his father’s maps.
blocks.ko: 장안에서 세 번째 황제는 백제가 끝났고 그 왕이 도성에서 상심하여 죽었다는 말을 듣는다. 그리고 아버지의 지도를 꺼낸다.

lines: 아버님은 동쪽에 세 번 가셨다가 기침을 하며 돌아오셨지.
백제는 고구려 등 뒤의 칼이었고, 이제 그 칼을 우리가 쥐었어 — 아니. 이건 아버님이 하실 말 같군. 그래도 적어 두게.
en: Father went east three times and came home coughing.
Baekje was the knife at Goguryeo’s back, and now we’re holding it — no. That sounds like something he would say. Write it down anyway.

lines: 장수 넷이요. 지도 네 귀퉁이에 하나씩. 그래야 아무도 혼자 했다고 우기며 돌아오지 못하죠.
en: Then don’t say it like him. Say it like you.
Four generals. One for each side of the map, so none of them can come home claiming he did it alone.

blocks.html: That is how the Four Beasts are chosen: by a woman who knows how generals talk at banquets.
blocks.ko: 사신(四神)은 그렇게 뽑힌다. 장수들이 잔치에서 무슨 말을 하는지 아는 여자에 의해.

blocks.label: The Four Beasts
blocks.ko: 사신

blocks.html: The Third Emperor launches the Eighth Invasion of Goguryeo — his father’s war, inherited along with everything else.
blocks.ko: 황제가 제8차 고구려 원정을 일으킨다. 다른 모든 것과 함께 물려받은, 아버지의 전쟁이다.

blocks.title: Four Beasts · 사신
blocks.caption: Gaozong’s expeditionary colours: White Tiger, Red Fowl, Blue Dragon, Black Tortoise.
blocks.ko: 고종의 동정 색깔. 백호, 주작, 청룡, 현무.

blocks.title: Four Dragons · 사룡
blocks.caption: Taizong’s older roster — the grammar the son inherited with the war.
blocks.ko: 태종의 옛 명부 — 아들이 전쟁과 함께 물려받은 문법.

blocks.html: Samhan never learns their names. It learns their banners, which is the entire purpose of a banner.
blocks.ko: 삼한은 끝내 그들의 이름을 배우지 않는다. 깃발을 배운다. 깃발이란 원래 그러라고 있는 것이다.

lines: 짐이 이미 백제를 멸하여 너희 나라의 근심을 제거하였는데, 이제 고려가 지리의 험함을 믿고 예맥(穢貊)과 함께 악한 짓을 하여 큰 나라를 섬기는 예를 어기고 이웃 나라와 사이좋게 지내는 의리를 저버리고 있다. 짐은 병사를 보내어 치려고 하니, 너도 돌아가 너희 국왕에게 고하여 군대를 출동시켜 우리와 함께 망해가는 오랑캐를 섬멸케 하라.
en: I have already destroyed Baekje and removed your country’s worry; yet now Goryeo trusts in the ruggedness of its land, joins the Yemaek in wickedness, breaks the rite of serving a great state, and abandons the duty of living peaceably with its neighbours. I am sending soldiers to strike it — so return and tell your king to send out his army, and with us annihilate these failing barbarians.
zh: 朕已滅百濟，除爾國之憂；而高麗恃險，連穢貊為惡，失事大之禮，棄睦鄰之義。朕將發兵討之——歸告爾王出師，與我共滅此將亡之蠻夷。
zhLatn: Zhèn yǐ miè Bǎijì, chú ěr guó zhī yōu; ér Gāolí shì xiǎn, lián Huìmò wéi è, shī shì dà zhī lǐ, qì mùlín zhī yì. Zhèn jiāng fābīng tǎo zhī——guī gào ěr wáng chūshī, yǔ wǒ gòng miè cǐ jiāng wáng zhī mányí.

blocks.html: Baekje has no king. Across the sea, an exiled prince is packing his bags…!
blocks.ko: 백제에는 임금이 없다. 바다 건너, 쫓겨난 왕자 하나가 짐을 꾸린다…!

images.alt: La Tour’s candle: a Baekje envoy holds the Seven-Branched Sword upright before his closed eyes, gold inlay glittering
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Georges de La Tour’s candlelit devotion. Close three-quarter in a black room: a Baekje envoy in dark court silk and a black gauze cap holds the Seven-Branched Sword upright in both hands before his face, eyes closed. The relic: a straight iron central blade with three short curved branches alternating up each side, six branches in all, a column of gold-inlaid characters down the centre (illegible glints, no readable text). One candle on the table below is the only light: it lights his face and fingers from beneath and makes every branch and the gold inlay glitter; the room is black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. images.alt: The third pose: Pung alone finally nails it while the others sit around on the rice and the rocks
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE hero print: a Meiji musha-e warrior print in the manner of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi’s “Mirror of Famous Generals” and Utagawa Kuniyoshi, crossed with Korean minhwa colour and re-painted in the house watercolor-and-oil — bold calligraphic ink contours, flat saturated colour blocks, patterned textures (snow stipple, fur strokes, claw waves, petal and ember scatter), a violent diagonal composition that fills the frame edge to edge, the hero in an extreme dynamic pose; then painted over with granulated watercolour washes, paper grain and oil-glazed darks so it reads as a painting, not a flat print. Faces stay clean webtoon ink line matching the attached portrait. One accent colour per hero. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. NO text cartouches, NO title boxes, NO calligraphy, NO seals, NO lettering of any kind. The shingle below Juryu in the last red light. King Pungjang alone in the centre of the frame in a perfect, heroic, full-body pose at last, arms and legs flung out like a hero print, robe flaring, crown gleaming, triumphant; around him the others have already stopped and sit about: the stocky lord in the gilt cap sitting on a pile of rice bales eating, the shaven monk in red kasaya cross-legged with beads, the seven-foot general leaning on his spear looking away, the huge bearded admiral lying back laughing, the young Yamato captain alone politely applauding, the bald general with the topknot tail facepalming with the tally board. Low wide. Radial ink rays converging on the king. Comic and a little sad. Topknots, no brimmed hats. CANON — KING PUNGJANG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_pungjang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Prince years: smooth beardless face, soft eyes, black hair in a topknot bound with a red-and-gold cord and a gold pin. Dress: Red robe with black sleeves striped in gold, gold-brocade crossed collar, braided red-and-gold cord sash. Crown: Baekje king, as the attached crown (ignore its studio backdrop and logo): a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls; the king’s red robe and wide-sleeved layers as the Baekje king on the costume chart. Now: King Pungjang (stage portrait): sharper face, a small chin goatee, loose strands falling from the topknot; red king's robe with dark-navy-lined sleeves, gold-scroll shoulders and a long gold cord sash. Demeanor: Formal, slightly foreign-accented royal speech, brittle when contradicted; raised in Yamato, crowned by the general he beheaded. #e6c76a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Tang dress. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. blocks.html: A Baekje king sends the King of Wa a sword with seven branches. It is a gift. It is also a message.
blocks.ko: 백제의 임금이 왜왕에게 가지가 일곱 달린 칼을 보낸다. 선물이다. 전갈이기도 하다.

blocks.html: Baekje–Wa relations continue to flourish and Wang In spreads western literature to the Yamato kingdom.
blocks.ko: 백제와 왜의 교류는 더욱 깊어지고, 왕인이 왜국에 한학을 전한다.

lines: 先世以來未有此刀百濟王世─奇生聖音故爲倭王旨造傳示後世
선세 이래 이런 칼은 없었다. 백제왕이 세세토록 특별히(각별히) 성음(聖音)을 내었기에 왜왕을 위하여 훌륭하게 만들었다. 후세에 전하여 보이도록 하라.

blocks.html: It is iron, two and a half feet long, with six branches off a central blade and sixty-one characters inlaid in gold down both sides. It has never been sharpened. It was never going to be.
blocks.ko: 쇠로 되어 있고 길이는 두 자 반, 가운데 몸통에서 가지 여섯이 뻗어 나오며, 앞뒤로 금상감한 글자 예순한 자가 있다. 한 번도 날을 세운 적이 없다. 애초에 세울 물건이 아니었다.

blocks.html: The inscription is the interesting part, because the two countries have spent fifteen hundred years disagreeing about a single verb: whether Baekje presented it upward, or bestowed it downward.
blocks.ko: 흥미로운 것은 명문이다. 두 나라가 천오백 년 동안 동사 하나를 두고 다투어 왔기 때문이다. 백제가 그것을 위로 바친 것인지, 아래로 내린 것인지.

en: Which is it?

lines: 그건 읽는 사람이 어느 나라 사람이냐에 달렸지.
en: That depends on which country is doing the reading.

blocks.html: What is not in dispute: Baekje sent scholars, craftsmen, weavers, horse-handlers, potters and the written word across that water for three hundred years, and when Baekje finally needed ships, the East sent forty-two thousand men to die in a river for it.
blocks.ko: 다투지 않는 사실은 이렇다. 백제는 삼백 년 동안 그 바다 건너로 학자와 장인과 직공과 말 다루는 이와 옹기장이와 글자를 보냈다. 그리고 마침내 백제에 배가 필요해졌을 때, 동토는 사만이천 명을 보내 강에서 죽게 했다.

blocks.html: Whichever verb it was, it was paid.
blocks.ko: 어느 쪽 동사였든, 값은 치러졌다.

blocks.html: Gwishil Boksin sends to Yamato the East with a hundred Tang prisoners as a present, and asks for two things: an army, and Prince Pung, who has lived there for twenty years.
blocks.ko: 귀실복신이 당나라 포로 백여 명을 선물로 딸려 왜국에 사람을 보내 두 가지를 청한다. 원병, 그리고 스무 해를 그곳에서 산 부여풍.

blocks.caption: Gwishil Boksin. He raised a dead country once, and he kept the receipts.
blocks.ko: 귀실복신. 쓰러진 나라를 한 번 일으켰고, 영수증은 다 챙겨 두었다.

blocks.title: Restoration Army · 백제부흥군
blocks.caption: King at the apex and four founding generals beneath — five captains, one lost country.
blocks.ko: 왕 아래 네 장군 — 부흥군 오장, 나라 하나.

blocks.html: Asuka, the tenth month. The Baekje envoy has come the whole way with frost in his beard and a hundred Tang soldiers roped neck to neck behind him, a present, which is a polite word for proof. The empress is sixty-six. She has buried two husbands, held this throne twice and sat through a great many envoys, and she lets this one finish.
blocks.ko: 아스카, 시월. 백제 사신은 수염에 서리를 얹은 채 먼 길을 왔고, 그 뒤로 당나라 병사 백 명이 목과 목을 밧줄로 엮인 채 서 있다. 선물이다. 증거를 점잖게 부르는 말이다. 여제는 예순여섯이다. 남편 둘을 묻었고, 이 자리에 두 번 올랐고, 사신이라면 질리도록 받아 보았다. 그녀는 이 사신이 말을 끝낼 때까지 둔다.

blocks.html: The court across the cold sea, where favours are counted in ships.
blocks.ko: 차가운 바다 건너의 궁정. 은혜는 배로 센다.

blocks.caption: The Eastern Prince. He does the arithmetic before anyone asks for it.
blocks.ko: 동쪽의 왕자. 누가 묻기 전에 셈부터 한다.

lines: …그건 첫 장일 뿐이고요. 나머지 셈은 언제 내놓는답니까?
en: A hundred prisoners. Generous.
…That’s the first page, though. When do they show us the rest of the bill?
ja: 捕虜百人とは。気前のよいことだ。
……それは一枚目にすぎぬ。残りの勘定はいつ出てくる。
jaLatn: Horyo hyakunin to wa. Kimae no yoi koto da.
…Sore wa ichimaime ni suginu. Nokori no kanjō wa itsu dete kuru.

blocks.html: The envoy tells him. Soldiers, and the prince. Every head in the hall turns to the prince, who has lived in this palace for twenty years and who discovers that he has been sitting very straight.
blocks.ko: 사신이 답한다. 군사, 그리고 왕자. 전각 안의 모든 고개가 왕자에게로 돌아간다. 이 궁에서 스무 해를 산 그는, 자기가 아까부터 몹시 꼿꼿이 앉아 있었다는 걸 그제야 안다.

lines: 보내 주시오! 나는 찬 바다를 건너 본 사람이오.
숙신 놈들 화살도 맞아 봤소. 서쪽 바다는 그냥 좀 따뜻할 뿐이지. 당나라 황제 모자라도 벗겨 오리다!
en: Send me! I’ve crossed the cold sea.
I’ve taken Mishihase arrows. The western sea’s only warmer. I’ll bring you back their emperor’s hat!
ja: わしを遣わされよ！ 冷たい海なら渡ってきた。
粛慎の矢も受けた。西の海はちと暖かいだけよ。唐の帝の冠でも剝いで参ろう！
jaLatn: Washi o tsukawasare yo! Tsumetai umi nara watatte kita.
Mishihase no ya mo uketa. Nishi no umi wa chito atatakai dake yo. Tō no mikado no kanmuri demo haide mairō!

lines: 어머님, 누가 묻기 전에 제가 먼저 묻겠습니다.
왕자. 저들이 원하는 게 그대요, 그대의 이름이오?
en: Before anyone asks him anything, Mother, I will.
Prince. Do they want you, or your name?
ja: 母上、誰より先に私がお尋ねします。
王子。あちらが欲しいのはそなたか、それともそなたの名か。
jaLatn: Hahaue, dare yori saki ni watakushi ga otazune shimasu.
Ōji. Achira ga hoshii no wa sonata ka, soretomo sonata no na ka.

lines: 저는 아직 백제의 아들입니다. 말을 몇 개… 잊었을 뿐이지요.
en: …Both, I expect. The name first.
I am still a son of Baekje. I have only… forgotten some of the words.

blocks.html: The empress has let all of it run: her son’s arithmetic, the admiral’s hat, the prince’s missing words. Then she speaks once.
blocks.ko: 여제는 그 모든 것을 흘려들었다. 아들의 셈도, 제독의 모자도, 왕자가 잃어버린 말들도. 그러고는 한 번 입을 연다.

blocks.caption: The Eastern Empress. She has outlived two reigns and most of her ministers’ opinions.
blocks.ko: 동쪽의 여제. 두 번의 치세와 대신들 의견 대부분보다 오래 살았다.

lines: 군사를 청하는 일은 옛날부터 있었다. 쓰러지는 집을 붙드는 일은 그보다 더 오래되었지.
바다도 국경이다, 아들아. 서쪽 지붕에 불이 붙으면, 다음은 우리 처마야.
배를 내주어라. 저 아이에게는 관을 씌우고 아내를 붙여 보내라. 볼모 꼴로 도착하지 않게.
en: Asking for soldiers is old. Holding up a falling house is older.
The sea is also a border, my son. When the western roof catches, our eaves are next.
Give them the ships. Give the boy a cap of rank and a wife, so he does not arrive looking like a hostage.
ja: 援軍を乞うは古くからのこと。傾く家を支えるは、なお古い。
海もまた境ぞ、我が子よ。西の屋根に火がつけば、次はこちらの軒。
船を出せ。あの子には冠を授け、妻を添えて送れ。人質のような顔で着かぬように。
jaLatn: Engun o kou wa furuku kara no koto. Katamuku ie o sasaeru wa, nao furui.
Umi mo mata sakai zo, waga ko yo. Nishi no yane ni hi ga tsukeba, tsugi wa kochira no noki.
Fune o dase. Ano ko ni wa kanmuri o sazuke, tsuma o soete okure. Hitojichi no yō na kao de tsukanu yō ni.

blocks.hanja: 乞師請救、聞之古昔。扶危繼絶、著自恆典。……雲會雷動、俱集沙㖨、翦其鯨鯢、紓彼倒懸。
blocks.ko: 군사를 빌고 구원을 청하는 일은 옛적부터 들어 온 바요, 위태로운 것을 붙들고 끊긴 것을 잇는 일은 떳떳한 법도에 적혀 있다. …… 구름처럼 모이고 우레처럼 움직여 사탁에 함께 모여, 그 고래를 베고 거꾸로 매달린 이들을 풀어 주라.
blocks.html: To beg for troops and plead for rescue, this we have heard of from of old; to steady the falling and continue the severed line is written in the constant laws. …… Gather like clouds and move like thunder, assemble together at Sataku, cut down its whales and loosen those who hang upside down.
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) vol. 26, Empress Saimei 6 (660), 10th month — the edict to aid Baekje

blocks.html: Abe is out of the hall before the edict is copied. The prince goes to find a tailor. The eastern prince, who agrees with his mother on everything she has decided, writes the cost of it down on a separate sheet anyway.
blocks.ko: 칙서가 베껴지기도 전에 아베는 전각을 나가고 없다. 왕자는 재봉사를 찾으러 간다. 어머니가 정한 일이라면 무엇이든 따르는 동쪽 태자는, 그래도 그 값을 따로 한 장에 적어 둔다.

blocks.html: The eastern empress raises ships, grain and soldiers for the restoration.
blocks.ko: 동쪽의 여제가 부흥군을 위해 배와 곡식과 군사를 일으킨다.

blocks.html: She dies the next year. Her son takes the throne and keeps her promise. Baekje's refugees start coming home from everywhere they ran.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 이듬해 죽는다. 아들이 자리를 잇고, 어머니의 약속을 지킨다. 흩어졌던 백제 사람들이 도망친 곳곳에서 돌아오기 시작한다.

blocks.label: Roll Call
blocks.ko: 점호

blocks.html: Juryu, the ninth month of 661. Prince Pung comes ashore below the fortress with a cap of rank, a Yamato wife, five thousand eastern soldiers and an admiral nobody asked for, and finds the founders of the restoration drawn up on the shingle to meet him. Boksin has written the order of introductions on a tally board. He has made them rehearse it twice.
blocks.ko: 주류, 661년 구월. 부여풍이 성 아래 자갈밭에 내린다. 관을 쓰고, 왜국 아내를 데리고, 동쪽 군사 오천과 아무도 청하지 않은 제독 하나를 거느리고. 부흥군을 세운 장수들이 자갈밭에 줄지어 그를 맞는다. 복신은 소개 순서를 목간에 적어 두었다. 연습도 두 번이나 시켰다.

blocks.html: Bad farmland, good cliffs. Rebels pick the cliffs.
blocks.ko: 농사엔 나쁘고 벼랑은 좋다. 반란군은 벼랑을 고른다.

blocks.html: The board begins with Boksin. The order lasts until Abe no Hirafu, who is not on it, leaps from the gunwale of the first boat into surf up to his knees, flings his arms wide in his wolf-fur and his red cape, and introduces himself to the fortress, the gulls and the Tang scouts on the far ridge.
blocks.ko: 목간은 복신으로 시작한다. 그 순서는, 목간에 이름도 없는 아베노 히라부가 첫 배 뱃전에서 무릎까지 오는 파도 속으로 뛰어내릴 때까지만 간다. 늑대 모피와 붉은 망토 차림으로 두 팔을 활짝 벌리고, 그는 성채와 갈매기들과 건너편 능선의 당나라 척후들에게 자기를 소개한다.

lines: 아베노 히라부요! 북쪽 찬 바다의 장군!
배 백팔십 척으로 에미시를 쓸었고, 숙신 놈들 화살은 이빨로 받았소! 다음은 당나라요! 하하!
en: Abe no Hirafu! General of the cold northern sea!
A hundred and eighty ships against the Emishi, and I caught Mishihase arrows in my teeth! Tang’s next! Ha!
ja: 阿倍比羅夫なり！ 北の冷たき海の将軍！
百八十艘で蝦夷を平らげ、粛慎の矢は歯で受け止めた！ 次は唐よ！ はっはっ！
jaLatn: Abe no Hirafu nari! Kita no tsumetaki umi no shōgun!
Hyakuhachijissō de Emishi o tairage, Mishihase no ya wa ha de uketometa! Tsugi wa Tō yo! Hahha!

en: You’re not on the board, Admiral.
…Lovely entrance, though.

blocks.html: Echi no Takutsu waits until the admiral has finished, which takes a while. Then he walks up the shingle, turns his back on the Baekje generals and bows to the sea he has just crossed, low and long, the tails of his white headband lifting in the wind, before he turns round and says the one thing he has prepared.
blocks.ko: 에치노 다쿠쓰는 제독이 다 끝낼 때까지 기다린다. 한참 걸린다. 그러고는 자갈밭을 걸어 올라가, 백제 장수들에게 등을 돌리고, 방금 건너온 바다를 향해 낮고 길게 절한다. 흰 머리띠 끝이 바람에 들린다. 그런 다음 돌아서서, 준비해 온 단 한 마디를 한다.

lines: 이 나라에서 내 이름을 아는 사람은 없소. 그러니 내 이름 대신 이 나라 이름을 외치겠소.
구다라 만세. 구다라에 목숨이 하나 필요하거든, 내 것부터 쓰시오.
en: No one in this country knows my name. So instead of mine, I will say yours.
Long live Kudara. If Kudara needs a life, begin with mine.
ja: この国に我が名を知る者はおらぬ。ならば我が名の代わりに、この国の名を叫ぼう。
百済万歳。百済に命が一つ要るなら、まず我がものを使われよ。
jaLatn: Kono kuni ni waga na o shiru mono wa oranu. Naraba waga na no kawari ni, kono kuni no na o sakebō.
Kudara banzai. Kudara ni inochi ga hitotsu iru nara, mazu waga mono o tsukaware yo.

en: …He means it.

blocks.html: Dochim introduces himself sitting down. He has found a flat rock above the tideline and settled on it in his red kasaya, the beads running through one hand and the gilt staff across his knees, and he smiles at the new king the way a monk smiles at a donor whose gift has not yet arrived.
blocks.ko: 도침은 앉은 채로 자기를 소개한다. 물때선 위 평평한 바위에 붉은 가사 차림으로 자리 잡고, 한 손으로 염주를 굴리며 금빛 석장을 무릎에 가로놓은 채, 아직 시주가 도착하지 않은 시주자에게 스님이 짓는 웃음을 새 임금에게 짓는다.

blocks.caption: Dochim. A monk with a general’s staff, in no hurry about either.
blocks.ko: 도침. 장수의 지팡이를 든 승려. 둘 다 서두르지 않는다.

lines: 도침입니다. 이제는 어느 절의 중도 아니고, 영군장군이라 불리지요.
부처님께서는 모든 것이 덧없다 하셨습니다. 사비의 당나라 군도 그 모든 것 가운데 하나입니다.
내일 새벽에 떠납니다. 오늘 밤은 푹 주무십시오.
en: Dochim. A monk of no temple, now. They call me General of the Spirit Army.
The Buddha taught that all things are impermanent. The Tang garrison at Sabi is one of those things.
We march at dawn. Do sleep well tonight.

blocks.html: Good son, those who uphold and protect the true Dharma need not take the five precepts or keep the monk’s deportment. They should carry swords, bows and arrows, and spears, and guard the pure monks who keep the precepts.
blocks.ko: 선남자여, 바른 법을 지키는 이는 다섯 가지 계를 받지 않고 위의를 닦지 않더라도, 마땅히 칼과 활과 화살과 창을 들고 계를 지키는 청정한 비구를 수호해야 한다.
blocks.hanja: 善男子！護持正法者，不受五戒，不修威儀，應持刀劍、弓箭、鉾槊，守護持戒清淨比丘。
blocks.source: Nirvana Sutra (大般涅槃經) fasc. 3, The Adamantine Body (金剛身品), tr. Dharmakṣema · T12n0374, p. 383b

blocks.html: Boksin, who did not write “General of the Spirit Army” on the board, makes a small mark beside it.
blocks.ko: 목간에 ‘영군장군’이라고 쓴 적 없는 복신이, 그 옆에 작은 표시를 하나 한다.

blocks.html: Heukchi Sangji is seven feet tall. The autumn Sabi fell he walked into Imjon with a handful of men and walked out ten days later with thirty thousand, and he regards the whole business of a roll call as a kind of weather. When his turn comes he steps forward exactly one pace.
blocks.ko: 흑치상지는 키가 칠 척이다. 사비가 무너진 가을, 그는 몇 안 되는 사람을 데리고 임존성에 들어가 열흘 만에 삼만을 데리고 나왔다. 그에게 점호 같은 건 날씨 비슷한 것이다. 차례가 오자 그는 정확히 한 걸음 앞으로 나선다.

blocks.caption: Heukchi Sangji. The biggest man on the beach, and the hardest to line up.
blocks.ko: 흑치상지. 해변에서 제일 큰 사내, 그리고 줄 세우기 제일 어려운 사내.

en: Heukchi Sangji. Imjon.
…That’s it.

lines: 장군, 팔. 팔 동작 말입니다. 얘기했잖습니까.
en: The arms, General. We discussed the arms.
You discussed the arms.

blocks.html: Satek Sangya has worn the tall gilt cap of his house for the occasion, which is the only concession he makes to it. He does not look up from the ledger.
blocks.ko: 사택상여는 이날을 위해 집안의 높은 금동관을 쓰고 나왔다. 그가 이날에 해 주는 양보는 그게 전부다. 그는 장부에서 눈을 들지 않는다.

lines: 사택상여. 배 마흔 척, 쌀 천백 섬, 화살 삼만, 밧줄은 세다 말았고.
아직 아무도 값을 안 쳤어. 이게 내 인사요.
en: Satek Sangya. Forty boats, eleven hundred bales of rice, thirty thousand arrows, and I stopped counting the rope.
Nobody has paid me yet. That’s my pose.

blocks.html: Then Gwishil Boksin, who wrote the board, steps out in front of all of them, plants the red shaft in the shingle and does the arms exactly as rehearsed.
blocks.ko: 그리고 목간을 쓴 귀실복신이 모두의 앞으로 나와 붉은 자루를 자갈에 꽂고, 연습한 그대로 팔 동작을 해 보인다.

lines: 귀실복신. 나라가 쓰러졌을 때 한 번 일으켰고, 두 번 쓰러지면 두 번 일으킬 사람이오.
돌아오신 걸 환영합니다, 전하. 전하의 군대입니다.
en: Gwishil Boksin. I raised this country once when it fell, and if it falls twice I’ll raise it twice.
Welcome home, Majesty. Your army.

blocks.html: Everyone looks at the king. Nobody has given Pung a line. He has been in the country for less than an hour and has spent most of it being bowed at, and he ad-libs.
blocks.ko: 모두가 왕을 본다. 풍에게 대사를 준 사람은 아무도 없다. 이 땅에 내린 지 한 시진도 안 되었고, 그동안 절만 받았다. 그는 즉석에서 지어낸다.

lines: 나는 부여풍. 의자왕의 아들이고… 백제의, 그… 왕이다.
en: I am Buyeo Pung, son of King Euija, and… king of— of Baekje.
…Is that right? Is “restoration” the word?
Close enough, Majesty.

blocks.html: Boksin counts them in. “Baekje— Restoration— Army!” Takutsu and the admiral land it perfectly, which is embarrassing for everyone else. Dochim does half and goes back to his beads. Sangya is still counting. Sangji folds his arms, which is at least an arm. The new king is a beat late and on the wrong foot.
blocks.ko: 복신이 박자를 센다. “백제— 부흥— 군!” 다쿠쓰와 제독은 완벽하게 해낸다. 나머지 모두가 민망해진다. 도침은 반쯤 하다 말고 염주로 돌아간다. 상여는 아직 세는 중이다. 상지는 팔짱을 낀다. 그래도 팔은 팔이다. 새 임금은 한 박자 늦고, 발도 반대다.

blocks.html: They try it twice more before supper. For the second, Boksin puts the king on a rock in the middle so that everyone is at least pointing at the same man, and Abe lifts Sangji off the ground to make the shape symmetrical, which nobody asked for and Sangji does not forgive. For the third, Dochim declines to stand, Sangya sits down on the rice, and the king, finally, gets the arms right, a beat after everyone else has stopped.
blocks.ko: 저녁 전까지 두 번 더 해 본다. 두 번째에는 복신이 왕을 한가운데 바위 위에 올려 세운다. 적어도 모두가 같은 사람을 가리키게 하려고. 아베는 모양을 맞추겠다며 상지를 땅에서 번쩍 들어 올린다. 아무도 부탁하지 않았고, 상지는 용서하지 않는다. 세 번째에는 도침이 일어서기를 사양하고, 상여는 쌀가마 위에 주저앉고, 왕은 마침내 팔 동작을 제대로 해낸다. 다들 멈추고 한 박자 뒤에.

blocks.html: On the far ridge two Tang scouts watch the whole performance, and that night Liu Rengui files their report under morale.
blocks.ko: 건너편 능선에서 당나라 척후 둘이 이 공연을 처음부터 끝까지 지켜본다. 그날 밤 유인궤는 그 보고를 ‘사기(士氣)’ 항목에 철해 둔다.

blocks.html: The crown is Pung’s. The army is Boksin’s. Everyone can see the arithmetic of that, including both of them.
blocks.ko: 왕관은 풍의 것이고, 군사는 복신의 것이다. 그 셈은 누구 눈에나 보인다. 두 사람 눈에도.

lines: 대야성은 성이 무너져서 함락된 게 아니오. / 문이 안에서 열렸지.
en: Daeya did not fall because a wall came down. / A door was opened from the inside.

lines: 검일 하나 때문에 나라 전체를 의심할 셈인가.
en: You mean to suspect an entire country because of one Gumil.

lines: 아니. / 나라마다 검일이 하나씩 있다는 얘기요. / 우리한테도 있었고. / 그러니 백제 검일을 찾고, 고려 검일을 찾고, 필요하면 당의 검일도 찾아야지.
en: No. / I mean every country has a Gumil in it. / We had ours. / So find Baekje’s. Find Goguryeo’s. And if it comes to it, find the Tang’s.

blocks.html: It takes eleven years. A captured Silla servant named Jomi-gon is sent back into Baekje as a household man to the minister Imja, and spends years being useful, and one evening asks a question he has been carrying since he left.
blocks.ko: 십일 년이 걸린다. 사로잡혔던 신라의 종 조미곤이 좌평 임자의 집사람으로 백제에 되돌려 보내지고, 여러 해 쓸모 있는 사람으로 지내다가, 어느 저녁 떠나올 때부터 품고 있던 질문 하나를 한다.

lines: 나으리. / 나라가 망하면 나으리 가문은 어찌 됩니까?
en: My lord. / When the country falls, what becomes of your house?

blocks.html: Imja does not report the question, which is the answer.
blocks.ko: 임자는 그 질문을 고하지 않는다. 그것이 곧 대답이다.

blocks.html: Boksin and Pung will not need a Gumil. They will do it to each other unassisted, which Chunchu also predicted, in a sentence his son has written down and kept.
blocks.ko: 복신과 풍에게는 검일이 필요 없을 것이다. 아무 도움 없이 서로에게 그 일을 할 것이다. 이 또한 춘추가 예언한 것이고, 그 문장은 아들이 적어 간직하고 있다.

blocks.html: Chunchu had put it in a sentence his son kept — not a line from the annals, only counsel: where blood ties are strong, the state grows weak.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 한 문장으로 남겨 아들이 간직한 것 — 본기의 기록이 아니라 조언일 뿐. 혈연이 강하면, 국력은 약해진다.

blocks.html: Pung was the only prince left, so they crowned him. Boksin did the crowning. Boksin is starting to regret it.
blocks.ko: 남은 왕자가 풍뿐이라 그를 왕으로 세웠다. 세운 사람은 복신이다. 복신은 그걸 후회하기 시작한다.

blocks.html: Boksin, the lead general of the Revival Society, commands its armies — and begins to resent the king he crowned.
blocks.ko: 부흥군의 총사 복신이 군을 지휘한다 — 그리고 제 손으로 세운 임금을 못마땅해하기 시작한다.

blocks.html: Boksin sends a messenger to the Tang walls with a question.
blocks.ko: 복신이 당의 성벽으로 사자를 보내 묻는다.

lines: 날만 말씀하시오. 제대로 배웅해 드리고 싶으니.
en: When are you gentlemen going home, Ambassador?
Name the day. We’d like to see you off properly.

lines: 손님은 주인이 제 집을 건사할 수 있을 때 떠나는 법이오. 이 집 주인은 왕이 둘에 군대가 하나, 지붕은 없소. 저녁은 먹고 가겠소.
en: Tell him we are guests.
Guests leave when the host can keep his own house. This host has two kings, one army and no roof. We’ll stay for dinner.
zh: 主人能守其家，客乃去。此家二主一軍，無屋可遮。我們留下吃晚飯。
zhLatn: Gàosu tā, wǒmen shì kè.
Zhǔrén néng shǒu qí jiā, kè nǎi qù. Cǐ jiā èr zhǔ yì jūn, wú wū kě zhē. Wǒmen liúxià chī wǎnfàn.

blocks.html: Then Prince Pung wants to move house. The hill is barren, he says. The people will starve. Down on the plain there is rice.
blocks.ko: 그러다 풍왕이 이사를 하겠다고 한다. 산은 메말랐다고. 백성이 굶을 거라고. 아래 들판에는 쌀이 있다고.

blocks.html: After 2 months, they’re forced to move back because it is too close to the Silla border.
blocks.ko: 두 달 만에, 신라 국경에 너무 가깝다는 이유로 다시 돌아올 수밖에 없게 된다.

lines: 이 주유(州柔)[3]는 농토와 멀리 떨어져 있고 토지가 척박하여 농업과 양잠에 적합하지 않은 땅이고, 이곳은 방어하기 좋아 싸울 만한 곳이다. 여기에서 오래 머문다면 백성들이 굶주릴 것이니 이제 피성(避城)으로 옮기는 것이 좋겠다. 피성은 서북쪽으로는 띠를 두르듯 고련단경(古連旦涇)이 흐르고 동남쪽으로는 깊은 수렁과 커다란 둑으로 된 제방이 자리하고 있으며, 땅으로 둘러싸여 있고 도랑을 터트리면 물이 쏟아진다. 꽃과 열매가 있는 나무에서 얻는 토산물은 삼한(三韓)에서 가장 기름질 것이며, 옷과 음식의 근원은 천지 사이에 숨어 있는 곳일 것이다. 비록 낮은 땅(평지)이라고 하지만 어찌 옮기지 않겠는가?
en: This Juryu lies far from farmland, its soil barren and unfit for farming or sericulture; it is good ground for defence and for battle. If we stay long the people will starve — better now to move to Pisong. Pisong has the Goryeondangyeong running about it like a sash to the northwest, and to the southeast deep marshes and great embankments; ringed with earth, and when the sluices are opened the water pours forth. The produce of its flowering and fruiting trees will be the richest in all Samhan, and the source of clothing and food lies hidden between heaven and earth there. Low ground it may be — but why should we not move?

lines: 피성과 적이 있는 곳과의 거리는 하룻밤이면 갈 수 있습니다. 서로 이렇게 매우 가까우니 만약 예기하지 못한 일이 있게 되면 후회해도 소용이 없을 것입니다. 굶는 것은 나중의 일이고 망하는 것이 먼저입니다. 지금 적이 함부로 오지 않는 것은 주유가 산이 험한 곳에 있어 모두 방어물이 되며, 산이 높고 계곡이 좁아 지키기 쉽고 공격하기 어렵기 때문입니다. 만약 낮은 땅에 머물면 어찌 굳건히 살겠으며 흔들리지 않음이 오늘날에 미치겠습니까?”
en: Pisong lies a single night’s march from the enemy. So close that if the unexpected comes, regret will be useless. Starving is a later matter; ruin comes first. The reason the enemy does not come freely now is that Juryu sits in rough mountains — every slope a defence, the peaks high and the valleys narrow, easy to hold and hard to attack. If we sit on low ground, how shall we stand firm, and how shall we last until today’s tomorrow?

blocks.html: The men move once, move back, and start looking at each other differently.
blocks.ko: 군은 한 번 옮겼다가 되돌아왔고, 그 뒤로 서로를 보는 눈이 달라진다.

blocks.html: Baekje has its king back. Now the emperor turns north, to walls that have never fallen…!
blocks.ko: 백제는 왕을 되찾았다. 이제 황제의 눈은 북쪽으로 향한다. 한 번도 무너진 적 없는 성벽으로…!

toneNote: Sieges, rivers, winters — the war grinds until only endurance is left.
title: The Final Stand
