images.alt: Poster key art: Yeon Gesomun stands on the red gate of Pyongyang at dusk with the three-legged crow on his shoulder, both staring west
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Dusk on the ridge wall of Pyongyang: the red two-storey munru gate pavilion, grey stone ramparts, storm clouds. Low angle from the wall walk. INTERACTION: Yeon Gesomun stands on the parapet in red-and-black robes with his crow swords fanned on his back, one boot up on the stone, and the black three-legged crow Samjogo sits on his shoulder (three legs — exactly three) pressing its head against his cheek; he reaches up with two fingers and strokes its breast, both of them staring west at the coming storm. One red sunset break (#d0362f) under the cloud lights his face, the crow and the gate’s red timbers; the rest falls into ink. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | SAMJOGO (삼족오, three-legged crow, guardian of Goguryeo, guide of jumong) — attached board /obj_samjogo.png: Black three-legged crow — always THREE legs visible; red sun motif as the one accent — match the board. Owned by no one; watches from branches and far banks, flies ahead to show Jumong the way. | PLACE pyongyang_fortress — attached board /pl_pyongyang_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang fortress: the same red two-tier munru on the stone ridge in every still. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Red Sun's capital sits on its ridge. A red two-storey gate, grey stone, and clouds that always look about to pick a side. There is only one gate anyone remembers.
blocks.ko: 붉은 해의 도성이 능선 위에 앉아 있다. 붉은 이층 문루, 회색 돌, 어느 편을 들지 막 정하려는 듯한 구름. 사람들이 기억하는 문은 그 하나뿐이다.

blocks.caption: A fleet up the river, an army at the Amnok, and a winter about to pick a side.
blocks.ko: 강을 거슬러 오르는 함대, 압록강의 군대, 그리고 곧 편을 고를 겨울.

blocks.html: The impenetrable walls of Pyongyang are tested once again.
blocks.ko: 난공불락의 평양성이 또다시 시험대에 오른다.

lines: 성왕께서 활을 메신 이래 칠백 년 동안 그랬듯이.
en: Pyongyang does not fall.
Not since the Holy King strung his bow. Seven hundred years.

blocks.html: In Luoyang the Third Emperor announces that he will lead the next army himself. The Empress sends up a memorial the same night.
blocks.ko: 낙양에서 황제가 다음 원정은 친히 이끌겠다고 선포한다. 황후는 그날 밤 상소를 올린다.

lines: 소릉의 여섯 마리 말한테 어떻게 됐는지 물어보세요.
en: Your father went in person, Majesty.
Ask the six horses at Zhaoling how that went.
zh: 陛下去問昭陵那六匹馬，結果如何。
zhLatn: Xiāndì yì céng qīnzhēng, Bìxià.
Bìxià qù wèn Zhāolíng nà liù pǐ mǎ, jiéguǒ rúhé.

en: …We will send someone.
zhLatn: …Zhèn qiǎn rén qù.

blocks.html: The emperor meant to lead the great army after them himself. On the guisi day the Empress sent up a memorial against a personal campaign in Goguryeo, and an edict followed her advice.
blocks.ko: 황제는 몸소 대군을 이끌고 뒤따르려 하였다. 계사일, 황후가 표를 올려 고구려 친정을 간하니, 조서를 내려 그 말을 따랐다.
blocks.hanja: 上欲自將大軍繼之；癸巳，皇后抗表諫親征高麗；詔從之。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 200, Tang Gaozong, Longshuo 1 (661), fourth month

blocks.html: The someone is the Red Fowl. He comes up the Taedong in the eighth month, takes the river forts one by one, and sits down in front of Pyongyang to wait for winter to soften it. Winter has never been on anybody’s side but Goguryeo’s.
blocks.ko: 그 다른 사람이 주작이다. 그는 팔월에 대동강을 거슬러 올라와 강가의 성들을 하나씩 떨구고, 평양 앞에 앉아 겨울이 성을 무르게 해 주기를 기다린다. 겨울은 고구려 말고는 누구 편도 든 적이 없다.

blocks.html: In the ninth month, Namseng holds the great river with tens of thousands. It freezes overnight. At dawn the White Dragon walks his army across the ice, drums going. He kills thirty thousand men guarding a river that is no longer there.
blocks.ko: 구월, 남생이 수만 군사로 큰 강을 지킨다. 강이 하룻밤 새 언다. 새벽, 백룡이 북을 울리며 군대를 얼음 위로 걸려 건넌다. 이제 거기 없는 강을 지키던 삼만이 베인다.

blocks.html: When the White Dragon arrived, the river had frozen solid. He led his men across on the ice, drumming and shouting as they came, and our army broke and ran. He pursued for dozens of li and killed thirty thousand. The rest all surrendered; Namseng barely got away with his life.
blocks.ko: 계필하력이 이르렀을 때 마침 강물이 꽁꽁 얼어붙었다. 하력은 군사를 이끌고 얼음을 타고 강을 건너 북 치고 함성을 지르며 나아가니, 우리 군사가 무너져 달아났다. 하력은 수십 리를 쫓아가 삼만 명을 죽였다. 남은 무리는 모두 항복하고, 남생은 겨우 몸만 빠져나왔다.
blocks.hanja: 契苾何力至，値氷大合，何力引衆乘氷渡水，鼓噪而進，我軍潰奔。何力追數十里，殺三萬人。餘衆悉降，男生僅以身免。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 22, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 20 (661), ninth month

blocks.html: He reached the Yalu. Gaesomun had sent Namseng with tens of thousands of picked troops to hold the crossing, and no one dared ford it. Then the ice closed. Heli* led his men over with a roar; the bandits panicked and broke. Thirty thousand heads were taken and the rest surrendered. Namseng slipped away.
blocks.ko: 압록수에 이르니, 개소문이 남생에게 정병 수만을 주어 험한 곳을 막게 하여 아무도 감히 건너지 못하였다. 마침 얼음이 얼어붙자 하력*이 군사를 이끌고 함성을 지르며 건너니, 적이 놀라 마침내 무너졌다. 삼만 급을 베고 남은 무리는 항복하였으며, 남생은 몸을 빼어 달아났다.
blocks.hanja: 次鴨綠水，蓋蘇文遣男生以精兵數萬拒險，眾莫敢濟。會冰合，何力引兵噪而濟，賊驚，遂潰。斬首三萬級，余眾降，男生脫身走。
blocks.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 110, Biography of Qibi Heli (契苾何力), Longshuo 1 (661)

notes.html: Qibi Heli: the steppe prince this book calls the White Dragon.
notes.ko: 계필하력, 이 책의 흰 용(백룡)이다.

lines: 강 하나다, 남생아. 강 하나를 맡겼다.
얼 줄 몰랐다는 소리는 하지 마라. 거긴 해마다 언다.
en: One river, Namseng. I gave you one river.
Don’t tell me you didn’t know it would freeze. It freezes every year.

blocks.html: The Red Fowl’s army freezes in the snow outside the walls, eats its horses, and waits for rice.
blocks.ko: 주작의 군대는 성 밖 눈밭에서 얼어붙은 채, 제 말을 잡아먹으며 군량을 기다린다.

blocks.html: In the twelfth month, a letter comes down from the north. The Red Fowl is out of rice. Munmu reads it to his generals. Nobody offers. Everyone knows that road in winter. Kim Yushin, who is sixty-six, offers.
blocks.ko: 섣달, 북쪽에서 편지가 내려온다. 주작의 군량이 떨어졌다. 문무가 장수들 앞에서 읽는다. 아무도 나서지 않는다. 섣달의 북쪽 길이 어떤지 다들 안다. 예순여섯의 김유신이 나선다.

lines: 외숙. 외숙은 안 되오. 젊은 사람을 보내시오.
en: Uncle. Not you. Send someone younger.

lines: 젊은 사람들은 길을 모릅니다, 전하. 한슬이와 저는 압니다.
en: The younger ones don’t know the road, Majesty. Hanseul and I do.
Load the carts.

blocks.caption: Rice for the Red Fowl, through enemy country, in the dead of winter, driven by a man of sixty-seven.
blocks.ko: 주작에게 보낼 쌀. 적의 땅을 지나, 한겨울에, 예순일곱 먹은 사내가 끌고 간다.

blocks.html: The White Tiger has thirteen sons. Yeon Gesomun can count to thirteen…!
blocks.ko: 백호에게는 아들이 열셋 있다. 연개소문은 열셋까지 셀 줄 안다…!

images.prompt: 16:9 low worm's-eye at the waterline of a winter river: YEON GESOMUN on his huge red-bay war stallion Damul in Goguryeo gaema barding (match the attached armored board: steel lamellar caparison laced red, steel chamfron, red plume, black mane falling over the steel) crashes into a knot of three Tang riders, a crow-ring sword in EACH hand flung wide in a scissoring cross-cut, four more hilts fanned on his back, red wing-flaps at the shoulders. Damul's body is the centre of the picture, chest-first, forelegs driving through the water. Behind him RED Goguryeo banners with the black crow; around the Tang riders VERMILION Tang banners with the yellow disc. Ice-grey spray frozen in the air, foreground water near-black. Gesomun and Damul lit by one cold cloud break; the Tang riders two values darker. All faces drawn webtoon-style, not photographic. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Armor: Goguryeo kit: steel lamellar with red-edged plates and RED WING shoulder-flaps, peaked helm with plume — red cloth, never gold plate. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | DAMUL (다물, gesomun's horse) — attached board /obj_damul_gaema.png: The biggest horse on any field: a red-bay Goguryeo war stallion, coat a deep BROWN-RED like oxblood lacquer (browner and darker than Hadong, redder and larger than Bisamun), a thick BLACK mane and BLACK tail, black lower legs, heavy arched neck — match the board. In battle it wears Goguryeo 개마 (gaema) barding as in the Anak Tomb No. 3 mural: steel lamellar skirts over the body and neck, a steel chamfron on the face, red cords and a red plume; the black mane falls over the steel. Named for 다물 (多勿), the old Goguryeo word for winning back the lost land; charges into water and spears without being asked, bites other horses. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Goguryeo banners: red silk with the black three-legged crow inside a studded black sun-ring. Attached flag /flag_goguryeo.png. Tang banners: vermilion silk with a yellow sun disc and a dark brush glyph inside it — painted as an illegible brush mark, never readable text. Attached flag /flag_tang.png. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Not a katana, not a tsuba, not a short jian, not a ball pommel. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow aura / emissive skin around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide; katana / tsuba / random sabre length instead of sw_bidam 환두대도.

RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: The White Tiger drives his host into the Snake River. They still believe rivers are roads. Yeon Gesomun has been waiting for a man who thinks that. Old men in the north remember another river that ate an army. The Snake is younger. It's hungrier. And it has Yeon's teeth.
blocks.ko: 백호가 군대를 몰아 사수로 들어온다. 그들은 아직 강을 길이라고 믿는다. 연개소문은 그렇게 믿는 자를 기다려 왔다. 북쪽 늙은이들은 군대를 삼킨 강을 하나 더 기억한다. 사수는 그보다 젊다. 더 굶주렸다. 그리고 연의 이빨을 가졌다.

blocks.html: Shallow, slow, and patient with men who think rivers are roads.
blocks.ko: 얕고 느리며, 강을 길로 아는 자에게 참을성이 많다.

blocks.caption: The White Tiger thought the river was a road. Yeon is standing in the middle of it.
blocks.ko: 백호는 강을 길이라 여겼다. 연개소문은 그 한가운데 서 있다.

blocks.label: Thirteen Sons
blocks.ko: 열세 아들

blocks.html: The river does not take them in a heap. Yeon counts. Chang’an’s clerks will later write thirteen sons as if a number were a grave. It is a morning. The water is February-cold and already learning names.
blocks.ko: 강은 그들을 한 더미로 데려가지 않는다. 연이 센다. 장안의 서기들은 나중에 아들 열셋이라 적을 것이다. 숫자가 무덤인 양. 아침이다. 물은 이월처럼 차고, 이미 이름을 배운다.

blocks.html: The thirteenth and the twelfth come together at the first bend — brothers who still share a horse’s width. Yeon meets them in the shallows where the current lies. One stroke. Two bodies. The horse walks on a few steps with no one left to tell it to stop.
blocks.ko: 열셋째와 열둘째가 첫 굽이에서 함께 온다 — 아직 말 한 필의 너비를 나누는 형제. 연은 물살이 거짓말하는 여울에서 그들을 맞는다. 한 번. 두 몸. 말은 멈추라는 사람이 없어진 채로 몇 걸음을 더 간다.

en: Thirteen.
Twelve.

blocks.html: The eleventh tries the reeds. Reeds keep a secret until a man breathes too loud. Yeon does not spend a speech on a boy hiding in grass.
blocks.ko: 열한째는 갈대를 고른다. 갈대는 사람이 숨소리를 크게 내기 전까지만 비밀을 지킨다. 연은 풀에 숨은 아이에게 연설을 쓰지 않는다.

en: Eleven.

blocks.html: The tenth and the ninth have turned back toward their father. That is the expensive choice: love draws a straight line, and Yeon has been cutting straight lines since the banquet taught him how a room empties. They die reaching for a sleeve that is still too far upriver.
blocks.ko: 열째와 아홉째는 아버지를 향해 되돌아선다. 값비싼 선택이다. 사랑은 직선을 긋고, 연은 연회가 방이 비는 법을 가르쳐 준 뒤로 직선을 잘라 왔다. 아직 너무 상류에 있는 소매를 잡으려다 죽는다.

en: Ten.
Nine.

blocks.html: The eighth is the archer. He puts three shafts into the rim of Yeon’s shield and a fourth into the air where Yeon was. He does not finish the fifth. Yeon takes the bow out of the water afterward and breaks it across his knee, because a river should not keep a weapon that almost learned his height.
blocks.ko: 여덟째는 활이다. 연의 방패 테에 셋, 연이 있던 허공에 넷째. 다섯째는 끝내지 못한다. 연은 나중에 물에서 그 활을 건져 무릎으로 꺾는다. 제 키를 거의 배운 병기를 강이 간직하게 둘 수는 없으니까.

en: Eight. The bow ends here.

blocks.html: The seventh almost makes the far bank. Almost is the dearest word a river sells. Yeon’s throw finds him between the shoulder-blades; the current finishes the courtesy of carrying him the rest of the way.
blocks.ko: 일곱째는 거의 건너편에 닿는다. 거의는 강이 가장 비싸게 파는 말이다. 연의 던짐이 어깨뼈 사이를 찾고, 물살이 나머지를 데려가는 예의를 끝낸다.

blocks.speaker: the seventh
en: Baekju…
Home…
zhLatn: Báizhōu…
Huí jiā…

en: Seven. Home is not that bank.

blocks.html: Three at once in a knot of horses — the sixth, the fifth, the fourth — the way a man takes a cluster when the line has already broken. They shout one father’s name in three pitches. The Snake does not sort pitches.
blocks.ko: 말 엉킴 속에서 셋이 한꺼번에 — 여섯째, 다섯째, 넷째. 전열이 이미 끊긴 뒤에 송이를 따는 법이다. 그들은 한 아버지의 이름을 세 음으로 부른다. 사수는 음을 가리지 않는다.

en: Six. Five. Four.
Some days you count in threes.

blocks.html: The third is old enough to bargain. He offers the banner, the Lingnan levy, a road south, if the Magreji will count him as a messenger instead of a son.
blocks.ko: 셋째는 흥정할 나이다. 깃발과 영남의 병과 남쪽으로 가는 길을 내놓는다. 대막리지가 자신을 아들이 아니라 전령으로 세어 준다면.

blocks.speaker: the third
lines: 열셋 가운데 입을 연 자는 저뿐입니다.
en: Let me go as a messenger.
Among the thirteen I am the only one who opened his mouth.
zh: 十三子之中，開口的只有我。
zhLatn: Róng wǒ zuò shǐzhě qù.
Shísān zǐ zhī zhōng, kāikǒu de zhǐyǒu wǒ.

en: You did not come as a messenger.
That is why you are three.

blocks.html: The second is younger. He still wears a name-tab the southern clerks wrote and never expected to read at this latitude. He does not speak. Yeon does not ask him to. The river takes the tab first; the boy follows it as if following orders.
blocks.ko: 둘째는 더 어리다. 남쪽 서기가 적어, 이 위도에서 읽힐 줄은 몰랐던 이름패를 아직 달고 있다. 그는 말하지 않는다. 연도 시키지 않는다. 강이 패를 먼저 가져가고, 아이는 명령이라도 따르듯 그 뒤를 따른다.

en: Two.

blocks.html: The first — the eldest — holds the White Tiger banner with both hands so the silk will not touch the water. He lasts longer than the others because he has decided to be a flagpole. Yeon cuts the pole. The cloth goes under. The boy goes with it, still holding on, which is how eldest sons are trained.
blocks.ko: 첫째 — 맏이 — 는 백호의 깃을 두 손으로 잡아, 비단이 물에 닿지 않게 한다. 남들보다 오래 가는 것은 스스로 깃대가 되기로 해서다. 연이 대를 벤다. 천이 가라앉는다. 아이도 함께, 아직 놓고 있지 않은 채로. 맏이를 그렇게 가르친다.

en: One.
Now the tiger.

blocks.label: The White Tiger
blocks.ko: 백호

blocks.html: Then only the tiger is left. The White Tiger of Baekju — White Prefecture, a white that is a hometown and not this river — stands where the Lingnan boys can still see him if any of them still have eyes. Someone shouts to break east, toward any camp that is not this one.
blocks.ko: 이제 호랑이만 남는다. 백주 사람, 백호 — 흰 것은 고향이지, 이 강이 아니다 — 영남의 아이들이 아직 눈이 있다면 볼 수 있는 자리에 선다. 누군가 동쪽으로 뚫으라고 소리친다. 여기가 아닌 아무 진영으로.

blocks.speaker: aide
en: Commander! Toward You Boying’s camp—
Live, and leave the account!
zhLatn: Zǒngguǎn! Wǎng Liú Bóyīng yíng—
Huózhe bǎ zhàng liúxià!

lines: 두 황제의 은혜를 너무 많이 입었다.
이 나라를 멸하지 않고는 돌아가지 않는다.
내가 데려온 남쪽 자제가 이미 다 죽었는데 —
이 몸 하나만 살아서 무엇을 하겠느냐.
en: I have eaten too much favour under two emperors.
I will not go home while this kingdom still stands.
The southern boys I brought are already dead —
what would this one body do, alive?
zhLatn: Shòu liǎng cháo ēnzé yǐ guò.
Bù miè cǐguó, bù guī.
Wǒ suǒ lǜ nán zǐdì yǐ jìn sǐ—
Dú liú cǐ shēn, hé wéi?

blocks.html: He does not run. The arrows make a hedgehog of him — the phrase southern records prefer when they cannot bear to write that he was outfought. Yeon walks the last three steps through water that is no longer sure whether it is a river or a grave, and finishes what the shafts began.
blocks.ko: 그는 달리지 않는다. 화살이 그를 고슴도치로 만든다 — 남쪽 기록이, 싸워 졌다고 쓰기 싫어할 때 고르는 말. 연은 강인지 무덤인지 더 이상 확신하지 않는 물을 세 걸음 걸어, 화살이 시작한 일을 끝낸다.

blocks.hanja: 龐孝泰與蓋蘇文戰於蛇水之上 擧軍沒 與其子十三人皆戰死
blocks.ko: [백호가] 개소문과 사수 위에서 싸워, 온 군사가 몰사하고, 그 아들 열세 사람과 더불어 모두 전사하였다.
blocks.html: [The White Tiger] fought Yeon Gaesomun on the Snake River; the whole army was lost, and he and his thirteen sons all died in battle.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 22, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 21 (662); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1 · cf. Zizhi Tongjian Tang Longshuo 2

en: White Tiger.
Titles drown too.

lines: 아직도 정신 못 차렸나, 이 새끼들아?!
en: Still haven’t come to your senses, you bastards?!
I am… none other than… Yeon Gesomun!!

blocks.html: The courier finds Xue Rengui a thousand miles the other way. He has just ended a war in the far west with three arrows. His soldiers are already singing about it. He is given the dead man's title, White Tiger II. And the bill.
blocks.ko: 파발은 천 리 반대편에서 설인귀를 찾아낸다. 그는 서쪽 끝에서 화살 세 대로 전쟁 하나를 막 끝냈다. 병사들은 벌써 그 노래를 부른다. 그는 죽은 자의 이름을 받는다. 백호 2세. 그리고 그 셈도.

lines: 죽은 자의 셈은, 산 자가 갚는 법입니다.
en: White Tiger… I will take the name.
The dead man’s account is paid by the living.
zhLatn: Báihǔ… cǐ míng, wǒ lái jiē.
Sǐzhě zhī zhàng, yóu shēngzhě lái cháng.

blocks.html: He says it without triumph. The White Tiger’s thirteen sons are still a silence in the Tang camp; Xue Rengui’s job is to make sure that silence does not become the empire’s last word on the east.
blocks.ko: 의기양양하지 않다. 백호의 아들 열셋은 여전히 당진의 침묵이고, 설인귀의 일은 그 침묵이 제국의 동쪽에 대한 마지막 말이 되지 않게 하는 것이다.

blocks.html: The fangtian ji goes east again. Men who never learned his birth name learn the white coat and the crescent blade — and begin, quietly, to fear the second tiger more than the first.
blocks.ko: 방천화극이 다시 동쪽으로 간다. 본명을 배우지 못한 자들이 흰옷과 초승달 날을 배우고 — 슬그머니, 첫 번째 호랑이보다 두 번째를 더 두려워하기 시작한다.

blocks.label: Yumla Defied
blocks.ko: 염라를 거역하다

blocks.html: In the worst hour of the fighting — arrows spent, horse down, a Tang blade a finger from his throat — the air thins the way Tamla stories promised. Kangrim and Haewonmek are there. Ledger half-open between them.
blocks.ko: 싸움의 가장 나쁜 시각 — 화살 떨어지고 말 쓰러지고 당의 칼이 목에서 손가락 하나 간격일 때 — 탐라 이야기가 약속한 대로 공기가 옅어진다. 강림과 해원맥이 있다. 명부는 둘 사이에서 반쯤 열려 있다.

en: Yeon Gesomun.
Your page is… persuasive today.
Commander. If you walk away now —
are you choosing Goguryeo, or choosing not to be finished by anyone else’s schedule?
lines: 고구려를 고르는 겁니까, 아니면 남의 일정에 끝나지 않기를 고르는 겁니까?

en: Any last words?
Say them now. The blade is already practicing your name.
lines: 지금 하시게. 칼이 이미 네 이름을 연습 중이니.

en: Kangrim. Haewonmek.
Both.
And neither is your business until I am done.
lines: 그리고 내가 끝날 때까지 네 알 바 아니다.

en: Not today.
I still have sons to disappoint.

blocks.html: The soul leaves the body the way a red coat leaves a peg — still his face, still his will. He cuts the escorts in the thinning air, ledger and last-words both, then finds the ice again. Eyes go from dead to locked. The Tang soldier is still in the middle of the stab when the wrist stops.
blocks.ko: 혼이 몸을 떠난다. 못에서 붉은 도포가 벗기는 것처럼 — 얼굴도 의지도 그대로다. 옅어진 공기 속에서 사신 둘을 자른다. 명부와 유언을 함께. 그리고 다시 얼음을 찾는다. 눈이 죽은 빛에서 잠긴 빛으로 바뀐다. 당의 병사는 아직 찌르는 중간에 있고, 손목이 멈춘다.

blocks.html: He stands up on will alone. The blade misses. Both reapers close the ledger with something like respect — the rare expression of His Majesty’s escorts impressed by rudeness. They fail, together, at the Snake River.
blocks.ko: 의지 하나로 일어선다. 칼이 빗나간다. 두 사자가 명부를 덮으며 존중에 가까운 표정을 짓는다 — 무례에 감명받은, 폐하의 사신의 드문 얼굴. 사수에서, 둘이 함께, 실패한다.

en: Hah.
Keep the country a little longer, then.
I hate refiling — and Your Majesty hates wasted parchment.
lines: 그럼 나라 좀 더 붙들고 있어.
서류 다시 넣기 싫거든 — 폐하께서도 헛된 종이를 싫어하시니.

en: Next time we bring a longer chain.
Or a taller boss.

blocks.label: The Rice Road
blocks.ko: 군량길

blocks.html: In the second month a train of carts comes up out of the south through snow to the axles. Kim Yushin is sixty-seven, and he has walked half the road beside his white horse so that Hanseul can carry a sack of rice instead of him.
blocks.ko: 이월, 바퀴 축까지 차는 눈을 뚫고 남쪽에서 수레 행렬이 올라온다. 김유신은 예순일곱이고, 한슬이가 자기 대신 쌀 한 섬을 질 수 있도록 길의 절반을 흰 말 곁에서 걸어왔다.

blocks.html: The Tang camp outside Pyongyang has been eating its horses. Men sit hugging their knees in the snow and look at the carts as if they might be another rumour.
blocks.ko: 평양 밖 당의 진영은 제 말을 잡아먹고 있었다. 병사들은 눈 속에 무릎을 끌어안고 앉아, 수레를 또 하나의 헛소문인 양 바라본다.

en: Silla is late.
…Unload it. All of it. Then we go home.
zhLatn: Xīnluó lái chí le.
…Xièxià. Quán xiè. Ránhòu huí jiā.

lines: 말 가슴까지 차는 눈을 뚫고 왔습니다, 장군.
en: We came through snow to the horse’s chest, General.
You may eat it slowly.

blocks.html: The Red Fowl takes the rice, breaks camp within the week, and sails. The road back is Yushin’s problem. Goguryeo’s horsemen follow the empty carts all the way to the Imjin, and the white horse carries him across it.
blocks.ko: 주작은 쌀을 받고, 그 주 안에 진을 걷고, 배를 탄다. 돌아가는 길은 유신의 몫이다. 고구려 기병이 빈 수레를 임진강까지 쫓아오고, 흰 말이 그를 태우고 강을 건넌다.

blocks.html: And on an island far to the south, someone is asking: whose side are we on now?
blocks.ko: 그리고 저 남쪽 섬에서, 누군가 묻는다. 이제 우리는 누구 편인가?

images.alt: Tamla’s envoys as tiny orange boats on a vast black sea — the island a far silhouette in mist-white fog
images.prompt: Minimal vast epic cinematic still matching the visual bible: huge BLACK sea, mist-WHITE fog band, one distant volcanic island, two tiny ORANGE-sailed envoy boats. Wet black water mirroring orange. No faces, no anime, no clutter, no text, no watermark.

images.alt: A lone orange tree bent by wind - Tamla's lonely submission to the mainland powers
images.prompt: Cinematic composition: A single orange tree bearing fruit, bent by wind, against a vast pale sky

blocks.html: After the Snake River, Tamla quietly changes sides.
blocks.ko: 사수의 싸움이 끝나자, 탐라는 조용히 편을 바꾼다.

blocks.html: The island kingdom sends its envoys to Silla and the Tang, ending seven centuries beside Baekje.
blocks.ko: 섬나라는 신라와 당에 사신을 보내, 칠백 년을 함께한 백제와의 인연을 끝낸다.

blocks.html: Dodongeumnyul (some copies say -jin), lord of Tamla and a jwapyeong, came and surrendered. Tamla had been Baekje's vassal since the Wude years, which is why its lord carried the Baekje rank of jwapyeong. Now it submitted and became a dependency.
blocks.ko: 탐라국주 좌평 도동음률〈진이라고도 한다〉이 와서 항복하였다. 탐라는 무덕 연간 이래 백제의 신하였으므로 좌평을 관호로 삼았는데, 이때에 이르러 항복하여 속국이 되었다.
blocks.hanja: 耽羅國主佐平徒冬音律〈一作津。〉來降。耽羅自武德以來，臣屬百濟，故以佐平爲官號，至是，降爲屬國。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 2 (662), second month

blocks.html: Early in Longshuo there was a land called Danluo, whose king, Yuri Dora, sent envoys to court. It lies on an island south of Silla's Muju. Its ways are plain and rough: they wear the hides of great pigs, live in leather huts in summer and in pit-houses in winter. … At first it was attached to Baekje. … Later it attached itself to Silla.
blocks.ko: 용삭 초에 담라라는 나라가 있어, 그 왕 유리도라가 사신을 보내 입조하였다. 나라는 신라 무주 남쪽 섬 위에 있으며, 풍속이 소박하고 거칠어 큰 돼지 가죽을 입고, 여름에는 가죽 집에, 겨울에는 움집에 산다. … 처음에는 백제에 붙었다. … 뒤에는 신라에 붙었다.
blocks.hanja: 龍朔初，有儋羅者，其王儒李都羅遣使入朝，國居新羅武州南島上，俗樸陋，衣大豕皮，夏居革屋，冬窟室。…初附百濟。…後附新羅。
blocks.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Danluo (儋羅, Tamla), Longshuo era (661–663)

blocks.html: Baekje is supposed to be finished. Nobody told the fortresses. And in Surabol, a great lord calls in sick…!
blocks.ko: 백제는 끝났어야 했다. 아무도 성들에게 그 말을 전하지 않았다. 그리고 서라벌에서는 한 대귀족이 병을 핑계 댄다…!

images.at: He hears it from a Tang officer who is sorry for him
images.alt: In a Chang'an palace corridor, Kim Punghun sits on the step with his helmet in his lap; a Tang officer's hand rests on his shoulder.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night at the Tang palace in Chang'an (attached board): a long roofed corridor on the red rammed-earth terrace, vermilion columns receding diagonally. Medium close, low three-quarter. A young Silla nobleman serving in the emperor's guard sits on a white stone balustrade step where his legs gave out, his face turned down and away from the lens into shadow, guard's helmet in his lap, one hand over his mouth. A Tang officer in a vermilion robe stands beside him, half out of frame, one hand resting awkwardly on his shoulder. Red lantern spill, cool blue-green shadows, distant lantern bokeh down the corridor, reflective dark stone floor. One hard key from a lantern beside them. Unarmed. CANON — PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) — black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding into rice paper, dry calligraphic brush for roofs, columns, smoke and robes, the vermilion and gold reduced to small accents in a world of ink; officials, guards and other Tang figures are ink figures too. The ONE exception is the Second Emperor himself: he keeps the house webtoon figure render in full colour (yellow robe, black futou, drawn face), a coloured man inside an ink empire. Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: Naesaji
blocks.ko: 내사지성

blocks.html: Two summers after Sabi, Baekje is supposed to be finished. Nobody has told the fortresses. The leftovers gather at a hill fort east of the old capital. They do what a kingdom does with no king nearby. They collect grain. They hang collaborators. They send boys to watch the Silla roads.
blocks.ko: 사비가 떨어지고 두 해 여름. 백제는 끝났어야 했다. 아무도 성들에게 그 말을 전하지 않았다. 남은 자들이 옛 도읍 동쪽의 산성에 모인다. 임금이 곁에 없는 나라가 하는 일을 한다. 곡식을 걷는다. 부역자를 매단다. 신라 길목에 소년들을 세워 망을 보게 한다.

blocks.html: Munmu names nineteen generals for it. One of them is Kim Jinju. He is True Bone, from a good family. He led men at the Yellow Mountain. He has a son in the emperor's guard.
blocks.ko: 문무는 이 일에 장군 열아홉을 붙인다. 그중 하나가 김진주다. 좋은 집안의 진골이다. 황산벌에서 군사를 이끌었다. 아들 하나가 황제의 숙위로 가 있다.

blocks.html: Jinju sends word that he is ill. So does Jinheum, governor of Namcheon. Neither of them is ill. They stay at home through the whole of the campaign, eat well, receive visitors, and are seen at a gyuku match.
blocks.ko: 진주는 병이 났다고 기별을 보낸다. 남천주총관 진흠도 그렇게 한다. 둘 다 아프지 않다. 그들은 싸움 내내 집에 머물며 잘 먹고, 손님을 맞고, 격구장에서 눈에 띄기까지 한다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Jinju
lines: 산성 하나에 장군이 열아홉이야. 스무 번째는 필요 없어.
게다가 전쟁은 끝났잖나. 누군가는 그렇다고 말해야지.
en: Nineteen generals for one hill fort. They don’t need a twentieth.
Besides. The war’s over. Somebody should say so.

blocks.html: Naesaji falls without him. Kim Heumsun takes it in a fortnight and reports it to the king in two lines, and then, because he is honest and it is his duty, he reports who was missing.
blocks.ko: 내사지성은 그 없이 떨어진다. 김흠순이 보름 만에 성을 빼앗고 왕에게 두 줄로 보고한 뒤, 정직하고 그것이 직분이므로, 누가 빠졌는지도 보고한다.

lines: 싸움 내내. 둘 다. 격구 칠 만큼은 멀쩡하고.
en: Ill.
The whole campaign. Both of them. And well enough for gyuku.

blocks.speaker: Kim Jinju
lines: 전하, 열이 오르내렸습니다. 사람이 앓는 날을 고를 수는—
en: Majesty, the fever came and went. A man cannot choose his days—

lines: 내 아버님은 이 전쟁에서 하루도 쉬신 적이 없다. 내 누이는 죽을 날을 고르지도 못했다.
en: My father never had a day off from this war. My sister didn’t get to choose hers.
Take them out.

blocks.html: Jinju and Jinheum are beheaded, and their households with them, down to the cousins. It is the first time Munmu kills his own nobility, barely a year into the reign, and after it nobody mistakes the new king for a soft one.
blocks.ko: 진주와 진흠은 목이 베이고, 그 집안도 사촌까지 함께 죽는다. 문무가 제 귀족을 죽인 것은 이것이 처음이고, 왕위에 오른 지 겨우 한 해 남짓이다. 그 뒤로 누구도 새 왕을 무르다고 착각하지 않는다.

blocks.html: In the eighth month the remnant rebels of Baekje gathered at Naesaji Fortress and did harm. Heumsun and the others, nineteen generals in all, were sent and broke them. Jinju, commander of the Great Banner, and Jinheum, commander of Namcheon, had pleaded illness and idled at their ease, careless of the kingdom's business. In the end they were put to death and their clans wiped out with them.
blocks.ko: 8월, 백제의 잔적이 내사지성에 모여 악행을 저지르니, 흠순 등 열아홉 장군을 보내 쳐서 깨뜨렸다. 대당총관 진주와 남천주총관 진흠이 병을 핑계 대고 한가로이 지내며 나랏일을 돌보지 않으므로, 마침내 그들을 베고 그 일족까지 멸하였다.
blocks.hanja: 八月，百濟殘賊，屯聚内斯只城作惡，遣欽純等十九將軍，討破之。大幢摠管眞珠、南川州摠管眞欽，詐稱病，閑放不恤國事，遂誅之，并夷其族。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 2 (662), eighth month

blocks.html: The annals aren't done with him. Eight years later, the same pages send a Jinju to behead a traitor governor. Later tellers like that version better. They even give him the credit for this hill fort. Either Silla had two men of the name, or a clerk killed him once and forgot. Only one person never mixes them up: his son.
blocks.ko: 연대기는 아직 그를 놓아주지 않는다. 여덟 해 뒤, 같은 책은 진주라는 사내를 보내 배신한 총관의 목을 베게 한다. 뒷날의 이야기꾼들은 그쪽이 더 좋다. 이 산성을 꺾은 공까지 그에게 돌린다. 신라에 그 이름이 둘이었거나, 서기가 그를 한 번 죽여 놓고 잊었거나. 판본을 한 번도 헷갈리지 않는 사람은 하나뿐이다. 그의 아들.

blocks.html: Suse, commander of Hanseong-ju, took … of Baekje …; it happened that the plot came to light, and the daeachan Jinju was sent to put him to death.
blocks.ko: 한성주총관 수세가 백제의 … 나라를 취하려 하다가 마침 그 일이 드러나니, 대아찬 진주를 보내 그를 베었다.
blocks.hanja: 漢城州摠管藪世取百濟…國，適彼事覺，遣大阿飡眞珠，誅之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), twelfth month (the woodblock is damaged here)

blocks.html: Kim Punghun is at Chang’an when the news comes, in the emperor’s guard, where the sons of vassal houses are kept. He hears it from a Tang officer who is sorry for him, which is worse. He asks for leave to go home for the mourning and is told, kindly, that he has no home to go to.
blocks.ko: 소식이 왔을 때 김풍훈은 장안에 있다. 번국 집안의 아들들을 두는 황제의 숙위다. 그는 그 소식을 그를 딱하게 여기는 당나라 장교에게서 듣는다. 그게 더 나쁘다. 그는 상을 치르러 돌아가게 해 달라고 청하고, 돌아갈 집이 없다는 말을 친절하게 듣는다.

lines: 황제의 배는 언젠가 동쪽으로 갑니다. 배 한 척쯤은 기다릴 수 있습니다.
en: …Then I will wait.
The emperor’s ships go east sooner or later. I can wait for a ship.

blocks.html: Back at Juryu, a monk and a general share one army. We have to go back to see who keeps it…!
blocks.ko: 주류에서는 승려와 장군이 한 군대를 나눠 쥐고 있다. 누가 그 군대를 갖게 되는지, 조금 거슬러 올라가 보자…!

images.at: Boksin plots to kill the king by pretending to be sick
images.alt: Boksin's feigned sickbed betrayed — the general seized by King Pungjang's guards in torchlight
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of Boksin's downfall, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (663), scene: general Gwisil Boksin caught in his feigned-sickness plot, dragged from a sickbed by King Pungjang's guards inside the mountain fortress of Juryu, torchlight on stone, the restoration devouring itself, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: bound with a leather thong through the palms
images.alt: Caravaggio’s Martyrdom of St Matthew: Boksin on his knees, palms bound, spitting upward as the sword rises over him
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Caravaggio’s Martyrdom of Saint Matthew. A dark hall at Juryu fortress at night: General Boksin kneels on the floor, palms bound together with a leather thong, head thrown back, spitting up at the dais. Over him an executioner raises a ring-pommel sword two-thirds into the frame, the blade high and catching the light. Far back on the dais King Pung sits in shadow, half-turned away, only his hand on the throne arm lit. One brazier at floor level is the key, raking up Boksin’s face and the raised blade; the room is black. No gore. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — GWISHIL BOKSIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gwisil_boksin.png (face only; invent a new pose). #a8781f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KING PUNGJANG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_pungjang.png (face only; invent a new pose). #e6c76a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. blocks.label: Dochim
blocks.ko: 도침

blocks.html: Before Boksin and the king, there were Boksin and the monk. Dochim raised the first banner with him, the autumn Sabi fell. He put down his begging bowl for a spear. He named himself General of the Spirit Army. For a year the two held the west between them. The enemy garrison couldn't even go out for water.
blocks.ko: 복신과 왕 이전에, 복신과 승려가 있었다. 사비가 떨어진 가을, 도침이 그와 함께 첫 깃발을 들었다. 바리때를 내려놓고 창을 든 승려였다. 스스로 영군장군이라 불렀다. 한 해 동안 둘은 서쪽을 나눠 쥐었다. 적의 수비대는 물 길으러도 못 나왔다.

blocks.html: All fear death; there is none who does not dread the pain of the rod. Take yourself as the measure: do not kill, do not strike.
blocks.ko: 모든 이가 죽음을 두려워하고, 매의 아픔을 겁내지 않는 이가 없다. 제 몸에 견주어 헤아려, 죽이지 말고 매질하지 말라.
blocks.hanja: 一切皆懼死，莫不畏杖痛，恕己可為譬，勿殺勿行杖。
blocks.source: Dhammapada (法句經) ch. 18, Sword and Rod (刀杖品), tr. Weiqinan & Zhu Jiangyan · T04n0210, p. 565b

blocks.html: Then a Tang envoy came to the walls with a letter, and Dochim sent him back with it unread and a message that the General of the Spirit Army did not receive men of so small a rank. It was a good line. Boksin heard it and understood that the monk had begun to think of himself as the one in charge.
blocks.ko: 그러다 당의 사신이 서신을 들고 성 아래 왔고, 도침은 그것을 읽지도 않은 채 돌려보내며, 영군장군은 그리 낮은 벼슬아치를 맞지 않는다고 전하게 했다. 근사한 말이었다. 복신은 그 말을 듣고, 그 승려가 자기가 우두머리라고 여기기 시작했음을 알았다.

lines: 이 군대는 부처님이 내게 주셨다, 복신. 자네는 먹이기만 했지.
en: The Buddha gave me this army, Boksin. You only fed it.
Feed it well. It is going to Sabi.

lines: 물론입니다, 장군. 영군께 필요한 건 무엇이든.
그럼 오늘 저녁 드시지요. 단둘이. 사비 이야기를 하십시다.
en: Of course, General. Whatever the Spirit Army needs.
Supper tonight, then. Just the two of us. We’ll talk about Sabi.

blocks.html: Dochim comes to supper. He does not leave it. By morning his men have been folded into Boksin’s army without a vote, and Prince Pung, newly crowned and still learning the names, is told that the monk has gone on a long retreat.
blocks.ko: 도침은 저녁을 먹으러 온다. 그리고 돌아가지 못한다. 아침이 되자 그의 군사들은 아무 표결도 없이 복신의 군에 접혀 들어가 있고, 갓 왕관을 쓰고 아직 이름들을 외우는 중인 풍 왕자는, 그 승려가 긴 수행을 떠났다는 말을 듣는다.

lines: …그렇구려. 하면 지금 그의 군사는 누가 거느리오?
en: A retreat. In the middle of a war.
…I see. And who commands his men now?

lines: 제가 거느립니다, 전하. 전하께서는 그런 걱정 하실 일이 없도록.
en: I do, Majesty. So that Your Majesty need never worry about it.

blocks.html: Pung remembers the answer. He has two years to think about it.
blocks.ko: 풍은 그 대답을 기억한다. 그에게는 그것을 곱씹을 두 해가 있다.

blocks.label: The Jar
blocks.ko: 항아리

lines: 결국 이 나라를 두 번 세우는 건 나요.
en: In the end it is I who raise this country twice.
And it is he who wears the crown.
…And he will want to move again.

blocks.html: Boksin plots to kill the king by pretending to be sick, but is caught and executed instead.
blocks.ko: 복신은 병을 핑계로 임금을 죽이려 하지만, 발각되어 도리어 처형된다.

blocks.html: Two summers later, in the sixth month of 663, King Pungjang has the general who crowned him bound with a leather thong through the palms, and asks the room whether a man like that should be cut down. The room says yes, Jipdeuk first. Boksin spits at him.
blocks.ko: 두 해 뒤, 663년 유월, 풍장왕은 자신을 왕위에 올린 장군의 손바닥을 가죽끈으로 꿰어 묶고, 이런 자를 베어야 하느냐고 좌중에 묻는다. 좌중은 그렇다고 한다. 집득이 맨 먼저. 복신은 그에게 침을 뱉는다.

blocks.hanja: 福信即唾於執得，曰：「腐狗癡奴！」王勒健兒，斬而醢首。
blocks.html: Boksin at once spat at Jipdeuk and said: “Rotten dog, idiot slave!” The king ordered his strong men to behead him, and had the head pickled.
blocks.ko: 복신이 곧 집득에게 침을 뱉으며 말했다. “썩은 개, 어리석은 종놈아!” 왕이 건아들에게 명하여 그를 베고 그 머리를 젓갈로 담갔다.
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 27, Tenji 2 (663), sixth month

blocks.html: Two generals stand at the back while the head is salted. Heukchi Sangji, who took two hundred fortresses back for Boksin in a single season, watches the king’s hands. Satek Sangya watches the jar.
blocks.ko: 머리를 소금에 절이는 동안 두 장수가 뒤쪽에 서 있다. 한 철에 복신에게 이백 성을 되찾아 준 흑치상지는 임금의 손을 본다. 사택상여는 항아리를 본다.

lines: …세워 주지도 않은 우리는 어떻게 할 것 같나.
en: The man who crowned him. In a jar.
…What do you think he does with the ones who didn’t?
Same thing. Less salt.

blocks.html: However, there is still a problem. Boksin was the most competent general of the movement, and there is only one chance left.
blocks.ko: 그러나 문제가 남는다. 복신은 부흥군 최고의 장수였고, 이제 기회는 단 한 번뿐이다.

blocks.html: Four banners. One river mouth. The West, Samhan and the East meet on a single tide…!
blocks.ko: 깃발 넷. 하구 하나. 서쪽과 삼한과 동쪽이, 한 물때 위에서 만난다…!
