images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE battle frame. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. The Battle of the White River (Baekgang), late summer 663: the wide muddy Geum estuary of the attached pl_white_river board — tidal flats, reed banks, low grey hills on both shores. High three-quarter view from a headland at grey dawn: the Tang fleet of tall multi-storey tower-ships moored in ONE long dark line across the channel like a wall, vermilion banners hanging; far out on the slate sea a scatter of small open Yamato war-boats with white-and-red pennants; one thin smoke column already rising from a hulk burned yesterday; gulls. Device: the dark horizontal wall of hulls cutting the estuary in two; the upper half is pale cream sky and slow smoke. HEEWON BATTLE STYLE — this is a battle frame, and every still of this battle shares ONE look so the set plays as one film. Copy the BRUSHWORK AND STYLIZATION of the two attached style_battle boards ONLY — never their ships, flags, figures or composition (the painted board shows 19th-century steam and sailing ships; this battle is 7th-century East Asia). The look is the background art of a hand-painted 2D animated epic crossed with an East Asian woodblock battle scroll. SMOKE AND CLOUD are the big shapes: towering sculpted columns and rolling banks painted as broad soft gouache masses, lit warm orange from the fires underneath and cooling to slate and charcoal at the top; where they curl they break into stylised scroll-cloud spirals outlined in thin ink, like a painted screen. WATER is Hokusai: heavy slate-teal swells with claw-like cream-white foam crests drawn in ink line, spray as stippled dots. FIRE is flat curling ribbons of vermilion and orange with darker red edges licking up hulls, sails and banners — never photographic flame. BANNERS are long silk ribbons whipping in the wind, kingdom colour only, their marks illegible brush strokes. FIGURES are many small drawn silhouettes — soldiers packed in boats, oars, spears, shields — read as massed shapes, the nearest ones dark against the bright smoke; named heroes are drawn larger with clean webtoon faces. DEPTH is layered like stage flats: dark foreground waves, boats and figures; midground ships or ranks in clear silhouette; background smoke, haze and a pale sky that fades like cream paper; a few seabirds or embers. PALETTE is fixed for the whole battle: cream-paper sky, slate blue-grey and teal water, charcoal smoke, vermilion-and-orange fire, ink black, plus each kingdom's banner colour — no purple sunset, no neon, no other hues. Painted texture everywhere (gouache grain, dry-brush, ink line on waves and clouds); not photoreal, not 3D, not a map or satellite view, not a manga speed-line panel. SHIPS are 7th-century only: Tang multi-storey louchuan tower-ships with stacked timber cabins, rows of oars and battened junk sails; Yamato and Baekje open oared war-boats with a single mast — never European hulls, cannon, funnels or square-rigged masts. OVERRIDES of the house rules below for battle frames: massed hosts and fleets are allowed as silhouetted masses; daylight through smoke is allowed (the dark masses are the smoke, the bright break is the pale sky or the fire); still ONE device (a waterline, a smoke column, a ring of hulls, a ford) and big quiet areas of smoke or sky. CANON — PLACE White River (백강 (금강 하구)) — attached board /pl_white_river.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Tang banners: vermilion silk with a yellow sun disc and a dark brush glyph inside it — painted as an illegible brush mark, never readable text. Attached flag /flag_tang.png. Wa banners: red silk with a gold many-petalled sunburst. Attached flag /flag_wa.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

FIRE is flat curling ribbons of vermilion and orange with darker red edges licking up hulls, sails and banners — never photographic flame. BANNERS are long silk ribbons whipping in the wind, kingdom colour only, their marks illegible brush strokes. FIGURES are many small drawn silhouettes — soldiers packed in boats, oars, spears, shields — read as massed shapes, the nearest ones dark against the bright smoke; named heroes are drawn larger with clean webtoon faces. SHIPS are 7th-century only: Tang multi-storey louchuan tower-ships with stacked timber cabins, rows of oars and battened junk sails; Yamato and Baekje open oared war-boats with a single mast — never European hulls, cannon, funnels or square-rigged masts. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: A burning ship, a swordsman on its deck
ONE horizontal loaded brushstroke across the lower third, black sumi, bristles splitting so white paper shows through the stroke (flying white).
images.prompt: Minimal East Asian ink painting. Off-white paper, vast empty. ONE horizontal loaded brushstroke across the lower third, black sumi, bristles splitting so white paper shows through the stroke (flying white). The stroke is a river. A tiny boat is two marks on it, one small standing figure no taller than a fingernail, seen from far away, no face detail. Nothing else. No mountains, no trees, no seal, no calligraphy, no signature, no red stamp. Painterly dry brush, not a drawing, not a photograph.

blocks.html: Chang’an’s clerks still count to thirteen when they hear the word river. This mouth is not that river. The tiger already died in February water, with every son numbered. The White River has come for sails.
blocks.ko: 장안의 서기들은 아직도 강이라는 말만 들어도 열셋까지 센다. 이 하구는 그 강이 아니다. 호랑이는 이미 이월의 물에서, 아들마다 번호를 매긴 채로 죽었다. 백강이 온 것은 돛을 위해서다.

blocks.html: The epic battle: for the first time the West, Samhan, and the East meet in one mouth of water. Tang and Silla hold the banks; Baekje’s restoration and a Yamato expeditionary fleet come in on the tide — and discover, too late, that tide is not a friend you can hire.
blocks.ko: 대전투: 중원과 삼한과 왜가 역사상 처음으로 한 물목에서 맞붙는다. 당과 신라가 양쪽 언덕을 잡고, 백제 부흥과 야마토 원정 함대가 밀물을 타고 들어온다 — 그리고 너무 늦게야 안다. 밀물은 고용할 수 있는 친구가 아니라는 것을.

blocks.label: Four Banners
blocks.ko: 네 깃발

blocks.html: Count the banners before the water does. Tang comes by sea, twice. The Black Tortoise has held the old capital for two winters with a garrison too small to deserve the word. The emperor wrote that he could come home. He wrote back that he'd rather not. So in spring the emperor sends him seven thousand more. The Silla annals, which like round numbers, make it four hundred thousand.
blocks.ko: 깃발부터 세자. 물이 세기 전에. 당은 바다로, 두 번 온다. 현무는 수비대라 부르기도 민망한 병력으로 옛 도성을 두 겨울째 지키고 있다. 황제가 돌아와도 좋다고 썼다. 그는 차라리 남겠다고 답했다. 그래서 봄에 황제는 칠천을 더 보낸다. 둥근 숫자를 좋아하는 신라의 사서는 그것을 사십만이라 적는다.

blocks.html: Silla comes by land. King Munmu, in the third year of his reign, rides out of Surabol with Kim Yushin and twenty-eight generals behind him, thirty in another copy of the list. Yushin is sixty-eight and still sits a horse as if the horse had asked him to.
blocks.ko: 신라는 뭍으로 온다. 즉위 삼 년째의 문무왕이 김유신과 장군 스물여덟을 거느리고 서라벌을 나선다. 다른 사본에는 서른이다. 유신은 예순여덟인데도, 말이 먼저 청하기라도 한 것처럼 여전히 말 위에 앉아 있다.

blocks.html: Baekje is what is left of it: a hill fortress called Juryu, a king who spent his boyhood in Yamato, and no Boksin. Two months ago the king had the general who crowned him beheaded, and the head is still in its jar.
blocks.ko: 백제는 남은 것이 전부다. 주류라는 산성 하나, 소년 시절을 야마토에서 보낸 왕 하나, 그리고 복신이 없다. 두 달 전 왕은 자신을 왕위에 올린 장군의 목을 베었고, 그 머리는 아직 젓갈 단지 속에 있다.

blocks.html: Silla heard, and moved at once. A kingdom that executes its best general is a kingdom with its door open.
blocks.ko: 신라는 소식을 듣자마자 움직였다. 제 최고의 장수를 처형한 나라는 문이 열린 나라다.

blocks.html: Upriver, King Pungjang still believes enough sails can restore a kingdom. For three summers the East has sent him ships. A thousand, if you trust the enemy's count. Forty-two thousand men. Takutsu is among the captains who still say Kudara. They come down on the eighth month's water, packed too tight to row. They are shouting for a victory the tide has already priced differently.
blocks.ko: 상류에서 풍장왕은 아직, 배만 넉넉하면 나라를 되찾을 수 있다고 믿는다. 세 해 여름 동안 동쪽은 배를 보내 주었다. 적의 셈을 믿는다면 천 척이다. 군사는 사만 이천. 다쿠쓰도 그 장수들 사이에 있다. 아직 쿠다라라고 부르는 사람들이다. 그들은 노를 젓지도 못할 만큼 빽빽하게 팔월의 물을 타고 내려온다. 밀물이 이미 다른 값을 매긴 승리를 외치면서.

blocks.html: Takutsu brought Prince Pung home two years ago with five thousand men. Last winter he was the only one in the hall who told the new king not to move the court down to the plain, and he was right, and he was thanked for it the way men usually are.
blocks.ko: 다쿠쓰는 두 해 전 오천 군사로 풍 왕자를 고향에 데려다주었다. 지난겨울 새 왕에게 조정을 평지로 옮기지 말라고 말한 사람은 그 전각에서 그 하나뿐이었다. 그가 옳았고, 사람들이 대개 받는 방식대로 고맙다는 말을 들었다.

blocks.html: On the thirteenth day of the eighth month, with the Silla army already on the road to Juryu, the king of Baekje announces that he will leave it.
blocks.ko: 팔월 열사흘, 신라군이 이미 주류로 오는 길 위에 있는데, 백제왕은 주류를 떠나겠다고 선언한다.

en: Yamato’s relief general, Lord Iohara, is crossing the sea with ten thousand men and more.
Generals, make ready for him.
I shall go down to Baekchon myself, and receive them there with a feast.
lines: 야마토의 구원장 이오하라 공이 건아 만여를 이끌고 바다를 건너오고 있소.
과인은 몸소 백촌으로 내려가, 그들을 잔치로 맞겠소.

en: Majesty. And Juryu?
Juryu has walls.
…It had a general, too.

blocks.label: The Throat of the River
blocks.ko: 강의 목

blocks.html: At Ungjin the allied generals argue about where to begin. Garim fortress sits where the road crosses the river, and most of the room wants it first.
blocks.ko: 웅진에서 연합군 장수들은 어디서부터 시작할지를 두고 다툰다. 가림성은 뭍길과 물길이 엇갈리는 자리에 앉아 있고, 좌중 대부분은 그곳부터 치자고 한다.

en: Garim is steep and strong.
Rush it and we bleed men. Sit under it and we bleed days.
Juryu is the nest. Pull the root, and the branches come down by themselves.
lines: 서두르면 군사를 잃고, 눌러앉으면 날을 잃소.
주류가 소굴이오. 뿌리를 뽑으면 가지는 저절로 떨어지오.

blocks.html: So the armies split. Most of the generals take the land road. The Black Tortoise takes the water: a hundred and seventy warships, heading for the river mouth. On his deck stands Buyeo Yung.
blocks.ko: 그래서 군은 갈라진다. 장수들 대부분은 뭍길을 탄다. 현무는 물을 맡는다. 전선 백칠십 척이 하구를 향해 내려간다. 그 갑판 위에 부여융이 서 있다.

blocks.title: Four banners, one river mouth
blocks.caption: Tang by sea twice, Silla by land, and the East arriving in a hurry. Everyone is headed for the same mud.
blocks.ko: 바다로 두 번 온 당, 땅으로 온 신라, 서둘러 오는 동쪽. 다들 같은 갯벌로 간다.

blocks.html: Euija’s eldest. He knelt at Sabi three summers ago, was taken to Chang’an with his father, and has come back in a Tang officer’s coat to fight his younger brother for the right to tell the survivors what happened to them. Nobody on the deck says this. Everybody on the deck knows it.
blocks.ko: 의자의 맏아들. 세 해 전 여름 사비에서 무릎을 꿇었고, 아버지와 함께 장안으로 끌려갔다가, 이제 당나라 장수의 옷을 입고 돌아와 아우와 싸운다. 살아남은 이들에게 그들에게 무슨 일이 있었는지 말해 줄 권리를 두고. 갑판 위의 누구도 이 말을 하지 않는다. 갑판 위의 누구나 그것을 안다.

en: Your brother’s banner will be on that fleet.
When it comes, can you look at it?
lines: 아우의 깃발이 저 함대에 있을 것이오.
그때가 오면, 그것을 볼 수 있겠소?

en: I have looked at worse.
…I looked at my father.

blocks.html: The Black Tortoise has already learned the river's grammar. A narrow mouth. Sandbars that shift like lies. A current that punishes anyone who charges out of line. He anchors his hundred and seventy ships across the throat and waits. On the east bank, Kim Yushin's army keeps the shore from becoming a pier.
blocks.ko: 현무는 이미 강의 문법을 배웠다. 좁은 하구. 거짓말처럼 움직이는 모래톱. 대열 없이 덤비는 자를 벌하는 물살. 그는 백칠십 척을 목구멍에 가로질러 닻을 내리고 기다린다. 동쪽 기슭에서는 김유신의 군대가 그 기슭이 부두가 되지 않게 막는다.

blocks.label: The Shore
blocks.ko: 강기슭

blocks.html: On the bank the Baekje horsemen guard the landing. They are the last mounted men the restoration can field, drawn up in front of the beached hulls the way you stand in front of a door you cannot afford to lose. Silla’s cavalry comes at them first, out ahead of the Tang foot, because the king of Silla wants it written down later who went first.
blocks.ko: 강기슭에서는 백제 기병이 상륙지를 지킨다. 부흥군이 말에 태울 수 있는 마지막 사람들이다. 잃어서는 안 되는 문 앞에 서듯, 뭍에 끌어올린 배들 앞에 늘어서 있다. 신라 기병이 당의 보병보다 앞서 먼저 들이친다. 누가 먼저 갔는지 훗날 적혀 있기를 신라왕이 바라기 때문이다.

en: Riders. With me.
When they write this down in Chang’an, I want Silla in the first line.
lines: 장안에서 이걸 적을 때, 첫 줄에 신라가 있어야 한다.

blocks.html: The shore camp goes in one charge. Yushin watches it from the ridge with the reins loose in one hand, which is how old generals watch something they no longer need to do themselves.
blocks.ko: 강기슭의 진은 한 번의 돌격으로 무너진다. 유신은 고삐를 한 손에 느슨하게 쥔 채 능선에서 그것을 지켜본다. 이제는 몸소 할 필요가 없는 일을 늙은 장수들은 그렇게 지켜본다.

en: The unification of Samhan is not far off…

blocks.label: The Twenty-Seventh Day
blocks.ko: 스무이레

blocks.html: The first Yamato ships to arrive do not wait for the rest. They row straight at the Tang line on the evening water, and the Tang line does not move. It does not chase them, either. When the Yamato boats fall back, the hundred and seventy are exactly where they were that morning, in the same order, at anchor.
blocks.ko: 먼저 도착한 야마토의 배들은 나머지를 기다리지 않는다. 저녁 물을 타고 당의 대열로 곧장 저어 간다. 당의 대열은 움직이지 않는다. 쫓지도 않는다. 야마토의 배들이 물러났을 때, 백칠십 척은 아침에 있던 그 자리에 같은 순서로 닻을 내리고 있다.

blocks.html: The Black Tortoise has seen men of Wa once before, in the emperor's city. They were envoys in court silk, and they bowed in all the right places. The court kept them in a guesthouse for two winters, so they couldn't carry home where the fleet was going. These are their cousins. They row standing up. They shout from too far away. They charge a hundred and seventy anchored hulls in boats built for rice. Nobody in his army has fought them before. He watches the first wave break on his line like a scholar reading a new script. He is looking for the grammar.
blocks.ko: 현무는 왜인을 한 번 본 적이 있다. 황제의 도성에서였다. 비단 조복을 입은 사신들이었고, 절할 자리마다 꼬박꼬박 절했다. 조정은 그들을 두 겨울 동안 객관에 붙잡아 두었다. 함대가 어디로 가는지 고국에 전하지 못하게. 지금 저들은 그 사신들의 사촌쯤 된다. 선 채로 노를 젓는다. 소용없는 거리에서 고함을 지른다. 쌀 나르는 배로, 닻 내린 백칠십 척에 곧장 달려든다. 그의 군대에서 이들과 싸워 본 사람은 없다. 그는 첫 물결이 전열에 부서지는 것을 지켜본다. 처음 보는 글자를 읽는 학자처럼. 문법을 찾으면서.

en: General— those are Wa? They’re…
…they’re rowing standing up.
The last Wa I saw were bowing to the Son of Heaven.
Watch their oars, not their faces. The faces will stay brave all day.
lines: 내가 마지막으로 본 왜인은 천자께 절을 하고 있었지.
얼굴 말고 노를 봐라. 얼굴은 하루 종일 용감할 테니.

en: Nobody chases.
Tomorrow they will all come back together, and they will come angry.
lines: 내일 저들이 한꺼번에 돌아올 것이다. 화가 나서.

blocks.label: The Twenty-Eighth Day
blocks.ko: 스무여드레

blocks.html: That night the Yamato captains and the king of Baekje hold council on a deck, and nobody looks at the sky. Abe no Hirafu does most of the talking. He is the rear general, a big man in a wolf-fur mantle who spent three summers chasing the Emishi along the cold northern coast, and he has the habit of men who have lived through bad water: he believes the sea gives way to whoever moves first.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 야마토의 장수들과 백제왕은 갑판 위에서 군의를 연다. 아무도 하늘을 보지 않는다. 말은 대부분 아베노 히라부가 한다. 후장군인 그는 늑대 털 망토를 두른 덩치 큰 사내로, 세 해 여름을 북쪽 찬 바다 해안에서 에미시를 쫓으며 보냈다. 험한 물에서 살아 돌아온 사람들의 버릇이 그에게도 있다. 바다는 먼저 움직이는 쪽에 길을 내준다고 믿는 것이다.

en: Yesterday was the vanguard. Today it’s all of us!
Ha— we go first. Whoever hits first, the other side gives way. That’s the sea. Every sea.
lines: 어제 건 선봉이었소. 오늘은 전부 가는 거요!
하— 우리가 먼저 치는 거요. 먼저 들이받는 쪽 앞에서 저쪽은 물러나게 돼 있소. 바다란 게 그렇소. 어느 바다든.

en: …Yes. First.
Let them see the king’s ship at the front.
lines: 왕의 배가 맨 앞에 있는 것을 저들이 보게 하시오.

en: The tide turns before noon.
…Nobody is listening. Good. Then I will go first too.
lines: …아무도 듣지 않는군. 좋소. 그럼 나도 먼저 가겠소.

blocks.title: The Baekgang, eighth month, 663

units.label: Tang fire & crossbow
units.sub: waiting on the turn of tide

units.label: Buyeo Yung
units.sub: on the Tang deck, against his brother

blocks.note: Four charges into a formed Tang line, against the tide, in a river mouth too narrow for the eastern numbers. Smoke, flame, and a cinnabar sea.

blocks.html: The first charge hits a wall of hulls. The second finds the current turning against them — Tang waits for that turn the way a patient general waits for thirst. On the third and fourth, fire travels faster than orders: arrows wrapped for flame, ships brushed together until one burning deck becomes a neighbourhood. Four hundred eastern ships do not sink so much as spend themselves into light.
blocks.ko: 첫 돌격은 선체의 벽에 부딪친다. 두 번째는 물살이 거꾸로 도는 것을 만난다 — 당은 목마른 자를 기다리듯 그 돌음을 기다렸다. 세 번째와 네 번째에 불이 명령보다 빠르다: 불붙인 화살, 갑판이 서로 스쳐 한 척의 불길이 이웃이 된다. 왜의 배 사백 척은 가라앉는다기보다, 빛으로 자신을 써 버린다.

blocks.hanja: 焚其舟四百艘 煙焰漲天 海水皆赤
blocks.ko: 그 배 사백 척을 불사르니, 연기와 불꽃이 하늘에 가득하고, 바닷물이 모두 붉었다.
blocks.html: They burned four hundred of their ships; smoke and flame filled the sky, and the seawater was all red.
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 84, Liu Renkui (劉仁軌) — Battle of the White River mouth (663) · cf. Samguk Sagi bk. 28, Baekje Annals: 煙炎灼天 海水爲丹

blocks.html: Then the wings close. The Tang ships that looked like a wall turn out to have been a door with two leaves, and they swing shut from left and right around the Yamato centre, so tight that the eastern ships cannot turn bow or stern, and men who cannot row and cannot climb go into the water in their armour.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 양 날개가 닫힌다. 벽처럼 보이던 당의 배들은 알고 보니 두 짝짜리 문이었고, 그 문이 좌우에서 야마토의 중군을 감싸며 닫힌다. 너무 빽빽해서 왜의 배들은 이물도 고물도 돌리지 못하고, 노를 저을 수도 기어오를 수도 없는 사람들이 갑옷을 입은 채로 물에 뛰어든다.

blocks.html: From the king’s ship Pung can see the far bank, and on it the Silla banners his father’s enemy raised and did not live to see here.
blocks.ko: 왕의 배에서 풍은 건너편 언덕을 볼 수 있다. 그 위에, 아버지의 원수가 세웠으나 살아서 이곳에서 보지는 못한 신라의 깃발들이 있다.

en: Chunchu, you wretch… how dare you, to His Majesty…!
Long live Kudara — Land of the Heavenly Deer….!
ja: 百済万歳……！
jaLatn: Kudara banzai…!

blocks.html: His ship is burning under him and he does not leave it. He fights on the deck until there is not enough deck left to fight on.
blocks.ko: 발밑의 배가 타고 있는데 그는 배를 떠나지 않는다. 싸울 갑판이 남지 않을 때까지 갑판 위에서 싸운다.

en: Baekje must survive….
ja: 百済は生き残らねばならない……。
jaLatn: Kudara wa ikinokoraneba naranai….

blocks.hanja: 朴市田來津仰天而誓，切齒而嗔，殺數十人，於焉戰死。
blocks.html: Echi no Takutsu looked up to heaven and swore an oath, gnashed his teeth in fury, killed some dozens of men, and there fell in battle.
blocks.ko: 에치노 다쿠쓰는 하늘을 우러러 맹세하고 이를 갈며 성내어 수십 명을 죽이고, 거기서 싸우다 죽었다.
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 27, Tenji 2 (663), eighth month

en: Hold the line. Let the tide finish what the bowstrings began.
A river mouth is a judge. Today it judged the East.
lines: 대열을 지켜라. 활시위가 시작한 일을 밀물이 끝내게 두어라.

blocks.html: At the back of the fleet Abe no Hirafu’s ships are still afloat. He has seen a lost tide before, on a colder sea. He turns them for home and hauls in every swimmer the hulls will carry, men in half their armour, men with no oars, and he does not laugh again until Tsukushi.
blocks.ko: 함대 맨 뒤에서 아베노 히라부의 배들은 아직 떠 있다. 진 물때는 전에도 본 적이 있다. 더 찬 바다에서. 그는 뱃머리를 고향으로 돌리고, 배가 버틸 수 있는 만큼 헤엄치는 자들을 끌어올린다. 갑옷을 반쯤 벗은 자, 노도 없는 자. 그리고 쓰쿠시에 닿을 때까지 다시는 웃지 않는다.

blocks.label: Brothers
blocks.ko: 형제

blocks.html: In the smoke a small boat gets away from the king’s ship with a handful of men in it and turns north. It is Pung. He leaves behind his fleet, his allies, his capital on the hill, and his sword.
blocks.ko: 연기 속에서 작은 배 한 척이 몇 사람을 태우고 왕의 배를 빠져나와 북쪽으로 머리를 돌린다. 풍이다. 그는 함대도, 동맹도, 언덕 위의 도읍도, 그리고 제 칼도 두고 간다.

blocks.html: They bring the sword to the Tang flagship. It is a Baekje ring-pommel blade with the ring worn smooth, nothing like a king’s, and the Black Tortoise hands it to the one man aboard who would know.
blocks.ko: 칼은 당의 기함으로 올라온다. 고리가 닳아 매끈해진 백제의 환두대도다. 왕의 칼 같은 데는 하나도 없다. 현무는 그것을 배 위에서 알아볼 단 한 사람에게 건넨다.

en: Whose?
…My brother’s.
Our father gave it to him the year they sent him east. He was seven.
lines: 동쪽으로 보내던 해에 아버지께서 주셨소. 일곱 살이었소.

en: Shall I send boats after him?
…North is Goguryeo. Let Goguryeo keep him.
He was always better at being sent away than I was.
lines: 그 애는 늘 나보다 떠나보내지는 데 능했소.

blocks.label: Juryu
blocks.ko: 주류

blocks.html: Juryu holds ten more days without its king. On the seventh day of the ninth month it opens its gate. Pung’s younger brothers, the princes Chungseung and Chungji, walk out at the head of what is left: soldiers, women, the Yamato men who missed the boats, and an envoy from Tamla who came up the hill to bargain for an island and is now surrendering for it.
blocks.ko: 주류는 왕 없이 열흘을 더 버틴다. 구월 이렛날 성문이 열린다. 풍의 아우들, 충승 왕자와 충지 왕자가 남은 것들의 맨 앞에서 걸어 나온다. 군사들, 여자들, 배를 놓친 야마토 사람들, 그리고 섬 하나를 흥정하러 산을 올랐다가 이제 그 섬을 위해 항복하는 탐라의 사신.

blocks.html: The people who are not surrendering go south, toward the port at Terye where the Yamato ships will take them off. On the road they say the thing to one another that the Yamato chronicle wrote down, because nobody was left in Baekje to write it.
blocks.ko: 항복하지 않는 사람들은 남쪽으로, 야마토의 배가 그들을 태워 갈 테례성 포구로 간다. 길 위에서 그들은 서로에게 그 말을 한다. 야마토의 사서가 받아 적은 말이다. 백제에는 그것을 적을 사람이 남지 않았으니까.

blocks.hanja: 州柔降矣，事無奈何。百濟之名，絕于今日。丘墓之所，豈能復往。
blocks.html: Juryu has surrendered. Nothing more can be done. The name of Baekje ends today. The place of our ancestors’ graves — how can we ever go back to it?
blocks.ko: 주류가 항복하였으니 일은 어찌할 수 없다. 백제의 이름은 오늘로 끊어졌다. 조상의 무덤이 있는 곳을 어찌 다시 갈 수 있으랴.
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 27, Tenji 2 (663), ninth month

blocks.html: One fortress doesn't hear it. Its commander shuts the gate and holds all autumn, and the siege goes home. In the end it falls to its own people's hands. Sangji and Sangya have changed sides. The Black Tortoise hands back their armour and points them up the slope.
blocks.ko: 한 성만은 그 말을 듣지 않는다. 성주는 문을 닫고 가을 내내 버티고, 포위군은 돌아간다. 결국 그 성은 제 나라 사람 손에 떨어진다. 상지와 상여가 편을 바꾼 것이다. 현무는 그들에게 갑옷을 돌려주고 비탈 위를 가리킨다.

en: The north wall is the low one.
I built it.

blocks.html: Ji Subsin leaves his wife and children inside and goes north to Goguryeo, which by now is where Baekje’s last kings go.
blocks.ko: 지수신은 아내와 자식들을 성안에 두고 북쪽 고구려로 간다. 이제 백제의 마지막 왕들이 가는 곳이 그곳이다.

blocks.html: When the water cools to ordinary colour again, the restoration has no fleet worth the word. The Black Tortoise sits down with Kim Yushin. Neither of them believes a word the other says, and they get a great deal done — which is how alliances sound after four hundred ships have paid for the silence.
blocks.ko: 물이 다시 평범한 빛으로 식으면, 부흥에는 함대라 부를 것이 없다. 현무가 김유신과 마주 앉는다. 둘 다 상대의 말을 한마디도 믿지 않으면서, 아주 많은 것을 정한다 — 배 사백 척이 그 침묵의 값을 치른 뒤의 동맹이란 그런 소리다.

blocks.html: Two reapers failed to take Yeon Gesomun at the river. The ledger still has his name in it…!
blocks.ko: 두 저승사자는 강에서 연개소문을 데려가지 못했다. 장부에는 아직 그의 이름이 적혀 있다…!

images.alt: Aged Gesomun on a timber deathbed talking; calm Yumla stands at the bedside — only these two, one violet lamp
images.prompt: Painterly anime-adjacent cinema, halfway realistic. Intimate 16:9. Pitch-black room, one violet lamp. Aged Gesomun LIES on a low timber deathbed. Yumla STANDS leaning down to talk. Violet #7c3aed. Only these two. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: The attached portrait is a likeness hint only.
images.prompt: Traditional sumi on bare Xuan paper, real brush bones: pressed start, thick belly, dry split tail, flying white. Not a modern graphic. The attached portrait is a likeness hint only. Do not paste it. ONE device: a low horizontal bed-stroke. An old man lies on it, a few bony marks, beard a dry flick. A second tiny figure stands at the head, leaning. One violet-dark lamp speck, real pigment, not a glow. Vast empty paper. No text, no seal, no watermark.

images.alt: The Eternal General on his deathbed, his sons gathered close
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of yeon deathbed, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (665), scene: The Death of Yeon Gesomun, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: That is precisely why I am telling you.
images.alt: Mantegna’s Lamentation: Gesomun dying, foreshortened from his feet, his crow swords on the wall above, his sons at the edge
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Mantegna’s Lamentation of Christ. Extreme foreshortening from the foot of the bed: Yeon Gesomun lies on his back on a low bed under a red coverlet, old now, the soles of his bare feet huge in the foreground, his head raised a little on the pillow, eyes open and hard. On the black wall above the bed his five crow-ring swords hang in their scabbards, two drawn a hand-width so the steel shows. At the left edge his sons Namseng and Namgun lean in, faces half lit. One oil lamp beside the pillow is the only light, raking along his body and up the bared steel; the room drowns in black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | YEON NAMSENG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_namseng.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Gesomun's eldest; heir who kneels west in 666. Fighting: His father's forward grip with one crow sword — never his father's two. #c25a4e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | YEON NAMGUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_namgun.png (face only; invent a new pose). #9e3b32 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: King Yumla
blocks.ko: 염라대왕

blocks.html: The Eternal General is dying.
blocks.ko: 영원의 대장군이 죽어 가고 있다.

en: Do not… fight amongst yourselves…

lines: 아버지는 형제를 곁에 두신 적이 없습니다.
하나는 남쪽 국경 끝으로 보내셨고, 나머지는 다 베어 버리셨죠.
en: Father.
You never kept a brother close.
One you sent to the far end of the southern border. The rest you cut down.
…That is precisely why I am telling you.

blocks.hanja: 汝等兄弟 和如魚水 勿爭爵位 若不如是 必爲隣咲
blocks.html: You brothers, be as close as fish and water. Do not quarrel over rank. If you do not heed this, you will surely be the laughingstock of your neighbours.
blocks.ko: 너희 형제는 물고기와 물처럼 화목하고, 벼슬을 두고 다투지 마라. 그렇지 않으면 반드시 이웃의 웃음거리가 될 것이다.
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 27, Emperor Tenji, yr. 3 (664) — the dying words of the Goguryeo minister 蓋金

blocks.html: He expects one of them — Kangrim with his Question, or Haewonmek with his last words. He has been rehearsing a refusal.
blocks.ko: 그는 둘 중 하나를 기대한다. 물음을 든 강림, 아니면 유언을 묻는 해원맥. 거절할 대사는 이미 연습해 두었다.

en: …Which of you failed me at the Snake River?
Come on. Ask. I am ready to say no again.
lines: 자. 물어라. 이번에도 아니라고 할 준비는 됐다.

blocks.html: It is not either of them. Purple of sentence, not crow-dark of the fetch — Yumla himself stands in the room. The judge, not the clerks. A king for a king.
blocks.ko: 둘 중 아무도 아니다. 거둬 가는 자의 까마귀빛이 아니라 판결의 자주빛 — 염라 본인이 방에 서 있다. 서기가 아니라 심판관. 왕에게 왕.

en: Yeon Gesomun.
My two best men could not bring you at the Snake River.
A man like you — only another king could carry you off.
Consider the courtesy returned.
lines: 내 두 최고의 부하가 사수에서 그대를 데려오지 못했지.
그대 같은 사내 — 다른 왕이 아니면 데려갈 수 없다.

en: …Hah.
So the clerks failed, and the boss clocked in.
Fine. I always preferred dealing with the top.
lines: 좋아. 나는 원래 윗사람과 거래하는 편이니까.

en: The minutes will remember the joke.
Now — walk. Judgment keeps better hours than Supreme Commanders.
lines: 이제 — 걷거라. 심판은 대막리지보다 시간을 잘 지킨다.

blocks.html: Yeon catches a vision of something at the very end. A young man, centuries off, saying Goryeo as if it had never gone.
blocks.ko: 마지막 순간, 연의 눈앞에 무언가가 스친다. 몇백 년 뒤의 젊은 사내 하나가, 사라진 적 없다는 듯 고려라는 이름을 입에 올린다.

blocks.html: He dies in his sleep, which is not how anyone expected it to go.
blocks.ko: 그는 잠결에 숨을 거둔다. 누구도 그러리라 예상하지 않았던 방식으로.

lines: 야... 그런 사람도 결국 염라 앞엔 서긴 하네.
en: Well… even a man like that stands before Yumla in the end.

blocks.html: His eldest, Namseng, takes on the title of Supreme Commander. He is thirty-one, and it is very heavy.
blocks.ko: 맏아들 남생이 대막리지의 자리를 잇는다. 서른한 살이다. 그 자리는 아주 무겁다.

blocks.caption: His father’s chair. It was built for one man, and it shows.
blocks.ko: 아버지의 자리. 한 사람을 위해 짠 자리라, 티가 난다.

blocks.html: Yeon Jungto, who raised the two younger boys at his own table, is at the southern border when the news comes. He writes to Namgun that night. The answer, when it comes, is in a secretary’s hand.
blocks.ko: 두 어린 조카를 제 밥상에서 키운 연정토는 그 소식이 왔을 때 남쪽 국경에 있다. 그는 그날 밤 남건에게 편지를 쓴다. 답장은, 오기는 오는데, 서기의 글씨다.

en: Gesomun… he really did have a gift, didn’t he.

lines: 개소문 어른께서 살아 계셨으면 이런 꼴은 안 났지.
en: If the old man were alive we would not be in this state.

blocks.html: — Yeon Gesomun —
blocks.ko: — 연개소문 —

blocks.html: Every single thing he said about his country was correct. The court was rotten. The tribute was a slow surrender. Taizong was coming whether or not they were polite about it. He was the only man in the room who could see it, and he was right, and being right is what destroyed him.
blocks.ko: 제 나라에 대해 그가 한 말은 하나도 빠짐없이 옳았다. 조정은 썩었다. 조공은 느린 항복이었다. 황제는 그들이 예의를 갖추든 말든 올 것이었다. 그 방에서 그것을 볼 수 있는 사람은 그뿐이었고, 그는 옳았다. 그리고 옳았다는 것이 그를 무너뜨렸다.

blocks.html: Because a man who is right and impatient does not build. He replaces. He killed the council and became the council. He killed the command and became the command. For twenty-two years Goguryeo did not need institutions, because it had him, and he was better than institutions — faster, braver, entirely unaccountable.
blocks.ko: 옳으면서 성마른 사람은 세우지 않는다. 갈아치운다. 그는 회의를 죽이고 회의가 되었다. 군령을 죽이고 군령이 되었다. 스물두 해 동안 고구려에는 제도가 필요 없었다. 그가 있었으니까. 그리고 그는 제도보다 나았다 — 더 빠르고, 더 담대하고, 누구에게도 책임지지 않았다.

blocks.html: He outlasted the Second Emperor’s war and broke the White Tiger at the Snake River with his own hands, and every victory made the kingdom lean on him a little harder, until the whole weight of it rested on one man’s spine. A spine is a magnificent thing, but no one has ever built a house on one.
blocks.ko: 그는 황제의 전쟁을 버텨 냈고 사수의 백호를 제 손으로 부수었으며, 그 승리 하나하나가 나라로 하여금 그에게 조금씩 더 기대게 만들었다. 마침내 그 모든 무게가 한 사내의 등뼈 위에 얹혔다. 등뼈는 훌륭한 것이지만, 등뼈 위에 집을 지은 사람은 없다.

blocks.html: His last words were: do not fight one another. His eldest son answered that he had never kept a brother close: one sent to the border, the rest cut down. Both of them were telling the truth, and neither of them could hear it.
blocks.ko: 그의 마지막 말은 이러했다. 서로 싸우지 말아라. 맏아들은 아버지께서는 형제를 곁에 두신 적이 없노라고, 하나는 국경으로 보내고 나머지는 다 베어 버리셨노라고 대답했다. 둘 다 진실을 말하고 있었고, 둘 다 그것을 듣지 못했다.

blocks.html: He held the north for a generation and left nothing behind him that could hold it for a year. Nine months after they buried him his sons were at war with each other. Twenty-six months after that his eldest was riding west to show the Third Emperor the road in.
blocks.ko: 그는 한 세대 동안 북방을 지켰고, 그것을 일 년이라도 지탱할 무엇도 남기지 않았다. 그를 묻은 지 아홉 달 만에 아들들은 서로 전쟁을 벌였다. 그로부터 스물여섯 달 뒤, 맏아들은 황제에게 들어오는 길을 일러 주러 서쪽으로 말을 몰았다.

blocks.html: “Do not fight amongst yourselves.” He had three sons. How long do you think that lasts?
blocks.ko: “서로 싸우지 마라.” 아들은 셋이었다. 그 말이 얼마나 갈 것 같은가?

blocks.html: The Third Emperor invades Goguryeo again. Nobody is counting anymore. This time, he has a guide.
blocks.ko: 황제가 또 고구려를 친다. 몇 번째인지 이제 아무도 세지 않는다. 이번에는 길잡이가 있다.

lines: 짐이 이미 백제를 멸하여 너희 나라의 근심을 제거하였는데, 이제 고려가 지리의 험함을 믿고 예맥(穢貊)과 함께 악한 짓을 하여 큰 나라를 섬기는 예를 어기고 이웃 나라와 사이좋게 지내는 의리를 저버리고 있다. 짐은 병사를 보내어 치려고 하니, 너도 돌아가 너희 국왕에게 고하여 군대를 출동시켜 우리와 함께 망해가는 오랑캐를 섬멸케 하라.
en: I have already destroyed Baekje and removed your country’s worry; yet now Goryeo trusts in the ruggedness of its land, joins the Yemaek in wickedness, breaks the rite of serving a great state, and abandons the duty of living peaceably with its neighbours. I am sending soldiers to strike it — so return and tell your king to send out his army, and with us annihilate these failing barbarians.
zh: 朕已滅百濟，除爾國之憂；而高麗恃險，連穢貊為惡，失事大之禮，棄睦鄰之義。朕將發兵討之——歸告爾王出師，與我共滅此將亡之蠻夷。
zhLatn: Zhèn yǐ miè Bǎijì, chú ěr guó zhī yōu; ér Gāolí shì xiǎn, lián Huìmò wéi è, shī shì dà zhī lǐ, qì mùlín zhī yì. Zhèn jiāng fābīng tǎo zhī——guī gào ěr wáng chūshī, yǔ wǒ gòng miè cǐ jiāng wáng zhī mányí.

blocks.label: The Provinces
blocks.ko: 지방 순시

blocks.html: In the spring Namseng goes out to inspect the provinces, as a new Supreme Commander should, and leaves his two younger brothers to keep the capital.
blocks.ko: 봄, 남생은 새 대막리지답게 지방 순시에 나서고, 두 아우에게 도성을 맡긴다.

blocks.html: Within a month there are men whispering in both directions. To Namgun and Namsan: your brother means to be rid of you when he comes back. To Namseng, at every post station: your brothers do not mean to let you back in.
blocks.ko: 한 달이 못 되어 양쪽으로 귓속말하는 자들이 생긴다. 남건과 남산에게는, 형님이 돌아오면 너희를 치울 생각이라고. 역참마다 남생에게는, 아우들이 형님을 들이지 않을 생각이라고.

lines: …그래도 한 사람 돌려보내라. 조용히. 저녁 자리에서 무슨 말들을 하는지 알고 싶다.
en: Nonsense. They are my brothers.
…Send someone back anyway. Quietly. I want to know what they say at supper.

blocks.html: The man he sends is caught at the Pyongyang gate within the week. Namgun reads the orders found on him twice, and the second time he reads them as a confession.
blocks.ko: 그가 보낸 자는 한 주 만에 평양 성문에서 붙잡힌다. 남건은 그 몸에서 나온 지시를 두 번 읽고, 두 번째에는 자백으로 읽는다.

lines: 성문 닫아라! 폐하께 아뢰어라, 대막리지가 반역했다고!
en: He sends spies. To his own brothers.
Shut the gates! Tell the king the Supreme Commander has rebelled!

blocks.html: A messenger comes to the provincial camp with an urgent message. Namseng meets him in his quarters.
blocks.ko: 전령이 급보를 들고 순시 중인 진영으로 온다. 남생이 처소에서 그를 맞는다.

blocks.html: He rides back to his own capital and finds the gate shut. His brother comes up onto the wall.
blocks.ko: 그는 제 도성으로 말을 몰아 돌아오고, 성문이 닫혀 있는 것을 본다. 아우가 성벽 위로 올라온다.

en: Open the gate, Namgun.
You are speaking to the Supreme Commander.

lines: 이런 건방진 것이... 아닐, 그러면 어떻게 하란 말이냐?
en: Insolent— no. Then what would you have me do?
Traitor.
Traitor…?

lines: 조선이 어떻게 몰락되었습니까? 왕의 최측근의 배신 때문이였죠.
원래 인간이 높을수록, 그 그림자도 길다고 들었습니다.
개소문 사후, 고려에는 그의 그림자에 미칠 자도 없을 것입니다.
en: How did Joseon fall? Through the betrayal of the king’s closest men.
They say the taller a man stands, the longer his shadow.
After Gesomun, there is no one in Goryeo who can reach even his shadow.
And his sons—

blocks.html: Namseng goes north to the old capital at Gungnae, and sends his son to Chang’an to ask the Third Emperor for an army.
blocks.ko: 남생은 북쪽 옛 도읍 국내성으로 가서, 아들을 장안에 보내 황제에게 군대를 청한다.

blocks.html: Namseng was afraid and dared not go in. Namgun killed Namseng's son Heonchung. Namseng fled to hold Gungnae Fortress, went over to Tang with his followers and his Khitan and Mohe troops, and sent his son Heonseong to plead his case.
blocks.ko: 남생은 두려워 감히 들어가지 못하였다. 남건은 남생의 아들 헌충을 죽였다. 남생은 국내성으로 달아나 지키며, 제 무리와 거란·말갈 병사를 거느리고 당에 붙어, 아들 헌성을 보내 하소연하게 하였다.
blocks.hanja: 男生懼不敢入。男建殺其子獻忠，男生走保國內城，率其衆與契丹、靺鞨兵附唐，遣子獻誠訴之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun (with Namseng)

blocks.html: His heart was loyal, but matters went wrong at the centre. He had just gone out to comfort the border folk and tour the wild marches, to survey the old lands of the dawn country and ask for new officers to govern them. Then his two younger brothers, Namsan and Namgun, turned vicious and rebellious in a single morning. Heartless to their own blood, they raised troops and shut him out from within. His little son with the gold ring fell suddenly into the whale's jaws, and left the long table and his parents' arms for ever.
blocks.ko: 공은 속마음으로 정성을 다했으나, 일은 조정 한가운데서 어그러졌다. 공이 막 변방 백성을 어루만지고 거친 들을 순시하러 나가, 동쪽 옛 땅을 살피고 새 관원을 청하려 할 때였다. 두 아우 남산과 남건이 하루아침에 흉악하게 패역하여, 혈육도 아랑곳없이 군사를 일으켜 안에서 막아섰다. 금고리를 찬 어린 아들은 졸지에 고래 아가리에 떨어져, 진수성찬 차린 긴 자리와 부모의 품을 문득 떠났다.
blocks.hanja: 公情思內款，事乖中執。方欲出撫邊甿，外巡荒甸，按嵎夷之舊壤，請羲仲之新官。二弟產建，一朝兇悖，能忍無親，稱兵內拒。金環幼子，忽就鯨鯢，玉膳長筵，俄辭顧復。
blocks.source: Epitaph of Yeon Namseng (泉男生墓誌) — Luoyang, 679; transcription in the Korean Ancient History DB (한국 고대 사료 DB)

blocks.label: Defection of Yeon Namseng
blocks.ko: 연남생의 투항

blocks.html: Namseng rides west, across the river his father spent a lifetime holding.
blocks.ko: 남생은 서쪽으로 말을 몬다. 아버지가 평생을 걸어 지킨 그 강을 건너서.

blocks.caption: North to the old capital, then west over the Liao. His father spent a lifetime stopping men riding this road the other way.
blocks.ko: 북쪽 옛 도읍으로, 다시 서쪽으로 요하를 건너. 아버지는 평생 이 길을 반대로 달려오는 자들을 막았다.

en: Goryeo is nothing but swindlers and thieves —
a people beyond hope.

lines: …아버님께서 요하에서 만난 아이 이야기를 하신 적이 있소.
en: …My father spoke of a boy he met at the Liao.
One who would not kneel.
zh: ……先帝說過，在遼水遇見一個孩子。
zhLatn: …Xiāndì shuō guò, zài Liáoshuǐ yùjiàn yí ge háizi.
Bù kěn xiàguì de.

lines: 스무 해 전입니다, 폐하. 선제와 저. 선제께서 요수를 건너오셨을 때.
en: Twenty years ago, Majesty. Your father and I, when he crossed the Liao.
I did not kneel then.

blocks.html: He is thirty-two years old, and his brother has taken his title, his city and his father’s seat, and this is the second time in his life he has been offered a house in Chang’an. Nobody flogs him for the answer this time.
blocks.ko: 그는 서른둘이고, 아우가 그의 관작과 도성과 아버지의 자리를 빼앗았으며, 장안의 집을 제안받은 것은 평생 두 번째다. 이번에는 그 대답 때문에 매를 맞지 않는다.

lines: 페하께선, 혼자는 결코 삼한정벌은 못 하실 겁니다.
en: Your Majesty will never conquer Samhan alone.
Emperor… Your Majesty… ten thousand years…!

blocks.html: Namseng is given a Tang title, and a vanguard command against his own country.
blocks.ko: 남생은 당의 관작과 함께, 제 나라를 치는 선봉의 지휘를 받는다.

blocks.html: In the south their uncle Yeon Jungto, who raised two of them, waits to hear which nephew will send for him. Neither does. He takes twelve cities over to Silla, and the family is finished in three directions at once.
blocks.ko: 남쪽에서는 그 둘을 키운 숙부 연정토가 어느 조카가 자기를 부르러 올지 기다린다. 아무도 오지 않는다. 그는 열두 성을 들고 신라로 넘어가고, 그 집안은 한꺼번에 세 방향에서 끝난다.

blocks.html: Namseng knows the road in. Now he rides it home, with the whole Tang army at his back…!
blocks.ko: 남생은 들어가는 길을 안다. 이제 그는 당의 대군을 등 뒤에 달고, 그 길로 집에 돌아온다…!
