images.alt: The Gwanghwamun Admiral Yi statue, painted: old Yushin as the towering bronze general, ring-pommel sword planted, Pyongyang’s walls behind
images.prompt: A painted parody of the ADMIRAL YI SUN-SIN STATUE at Gwanghwamun: an oil painting of the towering dark bronze monument seen from a steep worm’s-eye angle on its tall stone pedestal, thick brushwork, bronze glinting. Same pose: a standing general in armor, feet apart, looking far ahead, a long sword held upright in front of him in its scabbard, both hands resting on it. The general is the old KIM YUSHIN (attached old portrait: face, white beard) in bronze steel lamellar (attached ref), marshal-blue #2A5FB8 cloth peeking at the collar as patina; the sword is the attached ring-pommel 환두대도, small ring pommel up. Behind the pedestal, the red two-tier gate pavilion and stone walls of the attached Pyongyang fortress under a wide autumn sky. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

blocks.label: The Ninth Invasion
blocks.ko: 제9차 침공

blocks.html: Three of the emperor's four beasts come for the city at once. The Blue Dragon leads. The Black Tortoise and the second White Tiger ride behind him.
blocks.ko: 황제의 네 짐승 가운데 셋이 한꺼번에 이 성으로 온다. 청룡이 앞장선다. 현무와 두 번째 백호가 뒤를 따른다.

blocks.caption: Three beasts, three roads, one city.
blocks.ko: 짐승 셋, 길 셋, 성 하나.

en: Breaking a fortress… is like farming.
You know the season, you bring the water, you harvest.
Today is a harvest day.
zhLatn: Pòchéng… rú nóngshì.
Zhī shíjié, yǐn shuǐ, shōugē.
Jīnrì shì shōuchéng zhī rì.

blocks.html: There is no cruelty in him, which is precisely what makes him difficult: the men of Goguryeo can hate a butcher, but they cannot quite hate a farmer who treats siege-work as weather.
blocks.ko: 그에게는 잔인함이 없고, 바로 그래서 상대하기가 어렵다. 고구려 사람들은 학살자라면 미워할 수 있다. 그러나 공성을 날씨처럼 다루는 농부는, 끝까지 미워하기가 어렵다.

en: Brother…
At last… I set foot on Pyongyang’s ground—
Goguryeo… never dies….!

blocks.label: Betrayal from Inside
blocks.ko: 안에서 열린 문

blocks.html: When the Tang ring closes, Namgun needs one man nobody can buy. He picks a monk. Shinsung has kept a small temple at the foot of the hill for twenty-five years. He has never asked anyone for anything.
blocks.ko: 당의 포위가 조여 오자, 남건에게는 아무도 살 수 없는 사람 하나가 필요하다. 그는 승려를 고른다. 신성은 언덕 아래 작은 절을 스물다섯 해 지켜 왔다. 누구에게도 무엇 하나 청한 적이 없다.

lines: 스님은 가문도 없고, 파벌도 없고, 자식도 없소.
이 성에서 성을 팔아넘기는 게 상상이 안 되는 사람은 스님뿐이오.
en: You have no clan, no faction, no sons.
You’re the only man in this city I can’t imagine selling it.

lines: 그럼 대막리지의 상상에 걸맞도록 애써 보겠습니다.
en: Then I shall try to be worthy of your imagination, Mangniji.

blocks.html: For five days a novice walks out of the lesser house before dawn with an alms bowl and comes back with it empty, and nobody thinks to ask why a monk’s bowl should come back empty from the direction of the Tang lines. On the fifth night the bell that has sat on the floor of the lesser house since the year the Daoists came is struck once.
blocks.ko: 닷새 동안 한 사미승이 새벽마다 바리때를 들고 작은 절을 나섰다가 빈 바리때로 돌아온다. 스님의 바리때가 왜 당의 진 쪽에서 비어서 돌아오는지 아무도 묻지 않는다. 닷새째 밤, 도사들이 오던 해부터 작은 절 바닥에 놓여 있던 종이 한 번 울린다.

blocks.html: There is no peace in the three worlds; they are like a burning house, full of every suffering, truly to be feared. Always there are birth and age, sickness and death and grief: fires like these, blazing without end.
blocks.ko: 삼계는 편안함이 없어 불타는 집과 같으니, 온갖 괴로움이 가득하여 참으로 두렵다. 늘 나고 늙고 병들고 죽는 근심이 있어, 이러한 불길이 쉬지 않고 타오른다.
blocks.hanja: 三界無安，猶如火宅，眾苦充滿，甚可怖畏。常有生老、病死憂患，如是等火，熾然不息。
blocks.source: Lotus Sutra (妙法蓮華經) ch. 3, Parable (譬喻品), tr. Kumārajīva · T09n0262, p. 14c

blocks.html: Yeon once tried to starve the temples with the emperor's Daoists. The monks have waited a generation. Shinsung doesn't make a speech about doctrine. He opens a gate. Betrayal is a liturgy too. It's just performed from the inside.
blocks.ko: 연은 한때 황제의 도사들을 들여 절을 굶기려 했다. 승려들은 한 세대를 기다렸다. 신성은 교리를 연설하지 않는다. 문을 연다. 배신도 의례다. 안에서 올릴 뿐.

blocks.html: The monk Shinsung and general Yomyo open the gates of the Fortress, letting the Tang army inside.
blocks.ko: 승려 신성과 장수 요묘가 성문을 열어, 당군을 안으로 들인다.

blocks.label: Last Words
blocks.ko: 유언

blocks.html: Namgun is thirty-one. He leads the last stand against the Blue Dragon himself.
blocks.ko: 남건은 서른한 살이다. 청룡에 맞선 마지막 항전을 몸소 이끈다.

en: Silla’s sacred blood — rot!
Goguryeo will take the final victory!
You may rule this soil — our name will have the last word!
lines: 이 땅을 다스린다 해도 — 우리 이름이… 마지막에…!

blocks.html: The wall is already lost. He knows it. He says it anyway, to the men who can still hear, and to a bloodline across the river he can't see. Somebody, centuries from now, will be listening.
blocks.ko: 성벽은 이미 졌다. 그도 안다. 그래도 말한다. 아직 들을 수 있는 사람들에게, 강 건너 보이지 않는 핏줄에게. 몇백 년 뒤의 누군가가 그 말을 듣고 있을 것이다.

en: Goguryeo… never dies….!

blocks.html: When the gate towers burn, Namgun stabs himself in his own hall. He does it badly, the first thing he has done badly in the whole war, and the Tang surgeons save him so that he can be sent alive to the farthest edge of the empire.
blocks.ko: 문루가 불타자 남건은 제 전각에서 스스로를 찌른다. 서툴게 찌른다. 그 전쟁 내내 그가 처음으로 서툴게 한 일이다. 당의 의원들이 그를 살려 내고, 그는 산 채로 제국의 가장 먼 끝으로 보내진다.

blocks.html: When the city falls, the empire doesn't send a stranger to hold it. It sends Xue Rengui. The white coat becomes a banner over a broken capital. He governs well enough that even the conquered prefer him to chaos.
blocks.ko: 성이 떨어지자, 제국은 낯선 자를 보내지 않는다. 설인귀를 보낸다. 흰 전포가 무너진 도성 위의 깃발이 된다. 그는 정복당한 사람들조차 혼란보다는 그를 택할 만큼 다스린다.

lines: 나는… 여러분의 원수가 되고 싶지 않았습니다.
다만 폐하의 동쪽을, 빈손으로 둘 수는 없었습니다.
en: I… did not wish to be your enemy.
But I could not leave His Majesty’s east empty-handed.
zh: 但不能讓陛下之東空手而歸。
zhLatn: Wǒ… běn bù yuàn yǔ zhūwèi wéi dí.
Dàn bùnéng ràng Bìxià zhī dōng kōngshǒu ér guī.

blocks.html: The minutes are shorter than the kingdom. Goguryeo had stood seven hundred years. The king was taken to Chang’an. The record, for its part, writes only the month and the surrender.
blocks.ko: 기록은 나라보다 짧다. 고구려는 칠백 년을 섰다. 왕은 장안으로 잡혀 갔다. 편년은, 제 몫으로는, 달과 항복만을 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 九月 拔平壤城 高句麗王藏降
blocks.ko: 구월에 평양성을 함락하니, 고구려왕 장이 항복하였다.
blocks.html: In the ninth month they took Pyongyang Fortress; King Bojang of Goguryeo surrendered.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 22, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 27 (668), 9th month; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 328 · cf. Zizhi Tongjian Tang Zongzhang 1

blocks.html: Before the captives are shown to the living emperor, the Blue Dragon takes them up the mountain to show them to the dead one. The king of Goguryeo is made to bow at Zhaoling, in front of the door the Second Emperor said his horses would guard. The six stone horses stand in their row. The purple one is nearest the door.
blocks.ko: 포로들을 산 황제에게 보이기 전에, 청룡은 그들을 산 위로 데려가 죽은 황제에게 먼저 보인다. 고구려의 왕은 소릉에서, 선제가 제 말들이 지키리라 했던 그 문 앞에 절하게 된다. 여섯 돌말이 줄지어 서 있다. 자줏빛 말이 문에 가장 가깝다.

blocks.html: The seventeen grades stop at one another. In the tenth month, after the city is open, King Munmu cuts a rank the grades did not have, and gives it to the man who has been Marshal since the yard.
blocks.ko: 열일곱 관등은 서로에게서 멈춘다. 성이 열린 뒤 열째 달, 문무왕이 그 관등에 없던 자리를 하나 베어, 연무장에서부터 대장군이던 사람에게 준다.

en: Marshal.
Majesty.
You have been Marshal since before I could hold a bow.
The yard still says it.
The seventeen grades do not reach you anymore.
The word is enough.
I know what I am.
There was already a grade above the seventeen.
I had them cut one above that.
태대각간. Supreme General.

blocks.caption: A rank above every rank. They had to invent it for him.
blocks.ko: 모든 품계 위의 품계. 그를 위해 새로 만들어야 했다.

en: A new name for an old man.
It is the name of the man who opened this city.
Wear it.
You may keep Marshal for the boys on the yard.
…As you command.

blocks.html: The story isn’t over yet. The Third Emperor still controls large swaths of Samhan. The final war begins…!
blocks.ko: 이야기는 아직 끝나지 않았다. 황제는 여전히 삼한의 넓은 땅을 쥐고 있다. 마지막 전쟁이 시작된다…!

toneNote: Ally turns on ally; victory measured in what survives, not what is won.
title: Silla-Tang War

images.at: cleaning a stall that is empty
images.alt: Old Yushin scrubs Hanseul's empty stall; Munmu stops at the stall door.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior night, a timber stable in Surabol. Low three-quarter from the straw. ONE device: a dark wooden stall partition as a hard vertical splitting the frame. Kim Yushin, seventy, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait with the beard gone grey, plain blue po, sleeves tied back, bent over a brush scrubbing the boards of an EMPTY stall; on the peg above him hangs an old halter with a white horsehair caught in it. At the stall door, King Munmu, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, crimson robe, has stopped with one hand on the gatepost and does not come in. No horse in frame — the empty stall is the subject. A lantern hung on a post rakes gold across the straw, the timber grain and Yushin's knuckles; Silla blue #2A5FB8 catching in his sleeve. Foreground: out-of-focus straw and a wooden water bucket. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: Bear Ford
blocks.ko: 웅진

blocks.html: Two springs after the river, the empire names a governor for what is left of Baekje. It is Buyeo Yung. He once knelt at Bupmin's horse and was spat on. Then he went to the emperor's city and came back in imperial robes. Now he will rule from the fortress where his father was arrested.
blocks.ko: 강의 싸움이 끝나고 두 번째 봄, 제국은 남은 백제를 맡을 도독을 세운다. 부여융이다. 그는 한때 법민의 말 앞에 꿇어 침을 맞았다. 그러고는 황제의 도성에 갔다가 황제의 관복을 입고 돌아왔다. 이제 그는 아버지가 붙잡혀 간 바로 그 성에서 다스린다.

blocks.html: The court in Surabol hears the name and goes very quiet. Their men died for this ground. An emperor promised it to Chunchu by lamplight. Now a Baekje prince sits on it again, with the emperor's seal in his hand.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 조정은 그 이름을 듣고 아주 조용해진다. 자기 사람들이 이 땅을 위해 죽었다. 황제는 등잔불 아래 이 땅을 춘추에게 약속했다. 그런데 이제 그 위에 다시 백제 왕자가 앉아 있다. 황제의 도장을 쥐고.

en: Everything south of Pyongyang, and the whole of Baekje.
My father made me learn it by heart.

blocks.html: Yung moves into the commandery offices in the spring. The rooms his father was taken from have been whitewashed. Liu Rengui shows him the registers, and the calendar, and the list of names he may not write.
blocks.ko: 융은 봄에 도독부 관아로 들어간다. 아버지가 끌려 나간 방들은 하얗게 회칠이 되어 있다. 유인궤가 그에게 호적과 역서와, 써서는 안 될 이름 목록을 보여 준다.

lines: 도독의 백성이오. 이제 모두 숫자요. 돌보기가 훨씬 쉬워지지.
en: Your households, Commander. Every one of them a number now. It makes them much easier to look after.
zh: 都督之戶口，今皆為數。易於撫養。
zhLatn: Dūdū zhī hùkǒu, jīn jiē wéi shù. Yì yú fǔyǎng.

en: …My father counted them by name.
He was wrong about most things. Not that.

blocks.label: The Altar
blocks.ko: 제단

blocks.html: The next summer, the empire makes the two men who rule the south swear to be brothers. It picks a hill outside Bear Ford. The clerks name it the Mountain Where One Goes for Gain. They mean it kindly.
blocks.ko: 이듬해 여름, 제국은 남쪽을 다스리는 두 사내에게 형제가 되겠다고 맹세하게 한다. 웅진 밖 언덕 하나를 고른다. 서기들은 그 산을 '이익을 좇아가는 산'이라 적는다. 좋은 뜻으로 지은 이름이다.

blocks.html: A hill outside Bear Ford, named by optimists.
blocks.ko: 웅진 밖의 언덕. 낙관주의자들이 붙인 이름.

blocks.html: An imperial envoy presides. The Black Tortoise wrote the oath. On one side of the altar stands Munmu. On the other stands Yung. Munmu last saw that face at the height of his horse's knees.
blocks.ko: 칙사가 주관하고, 맹세문은 현무가 지었다. 제단 한쪽에 문무가 선다. 다른 쪽에 융이 선다. 문무가 그 얼굴을 마지막으로 본 건 제 말의 무릎 높이에서였다.

blocks.hanja: 王與勅使劉仁願 熊津都督扶餘隆 盟于熊津就利山
blocks.html: The king, with the imperial envoy Liu Renyuan and Buyeo Yung, Commander-in-chief of Ungjin, swore a covenant on Mount Chwiri at Ungjin.
blocks.ko: 왕이 칙사 유인원, 웅진도독 부여융과 더불어 웅진 취리산에서 맹약하였다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 5 (665), eighth month

blocks.label: The White Horse
blocks.ko: 백마

blocks.html: An oath of this weight needs a white horse. The Tang adjutant has been walking the Silla lines all morning looking for one, and stops in front of the only white horse in the camp.
blocks.ko: 이만한 맹세에는 흰 말이 있어야 한다. 당의 부관이 아침 내내 신라의 진을 돌며 흰 말을 찾다가, 진영에 단 한 마리뿐인 흰 말 앞에서 멈춘다.

blocks.speaker: Tang adjutant
en: That one. Whose is he?
zhLatn: Nà pǐ. Shéi de?

blocks.html: Hanseul is past twenty. He has carried Yushin across the Yellow Mountain. He has carried rice through snow up to his chest. His muzzle has gone grey. On a white horse, only the man who feeds him notices.
blocks.ko: 한슬은 스무 살이 넘었다. 유신을 태우고 황산벌을 건넜다. 가슴까지 차는 눈 속으로 쌀을 날랐다. 주둥이가 하얗게 셌다. 흰 말이라, 먹이를 주는 사람 말고는 아무도 모른다.

lines: 안 되오. 다른 말을 찾으시오. 저건 외숙의—
en: No. Find another. That is my uncle’s—
Let them have him, Majesty.
Uncle.

lines: 흰 말을 달라 했습니다. 갈색 말로 하면 맹세가 초라하지요.
en: A white horse is what they asked for. It would be a poor oath on a brown one.
…I’ll walk him up myself.

blocks.html: He leads Hanseul up the hill by the halter, the way he led Hangyul across the Wolseong yard eighteen years before, talking to him in the low voice he keeps for horses and uses on no one else. At the altar he holds the head himself.
blocks.ko: 그는 고삐를 잡고 한슬이를 언덕 위로 끈다. 열여덟 해 전 월성 마당에서 한결이를 끌던 그대로, 말에게만 쓰고 사람에게는 한 번도 쓰지 않는 낮은 목소리로 말을 건네면서. 제단 앞에서 그는 말머리를 손수 잡는다.

blocks.html: The knife is Tang. The blood goes into a bowl, and both men touch it to their lips. Yung does it without looking at anyone. Munmu does it looking at his uncle’s hands.
blocks.ko: 칼은 당의 것이다. 피가 사발에 담기고, 두 사내가 그것을 입술에 댄다. 융은 아무도 보지 않고 한다. 문무는 외숙의 손을 보면서 한다.

lines: …형제처럼 지내며 재앙을 나누고 근심을 서로 보살펴, 길이 하나가 될지어다.
이 맹약을 어기는 자는 신명이 굽어보시어 온갖 재앙이 내리고, 자손이 자라지 못하며, 그 사직을 지킬 자가 남지 않으리라.
en: …Let them be as brothers, sharing disaster and pitying each other’s sorrows, forever as one.
Whoever breaks this covenant, may the gods see it; may a hundred calamities fall on him, may his sons not grow, and may no one remain to keep his altars.
zh: ……結為兄弟，分災恤患，永以為好。
有背此盟者，明神鑒之，百殃是降，子孫不育，社稷無守。
zhLatn: …Jié wéi xiōngdì, fēn zāi xù huàn, yǒng yǐ wéi hǎo.
Yǒu bèi cǐ méng zhě, míngshén jiàn zhī, bǎi yāng shì jiàng, zǐsūn bú yù, shèjì wú shǒu.

blocks.html: The covenant is written out three times. One copy is buried at the altar with the horse. One goes to Chang’an. The third is carried to Surabol and laid up in Silla’s ancestral temple, where the kings of Silla will have to walk past it every time they visit their fathers.
blocks.ko: 맹세문은 세 벌 쓰인다. 한 벌은 말과 함께 제단에 묻힌다. 한 벌은 장안으로 간다. 나머지 한 벌은 서라벌로 옮겨져 신라의 종묘에 모셔진다. 신라의 왕들이 선왕을 뵈러 갈 때마다 그 앞을 지나가야 하는 자리다.

blocks.title: The covenant of Mount Chwiri
blocks.hanja: 往者，百濟先王迷於逆順，不敦鄰好，不睦親姻，結託高句麗，交通倭國，共爲殘暴，侵削新羅，剽邑屠城，略無寧歳。……故立前百濟大司稼正卿扶餘隆，爲熊津都督，守其祭祀，保其桑梓，依倚新羅，長爲與國，各除宿憾，結好和親，各承詔命，永爲藩服。……約之以婚姻，申之以盟誓，刑牲歃血，共敦終始，分災恤患，恩若弟兄，祗奉綸音，不敢失墜，旣盟之後，共保歳寒。若有背盟，二三其德，興兵動衆，侵犯邊陲，明神鑒之，百殃是降，子孫不育，社稷無守，禋祀磨滅，罔有遺餘。故作金書鐵券，藏之宗廟，子孫萬代，無敢違犯。神之聽之，是享是福。
blocks.html: In days past, the late king of Baekje lost his way between loyalty and revolt. He kept no faith with his neighbours and no peace with his in-laws. He bound himself to Goguryeo and dealt with Yamato, and together they did violence: they cut into Silla, plundered its towns and butchered its forts, and there was hardly a year of peace. … Therefore Buyeo Yung, once Baekje’s minister of farming, is made Commander of Ungjin, to keep his fathers’ rites and guard the trees of his home. Let him lean on Silla and stand with it for ever. Let each put away old grudges, join in friendship and kinship, receive the imperial command, and remain a fence of the empire for all time. … They are bound by marriage and sworn by oath. The victim is killed and the blood is touched to the lips. Together they will keep faith to the end, share disaster and pity each other’s sorrows, as kind as brothers. They will keep the emperor’s word and never let it drop. After this oath they will stand together through the cold years. If either breaks the oath, turns two-faced, raises troops and crosses the border, may the bright gods see it. May a hundred calamities fall on him, may his sons not grow, may no one remain to keep his altars, and may his sacrifices be wiped out until nothing is left. So it is written in gold on iron and laid up in the ancestral temple, and for ten thousand generations no son or grandson will dare break it. Gods, hear it. Accept it, and bless it.
blocks.ko: 지난날 백제의 선왕은 순리와 역리를 헤아리지 못하여, 이웃과 좋게 지내지 않고 인척과도 화목하지 않았다. 고구려와 손잡고 왜국과 내통하여 함께 포악한 짓을 하니, 신라를 침범해 깎아 먹고 고을을 노략하고 성을 도륙하여 편안한 해가 거의 없었다. …… 그러므로 옛 백제의 대사가정경 부여융을 웅진도독으로 세워, 그 제사를 지키고 고향을 보전하게 한다. 신라에 기대어 길이 우방이 되고, 각자 묵은 원한을 풀고 좋게 지내며 화친하고, 각각 조명을 받들어 길이 번국이 되라. …… 혼인으로 묶고 맹세로 다짐하며, 희생을 잡아 피를 마시고 처음과 끝을 함께 도탑게 한다. 재앙을 나누고 근심을 서로 돌보며 은혜를 형제처럼 하고, 천자의 말씀을 받들어 감히 떨어뜨리지 않으며, 맹세한 뒤에는 추운 해를 함께 견딘다. 만약 맹세를 어기고 마음을 둘 셋으로 바꾸어, 군사를 일으키고 무리를 움직여 변경을 침범하면, 밝은 신이 굽어보시어 온갖 재앙이 내리고, 자손이 자라지 못하며, 사직을 지킬 자가 없고, 제사가 끊어져 남는 것이 없으리라. 그러므로 쇠 문서에 금으로 써서 종묘에 간직하니, 자손 만대에 감히 어기지 말라. 신이여 들으시고, 흠향하시고 복을 내리소서.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 5 (665), eighth month · the words of Liu Rengui (劉仁軌之辭也)

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: On the road home nobody in the Silla column says anything about the horse.
blocks.ko: 돌아오는 길에 신라의 행렬 누구도 그 말 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.html: In Surabol the anger is louder. Men bled for this land in three wars. An emperor promised it to them. Now they have sworn on a dead horse never to take it. The young officers say betrayal in the barracks. The older ones say nothing. They start counting Tang garrisons.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서는 분노가 더 크다. 사람들은 세 번의 전쟁에서 이 땅을 위해 피를 흘렸다. 황제가 약속한 땅이었다. 그런데 이제 죽은 말 위에서 그 땅을 갖지 않겠다고 맹세했다. 젊은 장교들은 병영에서 배신이라는 말을 한다. 나이 든 장교들은 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 당의 주둔지를 세기 시작한다.

blocks.html: That night the king finds his uncle in the stable, cleaning a stall that is empty.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 왕은 마구간에서 외숙을 찾아낸다. 빈 마구간을 치우고 있다.

lines: 흰 말은 내가 다시 구해 드리겠소, 외숙.
en: I’ll find you another white horse, Uncle.

lines: 말 대신 전쟁을 하나 찾아 주십시오. 또 무슨 맹세를 시키기 전에, 한 번만 더 가 보고 싶습니다.
en: I’m seventy, Majesty. I’ve buried three.
Find me a war instead. I’d like to go to one more before they make me swear to something else.

blocks.html: To find the first king of this land, we have to go back before there were kingdoms… to a bear in a cave…!
blocks.ko: 이 땅의 첫 임금을 찾으려면, 나라가 생기기도 전으로 거슬러 올라가야 한다. 동굴 속 곰 한 마리에게로…!

images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Inside a cave: a bear and a tiger crouch in darkness with a bundle of mugwort and a pile of garlic between them; a single shaft of daylight from the cave mouth stops just short of them; the tiger’s head turns to the light, restless; the bear sits still. ONE device: the light shaft that does not reach them. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — DANGUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dangun.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8956a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | GOM (곰, dangun's great bear, guardian of Old Joseon) — attached board /obj_bear.png: HUGE dark-brown bear, far bigger than a man — massive shoulder hump, thick shaggy dark chocolate-brown fur with lighter tips catching the light, broad heavy head, small dark eyes, short round ears, long curved claws — match the board. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Ungnyeo's first shape: the bear that kept to the cave for a hundred days on mugwort and garlic and came out a woman. In the shape she left behind it stays near her son: patient, enormous, gentle with him and with no one else. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Between them one ritual barrel drum, a stick just touching the skin, the player only a small kneeling mark. A tiny bleed of vermilion only where the stick meets the drum. Vast white between heaven and earth. Visceral realistic sumi, flying white. No text, no seal, no watermark, no sun or moon drawn as icons.

images.prompt: Original East Asian ink painting on plain white paper. A gayageum seen from the side, almost all strings cut and hanging as broken hairlines that become one long road-stroke leaving the frame. One string still taut. No person, or only a departed handprint in pale ink. A small bleed of ash-blue only on the one remaining string. Flying white, dry brush, the feeling of a kingdom already gone. No text, no seal, no watermark, no map.

blocks.html: Before there are any kingdoms, there is a son in heaven who keeps looking down. He is Hwanung. His father Hwanin, the Lord of Heaven, notices, looks down himself at a mountain called Taebaek and the people living around it, and decides the world could use his son.
blocks.ko: 나라라는 것이 하나도 없던 때, 하늘에 자꾸 아래를 내려다보는 아들이 있다. 환웅이다. 아버지인 하늘의 임금 환인이 그것을 알아채고, 저도 태백이라는 산과 그 둘레에 사는 사람들을 내려다본 뒤, 세상에 아들이 쓸모 있겠다고 정한다.

blocks.caption: The Lord of Heaven. He has been watching this peninsula since before it had names.
blocks.ko: 하늘의 주인. 이 반도에 이름이 생기기 전부터 내려다보고 있었다.

blocks.title: Old Joseon · 고조선
blocks.caption: Heaven’s mandate made into a capital: Hwanin → Hwanung → Dangun → Asadal.
blocks.ko: 하늘의 명을 수도로 만든 계보. 환인 → 환웅 → 단군 → 아사달.

blocks.html: Hwanin does not plough — he opens the sky. Three seals go down with his son, so that nobody on the ground can mistake him for a prince playing at exile. Every later king in this chronicle will cut seals of his own, and every one of them is copying these.
blocks.ko: 환인은 갈지 않는다 — 하늘을 연다. 아들과 함께 천부인 셋이 내려간다. 땅의 누구도 그를 유배 놀이 하는 왕자로 착각하지 못하게. 이 편년의 후대 임금들은 저마다 제 인장을 새길 것이고, 그 모두가 이것을 베낀다.

blocks.html: Hwanung lands on a mountain under the sacred birch. He names the ground beneath it the Divine City. Three thousand followers come down with him. Among them are the lords of wind, rain and cloud. Someone has to argue with the weather.
blocks.ko: 환웅은 신단수 아래 산에 내려앉는다. 그 밑의 땅을 신시라 부른다. 무리 삼천이 함께 내려온다. 그 가운데 바람과 비와 구름의 우두머리들이 있다. 누군가는 날씨와 말다툼을 해야 하니까.

blocks.caption: Hwanung. A son of heaven who kept looking down until his father let him go.
blocks.ko: 환웅. 자꾸 아래를 내려다보다가, 끝내 아버지가 보내 준 하늘의 아들.

blocks.hanja: 乃授天符印三箇 雄率徒三千 降於太伯山頂神壇樹下 是謂神市 熊女與婚 生子 號曰壇君王儉
blocks.ko: 이에 천부인 셋을 주어 다스리게 하니, 환웅이 무리 삼천을 이끌고 태백산 꼭대기 신단수 아래로 내려와 이를 신시라 하였다. 웅녀와 혼인하여 아들을 낳으니, 이름하여 단군왕검이라 하였다.
blocks.html: He granted three heavenly seals and sent him to govern. Hwanung led a following of three thousand and descended under the sacred altar-tree on the summit of Mount Taebaek; this was called the Divine City. He married the bear-woman, and she bore a son named Dangun Wanggeom.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonder 1 — Old Joseon (Dangun); Ha & Mintz tr., pp. 32–33

blocks.html: That is the short way to tell it, the way it is carved on stones. The long way begins, as long ways do, with a bear who wanted something so badly that she outlasted a tiger for it.
blocks.ko: 그것이 짧게 전하는 방식이고, 돌에 새기는 방식이다. 길게 전하는 방식은, 긴 이야기가 늘 그렇듯, 무언가를 너무나 간절히 원한 나머지 호랑이보다 오래 견딘 곰 한 마리에서 시작된다.

blocks.html: From there he hands out civilisation in instalments. Laws. Punishments. Lifespans. Illness. Good and evil. Medicine. Three hundred and sixty matters in all. Somebody counted.
blocks.ko: 거기서 그는 훗날 문명이라 불릴 것을 할부로 나눠 준다. 법. 형벌. 수명. 병. 선과 악. 의술. 모두 삼백육십 가지. 누군가 세어 두었다.

blocks.html: A bear and a tiger come to him and ask to be made human. He gives them a bundle of mugwort, twenty cloves of garlic, and one instruction: stay out of the sun for a hundred days.
blocks.ko: 곰과 범이 그를 찾아와 사람이 되게 해 달라 청한다. 그는 쑥 한 줌과 마늘 스무 쪽을 주고 한 가지를 이른다. 백 일 동안 햇빛을 보지 마라.

blocks.html: The bear stays. She comes out a woman on the twenty-first morning, garlic still on her breath, and finds the mountain already staffed — wind, rain, cloud, and not one of them a husband. So she stands under the sacred tree. Not once. Every day, on the path he has to take if he means to reach the hall.
blocks.ko: 곰은 남는다. 스무하루째 아침, 입가에 마늘 냄새가 남은 채로 여자가 되어 나오니, 산은 이미 사람이 가득하다 — 바람, 비, 구름, 그리고 남편이 될 이는 하나도 없다. 그래서 신단수 아래에 선다. 한 번이 아니다. 그가 전각으로 가려면 반드시 지나야 하는 길에, 날마다.
blocks.art: Open on the cave mouth: the tiger’s tracks leading away into the snow, then her first step into daylight.

blocks.caption: Ungnyeo. Twenty-one days in a cave, and the tiger left first. A husband should be easy.
blocks.ko: 웅녀. 동굴에서 스무하루, 먼저 나간 건 호랑이였다. 지아비 하나쯤이야.

blocks.html: He means to reach the hall. On the third evening he gets as far as the birch, and the seal in his hand becomes a thing he is holding for no reason he can name.
blocks.ko: 그는 전각에 닿을 작정이다. 사흘째 저녁, 자작나무까지는 온다. 손의 인장은, 왜 들고 있는지 스스로도 말할 수 없는 물건이 된다.

en: You're going to walk past again.
…Not today.
Yesterday you did.
And the day before. I was standing right here.
I saw you.
The garlic reached this far.
Twenty-one days of that, and this is what came out.
…I was going to say don't come closer.

lines: 가지 마. 아니— 가지 마시오. 손이—
en: Too late.
Stay. I mean— don't go. Your hand—
You already have the hand.
…Scared of the rest?
I am.
Because you're looking at me.

lines: 나무는 보고 있을 테니까. 나는… 더.
en: Then come down.
The tree can watch. I want… more.

blocks.html: The kiss is clumsy. Beard, a new mouth, birch bark at her back. She makes a small furious sound and tries again, and the second one lands.
blocks.ko: 입맞춤은 서투르다. 수염, 처음 쓰는 입, 등에 닿는 자작나무 껍질. 그녀가 짧게 성난 소리를 내고 다시 하고, 두 번째는 닿는다.

blocks.html: White silk goes down among the roots. The fur at her throat opens under his mouth. She laughs once, startled at the sound, and pulls him down by the hair.
blocks.ko: 흰 비단이 뿌리 사이에 내려앉는다. 목덜미의 털깃이 그의 입 밑에서 풀린다. 그녀는 한 번 웃는다. 그 소리에 스스로 놀라서. 그리고 머리카락을 잡아 그를 끌어내린다.

blocks.html: By the time the moon clears the snow on the peak, the rust-red sash is somewhere in the moss, and neither of them has gone back up the path.
blocks.ko: 달빛이 봉우리의 눈에 닿을 때쯤, 붉은 띠는 이끼 어딘가에 있고, 둘 다 그 길로 돌아 올라가지 않았다.

en: …You're going already?
I can't.
I don't know where I put the seal.
Under my head.
I took it. …Don't go.
…Thief.
Marry me in the morning.
Right now I'm here.

blocks.html: Their son is Dangun. The name on the stone is Wanggeom: a king who governs, not one who inherits a bone rank. He founds Asadal where the mountain meets the plain. He rules for fifteen hundred years, and then he becomes the mountain.
blocks.ko: 그 아들이 단군이다. 돌에 새긴 이름은 왕검. 골품을 물려받은 임금이 아니라 다스리는 임금이다. 그는 산과 들이 만나는 곳에 아사달을 세운다. 천오백 년을 다스리고, 산이 된다.

blocks.caption: Dangun. Half heaven, half bear, and all the paperwork of a first king.
blocks.ko: 단군. 반은 하늘, 반은 곰, 그리고 첫 임금의 서류는 전부 그의 몫.

blocks.html: Where the mountain meets the plain, and the first crown met both.
blocks.ko: 산이 들을 만나는 곳. 첫 왕관이 둘 다를 만난 곳.

blocks.html: Every later crown in these kingdoms argues, one way or another, back to the woman who used to be a bear.
blocks.ko: 이후 이 왕국들의 왕관은, 어떤 식으로든, 한때 곰이었던 여자에게로 거슬러 올라간다.

blocks.label: The Fall of Joseon
blocks.ko: 조선의 멸망

blocks.html: Joseon outlives its founder by a long way. Two thousand years on it is still there, run by other kings now, from a walled city on the Taedong that has kept his name: Wanggeom. In the autumn of 109 BC, Han comes to the gate.
blocks.ko: 조선은 시조보다 훨씬 오래 산다. 이천 년이 지나도 여전히 거기 있다. 이제는 다른 임금들이, 그의 이름 왕검을 그대로 지닌 대동강가의 성에서 다스린다. 기원전 109년 가을, 한나라가 그 성문 앞에 온다.

blocks.html: It takes the empire of the West a year to take one fortress, and they do not take it. Wanggeom holds through a siege that begins in the autumn and is still going the following autumn.
blocks.ko: 서토의 제국이 성 하나를 얻는 데 한 해가 걸리고, 결국 얻지 못한다. 왕검성은 가을에 시작해 이듬해 가을까지 이어지는 포위를 견딘다.

blocks.html: So they stop attacking the walls and start talking to the men behind them, which is cheaper and has never once failed.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그들은 성벽을 치는 일을 그만두고, 성벽 뒤의 사람들과 이야기하기 시작한다. 더 싸고, 단 한 번도 실패한 적 없는 방법이다.

blocks.html: King Ugeo has stopped sleeping in the palace. He sleeps on the wall, where he can hear the Han camp coughing, and his son, Prince Jang Hang, has started sleeping somewhere else.
blocks.ko: 우거왕은 궁에서 자지 않은 지 오래다. 한나라 진영의 기침 소리가 들리는 성벽 위에서 잔다. 태자 장항은 언제부턴가 다른 데서 잔다.

lines: 성문만 열면 성 안 사람은 아무도 건드리지 않겠답니다.
en: Father. They’ve sent terms again.
Open the gate, they say, and nobody inside gets hurt.
They said that last autumn.
Who brought it to you?
…Does it matter who?
It matters.
Get off my wall.

blocks.html: Noin, one of the ministers who have been doing the talking, goes over the wall that week and dies on the road before he reaches the Han tents. Another of them, Sam, does not bother with the road. One night at the start of summer he sends men up the wall-stair instead.
blocks.ko: 말을 주고받던 대신 가운데 하나인 노인이 그 주에 성벽을 넘어가다, 한나라 장막에 닿기도 전에 길에서 죽는다. 또 다른 대신 삼은 길로 나서지 않는다. 초여름 어느 밤, 그는 성벽 계단으로 사람들을 올려 보낸다.
blocks.art: Torchlight on the wall-stair, knives, the king turning from the parapet too late.

en: Majesty—!
blocks.speaker: Seong Gi

lines: 사람들 데리고 나가. 살아서… 어디서든, 새로 나라를 세워라.
en: …Seong Gi?
Don’t hold the city. Not for me.
Get the people out. Live… and make a new country. Anywhere.

blocks.html: Seong Gi closes the king’s eyes, goes back up to the parapet, and holds the city anyway.
blocks.ko: 성기는 임금의 눈을 감기고, 다시 성가퀴로 올라가, 그래도 성을 지킨다.

blocks.html: He holds it until Noin’s son Choi and the prince go down into the lanes, where people have been eating bark since the spring.
blocks.ko: 노인의 아들 최와 태자가 골목으로 내려갈 때까지는 지킨다. 골목 사람들은 봄부터 나무껍질을 먹고 있었다.

lines: 그럼 이제 누구 때문에 굶는 거요? 저 사람?
en: The king is dead.
So who are you starving for now? Him?
blocks.art: Choi pointing up at Seong Gi on the wall.

blocks.html: Before morning Seong Gi is dead too.
blocks.ko: 아침이 오기 전에 성기도 죽는다.

blocks.html: Someone lifts the bar.
blocks.ko: 누군가 빗장을 든다.
blocks.art: Wordless. The gate of Wanggeom swings open from the inside; Han banners wait in the grey light.

en: The wall did not come down.
A door was opened from the inside.

blocks.html: Han takes Wanggeom. Some of the people the king told to live go south over the mountains. They settle in six villages around Surabol. Two generations later, they'll go looking for a king. The rest stay, and the empire cuts them into four pieces. The last piece is still collecting taxes four hundred years later.
blocks.ko: 한나라가 왕검성을 차지한다. 임금이 살라고 한 사람들 가운데 일부는 산을 넘어 남쪽으로 간다. 서라벌 둘레 골짜기에 여섯 마을을 이룬다. 두 세대 뒤, 그들은 임금을 찾아 나설 것이다. 나머지는 남아, 제국의 손에 넷으로 쪼개진다. 그 마지막 하나는 사백 년 뒤에도 세금을 걷고 있다.

blocks.html: Eight hundred years later, the empire comes back to the same river to do the same thing. This time, Goguryeo has a prince left…!
blocks.ko: 팔백 년 뒤, 제국이 같은 강으로 돌아와 같은 짓을 한다. 이번에는 고구려에 왕족 하나가 남아 있다…!

Gold Tang banners, a few remaining red Goguryeo roofs. Xue Rengui a small white-armored figure at the east gate. Painterly cinema. Flat sky, no clouds. No text, no watermark.

blocks.label: The Protectorate
blocks.ko: 안동도호부

blocks.html: Nearly eight hundred years after Wanggeom, the empire of the West comes back to the Taedong and does the same thing again. The Third Emperor sets up a Protectorate over Goguryeo, staffs it with his own officials, and seems surprised that anyone minds.
blocks.ko: 왕검성으로부터 팔백 년 가까이 지나, 서토의 제국이 다시 대동강으로 와서 같은 일을 되풀이한다. 황제는 고구려 땅에 안동도호부를 세우고 제 관리들로 채운 뒤, 누가 싫어하는 걸 보고 놀란 눈치다.

blocks.html: Geom Mojam raises the old flag on the Taedong. He puts a royal cousin, Anseung, under it. Then they quarrel.
blocks.ko: 검모잠이 대동강에서 옛 깃발을 세운다. 왕족 안승을 그 아래 세운다. 그러고는 둘이 다툰다.

blocks.html: Mojam, a daehyeong of Goguryeo from Surim Fortress, gathered the surviving people, marched from Gungmo Fortress to south of the Pae River, and killed the Tang officials and the monk Beop'an. Heading for Silla, he reached Saya Island in the western sea, found Anseung, son of the Goguryeo minister Yeon Jungto, brought him into Hanseong, and set him up as lord.
blocks.ko: 고구려 수림성 사람 대형 모잠이 남은 백성을 거두어 모아, 궁모성에서 패강 남쪽에 이르러 당의 관인과 승려 법안 등을 죽였다. 신라로 향해 가다가 서해 사야도에 이르러, 고구려 대신 연정토의 아들 안승을 만나 한성 안으로 맞아들이고 임금으로 받들었다.
blocks.hanja: 高句麗水臨城人牟岑大兄，收合殘民，自窮牟城，至浿江南，殺唐官人及僧法安等。向新羅行，至西海史冶島，見高句麗大臣淵淨土之子安勝，迎致漢城中，奉以爲君。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), sixth month

blocks.html: The great chief Geom Mojam led his people in revolt and set up An Shun, King Jang's grandson through a daughter, as their lord.
blocks.ko: 대장 겸모잠이 무리를 거느리고 반란을 일으켜, 장왕의 외손 안순을 세워 임금으로 삼았다.
blocks.hanja: 大長鉗牟岑率衆反，立藏外孫安舜爲主。
blocks.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo, Zongzhang 2 / Xianheng 1 (669–670)

blocks.html: The quarrel is about whether to fight. Geom Mojam wants to hold the Taedong and die on it if he has to. Anseung has seen what the Tang do to cities that hold, and would rather be a guest somewhere than a corpse in a capital.
blocks.ko: 다툼은 싸울 것이냐 말 것이냐를 두고 벌어진다. 검모잠은 대동강을 지키다 죽어야 한다면 죽겠다고 한다. 안승은 버티는 성에 당이 무슨 짓을 하는지 보았고, 도성의 시체가 되느니 어딘가의 손님이 되는 편을 택한다.

blocks.speaker: Geom Mojam
lines: 평양 땅에는 사백 년 묵은 임금들이 묻혀 계시오. 그분들을 두고 신라 사랑채로 가겠다는 거요?
en: Pyongyang has kings in its soil four hundred years deep. You want to leave them for a Silla guest room?

blocks.speaker: Anseung
lines: 땅속의 임금들은 기다려 주실 거요. 그 위의 사천 호는 못 기다리오.
en: The kings in the soil will keep. The four thousand households above it won’t.

blocks.html: That night Anseung has him killed. It is the first Goguryeo blood the revival spills, and it is spilled by Goguryeo.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 안승은 그를 죽인다. 부흥군이 흘린 첫 고구려 피이고, 그것을 흘린 것도 고구려다.

blocks.html: Munmu gives him a title, a district, and a name for the thing: Goguryeo, still standing, inside Silla. It is a useful fiction and both sides know exactly how useful.
blocks.ko: 문무왕은 그에게 관작과 고을과 이름 하나를 준다. 신라 안에 여전히 서 있는 고구려. 쓸모 있는 허구이고, 양쪽 다 그것이 얼마나 쓸모 있는지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: Silla settles him in a town that was somebody else's kingdom ten years ago. Within the year he is called King of Goguryeo. In time he gets a bride, and a seat at Munmu's feasts. Well below the king's.
blocks.ko: 신라는 그를 열 해 전까지 남의 나라 땅이던 고을에 앉힌다. 그해가 가기 전에 그는 고구려왕이라 불린다. 때가 되자 신부도 얻고, 문무의 잔치에 자리도 얻는다. 왕의 자리보다 한참 아래다.

lines: 신라 안에 고구려 왕이라. 황제가 질색하겠군.
en: A king of Goguryeo in Silla. The emperor will hate it.
Good. Give him a seal. A big one.

blocks.html: The King of Silla charges Anseung, heir of Goguryeo. … The rightful heir of the former kings is you and no one else; who but you should keep their sacrifices? … We open this patent and name you King of Goguryeo. Gather the surviving people, revive the old line, be our neighbour for ever and deal with us as a brother. Be reverent, be reverent!
blocks.ko: 신라왕은 고구려의 대를 이을 아들 안승에게 명한다. … 선왕의 바른 후사는 오직 공뿐이니, 제사를 받들 이가 공이 아니면 누구이겠는가? … 이에 책서를 펴서 공을 고구려왕으로 봉하노니, 공은 남은 백성을 어루만져 모으고 옛 왕업을 이어 일으켜, 길이 이웃 나라가 되어 형제처럼 지낼지어다. 삼가고 삼갈지어다.
blocks.hanja: 新羅王致命高句麗嗣子安勝。…先王正嗣，唯公而已，主於祭祀，非公而誰？…就披策命公爲高句麗王，公宜撫集遺民，紹興舊緖，永爲鄰國，事同昆弟，敬哉敬哉。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), eighth month — patent investing Anseung

blocks.html: Xue Rengui sends a letter. Munmu has been waiting twenty years to answer it…!
blocks.ko: 설인귀가 편지를 보낸다. 문무는 그 답장을 스무 해 동안 기다려 왔다…!

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior, deep night, the king's writing room in Surabol. Low WORM'S-EYE from beside the scribe's desk. ONE device: one tall lattice window, black, with a sliver of moon. King Munmu, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, in his crimson robe, STANDING, one fist pressed against the window frame, turned half back toward the room, jaw set, mouth open dictating — tired and furious, his father's charm gone hard. In the foreground the scribe's bent back and brush hand over a long paper scroll, out of focus, the writing a soft blur, nothing readable. An ink-stone and spent candle stubs on the desk. Munmu's shadow climbs the receding plaster wall. Key: the desk lamp from below, crimson #C41E3A specular on his silk; the rest umber black. CANON — KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.
