FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The First Letter
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 편지

blocks.html: In high summer, a Tang monk is rowed ashore under a white flag. He carries a letter from the fleet. The fleet belongs to Xue Rengui, the second White Tiger. He has sat off the coast all summer. If it can be managed, he'd like to win this war by post.
blocks.ko: 한여름, 당나라 승려 하나가 흰 깃발을 단 배로 뭍에 오른다. 함대에서 온 편지를 들고서. 함대의 주인은 두 번째 백호, 설인귀다. 그는 여름 내내 해안 밖에 떠 있었다. 될 수만 있다면, 이 전쟁을 편지로 이기고 싶다.

blocks.speaker: Imyun
lines: 대총관께서 문안을 여쭙니다, 전하. 소리 내어 읽어 주십사 하셨습니다.
en: The Commander sends his respects, Majesty. He asks that it be read aloud.
He says it reads better aloud.
zh: 大總管問候大王。請高聲宣讀。
zhLatn: Dà zǒngguǎn wènhòu dàwáng. Qǐng gāoshēng xuāndú.
Tā shuō dú chūlái gèng hǎo.

lines: 신라 왕께, 동방 행군대총관 설인귀가 문안드립니다.
맑은 바람은 도성에서 그대 해안까지 만 리를 불고, 그 사이 바다는 삼천 리입니다. 그 길을 다 건너와 드릴 말씀은 하나뿐입니다.
그대의 아버님은 선제 앞에 무릎을 꿇었고, 일으켜 세워졌습니다. 관복을 받고, 형제를 얻고, 군대를 얻었지요. 그대는 그분의 왕관을 받았고요.
그런데 이제 그대는 황제의 병사들이 피 흘린 땅을 차지하고, 황제의 반역자들을 감싸 주고 있습니다. 그대의 아우는 장안에서, 형님 소식을 물을까 봐 고개를 들지 못합니다.
돌아설 길이 남아 있을 때 돌아서십시오.
이 일 하나만 빼고 모든 일에서, 전하의 종으로 남기를 영광으로 여기며 —
en: To the King of Silla, from Xue Rengui, Commander of the Eastern Fleet, greetings.
A clear wind blows ten thousand li from the capital to your coast, and the sea between is three thousand. I have come all of it to say one thing.
Your father knelt before the Second Emperor and was raised up. He was given robes, and a brother, and an army. You were given his crown.
And now you take the land the emperor’s soldiers bled for, and you shelter his rebels, and your own brother waits in Chang’an, ashamed to be asked about you.
Turn back while there is still a road to turn on.
I have the honour to remain, in all things but this, Your Majesty’s servant —
Xue Rengui.
zh: 新羅王足下：東方行軍大總管薛仁貴致意。
清風萬里，大海三千。仁貴遠來，只為一言。
先王跪於先帝之前，蒙恩而起；賜之冠服，結為兄弟，假以兵馬。王受其冠。
今王據天兵流血之地，庇朝廷之叛臣；令弟在長安，人問及王，羞不能答。
仁貴除此一事之外，萬事皆為大王之僕——
zhLatn: Xīnluó wáng zúxià: Dōngfāng xíngjūn dà zǒngguǎn Xuē Rénguì zhìyì.
Qīngfēng wàn lǐ, dàhǎi sān qiān. Rénguì yuǎn lái, zhǐ wèi yì yán.
Xiānwáng guì yú xiāndì zhī qián, méng ēn ér qǐ; cì zhī guānfú, jié wéi xiōngdì, jiǎ yǐ bīngmǎ. Wáng shòu qí guān.
Jīn wáng jù tiānbīng liúxuè zhī dì, bì cháotíng zhī pànchén; lìngdì zài Cháng’ān, rén wèn jí wáng, xiū bù néng dá.
Jí lù wèi jué, huítóu kě yě.
Rénguì chú cǐ yí shì zhī wài, wànshì jiē wéi dàwáng zhī pú——
Xuē Rénguì.

blocks.html: It is like a man who goes out with his sling and never sees the dry well at his feet, or reaches for the cicada and never knows the oriole is behind him. That is Your Majesty, not knowing your own measure. … Alas! Once loyal and righteous, now a rebel subject. I grieve that what began in good fortune ends in ill, that what grew from one root ends in different branches. The wind is high and the air is sharp; the leaves fall and the year turns sad. I lean on the mountain and look far off, and it wounds my heart.
blocks.ko: 이는 탄궁을 들고 나서면서 마른 우물의 위험을 보지 못하고, 매미를 잡으려 나아가면서 뒤에서 노리는 꾀꼬리를 알지 못하는 것과 같으니, 이것이 왕께서 스스로를 헤아리지 못하시는 바입니다. … 아아, 예전에는 충의의 신하였는데 이제는 역신이 되셨습니다. 처음은 길하였으나 끝이 흉함이 한스럽고, 뿌리는 같았으나 끝이 갈라짐이 원망스럽습니다. 바람은 높고 기운은 매서우며, 잎이 지니 한 해가 서럽습니다. 산에 기대어 멀리 바라보니 가슴이 아픕니다.
blocks.hanja: 亦由持彈而往，暗於枯井之危，捕蟬而前，不知黄雀之難，此王之不知量也。…嗚呼，昔爲忠義，今乃逆臣，恨始吉而終凶，怨本同而末異。風高氣切，葉落年悲，憑山遠望，有傷懷抱。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — Xue Rengui's letter, carried by the monk Imyun

blocks.html: The monk is given a bed, a meal, and as long as it takes. The king does not go to bed at all.
blocks.ko: 승려에게는 잠자리와 끼니와, 필요한 만큼의 시간이 주어진다. 왕은 아예 잠자리에 들지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Writing Room
blocks.ko: 글방

blocks.html: By the second night the king’s writing room is full of men with opinions. One of them, an official named Daeto, has more than most.
blocks.ko: 이틀째 밤, 왕의 글방은 할 말 있는 사내들로 가득하다. 그중 대토라는 관리는 남들보다 할 말이 많다.

lines: 전하, 여기저기 말 한두 마디 누그러뜨린다고 손해 볼 건 없습니다.
저들은 웅진 앞바다에 함대가 있고, 인문 공도 데리고 있습니다. 국경을 잘못 알았다고 하면 안 되겠습니까? 국경이야 다들 잘못 아는 거잖습니까.
en: Majesty, a softer word here and there costs nothing.
They have a fleet off Bear Ford. They have Prince Inmun. Could we not say we were mistaken about the border? Everyone is mistaken about borders.
We were not mistaken.
Write it the way I say it.

blocks.html: There is another reason the room is careful. Nine summers ago, the king killed a great lord and his whole house for calling in sick. The lord's son wasn't in the house. He's in the emperor's guard. Somebody there will have told him by now.
blocks.ko: 방 안이 조심스러운 까닭이 하나 더 있다. 아홉 해 전, 왕은 병을 핑계 댄 대귀족 하나를 집안째 죽였다. 그 아들은 집에 없었다. 황제의 숙위에 있다. 거기 누군가가 벌써 그에게 말해 주었을 것이다.

blocks.label: The Reply
blocks.ko: 답서

lines: 그대의 편지는 승려 편에 왔고, 청한 대로 소리 내어 읽었소. 과연 소리 내어 읽으니 낫더이다. 이 편지도 그럴 것이오.
en: To the Commander of the Eastern Fleet, from the King of Silla.
Your letter came by a monk, and was read aloud as you asked. It does read better aloud. So will this.

blocks.html: He dictates the rest standing up, and does not stop for most of the night.
blocks.ko: 그는 나머지를 선 채로 받아쓰게 하고, 밤새 거의 멈추지 않는다.

lines: 정관 이십이 년에 내 아버님이 장안에 가셨소. 선제께서는 아버님을 돌말들이 늘어선 회랑으로 데려가 말씀하셨지. 평양 이남과 백제 땅은 모두 신라의 것이다, 영원히.
아버님은 내가 스물둘일 때 그 말을 외우게 하셨소. 나는 지금도 외우오. 황제의 서기들도 외우고 있으리라 믿소.
en: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan my father went to Chang’an. The Second Emperor took him into a gallery of stone horses and said: everything south of Pyongyang, and the whole of Baekje, shall be Silla’s, forever.
My father made me learn those words when I was twenty-two. I have them still. I expect the emperor’s clerks have them too.

blocks.html: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan my late father went to court and received, face to face, the gracious edict of the Second Emperor: ‘We make war on Goguryeo now for no other reason than pity for you, Silla, caught between two kingdoms, invaded again and again, never a year of peace. Mountains, rivers and land are not what We covet; jade, silk, sons and daughters We have already. When We have pacified the two kingdoms, the land south of Pyongyang and the land of Baekje shall all be given to you, Silla, to rest in for ever.’
blocks.ko: 선왕께서는 정관 22년에 입조하시어 태종 문황제의 은혜로운 칙명을 직접 받드셨습니다. ‘짐이 지금 고구려를 치는 것은 다른 까닭이 아니다. 너희 신라가 두 나라 사이에 끼여 늘 침략을 당하고 편한 해가 없음을 가엾이 여기기 때문이다. 산천과 토지는 내가 탐내는 바가 아니요, 옥백과 자녀는 나에게도 넉넉하다. 내가 두 나라를 평정하면 평양 이남과 백제 땅을 모두 너희 신라에 주어, 길이 편안하게 하리라.’
blocks.hanja: 先王貞觀二十二年，入朝，面奉太宗文皇帝恩勅。『朕今伐高麗，非有他故，憐伱新羅，攝乎兩國，毎被侵陵，靡有寧歳。山川土地，非我所貪，玉帛子女，是我所有。我平定兩國，平壤已南百濟土地、並乞伱新羅，永爲安逸。』
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — King Munmu's reply to Xue Rengui

lines: 그대의 주작이 평양 밖에 앉아 제 말을 잡아먹고 있을 때, 내 외숙은 예순일곱이었소. 가슴까지 차는 눈 속을, 제 흰 말이 자기 대신 쌀을 지도록 그 곁에서 걸어갔소. 그대의 병사들은 수레를 보고 울었소. 그대의 장군은 쌀을 받고 그 주에 배를 타고 돌아갔고.
늦었다 하더이다. 우리는 늘 늦소. 그래도 갔소.
en: When your Red Fowl sat outside Pyongyang eating his horses, my uncle was sixty-seven. He walked beside his own white horse through snow to its chest so the horse could carry rice instead of him. Your soldiers wept when they saw the carts. Your general took the rice and sailed home the same week.
We were late, he said. We are always late. We came anyway.

blocks.html: South we carried grain to Bear Ford, north we fed Pyongyang; little Silla supplied two places at once, until our people were spent and our oxen and horses dead. … The people of Silla had not even enough grass roots to eat, while the Han soldiers at Bear Ford had grain to spare. … Ten thousand Han soldiers were clothed and fed by Silla for four years. From Liu Renyuan down to the last private, their skin and bones may have been born in Han land, but their blood and flesh are all Silla's.
blocks.ko: 남으로는 웅진에 실어 나르고 북으로는 평양에 대느라, 작은 신라가 두 곳을 나누어 감당하니 사람의 힘은 다하고 소와 말은 모두 죽었습니다. … 신라 백성은 풀뿌리조차 모자랐는데, 웅진의 당병은 양식이 남아돌았습니다. … 당병 1만이 4년 동안 신라에서 입고 먹었으니, 인원부터 졸병에 이르기까지 가죽과 뼈는 비록 당나라 땅에서 났으나, 피와 살은 모두 신라의 것입니다.
blocks.hanja: 南運熊津，北供平壤，蕞小新羅，分供兩所，人力疲極，牛馬死盡。…新羅百姓，草根猶自不足，熊津漢兵，粮食有餘。…一萬漢兵，四年衣食新羅，仁願已下，兵士已上，皮骨雖生漢地，血肉倶是新羅。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — King Munmu's reply to Xue Rengui

lines: 그러고 나서 그대들은 백제를 백제 왕자에게 돌려주었소. 당의 도장을 찍어서, 웅진에. 그러고는 우리를 취리산이라는 산으로 데려가, 죽은 말 위에서 그자의 형제가 되겠다고 맹세하게 했지.
그 말은 내 외숙의 말이었소. 외숙이 손수 끌고 올라갔소. 나는 그 손을 보았소.
en: Then you gave Baekje back to a Baekje prince, with a Tang seal, at Bear Ford. Then you took us up a hill called Gain and made us swear to be his brother over a dead horse.
The horse was my uncle’s. He walked it up himself. I watched his hands.

lines: 평양에서는 우리 군사가 먼저 성문을 넘었소. 그러자 그대들의 도호부가 와서 우리 몫을 없음이라 적었지.
그대는 내가 반역자를 감싼다 하오. 나는 그대의 관리들이 세어 볼 생각도 하지 않은 백성을 감싸는 것이오.
en: At Pyongyang our men went through the gate first. Then your Protectorate came and wrote our share down as nothing.
You say I shelter rebels. I shelter the people your officials could not be bothered to count.

blocks.html: Alas! While the two kingdoms stood, we were the hounds that ran at your pointing finger. Now the game is all taken, and it is we who are threatened with the pot. Baekje, the bandits' leavings, is rewarded the way Han once paid off an old enemy; Silla, which died for Han, is cut down the way Han once killed a man for sparing it. Though the sun's light no longer turns our way, the sunflower's heart still faces the sun.
blocks.ko: 아아! 두 나라가 아직 평정되지 않았을 때는 손짓 하나에 사냥개처럼 내달렸는데, 들짐승이 다하자 도리어 삶아 죽이려는 핍박을 받습니다. 적의 찌꺼기인 백제는 도리어 원수에게 내리는 상을 받고, 한나라를 위해 목숨 바친 신라는 벌써 은인에게 내리는 칼을 받습니다. 태양의 빛이 비록 이쪽으로 돌아 비추지 않더라도, 해바라기의 본심은 여전히 해를 향합니다.
blocks.hanja: 嗚呼。兩國未定平，蒙指蹤之驅馳，野獸今盡，反見烹宰之侵逼。賊殘百濟，反蒙雍齒之賞，殉漢新羅，已見丁公之誅。大陽之曜，雖不廻光，葵藿本心，猶懷向日。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — King Munmu's reply to Xue Rengui

lines: 내 아우는 장안에 있소. 잘 있다고 전해 주시오. 내가 그 이름을 불렀다고도.
그대들이 구하러 왔다던 그 나라의 왕으로 남기를 영광으로 여기며 —
en: My brother is in Chang’an. Tell him I am well. Tell him I said his name.
I have the honour to remain the king of the country you came to save —
Bupmin.

blocks.html: Daeto copies it out fair. His hand is very steady. Later that night he writes a second letter, a short one, to a different address, and puts it in his sleeve, and does not send it yet.
blocks.ko: 대토가 그것을 정서한다. 손이 아주 차분하다. 그날 밤 늦게 그는 두 번째 편지를 쓴다. 짧은 편지다. 받는 곳이 다르다. 그는 그것을 소매에 넣고, 아직은 보내지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Second Letter
blocks.ko: 두 번째 편지

lines: 전하의 편지를 받아, 소리 내어 읽었습니다. 오후 한나절이 걸리더군요.
전보다는 적은 일에서, 전하의 종으로 남기를 영광으로 여기며 —
en: Your Majesty’s letter has been received, and read aloud. It took most of an afternoon.
Nowhere in it is the word “sorry.”
I have the honour to remain your servant, in fewer things than before —
Xue.
zh: 大王來書已收，高聲讀畢，費去大半個下午。
仁貴於更少之事上，仍為大王之僕——
zhLatn: Dàwáng láishū yǐ shōu, gāoshēng dú bì, fèi qù dà bàn ge xiàwǔ.
Tōngpiān bú jiàn yí ge “zuì” zì.
Rénguì yú gèng shǎo zhī shì shàng, réng wéi dàwáng zhī pú——
Xuē.

lines: 대총관의 편지를 받았소. 읽는 데 시간이 하나도 안 걸렸소.
en: The Commander’s letter has been received. It took no time at all.
Nowhere in it is the word “rice.”
I have the honour to remain the king —
B.

lines: 그럼 사과는 제가 직접 받으러 가겠습니다.
en: Then I will come and fetch the apology myself.
zh: 那麼，這一聲歉，仁貴親自來取。
zhLatn: Nàme, zhè yì shēng qiàn, Rénguì qīnzì lái qǔ.
——Xuē.

en: Come, then.

blocks.label: Seventy Ships
blocks.ko: 일흔 척

blocks.html: He comes. In the tenth month, off the western coast, a Silla squadron finds seventy Tang transports riding low with grain for the garrison at Bear Ford, and takes them: hulls, crews, one Tang colonel, and all of the rice.
blocks.ko: 그는 온다. 시월, 서해안 앞바다에서 신라 선단이 웅진 주둔군에게 갈 곡식을 싣고 무겁게 떠가는 당의 수송선 일흔 척을 찾아내 사로잡는다. 배와 사공과 당나라 낭장 하나, 그리고 쌀 전부를.

blocks.html: Winter, the sixth day of the tenth month: we struck more than seventy Tang grain transports and captured the colonel Qianer Dahou and over a hundred soldiers. The drowned were past counting. The geupchan Dangcheon's merit was first, and he was raised to sachan.
blocks.ko: 겨울 10월 6일, 당의 조운선 70여 척을 쳐서 낭장 겸이대후와 사졸 백여 명을 사로잡았다. 물에 빠져 죽은 자는 이루 셀 수 없었다. 급찬 당천의 공이 으뜸이어서 사찬의 관등을 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 冬十月六日，撃唐漕船七十餘艘，捉郞將鉗耳大侯、士卒百餘人。其淪沒死者，不可勝數。級飡當千功第一，授位沙飡。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), tenth month

en: Send word to the White Tiger that his rice has arrived.
Late. As usual.

blocks.html: The Tang are coming south. Silla is winning. That is exactly when armies start to chase…!
blocks.ko: 당군이 남쪽으로 내려온다. 신라가 이기고 있다. 군대가 쫓기 시작하는 건, 꼭 그런 때다…!

A blue Silla army is strung out on the road in pursuit, not yet in line. Mohe cavalry in brown furs crash the flank among pines. Real terrain. Painterly cinema. Flat sky, no clouds. No text, no watermark.

images.at: A room in Surabol, a year before Baekje falls
images.alt: In a lamplit Surabol room, Chunchu lays out the coming decades for his son like a field
images.prompt: Intimate cinematic CLOSE-UP still, 16:9. Kim Chunchu and his grown son Bupmin alone at night over maps, lamplight, quiet conspiratorial intimacy. Painterly digital art, cinematic chiaroscuro, stylized not photoreal not anime. No text, no watermark.

images.alt: Munmu seals his abject apology to the emperor with a crooked smile while masons raise a wall behind him.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Over-the-shoulder medium at dusk in a hilltop fortress works in Silla. ONE device: a half-built stone wall stepping diagonally up across the frame. King Munmu, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, crimson robe, sitting on a cut granite block amid the masons' work, a folded letter of apology in one hand, pressing the seal down on it with the other, wearing a dry crooked half-smile — the words are abject, the face is not. Behind him, small and dissolving into dusty haze, labourers haul stone up the slope. Foreground: an out-of-focus mason's rope and a stone block. Key: a low sun shaft through the dust raking across his face, the paper (nothing readable) and the folds of his silk; crimson specular; storm-dark sky above the ridge. CANON — KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: Stone Gate
blocks.ko: 석문

blocks.html: The Tang take Hansi and Mapeup and come south. Silla and what is left of the Goguryeo revival meet them, cut down several thousand, and then make the mistake that costs the year: they chase.
blocks.ko: 당군이 한시성과 마읍성을 취하고 남하한다. 신라와 고구려 부흥군의 남은 이들이 맞서 수천을 베고, 그리고 그해를 대가로 치를 실수를 저지른다. 뒤를 쫓은 것이다.

blocks.caption: The Tang come south and turn. Silla gives chase. Watch where the chase ends.
blocks.ko: 당군이 남으로 내려왔다가 돌아선다. 신라가 쫓는다. 그 추격이 어디서 끝나는지 보라.

blocks.html: At Seokmun the Tang turn around. The Mohe cavalry come in on a Silla army that has not yet formed up, and it is over in an afternoon.
blocks.ko: 석문에서 당군이 돌아선다. 아직 진을 펴지도 못한 신라군의 옆구리로 말갈 기병이 들이친다. 한나절 만에 끝난다.

blocks.html: A narrow place that looks like a way out, until it isn’t.
blocks.ko: 빠져나갈 길처럼 보이다가, 아니게 되는 좁은 곳.

blocks.html: Our troops and the Goguryeo troops met the enemy and took several thousand heads. When Gao Kan and the rest fell back, we chased them as far as Seokmun and fought there, and our army was routed. The daeachan Hyocheon, the sachan Uimun and Sanse … and others died there.
blocks.ko: 우리 군사가 고구려 군사와 함께 맞받아 싸워 수천 급을 베었다. 고간 등이 물러나자 석문까지 뒤쫓아 싸웠는데, 우리 군사가 크게 패하여 대아찬 효천, 사찬 의문·산세 … 등이 전사하였다.
blocks.hanja: 我兵與高句麗兵逆戰，斬首數千級。高侃等退，追至石門戰之，我兵敗績，大阿飡曉川、沙飡義文、山世…等死之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 12 (672), eighth month

blocks.html: Twelfth month: Gao Kan fought the Goguryeo remnants at Mount Baeksu and broke them. Silla sent troops to rescue Goguryeo, and Gao Kan broke those too.
blocks.ko: 12월, 고간이 고구려의 남은 무리와 백수산에서 싸워 깨뜨렸다. 신라가 군사를 보내 고구려를 구원하자, 고간이 그마저 쳐서 깨뜨렸다.
blocks.hanja: 十二月，高侃與高麗餘眾戰於白水山，破之。新羅遣兵救高麗，侃擊破之。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 202, Tang Gaozong, Xianheng 3 (672), twelfth month

blocks.title: Seokmun, eighth month, 672

units.label: The pursuit
units.sub: strung out, not yet in line

units.label: Seven commanders
units.sub: Hyocheon, Uimun, Sanse, Neungsin, Duseon, Annaham, Yangsin

blocks.note: Seven named commanders died at Seokmun. Silla stopped attacking after it, and spent three years building walls instead.

blocks.html: Silla sends an apology to Chang’an and hands back the prisoners. Then it goes quiet, and starts building.
blocks.ko: 신라는 장안에 사죄사를 보내고 억류한 포로를 돌려보낸다. 그러고는 조용해지고, 성을 쌓기 시작한다.

blocks.html: Your servant, guilty unto death, respectfully reports. … All the bamboo of the Southern Mountain would not be enough to write down your servant's crimes, nor all the forests of Baoxie to make his shackles. Flood our ancestral temple, tear your servant limb from limb: in this I await the imperial decision, and accept execution with a willing heart.
blocks.ko: 신 아무개는 죽을죄를 지었기에 삼가 아룁니다. … 남산의 대나무를 다 써도 신의 죄를 적기에 모자라고, 포야의 숲을 다 베어도 신의 형틀을 만들기에 모자랍니다. 종묘사직을 허물어 못으로 만들고 신의 몸을 찢어 죽이시더라도, 모든 일은 칙명의 처분을 따를 것이니 달게 죽음을 받겠습니다.
blocks.hanja: 臣某死罪謹言…南山之竹，不足書臣之罪，褒斜之林，未足作臣之械。瀦池宗社，屠裂臣身，事聽勅裁，甘心受戮。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 12 (672), ninth month — memorial of apology to the Tang court

blocks.title: A room in Surabol, a year before Baekje falls

lines: 법민아. 백제가 무너진 다음에 무슨 일이 일어날 것 같으냐?
en: Bupmin. What do you think happens after Baekje falls?
We move on Goryeo.
And after that.
…Unification.
No. / After that, it is our turn.

blocks.html: He lays it out the way another man would lay out a field. The Tang will not go home. They will put a governor in Sabi and call it a commandery. They will give you a title with the word province in it and expect you to be flattered. They will keep your brother in Chang’an and call him a guest.
blocks.ko: 그는 다른 사람이 밭을 펼쳐 보이듯 그것을 펼쳐 놓는다. 당은 돌아가지 않는다. 사비에 도독을 앉히고 도독부라 부를 것이다. 너에게 주(州)라는 글자가 들어간 벼슬을 주고 네가 우쭐하기를 바랄 것이다. 네 아우를 장안에 두고 손님이라 부를 것이다.

lines: 그때 절대로 먼저 치지 마라. / 저들이 고려에서 지칠 때까지 기다려라. / 성은 하나씩 되찾고, 되찾을 때마다 사죄 사절을 보내라. / 저들이 원하는 건 땅이 아니라 문서니까.
en: When it comes, never strike first. / Wait until they have exhausted themselves in the north. / Take the fortresses back one at a time, and send an apology after each one. / What they want is not the land. It is the paperwork.
…And the sea?

lines: 바다는 마지막이다. / 저들이 말을 다 잃은 뒤에.
en: The sea is last. / After they have lost the horses.
Father. How do you know all of this?

lines: 이세민한테 배웠다. / 그자가 나한테 하려던 걸 그대로 적어 뒀거든.
en: Li Shimin taught me. / I wrote down everything he intended to do to me.

blocks.html: One lieutenant came home from Stone Gate alive. His father is Kim Yushin…!
blocks.ko: 석문에서 살아 돌아온 비장이 하나 있다. 그의 아버지는 김유신이다…!

images.alt: Rembrandt’s Prodigal Son, refused: Wonsul kneels at his father’s shut gate offering his sword flat on both palms
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Rembrandt’s Return of the Prodigal Son, with no father in the doorway. Night outside a Silla noble house in Surabol: Wonsul, Yushin’s young son, kneels on the stone step before a shut timber gate with iron bosses, head bowed, in torn grey steel lamellar with blue cloth at the collar, holding his ring-pommel sword out flat on both upturned palms. Behind the gate’s lattice window above him one lamp burns, and the shadow of an old man stands behind the paper, turned away. The lamp rakes down across his bowed head and the offered blade; the street is black rain. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Wonsul, Yushin’s second son, is told to die there and does not. He comes home. His father will not see him, and his mother will not either, and he spends the rest of his life trying to give the afternoon back.
blocks.ko: 유신의 둘째 아들 원술은 그 자리에서 죽으라는 말을 듣고도 죽지 않는다. 살아 돌아온다. 아버지는 그를 보지 않고, 어머니도 보지 않는다. 그는 남은 평생 그 한나절을 되돌리려 애쓰며 산다.

blocks.html: Yushin's son Wonsul, a lieutenant, also meant to die fighting. His aide Danneung stopped him: “For a true man, dying is not the hard part. Choosing where to die is. If you die and achieve nothing, better to live and earn it later.” … Danneung held the bridle and would not let go, and so he could not die.
blocks.ko: 유신의 아들 원술은 비장으로서 그 역시 싸우다 죽으려 하였다. 그를 보좌하던 담릉이 말리며 말하였다. “대장부는 죽는 것이 어려운 것이 아니라, 죽을 자리를 가리는 것이 어려운 법입니다. 죽어도 이루는 것이 없다면, 살아서 뒷날의 공을 도모하느니만 못합니다.” … 담릉이 고삐를 붙들고 놓지 않으니, 마침내 죽지 못하였다.
blocks.hanja: 庾信子元述，為裨將，亦欲戰死，其佐淡凌，止之曰：「大丈夫，非死之難，處死之為難也。若死而無成，不若生而圖後效。」…淡凌攬轡不放，遂不能死。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 43, Biographies — Kim Yushin, part 3 (Wonsul, 672)

lines: 왕명을 욕되게 하고 가문의 이름까지 더럽혔으니, 내 아들이 아니다.
en: He shamed the king’s command and the family name with it. He is not my son.

blocks.html: The retreat is almost beside the point. Wonsul ran and lived; a hundred men did the same that afternoon and kept their fathers. But a house that arrived in Silla by treaty rather than by birth does not get to be ordinary — it has to be exemplary, permanently, in every generation, or it is simply Gaya again.
blocks.ko: 실은 퇴각이 문제의 핵심도 아니다. 원술은 달아나 살았고, 그날 오후 백 명이 같은 일을 하고도 아버지를 잃지 않았다. 그러나 태생이 아니라 조약으로 신라에 들어온 집안에게 평범함은 허락되지 않는다 — 대대로, 영구히, 본보기여야 한다. 그러지 못하는 순간 그저 다시 가야일 뿐이다.

lines: 남의 아들은 물러나도 되네. / 내 아들은 안 되고.
en: Another man’s son may retreat. / Mine may not.

blocks.html: Yushin goes to the king and asks, in so many words, for his son to be put to death. It is the most formal request he has made in fifty years of service, and he makes it standing.
blocks.ko: 유신은 왕에게 가서, 말 그대로 아들을 죽여 달라고 청한다. 쉰 해를 섬기며 올린 청 가운데 가장 격식을 갖춘 청이고, 그는 그것을 선 채로 올린다.

lines: 외숙. 그 애는 비장이었습니다. 비장은 따라가는 자리입니다.
석문에서 살아 돌아온 자를 다 죽이면, 다음 싸움에서 질 군사도 안 남습니다.
en: Uncle. He was a lieutenant. Lieutenants follow.
If I execute every man who lived through Seokmun, I won’t have an army left to lose the next one with.

lines: 다만 제 집에 다시 들이라고는 하지 마십시오.
en: Then do not execute him, Majesty.
But do not ask me to call him back into my house.

blocks.html: Wonsul does not go home. He goes into the hill farms east of the capital and works another man’s fields under no name at all, which is the one punishment his father did not think to ask for. He does not write. Twice he comes as far as the road below his father’s gate and turns back at the sight of the lamp.
blocks.ko: 원술은 집에 가지 않는다. 도성 동쪽 산골 농가로 들어가 이름도 없이 남의 밭을 간다. 아버지가 미처 청하지 못한 단 하나의 벌이다. 그는 편지를 쓰지 않는다. 두 번, 아버지 집 대문 아래 길까지 왔다가 등불을 보고 돌아선다.

blocks.speaker: Farmer
en: You hold a hoe like it owes you money.
Soldier, were you?

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: No.
…Not a good one.

blocks.html: Yushin is old now. The three sisters in the steam are not. They have kept his ledge warm for fifty years…!
blocks.ko: 유신은 이제 늙었다. 김 속의 세 자매는 아니다. 그들은 쉰 해 동안 그의 바위 자리를 데워 두었다…!

ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: Wonsul stands in the road until dark
images.alt: Wonsul, seen from behind, stands alone in the road before his mother's shut gate as night falls.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Far wide RÜCKENFIGUR at dusk falling into night on a packed-earth road below a Silla noble house in Surabol. ONE device: the road as a long line leading to a shut timber gate with iron bosses under a giwa-roofed gatehouse, one lamp lit above it. A lone young man seen only from behind — plain undyed hill-farmer's clothes, plain topknot, a hoe-callused hand hanging at his side — stands small in the lower third in the middle of the road, not moving; his long shadow stretches toward the gate. A servant is just slipping back through a narrow side door. The compound wall recedes at an angle. Granulated watercolor dusk sky with one last pale break over the gatehouse roof. Foreground: dark out-of-focus roadside grasses. His face is never shown. CANON — COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog.
